and continue fighting, the battle is finished through incapacitation. Superman can remain alive, physically intact, and enormously more durable than Gojo while still losing. If he can remain functional enough to escape the Domain instead, Gojo loses the cleanest win condition he has demonstrated.

Give Clark full information before the fight and the situation becomes different. He now knows what Gojo’s hand sign means and can use his enormous speed advantage to create distance before the barrier closes. That’s a useful alternate scenario, but it isn’t the battle we're analyzing because neither fighter begins with a guide to the other’s abilities.

The normal first encounter gives Gojo a valuable information advantage, but not a guaranteed trap. Infinity reveals itself safely when Superman’s first attack stops, allowing Clark to begin learning without harming Gojo. Unlimited Void is more dangerous because Clark may only understand it after the effect begins, yet his reaction speed leaves open the possibility that he exits the forming barrier before that happens.

Gojo’s Six Eyes don’t give him perfect knowledge of Superman either. He has to learn that Clark is absurdly durable by watching his techniques underperform and adjust from there. The difference is that Infinity keeps him alive while he gathers that information, giving him room to make mistakes that Clark doesn’t have once the Domain closes.

Across fresh fights where neither character starts with matchup knowledge, the same two interactions decide the result. Superman reaches Infinity first because he’s overwhelmingly faster and discovers that ordinary physical contact fails. Gojo learns that conventional damage isn’t enough and reaches Unlimited Void while Clark still lacks the information that would tell him exactly what the Domain does. Whether Clark’s reactions carry him out before it closes, and what sustained exposure does if he is caught, remain the major unresolved crossover questions.

The physical mismatch never disappears during any of this. Superman remains stronger, faster, tougher, and more experienced across a broader range of opponents. Gojo stays competitive because those advantages don’t automatically answer Infinity, while Unlimited Void gives him a credible route to incapacitation if its timing and mental effect break in his favor.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Put every normal stat next to each other and Superman destroys Gojo. Clark is faster by an absurd margin, hits much harder, survives vastly more punishment, has better long distance mobility, and has spent years facing threats far beyond the scale Gojo normally deals with. If Superman could reliably put his hands on him, this fight could end almost immediately.

Infinity prevents the obvious version of that outcome with Gojo’s normal defenses already active. Clark’s punches don’t demonstrate the spatial interaction needed to reach Gojo, while ranged attacks like heat vision and freeze breath should plausibly face the same intervening-space problem even though their exact crossover interaction is not directly established. Gojo doesn’t have to become faster or stronger than Superman for Infinity to remain the central defensive problem.

His own physical offense isn’t impressive enough to reverse the stat gap. Red and Blue can affect Clark without providing convincing finishing damage, and Hollow Purple’s actual manga showings don’t support treating it as automatic existence erasure. Gojo’s victory comes from
using those techniques long enough to understand that damaging Superman’s body is the wrong fight.

Unlimited Void gives Gojo his best answer. Superman has impressive mental resistance and superhuman information processing, but neither establishes a reliable immunity to a completed Domain continuously flooding his mind with information. If Clark is caught and sustained exposure prevents him from acting, Gojo can win through incapacitation without overcoming Kryptonian durability. What neither canon settles is whether Superman escapes during the Domain’s formation or how long his abnormal mind remains disabled once exposed.

Superman would handle the matchup much better with advance knowledge. He could recognize the Domain setup and use his speed to leave before Gojo encloses him, turning the fight into a much longer problem where Gojo has difficulty landing his best technique. Even without that knowledge, his reactions make the first activation uncertain rather than guaranteed. Advance knowledge simply makes the correct response much more obvious.

Across independent fights that reset both characters to the same starting conditions, there isn’t a clean consistent winner established by canon. Infinity gives Gojo protection against Superman’s most straightforward offense, and Clark’s normal behavior gives Gojo a credible opportunity to attempt Unlimited Void before Superman understands it. But Superman’s enormous reaction advantage means he may still escape as the Domain forms, and his exact response to sustained information overload is unknown.

That’s what makes the title sound ridiculous until you look at the abilities instead of the stat sheet. Superman dominates almost every category people normally use to decide a fight, but Gojo has a passive defense Clark can’t reliably bypass through his straightforward physical offense and an incapacitation technique that could be decisive if Clark is caught. The matchup turns on those unusual mechanics rather than on who can punch harder.

Gojo’s path to victory is sustained Unlimited Void after Infinity denies Superman’s straightforward offense long enough for him to attempt it. Clark’s path is using his overwhelming speed and reactions to avoid that Domain, then exploiting any workable interaction he can find with Infinity while Gojo struggles to damage him conventionally. Under the versions and starting conditions we've established, Gojo has a credible hax-based win condition, but the unresolved timing of Domain Expansion and Superman’s response to information overload keep the matchup from supporting a clear, consistent winner.

scripts.title: Gojo VS The Avengers Isnt Even Close

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Gojo versus the Avengers sounds like a fight the Avengers should win on numbers alone. They've got Hulk, Thor, Captain Marvel, Doctor Strange, Scarlet Witch, Iron Man, and enough firepower to level a battlefield. The problem is that almost all of them still have to actually reach Gojo before any of that matters.

That's what makes this matchup weird. Infinity can shut down most normal attacks, while Gojo still has Blue, Red, Hollow Purple, Reverse Cursed Technique, and Unlimited Void to fight back. So we're going through the Avengers one by one, starting with the people who have no real answer for Infinity and working up to the few who can at least make Gojo think. Even then, once you break down how their abilities actually interact with his, Gojo clears the ladder a lot easier than the Avengers lineup makes it sound.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Gojo’s first opponents would be Hawkeye, Black Widow, Falcon, Winter Soldier, and Spider-Man. Most of them rely on weapons, physical attacks, or movement, which makes Infinity a huge problem right away because every punch, bullet, arrow, missile, or web still has to cross the space around Gojo before it can reach him.

Hawkeye and Black Widow would have the least to work with. Clint can switch between explosive arrows, shock arrows, and other trick shots, while Natasha can use firearms, explosives, and close range weapons. None of those gives them a real answer for Infinity. Their attacks would slow down and stop before touching Gojo, and neither one has the durability to survive much once he starts fighting back.

Falcon has more mobility and can attack from the air, but that only changes the angle. His guns, missiles, and Redwing still need to travel toward Gojo, so Infinity stops them the same way. He could try attacking the ground or the area around Gojo instead, but Gojo can use Limitless and Blue for rapid aerial repositioning and avoid getting trapped as easily by the environment. I would not treat his more explicit teleportation as a guaranteed escape button, because that technique has conditions the series never fully defines.

Winter Soldier brings more strength and durability than Hawkeye or Black Widow, but he still fights through direct contact and weapons. His metal arm could hit hard enough to hurt most people in the MCU, but strength does not matter if the punch never reaches Gojo. Guns and knives create the same problem, so Bucky does not have much of a path to victory. Spider-Man would last much longer than the rest because his speed, agility, and spider-sense make him much harder to hit. He could avoid some uses of Blue, move through the battlefield quickly, and react before Gojo finishes certain attacks, but spider-sense only helps Peter know danger is coming. It does not give him a way through Infinity.

Peter could try webbing Gojo, rushing him from different angles, or using the environment to create pressure, but all of those still depend on something reaching Gojo physically. Once Gojo starts using Blue to pull Peter off balance or control where he can move, Spider-Man loses a lot of the freedom that makes him difficult to catch.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The next group would be Black Panther, War Machine, Ant-Man, and Iron Man. They bring better technology, stronger defenses, and more ways to attack from range, but each one still needs some kind of method for getting around Infinity if they want to actually hurt Gojo.

Black Panther has the easiest problem to explain. His vibranium suit can absorb huge amounts of kinetic energy and lets him survive hits that would destroy a normal person, but T’Challa still needs to physically reach Gojo. His claws, punches, and stored kinetic blasts all start from somewhere and move toward the target, so Infinity keeps him outside striking range.

War Machine has far more firepower and could fill the battlefield with missiles, bullets, and explosives. Rhodey would probably try to overwhelm Gojo with several attacks at once, which could destroy the area around him even if none of the weapons touch his body. Gojo can still move through the air and use Blue to reposition himself, so blowing apart the ground would make the fight more annoying without giving Rhodey a reliable hit.

Ant-Man is more interesting because shrinking sounds like something that could slip through Infinity. The problem is that Infinity is not a physical shield with tiny gaps Scott can fit through. It affects the space between Gojo and whatever approaches him. Scott could shrink down to microscopic size and still have to cross that distance, so becoming smaller does not get him any closer.

Iron Man would be the hardest fight in this section because Tony has the tools and intelligence to start testing the defense instead of repeating the same attack. His nanotech armor gives him repulsors, missiles, lasers, blades, shields, flight, and the ability to switch between them very quickly.

Tony would probably notice almost immediately that projectiles stop before touching Gojo. From there, he could attack the ground under him, bring structures down nearby, or use explosives around the battlefield instead of aiming directly at his body. That is a smarter approach because it forces Gojo to move rather than waiting behind Infinity.

Even then, Tony would still struggle to turn that into a clean hit. Gojo can use Limitless and Blue for rapid aerial repositioning and control parts of the battlefield himself, though I would not assume his conditional teleportation automatically gets him out of every environmental trap. Repulsors and lasers still move toward him through space, nanotech blades still need to touch him, and restraints have the same problem. Gojo could also use Blue to pull Tony out of his flight path or drag pieces of the armor where he wants them. Tony is durable enough to survive some punishment, but Red would hit hard enough to damage the suit, and Hollow Purple becomes an option if Gojo wants to end the fight quickly.

Tony makes the matchup more complicated because he can adapt, but adaptation only helps if he finds a real bypass. Nothing in his normal MCU arsenal clearly gives him one, so Gojo still takes the group.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Hulk would be the first Avenger where raw strength becomes ridiculous. He can smash through buildings, throw huge objects, survive explosions, and overpower almost anyone once he gets close. If Hulk ever lands a clean punch on Gojo without Infinity protecting him, Gojo would take serious damage.

Getting that punch to connect is the entire problem. Hulk can charge, jump, throw debris, or create shockwaves by smashing the ground, but each one still travels toward Gojo through space. Infinity slows that approach before contact, so Hulk’s strength does not get a chance to matter in the way it normally does.

Hulk would be much harder for Gojo to put down than the earlier Avengers. Blue could throw him around and Red could send him flying, but Hulk has survived enough physical punishment that neither one should be treated like an instant win.

Hollow Purple gives Gojo a much stronger option. Hulk has great durability, but Purple is an unusual Limitless-based attack rather than something with a clean MCU equivalent, so there is no reliable way to translate Hulk’s normal durability feats into exactly how well he would take it. It should not be treated like automatic existence erasure either. What we can say is that it is Gojo’s most dangerous direct attack, and Hulk’s size and habit of charging straight at opponents would not help him avoid a clean hit.

Unlimited Void is probably the cleanest answer because Hulk has no shown defense against the kind of mental overload Gojo’s domain creates. His strength and durability do nothing once the domain starts flooding his mind with information, and he would stop being able to fight properly long before he finds a way through Infinity.

Hulk can take more damage than most of the Avengers, but he still cannot make his biggest advantage matter. Gojo wins because Hulk has no reliable way to touch him and no clear answer for Unlimited Void.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Thor would be a much harder matchup because he brings lightning, flight, Mjolnir or Stormbreaker, and some of the best durability in the Avengers on top of his physical strength. He still has the same problem with Infinity, but he has more ways to test it than Hulk does. Stormbreaker is the first thing worth looking at because it has one of the strongest weapon feats in the MCU. Thor throws it through a blast from the completed Infinity Gauntlet and buries it into Thanos’ chest. That proves how much power the weapon can push through, but it does not prove it can ignore space itself.

If Thor throws Stormbreaker at Gojo, the axe still has to travel from Thor’s hand to Gojo’s body. Infinity should slow it down before contact. The same applies to Mjolnir. It can change direction, return to Thor, and hit with huge force, but it is still moving through space the entire time. Lightning is where Thor becomes more interesting. He does not always fire lightning like a normal projectile, and there are times where it appears around a target or comes down from above. If that lightning still has to propagate through space into Gojo, Infinity should interfere with it. If an MCU lightning effect is genuinely generated directly at Gojo’s position instead, neither series establishes how that would interact with Infinity, so I’d leave it as a possible but unresolved bypass rather than assume Thor can land it.

Even then, Gojo has ways to handle damage if something gets through. Cursed energy reinforcement helps him take hits, and Reverse Cursed Technique gives him a way to heal as long as the damage does not kill him outright. Thor would need to keep landing attacks while dealing with Gojo’s own offense.

Thor is durable enough that Red should not immediately end the fight. He survived the energy of a star long enough to forge Stormbreaker and has taken repeated hits from Hulk and Thanos, so Gojo would need something stronger or more precise if he wants a clean finish.

Unlimited Void becomes the problem again. Thor has no clear mental resistance feat that would let him function normally after being caught inside the domain. His physical toughness would not protect him from the information overload, and once his mind locks up, Gojo has plenty of time to finish the fight.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Captain Marvel would be the strongest pure physical matchup so far. Carol combines flight, huge speed, ranged energy attacks, enough strength to overpower Thanos for short periods, and durability that lets her fly straight through massive ships without slowing down.

If she flies at him at full speed, she still has to cross the space around his body. Infinity is automatic for adult Gojo, so he does not need to manually react to Carol every time she rushes him. Her speed can make it harder for Gojo to attack back, but it does not let her skip the effect protecting him.

Her energy blasts face the same problem. They travel from Carol toward the target, which means they still have to pass through Infinity. She could attack the environment or create large explosions nearby, but Gojo can move through the air and reposition with Blue before that turns into a reliable way of hurting him.

Carol’s durability would make the offensive side much harder for Gojo. Red could knock her away without necessarily doing enough damage to stop her, and Blue may have to work harder to control someone who can generate that much force while flying.

Hollow Purple would be Gojo’s best direct damage option, but its exact interaction with Carol’s MCU durability is hard to quantify. Purple is an unusual Limitless-based attack rather than a normal energy blast, while Carol has survived enormous amounts of energy and physical punishment. That means I would not call it an automatic erasure or assume she can simply tank some fixed amount of it. A clean Purple is still Gojo’s most dangerous direct way of trying to put her down.

Unlimited Void gives Gojo another route that avoids the durability argument entirely. Carol has never shown resistance to having her mind overloaded with endless information. Once she is trapped inside the domain, her speed and strength become much less useful because she cannot fight normally.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Doctor Strange would be the first Avenger who gives Gojo a genuinely different kind of problem because most of Strange’s best abilities do not depend on hitting someone with raw force. He can open portals, trap people in the Mirror Dimension, separate a person from their body, create restraints, duplicate himself, and control the battlefield in ways that are much harder to compare directly with a punch or energy blast.

Portals would be the first thing to look at. Strange can open one directly near an opponent, move attacks through it, or use it to change where someone is standing. If he opens a portal behind Gojo and sends something through, the object still has to move from the portal to Gojo, so Infinity should stop the final part of the attack. The better option would be trying to place the portal itself around Gojo or use it to remove part of the space he is standing in.

That interaction is not something either universe gives us a clean answer for. Gojo’s Six Eyes and spatial awareness would help him recognize that Strange is doing something unusual, but Strange’s sorcery is not established as cursed energy, and Gojo has no specific feat proving he can resist a portal forming around the space he occupies. So trying to portal Gojo himself or remove the space around him is a legitimate possible Infinity bypass and battlefield-removal win condition for Strange, not a guaranteed success or something I would assume Gojo automatically reacts out of.

The Mirror Dimension would be one of Strange’s strongest options because it changes the battlefield without needing to damage Gojo directly. If Strange can pull Gojo into it, then he can reshape the environment, fold buildings, change gravity, and control the space around them in ways normal fighters cannot. Infinity would still protect Gojo from physical contact, but the dimension itself could become a problem if Strange starts moving the whole environment instead of throwing attacks at his body.

The problem for Strange is actually keeping Gojo trapped there. Gojo has exceptional mobility through Limitless and Blue, and he has demonstrated teleportation under conditions the series never fully explains, but I would not assume that teleportation automatically lets him leave another dimension. His spatial abilities may help him understand and respond to what Strange is doing, and he does not need to beat Strange inside the Mirror Dimension by playing along with the terrain. Blue or Red could interrupt Strange before he gets full control, and Hollow Purple could force Strange to defend instead of constantly changing the battlefield.

Astral projection is another interesting possibility because Infinity does not clearly protect against something that attacks the soul or astral form directly. The problem is that Strange's demonstrated MCU version requires him to physically strike or touch the target first. Infinity already prevents that contact unless Strange finds another way around it, so astral projection is not an independent bypass here. It only becomes useful if one of his spatial tricks creates an opening first.

Strange could also use the Crimson Bands or other magical restraints, but those still tend to move toward the opponent before wrapping around them. Infinity should slow them the same way it slows other incoming attacks. The restraints themselves could be strong enough to hold Gojo if they somehow got around him, but Strange does not have a clean way to guarantee that happens.

The Time Stone would make this fight much more complicated if we allowed Strange to use it, but the late-stage Avengers version in Endgame no longer has it as a normal part of his arsenal. If we are using Infinity War Strange with the Time Stone, then he can loop events, look through possible futures, and manipulate time directly, which gives him a much stronger argument. Even then, he still needs a practical way to turn that information into a win.

Unlimited Void makes the matchup even worse for him. Strange has excellent mental discipline and experience with strange dimensions, but he has never shown a clear defense against having endless information forced into his mind all at once. If Gojo gets him inside the domain, Strange probably loses before he can cast his way out.

That means Strange is the first Avenger with abilities that could realistically interact with Infinity in a strange way, but the fight still favors Gojo. Strange has more tools, but Gojo has the easier win condition. Strange has to find the right spatial or astral trick and make it work before Gojo gets a domain or a clean attack. Gojo only needs one strong opening.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Scarlet Witch would be the hardest individual matchup for Gojo because Wanda’s powers are much less dependent on normal contact than almost anyone else on the team. By Endgame and especially later in the MCU, she can use telekinesis, energy attacks, mental effects, and reality manipulation at a level that makes her dangerous even to people who are physically much stronger than she is.

The first question is whether her telekinesis can affect Gojo directly through Infinity. Wanda often moves people and objects without firing a visible projectile first. She can lift someone, restrain them, or crush them from a distance just by focusing on the target. If that effect starts directly on Gojo’s body instead of traveling toward him, then Infinity may not stop it the same way it stops a punch or beam.

That would give Wanda one of the few real ways to pressure him without solving Infinity first. She could try to lift him, pin his arms, crush the ground around him, or attack his body from several directions at once. Gojo would still have cursed energy reinforcement and Reverse Cursed Technique, but he would actually need to respond instead of standing still and letting Infinity handle everything.

Gojo would also have his own telekinetic control through Blue, which makes the fight much less one-sided than it sounds. If Wanda tries to lift him, Gojo can pull himself toward another point, distort the space around them, or use Red to blast her away before she keeps control long enough to do serious damage.

Wanda’s physical durability is much lower than her offensive power, and that matters a lot here. She can take some hits and protect herself with magic, but she is not built like Thor or Captain Marvel. A clean Red could hurt her badly, and Hollow Purple would be extremely dangerous if she does not get out of the way.

Her mental abilities are still worth mentioning because Infinity does not automatically make Gojo immune to mind manipulation. Wanda has controlled minds and created visions before, but Endgame-era Wanda has not consistently shown that she can instantly apply precise psychic control to an actively fighting opponent at range. That makes it a possible interaction rather than her strongest practical win condition here; her direct telekinesis is the much better demonstrated bypass argument.

Gojo also has strong mental control and years of experience fighting through cursed techniques, but I would not use that as proof that he can simply resist Wanda if a psychic effect does land. The bigger limitation is on Wanda's side: this version of her has a much clearer record of using telekinesis offensively in a live fight than immediately shutting an opponent down through ranged mind control.

Reality manipulation is where the discussion gets even harder. If we use Wanda at her strongest later MCU levels, she can change matter and alter reality around people in ways Infinity is not designed to answer directly. If she simply changes the environment Gojo is standing in or alters something about his body without sending an attack through space, Infinity may not matter.

But for this battle brief, we are using late-stage Avengers from Infinity War and Endgame, which means we should not automatically give Wanda every feat she gets later in WandaVision or Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. Endgame Wanda is extremely powerful, but her abilities are still much more focused around telekinesis, energy, and direct control than full reality rewriting on the scale she reaches later.

That version of Wanda can absolutely threaten Gojo if her telekinesis is the kind of effect that acts directly on his body, but that interaction is still a crossover assumption rather than something either canon proves. If Infinity does not intercept it, the problem becomes surviving long enough to finish the job. Gojo is faster, better in close combat, and can use Blue or Red without needing much setup. Wanda has strong reactions, but she still struggles when someone gets through her defense quickly.

Unlimited Void is probably the biggest reason Gojo wins. Wanda has very strong mental powers, but she has no feat showing that she can function normally after being hit with an endless flood of information from every direction. Her mind is powerful, but the domain does not work like a normal psychic attack she can simply push back against.

She could try to stop Gojo before the domain opens, and that is probably her best chance. If she grabs him with telekinesis and starts crushing him immediately, Gojo may need Reverse Cursed Technique while trying to break her focus. Blue could pull her off balance, Red could force her to defend, and if he gets even a small opening, Unlimited Void ends the fight.

Wanda is the first Avenger where Gojo cannot just stand behind Infinity and wait for the opponent to realize nothing works. She has a real argument for bypassing the defense because her telekinesis may affect the target directly. Even with that, Gojo still has the better overall matchup because his defense, speed, healing, and domain give him more ways to survive one mistake than Wanda has.
Gojo wins, but Wanda makes him work for it more than anyone else on the ladder.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Before getting to the full team, it’s worth looking at what happens when the Avengers start combining their biggest physical threats. Thor and Captain Marvel together would create far more pressure than either one alone because Gojo would have to deal with two extremely fast and durable opponents attacking from different directions.

Carol could stay in the air and keep moving around Gojo while Thor attacks with lightning and Stormbreaker. That would force Gojo to keep track of several attacks at once, especially if Thor uses lightning from above while Carol tries to rush him from another angle.

That could make landing Hollow Purple harder. The attack is powerful, but it is not something Gojo casually fires every second. Carol is fast enough to move out of a bad line, and Thor can use Mjolnir or Stormbreaker to change position quickly.

Blue would be more useful because Gojo can use it to mess with their movement. Pulling Thor away from Stormbreaker or dragging Carol off her flight path could create the small opening he needs. Red could then separate the two and stop them from keeping the pressure together. The problem for the Avengers is that combining physical attackers does not solve the main issue. Two people who cannot touch Gojo do not suddenly gain a bypass just because they attack at the same time.

Unlimited Void would also punish both of them together. If Gojo catches Thor and Captain Marvel inside the domain, neither has a clear way to defend their mind. The fight becomes easier for Gojo once he decides to stop trying to trade attacks and uses the ability that ignores their biggest strength.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Doctor Strange and Scarlet Witch together would be much more dangerous than pairing the strongest physical Avengers. Strange can change space and control the battlefield while Wanda can test the team’s best plausible Infinity bypass: telekinesis or other effects that may act directly on Gojo instead of traveling toward him. Whether that actually bypasses Infinity is uncertain, but if it does, Strange is exactly the kind of teammate who could capitalize on the opening.
This would be the Avengers’ best 2 person combo by far.

Strange could start by forcing Gojo to deal with portals, restraints, and changing terrain while Wanda uses telekinesis to try to hold him in place. If Gojo focuses on Wanda, Strange can move her out of danger. If he focuses on Strange, Wanda has more time to attack directly.

The Mirror Dimension could also become much more useful with Wanda involved. Strange could pull the fight somewhere he has more control, while Wanda keeps pressure on Gojo inside that space. Gojo would still have Infinity, but the whole battlefield could be moving around him while Wanda attacks his body directly.
This is where Gojo would need to stop testing what they can do and go for a fast finish.

Strange is the easier target physically, so Gojo would probably remove him first. A well-placed Blue could pull Strange out of position before he finishes a spell, while Red could hit hard enough to take him out of the fight. Wanda could try to protect him, but that means she is spending concentration on defense instead of attacking Gojo.
If Strange goes down, Wanda loses the person giving her the best control over space and movement. Gojo can then focus everything on her.

If Wanda gets Gojo with telekinesis first, the fight becomes dangerous because she could try to crush him before he can use his domain. Reverse Cursed Technique would give him some time, and Gojo does not need to move his whole body to activate every technique. He could still use Blue or Red while restrained if he can maintain enough control.

Unlimited Void would probably be what decides it. Strange and Wanda are both mentally strong, but neither has a proven answer for the domain’s information overload. Once Gojo opens it, the Avengers have to stop the domain itself or avoid being caught.

Strange might try escaping through a portal, but the domain’s sure hit activates inside the barrier, and opening a portal while his mind is already being overwhelmed would be extremely difficult. Wanda could try breaking the barrier from inside, but Gojo’s domains are strong enough that she would need to do it almost instantly.

This duo is the first time Gojo could realistically lose if he gives them too much time to work together. Strange creates opportunities, Wanda has a possible Infinity bypass, and both of them can attack without relying on simple physical force.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: The full Avengers team would be the hardest version of the fight because the weaker members finally have a useful role. Hawkeye, Black Widow, Falcon, Winter Soldier, Spider-Man, Black Panther, War Machine, Ant-Man, Iron Man, Hulk, Thor, Captain Marvel, Doctor Strange, and Scarlet Witch attacking together gives Gojo far more to watch at once.

The team’s best strategy would revolve around Strange and Wanda. Everyone else should be there to create noise, movement, and pressure while those two look for the actual opening. Thor and Captain Marvel could stay on Gojo physically so he has less time to attack Strange. Hulk could destroy the battlefield around him, Iron Man and War Machine could fill the air with explosives, Spider-Man could keep moving around the edges, and Ant-Man could change size to make targeting more complicated.
That is the Avengers’ best chance.

If Wanda’s telekinesis can act directly on Gojo and Infinity does not intercept that interaction, she could potentially hold or pressure him long enough for Strange to add another effect. Thor or Captain Marvel could then be waiting for any moment where Infinity drops or Gojo’s concentration gets interrupted. That is the team’s best plausible route, not an established property of Wanda’s telekinesis.
The weaker Avengers also become liabilities once Gojo attacks back.

Blue can pull several people into one area, Red can clear large sections of the battlefield, and Hollow Purple can force everyone to move at once. Hawkeye, Black Widow, Falcon, Winter Soldier, and even Spider-Man cannot afford to take many direct hits. Gojo could remove a large part of the team very quickly if he stops focusing on individual fights and starts using wider attacks.
That would make the numbers advantage disappear fast.

Iron Man could try to protect weaker members with shields, Strange could portal people out of danger, and Wanda could block some attacks with telekinesis, but every defensive move keeps one of the key Avengers from attacking Gojo.

The moment Strange or Wanda goes down, the team’s chance of winning drops massively. Thor, Hulk, and Captain Marvel can keep fighting for a long time, but they go back to having no reliable Infinity bypass.
Gojo would understand that and target Strange or Wanda first.

The Six Eyes would help him keep track of where the real threats are, even with everyone moving around him. Strange casting a spell or Wanda building telekinetic pressure would stand out far more than Hawkeye firing another arrow or Hulk charging from the side.
Gojo could use Blue to pull Strange away from the group, Red to force Wanda off balance, or simply open Unlimited Void before the team has time to set up their full strategy.

Anyone Gojo successfully catches inside Unlimited Void would be in enormous trouble. Hulk, Thor, Captain Marvel, Spider-Man, Iron Man, and the others have no clear demonstrated resistance to the information overload. Strange and Wanda also have no directly comparable demonstrated counter, although their magical and mental abilities make the exact cross-universe interaction less certain. The other uncertainty is how much of a large, mobile team Gojo can actually catch in one activation.

The Avengers could try spreading out so Gojo cannot catch everyone in one domain, but that makes it harder for them to coordinate their best attacks. Strange and Wanda need protection if they are going to get enough time to work, and spreading the team too far gives Gojo more chances to isolate them.

They could also try having Strange trap Gojo in the Mirror Dimension before he uses his domain, but that requires Strange to get the setup off while Gojo knows he is one of the two people who actually matters.
Gojo would not spend the opening minutes fighting Hulk while Strange stands in the back preparing something. He is smart enough to understand the matchup once he sees what everyone can do.

That is why the full-team matchup is much less clean than most of the individual fights. Gojo has the simpler demonstrated path to victory: most of the Avengers still cannot bypass Infinity, while Strange and Wanda have to make one of their less conventional spatial or direct-effect interactions work before Gojo removes them or opens his domain.

The Avengers have a possible plan, but it depends on several things going right at the same time. Strange needs to control the battlefield, Wanda needs to get a direct effect on Gojo, the physical fighters need to keep enough pressure on him to stop him from immediately targeting the casters, and everyone has to avoid Unlimited Void.
Gojo’s plan is much simpler. Keep Infinity active, remove Strange or Wanda first, and use his domain once enough of the team is in range.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Gojo clears most of the Avengers ladder much easier than the lineup makes it sound. Hawkeye, Black Widow, Falcon, Winter Soldier, Black Panther, War Machine, Ant-Man, Spider-Man, and Iron Man do not have a reliable way through Infinity. Hulk adds huge strength and durability, but strength does not solve the distance problem. Thor brings lightning and weapons but Stormbreaker and Mjolnir still have to reach Gojo. Captain Marvel is even faster and harder to hurt, yet her best attacks still run into the same defense.

Doctor Strange and Scarlet Witch are where the matchup becomes interesting. Strange can manipulate space, and Wanda can use telekinesis in ways that may affect Gojo without a normal projectile. Those are legitimate interactions that deserve to be taken seriously. Gojo can keep Infinity running automatically, heal damage with Reverse Cursed Technique, use Blue and Red to control the fight, hit hard enough with Hollow Purple to threaten even durable Avengers, and finish the matchup through Unlimited Void without needing to overpower Thor, Hulk, or Captain Marvel physically.

The full Avengers team makes the fight harder because Strange and Wanda get more protection and more distractions to work with. Their best possible strategy would be having the physical Avengers keep Gojo busy while Strange controls the battlefield and Wanda tries to attack him directly.
That plan can work if everything lines up perfectly.

Gojo still has the cleaner demonstrated path because he understands very quickly which two people matter. Once Strange or Wanda is removed, most of the Avengers lose their only realistic arguments for getting around Infinity. So the title is pretty accurate in the sense that the numbers mismatch is misleading: most of the team can hit much harder than Gojo ever wants to take directly, but their attacks still cannot reach him. The full-team result is less absolute, though, because Strange and Wanda introduce cross-universe interactions that neither canon defines well enough to turn into a reliable win percentage.

scripts.title: How Does Gojos Infinity Actually Work

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Gojo’s Infinity looks simple from the outside. Someone tries to punch him, stab him, or shoot something at him, and it just stops before making contact.

But Infinity isn’t an invisible wall around his body. Gojo is using Limitless to control the space between himself and whatever is coming toward him, so the closer an attack gets, the more its movement gets slowed down until it looks like it’s frozen right in front of him.
And that one idea is the base for almost everything else he does. Blue, Red, Hollow Purple, even the way his domain works all come from different ways Gojo manipulates the same technique.
So to understand why people can’t touch Gojo, you first have to understand what Limitless is actually doing to space.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Infinity is the neutral form of Limitless, which is Gojo’s inherited cursed technique. Limitless lets him manipulate space, and Infinity is what happens when he uses that technique defensively around himself. The easiest way to picture it is that there’s still a normal amount of space between Gojo and whatever is coming toward him, but Limitless keeps dividing that distance into smaller and smaller pieces. The closer the attack gets, the more its remaining approach is divided into smaller and smaller intervals, so from the outside it looks like the attack is slowing down until it practically stops. That's why punches, blades, and projectiles can hang right in front of him without actually touching him.

Gojo himself compares the idea to Achilles and the tortoise. Achilles keeps getting closer, but there’s always another smaller gap left before he reaches the tortoise. That's a useful way to picture Infinity, but it’s still an analogy for what the cursed technique is doing. Jujutsu Kaisen isn’t saying Gojo is literally solving a real physics problem around his body every second. Limitless takes that mathematical idea and makes it real through cursed energy.

He can also change how much space Infinity covers. We’ve seen him expand it outward to keep things away from him and increase its output enough to physically pressure an opponent. So even the basic defensive version isn’t just a fixed bubble sitting around his skin. Gojo is controlling how Limitless behaves around him depending on what he needs.

The reason this matters is that Infinity is only the starting point. Once Gojo starts changing what Limitless does to space instead of simply keeping things from reaching him, you get Blue, Red, and eventually Hollow Purple.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Blue is what happens when Gojo strengthens the normal Limitless technique with more cursed energy. Instead of only slowing something down as it approaches him, he creates a point where space is being forced to converge. Everything around that point gets dragged inward, which is easiest to picture as the surrounding space converging toward that point rather than as a literal physical collapse with fully defined real-world mechanics.

That’s why Blue looks like attraction. If Gojo places Blue near 2 targets, he can pull them toward the same spot. If he puts enough output into it, the attraction can crush objects, tear through buildings, or drag someone around without him physically touching them. He can also move the point itself, which makes Blue useful for way more than just firing a blue orb at somebody.

Gojo also uses Blue to improve his own movement. By manipulating space around himself, he can pull his body toward a point and move much faster than he would through normal physical movement alone. That's part of why his speed can be so hard to read in fights. He isn’t always just running or jumping faster. Sometimes he’s using Limitless to change how he moves through the space around him.

And this is where the relationship between Gojo’s techniques starts becoming obvious. Infinity keeps an approaching object from ever finishing the distance to him. Blue takes that same control over space and pushes convergence much harder, turning it into an offensive pull.
Red does the exact opposite.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Cursed Technique Reversal Red comes from applying positive energy generated through reverse cursed technique to Limitless, producing the opposite effect from Blue. Blue is created through the normal application of cursed energy, while Red uses positive energy generated through reverse cursed technique. That flips the effect from convergence into divergence, so instead of space pulling inward, Red violently pushes outward.

That's why Red hits like a huge repulsive blast. When Gojo uses it against someone, he isn’t firing a normal projectile that explodes on contact. He’s creating an outward force through Limitless that launches whatever is in front of him away. It’s the same inherited technique behaving in the opposite direction.

This was also a big deal for Gojo himself because teenage Gojo could use Blue before he understood how to use Red. During Hidden Inventory, he knew the theory behind cursed technique reversal but couldn’t make it work consistently. After Toji nearly killed him, Gojo finally understood reverse cursed technique properly, which let him produce the positive energy needed for Red.

That moment is important because Red isn’t just another move he unlocked later. It proves that Gojo has learned to run Limitless in both directions. He can create attraction with Blue and repulsion with Red, which means he now has access to both sides of the technique.
And once he can use both at the same time, he can do something much worse.

Hollow Purple is created by combining Blue and Red. The convergence from Blue and the divergence from Red collide, producing what the series describes as an imaginary mass that rushes forward with huge destructive power.
So Purple isn’t some random ultimate attack that has nothing to do with Infinity. It’s the end result of Gojo taking the 2 opposite applications of the same technique and forcing them together.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Hollow Purple is probably where people overcomplicate Gojo the most because it looks like an attack that should just erase anything it touches. The canon explanation is more specific. Purple comes from combining the convergence of Blue with the divergence of Red, creating an imaginary mass that moves forward and destroys what it hits.

The important part is that Purple is incredibly destructive, but you shouldn't automatically treat it like some literal existence eraser that ignores durability no matter who it hits. We’ve seen it tear through huge areas and remove major sections of Toji’s body, and later uses show just how large Gojo can make it. But the series still treats it as an attack with output, range, and damage rather than a magic button that says the target no longer exists.

That makes the relationship between all 4 applications much cleaner. Neutral Infinity slows anything trying to reach Gojo. Blue pulls space inward. Red pushes it outward. Purple smashes those opposite effects together into one attack.
But none of this would be practical for Gojo without the Six Eyes.

Limitless is an extremely difficult technique to control because it requires ridiculous precision with cursed energy. Other members of the Gojo clan can inherit Limitless, but the Six Eyes are what let Gojo use it at the level we actually see. They give him extremely detailed perception of cursed energy and let him control his own cursed energy with absurd precision.
The biggest advantage is efficiency. Gojo loses an almost nonexistent amount of cursed energy when using his technique, which is why he can keep doing things that would completely drain
another sorcerer. That doesn’t mean he has literally infinite cursed energy. He’s just so efficient that the amount wasted when he uses it is almost zero.
That efficiency is what eventually lets Infinity become something Gojo can leave running constantly instead of manually turning it on every time somebody attacks him.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: When Gojo was younger, Infinity wasn’t always running automatically. He had to control it himself, and keeping it active for too long would tire him out. After Hidden Inventory, he starts working on making the defense automatic so he doesn’t have to consciously decide whether every single thing around him should be stopped.

The system he develops can judge approaching objects based on things like cursed energy, mass, speed, and shape. That's why Infinity can stop a weapon or an attack while still letting normal things through. Gojo isn’t walking around sealed inside a completely airtight bubble where nothing can ever reach him. The technique is constantly filtering what counts as a threat. The Six Eyes make that possible because they give him the perception and cursed energy control needed to run Limitless with insane accuracy. He also uses reverse cursed technique to keep his brain refreshed, which helps him maintain Infinity without eventually frying himself from the constant load.

That answers one of the biggest questions about how Gojo lives normally. Air can reach him. He can eat, drink, touch people, wear clothes, and interact with the world because Infinity isn’t blindly stopping every molecule that approaches his body. He can let harmless things through and block dangerous ones.

That's why the characters who get around Infinity usually don’t do it by being faster or hitting harder. They use abilities or tools that interfere with the technique itself, cancel it, adapt to it, or create an attack that doesn’t approach Gojo in the normal way.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Unlimited Void is where people sometimes mix Infinity up with Gojo’s domain and assume it is just a bigger version of the same defense. It isn’t. Infinity controls the space around Gojo, while Unlimited Void is Gojo manifesting Limitless through his innate domain, where the domain's sure-hit overwhelms the target with effectively boundless information.
Once someone is caught inside, their brain is overwhelmed by a seemingly endless stream of information they cannot properly process or turn into normal action.
Gojo describes it as being given everything and nothing at the same time. The target is technically receiving information, but they can’t finish processing any of it.

That's why someone caught in Unlimited Void can look completely frozen even though their mind is being overwhelmed. It’s not physical paralysis from Infinity slowing their body down. Their brain is getting hit with so much information that even a simple action becomes impossible to complete.

The domain also gives Gojo the normal advantage that comes with domain expansion, a sure hit effect. An opposing domain's guaranteed-hit effect can circumvent the defensive advantage Infinity normally gives Gojo, rather than every technique used inside a domain automatically bypassing it. That becomes important when we start looking at how other characters get around his defense. Unlimited Void also shows how far Gojo has pushed Limitless compared to simply using Infinity as a wall. Neutral Infinity controls what can reach him, Blue and Red change how space behaves offensively. Purple combines those opposite effects. Unlimited Void manifests Limitless through Gojo's innate domain, with its own information-overload sure-hit rather than simply feeding someone the same thing Infinity, Blue, or Red normally manipulates.
And this is where the idea that Gojo is impossible to touch starts breaking down, because jujutsu has several mechanics that don’t care about approaching him normally.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: The cleanest way to get past Infinity is to shut the technique off.

The Inverted Spear of Heaven does exactly that. The weapon carries a cursed technique that forcibly cancels other cursed techniques when it makes contact with them. That’s why Toji could use it against Gojo during Hidden Inventory. He didn’t swing fast enough to somehow beat Infinity. The weapon itself neutralized Limitless, which let the blade reach Gojo normally.

Black Rope works in a similar way, although the exact mechanic is different. It interferes with and disturbs cursed techniques, which is why Miguel could use it against Gojo. The rope wasn’t stronger than Infinity. It was messing with the technique that created Infinity in the first place. Domain Amplification is another major counter. Instead of using a normal cursed technique to hit Gojo, the user coats themselves in a thin domain that can neutralize an opposing technique on contact. Jogo and Hanami use it specifically because their normal attacks can’t get through Infinity. While Domain Amplification is active, they can physically make contact with Gojo, although using it also limits their ability to use their own innate techniques at the same time. Domains create another route. A domain's guaranteed-hit effect can circumvent Infinity through domain mechanics rather than having to beat the defense like a normal punch or projectile. That’s why Gojo can still be threatened by an opposing domain's sure hit even though Infinity normally stops attacks before they reach him. He can answer with his own domain, use anti domain methods, or overpower the opponent, but Infinity by itself doesn’t make him immune to domain mechanics.

Mahoraga gets around Infinity in a completely different way. Its ability is adaptation. Once it is exposed to a phenomenon enough, the wheel turns and Mahoraga starts developing a way to deal with it. During the Sukuna fight, Mahoraga eventually adapts to Infinity and can physically reach Gojo even though the technique is still active.

That adaptation is what gives Sukuna the model he needs later. Sukuna doesn't just become fast enough to cross Infinity, and he doesn’t overpower it with a bigger slash. He changes what his slash targets. Instead of sending an attack through the space between himself and Gojo, he targets the space itself, cutting the area where Gojo exists.
That is why the attack can bypass Infinity. There is no normal projectile crossing the distance for Infinity to slow down. The space containing Gojo is being cut directly.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: So can Gojo breathe while Infinity is active? Yes. Infinity isn’t blocking every molecule around him. After Hidden Inventory, Gojo develops an automatic filtering system that judges what should be stopped based on things like cursed energy, speed, mass, and shape. Air, normal clothing, food, and other harmless things can still reach him.

He can also touch people whenever he wants. Infinity isn’t permanently forcing everything away from his body. Gojo can lower it, adjust it, or allow specific things through. That’s why he can grab people, carry Yuji, fight hand to hand, and interact normally with the world without constantly pushing everything away from himself.

Extreme speed by itself shouldn’t bypass Infinity either. Before Gojo automated the technique, catching him before he could react would obviously be more useful. Adult Gojo is different. Infinity is already running, so an attack being faster doesn’t suddenly remove the effect of the technique. You still need a reason the attack can get through.

Raw force has the same problem. If a punch is 100 times stronger, it still has to reach him first. Infinity doesn’t care that the attack would destroy a mountain after contact if the attack never finishes crossing the space in front of Gojo.

Poison is a little more interesting because Gojo specifically mentions wanting his automatic system to become better at identifying poisonous substances. That tells us his filtering isn’t just a magic setting that instantly understands every possible threat. He had to develop the system and improve what it could recognize.

The reason Gojo feels impossible to fight isn’t because Infinity has no counters. It’s because getting through Infinity is only the first problem. Even if you solve that, you still have to deal with the six eyes, blue, red, purple, reverse cursed technique, Unlimited Void, and Gojo himself.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The biggest thing Infinity changes isn’t just whether Gojo gets hit. It changes how he’s allowed to fight. Most fighters have to respect distance because getting too close means they’re putting themselves in range too. Gojo can stand right in front of someone and let them swing first because he knows the attack is going to slow down before it reaches him. That lets him fight way more aggressively than someone with normal durability ever could.

You can see that in the way he uses hand to hand combat. He'll get close, let someone commit to an attack, then punish the opening without needing to retreat or block in the normal way. If the other person can’t get through Infinity, every exchange is already unfair because they have to worry about Gojo’s punches while Gojo barely has to respect theirs.

Blue makes that even worse. Gojo doesn’t only use it as a big attack where everything gets pulled into one point. He can use it to control movement, drag opponents where he wants them, and move himself in ways that don’t look like normal running or jumping. So when someone thinks they've created space, Gojo can close that gap almost instantly by using Limitless to pull himself toward a point.

That means his physical speed can be hard to separate from his technique. Sometimes he really is just moving extremely fast. Other times he’s using Blue to change his position. Either way, the person fighting him has to react to someone who can ignore their normal defensive range and then suddenly appear much closer than expected.

Infinity also lets Gojo take risks that would be stupid for almost anyone else. He can stand still while an attack comes at his face, wait until the last second, and use that time to read what the opponent is doing. He can walk through attacks without breaking his rhythm. He can focus on offense because he doesn’t need to spend as much attention on dodging every punch, blade, or projectile.

That’s one reason getting through Infinity doesn’t automatically mean you’re beating Gojo. Toji had the Inverted Spear of Heaven, Jogo and Hanami had Domain Amplification, and Sukuna had multiple ways to pressure him, but they still had to actually fight Gojo after getting past the defense. Infinity is only one layer of what makes him dangerous.

The scary part is how all of these pieces work together. Gojo can use Infinity to control who gets close, Blue to change positioning, Red to blow someone away, and then pull them back in again if he wants. He can keep switching between those options while fighting normally, which makes it hard for an opponent to ever settle into one rhythm.

So Gojo doesn't fight like someone hiding behind a shield. He fights like someone who gets to ignore a rule everyone else has to follow. Other people have to respect the possibility of getting hit every time they move into range. Gojo usually doesn't.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: There are also a bunch of questions about Infinity where the answer gets way simpler once you stop thinking of it as a literal wall around Gojo.

The first one is whether Infinity creates an infinite amount of physical distance. The safest way to say it is that the technique makes the approach behave like the distance is being divided over and over, so the target keeps slowing down before it can reach him. The series uses mathematical ideas to explain it, but that doesn’t mean Gojo has literally stretched the room into an infinite number of kilometers.

That’s also why asking whether someone can just punch hard enough usually misses the point. A stronger punch still has to reach him. If Infinity is working normally, force only matters after contact, and the whole problem is that contact never happens.

Speed works the same way. Moving faster doesn’t automatically bypass Infinity because the technique isn’t just Gojo reacting and putting up a shield at the last second. Adult Gojo has it running automatically, so a faster attack still has to deal with the same effect unless there’s some other reason the technique can’t stop it.

People also ask whether Gojo has to see an attack coming. Once the automatic version is running, he’s not manually checking every threat with his eyes. His system is filtering what approaches based on things like cursed energy, mass, speed, and shape, so attacking from behind doesn’t automatically solve the problem.

Poison is more interesting because Gojo talks about improving the automatic system so it can recognize poisonous substances. That tells us the filter isn’t magically perfect at identifying every danger from day 1. He actually had to train it and make it better.

Teleportation is another question people argue about a lot, but the answer depends completely on how the teleportation works. If an attack still has to cross the space around Gojo, Infinity should still matter. If an ability literally places something directly inside the protected space without traveling through the distance first, that becomes a different interaction. Jujutsu Kaisen doesn’t give us one universal rule for every possible teleportation power, so saying all teleportation beats Infinity would just be guessing.

The same goes for attacks that appear directly on a target. You have to look at the actual technique. Sukuna’s final method works because the slash targets the space itself rather than traveling toward Gojo like a normal projectile. That's very different from simply saying, “the attack spawned on him.”

And finally, Infinity can be bypassed without being destroyed. That distinction is important. Toji neutralizes it with the Inverted Spear of Heaven. Domain Amplification lets users make contact by interfering with the technique. Domain sure hits work through domain mechanics. Mahoraga adapts to it. Sukuna uses that adaptation to learn a slash that cuts the space Gojo occupies. That’s what makes Gojo’s ability so interesting in the first place. Once you understand those rules, Infinity stops looking like some random invisible force field and starts making sense as one part of a much bigger system built around Limitless.

scripts.title: How Id Survive Thanos

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If | got dropped into the MCU a few weeks before Infinity War, I'd have 1 huge advantage over basically everyone else on Earth. | already know Thanos is coming.

I'd know where the Infinity Stones are, when the Black Order is about to attack, what happens on Titan, and that everything ends with Thanos snapping away half of all life. The problem is I'm still just a normal person. | can’t fight him, | can’t build some Stark level weapon, and nobody important has any reason to believe me.
So my first goal wouldn’t be stopping Thanos. It would be proving | know what's coming before the timeline gets too far ahead of me.

Because once the Snap happens, there’s no bunker or survival trick that can save me from a random 50 percent chance. If | want to survive Thanos, | probably have to stop him before he ever gets that far.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: I'd want to enter the MCU around 3 weeks before Infinity War. That's enough time to make a plan, but not enough time to completely rewrite the world before Thanos starts moving. I'd have whatever | normally carry, my own memories of the movies, and no special access to Stark, S.H.I.E.L.D., Wakanda, or any other place that could actually help me. The first few days would mostly be spent proving to myself that I’m in the right point of the timeline and figuring out which pieces of information | can use without getting myself arrested.

Trying to contact Tony Stark first would probably be a waste of time. Stark Industries would get thousands of messages from random people claiming aliens are coming, and I’d sound exactly like one of them. Nick Fury would be even harder to reach, and walking toward Avengers facilities without permission is a good way for an ordinary person to get stopped before anyone important ever hears the warning.

Doctor Strange gives me a much better option because | actually know where to find him. I’d go to the New York Sanctum before the invasion begins and tell him something specific enough that he can remember it even if he thinks I’m insane. | wouldn't start with a giant speech about the entire future. I’d tell him that within the next few weeks Bruce Banner, who has been missing from Earth for years, is going to crash through the Sanctum roof and warn him that Thanos is coming for the Infinity Stones. Right after that, Tony Stark will end up there, and 2 members of Thanos’ Black Order will attack New York because they want the Time Stone around Strange’s neck.

That gives Strange an actual prediction instead of asking him to trust my story. I’d also tell him names that shouldn't mean anything to him yet: Ebony Maw, Cull Obsidian and Thanos. If he asks how | know, I’d tell him the truth. | know events that haven’t happened yet, | can’t explain why, and I’m trying to prove it before the first attack.

Before leaving, I’d ask Strange to do one thing with the information. Don’t let the Time Stone leave Earth until we know whether my prediction is real. In the original timeline, Strange gets captured, Tony and Peter follow Maw’s ship into space, and that eventually brings the Time Stone directly into Thanos’ path on Titan. If Strange believes me early enough to avoid boarding that ship, the entire Titan situation might never happen.

| wouldn’t tell him every detail yet because the more | change, the less useful my memory becomes. My best advantage is knowing the order of events, and | don’t want to burn all of that before anyone even believes me.
After that, I'd leave New York.

That might sound weird after going through all the trouble of warning Strange, but | know exactly what happens once Maw arrives. Cars get thrown around, buildings get damaged, and civilians are caught right in the middle of the fight. I’m not helping anyone by standing nearby waiting to watch a movie scene happen in real life.

For the next few weeks, I’d stay somewhere outside the major locations | know are about to become important. I'd also create timestamped copies of everything | predicted and send the same warning to several places: Stark Industries, Avengers related contacts | can actually find publicly, local authorities near the Sanctum and maybe journalists. Most people would ignore it. That doesn’t matter yet. Once Bruce Banner literally falls through Strange’s roof and aliens attack the exact area | named, those messages become evidence that | knew before it happened.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The day Bruce returns to Earth is where I'd find out whether any of this worked.

If Strange remembers my warning, Bruce crashing through the Sanctum should immediately get his attention. Bruce saying Thanos’ name would confirm the most important part before Maw even reaches New York. Strange would now know | also predicted Tony's involvement, the Black Order attack and the reason they're coming.

That changes how much risk Strange should take. In the original timeline, Ebony Maw manages to restrain Strange and carries him onto the Q ship because the Time Stone is protected by a spell Maw can’t simply remove. Tony and Peter follow them into space, eventually kill Maw and continue toward Titan. If Strange already knows the kidnapping is coming, there’s no reason for him to stand around waiting for Maw to get close enough to repeat it.

He and Wong could prepare the Sanctum instead. Strange can open portals, move people instantly and fight from positions Maw isn’t expecting. He also knows Maw wants him alive because killing him doesn’t automatically give Maw the Stone. That gives Strange much more room to avoid capture than he had when the attack happened without warning.

I'd want to be nowhere near any of this. The second | know the New York attack has started, I'm staying indoors somewhere far away and following whatever information becomes public. My job isn’t to help Strange fight Cull Obsidian. I'd die immediately.

If Strange avoids being captured, my future knowledge is already breaking apart. Tony may never leave Earth. Peter may never end up on Maw’s ship. Thanos may still go to Titan later, but there’s no guarantee the same people are waiting for him there. From this point forward, | have to stop treating Infinity War like a schedule and start treating it like a list of things Thanos still needs,

He wants all 6 Stones. The Power Stone is probably already lost before | can do anything useful. Thanos attacks Xandar before the film begins, and as an ordinary person I have no realistic way to reach another planet and warn them. The Space Stone is aboard the Asgardian refugee ship with Loki, which is even farther outside anything | can affect. The Reality Stone is with the Collector on Knowhere. The Soul Stone is on Vormir. Those are basically unreachable for me.

Earth still has 2 Stones | can influence indirectly: Strange’s Time Stone and Vision’s Mind Stone. That makes Vision the next warning. I’d contact Strange again after the New York attack because now he has no reason to ignore me. I'd tell him that Vision and Wanda are in Scotland, Corvus Glaive and Proxima Midnight are going to ambush them, and the attackers are after the Mind Stone. Steve Rogers, Natasha and Sam eventually rescue them in the original timeline, but waiting for the ambush is pointless if we already know where it happens.

Strange has something | don't: access to Tony. If Tony stayed on Earth because Strange wasn’t kidnapped, Strange can put the warning directly in front of him. Tony already knows aliens just attacked New York for an Infinity Stone, Bruce is telling everyone what Thanos did to Asgard’s survivors and my earlier prediction just came true almost word for word. At that point, | don’t need Tony to believe I’m psychic. He only needs to believe | have useful intelligence.

The smartest move would be getting Vision out of Scotland before the Black Order reaches him. | wouldn't suggest bringing him to New York either. That just puts both Earth Stones in the same city. Wakanda becomes the obvious destination much earlier because Shuri is one of the few people who might actually be able to remove the Mind Stone without killing Vision. In the original movie they don’t start that process until Thanos’ army is already coming. I'd want them working on it as soon as possible.

That would be my first serious attempt at stopping the Snap. If Vision can survive without the Mind Stone and the Stone can be destroyed before Thanos reaches Earth, he can never complete the Gauntlet.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Getting Vision to Wakanda early creates a completely different problem because now I have to decide how much of the future to reveal.

| know Wanda can destroy the Mind Stone. | also know Thanos eventually gets the Time Stone and uses it to reverse that destruction, brings Vision back for a few seconds and takes the Stone anyway. So telling everyone to let Wanda destroy it immediately doesn’t solve the problem if Strange still has the Time Stone nearby.
That means the 2 Stones need completely separate plans.

Vision goes to Wakanda, where Shuri starts removing the Mind Stone as early as possible. Strange keeps the Time Stone somewhere else, and I'd strongly argue against bringing it anywhere near Wakanda. Putting both remaining Stones in one location would make Thanos’ job easier.

Tony would probably want to know what happens if they follow my plan, and this is where I'd finally tell him more. I’d explain that in the timeline | remember, he goes to Titan, fights Thanos alongside Strange, Peter and the Guardians, and they almost get the Gauntlet off. Then Peter Quill learns Gamora is dead, loses control and starts hitting Thanos while Mantis is holding him, which gives Thanos enough time to escape.
That detail would sound ridiculous before it happens, but Tony now has a reason to take it seriously because | already predicted Bruce, Maw and Cull.
I'd also tell him the part that matters most: Doctor Strange eventually gives Thanos the Time Stone voluntarily because he has seen millions of possible futures and believes only 1 leads to victory.

That information could make Strange furious because I’m telling him about a choice he hasn't made yet, but it also gives him a warning about his own future logic. If he later uses the Time Stone to search possible outcomes, he now knows that the path he remembers from my timeline ends with the Snap happening first.

| wouldn't ask him to use the Stone to look through millions of futures immediately either. The original Titan situation forces Strange into that because Thanos is almost there. On Earth, with more preparation time, everyone has other options.
The Mind Stone is the easier target.

Shuri believed she could separate Vision from it without destroying the parts of him that make him himself. The problem in Infinity War was time. Corvus interrupts the procedure while Thanos’ army is already attacking Wakanda. Starting hours or even days earlier changes that completely.
Once the Stone is removed, Wanda destroys it.
| wouldn't keep it in some vault because every vault on Earth is meaningless when Thanos can teleport through the Space Stone. Destroying it is much safer than hiding it.

If that works, Thanos now has a Gauntlet that can never be completed unless he somehow restores the Mind Stone. The Time Stone could potentially do that, which is why I'd still want the destruction separated from Strange and concealed as much as possible. We don't actually know the exact limits on reversing something like the Mind Stone from somewhere else, so | couldn't assume distance alone makes restoration impossible. Strange could portal Wanda and the Stone to an isolated location, let her destroy it and then leave. At minimum, Thanos would have to figure out what happened and how to undo it instead of finding both remaining Stones together.
Now Thanos has another problem. He may not even know where the Mind Stone was destroyed.

My own survival situation improves a lot here because I’m nowhere near Wakanda. | would stay far away from every Infinity Stone and every Avenger Thanos might target. Knowing important information makes me useful to Tony and Strange, but becoming physically useful to them would be terrible for my life expectancy.
I'd communicate remotely whenever possible.

That might also save me from the Black Order because there’s no reason they should know | exist. | haven’t fought them, I don’t have a Stone and I'm not standing beside an Avenger when they arrive. From Thanos’ perspective, I’m just another human somewhere on a planet he hasn't reached yet.
The safer | can stay while my information moves without me, the better.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Even if the Mind Stone is destroyed early, | wouldn’t assume we've won.

This is Thanos. Once he realizes Earth knows what he’s doing, he’s not going to politely follow the same route | remember. The original timeline stops being reliable the second Corvus and Proxima arrive in Scotland and find Vision missing, or Maw fails to leave Earth with Strange. The Black Order would report that something is wrong.
Thanos would know Earth somehow anticipated 2 separate attacks which would probably speed everything up.

Instead of waiting until the end of the movie to come to Earth, he might arrive much earlier once he has the Stones he can collect elsewhere. If he already has Power, Space, Reality and Soul, Earth still holds the only 2 he needs. Even if the Mind Stone is destroyed, he could come looking for Strange and then figure out what happened to Vision afterward.
That makes the Time Stone the biggest danger left.

At this point I'd push Strange to remove himself from Earth entirely if he can do it safely. Not Titan, because | know Thanos expects to operate there and can reach it. Strange has portals and access to dimensions and locations | can’t personally understand, so the exact hiding place should be his decision. The important thing is that the Stone shouldn't stay next to a population Thanos can threaten. Whatever location or realm Strange judges hardest for Thanos to locate or reach could buy us time, but | wouldn't assume any hiding place is completely safe from him once he has multiple Stones.

Thanos can be emotionally manipulated. On Titan, Mantis gets inside his head and confirms how deeply Gamora’s death affects him. Thor later catches him off guard because Thanos doesn’t expect Stormbreaker to push through the completed Gauntlet attack. Wanda is also physically capable of holding him back with 5 Stones while destroying the Mind Stone at the same time.
Those aren't things | can reproduce, but the Avengers can use them when planning.

Thor becomes especially important because | know he’s currently making Stormbreaker on Nidavellir. Nobody on Earth knows when he'll arrive, but | know he eventually comes through the Bifrost during the Wakanda battle. If | can convince Tony that Thor is still alive and building a weapon specifically to kill Thanos, then the goal becomes buying time for Thor rather than desperately trying to beat Thanos with whatever happens to be available.

I'd also tell them the most famous mistake in the entire fight. If Thor gets a clean shot, go for the head. That sounds stupidly simple, but it matters because | know Stormbreaker can bury itself in Thanos’ chest even when he already has all 6 Stones. Thor loses because the wound isn’t immediately fatal and Thanos still has enough time to Snap.
Now imagine Thor arrives against a Thanos who doesn’t have all 6 Stones and already knows exactly where he needs to aim.

That’s probably humanity’s best physical chance. My job during all of this would be getting farther away. I'd want a stocked location outside a major city with water, food, medicine, backup power and enough cash to function if normal payment systems fail. | wouldn’t need some underground doomsday bunker. The threat to me isn’t radiation or an army searching every house. It’s infrastructure falling apart if the Avengers fail.
By then I'd also have to accept something uncomfortable. | can improve their odds, but | can’t guarantee they win. So | still need a plan for the Snap.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: If Thanos completes the Gauntlet and his goal remains eliminating half of all life randomly, I’m either part of the half that stays or the half that disappears. Being underground doesn’t matter. Being on another continent doesn’t matter. Holding my breath, wearing armor or standing next to an Avenger doesn’t matter.
That means every decision before the Snap is about reducing the chance that the Snap happens at all.

But if it still happens, the smartest thing | can do is prepare for the world immediately afterward. I'd keep enough water and shelf stable food for several weeks, basic medication, first aid supplies, flashlights, batteries, a radio and some backup electricity if | can afford it. I’d also avoid living directly beside highways, airports, chemical plants or other places where half the people disappearing without warning could create secondary disasters.

The first few minutes after the Snap could be incredibly dangerous even for survivors. Half of drivers could vanish from moving vehicles. Pilots, surgeons, power plant workers and emergency dispatchers could disappear in the middle of whatever they're doing. The movies mostly show the emotional side of the Snap, but an ordinary person would also have to survive the accidents caused by millions of people suddenly not being there.
So if | know Thanos is close to getting the final Stone, I’m not driving anywhere.
