That could actually help Anakin become a better technical fighter because he spends years learning to control his body instead of just throwing his power around.

The frustration would still build. Anakin would see other Padawans getting more freedom while the Council keeps a closer eye on him. They would have a reason for that because Anakin can already hurt someone very badly if he loses his temper, and nobody knows how much stronger he will become. Anakin would still see it as another example of the Council treating him differently.

Obi-Wan would probably agree with him sometimes. He knows Anakin really can do things most Jedi cannot, and there would be moments where the Council is being overly cautious because they don’t understand what he is. Obi-Wan would also see the other side every time Anakin gets angry and relies on strength instead of patience.

Palpatine would notice all of this. He already takes an interest in Anakin when he’s young, and now there is another reason to stay close to him. He could listen whenever Anakin complains about being held back and slowly encourage the idea that the Jedi are uncomfortable with how powerful he is becoming.

He wouldn’t even need to lie very much. The Jedi really would be worried about Anakin. There would probably be meetings about how quickly he is getting stronger, how dangerous he could become, and what they should do if his emotions ever get out of control. Palpatine would take those real concerns and make them sound much more personal than they are.

At the same time, Anakin would still be learning the Force normally. His Viltrumite abilities wouldn't replace telekinesis, precognition, or lightsaber training. They would work alongside them. If Anakin senses an attack a moment early through the Force, his speed lets him react even faster. If he lands a hit after reading an opening, there is much more strength behind it than another Jedi would expect.

By the time Anakin reaches adulthood, Obi-Wan would know that physical training is no longer the difficult part. The real challenge would be making sure Anakin understands that being stronger than someone does not automatically make him right.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: By Attack of the Clones, Anakin would already know how to fly and would be much stronger than he was as a child. That would change the chase after Zam Wesell in Coruscant almost immediately. Once Anakin gets a clear look at where she is going, he could leave the speeder and follow her through the air instead of depending entirely on traffic and vehicles.

Obi-Wan would probably still hate the way Anakin handles it because he tends to rush into things before thinking them through. The difference is that falling from a speeder is no longer one of the biggest risks. Anakin can correct himself in the air and keep moving.

His assignment protecting Padmé would still bring them closer together. She remembers him as the kid from Tatooine, and now he has grown into someone who can do things even most Jedi can’t. Anakin would still be awkward around her, still have the same feelings, and still struggle to separate those feelings from his duty.

His powers could make the protective side of him worse. Anakin is already someone who believes he should be able to save the people he cares about, and being this hard to kill would give him even more confidence in that idea. He has spent years surviving things that would kill other people, so accepting that there are situations he cannot control would become harder.

That would matter when Shmi dies. Anakin would still feel her through the Force, go back to Tatooine, and find her in the Tusken camp. Once she dies in his arms, the massacre would happen much faster. He could cross the camp in seconds, tear through tents and structures, and kill people without needing to rely on his lightsaber every time.

When the anger finally drops, Anakin would have to look at what he did with a body that can cause far more damage than the Jedi ever expected. Obi-Wan’s lessons about holding back would suddenly have a much darker meaning, but Anakin would still hide it because admitting what happened would mean admitting the Council had good reason to worry about him. Geonosis would show the rest of the Jedi what Anakin is capable of in a real battle. He could move around the arena without needing platforms, fly toward Jedi who are being surrounded, and break battle droids apart physically when using a lightsaber would take longer. He would still need help because there are too many droids for one person to handle, but he could survive in parts of the battle where most Jedi would be overwhelmed very quickly.

The Separatists would also have weapons strong enough to hurt him. Heavy blasters, explosions, and concentrated fire would still do damage, especially because Anakin is still a young and relatively inexperienced Viltrumite whose body has not been tested anywhere near its eventual limits. His healing would help him recover, but he couldn’t just stand in front of an army and ignore everything being fired at him.

Dooku would be the first person who really tests him. Anakin could reach him faster and hit much harder, but Dooku has decades of experience and far better control of the Force. He wouldn't try to meet Anakin’s strength directly if he can avoid it. He could throw him off balance with telekinesis, keep objects between them, and wait for Anakin to get impatient enough to leave an opening.

A lightsaber would still be one of Dooku's best ways to hurt Anakin if he lands properly, but there is no canon answer for exactly how easily a lightsaber would cut through Viltrumite tissue. Anakin could still leave Geonosis badly injured if Dooku finds an opening, but the fight would probably be longer because getting that opening would be much harder against someone with Viltrumite reactions and durability.

Anakin would leave knowing that being stronger and faster than someone still doesn’t guarantee he can beat them. Against someone as skilled as Dooku, he would still need the discipline Obi-Wan has been trying to teach him for years.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Once the Clone Wars begin, Anakin would become useful to the Republic very quickly. He already takes dangerous missions in canon, and now there are a lot more situations where he can survive doing something nobody else should attempt.

If a Separatist position is protected by heavy guns, Anakin could fly around the main line and attack it from another direction. If clones are trapped somewhere a gunship can’t safely reach, he could go in alone and help get them out. He could move between positions without waiting for transport and stay in a fight much longer than most Jedi once people start getting tired or injured.

That would make the 501st trust him even more. The clones would constantly see Anakin put himself in danger to help them, and his powers mean he can sometimes take a hit that would kill one of them and still keep fighting. Rex would probably become one of the people who understands Anakin’s limits best because he would see firsthand what kinds of weapons can actually slow him down.

The Republic would start expecting more from him because of those abilities. Missions that would normally need several Jedi might be given to Anakin because commanders know he can survive the worst part himself. Every time he succeeds, they would be more willing to do it again.

The Council would have another reason to worry as the war continues. Anakin is still getting stronger because years of training, combat, and constant physical exertion keep developing a body whose limits nobody understands. He is already one of the strongest Jedi of his generation, and his Viltrumite physiology is being pushed harder than ever while his connection to the Force is growing too.
Some Jedi would start wondering what they could do if Anakin ever turned against them. They have seen what he can do to armies and how hard he is to hurt, so the question would be hard to avoid.

Palpatine would know those conversations are happening and would slowly make sure Anakin feels the effects of them. Maybe the Council adds supervision to certain missions or asks Obi-Wan for more reports about Anakin’s behavior. Anakin wouldn’t know exactly what was said behind closed doors, but he would notice when people start treating him differently.

Palpatine could use that frustration without needing to give Anakin some perfect speech every time. He could simply agree when Anakin says the Council doesn’t trust him and let Anakin build the rest of the argument himself.

Palpatine would also be learning as much as he can about Anakin's unusual biology during the war. Every time Anakin gets injured, there would be medical records showing how much damage he took and how quickly he recovered. Palpatine could quietly collect those reports to learn which ordinary attacks still hurt him, but the records alone would not reveal every hidden weakness in Viltrumite biology.

Anakin would mostly see the war as proof that he is ready for more than the Council gives him. He is winning battles, saving clones, and becoming one of the Republic’s biggest heroes, while Palpatine keeps treating him like someone whose abilities should be respected. That makes it much easier for Anakin to listen to him later when the relationship with the Jedi starts falling apart.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: As the war gets closer to its end, Anakin’s relationship with Padmé would become even more important to him because she is one of the few parts of his life that still feels separate from the Jedi and the war. He would already be used to surviving things that should kill normal people, so being around someone who can get hurt so easily would make him even more protective than he is in canon. Every battle reminds him that his own body can recover from almost anything, while Padmé does not have that same protection.

There would also be a longer-term problem Anakin does not understand yet. If his Viltrumite biology gives him the lifespan Viltrumites are capable of, he could remain physically young for far longer than Padmé. But because the Jedi still cannot identify what he is, Anakin has no way to know that yet, so it would not be part of his fear before the visions begin.

When those visions finally start during Revenge of the Sith, they would hit him just as hard as they do in canon. Anakin would see Padmé dying during childbirth and immediately assume the future is something he has to stop. The difference is that he has spent years proving to himself that physical limits can usually be beaten if he pushes hard enough. He survives explosions, crashes, blaster fire, and injuries that would end another Jedi’s career, so accepting that Padmé can die from something he cannot punch, outrun, or heal would be extremely difficult for him. He would start looking for answers in the Jedi Archives like he does with other problems, but the Order would not have anything that gives him what he wants. Jedi teachings about accepting death would frustrate him even more because Anakin would hear them as another version of the same advice he has been getting his entire life. Slow down, accept the limit, trust the process, and stop trying to control everything. He has spent years hearing that from people who could not do half of what he can do, and now they are telling him to accept losing Padmé too. Palpatine would know exactly how to use that. He would already understand Anakin’s fear of losing her, and he only needs to convince Anakin that the dark side might offer a way around the death he has seen. If Anakin believes Padmé can be saved, that possibility alone is enough to keep him listening.

That would make the promise of Sith knowledge even more attractive. Palpatine could tell him that the dark side has been used to extend life, preserve bodies, and push past limits the Jedi simply accept. He would not need to prove every claim immediately because Anakin is already desperate enough to listen once the possibility exists.

At the same time, Padmé would notice Anakin getting worse. He would ask more questions about medical care, spend more time checking on her, and become tense whenever she talks about the future. She would probably understand that something is wrong before he tells her about the visions because Anakin has never been good at hiding fear from her for long.

That tension would build right as Palpatine starts preparing his final move. Anakin would be more powerful than ever and still feel helpless around the one thing he cares about most, which gives Palpatine exactly the opening he needs.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: When Palpatine finally reveals that he is Darth Sidious, the conversation would still shock Anakin, but the power balance between them would feel very different. Anakin has spent years fighting armies and powerful Force users, and by this point his Viltrumite body has grown strong enough that Palpatine cannot assume a direct fight will be easy.

Anakin could still draw his lightsaber and threaten him the way he does in canon, but Sidious would know that one mistake could end the whole plan. If Anakin gets through his Force defenses and closes the distance, Palpatine would be dealing with someone strong enough to break bones, throw him across the room, and keep attacking even after taking serious damage. That means Palpatine would lean even harder on Padmé instead of trying to dominate the moment physically. He would keep the conversation focused on what the dark side might offer, because he knows Anakin has already reached the point where he is willing to listen if there is a real chance to save her.

Mace would still tell him to stay behind because his connection to Palpatine and fear for Padmé make him unreliable. Anakin would take that order badly because it fits everything he already believes about the Council. They keep him away from one of the most important moments in the war even though he may be one of the few people physically capable of stopping Sidious if the fight goes wrong.

The fight between Mace and Palpatine could still end with Mace getting the upper hand because Windu’s skill and Vaapad make him one of the best people in the Order to face Sidious. When Anakin arrives, though, the situation becomes even more tense because Palpatine knows he cannot afford to let Anakin think clearly for very long.

He would immediately bring the conversation back to Padmé. If Mace kills him, Anakin loses the only person who claims to know how to save her. That threat would still work because Anakin’s fear has not changed just because his body is stronger.

If Anakin chooses to interfere, the actual moment would be much more violent. He could move fast enough to stop Mace without needing the exact same lightsaber strike from canon. He might grab his arm, knock him away from Palpatine, or hit him hard enough to break the balance of the fight. Mace would still be able to use the Force against him, but dealing with Anakin and Sidious at the same time would be almost impossible.

Once Mace is out of the fight, Anakin would immediately understand what he has done. The problem is that he has already crossed the line in front of the Sith Lord he just helped save, and Palpatine would use that panic before Anakin has time to step away.

Anakin could fly between levels, break through doors without waiting for explosives, and reach sections of the Temple before Jedi have time to organize a defense. If a group tries to hold a corridor, he could attack from above or come through a wall instead of walking straight into the choke point.

That would make evacuation much harder. In canon, some Jedi have time to understand that the clones have turned and try to escape. Here, Anakin can cover distance so quickly that routes which should be safe could suddenly have him waiting at the other end.

Some of the strongest Jedi in the Temple could create real problems for him. If several Masters coordinate instead of fighting one at a time, they could use the Force to restrict his movement and force him into a more controlled lightsaber fight. Anakin would still have his own Force abilities, though, and his physical speed means even a small opening could let him break out before the group resets.

The younglings and civilians inside the Temple would have even less chance of escaping once Anakin reaches them. He would not need clones beside him to overpower anyone protecting those rooms, which makes that part of his fall even darker because his Viltrumite abilities remove many of the physical limits that might slow him down.

Obi-Wan and Yoda would see the results later and understand how serious the situation has become. They already know Anakin is powerful, but seeing what he did inside the Temple would tell them that stopping him may require more than one Jedi.

Palpatine would also start thinking ahead almost immediately. Anakin has done what he needed, but now Sidious has to consider what happens after the Jedi are gone. Canon Vader becomes physically damaged on Mustafar, which makes him easier for Palpatine to control later. This version is still healthy, still capable of becoming more dangerous through years of training and combat, and has already shown that he can tear through trained Jedi while combining the Force with Viltrumite abilities.

Palpatine would keep praising him publicly while quietly preparing contingencies just in case. Over the years, Sidious could turn that research into deliberate experimentation, exposing biological samples and eventually Anakin himself to controlled stresses and frequency sweeps under the cover of Imperial medical testing. Researchers could start broad, notice that certain high frequencies repeatedly cause unusual balance and disorientation responses, then narrow the range across later tests until they isolate the frequency that disrupts Anakin most severely. That gives Palpatine a demonstrated weakness he can spend years refining into a sonic failsafe.
Anakin would not be thinking that far ahead yet. He would still believe everything he is doing is leading toward saving Padmé, and that belief would carry him to Mustafar.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Obi-Wan would still follow Padmé to Mustafar after learning what Anakin has done. Padmé would still confront him about the Temple, the Jedi, and Palpatine, and Anakin would still be far enough into his fall that he tries to explain everything as something he did for their future.

The argument would probably become worse once Padmé realizes how far he has gone. Anakin might tell her that Palpatine can be removed later and that he has enough power to protect both of them without the Jedi or the Republic. From his point of view, that sounds possible because he genuinely may be strong enough to challenge Sidious someday.

Padmé would hear someone talking about controlling the galaxy because he thinks he knows what is best. That would scare her because it is exactly the kind of thinking she spent her political life fighting against.

When Obi-Wan appears, Anakin would still assume Padmé brought him there to betray him. The anger could lead to the same Force choke, but Obi-Wan would know how dangerous this version of Anakin is and would have even less reason to wait before intervening. He could force Anakin to release Padmé sooner so the choke does not last as long before the duel begins.
The duel that follows would look very different.

Obi-Wan would still have the advantage in discipline and knowledge of Anakin’s habits. He trained him for years and knows exactly how he fights when he gets angry. The problem is that most of the physical dangers on Mustafar no longer mean as much to Anakin. Falling from a platform is not a serious threat when he can fly, and lava is much easier to avoid when he is not limited to jumping from one piece of ground to another.

Obi-Wan would have to fight around Anakin’s speed instead of trying to match it. He could use the Force to redirect him, throw machinery into his path, and force him into tight spaces where flying at full speed becomes harder. Anakin would still be better in raw power, but every time he gets impatient, Obi-Wan could use his momentum against him.

The fight would probably last longer because Obi-Wan cannot rely on the same final mistake. There is no reason for Anakin to make a desperate jump over him when he can simply fly around the position or attack from another angle.

Obi-Wan could still threaten him with a lightsaber if Anakin gets careless, although there is no canon answer for exactly how easily the blade would cut through Viltrumite tissue at this stage. Even if Obi-Wan manages to badly wound him, Anakin’s healing gives him a better chance of staying conscious and continuing the fight.

The most realistic outcome is that Obi-Wan realizes he cannot finish the duel the same way and starts looking for a way to escape instead. He could damage the facility, separate them with collapsing machinery, or use the environment to slow Anakin long enough to reach Padmé’s ship.

That earlier interruption gives Padmé a specific divergence from canon. The choke is cut shorter before Anakin turns fully toward Obi-Wan, and once Obi-Wan realizes he cannot finish the duel the same way, he prioritizes escaping with her instead of remaining for the lava-bank ending. Padmé would still be in critical condition through childbirth, but the physical and emotional circumstances are no longer identical to canon: the choke ends sooner, Obi-Wan gets her away earlier, and she reaches the medical team after a different Mustafar sequence. In this timeline she stabilizes after childbirth and survives, even though the exact biological reason remains as unclear as the cause of her canon decline. She leaves with Luke and Leia and wants nothing to do with what Anakin has become.

Anakin would survive Mustafar without being burned into the body that becomes the Vader everyone knows. He might leave with injuries and scars, but he would still have his own face, lungs, limbs, and Viltrumite body.
That changes everything after Revenge of the Sith.

Palpatine would never get a crippled apprentice who depends on a suit to stay alive. He would get a healthy Anakin who is already one of the strongest Force users alive and may have far more time than a human in which to train, fight, and become even more dangerous.

The suit, the breathing, and the mechanical version of Darth Vader could simply never exist. The Empire would instead have a Vader who can fly through battlefields, survive weapons that would kill most Jedi, and has far more time and opportunity to develop his abilities while Palpatine gets older.
For the first time, Sidious would have to seriously think about whether turning Anakin was eventually going to create someone he could no longer control.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Once Anakin leaves Mustafar alive and mostly intact, Palpatine would understand that the relationship between them has changed. He still has the political power, the Empire, and far more experience with the dark side, but Anakin no longer depends on him physically. Sidious would not treat the next two decades like ordinary passive servitude. He would keep Anakin close enough to use while quietly testing contingencies, engineering dangerous assignments, and looking for weaknesses that could stop his apprentice if Anakin ever makes a move against him.

Anakin would recognize some of that pressure too. He still serves the Empire at first because he has already destroyed his old life and Palpatine can keep feeding his anger, but the relationship becomes a long cold war between master and apprentice. Sidious needs Anakin’s power while fearing what he may become, and Anakin increasingly understands that his master is preparing for the day one of them betrays the other.

Padmé surviving changes Luke and Leia’s side of the timeline just as much. Obi-Wan would have no reason to send Luke to the Lars family while Padmé is alive and capable of choosing what happens to her children. She would keep the twins hidden from Anakin and Palpatine through a tightly compartmentalized network of Obi-Wan, Bail Organa, and a small number of trusted allies, moving them between safe locations and keeping their identities and whereabouts separate even from most of the resistance rather than recreating Luke’s exact childhood on Tatooine.

Padmé would also become an important part of the resistance to the Empire. She already opposed Palpatine politically, and surviving Anakin’s fall gives her an even more personal reason to work with Bail Organa and other early rebels. Luke and Leia could therefore grow up around that resistance instead of discovering the conflict as adults. Obi-Wan could teach them about the Jedi and the Force while Padmé makes sure they understand what happened to their father.

A healthy Vader would make the rebellion more dangerous, but it would not automatically erase it. The galaxy is enormous, insurgent cells can hide across thousands of systems, and Palpatine still has to use Anakin strategically rather than station him everywhere at once. The rebellion that eventually forms would be different and probably more cautious, built around avoiding direct confrontations with Vader until it has weapons, intelligence, or Force users capable of surviving him.

That means Luke would not reach Anakin as the same inexperienced farm boy from canon, and the confrontation would not need to happen through the exact Death Star II chain of events. By the time Luke is old enough to face him, he could already be a trained member of the rebellion who knows Anakin is his father. Once Luke deliberately seeks him out, Palpatine would have the same basic opportunity he wanted in canon: bring the powerful son and increasingly dangerous father into the same confrontation and try to turn their conflict to his advantage.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Luke would still have the best chance of reaching him because he would be able to see the part of Anakin that never fully disappeared. The difference is that this Luke has grown up knowing who his father is, and this Vader would not look like a machine. When Luke finally gets in front of him, he would be standing in front of the same face Padmé knew, older and harder but still clearly Anakin. That would make their connection much more direct because there is less physical distance between the person Anakin was and the person he became.

Anakin would still resist at first. He has spent years as one of the most powerful people in the galaxy, and admitting that Luke is right would mean admitting that almost everything he did after Revenge of the Sith was built around fear and anger. Luke’s existence also forces him to confront the family he lost without being able to tell himself they simply died with Padmé.

If Palpatine succeeds in bringing that confrontation under his control, the final fight could become much shorter than the canon throne-room battle. Palpatine could attack with Force lightning, telekinesis, and everything else he has, and there is no canon answer for exactly how Viltrumite biology would handle Sith lightning. Anakin’s enhanced physiology could plausibly let him remain functional through more electrical damage than a normal human, but the lightning would still be a serious threat rather than something his durability automatically counters. He could also use Viltrumite speed to close the distance far faster than Palpatine expects, and once he gets through the Emperor’s Force defenses, the physical fight would be completely one sided.

Palpatine’s best chance would be using the weakness he spent years experimentally isolating and refining for exactly this possibility. A powerful sonic weapon tuned to the narrow frequency his repeated tests identified could disorient Anakin badly enough to create an opening, especially if Palpatine combines it with the Force. That would keep the fight from becoming a simple punch and make the weapon the payoff to decades of Sidious preparing for Anakin’s eventual betrayal rather than a countermeasure he suddenly produces at the end.

Luke could matter here because he would know Anakin is fighting through something that directly attacks his biology. If Luke destroys the sonic system or distracts Palpatine long enough for Anakin to recover, the balance shifts back immediately. Anakin would then have a clear path to Sidious before the Emperor can reset the fight.

Anakin would almost certainly win once he gets that opening. He could kill Palpatine himself or refuse to become another Sith master and let Luke help end the fight. Either way, the Empire loses the one person holding the entire system together.

What happens after that would depend on whether Anakin wants power or redemption. If he decides the galaxy still needs someone strong enough to control it, he could become an even more dangerous ruler than Palpatine because almost nobody can physically challenge him. He has the Force, Viltrumite abilities, and decades of military experience, which would make taking the throne easy.

If Luke gets through to him first, Anakin could finally understand why giving up control matters more than winning another fight. He could help dismantle the Empire, free occupied worlds, and spend the rest of his life trying to repair some of the damage he caused. That would not erase the Temple, the Jedi he killed, or the years he spent serving the Empire, but it would at least give him a path back that does not depend on dying five minutes later.

His lifespan would make that redemption much heavier too. Anakin could live for centuries, which means he would have to live with what he did for far longer than a normal human ever would. He could watch the Republic rebuild, see Luke and Leia grow old, and spend generations helping fix a galaxy he helped break.

That may be the biggest change of all. Canon Vader gets one final choice and dies shortly after making it. Viltrumite Anakin could make that choice and then spend hundreds of years proving whether he really meant it.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: If Anakin Skywalker was a Viltrumite, his body would make the problems already inside Anakin much harder to control.

He would grow up knowing he’s stronger than almost everyone around him, survive things other Jedi cannot, and keep hearing the Council tell him to hold back. Palpatine would have more reason to target that frustration, and once Anakin falls, the Jedi would be dealing with someone who has Viltrumite strength and speed on top of one of the strongest connections to the force in the galaxy.

Mustafar would probably never create the Vader everyone knows. Obi-Wan could still challenge him through skill and discipline, but cutting him apart and leaving him burned on the lava bank becomes much less likely once Anakin can fly, heal, and take far more damage.

That means Palpatine ends up with a much bigger problem than canon. Instead of a broken apprentice he can control for decades, he gets a healthy Anakin with centuries to keep developing through training and combat, and eventually very little reason to stay beneath him.

So Anakin being a Viltrumite would probably make his fall more dangerous, but it would also make Palpatine’s victory much less stable. If Luke still manages to bring his father back, Anakin could finally destroy Sidious and then live long enough to actually deal with everything he did.

scripts.title: What If Ben 10 Joined The Avengers

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Ben Ten showing up around the time the Avengers are forming would change a lot almost immediately. By this point, Ben already has years of experience dealing with aliens and the Omnitrix gives him a ridiculous amount of options in a fight, but S.H.I.E.L.D. has no reason to trust him yet.

He’d be dropped into the middle of a situation where Loki has just arrived, Fury is pulling together people who barely work as a team, and nobody on Earth really understands what kind of invasion is coming. Ben would probably recognize some of the signs faster than most of them, but that doesn’t mean Tony, Steve, or Fury are going to let a 16 yr old with alien technology walk straight into the Avengers.
So Ben would have to earn his way into the team during the exact crisis that created it.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Everything leading into The Avengers would still be moving the same way at first. Loki would arrive through the Tesseract, take control of Clint Barton and Erik Selvig, and escape with the cube before S.H.I.E.L.D. can contain him. Fury would start pulling the Avengers Initiative together, bringing Steve back into active duty, sending Natasha after Bruce Banner, and pulling Tony into the investigation.

Ben would arrive during that same window. A dimensional disturbance tied to the Tesseract could throw him into the MCU while he’s already transformed, which would immediately put S.H.I.E.L.D. on alert. Once Ben changes back into a 16-year-old from late in Omniverse, after gaining direct control over Alien X, with the Omnitrix on his wrist, Fury would want him contained until they understand what he is and where he came from. Ben would cooperate enough to avoid a fight, but he wouldn’t hand the Omnitrix over or let anyone try removing it.

S.H.1.E.L.D. wouldn’t have anything in its files that matches the watch. Ben could explain that the Omnitrix stores alien DNA and lets him transform into different species, and Tony would immediately want to study it. Ben would answer enough to show that he understands what he’s carrying while making it clear that nobody gets to take the watch apart. Steve would be less interested in the technology and more concerned about Ben being 16, which Ben would find frustrating after years of fighting alien threats on his own.

Ben would start proving himself while S.H.1.E.L.D. reviews Loki’s attack. He might not know the Chitauri by name, but Loki stealing the Tesseract while keeping Selvig alive would look familiar to someone who has dealt with alien invasions before. Selvig is useful because he understands the cube, which tells Ben that Loki is probably using it to open something rather than simply as a power source.

Tony would reach a similar conclusion from the energy data, and Fury would start taking Ben more seriously. Ben still wouldn’t be treated like an Avenger, especially because Fury has no idea what happens if Loki gets access to the Omnitrix or controls Ben the way he controlled Clint.

Once Loki is captured, Ben would meet the rest of the team. Thor would be the easiest for him to understand because Ben is already used to people from other worlds, while Loki would immediately take an interest in the Omnitrix. Ben would keep his answers short and quickly recognize that Loki is trying to keep everyone arguing while something else is being prepared outside the Helicarrier.

When the Helicarrier comes under attack, Ben would finally get his chance to show what he can do. Big Chill could move through damaged sections and reach trapped agents, Jetray could cross the carrier quickly when different areas are hit, and Humungousaur could move debris or hold damaged structures long enough for people to escape.

By the time Loki gets away, Steve and Tony have both seen that Ben can handle himself in a real crisis. Fury still wouldn't call him an Avenger, but he wouldn't leave him behind when the team goes after Loki again.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Once Tony figures out Loki is using Stark Tower to power the portal, Ben would go with the others because there’s no reason to keep him on the Helicarrier anymore. By the time they reach Manhattan, Selvig has already activated the Tesseract and the Chitauri are pouring through the opening above the city. Ben wouldn’t know their species beforehand, but he’d understand immediately that they’re using a centralized invasion route and that shutting the portal matters more than trying to defeat every soldier coming through it.

When the first Leviathan comes through, Ben could switch to Humungousaur and help Hulk bring it down before it gets deeper into the city. He wouldn’t try to replace Hulk in that fight because Hulk can hit harder and keep going without needing to switch forms, but Ben could grab part of the Leviathan’s armor, pull it off balance, and give Hulk a cleaner shot. The 2 of them working together would also keep the creature from crashing through as many buildings before it goes down.

Ben would keep changing forms depending on what the team needs. Big Chill could phase through damaged buildings and pull trapped civilians out without moving entire sections of debris, while Echo Echo could spread through several streets and warn people before Chitauri squads reach them. Chromastone would be useful against energy weapons because he can absorb and redirect energy, although Ben would still be careful around anything connected directly to the Tesseract because he has no idea what that kind of energy would do to the Omnitrix.

The biggest difference would come when Natasha reaches the portal generator and Selvig explains that Loki’s scepter can shut it down. Ben could use Brainstorm to look over the machine with Tony’s earlier data and help confirm that simply destroying it could make the Tesseract even more unstable. He wouldn’t suddenly understand everything Selvig built, but he’d know enough about alien technology to avoid smashing the one device holding an open portal above Manhattan.

The nuclear missile would still become the worst part of the battle. When Tony intercepts it and realizes he has to carry it through the portal, Ben could go Jetray and follow him long enough to keep Chitauri craft from getting in the way. Tony would still be the person carrying the missile because his armor can lock onto it and redirect its flight, while Ben focuses on clearing the route so Tony doesn’t have to fight his way upward with a nuclear weapon attached to him.

Ben could follow Tony farther through the portal without assuming a timeout would simply leave him helpless in space, since the completed Omnitrix has failsafes designed to keep him alive. He’d still turn back once Tony has a clear route to the command ship so he can help Natasha on the ground and avoid gambling on how the watch would respond to the portal closing, and Tony would still fall back through after the missile destroys the Chitauri command ship. Hulk could catch him before he hits the ground, keeping that part of the battle close to what originally happened.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The days after New York would be awkward for Ben because everyone else has somewhere to return to. Thor can take Loki and the Tesseract back to Asgard, Steve is still trying to build a life in the modern world, Bruce can disappear again if he wants, and Tony has Stark Tower. Ben has been thrown into another universe with no Gwen, Kevin, Grandpa Max, or Plumbers to contact, so staying on Earth means figuring out where he belongs while S.H.I.E.L.D. is still very interested in the device on his wrist.

Tony would actually help Ben on that point. He’d still be fascinated by the Omnitrix and would probably spend hours asking to scan it, but he’d understand why Ben doesn’t want an intelligence agency taking apart technology attached directly to his body. Tony could study the external readings with Ben’s permission and realize pretty quickly that the watch is operating far beyond anything Stark Industries can reproduce.

That would give the 2 of them a strange relationship. Tony sees a teenager carrying technology that makes most of his suits look simple, while Ben sees somebody smart enough to understand parts of the Omnitrix without immediately assuming he owns it. They’d annoy each other constantly, especially because Tony would keep trying to name transformations and Ben would keep telling him the aliens already have names.

Steve would still be more concerned about Ben himself. After watching him in New York, Steve couldn’t argue that Ben lacks experience, but he would question whether a kid should be expected to respond every time the Avengers face another world-ending threat. Ben would push back because he has already spent years doing exactly that, and sitting at home while people are in danger wouldn’t suddenly become easier because Steve thinks he’s too young.

Ben could also help Tony identify which pieces are dangerous to handle and which are mostly useless without the Chitauri network behind them. That would reduce some accidents during cleanup, although it wouldn’t stop every piece of alien technology from disappearing into private hands. Groups like Hydra already have people inside S.H.I.E.L.D., and Ben has no reason yet to know which agents are secretly working for someone else.

Fury would eventually stop treating Ben like a temporary problem and offer him a place whenever the Avengers are called together again. It wouldn’t come with the same formal structure S.H.I.E.L.D. uses for its agents because Ben has no interest in becoming one of Fury’s employees. He’d agree to work with the Avengers when something is too big for one person, while keeping control of the Omnitrix and making his own decisions about which missions he takes.

That arrangement would give Ben a reason to stay involved even while Tony keeps looking for a way to send him back to his own universe. By the time another major threat reaches Earth, Ben would already know how Steve leads, how Tony thinks during a fight, how dangerous Hulk can become when control slips, and how much better the team works when they actually share information before everything goes wrong.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Ben's biggest effect on the Avengers would become obvious when Ultron appears because the team suddenly has someone who can interact with technology in ways Tony and Bruce can’t. Ben would be older by then, with a few more years of experience fighting beside the Avengers, and Tony would already know that Upgrade and Brainstorm are the forms most likely to be useful whenever they’re dealing with a machine they don’t understand.

The early events around the HYDRA base could still happen because Ben wouldn’t know where the scepter has been hidden until the Avengers find it. He could help during the assault by using Big Chill to move through defensive positions or Humungousaur to clear heavier weapons, while Tony reaches the lab and finds the intelligence inside the Mind Stone. Ben would be interested in the scepter, but he’d also know better than to let the Omnitrix start interacting with something connected to an Infinity Stone without understanding it first.

Tony and Bruce would still experiment with the intelligence they find because Tony’s fear after New York hasn’t disappeared. Ben could be involved enough to know they’re trying to build a global defense system, but Tony might keep the most dangerous parts of the work between himself and Bruce until they know whether it functions. That would allow Ultron to emerge without Ben simply standing beside the computer waiting to stop him.

Once Ultron attacks, Upgrade becomes extremely useful and extremely risky. Ben could merge with one of Ultron’s damaged drones and immediately feel that the machine isn’t operating like ordinary hardware. Ultron’s intelligence is spread across networks and different bodies, so controlling 1 drone doesn’t give Ben control over the whole system.

Ben could still learn things from it. Upgrade might lock down a drone long enough for Tony to extract data, identify communication pathways Ultron is using, or stop one body from uploading itself somewhere else. Ultron would notice quickly that Ben can interfere with his machines at a level the other Avengers can’t, which would make the Omnitrix a priority whenever Ben is nearby.

That could make Ben avoid using Upgrade carelessly after the first few encounters. If Ultron can study how a Galvanic Mechamorph connects to technology, Ben wouldn’t want to stay merged long enough to give him more information than necessary. Brainstorm would become safer for analyzing captured systems because Ben can work through the problem without physically joining the network.

Ultron would still escape into the internet because the network is too large for Ben to shut down by himself. The Avengers would have an easier time isolating individual copies, though, and Tony could use what Ben learns to narrow down which systems Ultron is relying on. That would make the chase more controlled while still leaving Ultron dangerous enough to keep moving between bodies and locations.

Ben wouldn't be able to guarantee Vision is safe, so there would still be tension when he wakes up. Once Vision proves he can think independently and lifts Mjolnir, Ben would probably accept him faster than some of the others because his own life has taught him that being created from alien technology doesn’t automatically tell you what kind of person someone is.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: By the time Ultron raises Sokovia into the air, Ben would know that destroying robots is only part of the problem. Thousands of civilians are trapped on a city that’s being lifted high enough to become a weapon, and every Avenger would have to spend most of the battle keeping people alive while Ultron keeps sending new bodies at them.

Ben’s transformations would make him especially useful there because he can switch between rescue and combat without needing different equipment. Echo Echo could spread through damaged streets and locate civilians who are trapped inside buildings, while Big Chill could phase through walls and bring people out through routes that are blocked by debris. Humungousaur could lift collapsed sections long enough for people to escape, and Jetray could move between different parts of the city faster than almost anyone except Iron Man.

He’d still have to manage the Omnitrix intelligently because the watch can time out or switch him back, even if its failsafes make a lethal reversion much less straightforward than simply leaving him human at the worst possible moment. Ben would make shorter transformations whenever possible, using Humungousaur long enough to move something heavy before switching back and saving the next form for another part of the evacuation. Years of working with the Avengers would make him much better at calling out what he can handle instead of disappearing into another part of the battle and assuming everyone else knows where he went.

Ultron would also prepare specifically for him. Some drones could focus on keeping Ben away from damaged systems so he can’t use Upgrade, while others spread far enough apart that Echo Echo can’t simply overwhelm everything in 1 area. Ben would still tear through ordinary Ultron bodies with several of his forms, but he’d spend more time protecting people than chasing the main Ultron body.

That could change what happens with Pietro. When Clint goes back for the child during the evacuation and Ultron opens fire from the Quinjet, Ben would have several possible ways to reach them. If he’s close enough to go Jetray, he could cross the distance and pull Clint and the child out of the line of fire before Pietro has to put himself between them and the bullets.

Pietro would survive which would have consequences after Sokovia because Wanda wouldn't leave the battle having lost the only family she had left. She’d still hate Ultron and still have to live with everything that happened because she helped him at the beginning, but Pietro being alive would give her someone outside the Avengers to lean on while she decides whether she wants to stay with the team.

Ben could then help with the final evacuation while Thor and Iron Man destroy the city before it hits the ground. Hulk would still end up leaving in the Quinjet because Ben can’t be everywhere at once, and Natasha’s attempt to bring Bruce back would still fail once Hulk decides to disappear. Ben might be able to chase the Quinjet as Jetray for a while, but following Hulk across the ocean without knowing where he intends to go wouldn’t guarantee he brings him home.

After Sokovia, Ben would have another reason to question how the Avengers are making decisions. Tony and Bruce created Ultron without telling the whole team what they were doing, and everyone else had to deal with the consequences once it escaped. Ben has worked around powerful technology his entire life, so he’d understand better than most why good intentions don’t make experimentation safe when the device involved can think for itself.

He wouldn't walk away from the Avengers over it. Pietro surviving and the evacuation going better would also mean the team comes out of Sokovia with fewer personal losses, although the destruction of the country would still be enough to push governments toward demanding more control over what the Avengers are allowed to do.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: The Sokovia Accords would put Ben in an unusual position because he already has experience working with the Plumbers. He isn’t against oversight, reporting to people, or following rules when a larger organization is involved, so Steve’s argument that the Avengers should answer only to themselves wouldn’t automatically convince him. Ben would also know how dangerous it is when an organization gets control over when someone is allowed to use the power they personally carry.

The Omnitrix would make that problem harder. Governments could regulate where Ben operates with the Avengers, but Ben wouldn’t agree to anything that gives them ownership of the watch or allows someone else to decide when he can transform in an emergency. He has spent too much of his life protecting the Omnitrix from people who wanted to control it, and he wouldn't sign away that responsibility because the document comes from the United Nations. Tony would understand why Ben hesitates, even though he supports the Accords. By this point they’d known each other for years, and Tony knows Ben isn’t refusing because he wants to do whatever he wants without consequences. Ben could support some form of international oversight while pushing for limits on what governments can demand from individual Avengers, especially people like himself, Thor, or Vision whose abilities can’t be separated from them and locked in a warehouse.

The bombing in Vienna would still push everything forward before the team has time to reach a compromise. Bucky would be blamed, T’Challa would go after him, and Steve would try to reach Bucky before the authorities do. Ben wouldn’t know enough to declare Bucky innocent immediately, but he would recognize that Steve has personal information about him that the rest of the team doesn't.

Ben could stay with Tony at first because bringing Bucky in alive gives them a chance to figure out what happened. Once Zemo activates Bucky using the Winter Soldier commands, Ben would see direct proof that Bucky can be controlled against his will. That would make him much less comfortable treating everything Bucky does as a normal choice, especially because Ben has dealt with mind control and possession enough times to understand the difference.

The airport confrontation could still happen because Steve needs to reach Siberia and Tony is trying to stop the situation from getting worse. Ben would go with Tony, but he wouldn't be interested in beating Steve’s side into submission. He could use Echo Echo to divide the battlefield, Big Chill to freeze weapons or block routes, and Spidermonkey to restrain people without hitting them hard enough to cause serious injuries.

When Vision accidentally fires at Falcon and hits Rhodey instead, Ben could switch to Jetray and dive after him, catching Rhodey or slowing the fall enough to keep the impact from destroying his spine. Rhodey would avoid the spinal injury he originally suffers. The fight would still end with Steve and Bucky escaping because Ben wouldn't want to unleash his strongest transformations against teammates who are trying to leave rather than kill anyone. Tony would be angry, but Rhodey being safe would keep that anger from becoming mixed with the guilt and panic he had after watching his friend fall.

That would give Tony another reason to follow Steve toward Siberia with questions instead of arriving only to prove Steve wrong. The Avengers would still be divided over the Accords, Bucky, and everything Steve kept from Tony, but Ben’s presence would keep several parts of the conflict from becoming as damaging as they were the first time.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: By the time Thanos finally moves for the Infinity Stones, the Avengers would still have problems from Civil War, but the team wouldn't be as damaged as it originally was. Rhodey never suffers the spinal injury from the airport fight, Pietro is still alive, and Ben has been pushing Tony to focus on whoever manipulated the conflict instead of treating Steve as the only person responsible. Tony and Steve would still be angry with each other, especially once Tony learns that Bucky killed his parents while under Hydra control and that Steve knew more than he told him, but the Avengers would have a much easier time staying in contact when something serious happens.

Maw would still be difficult because his telekinesis gives him control over almost everything around Ben, and there’s no reason to assume the Omnitrix protects Ben from being lifted or pinned by an outside force. Ben could switch forms to escape certain holds, but Maw would quickly realize that keeping Ben from touching the watch is more useful than trying to overpower every transformation he uses. Tony would notice the same thing and start covering Ben whenever Maw focuses directly on him.

Ben could use Big Chill or Jetray to move through sections of the ship Tony and Peter can’t reach as easily, while Brainstorm helps him understand enough of the controls to stop Maw from simply changing course or locking them out. He wouldn't instantly know Chitauri or Q-Ship technology, but he’s spent years dealing with alien systems and would be far more comfortable experimenting with them than anyone else there.

Maw could still die once the group uses the ship’s environment against him, and Strange would still have to decide whether they return to Earth or take the fight toward Thanos. Ben would understand Tony’s reasoning because letting Thanos reach Earth with several Stones gives him more civilians to threaten and more people to protect during the fight. Strange could still choose Titan because he knows Thanos is going to come for the Time Stone either way.

Ben would still help the group get closer to removing the Gauntlet. Once Mantis gets control of Thanos, Ben could turn into Humungousaur and help hold the arm while Tony and Peter work the Gauntlet loose. If Quill starts losing control after learning Gamora is dead, Ben would have a better chance of physically stopping him before he reaches Thanos because he isn’t already using both hands on the Gauntlet.

With Ben stopping Quill before he breaks Mantis’ hold, Tony and Peter would likely have enough time to finish pulling the Gauntlet off while Humungousaur keeps Thanos’ arm pinned, although Thanos could still recover before they manage it. If they do get it free, Strange would make sure Thanos cannot immediately reclaim it. Rather than relying on an interplanetary portal to Earth, he could open a portal to an inaccessible location elsewhere on Titan and leave the Gauntlet there while the group focuses on containing Thanos.

That would completely change what happens in Wakanda. With the Gauntlet hidden elsewhere on Titan, Thanos would no longer have the Space Stone available to carry him straight to Earth. Once Mantis’ hold breaks, his immediate priority would be finding the hidden Gauntlet and recovering the Stones, giving Ben, Tony, Strange, Peter, and the Guardians a window to put distance between themselves and Thanos and leave Titan aboard the Benatar. Thanos himself would be stranded there for the immediate Wakanda battle. The heroes already in Wakanda would only have to hold the line against the Black Order and the Outriders instead of preparing for Thanos to appear behind them.

Vision would still be vulnerable because the Mind Stone is part of him, and the Black Order would still be trying to take it. Wanda, Pietro, Steve, and the others would have to buy time while keeping the Black Order away from Vision. Pietro’s speed would give the Wakandan defenders another way to intercept attackers or pull allies out of danger, while Wanda could stay focused on protecting Vision whenever the Black Order breaks through the defenses.
Thor would still arrive with Stormbreaker, but now he'd be joining a fight where Thanos himself cannot immediately reach Wakanda.
That gives the Avengers a real chance to finish the fight before the Snap ever happens.

Thor, Wanda, Vision, Steve, and the others could focus entirely on breaking the Black Order's assault instead of trying to stop Thanos from reaching the Mind Stone. Ben, Tony, Strange, Peter, and the Guardians would also be making their way back aboard the Benatar rather than being stranded on Titan after a loss, leaving Earth in a much stronger position once they return.

The battle would still cost lives because Thanos’ army is enormous and the Black Order remain dangerous, but half the universe wouldn't disappear while the Gauntlet and Thanos are separated on Titan. The first war with Thanos could end with Wakanda surviving the invasion, the Stones still separated, and the Avengers gaining time to decide how to deal with Thanos before he can find another way off Titan.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Stopping the Snap would remove the 5 year collapse that originally defined Endgame, but it wouldn't leave the Avengers with nothing to deal with afterward. Thanos’ army would still exist across the galaxy, the Infinity Stones would still be dangerous, and Earth would now know that someone came close to killing half of all life because several of the Stones were sitting within reach of the same planet.

Thor could help establish those connections because Asgard already understands the larger universe, while the Guardians give the Avengers another link to what’s happening farther out. Ben would fit naturally between those groups because he’s spent most of his life dealing with aliens as people instead of treating every species as a possible invasion force.

Tony would probably use that period to turn the Avengers into something much closer to the team he wanted after New York, just without handing control over to an artificial intelligence like Ultron. Ben would be involved in defensive technology, especially anything built from recovered alien systems, because Tony would trust him to point out when they’re experimenting with something they don’t understand well enough.

Pietro surviving Sokovia would continue changing Wanda’s life too. She'd still become an Avenger and still have to deal with the consequences of her powers, but she wouldn’t be carrying the loss of her brother on top of everything else. Ben would also have known both of them since Ultron, which gives Wanda another teammate outside Steve and Vision who understands what it feels like to be young while everyone around you expects you to handle threats that can destroy cities.

Rhodey staying healthy would keep him active longer, and the Avengers wouldn’t spend years separated after Civil War. Steve and Tony might never go back to being as close as they were before the Accords, but surviving Thanos together would give them a reason to work through the damage instead of leaving it unresolved until one of them dies.

Ben himself would become one of the most experienced Avengers despite being younger than most of the team. He arrived as a 16 year old Fury wanted watched, then fought through New York, Ultron, Civil War, and Thanos alongside people who originally had no idea whether they could trust him. By the time a new generation of heroes starts appearing, Ben would already be someone they look to during alien or technological threats because he has dealt with both for most of his life.

The Omnitrix would keep giving the Avengers options they never had before. Brainstorm could help with scientific problems, Big Chill could handle rescue situations where normal people can’t enter, Jetray could reach places before aircraft arrive, Echo Echo could cover large areas, and Humungousaur gives the team another heavy hitter whenever Hulk or Thor aren’t available. Ben wouldn't need to use Alien X to matter because most Avengers missions don’t require rewriting reality. They need someone who can choose the right tool quickly and understand what that tool can actually do.

Tony would probably keep asking about Alien X anyway once he learns Ben has a transformation that powerful. Ben would know enough about the form to avoid treating it like an emergency button he can press whenever a mission becomes difficult. By this point Ben has already reached an arrangement with Serena and Bellicus that lets him directly control Alien X once he gets that control, so the old deadlock is no longer the same limitation it used to be. The real reason he wouldn’t default to Alien X is that putting reality-warping power in the middle of an Avengers battle would be an absurd escalation when he has dozens of safer transformations available.

The Avengers would also give Ben something he lost when he arrived in this universe. He still wouldn't have Gwen, Kevin, or Grandpa Max around, and finding a way back to his original world would remain important to him, but years spent fighting beside the same people would make Earth feel less temporary. Tony would become someone Ben argues with constantly and still trusts when things get serious, Steve would eventually stop seeing him as a kid who needs to stay behind, and Thor would treat him like another warrior long before Ben is old enough to think of himself that way.

If Tony eventually finds a way to reopen the dimensional path that brought Ben there, Ben would have a much harder decision than he expected. Going home means seeing his family and friends again, but leaving permanently means walking away from a team he helped build through most of its history.

Ben would probably choose to go home if the path is stable because his own universe still has people who need him, but that doesn’t mean the connection has to close forever. If Tony can understand the dimensional technology well enough, the Avengers could eventually have a way to contact Ben when something happens that genuinely needs him.
By then, nobody would be debating whether Ben belongs with the Avengers. He would’ve earned that place years earlier.
(No need for an outro)

scripts.title: What If Ben 10 Scanned Aang

sections.name: INTRO
paras: The Omnitrix scanning Aang sounds like it should give Ben the Avatar, especially once it recognizes that Aang’s body works differently from the humans Ben already knows. Ben would probably expect 1 new transformation with access to all 4 elements and maybe even the Avatar State.

What he’d actually get is much stranger. The Omnitrix could copy the part of Aang’s biology that lets his body bend, but Aang’s connection to Raava and the Avatar Cycle isn’t something sitting inside his DNA. Ben would have the right body for bending and none of Aang’s years of training. So now Ben has to figure out how far that new transformation can actually go, while Aang shows him which parts of being the Avatar can’t be copied by the Omnitrix.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: This would use Ben during Alien Force, when he already understands the Omnitrix much better and can usually choose what he turns into. Aang would come from late in Avatar The Last Airbender, after he’s learned all 4 elements but before his final fight with Ozai. He’s already an airbending master and has spent months training the other elements, although air is still the one that comes most naturally to him.

Ben would reach Aang’s world through a damaged Plumber device. He could be following a piece of alien technology that starts pulling energy from another dimension, and when Ben tries shutting it down, the device opens a rift and throws him through. The Omnitrix would protect him from the worst of the fall, but by the time Ben gets back up, the portal is gone and he has no way to contact Gwen, Kevin, or anyone else.

It wouldn't treat Aang exactly like the humans Ben grew up around. Whatever differences exist between humans in Aang’s universe and Ben’s are apparently significant enough that the Omnitrix doesn’t classify Aang as the same genetic template as its wearer. His body comes from a world where people can be born with the ability to bend an element. The series never explains bending as something that comes purely from DNA, so the Omnitrix wouldn't be reading a simple “airbending gene.” It would be recognizing a human template whose body and chi are built around rules that don’t exist in Ben’s world.

That would be enough for the watch to attempt a scan. Aang would get nervous when a light suddenly moves across him, so Ben would explain what the Omnitrix does. He can use DNA from different life-forms to rebuild himself as a member of their species, and somehow the watch has decided Aang’s version of humanity is different enough to save as a new template.

Aang probably wouldn't know what to make of that until Ben starts asking questions about his abilities. Once Aang shows him airbending, Ben would understand why the Omnitrix reacted. Then Aang could explain that he can also bend water, earth, and fire.

Ben would immediately think he hit the jackpot. The watch just scanned someone who can control all 4 elements, so Ben would assume the new transformation comes with all 4 too. Once Aang mentions the Avatar State, Ben would probably become even more convinced that this is going to be one of the strongest forms he’s ever unlocked.

Aang would warn him that being the Avatar isn’t the same thing as being an Air Nomad. He was born with airbending because of the people he comes from. His ability to learn the other 3 elements comes from being the Avatar, and the Avatar exists because of a spiritual connection that has continued through many lifetimes.
He’d open the Omnitrix and choose the new transformation.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The transformation would probably disappoint Ben for the first few seconds because he’d still look human. His body could be slightly taller and more athletic, with the Omnitrix building him as a healthy version of someone from Aang’s world, but he wouldn’t suddenly have wings, armor, or any obvious new feature.

Ben would start testing the elements immediately. He’d try fire first, throwing his arm forward like he’s expecting something close to Heatblast. Nothing happens. He’d stamp at the ground and try earth next, then point toward some nearby water and wait for that to move too. He’d get nothing from either one.
Aang would probably tell him to slow down before Ben starts deciding the transformation is useless.

When Ben tries copying one of Aang’s basic airbending movements, he’d finally feel something. A weak gust could move through the grass in front of him. Ben would try the motion again with more control and get enough wind to push dust across the ground.

Somehow, the Omnitrix’s reconstruction of Aang’s unusual human template preserves the physical and chi configuration that allows his native airbending. Whether that comes from genetics, spiritual factors affecting the body, or some combination of both isn’t something either universe has a clean answer for. Aang was born an Air Nomad, so air is the bending ability connected to him before the Avatar’s spiritual role is involved. The watch can rebuild Ben into a body that works under those same rules, but it hasn’t copied the bond that lets Aang learn the other 3 elements.

He could ask Aang to demonstrate waterbending, then repeat the same movement and get nothing. Aang could show him a simple earthbending stance, but Ben’s transformation still wouldn’t move the ground. Fire wouldn’t appear either.

The Avatar State would be even further away. Ben’s eyes wouldn’t glow, he wouldn’t hear any past Avatars, and there would be no sudden increase in power. The watch scanned Aang’s physical template. Raava is a separate spirit connected to the Avatar across different lives, so copying Aang’s body wouldn’t create another Raava or place Ben into the Avatar Cycle.
Ben would be annoyed that the transformation isn’t what he expected, but he’d still have airbending, and once he sees what Aang can do with it, that would be enough to keep him interested.
The next problem would be learning how to use it.

Ben could make gusts because the transformation is capable of bending. Aang could make those same gusts hit exactly where he wants, curve around obstacles, lift him into the air, or stop an attack without throwing the person behind it through a wall.
Ben would have to learn that part himself.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Aang would start by correcting the way Ben stands.

Ben’s first instinct in a fight is usually to plant himself somewhere and attack. Even when he uses faster aliens, he tends to think about where the hit is coming from and how he can answer it. Airbending asks him to move differently. Aang would have him stay light on his feet, circle around attacks, and keep his body moving instead of turning every exchange into a contest of strength.

Aang could prove pretty quickly why that doesn’t mean much here. During a short practice match, Ben might throw several air blasts while Aang keeps slipping around them. Then Aang could catch Ben with one controlled gust that knocks his feet out from under him without hurting him.
Ben would start taking the lessons more seriously after that.

His habits would take longer to change. Aang would teach him how to use air to redirect an attack instead of meeting it directly. Ben could practice stepping around a strike while moving air with the same motion, then use another small gust to create distance. Once he gets comfortable with that, he’d start linking movements together instead of stopping every time he attacks. That’s where Ben’s experience with the Omnitrix would start helping him.

He could pick up the basic air blast first, then start using air to jump higher or slow himself before landing. Moving through the air would probably come naturally because Ben already understands how useful positioning can be from transformations like Jetray and Big Chill.
He’d also start modifying techniques around the way he fights.

Ben might use a short burst under one foot to change direction suddenly, then throw another gust from the side before an opponent turns around. He could use small blasts to throw off someone’s balance instead of wasting energy trying to launch them across the room.
Aang would let him experiment as long as Ben keeps control.

Aang could dodge several of Ben’s attacks while talking to him, then use one smooth movement to send Ben past him. Ben might learn quickly, but every practice session would remind him how much of bending comes from training instead of simply having access to the element.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: After enough practice, Ben would stop trying to move exactly like Aang.

He'd keep the basics Aang taught him, but his own fighting experience would start changing how he uses them. Ben has spent years switching between aliens with completely different powers, so he naturally looks for ways to make an ability fit whatever situation he’s dealing with. Airbending would become one of his better forms for controlling a fight without causing much damage.

If someone pulls a weapon, Ben can knock it out of their hand without hitting them directly. If several people are coming toward him, he can move around them and keep pushing them out of position. If a building is burning, he can move smoke away from people long enough for them to escape.
A fight with Fire Nation soldiers could show how different Ben and Aang are even while they’re using the same element.

Ben might rush into the group and use 2 quick air blasts to knock soldiers away from their weapons. When someone throws fire at him, he could use a gust to push it off course and immediately move to the next attacker. His style would still feel like Ben. He’d move quickly, take chances, and look for openings where he can finish an exchange fast.
Aang would move through the same fight with much more control.

He could redirect fire without sending it toward anyone else, move civilians out of danger, and keep several soldiers busy while Ben focuses on whoever is closest to him. He’d also know exactly how much force to use, something Ben would still be learning.

Ben could hit an enemy with too much air and send him farther than he meant to. Aang would correct him afterward because bending isn’t only about making the strongest gust possible. That lesson would matter because the Omnitrix might make Ben physically impressive without giving him Aang’s judgment.

If Ben has to fight while protecting someone behind him, he might focus too much on winning the exchange in front of him. Aang would already be thinking about where every attack is going, where the civilians are standing, and how the environment can help him avoid hurting anyone. Ben would slowly pick that up from him. He could start using air to create space before attacking, keep smoke and debris away from people, and block attacks for someone else instead of always using the first opening to strike back.
By the time they finish dealing with the soldiers, Ben would have a form that actually feels useful rather than like a weaker version of Aang.

He can already turn into aliens that are stronger than any normal bender. Airbending gives him control and movement that those forms don’t always have, especially in places where smashing through everything would create more problems.
Ben would still have 1 thing he wants to test before he’s satisfied.
He’d want to know whether there’s any way to reach the Avatar State.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Aang would explain the Avatar State again once Ben starts asking serious questions about it. The power comes from the Avatar’s spiritual connection and the knowledge carried through the Avatar Cycle. Aang can access abilities and experience from lives that existed long before he was born. His glowing eyes are connected to something much larger than the body Ben scanned.
Ben would still want to test whether his transformation can touch any part of that.

Aang could start with meditation because it doesn’t put either of them in danger. He’d show Ben how to sit, control his breathing, and pay attention to the energy moving through his body. Ben would probably struggle at first because sitting still has never been his favorite way to solve anything.
After enough time, he could start feeling the chi in the transformation more clearly.

Nothing else would happen. There wouldn't be another voice in Ben’s head or some hidden group of past lives waiting for him. Aang could take him somewhere with stronger spiritual activity and try again, but Ben would still remain himself.
The transformation would react to the physical parts of the training because Ben has a body capable of bending. The part that makes Aang the Avatar would stay with Aang.

Ben could even ask Aang to enter the Avatar State in front of him while the Omnitrix watches. The watch might read the enormous increase in energy around Aang and recognize that something is happening, but there would be no second scan. Raava isn’t another genetic template for the Omnitrix to store, and Aang isn’t changing into another species when the Avatar State activates.
That would finally settle what Ben has been testing since the moment he scanned him.

The Omnitrix can copy enough of Aang’s physical nature to give Ben access to airbending. Everything Aang built through training still has to be learned, and everything tied to his spiritual role stays outside the watch.

After spending time learning from Aang, he’d understand how much can be done with 1 element when someone actually knows how to use it. He’d also know that getting the Avatar State instantly would've skipped everything that makes Aang good at controlling it in the first place. Ben would keep the transformation and continue training with it, especially because he’s already started using air in ways that fit his own fighting style. Aang would keep teaching him because Ben is getting better, and the next real fight would give both of them a chance to see how useful the transformation becomes when Ben stops trying to turn himself into another Avatar.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Once Ben stops trying to force the transformation into something it isn’t, he’d start improving much faster. Aang could move past the basic forms and work more on movement, timing, and control, especially the parts Ben still struggles with when a fight gets crowded.

Ben would get better at using air to change direction without stopping, which would make the transformation much harder to hit. He could jump over someone, push himself sideways before landing, then use another gust to knock a weapon away before the person turns around. Aang would keep correcting the little things, especially when Ben uses too much force or wastes movement.

Aang would also start showing him how useful airbending can be outside a fight. Ben could clear smoke from a building, slow falling debris, help people get down from high places, or move through a crowded area without hitting anyone. That would give him more reasons to choose the form even when he has stronger aliens available.

They could test that during another run in with Fire Nation soldiers near a small Earth Kingdom town. Ben would use air to knock weapons away and keep fire from reaching the buildings, while Aang handles the larger group and keeps civilians moving toward safety.

Ben would look much better than he did earlier. He’d redirect fire instead of just blasting it back, use short gusts to pull people away from danger, and keep moving so the soldiers can’t surround him.
By the end of the fight, Ben would be using the transformation with enough control that Aang could trust him with harder techniques.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Ben would still be curious about the other bending styles, even after accepting that the Omnitrix didn’t give him water, earth, or fire.
Aang could use that curiosity to teach him something useful anyway.

Earthbending would help Ben understand how to stay grounded when he actually needs to. Airbending keeps him moving most of the time, but there are moments when running around creates more problems. Watching Toph would show him how much can be done by waiting, reading the other person, and moving at the right moment.

Waterbending would help with redirection. Katara could show him how a movement can guide an attack somewhere else instead of stopping it with force. Ben wouldn’t move water, but he could use the same idea with air and get much better at turning attacks away from civilians. Firebending would be useful for breathing. Once Zuko is around, Ben could see how much firebending depends on controlling breath and producing power without losing control. That would help with the way Ben sometimes burns through too much energy when he gets excited. Ben would start mixing pieces of those lessons into the way he already fights.
