He could use a firmer stance before throwing a stronger gust, then immediately return to lighter airbending movement. He could use circular motions to redirect something instead of pushing against it, and he’d become more careful about his breathing during longer fights.
Aang would probably enjoy seeing Ben build his own style because he’d know Ben is finally learning instead of trying to copy him exactly.
The Omnitrix timer would still be something Ben has to work around.
If the transformation runs out, the bending disappears with it. Ben would have to keep track of how long he’s been using the form and avoid wasting time on flashy attacks that don’t actually help.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The bigger problem would start with the Plumber device that brought Ben into Aang’s world. Part of it could’ve broken away during the rift and landed somewhere else. Fire nation engineers would eventually find it and realize it produces energy they can’t explain.
They wouldn’t build some completely new weapon from nothing. They'd start using the alien component to improve technology they already understand.

It could be added to one of their larger war machines, giving it much more power than it was designed to handle. The Fire nation would see that as an advantage because the machine can move faster, fire harder, or run much longer than before.
Ben would see the problem as soon as he gets close enough.

The Plumber component wasn't built to power Fire Nation machinery, and forcing that much energy through it would start making the same kind of dimensional instability that opened the rift in the first place.
At first, the signs could be small. Metal around the device bends strangely, objects move when nobody touches them, and short flashes appear around the machine whenever it fires.
Ben would know what those flashes mean if they keep using it, the machine could tear open another rift.
That would put the surrounding area in danger because the tear could start pulling in buildings, people, and anything else nearby.
Ben would tell Aang that they need the Plumber component intact if he wants a safe way home, so smashing the whole machine isn’t an option.
Aang would understand the bigger problem right away. They’d have to stop the Fire Nation machine, protect everyone around it, and get Ben close enough to shut the alien part down properly.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Aang would handle the outside first. He could use earth to damage the machine’s movement without bringing the whole thing down, then use water to cool areas that are starting to overheat. Firebending could keep flames under control when water can’t reach something safely, while air keeps smoke and loose debris away from everyone nearby.

Ben would start with a stronger alien to get through the outer defenses. Humungousaur could rip open part of the armor, giving Ben a way inside without destroying the section holding the Plumber component. Once the opening is there, Ben would switch back to the airbending form because he needs something smaller and more precise.

Inside, the space would be tight. Ben could use short gusts to keep loose metal away from the controls and push heat out through broken vents. If something starts falling, he could hold it in place for a few seconds while he moves underneath it.

Aang would stay outside and react to whatever Ben tells him. If a support is about to collapse, Aang could brace the base with earth. If part of the machine catches fire, he could move the flames away from the section Ben is working in. Toph could feel where the metal is shifting and warn them before the structure changes.

Aang could destroy the machine if he had to, but he wouldn’t know which connection powers the dimensional system or what happens if he breaks the wrong one. Ben would have to disconnect the alien component in the right order.

He could use air almost like another pair of hands, keeping wires separated while he reaches deeper into the machinery. Small gusts would let him move hot pieces without touching them and hold damaged parts away from the core long enough to work.

The timer would start getting low while he’s still inside. Ben would have to keep going because changing forms in the middle of the machine could leave him too large to move through it safely. Aang would start sending controlled air through the openings around Ben, helping keep the temperature down and reducing some of the pressure around the core.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: The Plumber component would start failing before Ben gets the last connection free.
A small rift could open directly above the machine, pulling loose metal upward and making the entire structure shake.
Aang would realize there isn’t enough time to handle everything normally.
He'd enter the Avatar State and Ben would see the change immediately.

Aang could use several elements at once to keep the area from coming apart. Earth would hold damaged structures in place, water could protect people from falling debris, and huge currents of air would fight against the pull of the rift.
Ben would stay exactly the same. He’d still have airbending and nothing else. That would answer the question he had from the beginning more clearly than any explanation could.

Ben would keep working on the Plumber core while Aang holds everything together outside. The pull from the rift would start dragging Ben toward the center, so he’d use air to keep himself against the floor while reaching for the final lock.
Aang could send another current through the machine to help him.
Ben would catch it and use the extra lift to move past a section of broken metal that had blocked him before.

He’d reach the core and disconnect it. The rift would begin shrinking as soon as the power source comes loose. Ben could get thrown backward when the machine shuts down, and the Omnitrix might time out before he reaches the opening.

Aang would catch him with air and pull him away from the wreckage. The Fire Nation machine would still be falling apart, so Aang and the others would have to finish controlling the damage while Ben waits for the Omnitrix to reset.
Once it does, Ben could use another alien to move the largest pieces away from the town.

sections.name: PART 11
paras: With the Plumber component recovered, Ben could finally repair enough of the device to open a stable path home.
Aang could take him through the same basic movements they started with, and Ben would look completely different from the person who could barely move grass with his first gust.
His breathing would stay steady, his feet would move naturally, and he’d be able to change direction without thinking through every step.

Aang could spar with him for a little while. Ben would avoid more attacks than before and find a few openings of his own, but Aang would still control the fight. He has years of experience that Ben can’t replace with a good transformation and a few days of practice.
Ben wouldn't be bothered by that anymore. He’d know the form can keep getting better if he keeps using what Aang taught him.
Aang could remind him to keep practicing the movements instead of relying on the Omnitrix to do everything for him.

sections.name: PART 12
paras: Back in his own world, the transformation would become one of Ben’s more unusual options.

It wouldn’t replace his strongest aliens, and Ben wouldn't use it every time something goes wrong. There are still situations where Humungousaur, Big Chill, Jetray, or another alien makes much more sense. Airbending would be useful when Ben needs control.
He could move civilians away from danger without grabbing them, clear smoke from enclosed spaces, slow falling objects, or fight inside a building without destroying half of it.

He could also keep practicing. The more Ben uses the form, the smoother his movements would become. He’d probably never move exactly like Aang because Ben would keep building techniques around his own instincts.

Gwen would probably understand the spiritual side of what happened better than Ben does at first. She already knows that powers don’t always come from biology, so Aang’s connection to Raava would make sense to her as something the Omnitrix couldn’t simply reproduce.
Kevin would probably care more about the fact that Ben now has a transformation that looks almost normal until he gets thrown across the room by a gust of air.
Every time he uses it, he’d still be working with what Aang taught him instead of relying on a power the watch automatically knows how to control.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Ben would never come away from scanning Aang as another Avatar.
He could still get a real airbending transformation and become much better with it after training with Aang. The Avatar State, Raava, and the other 3 elements would stay with Aang.
By the time Ben gets home, he’d have a new form he actually knows how to use and a much better idea of how far the Omnitrix can go.

scripts.title: What If Ben 10 Was In Invincible

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Mark Grayson had only just started figuring out what kind of hero he wanted to be when another teenager suddenly appeared with something far more complicated than Viltrumite powers.

Ben Tennyson already knew what it was like to fight aliens, deal with secret organizations, and carry technology powerful enough to change entire worlds. The difference was that this universe had never seen anything like the Omnitrix, and Ben had never encountered a species like the Viltrumites.

At first, that would make him one more young hero trying to help Mark survive a world that was becoming more dangerous by the day. But once Ben started noticing that Omni-Man wasn't telling the full truth about where he came from, his presence would begin changing much more than Mark’s first few months as Invincible.
Because Nolan was used to being the strongest alien in the room. He wasn’t used to fighting someone who could become a different one every few minutes.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Ben’s first problem wouldn't be figuring out that he was somewhere unfamiliar. He'd dealt with enough alien technology by this point to recognize when something had gone seriously wrong. The bigger issue would be realizing that the Omnitrix couldn’t immediately tell him how to get home. For this scenario, this is Alien Force-era Ben using the recalibrated Omnitrix before he gains full control over Alien X, so Serena and Bellicus still limit what he can reliably do with that transformation.

He'd arrive on Earth at roughly the same time Mark was beginning his career as Invincible, which meant superheroes already existed everywhere around him. That would make the situation less alarming than landing on a completely unprotected planet, but Ben still wouldn't assume these people could be trusted. In his own world, he’d already learned that having powers or government approval didn’t automatically make someone a hero.

His first real introduction to this universe would likely come during a public emergency. Ben wouldn't stay hidden for long if people were in danger, and the recalibrated Omnitrix gave him enough options to respond without knowing exactly what he was facing. Something like a collapsing building would push him toward Humungousaur or Swampfire, while civilians trapped somewhere inaccessible could be handled with Big Chill. He’d choose based on the problem instead of looking for the strongest alien available.

Mark was still new enough that seeing another teenage hero would immediately stand out, especially one who could transform into several completely different creatures within the same rescue. At first, Mark wouldn’t know whether Ben was a hero, an alien, or something the GDA had created, but Ben’s behavior would answer most of that before either of them had time to compare stories. The difference in experience would become obvious quickly. Mark had the raw power to lift enormous amounts of weight and survive impacts that would kill almost anyone else, but he was still learning how to use those abilities around civilians. Ben had been doing this since he was 10. He’d already learned that saving people often mattered more than defeating whatever caused the problem, so he’d be thinking about evacuations, structural damage and which transformation could solve the situation with the least collateral damage.

Ben would also immediately notice something strange about Mark. He wouldn’t know what a Viltrumite was yet, but Mark clearly wasn’t human in the normal sense. The strength, flight and durability would tell Ben that much. The Omnitrix wouldn’t automatically explain Mark’s entire species history to him, but Ben has spent years around alien biology and would recognize that Mark’s powers looked more like inherited physiology than something created by equipment or an accident.

Mark, meanwhile, would be fascinated by the Omnitrix. From his perspective, Ben could be standing next to him one second and become a flying alien, a living plant or a dinosaur sized powerhouse the next. Ben would probably explain the basic idea without giving him every technical detail, especially since he still wouldn’t know who in this universe might try to take the device from him.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Cecil would be interested in Ben for reasons that go far beyond adding another superhero to his contact list.

The GDA already monitors extraterrestrial activity, advanced technology and anything capable of threatening Earth. Ben manages to fall into all three categories at once. He’s apparently human, carries technology Cecil has never seen before and can transform into aliens with completely different biological abilities. From Cecil's perspective, understanding the Omnitrix becomes a national security issue almost immediately.

Mark grows into working with Cecil because the GDA gives him information, transportation and access to threats he otherwise wouldn't know existed. Ben already has experience with organizations that operate in the shadows. He grew up around the Plumbers, has dealt with people trying to steal the Omnitrix and knows exactly what happens when powerful technology becomes something everyone thinks they deserve access to.

So Ben would cooperate without becoming easy to control. He'd answer basic questions and make it clear that he wasn’t there to attack Earth, but he wouldn't allow the GDA to dismantle the Omnitrix or start running invasive tests on it. Even if Cecil presented it as a precaution, Ben knows the device is far too dangerous to hand over. The Omnitrix contains the genetic templates of enormous numbers of species, and in the wrong hands that makes it more than a weapon.

Cecil would probably respect the refusal more than he liked it. Ben isn’t some confused kid who accidentally found alien technology yesterday. He understands enough about the Omnitrix to know what he’s protecting, and trying to forcibly remove it would create a problem Cecil has no reason to start when Ben is already willing to help people.

The original Guardians would immediately see his usefulness. Red Rush handles speed, Martian Man provides shapeshifting, Green Ghost can become intangible, and the rest of the team covers different combat roles, but Ben can shift between several of those functions depending on what the situation requires. Jetray gives him extreme mobility, Big Chill gives him flight and intangibility, Echo Echo can create multiple bodies, while Humungousaur gives the team another heavy hitter.

He still wouldn’t replace any of them. The Omnitrix has time limits, mistransformations can happen, and Ben can only use one alien at a time. Its recharge period can also vary, meaning Ben cannot count on knowing exactly how long he will be stuck in human form after timing out. A coordinated team of experienced heroes can cover several problems simultaneously in a way Ben can't by himself.

Omni-Man already knows Earth contains unusual heroes, but Ben is different because his powers come from extraterrestrial technology Nolan doesn’t recognize. More importantly, Ben openly demonstrates knowledge of alien species that most people on Earth simply don’t have.

Nolan wouldn't immediately attack him. There’d be no reason to expose himself over a teenager who hadn't discovered anything yet. He would, however, want to know exactly what the Omnitrix can do and how much Ben understands about alien genetics.

Mark originally enters superhero work with almost nobody his age who can genuinely understand what he’s dealing with. William knows his normal life, Eve understands the superhero side better than most people, but Ben has been balancing both since childhood. He knows what it’s like to have school, relationships and family problems happening at the same time as threats that could wipe out entire cities.

Ben also wouldn't treat him like a rookie forever. He might have more experience, but Mark is already stronger than most of Ben’s regular transformations, and there would be situations where Ben simply can’t do what Mark can. Their relationship would work because each of them covers the other’s weaknesses. Mark brings raw power and endurance, while Ben brings versatility and much better instincts for unfamiliar alien problems.

When the Flaxans begin attacking Earth, Mark initially has no idea what they are or why they’re aging so quickly outside their own dimension. Ben wouldn't know the species either, but he’d immediately recognize that their equipment and biology are operating under unusual environmental conditions. Instead of focusing entirely on punching through their soldiers, he’d start looking at what was happening to them between attacks.

Brainstorm would become especially useful here. Ben could use the transformation’s intelligence to examine captured Flaxan technology, compare what changed when they entered Earth’s dimension and help the GDA understand that the invaders were being affected by the different flow of time.

That doesn’t prevent every invasion. The Flaxans eventually compensate for the problem, and their technology improves each time they return. But Cecil gets useful information sooner, while Mark has someone beside him who approaches the invasion as more than a straight fight.

When the Flaxans eventually return with equipment that lets them remain on Earth longer, Ben and Mark would fight them together. Humungousaur could tear through their larger machines while Mark handles anything that gets airborne, or Ben could switch to Echo Echo when sheer numbers become the bigger problem. The important difference is that Earth now has another hero capable of adapting every time the Flaxans change tactics.

In the original timeline, Omni-Man eventually enters the Flaxan dimension himself and devastates their civilization after they capture him. With Ben involved earlier, there’s a much better chance the invasion is contained before Nolan needs to make that same move, especially if Ben helps identify weaknesses in their dimensional technology.

More importantly, Mark starts becoming a better hero sooner. Ben can’t teach him how to be a Viltrumite, but he can teach him how to slow down and think about what kind of problem he’s actually facing before charging into it.

At first, that would only make Nolan mildly uncomfortable. Ben’s performance during the Flaxan attacks would also make the original Guardians interested in using him as a regular associate, and Cecil would encourage the arrangement because it keeps Ben working alongside a team the GDA already knows. After the latest Flaxan incursion, Ben would already be at Guardians headquarters helping the team and the GDA examine captured dimensional technology when Nolan’s secret summons brings the Guardians back to the same location. Nolan hadn’t invited Ben and would rather not have an unpredictable alien wildcard there, but aborting the meeting after everyone had assembled could create questions he didn’t want. Believing he was still strong enough to eliminate everyone in the room, he would proceed with the ambush despite Ben’s unexpected presence. But the longer Ben stays around the Grayson family, the more chances he gets to hear Nolan describe Viltrum, his people and the reason he supposedly came to Earth. Eventually, Ben is going to start asking questions Nolan really doesn’t want answered.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Nolan originally succeeds because the Guardians are caught completely off guard. By the time they understand he’s attacking them, several members are already badly hurt, and the fight quickly turns into a desperate attempt to survive against someone far stronger than any one of them.

With Ben involved, Nolan has a new problem. Ben’s transformations make the team harder to eliminate cleanly, and unlike most of the Guardians, Ben is used to fighting enemies whose abilities he doesn’t fully understand.

If Nolan attacks the team while Ben is present, Ben probably doesn’t start with Humungousaur and try to trade punches. The first few seconds would tell him that Nolan is physically beyond what most of his transformations can handle head-on. That would push him toward something more useful, like Big Chill.

Big Chill’s intangibility immediately complicates Nolan’s opening. Ben can avoid a direct hit, move through the battlefield without being trapped by debris, and freeze sections of the environment to interfere with Nolan’s movement or visibility. His cryokinesis might inconvenience Nolan, but Ben couldn’t assume it would freeze a Viltrumite of Nolan’s durability in place. More importantly, intangibility gives him those few seconds to keep other Guardians alive instead of trying to win the fight alone.

Red Rush already proves he can react to Nolan’s attacks for a while. Martian Man can restrain him. War Woman can actually hurt him. The team loses because Nolan breaks their coordination before those advantages can come together. Ben gives them another way to hold that coordination.

Echo Echo could split into multiple bodies and force Nolan to deal with several targets while the Guardians regroup. Diamondhead would give Ben a tougher defensive form if he needed to physically block an attack. Even something like Goop could briefly confuse or delay Nolan because destroying the slime body alone wouldn’t end the transformation, but that advantage would disappear once Nolan recognized the anti gravity projector as the form’s critical component.

That doesn’t suddenly make the Guardians stronger than Omni-Man. Nolan still has the raw power to kill almost anyone in the room if he gets a clean hit, and several of Ben’s aliens would go down just as quickly if he chose the wrong transformation.

That matters because Nolan's biggest advantage was surprise. Every extra second gives the Guardians more time to understand what’s happening and combine their abilities properly. Ben could help Martian Man maintain a restraint while War Woman attacks, or use Big Chill’s intangibility and environmental freezing to interfere with Nolan long enough for Red Rush to pull someone out of danger.

The most likely outcome is that at least a few Guardians survive, and that immediately damages Nolan’s ability to control the story afterward. Instead of Cecil investigating a room full of bodies with no living witnesses, he now has people who can say exactly who attacked them.
And once Cecil knows Omni-Man tried to murder the Guardians, Ben becomes one of the most important people on Earth.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Cecil wouldn't tell Mark immediately. Even with surviving Guardians confirming Nolan’s attack, accusing Mark’s father of being a murderer without understanding why would create another problem. Mark is still emotionally tied to him, and Cecil would want as much information as possible before forcing that confrontation.

He doesn’t know Viltrumites from his own universe because they don’t exist there, but the Omnitrix is designed around alien DNA. That gives Ben a way to study Nolan and Mark that nobody else on Earth has.

This has to be handled carefully, though. The Omnitrix doesn’t normally provide Ben with a full encyclopedia entry every time he sees an alien, and simply standing near Nolan or Mark wouldn’t automatically classify their species for him. Once Ben becomes suspicious, he could deliberately use the Omnitrix’s DNA-scanning function on them. A successful scan could confirm that their viable genetic material is distinct from baseline humans and compatible with the Omnitrix, but it still wouldn’t automatically tell Ben their species history, culture, weaknesses or even give him the name Viltrumite.

Ben already knows Mark’s powers appear tied to inherited extraterrestrial biology, but he still wouldn’t know the exact nature of Mark’s parentage unless Mark or Nolan explained it. Nolan’s story about being a peaceful representative from an advanced world starts looking very different once it’s placed next to the Guardians attack. Cecil would begin searching every extraterrestrial record the GDA has for anything connected to Viltrum, while Ben focuses on the biology.

Mark looks human because Viltrumites are physically similar to humans, but his abilities continue developing as the Viltrumite side of his biology expresses itself. Ben wouldn’t know every detail immediately, but he’d understand that Mark isn’t simply a human with inherited powers. He’s biologically becoming much closer to a full Viltrumite as he matures.

Ben would be important here because Mark has a reason to trust him. Ben isn’t a government agent trying to turn him against his father. He’s the friend who has been fighting beside him since the beginning, and he’s also the one person in the room who actually understands what alien genetics can mean. The discovery still wouldn’t tell them why Nolan attacked the Guardians.
And by this point, Nolan would know the situation is slipping away from him. The Guardians survived, Cecil is openly moving against him, and Ben has started looking into his biology.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Nolan wouldn't follow the original timeline anymore.

Once he realizes Cecil and Ben are closing in, he has no reason to spend weeks pretending everything is normal. His original plan depended on weakening Earth gradually and preparing Mark to understand the Viltrumite mission. That becomes much harder once Mark already knows his father attacked the Guardians.

He would still try to explain Viltrum first. Nolan wants Mark on his side, and killing him has never been the goal. He’d reveal that Viltrum isn’t the peaceful civilization Mark was told about and that Earth was always meant to become part of the Empire.

The difference is that Mark isn’t alone when this happens. Ben would be there because Cecil would have no reason to let Mark meet Nolan unprotected, and Mark himself would want someone he trusts nearby. That changes Nolan’s approach immediately. Ben isn’t family, so Nolan has far less patience for him.

Humungousaur would be the obvious mistake. Ben might use him instinctively because the form gives him enough strength to contend with heavy hitters, but Nolan is on another level. A direct exchange would end with Humungousaur getting thrown through buildings before Ben could establish any kind of rhythm.

Big Chill becomes far more useful because Nolan can’t solve intangibility with a harder punch. Ben could phase through attacks, use his freezing to disrupt the environment around Nolan and keep Mark from getting isolated, without assuming the cold itself can immobilize Nolan. Goop could briefly create a similar problem because destroying his physical body doesn’t necessarily remove the anti gravity projector controlling the form. Once Nolan understood what the projector was doing, though, his speed would let him target it directly, making Goop a poor long-term answer.
Echo Echo would also be valuable for creating multiple targets, although Nolan’s speed means the duplicates could disappear quickly if Ben tries to overwhelm him through numbers alone.

When Nolan starts gaining control of the fight, Ben would switch again. Diamondhead can take more punishment than many of his forms and create structures to interrupt Nolan’s movement. Jetray can keep up in the air better than most of Ben’s roster. Brainstorm could help him predict how Nolan is approaching the fight, but it wouldn’t suddenly make Ben physically fast enough to dodge everything.

Viltrumites are used to solving resistance through overwhelming physical superiority. Ben keeps turning the fight into a different problem every few minutes, and Nolan can’t rely on one approach working twice.
Eventually, though, the Omnitrix times out which is the opening Nolan needs.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Once Ben returns to human form, Nolan would move immediately. He knows the Omnitrix has limits now, and Ben without a transformation is physically helpless against him. That makes Ben the easiest way to force Mark to stop fighting.
Mark wouldn't let that happen.

This is where the relationship they built earlier changes the scene. Mark has spent months learning from Ben that protecting people isn’t separate from winning the fight. The moment Nolan goes after Ben, Mark throws himself between them even knowing he can’t overpower his father.

Mark wouldn’t know whether the Omnitrix needed a few more seconds or substantially longer to recharge, but he’d keep protecting Ben anyway. During that attempt, the Omnitrix would eventually become available again.

Ben's next transformation has to be something that changes the fight rather than simply repeating what already failed. Chromastone makes sense here because Nolan has already proven he can overpower Ben’s physical forms. Chromastone gives him high durability, flight and energy manipulation without requiring Ben to stand directly in front of Nolan trading punches.

What it would do is let Ben survive long enough to support Mark while Cecil and the surviving Guardians close in. If War Woman and the others are still alive because of Ben’s earlier intervention, Nolan is now facing the exact team he tried to eliminate, Mark, and an opponent who can keep changing abilities.

Nolan could still kill people if he commits fully, but every second he spends fighting them makes it harder to convince himself that Mark will eventually understand. Mark is openly rejecting Viltrum, the Guardians know what he did, and Ben represents everything Nolan’s worldview says shouldn't work: dozens of different alien species being used to protect one another rather than dominate each other.
Mark still wouldn't defeat his father physically. The turning point would remain emotional. Nolan would have multiple chances to kill Mark and eventually realize he can't make himself do it.
Ben and the surviving Guardians prevent the fight from becoming the same one sided destruction it was originally, while Mark’s rejection still gives Nolan the reason to stop.

Mark is alive, the Guardians are still standing, Cecil now knows exactly what Viltrum wants, and Ben has seen enough of Viltrumite biology to start preparing for whatever comes next. Earth doesn’t get the quiet period it had before. Now everyone knows an empire is coming. PART 8&

Nolan leaving Earth wouldn't feel like a victory. Mark would still be dealing with the fact that his father had lied to him for most of his life, but now there’d be less uncertainty about what comes next. Cecil knows Viltrum exists, the surviving Guardians know Nolan was preparing Earth for conquest, and Ben has already seen enough to understand that this isn’t a threat Earth can solve by waiting.

Instead of focusing only on rebuilding the Guardians and containing local threats, the GDA would start preparing for another Viltrumite to arrive. Any footage or biological data connected to Nolan and Mark becomes far more valuable, and Ben would be pulled into those preparations whether he liked Cecil’s methods or not.

He’d still keep control of the Omnitrix, but this is one situation where he’d willingly help with research. Brainstorm could assist with analyzing Nolan’s movement patterns, damage output and the kinds of attacks that actually slowed him down during the fight. Ben’s own experience would matter just as much because he now knows which transformations can survive around a Viltrumite and which ones are almost useless.

Humungousaur would still be valuable against most threats on Earth, but Ben would know better than to use him as a straight answer to someone like Nolan. Big Chill remains useful because intangibility changes the rules of the fight, while Echo Echo and Goop can create problems that aren't solved by one hard punch. Jetray gives Ben mobility, and Brainstorm gives him a way to think through situations where physical strength isn’t enough.

Instead of training mainly by learning how hard he can hit and how fast he can fly, he now has someone constantly pushing him to think about matchups. Ben has spent years fighting aliens that were stronger than some of his forms, so he understands that surviving usually comes down to figuring out what an opponent can’t handle.

The Guardians would change as well. If War Woman, Red Rush, Martian Man, or any of the others survived Nolan’s attack, Cecil now has experienced heroes who have already fought a Viltrumite and know exactly how badly an unprepared team can lose. Earth’s defense becomes less about hoping another Omni-Man never appears and more about building a response around the fact that one eventually will.

Ben’s presence also gives Cecil something he never had in the original timeline: access to a hero who can potentially adapt faster than the enemy. That doesn’t mean Earth is ready for the Viltrumite Empire. It just means the next one won’t be walking into a planet that has no idea what it’s dealing with. PART 9
When another Viltrumite finally comes looking for Nolan, Ben would understand almost immediately what the situation means.

The visitor wouldn’t need to introduce themselves for long. Their strength, flight and fighting style would match too closely with Nolan for Ben to miss it, and Mark would recognize the connection even faster.

Against most villains, the Omnitrix gives him several transformations that can end a fight by themselves. Against a Viltrumite, many of those aliens become support tools instead. Humungousaur can still hit hard, but he isn’t strong enough to reliably stand in front of a serious Viltrumite and trade blows for long. Diamondhead can survive more than Ben’s human body ever could, but repeated Viltrumite attacks would eventually break through his defenses.

Big Chill becomes one of his best options because phasing lets him avoid attacks that would otherwise take him out immediately. He can move through walls, approach from angles a Viltrumite isn’t expecting and freeze the environment around them to interfere with movement or visibility long enough for Mark to capitalize, without relying on the cold to hold a Viltrumite in place.

Echo Echo could also become useful, not because the duplicates are strong enough to overpower a Viltrumite, but because splitting into multiple bodies forces the opponent to identify the real threat while Mark attacks from another direction.
The problem is that Viltrumites are far more experienced than most of the enemies Ben normally fights.

An experienced Viltrumite comparable to Lucan or Thula could have spent years fighting entire civilizations. They aren't going to keep falling for the same trick. Once they realize Ben is the one creating problems, they'd start prioritizing him.

That’s where the Omnitrix’s failsafes and automatic protections become extremely important. Ben can still be hurt, but the device has repeatedly protected him from situations that should’ve killed him outright. That gives him a better chance of surviving a surprise hit than a normal human would have, but it doesn’t mean he can stand there taking Viltrumite punches indefinitely. Mark would become the shield whenever Ben needs time to transform again, while Ben becomes the person creating openings Mark couldn’t create alone.

If Ben can use Brainstorm long enough to study how the attacker fights, he could start identifying patterns in their movement. Viltrumites rely heavily on speed and direct physical pressure, so Ben wouldn't be trying to outmuscle them. He’d be trying to force them into bad positions where Mark can capitalize.
It becomes much less reliable once the Empire realizes what the Omnitrix actually is.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: The Omnitrix contains genetic samples from enormous numbers of alien species, and its entire purpose is built around understanding other forms of life rather than conquering them. That idea already clashes with Viltrumite ideology before Ben even uses it in combat.

That doesn’t automatically mean Ben gets a Viltrumite transformation the moment he sees one. The Omnitrix has rules around scanning unknown DNA and adding new samples, and Ben would still need the right conditions for that to happen.

But if compatible Viltrumite DNA were successfully scanned in this crossover, the consequences would be enormous. For this scenario, the Omnitrix would give Ben a healthy prime Viltrumite form appropriate to his age. It would not copy Nolan’s exact strength, centuries of conditioning or combat experience.

That wouldn't instantly make him stronger than every Viltrumite alive. Experience and conditioning still matter, and someone like Nolan or another veteran would know far more about how to use that physiology in combat. The real danger is that Ben would now have access to Viltrumite physiology on top of every other alien in the Omnitrix.
Ben stops being a nuisance and becomes something they'd want captured or killed before the device can spread that advantage any further.

That also puts Cecil in an uncomfortable position. From his perspective, a Viltrumite transformation inside the Omnitrix could become one of Earth’s best defenses. Ben would understand why Cecil wants it, but he’d also know how dangerous it would be to start treating the Omnitrix like a weapons program. Mark would probably side with Ben there. By this point, Mark has seen what Viltrumite thinking looks like when strength becomes the only thing that matters. Turning Ben into another tool built around having the strongest possible transformation starts moving in a direction neither of them would be comfortable with.

If a Viltrumite attack gets bad enough and the Omnitrix has access to a form capable of surviving it, he’s going to use it. He just wouldn't build his entire strategy around becoming the strongest thing in the room every time.

Ben knows that transformation exists, but Alien X isn’t a normal combat option. Using him creates its own problems because Ben has to deal with Serena and Bellicus before he can reliably act. In a fast-moving Viltrumite fight, that hesitation could make Alien X less useful than a weaker alien Ben can control immediately.
It would come from forcing Viltrum to deal with someone they can’t classify.

He can become stronger, faster, intangible, microscopic, intelligent or almost impossible to restrain depending on what the situation demands. Every time the Empire thinks it understands what kind of opponent he is, Ben can become something else.

Against multiple experienced Viltrumites at once, Ben and Mark could still be overwhelmed. The Omnitrix has limits, Ben can make the wrong choice, and a single mistake against someone that fast can end a fight immediately.

Mark has a partner who understands alien threats. Cecil has years more warning and better information. The Guardians have direct experience fighting Viltrumites. Nolan’s plan fell apart before he could isolate Mark, and the Empire now has to account for something unlike anything they expected to find on Earth.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Ben entering the Invincible universe wouldn't stop every tragedy, and it definitely wouldn’t make Viltrumites easy to defeat. What changes is how early everyone starts understanding the real threat. Mark learns faster, Nolan gets exposed sooner, the Guardians have a better chance of surviving, and Earth starts preparing for Viltrum before the Empire can control the situation.
Ben also becomes something Viltrum has very little experience dealing with. Their entire system is built around one species proving that it deserves to rule everyone else.

The Omnitrix is built around the exact opposite idea. And in a war where Viltrum believes strength comes from being the superior species, Ben would keep proving how dangerous it can be to understand all of them.

scripts.title: What If Ben 10 Was In The Boys

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If Ben 10 ended up in The Boys universe, seeing superheroes everywhere probably wouldn’t impress him that much. Ben’s been dealing with aliens and people with powers since he was 10, so at first he’d probably just assume this world has its own version of heroes.

I'd use 16 year old Omniverse Ben. During a fight with an alien using stolen Plumber tech, the device tears open a dimensional breach and pulls Ben through before it collapses. He lands in New York with the Omnitrix still working, but no idea where he is or how to get back.

The real shock would be finding out what Vought actually is. Once Ben sees how some of these Supes treat people when the cameras are off, he’d get involved pretty fast. Once Vought realizes this random kid can turn into completely different alien species with a watch they've never seen before, they’re obviously going to want it.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: I'd set this during early Season 2 and use 16 year old Omniverse Ben. He already has years of experience with the Omnitrix, so he is confident with it, knows how dangerous it can be, and has learned enough from Max and Azmuth to be suspicious whenever somebody starts treating the watch like equipment they can study or own. He is still cocky and still likes showing off sometimes, but he is not the 10 year old version of Ben who presses a button first and thinks about the consequences later.

Ben gets pulled into this universe during a fight in Bellwood with an alien smuggler using stolen Plumber transport tech. The device is meant to create controlled shortcuts between distant points, but it has already been damaged by the time Ben catches up to him. The smuggler tries to escape with the core, Ben transforms to stop him, and the fight pushes the device past what it can handle. Instead of opening one stable route, the core starts tearing through several possible destinations at once and creates a much larger breach around them.

The Omnitrix protects Ben when the tear collapses, but it cannot stop the jump itself. Ben gets thrown through and lands on a rooftop in New York hard enough to crack the concrete before changing back. The breach closes almost immediately, his phone cannot reach the Plumber network, and none of the systems he normally relies on recognize where he is. Ben spends the first few minutes assuming the transport device just threw him farther than expected, but the longer he looks around, the less anything matches.

The city still looks like Earth, which is what makes it confusing. The cars, phones, streets, and buildings are familiar, but the brands are wrong and the news is full of people Ben has never heard of. Homelander is on giant screens, A Train is selling products, Starlight is being interviewed like a celebrity, and Vought logos are everywhere. Ben has seen enough aliens, heroes, and weird organizations that none of that immediately scares him. If anything, he assumes Vought is probably this world’s version of some hero organization and starts thinking they might have the technology to help him get home.

He gets his first reason to question that before he ever reaches Vought Tower. A smaller Vought sponsored Supe is filming a promotional appearance near a busy street when part of the stunt goes wrong and sends a delivery truck through an intersection. The Supe is strong enough to help, but he stays focused on the cameras and starts trying to control the scene instead of the people in danger.

Ben does not wait around to figure out who is supposed to be in charge. He turns into XLR8 and clears people out of the truck’s path, then switches to Four Arms once it tips and starts sliding toward a packed bus stop. Four Arms catches the truck, plants it back on the street, and changes back while half the crowd is already filming him instead of the Vought hero they came to see.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: He agrees to visit Vought Tower, but only after making it clear that nobody touches the Omnitrix. The people meeting him laugh like he is being overprotective, which makes Ben trust them less, but he still goes because he needs access to their equipment. Inside the Tower, he sees how different Vought is from anything he is used to. There are merchandise rooms, media teams, giant displays for each member of the Seven, and people talking about rescues and public appearances like they are product launches.

During what is supposed to be a basic scan, Ben notices one technician running a second process aimed directly at his wrist. He shuts the machine down and asks what they were trying to read. The staff claim it was part of the examination, but Ben knows enough technology to tell the difference between scanning him and trying to map the watch.

Annie sees enough of that argument to understand what is happening. Later, when Ben is away from the executives, she quietly warns him not to assume Vought is helping because they care whether he gets home. Ben asks why she works there if she thinks that, and Annie gives him a short answer about things being more complicated than they look. Its not enough for Ben to understand the whole situation yet, but it's enough to make him leave the Tower wondering what Vought actually wants from him.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Ben still goes back the next day because Vought'’s lab is the only place he has found with equipment advanced enough to read the dimensional residue left around the Omnitrix. Getting home matters more to him than whether he likes the people running the building, and Ben is confident enough in himself to think he can use their resources without letting them use him. That gets harder once the questions keep drifting away from the breach. One scientist wants blood samples while Ben is transformed. Another asks whether the Omnitrix changes his DNA or replaces it. Somebody else starts asking what would happen if one of the aliens lost a piece of tissue during a transformation. Ben refuses every request that has nothing to do with getting him home, but the pattern becomes obvious enough that he stops trusting what the machines are doing too.

He turns into Grey Matter after everyone leaves the room and crawls inside one of the scanners instead of relying on what the Vought scientists tell him. It doesn’t t take long to find a second process running behind the dimensional analysis. Every time Ben transforms in the lab, the system has been collecting whatever biological and energy data it can read from the Omnitrix. Vought has already started organizing that information into separate files. XLR8 has estimated speed ranges, Four Arms has strength projections, and technicians are making guesses about how many other species might be stored in the watch. There are also notes discussing whether the Omnitrix can be disabled, removed, or reproduced if they ever get enough data.

Ben shuts the system down and confronts the lead scientist before anyone has time to hide it. The response makes the situation worse because nobody really apologizes. Vought frames the whole thing as a security issue and claims that any technology capable of producing that many

powers has to be understood in case it becomes dangerous. Ben hears the same excuse he has heard from people trying to steal alien tech before, just dressed up in corporate language. Annie gets him out before the argument turns into something security can use against him. This time she stops being vague and tells him what Vought actually did. Supes were not born as some chosen group of heroes. Compound V was given to children, often before they were old enough to understand anything about it, and Vought spent years hiding that from the public. Ben thinks she has to be exaggerating until she shows him internal records, medical files, and payments tied to families who agreed to the injections. That is the point where Vought stops looking like a bad hero company and starts looking much uglier to him. Ben got the Omnitrix when he was young too, but Max spent years teaching him that power meant responsibility and that the watch was never supposed to make him better than everyone else. Vought took kids, gave them abilities they never asked for, and then built careers around controlling what those kids became.

Ben leaves the lab with one useful thing besides the truth. Grey Matter copied enough of the dimensional readings to keep working on a way home without Vought, which means he no longer has to stay close to the people trying to study him.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Annie is the one who connects Ben to Hughie because she knows Vought is going to react once they realize he found the hidden files. Hughie already knows about the kid from the rescue footage, but meeting Ben is different from watching a clip online. Ben looks like a normal teenager until the Omnitrix comes up, and Hughie understands pretty quickly why Vought is obsessed with it.

The Boys bring him to one of their safe locations, where he meets Mother’s Milk, Frenchie, Kimiko, and eventually Butcher. Butcher wastes almost no time sizing him up as something that could be useful against Vought. Ben catches that immediately because he has dealt with adults trying to turn the Omnitrix into a weapon before, and he does not like the way Butcher keeps talking about Supes like every single one of them belongs in the same category.

That is where the biggest disagreement starts. Ben has spent years meeting aliens that could destroy cities and others that would risk themselves to save people. He has fought people with incredible powers and worked beside people just as dangerous. The idea that having powers tells you what kind of person somebody is does not make sense to him, especially with Kimiko standing in the same room.

Hughie gets further by keeping the focus on evidence. He and Annie show Ben what they already know about Compound V, the coverups, and the people Vought has hurt to protect itself. Ben agrees to help expose the company because that is a problem he understands. He just makes it clear that he is not going around killing Supes because Butcher thinks they might be bad.

Their first move is smaller than attacking Vought Tower. Annie knows about a storage site where older Compound V records and internal files are kept before being transferred into Vought's main systems. If they can get the original records out, Vought will have a much harder time claiming everything was fabricated later.

Ben uses the Omnitrix in a way nobody in the group expects. Grey Matter gets him through the physical security without setting off the main system, then Upgrade merges with the internal network and starts pulling files directly from the servers. Hughie and Annie sort through what matters while Upgrade moves past security blocks faster than Vought can close them.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: The lockdown forces everyone else to carry the first part of the escape because the Omnitrix is recharging. Frenchie gets one service door open, Mother’s Milk keeps them moving through areas with fewer guards, and Kimiko handles the people who get too close without turning the whole building into a massacre. Ben hates waiting for the watch because he knows exactly how much easier the situation would be with another transformation, but he also knows repeatedly slamming the dial is not going to make it recharge faster.

The stolen records make the escape harder because they cannot just abandon the drives and run. Hughie is carrying evidence that could prove Vought knowingly gave Compound V to children, and security is already trying to lock down every exit before they can leave with it. Ben starts using the building map he saw while connected as Upgrade to guide them through maintenance corridors instead of waiting around for the Omnitrix to come back.

When the watch finally reactivates, Ben chooses XLR8 because getting everyone out matters more than winning a fight. He moves Hughie and the drives through the next security section before the guards can close it, circles back for Annie, and clears a path toward the loading area. The Omnitrix does not give him exactly what he wants on the next transformation and lands him on Diamondhead instead of another speed form, so Ben adjusts rather than wasting time complaining about it.
Diamondhead works better for the situation anyway. He blocks gunfire from reaching the others, seals part of the hallway with crystal, and keeps security trapped on the wrong side without
having to seriously injure anyone. By the time Vought sends heavier teams downstairs, the group is already outside and moving away from the site.

Ben and the others get enough records out to prove what Compound V is and how Vought used it. Annie and Hughie start sorting through what can actually be released without giving Vought enough time to bury it, while Ben expects the company to send people after them next.

Vought goes after the story first. They release security footage showing Ben breaking into the facility with people they label criminals and describe him as an unknown enhanced attacker. The footage starts after the group enters, leaves out what was stored inside, and says nothing about Vought secretly scanning the Omnitrix before Ben ever turned against them.

Ben sees the story spreading online while the real files are sitting on the table in front of him, and that frustrates him more than the escape did. He wants to go back to Vought Tower and call them out directly because that is usually how Ben handles someone lying to his face, but Annie explains that Vought already has cameras waiting for exactly that reaction. If he storms into the building angry, they get footage of the dangerous alien kid attacking their headquarters and nobody hears what he was trying to say.

Ben doesn’t like it, but he listens. For the first time since arriving, the problem in front of him is not something he can solve by finding a better alien. Vought has already failed to understand the Omnitrix, so now they are trying to make everyone afraid of the person wearing it.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: The files from the storage site give Annie and Hughie something they can eventually take public, but they're still missing proof that Vought hasn't stopped doing this. Ben could go back to working on a way home at this point, and part of him wants to, but it’s hard to leave after seeing records of children being injected while Vought continues pretending Supes were born naturally. Grey Matter copied the dimensional readings from the lab, so Ben can keep working on that without Vought for now.

The Boys track a courier who regularly moves paperwork between Vought medical sites, and this is where Ben and Butcher immediately disagree again. Butcher wants to grab the guy and scare the location out of him. Ben points out that they don’t even know whether the courier understands what he’s carrying, and beating up a random employee because he works for Vought isn’t exactly his idea of investigating.
Ben uses Echo echo instead. Several copies follow the courier from different streets while staying far enough away that he never realizes he’s being watched, and they eventually trace
him to a small Vought clinic. Ben switches to big chill once they get there and phases through the exterior wall to check the place before anybody else goes inside.

The clinic makes the situation more complicated than Butcher expected. There are armed guards and Vought staff, but there are also families sitting in waiting rooms and children being prepared for appointments. Ben finds refrigerated Compound V inside a restricted section along with schedules showing more children are supposed to receive it. He comes back out and makes it clear they’re not storming a building full of kids just because Butcher wants the drugs destroyed.

They wait until the families are moved away from the treatment wing, then Ben gets inside again. Upgrade merges with the security system, locks the guards out of the records room, and shuts down the cameras while Annie copies the schedules, patient files, and shipment records. Ben also wipes anything that could identify the children because he knows releasing evidence doesn’t mean turning every victim into part of the story.

Butcher still wants the Compound V destroyed before they leave. Ben refuses when he realizes damaging the storage system could contaminate the clinic or put people nearby at risk, so they take enough sealed samples to prove what's there and leave the rest for authorities once the records become public. Butcher thinks that’s too careful, while Ben thinks blowing up a clinic to prove Vought hurts children would be unbelievably stupid.

That argument finally makes the difference between them clear. Ben’s willing to go after Vought as hard as he needs to, but he’s always checking who gets caught in the middle. Butcher is so focused on destroying the company and the Supes around it that he’s willing to accept damage Ben won't. They're still working toward the same target, but Ben’s already decided Butcher doesn’t get to choose how he uses the Omnitrix.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: The clinic records give Vought a different problem because they now know Ben isn’t only breaking into facilities. He’s collecting material that can survive outside their control. Security teams are given everything Vought has learned from footage of his transformations, including recordings of Echo Echo's sonic attacks, Upgrade taking over electronics, and the forms Ben has used against armed guards.

Ben discovers that during another attempt to recover evidence from a Vought storage building. He turns into Echo Echo expecting to overwhelm the guards from several directions, only for sonic equipment hidden around the corridor to activate almost immediately. The emitters flood the corridor with overlapping frequencies built from recordings of Echo Echo’s own attacks. Vought has not discovered some natural weakness in the species, but the interference makes it harder for Ben’s separated clones to coordinate cleanly, which is enough for him to realize somebody specifically prepared for that transformation.

He switches before the equipment can pin him down and gets Cannonbolt instead of what he was aiming for. Ben complains for about half a second before realizing Cannonbolt is perfect for smashing the emitters Vought built into the walls. He rolls through the corridor, takes out the
equipment from angles the guards weren't prepared for, and gets everyone through the security line before the system can reset.

That gives Ben an idea Vought can’t really prepare for. He stops leaning on the same handful of aliens whenever he has a familiar problem. Pesky Dust puts an incoming security team to sleep without giving them a fight to study, Jury Rigg tears apart a tracker Vought hides on one of their vehicles, and Wildmutt follows a Vought employee through a building after the company shuts down the cameras and electronic locks to keep Upgrade out.

Vought can study footage, but every answer they build only covers a tiny part of what the Omnitrix can do. They don’t know how many aliens Ben has, what abilities those species have, or which one he'll use when something goes wrong. The bigger headache is that Ben himself keeps improvising, so even knowing a transformation doesn’t tell them exactly how he'll use it. Annie starts seeing different language in Vought’s internal reports. They stop treating Ben like an unusual Supe because nothing about him fits Compound V anymore. The company knows he’s physically turning into separate alien species, and every attempt to understand the Omnitrix keeps running into technology they can’t reproduce.

Homelander eventually sees those reports. He isn’t nearly as interested in the science as the people around him are, but he notices how everyone talks about Ben. Vought can’t explain where his power came from, can’t remove it, and hasn’t managed to scare him into cooperating. Homelander has spent his entire life at the center of a system where almost every powerful person around him came from the same company, and now a teenager has walked in carrying something Vought had nothing to do with.

Stormfront takes the alien angle in a much uglier direction. Once the company needs another explanation for Ben breaking into Vought facilities, she starts presenting him publicly as an unknown extraterrestrial threat working with terrorists. Ben sees the coverage and recognizes the trick immediately because he’s spent years watching humans panic around aliens they don’t understand. He knows exactly what happens once Vought convinces people they should be scared before they've even met him.
PART 8&

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Homelander eventually decides he wants to meet Ben himself. He finds him after Ben and Hughie move one of the clinic witnesses to a safer location, landing in the road while Ben is still human and Hughie is trying very hard not to look terrified. Homelander’s attention goes straight to the Omnitrix because that’s the part of Ben nobody at Vought has been able to explain.

He starts by giving Ben an offer instead of attacking him. Vought can fix the headlines, give him access to their labs again, and make the accusations disappear if he stops working with The Boys. Ben almost laughs because the same company offering to protect him is the one that secretly scanned his watch and then called him a dangerous alien when he caught them doing it.

Homelander keeps pushing until Ben brings up Compound V and the children at the clinic. The friendly act disappears pretty quickly after that. Homelander grabs Ben before he can finish dialing the Omnitrix and throws him through the side of a parked car, which gives Ben just enough time to slam the watch on the way through.

Ben wanted something fast and gets Chromastone. That turns out to be useful when Homelander immediately follows with heat vision, because Chromastone absorbs the energy instead of taking the blast directly. Ben redirects it back and catches Homelander hard enough to knock him away from Hughie, then uses the opening to tell Hughie to get the witness out. Homelander closes the distance once he realizes the lasers aren't working the way he expected. Chromastone can handle the energy much better than a straight physical exchange, so Ben quick changes rather than letting Homelander turn it into one. XLR8 gets the remaining civilians off the street and moves Hughie far enough away that Ben doesn’t have to keep checking behind him every time Homelander attacks.

Ben’s next transformation gives him Diamondhead. Homelander can hit harder than plenty of things Diamondhead has fought, but Ben doesn’t need to stand there trading punches. He uses crystal structures to interrupt Homelander’s charges, changes the shape of the street around him, and keeps forcing him to break through obstacles instead of getting a clean shot at anyone leaving the area.

The problem is that Ben’s burning through the Omnitrix much faster than he wants. He doesn’t have Master Control, and although he can quick change between forms during the same active cycle, doing it repeatedly burns through that cycle faster and will eventually force the watch into a full recharge. Once Hughie and the witness are gone, there’s no reason for Ben to keep fighting just to prove he can.

He changes into Big Chill and phases through the ground before Homelander can grab him again. Homelander tears into the street trying to follow, but there’s no clear target to hit while Ben can move through solid material. Ben comes back up several blocks away, changes direction underground, and gets out before the watch finally returns him to human form. Homelander doesn’t walk away thinking he won. Ben survived his heat vision, escaped his strength, moved people out from under him, and left when he decided the fight was over. What bothers Homelander even more is that Ben never seemed interested in impressing him. For Ben, Homelander was another dangerous guy he needed to keep away from civilians, and Homelander can’t stand being treated that normally.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The encounter with Homelander convinces Ben that they can’t keep collecting evidence forever while Vought decides when every confrontation happens. Annie and Hughie finally have enough records, witnesses, and original files to release the Compound V story through people Vought can’t shut down with one phone call. The last thing they need is the physical archive tying several of those records directly to Vought’s internal system.

Ben goes after that archive knowing the company has already studied most of his obvious choices. He starts as Grey Matter and enters through maintenance space that normal security never considers an entrance, then reaches the server hardware and switches to Upgrade. Instead of downloading everything to one drive Vought can recover, he pushes copies into several outside systems Hughie has waiting.

Security realizes what's happening and starts physically disconnecting the network. Ben leaves the servers before they can trap Upgrade inside isolated hardware, changes into Goop, and slips through a sealed section while guards are still trying to figure out which doors matter. By the time they realize where he’s headed, the records are already leaving the building from several directions.

A Train reaches the facility before Ben gets out. Ben knows Vought has enough footage to expect XLR8, so he goes with Gravattack instead and increases the pull around the corridor until A Train can’t build speed properly. Every step becomes harder, and trying to accelerate only pushes him deeper into a field Ben can change around him.

A Train is still dangerous once Ben’s timer starts running down. Gravattack drops away before Ben wants it to, and A Train closes the distance while Ben is human. Hughie gets the last physical drive through an emergency exit while Ben gets the Omnitrix working again and comes back as Diamondhead just before A Train reaches him.

Ben gets out, but the encounter is a useful reminder that having the right alien doesn’t mean he controls every second of a fight. If the Omnitrix times out at the wrong moment, someone as fast as A Train can become a serious problem. Ben has better answers available than almost anyone in this universe, but he still has to reach those answers in time.

The Compound V evidence hits the public while Vought is still trying to contain the break in. Annie’s files match the medical records, witnesses confirm what happened, and the clinic schedules prove the program didn’t simply disappear years ago. Vought can attack Ben’s credibility all it wants, but it can’t make all of those pieces vanish at once.

Butcher sees the chaos as his chance to push harder. He wants Ben to go after Homelander while Vought is distracted, arguing that they might never get another opening this good. Ben refuses because he isn’t here to become Butcher's answer to every person he wants dead, and their argument circles right back to why Ben distrusted him in the first place.

Vought treated children like products because their powers were useful. Butcher is starting to look at the Omnitrix the same way from the opposite side, and Ben isn’t interested in being owned by either one of them. He'll stop Homelander if Homelander comes after people again, but he isn’t taking assassination orders from Butcher just because they happen to hate the same company.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Homelander comes after Ben once the Compound V story is already out and Vought’s control over the situation is slipping. At this point, killing Ben won't put the files back in the servers, but Homelander isn’t thinking that cleanly anymore. Ben embarrassed him once, helped expose the company that built his entire public identity, and keeps acting like Homelander’s reputation doesn’t mean anything.

Ben knows another confrontation is coming and makes sure it doesn’t happen around the witness safe house or a crowded street. He uses Vought's own tracking attempt against them, lets one of their devices keep transmitting long enough to draw Homelander toward an industrial area outside the busiest part of the city, then destroys it once Homelander arrives. Ben would rather fight somewhere with room than spend the entire battle moving civilians out of the way. He tries selecting way big first because dragging the fight out makes the Omnitrix timer a bigger problem. The watch gives him Rath instead, which is strong enough to take the first hit but probably the worst personality Ben could’ve gotten for somebody as easy to provoke as Homelander. Rath immediately starts yelling at him and charges before Ben has finished deciding what he wants to do.

Homelander figures out quickly that Rath’s aggression can be used against him. He stays in the air, makes Ben chase, and starts baiting him into attacks that leave him open. Ben gets a couple of solid hits in, but he also takes more damage than he should because Rath keeps trying to turn the fight into a brawl.

Ben changes before Homelander can take advantage of that. Big Chill phases through the next rush and freezes the ground when Homelander lands, buying Ben enough time to pull the fight farther into the empty part of the site. Homelander switches back to heat vision once grabbing him stops working, which gives Ben another reason to change instead of trying to force Big Chill to solve everything.

Humungousaur lets Ben meet Homelander physically without pretending every punch is equal. Ben can take the hits and return enough force to make Homelander work for it, but flight keeps giving Homelander angles Humungousaur can’t follow. Ben switches to Jetray and takes the fight into the air, where his speed and maneuverability keep Homelander from controlling the distance as easily.

That constant switching starts costing Ben. The Omnitrix gives him shorter windows, and Homelander finally notices that the dangerous moment isn’t when Ben becomes another alien. It's the few seconds where he becomes human again. Homelander starts waiting for those transitions instead of trying to overpower every form individually.

Ben gets caught during one of them. Homelander reaches him before he can make another deliberate selection, and the Omnitrix’s protective systems react when Bens life is in immediate danger. Ben transforms before the hit can kill him and comes out as Feedback just as Homelander fires heat vision at close range.

Feedback takes the blast into the plugs on his hands before it can reach his body. Homelander keeps firing for another second because he thinks more power will solve the problem, and that only gives Ben more energy to work with. Ben redirects it back in one concentrated burst that sends Homelander through part of the industrial structure and finally makes him understand that his heat vision is helping instead of hurting this form.

That does not suddenly make Homelander harmless. He comes back furious and tries to close the distance physically, so Ben does not stand there waiting to find out how long Feedback wants to trade punches. He uses the energy he already absorbed to keep Homelander off balance, then quick changes again once he has room. The point is not to prove one alien is stronger than Homelander. It is that every time Homelander adjusts to one answer, Ben can become something built around a completely different problem.

Homelander eventually realizes the fight is getting worse for him the longer it continues. Feedback has just turned his heat vision back on him hard enough to cause real damage, and Ben has already cycled through enough completely different aliens to make it obvious Vought still does not know what else the watch can produce. Ben is not trying to execute him either. He makes it clear that if Homelander leaves, Ben is going back to helping the people Vought hurt. If he keeps attacking, Ben still has transformations Homelander has never seen, while another bad attack could be turned against him just as easily.

Homelander leaves angry rather than give Ben another clean opportunity to embarrass him. Ben does not pretend that means the problem is over. Homelander is still out there, Vought still has money and influence, and releasing the Compound V files does not erase everything the company built. What changes is that Vought can no longer control the basic truth as easily. The records, samples, witnesses, and Annie’s own involvement give the public too many separate pieces to dismiss as one story invented by a strange kid from nowhere.

Ben also leaves Butcher with the same boundary he had from the beginning. He helped expose Vought because people were being hurt, not because he agreed that every Supe needed to die. Hughie and Annie understand that much better, and Ben trusts them enough to leave copies of what he recovered before turning his attention back to the problem that brought him here in the first place.

With the dimensional readings Grey Matter copied from Vought and everything Ben learned from the damaged Plumber technology that sent him here, he eventually gets enough information to make the Omnitrix recognize the path back to his own universe. It takes more work than pressing the dial and hoping for the right alien, but that is exactly the kind of problem Ben has spent years learning not to solve alone with brute force.

So Ben would leave The Boys universe having done something Vought was never prepared for. They understood powers as products they could create, study, market, and control. The Omnitrix gave Ben more power than almost anyone they had ever dealt with, but the real problem was that none of it belonged to them. Ben could fight Homelander when he had to, expose Vought without becoming Butcher’s weapon, and then go home still treating the watch the same way he did when he arrived: as something he was responsible for, not something that made him better than everyone else.

scripts.title: What If Beyonder Spider Man Was In Jujutsu Kaisen

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If Beyonder Spider-Man landed in the Jujutsu Kaisen world, Gojo would probably notice him before Peter even understood what a curse was. For this, I’m using the comic version of Peter while he’s empowered by the Beyonder, anchored to the reality-altering power Peter himself actually demonstrates instead of giving him every feat the Beyonder has ever had. When he applies that power to unfamiliar jujutsu mechanics, those uses are extrapolations of the reality alteration he already showed rather than separate abilities Peter canonically demonstrated. That still leaves Spider-Man with power far beyond anything he normally carries.

Peter would enter this world trying to save whoever is directly in front of him. He wouldn’t know why some people can see the creatures attacking them, what cursed energy is, or why the sorcerers around him treat certain abilities like absolute rules. Then Gojo sees Peter use power that doesn’t behave like a cursed technique at all, and suddenly the strongest sorcerer alive is looking at someone who doesn't fit anywhere inside the system he understands.

Kenjaku would notice the same thing and start changing his plans around Peter almost immediately. Sukuna would eventually realize that killing Peter through raw force is probably getting him nowhere, while Peter's refusal to casually sacrifice civilians gives both of them something much more useful to work with. Once that happens, every major event from Shibuya onward starts changing because Peter has enough power to stop disasters that were supposed to happen, but he still has to figure out who he can save without letting the people around him turn that restraint against him.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter's arrival happens at the exact moment Earth-20051 gives him access to the Beyonder’s power. In his own reality, that power only lasts for an impossibly short amount of time before Doom takes control of it, but during that instant Peter is capable of rewriting reality on a scale that goes far beyond anything Spider-Man normally touches. For this story, the transfer is interrupted before Doom can take the power back, and Peter gets thrown out of his universe while he is still carrying that same cosmic energy.

He appears in Tokyo without understanding where he went or why the world around him suddenly feels different. The city looks normal at first, but Peter can sense layers of information he never had access to before, including people moving through buildings blocks away and strange concentrations of energy gathering around places filled with fear. He does not immediately rewrite the city or start searching the planet because his first reaction is still the same one he has whenever something goes wrong: figure out whether anybody nearby needs help.

Peter finds the first curse attacking a group of civilians near an abandoned building. He can see it clearly even though the people running away cannot, and the creature is large enough that normal Spider-Man would have treated it like a serious fight. Peter reaches for it on instinct and stops when the curse comes apart before his hand even touches it. He didn’t punch through the body or burn it with energy; he wanted the thing away from the civilians, and the power inside him responded by removing it.

Megumi arrives seconds later expecting to find the curse still there. Instead, he finds Peter standing beside several terrified civilians while the cursed energy he had been tracking simply ends. Megumi cannot sense a technique being released, cannot find the remains of an exorcised curse, and cannot understand why Peter looks more confused about what happened than anybody else.

Peter asks Megumi what that creature was, which only makes the situation stranger. Megumi has spent his entire life around people who understand curses, while this stranger apparently erased one without knowing what a curse is. Peter notices Megumi watching him carefully and explains that he is Spider-Man, which does absolutely nothing to help.

Megumi tells Peter to come with him because leaving an unknown person with that kind of ability wandering through Tokyo would be irresponsible. Peter agrees because Megumi is the first person he has met who can explain what he just saw, although he keeps asking questions the entire way. By the time they reach Jujutsu High, Megumi has already decided this is something Gojo needs to see personally.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Gojo notices the problem before Peter finishes walking toward him. The Six Eyes give Gojo an absurd level of information about cursed energy, but Peter does not look like a sorcerer with an unusual amount of it. There is no normal cursed technique for Gojo to identify, and the energy surrounding Peter does not behave like anything produced through the jujutsu system.

Peter is equally interested in Gojo because the power inside him lets him perceive what is happening around Infinity.
