He can see that the space between them is being manipulated so anything approaching Gojo slows before making contact, but he does not immediately test whether he can break through it. Peter has known Gojo for less than a minute and has no reason to start trying to punch the guy explaining where he is.

Gojo eventually tests it himself. He asks Peter to tap his shoulder while keeping Infinity active, expecting Peter’s hand to stop before reaching him. Peter moves normally until his fingers reach the distorted space, pauses when he feels what Infinity is doing, and instinctively changes the distance rather than forcing his hand through it.

His fingers touch Gojo’s shoulder. Gojo moves away immediately and turns Infinity off while Peter apologizes because he thought Gojo wanted him to do that. What interests Gojo is the way Peter bypassed it. Peter did not become faster than Infinity and did not overwhelm it with cursed energy; he altered the space separating them so the distance Infinity was manipulating no longer worked the way Gojo expected.

That gets Peter a much more serious conversation. Gojo explains cursed energy, cursed techniques, barriers, and the basic reason curses exist, while Peter keeps stopping him whenever the answer sounds insane even by Marvel standards. Peter is especially bothered when he learns that negative human emotion keeps creating creatures capable of killing people who usually cannot even see them.

Yuji joins them while Gojo is explaining Sukuna. Peter meets him as a friendly teenager first and only realizes something else is inside him when Sukuna deliberately opens a mouth on Yuji's cheek to comment on the stranger in front of them. Peter freezes for a second, Yuji apologizes like this happens all the time, and Gojo casually explains that Yuji is currently carrying Ryomen Sukuna, the King of Curses.

Sukuna can sense enough about Peter to know he is looking at something completely abnormal. He does not know what the Beyonder is and cannot read Peter through normal cursed-energy rules, but he understands power well enough to recognize that this person is operating somewhere outside the scale he normally cares about. Peter has the opposite reaction and becomes far more concerned with the fact that a teenager is sharing his body with a mass murderer.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter spends the next several days learning how the jujutsu world works before deciding what he should change. Gojo gives him access to Jujutsu High because keeping Peter close is safer than letting the higher-ups discover him through secondhand reports, while Megumi and Yuji become the people Peter spends the most time around. Peter likes Yuji almost immediately and gets frustrated every time somebody talks about his eventual execution like it is an administrative detail.

Cursed energy itself is difficult for Peter to categorize because he does not naturally generate or use it the way sorcerers do. He can perceive it now because of the awareness that came with the Beyonder’s power, and he can interact with curses without needing cursed energy of his own. When Megumi asks whether Peter can exorcise one intentionally, Peter takes them to a controlled training area and removes a curse without damaging anything around it.

Megumi asks what technique Peter used, and Peter admits he does not have a name for it. He saw the curse, understood enough about what it was made of, and changed that specific thing until it stopped existing. Gojo listens to the explanation and realizes how dangerous Peter would be if he thought like a jujutsu sorcerer, because Peter is approaching curses without accepting most of the limits everyone in their world treats as permanent.

Kenjaku hears about Peter through reports from curses and curse users who notice incidents ending without normal exorcism traces. He initially assumes a new technique has appeared, then realizes there is no family history, barrier signature, or cursed-energy pattern connecting the events. A stranger has entered Japan and started changing cursed phenomena without participating in the system Kenjaku has spent centuries studying.

That changes what Kenjaku cares about before Shibuya even begins. Sealing Gojo is still useful, but Peter is now a larger unknown than anything inside the Prison Realm plan accounted for. Kenjaku starts gathering information without approaching him directly, using curses around Peter to see whether he attacks automatically, protects civilians first, follows fleeing enemies, or allows dangerous people to escape when killing them is unnecessary.

Peter notices the pattern after the third incident. Each curse appears somewhere crowded enough to force him toward rescue work, and none of them are strong enough to threaten him personally. He tells Gojo somebody is testing how he reacts, while Gojo reaches the same conclusion from the way the attacks keep avoiding areas where other sorcerers would normally respond first.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Kenjaku gets his clearest answer when Mahito becomes involved. Mahito wants to see Peter personally because someone who can alter reality should be able to perceive the shape of a soul in ways ordinary sorcerers cannot. Kenjaku tells him to avoid direct contact until they understand more, which lasts about as long as advice usually lasts when Mahito becomes curious.

Mahito creates transfigured humans in front of Peter and watches what he does. Peter immediately recognizes that the creatures are still people underneath what happened to them because the cosmic awareness inside him lets him see the damage reaching deeper than the body. He stops the first one without attacking and begins trying to understand what changed. Peter restores the victim and Mahito loses the smile for the first time because Idle transfiguration is built around changing the shape of the soul and forcing the body to follow it. Peter doesn’t heal the damage like reverse cursed technique and doesn’t resist Mahito through cursed energy. He looks at the person’s altered state, identifies what Mahito changed, and puts it back.

That makes Mahito attack him directly. His hand reaches Peter and tries to touch the shape of his soul, but Peter feels the manipulation the instant it begins and stops the change before it spreads anywhere. Mahito pulls his hand away and realizes Peter did not defend himself with cursed energy at all; Peter simply refused to let Mahito alter him.

Peter is much angrier about the humans Mahito changed than the attack on himself. He restrains Mahito by changing the space around his body so every direction leads back into the same few feet, leaving Mahito able to move without actually getting anywhere. Peter then starts restoring the remaining victims one at a time while asking Mahito how many other people he has done this to.

Yuji arrives before Peter decides what to do with him. The moment Yuji sees Mahito, his entire mood changes because this is the curse responsible for Junpei’s death and countless others. Peter realizes there is history between them and keeps Mahito trapped while Yuji explains enough for Peter to understand why everyone wants him dead.

Peter still does not kill Mahito. That decision is exactly what Kenjaku wanted to learn. Peter possesses more than enough power to erase Mahito immediately, but he will look for another option as long as he believes one exists. Kenjaku now knows Peter’s limits are coming from Peter himself rather than the abilities available to him, and that gives Kenjaku something he can plan around.

Gojo is less comfortable with the decision once he arrives. He tells Peter that Mahito is going to keep killing people if he escapes, while Peter answers that Mahito is currently trapped and they have time to decide what happens without executing him in the street. Peter anchors the trap so it holds even after he leaves, and Gojo puts Mahito under guard. Gojo does not push the argument further because Peter has already done something nobody else could: he restored people Mahito had transfigured instead of simply killing what was left of them.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Keeping Mahito alive destroys part of Kenjaku’s original Shibuya plan before the night ever arrives. Mahito cannot roam freely creating transfigured humans, fighting Yuji, or developing through the same sequence of battles, and Kenjaku now has to decide whether recovering him is worth revealing how much he knows about Peter. The larger objective of sealing Gojo remains because Gojo is still the biggest obstacle Kenjaku understands well enough to prepare for.

Peter creates a second problem because Gojo tells him about the growing signs around Shibuya before entering alone. In the original plan, the barriers and civilians force Gojo into a situation designed specifically around his limitations. Peter hears that thousands of civilians may be trapped inside and immediately refuses to stay outside simply because the enemy probably expects Gojo.

The first barrier gives Peter his first direct look at how jujutsu barrier conditions work. It allows ordinary civilians to remain trapped while controlling who can enter or leave under specific rules, and Peter can see the condition woven through the structure once Gojo explains what he is looking at. Peter could tear the barrier apart through raw reality alteration, but he does not know whether doing that carelessly would affect the civilians or other barriers connected to it.

He takes a narrower approach and changes the condition that prevents civilians from leaving. People begin crossing the curtain almost immediately which forces Kenjaku to abandon the pace he originally built around Shibuya. The civilians were supposed to keep Gojo constrained, fill the station with chaos, and create the environment where the Prison Realm could be activated at the right moment. Peter is emptying sections of the trap before Gojo even reaches the underground platform.

Peter changes how he responds. He creates temporary openings through the barriers that let trapped civilians move toward sorcerers outside, then gives Megumi and Yuji enough information to guide people through them while he stays close to Gojo. Peter does not need to personally carry every civilian out once he gives everyone else a safe route to do it.

By the time Gojo reaches the underground station, the crowd is already thinning and Peter is still beside him. Jogo, Choso, and the other pieces Kenjaku prepared are now facing 2 people instead of 1, and one of them does not operate through cursed energy at all. Gojo looks at Peter, realizes Kenjaku’s entire trap has already started falling apart, and tells him they should find out who went to this much trouble before they give that person time to build another one. PART 6

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Kenjaku still tries to use the Prison Realm because sealing Gojo remains the cleanest way to remove the one sorcerer he spent years planning around. When Geto’s body appears underground, Gojo freezes as the Prison Realm activates, and Peter immediately feels the space around Gojo beginning to lock into a fixed condition. Peter doesn’t smash the object or rewrite the entire area because he has no idea what happens to Gojo if he destroys a sealing technique during activation.

Instead, Peter reacts before the Prison Realm can fully capture Gojo. The instant he feels the sealing condition taking hold, Peter uses the Beyonder's power to disrupt that condition before it can finish binding Gojo, then pulls him several meters away without crossing the space between them normally. He is not simply outrunning an already completed seal; he is altering the trap while it is still taking hold. The sealing attempt fails before it can finish. Gojo snaps back into focus almost immediately, sees Kenjaku standing inside Geto's body, and realizes the trap he was supposed to disappear into just failed.

Kenjaku doesn’t stay to find out what Peter can do next. He releases the curses he still has prepared, collapses parts of the underground station, and uses the confusion to retreat through routes he built long before Shibuya started. Peter initially follows, but the moment he realizes civilians are trapped under falling debris, he turns around and starts holding the station together long enough for people to escape.

Gojo sees that choice and understands why Kenjaku kept using crowded areas against Peter. Peter has enough power to catch him, but Kenjaku can keep creating situations where chasing him means leaving people behind. Gojo stays to help because the station is still full of civilians and sorcerers who'll die if both of them disappear after the same target.

Jogo changes his own plan once sealing Gojo is clearly finished. He stops wasting time around the Prison Realm and goes after Yuji instead, because waking Sukuna now gives the curses a weapon Peter can’t attack carelessly. Yuji is helping Megumi move civilians when Jogo finds him, and several more fingers get forced into his body before Peter can reach them. Peter arrives just as Sukuna takes control, and he can tell immediately that Yuji’s body is being driven by someone else. Sukuna doesn’t rush him or start throwing attacks just to measure strength. He looks toward the busiest part of Shibuya and starts walking there because he wants to see whether Peter will risk hurting Yuji to stop him.

Peter folds the surrounding streets so every path Sukuna takes returns him to the same intersection. Cars, buildings, and civilians remain untouched while Sukuna keeps arriving back where he started, and after the second attempt he stops walking. He’s already learned more from Peter’s response than he would've learned from trading blows, because Peter can clearly contain him and is still avoiding anything that might damage Yuji.

Sukuna smiles and starts thinking around that restraint instead of trying to overpower it. Peter can control the battlefield almost however he wants, but Yuji gives Sukuna a body Peter refuses to treat like disposable material. That turns Yuji himself into the most useful protection Sukuna has.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Sukuna opens Malevolent Shrine because he knows Peter can keep changing the environment faster than he can physically escape it. The domain spreads through the surrounding area without forming a closed barrier, and slashes begin tearing through buildings, pavement, and everything else inside its range. Peter’s lack of cursed energy does not exempt him from the attack; Malevolent Shrine can cut targets without cursed energy through Dismantle, just as it tears through the physical environment around him.

The damage doesn’t stay on Peter for long. He repairs his own body almost as quickly as the slashes reach him, then starts moving civilians beyond the domain's range before the next wave can hit them. Entire groups disappear from damaged streets and reappear outside Shibuya while Peter keeps roofs, roads, and collapsing walls in place long enough for everyone still moving to get clear.

Gojo reaches them once most of the surrounding civilians are gone. He doesn’t immediately use Unlimited Void because Yuji would still be inside the body taking whatever happens to Sukuna, and neither Gojo nor Peter knows whether flooding the shared body with that effect risks Yuji too. Gojo attacks the openings Sukuna creates while Peter keeps the environment from collapsing around them.

Yuji starts fighting from inside before either of them finds a clean way to remove Sukuna. Peter feels the body resisting itself and notices Yuji’s presence pushing forward, so he stops trying to force the separation from outside. He stabilizes the physical damage instead and gives Yuji enough time to regain control on his own.

Malevolent Shrine disappears as Yuji retakes the body. Shibuya is still badly damaged, but the destruction ends much earlier because Sukuna never gets unrestricted time to tear through the city. Gojo stays free, more civilians make it out, and several sorcerers who would've been dragged through much worse fights are still alive when the night finally starts winding down. Yuji remembers enough to know people were hurt while Sukuna controlled him, and he immediately starts treating that as another reason he shouldn't be allowed to live. Peter stays with him afterward and makes him separate what Sukuna chose from what Yuji chose. He doesn’t tell Yuji the deaths don’t matter, because they do, but he refuses to let Yuji turn somebody else’s actions into proof that his own life has no value.

That changes Yuji long before Sukuna gets another opening. He still accepts responsibility for keeping Sukuna contained, but he stops assuming that dying is automatically the cleanest answer whenever containment becomes difficult. Peter doesn’t know it yet, but that makes Sukuna’s future plans much harder.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Kenjaku disappears after Shibuya instead of immediately launching the next phase of his original plan. Gojo is still active, Mahito remains trapped, and the chaos Kenjaku needed across Japan never reaches the same scale. He still has prepared vessels, cursed objects, barrier knowledge, and centuries of planning behind him, but the exact path toward the Culling Game has been broken badly enough that he has to improvise.

He activates a smaller number of incarnated sorcerers and curse users across separate locations rather than starting one massive nationwide game. Peter initially responds to every major cursed-energy spike because he can reach almost anywhere faster than the sorcerers already assigned there. After several attacks, Gojo points out that Kenjaku is learning to use Peter’s speed against him by making every emergency look like something Peter personally has to solve.

Peter hates the idea of staying back while someone else might get hurt, but he also understands what Gojo is saying. If everyone waits for Peter whenever something dangerous appears, Kenjaku only has to keep creating enough problems to move Peter wherever he wants. Peter starts helping the sorcerers build safer routes, stronger evacuations, and better communication instead of replacing them every time a fight begins.

Megumi joins once Sukuna’s interest in Ten Shadows becomes impossible to ignore. Peter has already noticed Sukuna reacting differently whenever Megumi’s technique comes up, while Gojo knows the history of Ten Shadows well enough to take that interest seriously. Megumi doesn’t like being treated like a possible target, but he’d rather know what Sukuna wants before the next possession starts.

They still don’t uncover every part of Sukuna’s plan. Yuji doesn’t remember the full terms of the binding vow he made, and Peter has no way to inspect a promise Yuji himself can’t consciously explain. Sukuna realizes that simply waiting for Megumi to stand unguarded will no longer work, so he uses Enchain’s one-minute window to manufacture the opening himself. He takes control at a moment when Yuji, Megumi, and the others are together, then moves immediately before Peter or Gojo can understand what the vow has just allowed him to do.

Peter reacts the second Sukuna moves toward Megumi, but the transfer doesn’t happen like an ordinary physical attack. Sukuna turns part of himself into a cursed object and forces Megumi into becoming the next vessel before Peter fully understands what he’s watching. Peter gets there while the process is still happening and can feel Megumi and Sukuna occupying the same body, but tearing them apart blindly risks destroying Megumi along with him.

Peter locks the surrounding space so Sukuna can’t leave with Megumi’s body. He keeps Megumi physically stable, calls Gojo and Yuta, and refuses to let Sukuna turn possession into an escape route. Sukuna gets access to Megumi, but he doesn’t get the isolation he needed to bury Megumi completely.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Sukuna starts using 10 Shadows while Megumi is still resisting from inside. Gojo attacks carefully because every hit lands on Megumi’s body too, and Peter handles anything that spreads away from the immediate fight so Sukuna can’t use shikigami to force everyone into separate directions. Yuta stays close to Megumi’s body and watches for any opening where healing or soul pressure can help without making the possession worse.

Megumi gets control of one hand first and ruins a Ten Shadows summon before Sukuna can finish it. A little later he manages to speak for a few seconds, which tells Peter the original soul is still active enough to push back. Peter's earlier experience studying Mahito's manipulation taught him more about how souls and bodies interact in this world, but he still doesn't assume Sukuna's possession works the same way. He waits until Megumi creates another opening, then follows the part of Sukuna's presence Megumi is already rejecting and narrows that connection instead of blindly tearing at both souls together.

The separation happens in stages because Peter refuses to gamble Megumi’s life on doing it all at once. Yuta keeps repairing the physical damage while Gojo holds Sukuna’s attention, and Peter keeps narrowing the connection until Sukuna can no longer anchor himself through Megumi’s body. Megumi finally forces the last part out with Peter helping from the outside rather than replacing his resistance completely.

Peter contains Sukuna's separated presence before it can reach another host. Yuji arrives shortly afterward and sees Sukuna outside both of the bodies he spent months using, while Megumi is still alive beside Yuta. Peter doesn't decide what happens next before either of them gets a say.

Yuji wants Sukuna gone, and Megumi agrees after everything Sukuna did through both of them. Peter listens because they were the people forced to carry him, and once they both give the same answer, he removes the contained presence without touching either host. That ends the immediate incarnation, but it does not automatically neutralize Sukuna’s remaining fingers. They are still dangerous cursed objects, so Peter, Gojo, and the others secure them separately and work out whether Peter’s reality alteration can safely destroy them without risking another vessel.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Kenjaku becomes the last major problem because almost every condition he expected to use has collapsed. Gojo was never sealed, Mahito never becomes available for absorption, Sukuna can’t complete the role Kenjaku expected from him, and the Culling Game never reaches the scale needed to prepare Japan for the merger. Kenjaku still understands barriers better than almost anyone alive, so he moves directly toward Tengen before Peter’s side can close the remaining path.

Peter reaches the Tombs of the Star Corridor with Gojo and Yuta instead of entering alone. By now he knows enough about jujutsu to understand that Tengen’s barriers are connected to systems spread across Japan, so he doesn’t rewrite them just because he has the power to do it. He isolates Kenjaku from the exits and leaves the larger barrier network untouched.

Gojo and Yuta handle the actual fight because they understand Kenjaku’s cursed techniques better than Peter does. Kenjaku still has Geto’s body, cursed spirit manipulation, centuries of experience, and knowledge of the environment, but he no longer has colonies, hostages, or several simultaneous disasters forcing everyone apart. Every route he prepared becomes much less useful once Peter prevents him from escaping the corridor.

Kenjaku eventually tries abandoning Geto’s body after the fight turns against him. Peter recognizes the same basic danger he saw when Sukuna moved between vessels and seals Kenjaku’s brain inside an empty pocket of space the moment it leaves Geto’s skull, before it can reach another host. Peter opens that pocket just long enough for Gojo to finish Kenjaku for good, while Yuta makes sure there’s nobody nearby Kenjaku could have used to continue.

With Kenjaku gone, Peter lets the people Mahito hurt decide what happens to him, and when Yuji gives the same answer he gave about Sukuna, Peter erases the curse he has kept trapped since before Shibuya. Afterward, Peter refuses to rebuild the entire jujutsu world around what he thinks would be better. Curses still form from human negativity, the higher-ups still created a system that treats young sorcerers like expendable weapons, and Tengen's barriers still affect how cursed energy behaves across Japan. Peter has enough power to force enormous changes, but he also knows he arrived here without understanding any of those systems and spent most of his time learning how dangerous that ignorance could be.

Peter eventually figures out how the dimensional accident brought him into this universe and finds a route home. Yuji asks why somebody who could’ve changed almost anything spent so much time asking other people what they wanted, and Peter tells him that having enough power to make a decision doesn’t mean you automatically know what everyone else should have to live with afterward.

By the time Peter leaves, Shibuya never becomes the massacre Kenjaku wanted, Gojo is never sealed away, the full Culling Game never begins, Megumi survives Sukuna’s attempt to take his body, and Gojo never reaches the isolated battle that originally killed him.

scripts.title: What If Clash Royale Had A 3rd Lane

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Imagine defending a Hog Rider on the left, a Minion Giant in the middle, and Royal Hogs on the right, all at the same time. That’s what Clash Royale could turn into if every match had a third lane.

The arena would need a wider layout, a third bridge, and probably another Princess Tower so the middle lane actually works. From there, split pressure gets much stronger, building placements change completely, and spending too much Elixir on one side could leave another lane wide open.
So what would 3 lane Clash Royale actually look like, and would it make the game more strategic or just make defense a mess?

sections.name: PART 1
paras: A third lane would need more than 1 extra bridge dropped into the middle of the current arena. The cleanest version would widen the map and add a third Princess Tower directly between the other two, with the King Tower sitting behind all three. Each Princess Tower would still be worth one crown, and taking the King Tower would still end the match immediately. If time expires first, the player who destroyed more Princess Towers would be ahead, with the usual damage-based tiebreak deciding things if the crown count is tied. That keeps the basic win condition familiar even though players now have another route to attack through.

The middle Princess Tower would need its own bridge and enough space on both sides for troops to path naturally without constantly drifting into the left or right lane. That means the arena probably gets wider by several tiles, especially around the river, because 3 bridges packed too closely together would create weird situations where troops placed in one lane suddenly retarget into another. The mode would need 3 clear pathing zones, with troops resolving toward the nearest valid lane based on where they're deployed. Units placed near a boundary could only split into another lane if their formation actually spans that boundary. That way players can tell where a Hog Rider, Giant, or split group is actually going before committing Elixir.

The King Tower would also need to sit slightly farther back. If the middle Princess Tower is directly in front of it, a straight center push could otherwise reach the King much faster than pushes from either side. Giving the middle tower enough space between itself and the King would keep all 3 lanes roughly equal in travel time, although the middle tower would still be strategically more valuable because destroying it opens the most direct route to the King. That could make center control a major part of the mode once players start trading tower damage.

Defensive tower coverage would need to be adjusted too. Right now, a troop crossing one bridge can sometimes be pulled into range of the opposite Princess Tower with the right placement. With 3 lanes, Supercell would have to decide how much overlap those towers are allowed to have. If the middle Princess Tower can help defend both side lanes too easily, then adding a 3rd lane barely matters. If every tower only covers its own lane, defending becomes much harder because troops can’t be pulled into as much shared damage.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The biggest problem with a 3rd lane would be Elixir. Players still generate Elixir at the same rate and still only bring eight cards, but now they have three different places where pressure can develop. Spending 5 or 6 Elixir defending one lane could leave enough room for the opponent to immediately attack somewhere else before the first defense is even finished.

That would make overcommitting much easier to punish. Imagine defending a Giant push on the left with a building and 2 support troops. In the current game, the opponent can punish opposite lane, but you still only have two routes to think about. In a 3 lane arena, they could send something cheap through the middle while threatening the right side at the same time, forcing you to decide which push deserves your remaining Elixir.

Cheap defensive cards would become even more valuable because one card handling an entire lane would save enough Elixir to cover the other 2. Skeletons, Ice Golem, Goblins, Archers, and other efficient defenders could become staples because spending 4 or 5 Elixir every time someone pressures one lane would quickly become impossible. Current Clash Royale already rewards cheap cycle and flexible defense, and the recent balance changes were partly aimed at reducing how much guaranteed value cheap Spirits were giving decks. A third lane would make that kind of cheap efficiency even more important.

Splash troops would gain value for a different reason. Cards like Valkyrie, Bomber, Executioner, Bowler, and Baby Dragon could defend groups of troops without requiring several separate cards, which helps when you still need Elixir available somewhere else. Their placement would matter more, though, because a splash troop standing in the left lane can’t instantly help with something crossing through center.

The result would probably be a game where players spread their defense out more and hold cards longer. Dropping a 4 Elixir support troop in the back becomes riskier because your opponent now has two other lanes they can attack before that troop reaches the bridge. Even a normal opening play like placing something behind the King Tower could give the opponent more ways to punish immediately.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Hog Rider would become one of the easiest cards to use with the 3rd lane because he can attack whichever tower currently has the weakest defense. A player who keeps placing their building toward the left side could suddenly see Hog pushed through center or right, and traditional defensive placements wouldn’t cover every route anymore.

Buildings like Cannon and Tesla would probably need new central placements specifically designed to pull Hog from 2 nearby lanes. The far lane would still be difficult to cover, so players might have to place a building slightly earlier based on where Hog is deployed instead of relying on one universal tile every time. That makes Hog more flexible, although the wider arena could also give defenders more time to react if the lane paths are slightly longer.

Royal Hogs would benefit even more because splitting them becomes much harder to deal with. Right now, players commonly split them between 2 lanes, but a 3 lane arena could potentially let their formation reach all 3 routes if it spans both lane boundaries. Something like 2 Hogs on one side and 1 in each of the other lanes would only work if the new pathing zones actually allow that deployment. If they can only reach the nearest 2 lanes, they'd still gain more splitting options without automatically creating 3 separate pushes.

3 Musketeers could also take advantage of those same pathing zones. If their deployment formation spans both lane boundaries, a player could potentially send one Musketeer into each lane, creating 3 separate ranged threats that all need answers. If the formation only reaches 2 zones, they would split across 2 lanes like they do now. The card would still cost a huge amount of Elixir, so the risk of playing it stays high either way.

Miner would become extremely useful beside all of this because he can support whichever lane gets the weakest response. If Royal Hogs are split across three routes and the defender spends most of their Elixir on the left side, Miner can appear on the middle or right tower and create another problem without needing to travel through the arena at all.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Beatdown decks would probably struggle more than most archetypes at first because they’re built around committing a large amount of Elixir into one powerful push. A Golem player might spend 8 Elixir in the back and then add support as it moves forward, which gives the opponent a long window to attack somewhere else. With 3 lanes available, that punishment becomes much harder to cover.

A Golem placed behind the left Princess Tower could lead to pressure through both center and right before it even reaches the bridge. The beatdown player then has to either spend Elixir defending those lanes and weaken the Golem push, or accept damage and hope the push takes enough towers to make the trade worth it. That would make tower trading much more common because trying to defend everything while building a heavy push could leave the deck with no Elixir for either job.

Goblin Giant, Electro Giant, Lava Hound, and other expensive win conditions would face the same basic issue, although some would adapt better than others. Lava Hound decks could still work because air support is harder to distract with ground pathing, while Electro Giant could benefit from forcing the defender to commit a lot of Elixir into one lane. Even so, every expensive tank creates another chance for the opponent to spread pressure somewhere else. Bridge spam might love the new arena because cards like Bandit, Battle Ram, Ram Rider, Royal Ghost, and other immediate threats become harder to cover when they can appear at three different bridges. A player could pressure left, wait for the defense, then instantly switch to center without sending anything all the way across the arena.

That would make reactive defending much more stressful because bridge spam already thrives on catching someone low on Elixir. With 3 lanes, the opponent has more choices after spotting that weakness. A P.E.K.K.A committed on one side could defend a huge push there, but it also represents seven Elixir that can’t help immediately if Battle Ram goes through center and Bandit goes right.

The wider map could stop bridge spam from becoming too strong if troop travel distance is increased slightly. If there’s more space between the bridge and Princess Towers, defenders get another moment to react before a Bandit or Ram connects. That kind of adjustment would probably be necessary because adding another bridge without changing travel time could create too many situations where one bad rotation loses a tower before the player can recover.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Buildings would probably need the most relearning because current Clash Royale defense relies heavily on specific placements. Players know where to put Cannon against Hog Rider, where Tesla can pull different win conditions, and how far a building can sit from the river while still dragging troops toward the middle. A third lane breaks a lot of those placements because there is no longer one central area between two towers.

The new arena would probably create 2 important defensive zones instead. One sits between the left and middle lanes, while the other sits between middle and right. A Cannon placed in the left center area could potentially pull troops from those 2 lanes, while anything coming through the far right bridge would ignore it. That means 1 building can still cover more than 1 route, but it can’t control the entire arena.

This would make building placement depend heavily on what the opponent has in rotation. Against Hog Rider, you might keep Cannon closer to the 2 lanes they've been using most. Against Royal Hogs, a more central placement could help pull part of the group while other troops clean up whichever Hogs stay outside its range. Against Giant or Golem, you might place the building specifically in that lane because pulling a heavy tank across multiple lanes could become too difficult on a wider map.

Siege decks would need even bigger adjustments. X-Bow and Mortar normally take advantage of bridge distance and tower sightlines that were designed around two lanes. With 3 Princess Towers, a siege building placed near the middle could potentially have several targets depending on how the arena is laid out, which would be incredibly hard to balance.

The cleaner solution would be keeping normal siege targeting and designing the arena around it. The three Princess Towers and legal siege placements would need enough spacing that an X-Bow or Mortar does not routinely have ambiguous access to multiple towers at once. Placements near lane boundaries could still create interesting sightline decisions, but range and normal targeting would determine what the building locks onto instead of giving siege cards a special lane-assignment rule. Mortar could become especially useful because its cheaper cost makes switching lanes easier. A player could pressure center with one Mortar, defend it cheaply, then cycle to another and place it on the right once the opponent has committed their counter somewhere else. X-Bow would have a harder time because 6 Elixir invested in 1 lane creates more room for pressure through the other 2.

Kiting would change just as much. Pulling Mega Knight, P.E.K.K.A, Mini P.E.K.K.A, or other melee troops into the center currently works because the map naturally funnels both lanes toward the middle. With 3 lanes, defenders would need to decide which neighboring lane they want the troop to move toward and place accordingly. Some old placements would stop working entirely because the closest target might now be the middle Princess Tower or a building sitting between lanes.

That extra pathing depth could become one of the best parts of 3 lane Clash Royale if it stays consistent. Players would have more options for pulling troops, protecting towers, and redirecting pushes, but every interaction would need clear rules. If troops constantly switch lanes for reasons players can’t predict, the mode would feel random instead of strategic.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Cycle decks would probably become some of the strongest options because they can defend one lane cheaply and get back to their pressure cards before the opponent can reset. Hog 2.6, Miner control, and other low cost decks already rely on making small positive trades, and a 3rd lane gives them more ways to turn those trades into damage. If someone spends 5 or 6 Elixir defending the left side, a cheap deck could immediately send pressure through center while still keeping enough Elixir to defend the right.

Spells would become more valuable too, but mostly because troops would be spread farther apart. Fireball, Poison, Arrows, and other area spells would have fewer chances to hit several important targets at once, so getting good value would depend much more on timing. Players who spread support across multiple lanes could force the opponent to choose which group deserves the spell, especially with cards like 3 Musketeers or Royal Hogs if the new pathing rules let their formations split that widely.

Cheap pressure would shape the meta more than anything else. Miner, Wall Breakers, Hog Rider, Royal Hogs, and bridge spam cards could all punish slow decks before those decks have enough Elixir to cover 3 different routes. That would probably push heavy beatdown lower unless those decks started running more cheap defensive cards than they normally would. Splash troops and flexible buildings would become almost mandatory because every deck needs something that can handle multiple threats without spending too much. Cards that only work well in one very specific matchup could become harder to justify when the opponent has three places to attack.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: The biggest issue is that Clash Royale’s current Elixir system was built for 2 lanes. Adding another route without changing Elixir generation means players would constantly have more threats than they can realistically answer, especially once double and triple Elixir begin.

One solution would be slightly increasing Elixir generation, but that creates another problem because faster Elixir also makes large pushes easier to build. Suddenly you could defend one lane, start pressure in another, and still have enough Elixir left to support a third push. That could make matches even more chaotic.

The safer option would probably be keeping normal Elixir and letting the 3rd lane exist as a mode specific challenge. Players would have to accept more tower damage, make smarter trades, and decide which lane matters most instead of trying to defend everything perfectly. Match length could move in either direction. An extra Princess Tower gives players another target to spread damage across, but stretched defenses and the direct center route to the King after the middle tower falls could also create faster finishes. Tower health and overtime would probably need testing rather than automatically being increased or reduced.

The mode could still be balanced, but it would need its own arena dimensions, building placements, pathing rules, and probably separate card balancing. Dropping a 3rd lane into regular Clash Royale without those changes would make cards like Royal Hogs, 3 Musketeers, Hog Rider, and cheap cycle pressure far too difficult to defend consistently.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: A third lane could make Clash Royale more strategic because players would have more choices for pressure, defense, and troop placement. Split pushes would become much stronger, buildings would need completely new placements, and every Elixir commitment would matter more because there are now 2 other lanes that can be attacked.
The problem is that the game was designed around 2 lanes from the beginning, so adding a 3rd one would change almost every important interaction at once.
As a separate game mode, it could be really fun. As the new standard version of Clash Royale, it would probably need so many balance changes that it would barely feel like the same game anymore.

scripts.title: What If Cosmic Spider-Man Was In The MCU

sections.name: INTRO
paras: The first time Peter Parker saved the universe, nobody knew he was doing it.

There was no battle in New York. No alien invasion. No army waiting for him on the other side of a portal. Peter was simply on patrol when a warning hit him that he initially mistook for his Spider-Sense. It felt completely different from his normal danger sense because the Enigma Force was already beginning to reach toward its chosen host, giving Peter his first awareness that something was approaching.
Far beyond Earth, something was moving through space. Peter couldn't see it. He couldn’t identify it. His instincts had never warned him about anything like this before.

Within hours, an ancient cosmic force would reach Earth searching for a champion. It had chosen Peter Parker. The Enigma Force would give him the Uni-Power, transforming an ordinary Spider-Man into a being capable of manipulating matter, generating enormous amounts of energy, flying through space, and perceiving threats far beyond the limits of human senses. For Peter, the problem wouldn’t be learning how to become more powerful.
And for the first time in Peter Parker’s life, being Spider-Man meant leaving the neighborhood behind entirely.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter initially thought the warning was his Spider-Sense, but it had never felt like this before.

He was standing on a rooftop in New York when the warning hit him. It wasn’t focused on a person or a specific location. It felt distant, as if his instincts were reacting to something far beyond the city.
Peter looked toward the sky.

The streets continued below him, traffic moved through the intersections, and the buildings around him were exactly where they were supposed to be. Whatever had triggered the unfamiliar warning wasn’t visible.

Peter waited. A point of light appeared in the distance and began moving toward Earth. It wasn’t an aircraft, and there was no indication that it had entered the atmosphere through any conventional means. Peter watched it approach while trying to understand what he was seeing.
The closer it came, the stronger the unfamiliar warning became.
Peter left the rooftop and followed it.

The object eventually stopped above the Atlantic Ocean. From Peter’s position, it looked like a concentrated field of energy suspended in the air. There was no visible machinery and no recognizable structure.
Peter approached carefully and the energy didn’t attack him. Instead, it responded to his presence.

Peter could feel something reaching toward him, but it wasn’t a physical force. It was more like information entering his mind, allowing him to understand something that he had no previous way of knowing.
This was the Enigma Force.

In the comics, the Enigma Force is the source of the Uni-Power. It travels through the universe and can select hosts during times of crisis, temporarily granting them the abilities of Captain Universe. Peter Parker has been one of those hosts before, and another version of Peter became the Cosmic Spider-Man of Earth-13.

The MCU’s Peter had never encountered it. He also had no idea why it had come to him. For this scenario, MCU Peter receives the core Uni-Power abilities associated with Peter’s Captain Universe transformation: vastly enhanced physical abilities, flight, energy projection, enhanced perception, force constructs, and matter manipulation. The Uni-Power also allows Peter to cross interstellar distances at extreme speeds when responding to the crisis rather than limiting his flight to conventional sublight travel. That does not mean every feat or ability shown by every Captain Universe host or the Earth-13 Cosmic Spider-Man automatically applies to him.

The answer wasn’t based on Peter being the strongest person available. The Uni-Power had chosen hosts with very different abilities and backgrounds throughout its history. What mattered was that the host was capable of facing the crisis in front of them.
Peter had spent years doing exactly that.
He had no cosmic experience. He wasn’t a god, a sorcerer, or a member of an intergalactic civilization. He was a young man who had always tried to help whoever happened to be in front of him.

That was enough. The Enigma Force connected with Peter. The limits of his body disappeared as the Uni-Power moved through him. His strength increased far beyond what his spider abilities had given him before. His senses expanded. His body became capable of surviving environments that would normally kill a human being.

Peter lifted from the surface of the water. He was flying. The Uni-Power was already responding to his thoughts, giving him abilities he had never possessed before. Peter could generate energy, manipulate matter and perceive his surroundings with a level of detail that went far beyond normal human senses.
For several seconds, Peter simply remained in the air. Then he looked down at the ocean. The water below him was still.
Peter had spent years learning how to use every advantage his spider abilities gave him. Now he had something completely different.
He had the Uni-Power. And he was about to discover how difficult it could be to remain Spider-Man when almost nothing was capable of stopping him.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Peter didn’t understand the full extent of what had happened to him yet. The first thing he noticed was how easy it was to move through the air. He’d spent years relying on webs and momentum to get around New York. Now he could simply rise from the ground and travel wherever he wanted. He flew back toward the city and stopped above the shoreline.

The Uni-Power had changed more than his strength. Peter’s senses had expanded, giving him access to information his normal senses couldn't provide. His vision could examine objects at microscopic levels, see through certain materials and observe distant objects with far greater clarity. He could also perceive energy around him in ways he never could before.

The abilities were overwhelming, but they weren’t random. Peter could feel the Uni-Power responding to his intentions. He reached toward a damaged piece of metal lying on the pier. The object lifted from the ground and changed shape in his hand. The Uni-Power allowed him to manipulate its molecular structure, something Peter had only ever seen performed through advanced technology or magic.

He reversed the change and let the metal fall. That was when Peter started to understand the problem. His old abilities had always forced him to work within certain limits. He could lift enormous amounts of weight, but there were things he couldn’t move. He could heal from injuries that would put another person in the hospital, but he could still be hurt. He could react to danger before it reached him, but he couldn’t know everything happening across the planet.

The Uni-Power changed that balance. Peter could now affect matter directly. He could generate energy. He could fly. He could create powerful force constructs and survive conditions that would normally be fatal.
Peter reached the area almost immediately.
A huge skyscraper construction crane snapped at its base, sending a massive section of steel and machinery hurtling directly toward the crowded intersection below.
Peter moved before anyone else had time to react. He leaped into the air and stopped its momentum with one hand.

Peter didn't flinch and effortlessly hoisted the massive rig and set it down in an empty lot. Peter had spent years finding creative ways to overcome problems that were stronger than him. A few hours later, Peter interrupted a robbery.

The criminals had weapons, but Peter didn’t need to fight them. He used a small amount of the Uni-Power to disable their equipment and restrained them before anyone was hurt. The entire encounter lasted seconds. Peter stood on the roof afterward, looking down at the street. He’d done exactly what Spider-Man was supposed to do.
People were safe. The criminals were going to be arrested. Nobody had been seriously injured.

Now he could solve many of those problems almost immediately. Peter wasn’t disappointed that he could save people more easily. He was wondering what would happen to him if saving people stopped requiring anything from him at all.

The question became more difficult when his awareness expanded beyond New York. The Uni-Power could alert Peter to major distant disturbances, especially events involving unusual amounts of physical or energetic activity. A massive storm developing far away or another unusually large disturbance could catch his attention, but he wasn’t passively aware of every emergency happening across the planet. He couldn’t identify every detail, and he couldn't respond to everything at once. The Uni-Power had expanded what Peter could perceive, but it hadn’t given him a reason to believe every problem in existence was now his responsibility.
That distinction mattered.
Peter had always wanted to help.
With this much power, Peter started believing that every problem belonged to him. Finally, there was no end to the things he could fix.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter spent the next few days trying to understand what the Uni-Power had actually given him. He didn’t have a manual, and the Enigma Force wasn’t explaining every ability ina way he could easily follow. Peter had to learn through experience, which meant starting with the things he already understood. He tested his strength, his flight, his energy manipulation and the strange control he now had over matter. The more he experimented, the clearer it became that the Uni-Power wasn’t simply making his existing abilities stronger. It was giving him an entirely different range of options. Captain Universe has traditionally possessed powers such as molecular manipulation, energy projection, flight, enhanced senses and force constructs, and Peter was beginning to discover those abilities for himself.

That created a problem Peter hadn't expected. His old Spider-Man powers had always encouraged him to think before acting because there were limits to what his body could handle. He could be injured, exhausted or overwhelmed. The Uni-Power changed those calculations. Peter could now fly directly to an emergency instead of spending time finding a route through the city. He could move objects that would have been impossible for him before. He could manipulate matter instead of relying entirely on physical force. When a damaged section of a building threatened to collapse, Peter could stabilize it almost immediately. When criminals tried to escape, he could stop them before they got very far. The work was still important, but Peter was starting to notice that the effort required from him had changed.

His patrols became shorter because he could respond to emergencies faster. Peter began checking police reports and emergency broadcasts before heading out, then using his expanded awareness to determine which situations actually required him. He wasn’t interested in replacing the police or deciding how every problem should be handled. He wanted to help people who were in immediate danger, just as he always had. The difference was that Peter now had the ability to intervene almost anywhere. That made restraint much harder. If he could prevent an accident several miles away, there was always a reason to do it. If he could stop a violent crime before anyone was injured, there was an argument for doing that too. The list never ended.

The temptation became personal when Peter realized what the Uni-Power could do for him. He was still living with the ordinary problems he’d had before becoming Captain Universe. He still had bills. He still needed to work. He still had responsibilities that couldn’t be solved by punching a supervillain. For the first time, Peter possessed the ability to change his circumstances almost instantly. His molecular manipulation could alter physical matter, and his energy abilities were far beyond anything he’d had access to before. Peter could have used that power to make his own life easier. He could have created wealth, built whatever technology he wanted and removed many of the practical problems that had followed him for years.
He didn’t.

Peter understood why that would be dangerous. The issue wasn’t whether he deserved to have a better life. The issue was what would happen once he started using cosmic power for his own convenience. There would always be another reason to justify it. He could improve his apartment, then his finances, then his equipment, then his entire life. Eventually, Peter would have to decide whether the rules applied to him at all. He had seen enough powerful people make that mistake to know where it could lead.

The bigger temptation was the rest of the world. Peter could see problems everywhere now, and some of them were much larger than anything he had dealt with in New York. He could imagine using the Uni-Power to dismantle weapons, interfere with conflicts or alter environments. He could potentially change the lives of millions of people without asking them what they wanted. Even if Peter believed he was helping, he would be making decisions for people who had never given him that authority. His intentions wouldn’t change the fact that he was imposing his own judgment on the entire planet.

That was where Peter drew the line. He would use the Uni-Power when someone needed immediate protection, but he wasn’t going to turn himself into the person responsible for controlling the world. Peter could still make mistakes. He could still misunderstand a situation. Having more power didn’t automatically make his judgment better, and Peter knew that better than most people. His responsibility was to use what he’d been given without allowing it to decide who he became.

For a while, that seemed manageable. Then the Uni-Power reacted to something Peter couldn’t identify. His awareness shifted away from Earth and toward deep space. He sensed a disturbance that was far beyond the normal activity of the Solar System. It wasn’t another robbery, accident or natural disaster. The scale was completely different, and the Enigma Force’s presence within Peter suddenly became much more focused.

The crisis that had brought the Uni-Power to Earth hadn’t been an accident. For this scenario, Peter’s bond with the Enigma Force gave him a limited awareness of the specific crisis it had selected him to confront: enough to sense its general direction and recognize when he was getting closer, but not enough to explain the problem or solve it for him. Peter had been chosen because something far beyond his neighborhood was approaching, and the closer it came, the more clearly that limited connection pointed him toward it. For the first time since becoming Captain Universe, Peter understood that the problems he’d been dealing with on Earth were only the beginning. The Enigma Force hadn’t come looking for Spider-Man because New York needed another superhero. It had come because a threat was developing that could affect far more than one city, one country or even one planet.
Peter looked toward the sky and realized that his new responsibility had finally arrived.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Peter left Earth after confirming that the disturbance was moving through deep space. The Uni-Power allowed him to travel far beyond anything his normal Spider-Man abilities could manage, and he quickly realized that the Solar System looked very different when he wasn’t limited to what could be seen from the ground. Planets, moons and fields of debris became obstacles he could navigate around with ease, while the expanded awareness granted by the Uni-Power helped him understand where the disturbance was strongest. Peter didn’t know exactly what he was looking for, but he could tell that something was interfering with the natural balance of the region.

The source was eventually revealed near the outer Solar System. A large concentration of energy had formed in space, creating distortions that were affecting nearby matter. Peter approached carefully and studied the phenomenon before making a move. He didn’t assume it was an enemy simply because it looked dangerous. His experience with the Uni-Power had already taught him that having the ability to act immediately didn’t mean he should. He needed to understand the problem first.

The Enigma Force gave Peter enough information to recognize the danger. The disturbance was part of a larger cosmic crisis, and if it continued unchecked, the effects could spread far beyond the area where it had first appeared. Peter couldn't identify every detail of what was happening, but he understood the important part. The event was growing, and the Uni-Power had chosen him because he was capable of intervening before it became something much worse.

Peter moved closer and began testing the edges of the disturbance. He used the Uni-Power to manipulate the surrounding matter and energy, looking for a way to contain the instability without making it worse. His first attempt failed. The energy pushed back against him and spread into the surrounding space. Peter immediately stopped and reassessed the situation. This wasn’t something he could solve by applying more force. The Uni-Power gave him extraordinary power, but Peter still needed to understand how that power interacted with the problem in front of him.

He changed his approach. Instead of trying to overpower the disturbance, Peter used the Uni-Power to create a containment field around the affected area. The construct held for several seconds before beginning to break apart. Peter reinforced it, then adjusted the structure again. Each attempt gave him more information. He wasn’t fighting a conventional opponent, and there was no simple target he could hit. He was trying to prevent a cosmic event from spreading, and that required control rather than brute strength.

Peter eventually found a way to stabilize the affected region. He redirected the excess energy into a controlled field and used the Uni-Power to restore the surrounding matter to a stable state. The disturbance began to shrink. Peter watched carefully, ready to intervene if it expanded again.

It didn’t. The immediate crisis was over, but Peter didn’t feel relieved. He could still sense something beyond the disturbance. The event he’d just contained hadn’t been the entire problem. It had been a symptom of something larger, and the Enigma Force had not yet released its hold on him.

Peter looked deeper into space and realized how far the consequences could reach. He had spent his life protecting one city, but the Uni-Power had given him a responsibility that extended far beyond Earth. The choice he’d been avoiding was becoming unavoidable. He could return home and continue being the Spider-Man he’d always been, or he could follow the crisis into the wider universe and find out what had caused it.
Peter chose to keep going.
He wasn’t abandoning Earth. He was making sure there would still be an Earth to return to.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Peter continued following the disturbance through the Solar System, but the farther he traveled, the less useful raw power became. The energy he had encountered wasn’t behaving like a normal physical object. It shifted whenever he interacted with it, spreading through space and changing its pattern whenever Peter tried to contain it. The Uni-Power gave him enough ability to manipulate matter and energy on an enormous scale, but Peter couldn’t simply force the entire phenomenon into submission. He needed to understand what was causing it.

That realization changed how Peter approached the crisis. He stopped treating the disturbance like an enemy and started treating it like a problem. He observed its movement, studied how it reacted to the Uni-Power and looked for a pattern. Peter had always relied on science when he was dealing with something he didn’t understand, and the fact that he now possessed cosmic abilities didn’t change that part of him. He still wanted to know how something worked before deciding how to fix it.

Eventually, Peter discovered that the disturbance wasn’t spreading randomly. At its center was a self-sustaining rupture in space that was drawing energy from high-energy regions around it. Each time the rupture reached another concentration of energy, it absorbed part of that energy and used it to expand, creating more instability and allowing the cycle to continue. Peter realized that if he simply followed it from one location to another, he’d spend the rest of his time reacting to the consequences. He needed to stop the feedback loop itself.

Peter used the Uni-Power to isolate the energy moving through the affected region. He created a series of force constructs around the disturbance, giving himself enough control to separate the unstable energy from the surrounding environment. The process required more concentration than he expected. The Uni-Power could provide the power, but Peter still had to decide where that power went. A mistake at this scale could affect everything around him. Peter managed to contain the disturbance long enough to study its source. What he found changed the situation completely. The energy wasn’t simply appearing from nowhere. Something beyond the Solar System was interacting with the region, creating the instability from a distance. Peter couldn't see the source clearly, but the Enigma Force could recognize the pattern.
The crisis was connected to something much larger.

Peter understood why the Enigma Force had been searching for a host. It hadn’t brought him to space because it needed someone to perform a single rescue. It had brought him here because the problem was continuing to grow, and stopping it required someone who could operate on a scale far beyond Earth.
Peter followed the signal.

The journey took him farther than he’d ever traveled before. The Earth became a distant point behind him, and eventually even the Solar System felt small. Peter had spent most of his life looking at the universe from the perspective of one city. Now he was moving through it himself. That experience changed his perspective. Every new world he passed contained people who had their own problems, their own histories and their own reasons to keep going. Peter couldn't know all of them. He couldn't protect all of them. The Uni-Power had expanded Peter's reach. It hadn't expanded his ability to be everywhere at once.

Peter finally reached the source of the disturbance and found the rupture feeding the entire chain of instability. The energy building around it was being pulled into the same feedback loop he had traced through the Solar System, and the longer it remained connected to those surrounding energy sources, the greater the chance that the damage would spread.

Peter didn’t have a perfect solution. He had to make one. He began by isolating the rupture from the external energy sources feeding it, using force constructs and the Uni-Power to cut off the flow without releasing the accumulated energy into the surrounding systems. Then he redirected that excess energy away and used his control over matter and energy to stabilize the affected region around the rupture. The process was slow compared with the other things he'd accomplished since becoming Captain Universe, but Peter didn’t rush it. He adjusted his approach whenever the energy shifted and continued until the rupture could no longer sustain its own expansion. Once the feedback loop lost the energy feeding it, the instability collapsed and the surrounding space stabilized. The crisis was over.
He kept working until the disturbance finally collapsed.
The surrounding space stabilized. The crisis was over.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Peter returned to Earth with a different understanding of what the Uni-Power meant. He had gone into space expecting to find something he could overpower, but the crisis had required patience, judgment and restraint. The power itself had never been the difficult part. Peter could do things that had once been outside the limits of his abilities, but having the ability to change something didn’t mean he understood the consequences of changing it. That lesson stayed with him as he crossed the distance back toward Earth.

The planet looked different from space. Peter had seen it countless times in photographs and through the windows of aircraft, but the view was different when he was standing above it with nothing separating him from the vacuum. There were no borders visible from where he was. The cities were points of light, and the problems that seemed enormous when he was standing in the middle of New York became impossible to distinguish from one another. For the first time, Peter could see the scale of what the Enigma Force had been asking him to consider.

His awareness still reached far beyond anything he had experienced before. Major disturbances across enormous distances could still enter Peter’s awareness, and some were serious enough that he could have intervened. He wasn’t monitoring every emergency on Earth, but each large event he did notice made the temptation to keep looking farther outward much harder to ignore. If he could reach a major disaster on the other side of the planet without much difficulty, why would he stay in New York?
That question followed Peter home.

He returned to his apartment and tried to continue his normal routine. It didn’t work. The Uni-Power was still with him, and Peter could still sense things that were happening far beyond the city. His old life had always required him to divide his attention between work, personal responsibilities and being Spider-Man. Now major disturbances anywhere in the world could periodically become part of that calculation. Peter could spend every hour chasing the large crises that entered his awareness and still find another one eventually demanding his attention.

For a while, he considered embracing it. He could travel anywhere almost immediately. He could respond to disasters before emergency services arrived. He could use the abilities of Captain Universe to protect people on a scale that Spider-Man had never been capable of before. The idea was difficult to reject because Peter's first instinct was always to help. If he had the means to prevent suffering, refusing to use them felt almost selfish.

But Peter also understood that there was a difference between helping someone and deciding how everyone should live. The Uni-Power gave him extraordinary control over matter and energy, but it didn’t give him perfect judgment. Peter could stop a war by destroying weapons, but he couldn't know what political consequences would follow. He could interfere with a natural disaster, but he couldn't predict every effect that intervention might have. He could impose his idea of a better world on everyone around him, but that would make him responsible for every decision they were no longer allowed to make for themselves.

Peter had spent enough time around people with enormous power to understand how easily that line could disappear. It would start with something reasonable. Preventing one disaster. Stopping one dangerous person. Making one decision because there wasn’t enough time to wait for anyone else. Then another decision would follow, and another. Eventually, Peter would be deciding what was best for them.
That wasn't what he wanted Spider-Man to become.

Peter's answer was to keep the Uni-Power focused on situations where his intervention was genuinely necessary. He would protect people from immediate threats, respond to crises that required abilities nobody else possessed, and step in when the consequences of doing nothing were too severe to accept. Outside of those situations, he would leave people room to make their own decisions. It wasn’t a perfect rule, but Peter knew that no rule could be perfect when the person enforcing it had his level of power.

The arrangement worked for a while. Peter continued helping people around New York while remaining aware of the wider universe. He became more comfortable with the abilities, and the Uni-Power stopped feeling like something he was borrowing from a stranger. It responded to his thoughts naturally, allowing him to move through the air, manipulate matter and generate energy without the effort those abilities would have required from an ordinary person.
Then the Enigma Force showed Peter something he hadn't expected.
It wasn’t another disaster.
It was a choice the Enigma Force was briefly allowing him to make.

Peter understood that the crisis which had brought the Uni-Power to him had been resolved. The immediate reason for the bond was gone, and normally the force would move on to another host in need. This time, however, the Enigma Force did not immediately sever the connection. Peter could feel that it was briefly permitting the bond to continue if he accepted that responsibility, rather than leaving the Uni-Power in his possession by right. Peter had known from the beginning that the connection was temporary. What he hadn't expected was how difficult it would be to decide whether to let that final opportunity pass.

For the first time, Peter could imagine what his life would look like if he kept the power. He could protect Earth from threats before they reached it. He could travel beyond the planet whenever something required his attention. He could become the kind of protector who watched over an entire civilization rather than a single neighborhood. There was a real argument for staying with the Uni-Power, especially when Peter knew how many people could benefit from having someone like him available.

He had stopped thinking about his own life. His apartment had become a place he returned to between emergencies. His work was something he squeezed into whatever time remained. Even when he was standing in New York, part of his attention was somewhere else, listening for another crisis. Peter was beginning to understand that becoming responsible for everything would eventually mean becoming responsible for nothing in particular.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Peter didn’t make the decision immediately. He spent another night moving through New York, paying attention to the parts of the city he had started overlooking since becoming Captain Universe. The Uni-Power made it easy to focus on distant threats because they were larger and harder to ignore, but Peter found himself drawn back toward ordinary problems. A shop owner dealing with a break in. A family waiting for help after an accident. Someone who had simply ended up in the wrong place at the wrong time. None of these situations required the power of Captain Universe, yet Peter still wanted to be there when they happened.
The Enigma Force remained with him while Peter came to that conclusion. It didn't need to convince him to stay, and Peter didn’t need to prove that he was worthy of the power. The
Uni-Power had already served its purpose. The crisis that had brought it to him was over, and another host would eventually need it somewhere else.
Peter accepted that.
He allowed the connection to end.

The awareness that had followed him since becoming Captain Universe began to fade, and the universe no longer felt as though it was pressing against the edges of his mind. His ability to manipulate matter and generate cosmic energy disappeared with the Uni-Power. Flight disappeared with the Uni-Power, and Peter immediately felt gravity take over.

Peter reacted on instinct and fired a web toward a nearby building. The line caught, and he swung downward before redirecting himself toward the roof of his apartment building. His landing wasn't graceful, but it was familiar. Peter stood there for a moment and looked at his hands, making sure everything had returned to normal.
His Spider-Sense was still there. His strength was still there. The Uni-Power was gone.

Peter felt relieved. For a short time, Peter Parker had been capable of protecting people on a scale that went far beyond anything Spider-Man had ever been asked to handle. He had seen worlds from a distance, dealt with a crisis that stretched beyond Earth and experienced what it was like to have enough power to change almost anything around him. None of that had made him stop caring about the person in front of him.
If anything, it had reminded him why he cared in the first place.

Peter went back inside his apartment and returned to the routine he’d had before the Enigma Force arrived. There were still bills to deal with, work to worry about and plenty of unanswered questions about what his life was supposed to look like after everything that had happened. The problems felt ordinary again, which was exactly what Peter wanted.

Later that night, his Spider-Sense alerted him to trouble a few blocks away. Peter grabbed his mask and headed outside. He didn’t need the Uni-Power to know where he was going. He knew the neighborhood, knew the streets and understood what could happen if nobody intervened. He reached the scene and stopped the crime before anyone was seriously injured. The situation wasn't important enough to attract the attention of the Avengers or any cosmic force. It wasn’t going to affect another planet. Nobody would write a history book about it.
Peter still stayed until he knew everyone was safe.
That was enough.
Peter simply didn’t need to stay there.

He belonged on the ground, where he could see the people he was protecting and understand what they needed. The universe could find another champion when the next cosmic crisis arrived. Peter Parker had a different responsibility waiting for him in New York, and for the first time since receiving the Uni-Power, he was completely comfortable with the fact that it was enough.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Peter expected things to return to normal once the Uni-Power was gone. In some ways, they did. He could no longer sense events happening across distant parts of the universe, and he couldn't manipulate matter or move through space without relying on his usual abilities. New York became his focus again, and the problems he encountered were familiar. At the same time, Peter knew that his experience with the Enigma Force had changed how he viewed his responsibility as Spider-Man.

He had spent a short period with enough power to intervene almost anywhere. That experience made Peter more aware of the difference between having the ability to help and actually being responsible for every problem. He couldn’t be everywhere, and he didn’t need to be. The people around him had their own lives and their own choices, and protecting them didn’t mean taking control of those things. Peter could offer help when someone needed it and step back when they didn't.

There was also the question of what his experience meant for the wider universe. The Uni-Power had been connected to Peter, and whatever cosmic forces were capable of sensing it could have become aware that a human from Earth had served as its host. Peter didn’t know which beings had noticed, and he had no reason to assume they were all friendly. He couldn't even be certain that the Enigma Force was finished with him forever. The force had moved between hosts throughout its history, and Peter understood that another crisis could eventually bring it back.

That possibility didn't frighten him as much as it once would have. Peter had already experienced the responsibility that came with the Uni-Power, and he knew that accepting it didn’t require him to stop being himself. If the Enigma Force ever returned, Peter would deal with that situation when it happened. Until then, he had a city to protect and a life to rebuild.

The experience also changed the way Peter looked at his own abilities. Before becoming Captain Universe, he had spent years trying to understand where the limits of his powers were. Afterward, he understood that power itself was never going to answer the questions that mattered most. Strength could stop a dangerous person. Speed could get him to a disaster faster. Cosmic abilities could even allow him to confront threats affecting entire worlds. None of those things could tell Peter what the right decision was.
That part would always be his responsibility.

Peter continued his patrols, but he stopped thinking of them as small compared with what he'd experienced in space. A robbery in Queens wasn't less important simply because Peter had once dealt with a cosmic crisis. A person trapped inside a damaged building didn’t become less deserving of help because Peter had once been capable of protecting an entire planet. The scale had changed, but the reason Peter put on the mask hadn't.
Weeks passed.
