Homelander would catch him there. The fight would be short because there’s no reason to pretend Wade suddenly has an answer for someone that strong. Homelander could break him apart badly enough that moving becomes almost impossible, but Wade would already have ruptured the storage system and ruined the samples before getting caught.

Instead of trying to prove he can kill him, Homelander could take Wade high above the city and throw him as far away from the tower as he can. Wade would eventually regenerate wherever he lands, but he’d be gone long enough for Vought to regain control of the building and for The Boys to disappear with the evidence.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Vought would survive the scandal because companies that large don’t disappear in one night, but the story would be much harder to bury than Wade's earlier comments. People have recordings of the broadcast, copies of the medical files are already outside Vought’s control, and several escaped subjects can identify themselves in the treatment records.

The company would try blaming rogue researchers and claim senior leadership never approved the experiments. Wade would respond by releasing pieces of his old contract and medical paperwork showing how early Vought started collecting his samples, which keeps the story alive every time the company tries moving past it.

Wade would be fine with that arrangement. He could work with them when a target deserves it, disappear for weeks when somebody offers him a completely unrelated mercenary job, and occasionally show up at their hideout with information nobody asked him to obtain. Hughie would probably become the person most willing to answer his calls, while Butcher would develop the habit of checking whether Wade is carrying explosives before letting him inside. Vought’s relationship with him would be finished in a different way. They can’t market him anymore because Wade has become directly connected to one of their ugliest scandals, and studying him again would require catching someone who now understands exactly what they want from him. Any future attempt would need to account for the fact that Wade will happily destroy his own body if that is what it takes to make containment harder.

Homelander would also approach him differently after the tower. He already knows Wade poses almost no serious threat in a direct fight, so future encounters wouldn't be about proving who is stronger. He’d be more likely to trap Wade somewhere remote, use people around him as leverage, or remove him from a situation before Wade can turn it into another public disaster. Wade would understand that too. His healing factor lets him survive Homelander, but survival only helps if he can eventually get back into the situation. Being buried underground, launched miles away, or locked somewhere without an exit can take him off the board without killing him. That leaves them with a much stranger rivalry than either of them expected. Homelander has finally found someone he can destroy physically without getting the permanent result he wants, while Wade has found someone he can’t beat with his usual mix of guns, swords, and refusing to stay down.

By the end, Wade would have carved out his own place in The Boys universe without joining either side. Vought tried turning him into a product, The Boys tried figuring out whether he was useful enough to tolerate, and Homelander learned that overwhelming strength doesn’t always make a problem disappear.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Deadpool would never become the strongest person in The Boys universe, and he wouldn't need to. What makes him dangerous there is that Vought can’t contain him forever, Butcher can't reliably control him, and Homelander can tear him apart for no reason.

Wade would end up in the weird space between all of them, taking jobs when he feels like it, helping The Boys when their targets overlap, and making Vought regret ever putting him in front of a camera.
And for Homelander, that might be the worst part. Wade just has to survive long enough to keep coming back.

scripts.title: What If Denji Became Ghost Rider

sections.name: INTRO
paras: A dumpster is a horrible place to die. Denji spent his entire life paying off debt and hunting devils for the Yazuka. The mobsters eventually betrayed him. They chopped him to pieces and left his remains to rot under the control of the Zombie devil. Denji died with absolutely nothing.
But Pochita sacrificed his own existence to fix that body. The small devil became Denji’s heart to give his only friend a second chance. That contract created Chainsaw Man.
But Pochita wasn't the only thing waiting in the dark.

The Spirit of Vengeance was drawn to Denji at the moment Pochita rebuilt him. Denji had spent his entire existence being exploited by the people in power, dying with years of cruelty left unanswered. For this Spirit, that made him a compatible host.
When Denji pulled the starter cord in his chest, the chainsaws tore through his skin just like they were supposed to.
Except this time, the metal caught fire.

His human face burned away, leaving a flaming skull in its place. The undead mob inside that warehouse thought they were dealing with a helpless kid. Instead they locked themselves in a room with a monster that burns souls. Denji woke up hoping for a second chance at a normal life, but the new entity sharing his body only wanted to punish the guilty.
PART 1 Denji woke with Pochita’s pull cord sticking out of his chest.

His body had been rebuilt around Pochita’s heart, but the warehouse around him was still full of the Yakuza members who had torn him apart. The Zombie devil watched from behind them while its new servants crowded closer, expecting the boy in the dumpster to stay dead.
Denji pulled the cord.

Chainsaws tore from his head and arms just as they did after Pochita became his heart, but something else came with them. Fire ran across the moving chains without damaging the metal. It spread over Denji’s shoulders and face, burning hot enough that the closest zombies hesitated before reaching him. Parts of his transformed face had changed as well. Beneath the machinery and torn flesh, exposed bone glowed through the flames.

Denji didn’t understand any of it. He had never seen Hellfire, knew nothing about Spirits of Vengeance, and had no reason to stop and figure it out while dozens of zombies were trying to kill him again.
He attacked.

The original Chainsaw Man had already been strong enough to tear through the Zombie devil’s army. Now every swing carried additional heat. Zombies that tried to grab his arms were cut apart before they could hold him down. Others caught fire when they came too close to the burning blades. The warehouse filled with blood as Denji forced his way through the mob toward the devil responsible for the attack.
The Zombie devil tried to bury him beneath its followers. Denji kept moving.

When several zombies dragged him to the floor, a length of metal suddenly snapped out from the flames around his arm. Denji barely had time to register it before the chain wrapped around one of the attackers. He pulled instinctively and sent the zombie crashing into the others.
That was the first sign the fire had brought more than heat. Denji tried the motion again. The chain responded.
The devil eventually became the only target left that mattered.

Denji reached it and tore into its body with the same relentless attack that had overwhelmed it in the original timeline. Hellfire spread across the cuts as the chainsaws opened its flesh. The added damage shortened the fight considerably, but the devil still died because Denji physically destroyed it. The flames did not erase it from existence, burn away its soul, or bypass the normal rules governing devils. They simply gave Denji another way to hurt it.
Once the Zombie devil stopped moving, Denji’s transformation began to fade. The chainsaws withdrew. The fire disappeared with them. The strange chain was gone as though it had never existed.
Denji was left standing among the bodies with no explanation for any of it.
He understood Pochita. Pochita had become his heart and given him another life.
The fire was different.

He could still feel something somewhere beneath his own thoughts, distant enough that he couldn't make sense of it. It carried an anger that did not feel like his. Denji had hated the Yakuza for what they did to him, but whatever had awakened alongside Pochita had reacted to them with something much stronger.
Before Denji could think about it for long, Public Safety arrived.

Makima entered the warehouse expecting to find the result of the Zombie devil incident. Instead, she found a living teenager surrounded by dead zombies and the remains of a devil, with evidence of a transformation that did not fit neatly into anything she had encountered there.
Denji noticed her for a much simpler reason.
She was the first person who looked at him after his resurrection and did not immediately try to kill him.

Makima approached him carefully. Denji was exhausted, hungry and still trying to understand why he was alive. Whatever strange presence had reacted so violently to the Yakuza stirred again when she came closer, but this time Denji had no idea what it was responding to.
He ignored it. Makima offered him food and a place within Public Safety. For Denji, that was enough.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Makima brought Denji into Public Safety because the Chainsaw devil inside him was already unusual enough to justify close observation. The fire made him even harder to classify. Denji could explain Pochita becoming his heart, but he had no explanation for the burning transformation or the chain that had appeared during the Zombie devil fight. Makima did not reveal how much that interested her. She simply kept Denji close and gave him exactly what he had spent most of his life without: regular meals, clean clothes, somewhere warm to sleep, and a reason to believe his life had finally improved.

He was assigned to work with Aki Hayakawa, whose patience with him disappeared almost immediately. Their personalities were incompatible, and Denji had little interest in the discipline or larger purpose Aki attached to devil hunting. Denjji still treated the job like work. He wanted food, money and whatever reward Makima might offer him next. Becoming stronger had not suddenly given him a heroic worldview.
That became obvious when Power entered the team.

Power offered Denji exactly the kind of deal he understood. If he helped rescue her cat, Meowy, she would let him touch her chest. Denji followed her without thinking much further than that. He did not know she was leading him to the Bat Devil or that she intended to trade him for Meowy’s life.
The betrayal only became clear once they reached the devil.

Power handed Denji over, hoping the Bat Devil would return her cat. Instead, the devil rejected Denji’s blood and turned on Power as well. It swallowed both Power and Meowy, leaving Denji to deal with a situation that had started as a crude personal bargain and had become something much worse.
Denji transformed.

The chainsaws returned first. Hellfire followed a moment later, spreading unevenly across the blades rather than covering his entire body as it had during the Zombie devil fight. Denji still had very little control over when the fire appeared or how much of it he produced. He only knew that it made every hit against the Bat devil more destructive.

The Bat devil was physically stronger than the enemies Denji had faced before joining Public Safety. It could fly, tear through buildings and attack from a distance. Denji compensated the same way he always did. He stayed close, accepted damage that would have stopped an ordinary hunter, and kept cutting whenever he had an opening.
The new chain appeared again when the Bat devil tried to gain distance.

This time Denji recognized the sensation before it happened. He threw out his arm and the burning chain extended from the fire around him, wrapping around one of the devil's limbs. Denji used it to pull himself closer rather than letting the bat devil escape into the air. The technique was crude, but it worked.
He eventually tore the devil apart and freed Power and Meowy.
The Spirit wanted the guilty punished.

Denji did not yet understand what that meant, and he had no interest in becoming responsible for judging everyone around him. Power had lied to him, used him and nearly gotten him killed, but Denji still did not want to hurt her once the fight was over. He was annoyed with her. He also understood why she had done it. She had been trying to save the only creature she cared about.
That difference mattered.

For the first time, Denji resisted the pressure instead of following it. Power survived, Meowy survived, and Denji returned with both of them. From the outside, it looked like another successful devil hunt. Makima saw something more useful. Denji’s second power didn’t respond only to devils, and Denji didn’t appear to be fully in control of it.
She now had another reason to keep watching him. PART 3

Denji’s next major assignment brought him into a hotel with Aki, Power, Himeno, Kobeni and Arai. What looked like a routine devil hunt turned into something much worse once the group realized they couldn't leave the 8th floor. The stairs looped back to the same hallway, the windows led nowhere useful, and even the clocks stopped moving. They’d been trapped inside a space controlled by the Eternity devil.

The group spent hours trying to understand the trap. Aki searched for a way out while Himeno kept everyone focused as long as she could. Kobeni deteriorated quickly under the pressure, especially once the Eternity devil revealed what it wanted. It would release everyone else if they killed Denji and gave it his heart.
That offer immediately changed the room.

Denji had already spent most of his life around people who were willing to sacrifice him when it became convenient, so the situation wasn’t particularly surprising. He also understood that the Eternity devil wanted Pochita specifically, even if he didn’t yet understand why the Chainsaw devil mattered so much to other devils.

Kobeni eventually snapped and lunged to attack Denji while Arai held him down. Aki threw himself in front of the blade to take the blow instead. If the Eternity devil could keep regenerating, then Denji could keep cutting it.
He jumped into the exposed mass of flesh and transformed.
Hellfire changed the amount of damage he could inflict, but it didn’t replace that cycle.

The flames appeared across his chainsaws once the fight had already begun. Denji had started getting better at recognizing the sensation that came before them, although control was still inconsistent. This time he managed to keep the fire concentrated around the blades instead of letting it spread across his entire body.
The Eternity devil regenerated every wound. Denji kept opening new ones.
That was exactly the kind of fight he was built for.

Hours passed. The others could hear Denji fighting from inside the hotel while the Eternity devil’s screams became increasingly desperate. Himeno eventually realized that Denji had created a closed system. As long as the devil kept bleeding, Denji had something to drink. As long as Denji could restore himself, he could keep cutting.
The strange presence inside him became stronger as the fight continued.

Denji noticed it every time the Eternity devil begged him to stop. The Spirit wanted him to continue. There was no confusion this time about whether the target had done something wrong. The Eternity devil had trapped 6 people, tried to convince them to murder Denji, and intended to kill them if its plan failed.
For once, Denji and the thing inside him wanted the same result.

The burning chain appeared again during the later stages of the fight. Denji used it more deliberately now, hooking into sections of the Eternity devil’s body and pulling himself through the mass whenever it tried to push him away. He still wasn’t graceful with it. Half the time he used the chain like an extension of his own reckless fighting style, dragging himself straight toward whatever he wanted to cut next.
Eventually the Eternity devil couldn't tolerate the pain any longer. It exposed its heart and begged Denji to kill it. Denji did.

The hotel returned to normal once the devil died, and the trapped hunters were finally able to leave. Denji had spent roughly 3 days fighting without meaningful rest, surviving by consuming the Eternity devil’s blood as he tore through it.
The victory mattered for another reason.
Makima would eventually notice that difference. So would the Spirit. PART 4

The attack on Public Safety began while Denji, Aki, Himeno and Power were eating together. The man sitting across from them was connected to the Yakuza Denji had killed during the Zombie devil incident. He was also the grandson of Denji’s former boss.
Denji barely had time to understand why he was there before the man pulled a gun and shot him in the head.

The restaurant erupted into chaos. Power reacted immediately, but the attack was part of a much larger operation. Across Tokyo, Public Safety hunters were being targeted at the same time. The people behind it knew where the division would be and had prepared specifically for them.

Aki survived the initial shooting and confronted the attacker outside. The man revealed that he was another hybrid, with the Katana devil serving as his heart. Aki used the Fox devil against him and then resorted to the Curse devil when that failed. The attack brought Katana Man down, but only temporarily.
Akane Sawatari restored the situation almost immediately.

Katana Man transformed again and overwhelmed Aki before he could recover. Himeno was already badly wounded by then. She understood that Aki was about to die. The Ghost devil's normal arm wasn't enough, and she was seconds away from offering everything she had in exchange for enough power to stop the attack.
In the original timeline, she eventually offered everything. This time, Denji woke up first.

The Spirit had already reacted to serious injuries before, but this was the first time Denji had been unconscious while it happened. The gunshot hadn't permanently killed him because Pochita’s heart still allowed him to recover, but he hadn’t received blood and nobody had pulled his starter. The Spirit couldn't replace either of those things. It could only force Denji's damaged body to move for a moment.
The change came from the other presence inside him.

Heat spread through his body before he opened his eyes. The bullet wound in his head remained, and the Spirit wasn't healing it. Fire moved around the injury as his fingers twitched against the floor. The Spirit forced just enough movement through his arm for his hand to find the cord in his chest.
Denji pulled it. The transformation interrupted the fight before Himeno could make that final sacrifice.

Chainsaws tore from Denji’s head and arms as Hellfire rolled across the blades. The bone beneath his transformed face burned brighter than it had during the Eternity devil fight. Denji didn’t stop to understand why the Spirit had brought him back into the fight. He saw Aki on the ground, Himeno disappearing piece by piece, and Katana Man standing between them.
Denji decided that was ensuhh and charged.

Katana Man was faster and far more experienced than the enemies Denji had fought before. His attacks could cross the distance between them almost instantly, cutting through Denji before he had time to react. Denji still took the first hit badly. His torso opened and he crashed into the street.
The difference was that Katana Man couldn’t end the fight with one clean attack anymore.

Denji’s chain snapped out before Katana Man could create distance. It wrapped around his arm and forced both hybrids back into close range. Denji used the chain less like a weapon and more like a way to keep the fight ugly. Every time Katana Man tried to reset and use his speed, Denji dragged him back toward the chainsaws.
Sawatari tried to intervene with the Snake devil.

Denji didn’t kill it outright. Doing that would’ve created consequences he had no reason to understand yet, and he was too focused on Katana Man to chase Sawatari once she backed away from the immediate fight.
Katana Man eventually made another attempt to rush him. This time Denji was ready enough to catch him.
The burning chain wrapped around his torso and stopped the attack before Katana Man could finish it. Denji pulled him close, expecting another chance to use the chainsaw on his head.
Something else happened instead.
For a moment, Denji couldn’t move.
The fire around his skull changed. The Spirit took control of the transformation just long enough to force Katana Man to look directly into the burning sockets beneath Denji’s chainsaw-covered face.
The Penance Stare activated for the first time.

Katana Man didn’t experience anything his grandfather had done. The Spirit judged him for his own actions. The people he’d helped hurt, the violence he’d personally committed, and the suffering created by the attack on Public Safety were forced back onto him at once.

Denji didn’t see any of it. He only saw Katana Man stop fighting. The effect lasted seconds, but when it ended, Katana Man collapsed and couldn't immediately transform again. Denji had no idea what he’d done. He hadn’t chosen the attack and didn’t understand why staring at someone had suddenly ended the fight.

The Spirit released control as quickly as it had taken it. Denji reverted soon afterward. Himeno was still alive. Katana Man was down long enough for the surviving Public Safety hunters to secure him before he could recover, while Sawatari used the confusion to escape. The ambush had still devastated Public Safety, but the attackers no longer got the chance to abduct Denji or regroup for the same second confrontation that happened in the original timeline.

She hadn’t escaped unharmed. She had already sacrificed part of herself before Denji returned to the fight, and that damage wasn’t something Ghost Rider could simply reverse. But Denji’s intervention happened early enough that she never had to surrender her entire body to the Ghost devil.

Aki didn’t lose the person who had spent years working beside him. Himeno remained part of the division, badly injured and forced to deal with the consequences of how close she had come to sacrificing everything. Denji and Power also returned to an apartment and team that hadn't been hollowed out by her death. Her injuries from the ambush kept her away from front-line operations while the division reorganized.
Makima would have to account for that change. She also had a second problem.

Denji had just demonstrated an ability that didn’t behave like a chainsaw, Hellfire or anything Public Safety could easily classify. Katana Man had been physically capable of continuing the fight until Denji looked at him.
After that, he wasn't.
Makima now had proof that whatever lived alongside Pochita could attack something deeper than the body.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: The Katana Man attack left Public Safety badly damaged. Several hunters were dead, others had resigned, and the surviving divisions were reorganized under Makima. Katana Man had been captured during the ambush instead of escaping with Denji, while Sawatari remained the loose end Public Safety had to pursue. That meant the later assault and Denji's second fight with Katana Man never happened in the same way. Denji understood very little about the larger operation behind the attack. What stayed with him was the moment Katana Man stopped fighting.
Denji hadn’t cut him apart. He hadn’t burned him. He had looked at him, and something inside Denji had done the rest.
That bothered him more than he expected.
He also hadn't been the one deciding when to use it.

Himeno survived the ambush, but recovery took her out of active field work. Denji had returned before she could offer her entire body to the Ghost devil, so the contract that killed her in the original timeline was never made. Her existing injuries were still severe enough to keep her away from the front line, and even after she recovered enough to remain with Public Safety, she shifted toward supporting and training the surviving hunters instead. That kept her alive without placing her directly into every operation that followed. Her presence still changed Aki’s life immediately. He wasn’t dealing with her death on top of everything else Public Safety had lost, and his focus shifted toward protecting the people he still had around him instead of carrying the same grief that had followed him in the original timeline.
Denji noticed the change without really knowing what to call it. Aki was still strict, still irritated by both him and Power, and still obsessed with the Gun devil. He just wasn’t as isolated.
For Denji, life returned to something almost normal again.

He ate at Aki’s apartment, argued with Power, went on assignments, and kept chasing whatever attention Makima offered him. That part of him hadn’t changed. Even after everything that happened during the ambush, Makima still represented the life he wanted. She had given hima home, work, food and affection when he’d had none of those things.
The Spirit continued reacting to her and Denji continued ignoring it. The difference was that he now understood the reaction wasn’t random.

The same pressure he had felt around Katana Man sometimes appeared when Makima was nearby. It wasn’t knowledge. Denji couldn’t suddenly see her past, identify crimes she had committed, or understand what she really was. He only knew that the presence inside him became restless around her in a way it didn’t around most other people.
Makima noticed Denji changing too.

She already understood his Chainsaw Man transformation well enough to recognize when something came from Pochita and when it didn’t. The fire, the chain and whatever had happened to Katana Man belonged to a second system. She began testing Denji without making the purpose obvious.

She watched how the fire responded during assignments. She paid attention to which enemies caused the Spirit to become more active. She observed whether Denji could summon the chain deliberately. Most importantly, she watched what happened when Denji chose not to follow the
pressure inside him.
Denji was slowly becoming better at resisting it. The Spirit wanted punishment. Denji didn’t always care.

That conflict became clearer whenever Public Safety dealt with humans rather than devils. Denji had grown up around criminals, debt collectors and people willing to hurt others for money. He didn’t divide the world neatly into good people and bad people. Sometimes he understood exactly why someone had done something terrible, even when the Spirit reacted as though understanding didn’t matter.
That difference started causing problems during transformations.
Denji learned to push back.

He couldn't remove the Spirit, and he still didn’t understand what it was, but he could refuse to let it decide every fight for him. The ability that ended Katana Man remained especially difficult. Denji couldn't activate it on command, and after seeing what it did, he wasn’t sure he wanted to.
That hesitation mattered more than any new attack.

The Spirit had chosen a host who had spent his whole life being told what to do by stronger people. The Yakuza had controlled his work. Makima now controlled almost every part of his new life. Denji wasn’t eager to accept another thing inside him deciding who deserved punishment.
For the first time since becoming Chainsaw Man, he started treating the Spirit as something separate from himself.

Makima reached the same conclusion. Whatever had bonded to Denji wasn’t simply another ability produced by Pochita. It had its own reactions, its own priorities and at least some ability to act without Denji’s permission.
That made it valuable. It also made Denji harder to control than she had originally expected.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Denji met Reze at a point when his life had started to feel stable. Public Safety was still dangerous, Makima still controlled most of his schedule, and the Spirit remained an uncomfortable presence inside him, but he finally had a routine. He had somewhere to live, people around him, and enough food that starvation was no longer the first thing he thought about every morning.
Reze disrupted that routine almost immediately.

She treated Denji with an ease he wasn’t used to. Their time together felt separate from Public Safety and separate from Makima. Denji liked that. He didn’t know she had been sent to take his heart, and the Spirit didn’t give him that information either.
It did react to her.

The reaction was weaker than what Denji felt around Makima, but it was there often enough that he noticed. He couldn't tell whether it meant Reze was dangerous, whether she had hurt someone, or whether the Spirit simply distrusted her. By then, Denji had already learned that the thing inside him could sense reasons for punishment without explaining them.
He chose to ignore it.
Denji wanted the relationship more than he wanted answers. That decision carried into the night Reze revealed what she really was.

Once she transformed into the Bomb devil hybrid, the Spirit’s reaction made sense. Reze had been trained as a weapon, and she was more dangerous than almost anyone Denji had fought. Her explosions could tear apart buildings, launch her through the air, and destroy Denji’s body faster than his normal regeneration could keep up without blood.

Hellfire gave Denji a way to keep pressure on Reze whenever she tried to create distance. His chains could reach farther than his biological chainsaws, and by this point he’d become good enough to use them without waiting for the Spirit to take over. He wrapped them around pieces of the environment, dragged himself through explosions, and occasionally caught Reze long enough to force the fight back into close range.

Explosions still tore him apart. Large enough blasts could separate limbs or leave him unable to move until he received blood. The Spirit made him harder to put down, but Reze was still capable of overwhelming him if he fought carelessly.
Denji fought carelessly anyway. The difference was that he now had more ways to recover from his mistakes.

During one exchange, the Spirit tried to push the transformation further. The fire spread from Denji’s chainsaws across his face, and he felt the same pressure that had come before the Penance Stare against Katana Man.
Denji resisted it.
He understood Reze had lied to him. He understood she had killed people and was trying to take his heart. He still didn’t want the Spirit deciding what happened to her.
That refusal became important once the fight reached its end.

Denji eventually used the sea to neutralize Reze’s explosions, following the same basic logic he reached in the original timeline. Water gave him a way to stop the battle without trying to overpower every explosion directly. His chains helped him hold onto her long enough to pull them both down.
When they surfaced, Denji had the chance to finish her but he didn't.

The Spirit wanted punishment, but Denji saw something else in Reze. She had been shaped into a weapon by people with more power than she had, just as Denji had spent most of his own life being used by the Yakuza and was now being directed by Public Safety. He didn’t excuse what she had done. He just couldn’t reduce her to the list of people she had hurt.
He let her go. Denji still wanted to run away with her.

For a short time, Reze considered doing the same. She eventually turned back toward the cafe where Denji was waiting. He had no way of knowing that. From his perspective, she had already chosen to leave. Makima intercepted Reze before she reached him.

Denji remained at the cafe with flowers, waiting for someone who never arrived. The Spirit didn’t warn him what had happened. It didn’t show him Reze’s death or identify Makima as the person responsible. Denji simply sat there until it became obvious Reze wasn’t coming.
Power eventually found him, and life moved forward. Denji told himself Reze had made her choice.

Makima allowed him to believe it. That lie became more dangerous now that the Spirit was part of him. Denji still trusted Makima enough to ignore every warning he felt around her, but the gap between what he believed and what she was actually doing continued to grow.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Denji’s growing reputation eventually drew attention from outside Japan. Foreign governments and assassins began targeting him for the Chainsaw devil’s heart, forcing Public Safety to increase his protection while several groups entered Tokyo at once.

The most dangerous threat came from Santa Claus. Through the Doll devil, civilians were turned into dolls and used to overwhelm the hunters. Denji could destroy individual dolls quickly with his chainsaws and Hellfire, but the Spirit couldn’t solve a fight where most of the attackers were victims being controlled by someone else.
The situation became much worse when Santa Claus used the hell devil to send the group to hell.
There, Denji encountered the Darkness devil.

The difference in power was immediate. The Darkness devil was a primal fear and overwhelmed the hunters before most of them could react. Denji’s arms were severed along with the others, and even after Beam gave him blood and restarted him, Ghost Rider’s power wasn’t enough to close the gap.

Denji attacked with burning chainsaws and managed to create light around himself, but the Darkness devil still tore through him. His chain couldn’t restrain it, and his regeneration couldn’t keep up with damage he could barely understand.
Makima eventually entered hell through Princi and confronted the Darkness devil long enough for the surviving hunters to return to Earth.

Back in Tokyo, Santa Claus had consumed flesh from the Darkness devil and become much stronger. Darkness now increased her power, so Denji covered his transformed body in hellfire and used the light to weaken that advantage while fighting through the dolls surrounding her.
Even then, he couldn't finish the battle by himself.

Santa Claus remained connected to her dolls and could continue through them. Denji’s power helped him survive and keep pressure on her, but Cosmo was ultimately the one who ended the threat by overwhelming Santa Claus’s mind with her ability.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Aki was killed during the Gun devil incident, and the Gun devil took over his corpse as a fiend. When he reached Denji’s apartment, Denji was forced to fight someone who still looked like his friend even though Aki was already gone.

Ghost Rider made Denji stronger, but it couldn’t restore a corpse or remove the devil possessing it. Denji ended the fight faster than he did originally, but the result stayed the same. Aki died, and Denji was left carrying the guilt.

Makima used that grief to pull him closer. Denji stopped trusting his own decisions and became even more dependent on her. Then Power arrived at Makima’s apartment with Denji’s birthday cake. Makima killed her in front of him.
That finally exposed what Denji had refused to see. Makima had built his new life around people he cared about, then destroyed those relationships to break him and separate him from Pochita.

The Spirit reacted to Makima more strongly than ever, but it couldn’t simply undo what she had done. Denji was still devastated, and Makima’s control over him came from months of manipulation rather than one supernatural attack.

When Denji eventually fought back, he didn’t rely on the Penance Stare. Makima’s contract with Japan’s Prime Minister redirected attacks against her onto Japanese citizens, and Denji had no way to know whether attacking her mind or soul would avoid that contract.

Instead, he used the weakness that defeated her in the original timeline. Makima was obsessed with Chainsaw Man and barely recognized Denji himself. Denji used Pochita as a distraction, approached Makima without being noticed, and struck when she thought Chainsaw Man was somewhere else.
He eventually consumed Makima, treating the act as love rather than an attack and preventing her contract from protecting her in the same way.
The Control devil later reincarnated as Nayuta. Kishibe brought her to Denji, who agreed to raise her.
Denji was still bonded to the Spirit of Vengeance, but he no longer treated its judgment as something he had to obey. Pochita had given him another life so he could pursue his own dreams.
Denji intended to keep choosing those dreams for himself. OUTRO Denji becoming Ghost Rider wouldn’t suddenly turn him into a perfect hero. He’d still be
impulsive, selfish, desperate for affection, and willing to make terrible decisions for very simple reasons.
The difference is that he’d have another force inside him constantly pushing toward punishment.

That would make him stronger, but it would also make his life harder. In the end, Denji’s biggest victory wouldn't be destroying Makima or mastering hellfire. It would be refusing to let another powerful being decide what his life was supposed to become.
Pochita gave Denji another chance to live and Denji would make sure that life still belonged to him.

scripts.title: What If Doctor Doom Was In The Boys

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Doctor Doom landing in The Boys universe wouldn’t be a normal superhero arrival. He’d see Vought ads everywhere, watch Homelander being sold as the most powerful man alive, and probably figure out within a day that most of it is manufactured image.

What would actually interest him is Compound V. A drug that can create powers, change biology, and build an entire class of superhumans would be far more important to Doom than getting into some pointless argument with The Seven.

Once he starts looking into Vought, he’d find the labs, the experiments, the money, and the way the company controls almost every Supe it creates. That's where the problem starts, because Vought would eventually realize Doom isn’t another Supe they can sign or scare into line.
He’d be studying them long before they understand what he is.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: This would be standard Earth-616 Doctor Doom from before he became Sorcerer Supreme, with his normal armor, personal magic, and the equipment he usually carries. He wouldn't have Latveria, his army, or his full labs waiting for him. The crossover could happen through one of Doom’s dimensional experiments going wrong and throwing him into another universe. He’s dealt with alternate realities before, so once he realizes the world around him doesn’t match his own, he’d start figuring out where he landed instead of wasting time trying to force his way back immediately.

He’d arrive in New York early in Season 3, when Vought still controls most of the Supe business and Homelander is the biggest name in the country. The events that follow would unfold over the next several weeks as the Season 3 situation changes around him. Doom’s armor would tell him quickly that something is off. Latveria doesn’t exist, none of the governments or organizations he knows show up in the right places, and there’s no trace of the Fantastic Four, Avengers, or anyone else from his world. What he does find everywhere is Vought.

Doom would start with the obvious information first. News reports, public records, Vought’s own marketing, government contracts, interviews with Supes, and anything else he can pull from local networks. He’d see that Vought controls far more than movie deals and sponsorships. The company manages the people with powers, decides what the public hears about them, and has been building relationships with politicians and the military for years.

The powers themselves would catch his attention pretty quickly. Homelander can fly, use heat vision, and take punishment that would kill most people. A-Train has super speed. Starlight can absorb electricity and throw it back as energy. The Deep has permanent physical changes that let him survive underwater. Doom would start comparing all of them and looking for where the powers came from, because there’s too much variety for it to look natural.

He’d find something strange in the timelines. A lot of major Supes had connections to Vought long before the public knew who they were. Some medical records would be missing. Other files would point toward private hospitals and programs that don’t have much public information attached to them. Doom wouldn’t know the name Compound V yet, but he’d already have a good reason to think Vought was creating these people somehow.

He’d need a place to work, so he’d take over an empty industrial building outside the busiest part of the city and turn it into a temporary lab. Most of the equipment around him would be far behind what he normally uses, but Doom can build around that. His armor already carries compact fabrication and robotics tools meant for field repairs and improvised construction, giving him enough of a technological seed to bootstrap better scanners, stronger power systems, and eventually simple Doombots from local components.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Doom would follow Vought’s medical shipments because they're easier to track than the people themselves. Public labs and hospitals would only show part of the picture, but private storage sites and late-night transports would tell him where the company keeps the material it doesn’t want anyone asking about.

He'd spend a few days watching 1 of those routes with Doombots before touching anything. That gives him the timing, the guards, the cameras, and the exact type of storage being used. The transport would look more like a medical shipment than a weapons convoy, which would tell Doom the cargo needs to stay cold and stable.

Once he’s sure, he’d take the shipment without turning the whole thing into a huge fight. A Doombot could block the road, disable the vehicle, knock the guards out, and move the cases somewhere else before Vought has time to send anyone important. Doom would get the blue serum back to his lab and finally have Compound V in front of him.

That’s where he’d spend most of his time. The first thing he’d notice is that the formula doesn’t produce the same result in everyone. Vought can use the same basic drug and end up with people who have completely different powers, which means the V is changing far more than 1 part of the body. Doom would start breaking it down, testing small samples, and looking for recurring biological effects involving growth, healing, energy output, and the nervous system. He wouldn't expect a few stolen cases to explain the entire formula.

The randomness would annoy him because Vought has been working on this for decades and still accepts outcomes they can’t predict well. Doom would see the company as having something extremely valuable without fully understanding how to control every result, but solving that problem would require far more than a few days of testing.

He wouldn’t inject himself. Doom already has armor, magic, and enough power to deal with most of this world without changing his body. He’d test the formula on tissue, small lab samples, and anything else that lets him watch how the V reacts without putting himself in the middle of the experiment.

That would make him want more data. The first shipment only tells him what the drug looks like outside a person. He’d need samples from different Supes, records from adult trials, and anything Vought has on people who reacted badly.

So the thefts would continue. Sometimes a Doombot would take a case from a transport. Other times Doom would get into a lab system and have the doors open before the staff even understands what happened. He’d stay away from Vought Tower for now because there are easier places to get the same information with less attention.

Vought would still notice after enough V starts disappearing. The company keeps close track of the drug because almost nobody outside the system is supposed to know it exists. Once several shipments go missing in ways that don’t look random, the security side of Vought would start trying to figure out who’s taking them.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The first problem Vought would have is that the footage doesn’t make much sense. Several sites would show what looks like the same armored person, but the timing wouldn't line up. A figure could be seen at 1 warehouse and then another location too quickly for Vought to believe it's the same person.
They'd eventually realize some of what they’re seeing is robotic.

That would make the situation more serious because Vought is used to dealing with Supes, criminals, and people stealing company information. An unknown person building advanced robots and targeting Compound V is a different kind of problem.

Doom would already know they’re looking for him. He’d have access to enough of their internal systems to see what security teams are searching for, what footage they’ve collected, and which Supes are being considered for the job.

He’d let them find 1 Doombot on purpose because he wants to see what they do. Black Noir would make sense as the first person Vought sends. He doesn’t talk, he can move quietly, and Vought uses him for work it doesn’t want turning into a public mess. Noir could track the Doombot into an empty building and attack it before anyone else is around.

The fight would give Doom a useful look at him. Noir is fast, strong, and keeps fighting after damage that would stop most people. He’d tear pieces off the Doombot and keep closing the distance, while the robot sends everything it sees back to Doom in real time.

Doom would use the fight like a test. He could have the Doombot block, fire back, and measure how much force Noir can take before slowing down. Once he has enough, the robot could destroy the parts Doom doesn’t want recovered and shut itself down.
Vought would get scraps of metal and a few damaged systems, but nothing that gives them a clear address or a way to copy what Doom built.

The next move would probably come through Vought’s business side. They'd try reaching him instead of sending another Supe into an unknown situation. Doom could get an offer for a private meeting, access to Vought labs, money, protection, and a place in the company’s hero lineup.

He’d take the call because the conversation itself gives him information. The people talking to him would keep asking about the armor, where it came from, how it works, and whether he’d agree to medical testing. Doom would hear pretty quickly that they’re more interested in the technology than the person wearing it.

He’d keep them talking long enough to see what they already know. They know he’s been taking Compound V. They know some of the armored figures are machines. They still don’t know where he came from, and they don’t know what he’s doing with the serum.

That’s enough for Doom. He’d leave the conversation with a better picture of how Vought handles something it can’t control. They offer money first, then access, then pressure. If that fails, they send someone stronger.
Doom would go back to the lab and keep working because he knows the next person they send is probably going to matter more than Black Noir.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Homelander would get involved once Vought tells him there’s an armored man stealing Compound V, building robots, and refusing every offer they've made. That alone would get under his skin because he’s used to people changing the way they act as soon as he enters the room.

The meeting would happen in public enough that neither side has much reason to start destroying the area. Vought could arrange a hero appearance near a place where Doom has been seen before and wait to see whether he comes close.

Doom would show up because he wants a direct look at Homelander after spending days working through footage and files. He already knows the basic powers, but seeing someone in person gives him better readings than any old video can.
Homelander would start by getting close and trying to read him. He’d look at the armor, use X-ray vision, and try to figure out whether there’s anything inside the suit that tells him who Doom is.
Doom would’ve planned for that after learning what Homelander can do. The armor would block the scan well enough that Homelander doesn’t get a useful look inside.

That alone would make the conversation more tense. Homelander could grab Doom’s shoulder or squeeze the armor while talking, expecting some kind of reaction. Doom’s shield would take the pressure, and his suit would record the force at the same time. He’d let Homelander give him exactly the kind of reading he came there to get.

Doom wouldn't waste the meeting trying to prove he’s stronger. He has enough experience with powerful people to know that starting a fight before he finishes his work doesn’t help him. He’d keep the conversation focused on Vought, Compound V, and why Homelander still follows a company that made him.

That question would bother Homelander because it goes straight at something Vought tries to keep buried. Homelander sees himself as above everyone else, but he still spends most of his life tied to the company that created and sold him.

Doom would understand that weakness very quickly. Homelander would also understand that Doom isn’t reacting the way most people do around him. That wouldn’t make him attack on the spot, because Vought still wants the armor and whatever research Doom has done on Compound V. It would make the next meeting much harder to keep calm.

Doom would leave with direct scans of Homelander’s strength, heat output, movement, and whatever else the armor can pick up. Once he gets back to the lab, he’d compare those readings with the Compound V samples he already has.
That gives him a much better idea of what Vought’s best result looks like.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Butcher would start hearing about Doom through the same mess Vought is trying to hide. Compound V shipments have gone missing, Black Noir got sent after an armored target, and Homelander met someone Vought won't talk about publicly.
They wouldn’t find Doom’s main lab quickly. He’d already covered the area with false records, cameras, and Doombots, and he’d see them looking long before they reach him.

Once Doom knows who they are, he’d let them reach a smaller location he can control. He’d already have a basic file on the group by then. Butcher’s history with Homelander, Hughie’s connection to A-Train, MM’s family history with Vought, Frenchie’s technical background, and Kimiko’s exposure to Compound V would all be easy enough to piece together once he knows where to look.

Kimiko would be the most useful to him scientifically because this meeting would happen after Soldier Boy's blast in Russia left her without her powers. With Butcher and Frenchie allowing it, Doom could scan her directly and compare her current cells with what he already knows about long-term Compound V exposure. A living Supe whose powers worked before the blast and then stopped gives him far more useful evidence than another bottle of serum sitting on a table.
Butcher would get to the point quickly. He’d explain what Vought does when nobody’s watching, what Homelander is really like, and where some of the company’s hidden operations are.

Doom would listen because Butcher knows things that don’t exist in clean company records. He knows witnesses Vought never documented, off-book facilities, personal habits and vulnerabilities the company never bothered to put in a database, and which people inside the company have been paid to cover things up.
That would immediately get Butcher interested because a more reliable version of V could be used against Homelander.
Doom wouldn't give it to him. He’d know exactly what Butcher plans to do with it, and he has no reason to hand over research he’s still working on.

They could still trade information. The Boys give Doom off-book locations, witnesses, and names he hasn’t found in Vought’s systems, and Doom gives them enough warning to stay away from certain Vought sites while he’s working there. He wouldn’t join the team, and Butcher wouldn't trust him enough to treat him like one of them anyway.

After they leave, Doom would start checking the locations Butcher mentioned against what he already has from Vought. A few would match old files. Others would point to places Vought hid even from parts of its own staff.
Those locations would give Doom the next thing he needs, more samples, more records, and a better look at the strongest Supes Vought has ever made.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: The new locations from Butcher would give Doom much better research than the stolen shipments ever could. Over the next several weeks, he’d combine those leads with stolen Vought files on people who survived adult exposure, people who died from it, and Supes whose powers changed over time. He still wouldn't completely solve Compound V, but he could identify recurring biological features across V-enhanced subjects and start designing countermeasures around those common points.

Kimiko's condition would give Doom the breakthrough he needs. By comparing his scans of her post-blast biology with his existing Compound V samples and Vought research, he could look for a physical difference that appears only after Soldier Boy's attack. If his tests indicate that active Compound V in her cells has been damaged or can no longer sustain the same biological effects, that gives him a specific vulnerability to target instead of just knowing that Soldier Boy can remove powers. This would still be Doom's inference from the evidence, not a mechanism the show explicitly explains. He wouldn't be recreating Soldier Boy's blast itself. Before building a weapon, Doom could expose Compound V-altered tissue samples to controlled combinations of radiation and energy, adjusting them until he reproduces the same kind of cellular disruption he measured in Kimiko. Only after producing that effect repeatedly in the lab would he scale the successful energy profile into an experimental pulse designed to target the same vulnerability in a living Supe.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Vought would eventually run out of patience once enough Compound V, research, and internal data disappear. They'd also start realizing that Doom is building countermeasures from the formula rather than simply stealing it. Once their scientists see altered test samples and specialized equipment around the sites he’s hit, the situation becomes much more serious.

The company would probably try to take his lab instead of killing him outright. Ashley and the rest of Vought leadership would want the armor, the research, and whatever he’s done to Compound V. Homelander would care far less about the science, but he’d be happy to be the person sent in once everyone else has failed.

Before that happens, Vought would use whoever is still available and loyal. By this point in Season 3, Starlight has broken publicly with Vought, Black Noir has disappeared after learning Soldier Boy is back, and Maeve is being held inside Vought Tower. That leaves A-Train and The Deep as the obvious Supes to send with Vought tactical teams and security personnel, even if neither is an ideal answer to Doom.
Doom would know they’re coming because he’d see the operation forming through Vought’s own network. He’d have time to move the most important research, set traps, and leave Doombots behind.

A-Train would be the hardest person for the robots to track at first because of his speed. Doom would handle that by changing the building rather than trying to make a Doombot faster than him. Doors could slam shut ahead of him, floors could become electrified, and narrow halls could fill with barriers that force him to slow down or change direction.

The tactical teams would get farther by working methodically behind the Supes, but Doom would have planned for ordinary armed personnel long before they arrived. Doombots, sealed sections, gas, automated defenses, and false routes could keep them occupied without forcing Doom to expose the equipment he actually cares about.

The Deep wouldn't matter much once the fight moves indoors. Vought could still break into parts of the lab eventually because A-Train, Deep, and enough tactical personnel attacking together can get through some of Doom's setup, but they wouldn't find what they came for. Most of the real research would already be gone, and the machines left behind would be there to waste their time.

Doom would use that attack to confirm how Vought's remaining loyal Supes and tactical teams move under pressure and how much they actually coordinate. He'd see pretty quickly that A-Train and Deep rely heavily on their individual powers while the human teams are operating around them. That becomes useful once Doom starts planning for Homelander.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Doom wouldn't attack every remaining Vought asset at once if he can avoid it. He has enough information by now to deal with the people still coming after him separately, without turning the city into a battlefield.

A-Train would be dangerous in open space because of his speed, so Doom would force him somewhere narrow. A Doombot could draw him into a building, then Doom could trap the exits and use sensors that track movement across the whole room instead of trying to follow him with normal eyesight. Once A-Train is forced to slow down, Doom can hit him with something strong enough to knock him out without needing a long fight.

The Deep would be much easier to neutralize once Doom gets him away from open water. Doom wouldn't need a specialized anti-Supe duel for him; restraints, Doombots, or magic would be enough to remove him from the fight while Doom stays focused on the threats that actually matter.

Vought's tactical personnel wouldn't change that balance either. Doom could disable or trap them without killing everyone, especially once their Supe support is gone. He'd care more about removing the people who can interfere with his work than proving he can beat every Vought operative in public.

Some of Vought's people could be left injured or restrained, especially if they stop fighting once the operation falls apart. Doom's goal would be to dismantle the response around him and force Vought toward the one confrontation he actually wants to study: Homelander.

Butcher would probably be watching all of this closely because the situation is moving in the direction he wanted. The problem is that Doom is taking control of more Vought research every time he wins.

Butcher would start wondering what happens after Homelander is gone. Frenchie and Hughie would probably have the same concern. Doom now understands enough about Compound V to exploit recurring weaknesses Vought never turned into weapons, has countermeasures built around Supe biology, and can manufacture machines that most of this world has no answer for.
The Boys would still want Homelander dead, but they'd be much less comfortable with Doom holding everything that comes after.
Doom wouldn't care. He’d already be focused on the last person Vought can send who has any chance of stopping him.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Homelander would come for Doom once Vought's attempts to raid him fail and the Supes still available to the company start getting beaten or removed from the fight. At that point, it becomes personal for him. Doom has ignored Vought, taken their secrets, embarrassed their heroes, and spent the entire time treating Homelander like a problem he can solve.

Homelander would probably attack first and attack hard. He'd use speed to close the distance immediately and try to overwhelm Doom before anything complicated can happen. Doom would enter the confrontation with layered force fields already active and calibrated from the strength, heat, and movement readings he collected during their first meeting. The point of letting Homelander strike those defenses would be to refine Doom's measurements, not because Doom needs to discover whether his armor can survive him.

The first few attacks would give Doom the refinements he wants. He'd already studied Homelander from their earlier meeting and prepared around those readings, so the armor could log what changes when Homelander is genuinely trying to kill him while Doom keeps the fight contained behind defenses built to handle far greater threats.

Homelander would use heat vision once brute force gets him nowhere. Doom could block it with his shields, redirect some of the energy, or use magic to move out of the line of fire. At that point, Homelander's speed would still deserve Doom's attention, but the exchange would be functioning more like a live test than a fight Doom is barely surviving.

Once Doom has enough data, he'd start dismantling the matchup. His normal energy weapons and magic already give him ways to hurt, restrain, or control Homelander, but Doom would still save the Compound V weapon for a deliberate experiment. He'd want to know whether the biological weakness he found in Kimiko can be reproduced against Vought's strongest result.

Homelander's speed would remain the one part Doom has to track carefully, especially if he tries to change angles faster than Doom can physically turn. But Doom's sensors, pre-calibrated shields, and magic mean speed alone doesn't turn Homelander into an equal opponent.
Once Homelander gets close enough for the controlled test Doom wants, Doom could trigger the first V based weapon.

A focused pulse built around the Compound V disruption Doom identified from Kimiko's post-blast scans could hit Homelander at point-blank range. Doom wouldn't know beforehand whether that mechanism would work on someone as powerful as Homelander, and it wouldn't be the same thing as Soldier Boy's blast. If the pulse works at all, the goal would be to disrupt Homelander's powers briefly rather than strip them away in 1 shot.

If Homelander’s heat vision weakens for a few seconds, his strength dips, or his body takes longer to recover from the next hit, Doom would know the experiment reached the same vulnerability. His armor could immediately analyze the size and duration of that response, then adjust the pulse’s output and timing around how quickly Homelander recovers. Doom would use that first opening to hit him with everything else at once.
A heavy energy blast could send Homelander through a wall. Magic could hold him in place long enough for another shot. Doom could keep hitting the same area instead of spreading damage around.

Homelander would get back up because he can take a huge amount of punishment. Once Doom confirms the experimental V based pulse affects him and calibrates it from that first response, he could use the adjusted version whenever Homelander gets close enough. Repeated exposure could make it harder for Homelander’s body to keep working at full power, and that gives Doom more room to use the rest of his weapons.
The fight would get worse for Homelander the longer it lasts because Doom can change tactics while Homelander keeps coming back to the same basic tools: strength, speed, flight, and heat vision.

Doom could eventually put him down with his normal combination of shields, energy weapons, and magic, using the V based pulse to weaken Homelander further once the experiment proves it works rather than treating the pulse as the only thing making victory possible.

He wouldn't need to kill him right away. Doom would probably keep Homelander alive long enough to study exactly how the altered Compound V affects him. That gives Doom 1 last piece of information Vought never had, because they spent years trying to make Homelander stronger while Doom was looking for the parts of him that can fail.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: With Homelander defeated, Doom could immediately turn back to dismantling the infrastructure that made him possible. Any lab that's producing unstable V could be shut down or emptied before Vought has time to move it.

Butcher would want the remaining Compound V destroyed. Doom wouldn't agree to that because he’d see useful science in it. He’d already proved that Vought’s version contains biological patterns that can be understood and exploited more precisely than Vought ever managed, and throwing away everything would make no sense to him.
That would create a new problem between Doom and The Boys.

Butcher would see a man who now has the same kind of research Vought used to build Homelander, except Doom has already found ways to weaponize weaknesses Vought overlooked. Hughie would probably be even more worried because Doom has never pretended he wants to make the world fair or democratic.
Doom could give The Boys enough information to expose Vought publicly, but he wouldn’t hand over the research itself. He’d keep the formulas, his own changes, and whatever he learned from Homelander.

He’d also make sure Vought can’t rebuild the same system quickly. Production equipment could be destroyed, key servers copied and wiped, and several hidden facilities exposed at once. Politicians and executives who relied on Vought keeping everything secret would suddenly have much bigger problems.

Doom wouldn't take over Vought and start wearing their logo. He’d have no interest in becoming another celebrity Supe or running a company built around commercials and approval ratings. He’d build something of his own. If he still can’t return to his universe, Doom would start creating a new base with the technology and research he took. Doombots could replace the temporary machines he built at the beginning, and the Compound V research would become 1 more part of a much larger system under his control.
The world of The Boys would lose the company that spent decades deciding which Supes become famous and which ones disappear.
In its place, there’d now be Doctor Doom.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Doctor Doom would be a nightmare for Vought because he’d understand what keeps the company powerful before he ever tries to fight its strongest people. Compound V gives him the information he needs, and weeks of stolen Vought research give him enough data to build weapons around recurring weaknesses in the Supes they created.
Homelander would still give him the hardest fight, especially with his speed and strength, but Doom has too many ways to change the matchup once he has time to study him.
By the end, Vought would be broken, Homelander would be beaten, and Doom would leave with the one thing he cared about most from the start, control over technology Vought never fully understood.

scripts.title: What If Gojo Became A Devil Hunter

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Gojo becoming a devil hunter would be a problem for almost everyone in Chainsaw Man, because most devils are built around fear and Gojo has spent his whole life fighting things that ordinary people can barely understand.

He'd enter this world with Infinity, the Six Eyes, and all of his usual techniques, but the bigger issue wouldn't be whether he can kill devils. It would be what happens once someone like Gojo starts working around public safety and gets close enough to see how Makima handles Denji, Aki, and Power.
Because Gojo is already used to powerful people hiding things behind authority, and Makima would have very little room for someone she can't easily control.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Gojo would arrive during the early Public Safety era, around the time Denji has only recently started working with Aki and Power. At first, the world would feel familiar enough that he’d probably assume the monsters around him are some kind of curse. That idea wouldn't last long once he actually fights one.

The Six Eyes would make it clear that devils aren’t running on cursed energy. Gojo could still tead their movement and understand what they’re doing in a fight, but the power behind them would be different from anything he deals with in jujutsu society. He’d kill the first weak devil easily, then start asking why normal people can see these things and why some humans are using powers connected to them.

He'd learn the basics pretty quickly. Devils are born from fear, stronger fears create stronger devils, and devil hunters can make contracts in exchange for power. That would immediately separate this world from his own because Gojo still has all of his normal abilities and doesn't need a contract to use any of them.

Once he starts helping during devil attacks, Public Safety would hear about him fast. Reports of someone stopping attacks before they can touch him and killing devils without any known contract would stand out, especially because nobody can connect him to an existing organization or devil.

Gojo would probably cooperate when Public Safety approaches because they clearly know more about this world than he does. He'd want access to their information, while they'd want to know what he is and where his abilities come from.

That would be enough to bring Gojo into Public Safety's orbit without making him one of their normal employees right away. He’d be willing to help kill devils, but the people running the organization would quickly realize that giving him orders is going to be much harder than getting him interested.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Once Public Safety brings Gojo in, the first problem is figuring out what he actually is. He has no devil contract, no record with any government group, and no known connection to a fiend or hybrid, yet he can stop attacks before they touch him and kill devils without using anything their hunters recognize. That would make him useful, but it would also make people nervous because public safety is used to understanding where power comes from.

Gojo would explain enough to keep things moving. He could tell them that his abilities come from cursed energy and that curses in his world are born from negative emotions. The idea would sound familiar to them because devils are also tied to human fear, but Gojo would make it clear that they are not the same thing. He would also explain that his abilities belong to him and do not come from some deal he made with another creature, which would be the part Public Safety finds hardest to understand.

They would probably test Infinity first because it is the easiest ability to see. A controlled shot, a knife, or even a weak devil trying to hit him would stop before reaching his body. Gojo would not need to give them a full lesson on Limitless for them to understand the important part. Most normal attacks are useless against him, and nobody in the room has a simple answer for getting around it.

Makima would offer him work because keeping Gojo close makes more sense than letting him move around Tokyo on his own. Gojo would accept because Public Safety has information he needs and a steady stream of devils he can learn from. He would help with missions and follow enough rules to avoid creating problems, but everyone would understand pretty quickly that he is not going to act like a normal employee.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Gojo would probably meet Aki first because Aki is the kind of person Public Safety could trust to watch someone unpredictable and report everything clearly afterward. Their personalities would clash almost immediately. Aki takes the job seriously because he has seen what happens when hunters make mistakes, while Gojo jokes around even in situations where everyone else is tense.

Aki’s opinion would change once they actually fight together. If a devil rushes Gojo and stops before reaching him, then gets crushed or pulled apart with Blue a moment later, Aki would understand that Gojo is relaxed because he has a real reason to be. He would still find him annoying, but he would stop treating the attitude like carelessness.

Denji would probably like Gojo much faster. Gojo would talk to him like a normal teenager instead of treating him like a weapon that happens to have a human face. He would not care that Denji turns into Chainsaw Man or that Public Safety sees him as something dangerous. What would stand out to Gojo is how little Denji expects from life and how easily basic food, a place to sleep, or a little attention can control what he does.

He would understand why hunters make those deals because many of them have no other way to fight. What he would question is how normal Public Safety makes it seem. Giving up years of your life or parts of your body just to stay useful would remind him of the way jujutsu society sends young sorcerers into dangerous situations and expects them to accept the damage as part of the job.

Gojo would start spending more time around Denji, Aki, and Power because he would see the same kind of problem he has seen before. They are all useful to the organization, but that does not mean the organization is looking out for them the way it should. He would not suddenly become their parent or start giving speeches about it, but he would pay attention when they are being pushed too far.

Makima would notice that relationship developing because Denji is especially important to her. The closer Gojo gets to him, the harder it becomes for her to be the only person Denji looks to for approval.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Smaller devil attacks would become much easier once Gojo is working with Public Safety. He could handle threats that normally need several hunters, which means fewer people die on missions where he is present. Public Safety would start sending him toward the worst situations because they know he has the best chance of walking out afterward.

The Eternity devil would be one of the first situations where raw strength does not solve everything immediately. Being trapped inside the same floor over and over is different from having something physically attack him. Infinity can stop the devil from hitting him directly, but it does nothing by itself to fix the space around the group.

Gojo would spend time figuring out what the devil is controlling and whether the loop has a point where the space connects back into itself. The Six Eyes could help him study what changes every time they move through the floor, while everyone else tries to stay calm. Having Gojo there would probably stop the group from turning on Denji as quickly because there is someone in the room who clearly believes they can survive long enough to work it out.

Denji could still end up solving the problem in the most Denji way possible by throwing himself into the devil and cutting it apart until it gives up. Gojo would let him do it once he understands the idea because Denji can heal through blood and the plan actually makes sense with the Eternity devil's ability. He would also be there to keep the others safe if the devil starts attacking them while Denji is inside it.

Watching Denji fight like that would stick with Gojo afterward. Denji has almost no sense of what amount of pain should make him stop because his entire life has taught him to accept suffering if he gets something out of it. Gojo would understand that this is bigger than him being reckless, and he would start watching more closely whenever Public Safety pushes him toward something dangerous.

The Katana Man attack would create a much bigger change. Public Safety still gets hit across Tokyo, and Gojo cannot protect every hunter at once, so the attack would still cause serious damage. The people fighting beside him would have a much better chance of surviving because gunfire, blades, and most direct attacks cannot reach him normally.

If Gojo is close to Aki and Himeno when the attack starts, Himeno may never need to give her entire body to the Ghost devil. Gojo could stop Katana Man with Blue, hold him in place long enough for Aki to move, or attack Sawatari before the Snake devil finishes the fight. Himeno surviving would change Aki’s path because one of the losses that pushes him deeper into revenge never happens.

That would also be the first time Gojo directly changes a death that was supposed to happen in the original story. Public Safety would see him as even more valuable after that, while Makima would have to start thinking about what else might change if he stays close to Denji and the others.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: After the Katana Man attack, Makima would have enough information to understand that Gojo creates problems beyond simple strength. He can keep people alive in situations where they would normally die, and that changes the way the people around him behave. Aki has Himeno, Denji has another adult he can trust, and Power has someone around who treats her like a person even when she is being ridiculous.

That matters because Makima gets a lot of control from knowing what people want and making herself part of the path toward getting it. Denji is the clearest example. He wants affection, food, comfort, and some kind of normal life, and Makima has been giving him small pieces of those things whenever she wants him to move in a certain direction.

Gojo would not immediately understand the full plan, but he would notice how Denji changes around her. Denji talks about her differently than he talks about anyone else, accepts dangerous work when she is involved, and rarely questions why she wants something. Gojo would probably tease Denji about the crush at first, then get more serious once he sees how useful that crush is to Makima.

Makima would start learning more about Gojo at the same time. She could send him on missions involving different kinds of devil abilities and watch how he handles them. One mission might involve a direct physical attack, another could involve an effect that changes the environment, and another could test whether he can protect several people at once.

Makima would also have to think carefully about using her own power on him. Gojo does not see her as someone above him, which makes ordinary authority and manipulation much less useful, but that alone would not protect him from the Control Devil. Her supernatural control depends on whether Makima herself can regard the target as inferior to her, and it is unclear how she would ultimately categorize someone as abnormal and powerful as Gojo. That would make their dynamic very different from the one Makima has with most people around her.

She would have more success going through the people Gojo cares about. Denji, Aki, and Power can still be hurt, moved around, or sent into dangerous situations, and Gojo cannot stay beside all three of them every second. Makima would remember that even if she does not act on it right away.

Gojo would start feeling more uncomfortable around her for his own reasons. She always seems to know more than she should, people obey her with very little pushback, and some devils react to her with a level of fear that does not fit an ordinary Public Safety officer. None of that gives him the full answer yet, but it gives him enough reason to start paying attention.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Gojo would begin with simple questions because he has no reason to confront Makima before he understands what he is looking at. He could ask Aki how long he has worked under her, what he knows about her past, and whether anyone else has ever held the same kind of authority inside Public Safety. Aki would probably defend her because he trusts the organization and has worked under her long enough to see her as part of it.

Power would give him a different kind of answer. She would be much more willing to admit that Makima scares her, even if she cannot explain why.
