Gojo would take that seriously because Power is a fiend and has instincts around devils that humans do not. If she is terrified of someone everyone else keeps calling an ordinary government officer, that is worth remembering.

He would check records next. Someone with Makima’s position should have years of reports, promotions, assignments, and people who worked with her before Denji arrived. If most of that history is missing, locked away, or vague enough that nobody can give him a straight answer, Gojo would start treating that as part of the evidence instead of a coincidence.

Makima would eventually hear that he is asking questions, but she would have no reason to confront him right away. She could keep him busy with missions outside Tokyo and limit how much information he can reach without making it obvious that she is blocking him. Gojo would notice the change in his assignments and become more careful about what he asks in front of people who report directly to her.

By this point, he would know enough to stop treating Makima like another strange boss inside Public Safety. He still would not know that she is the control devil, but her missing history, the fear she creates in devils, and the way people behave around her would give him a real reason to believe she is hiding something much bigger than a normal contract.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Once Gojo is already suspicious of Makima, the next major change would come from what happens to Aki and Power. In the original story, both of them become part of the path Makima uses to break Denji, and Gojo being around makes that much harder because he would notice how often the people closest to Denji are being pushed into situations they may not survive.

Aki would still keep chasing the Gun devil because that goal has been driving him for years, but Himeno surviving would already change how far he is willing to go. He would still hate the Gun devil and still be willing to risk himself, but he would have someone close to him constantly reminding him that throwing his life away is not the same as getting revenge. Gojo would probably add to that by questioning why Aki keeps giving up pieces of his future for contracts when he finally has people around him who care whether he comes back.

The Future devil contract could still happen, but Aki might approach it differently. If he learns that he’s going to die badly, Gojo wouldn't treat that prediction like something fixed just because a devil said it. He has already spent his life dealing with techniques that can predict or limit outcomes, and he would probably see the future as information rather than a sentence. Aki might still accept the contract because he needs the power, but he would now have someone around him constantly looking for ways to stop that future from happening.

The Gun devil incident would become the point where Gojo has to stop reacting to Makima and start acting before she does. If he learns that Aki is being sent into something connected to the Gun devil, he would want to know exactly who approved it and why. By this point, he would already suspect that Makima is setting up situations for reasons Public Safety is not being told, so he would not simply accept that Aki is going because the mission needs him.

If events still move toward Aki becoming the Gun fiend, Gojo would have a much better chance of stopping the damage before Denjji is forced to kill him. The moment Aki’s body changes, Gojo could use Infinity to keep him away from everyone else and Blue to control where he moves. He would also be able to protect Denji from the attacks while trying to understand whether Aki is still somewhere inside.

The fight would still be tragic because Aki is not acting like himself anymore, and Gojo would understand quickly that this is not something he can solve by simply beating him harder. Gojo could use his exceptional perception to study the physical changes in Aki’s body and look for anything he can interrupt, but the Six Eyes would not automatically reveal how a devil power works when it is not using cursed energy.

There is no guarantee he could save him, Chainsaw Man does not give an easy way to reverse someone becoming a fiend, and Gojo should not suddenly have a technique that solves every rule of the world. What changes is that Denji would not have to handle the entire situation alone.
If Aki still dies, Gojo would be there to stop the fight from turning into the same emotional collapse Makima wanted.

Power’s death would become even harder for Makima to arrange. If she tries to bring Power to Denji the same way she does in canon, Gojo is already watching both of them and would have a reason to be nearby whenever Makima suddenly wants one of them alone. She would need to separate Gojo from Denji first, which means the plan around Power has to change instead of simply playing out the same way.

That would probably be the moment Gojo finally understands that Makima is not just hiding information. Too many of the people Denji cares about keep ending up exactly where she needs them to be, and by now Gojo has enough pieces to stop treating that as coincidence.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Makima would know that Gojo is becoming a serious problem because his strength is only part of what makes him dangerous to her. He keeps people alive, gives Denji another person to trust, and asks questions that Public Safety normally gets away with avoiding. As long as he stays close to Denji, breaking Denji the way she wants becomes much harder.

She would probably start by moving Gojo away from Tokyo under a real excuse. A powerful devil could appear somewhere else in Japan, and Gojo would be the obvious person to send because he can handle something that might kill several normal hunters. The mission would not need to be fake because Makima has enough control over assignments to use a real threat for her own purpose.

Gojo would go if civilians are actually in danger, but he would stop assuming the timing is innocent. By this point, he would tell Aki, Denji, and Power to contact him directly if anything strange happens while he is gone. He might even leave one of them with a way to reach him outside normal Public Safety channels because he no longer trusts information to move through Makima first.

That would make isolating them harder, so Makima could start controlling the people around Gojo instead. A hunter he trusts might suddenly give him bad information, a report could send him to the wrong location, or someone who had been helping him with records could abruptly deny helping him, change their story, or start repeating Public Safety’s position instead. Gojo would notice those gaps because his memory is good enough to track what people told him before.

If someone who was helping him suddenly reverses their behavior without a clear reason, Gojo would immediately start considering coercion, surveillance, or some kind of supernatural control. That would bring him much closer to the truth because he already knows Makima has some kind of power she is hiding.

Gojo’s perception could still help without giving him a supernatural answer. He might notice subtle changes in the way affected people behave, but because Makima’s power is not using cursed energy, the Six Eyes would not reveal some external influence or identify the exact mechanism. The behavioral pattern would only give him more reason to suspect that Makima’s control is not just social or political.

Makima would realize he is getting too close and could try a more direct test. She might order him to do something that goes against his instincts, such as leaving Denji behind during a dangerous mission or handing over someone he believes is being used. Gojo would refuse if the order makes no sense, which would confirm that normal authority has almost no effect on him.

That would also tell Makima that controlling him through the same kind of relationship she has with other hunters is not working. Gojo does not see her as superior and has no desire to earn her approval, so her social leverage is weak. Her supernatural Control is a separate question because it depends on whether she can regard Gojo as inferior to herself, something neither of them has tested yet. If she cannot rely on ordinary manipulation, she needs another way to contain or remove him.

Gojo would probably understand the danger before she acts openly. He would start keeping Denji and the others closer, and he would stop telling Public Safety everything he discovers. That would create a quiet split inside the organization where Gojo is still taking missions but no longer trusts the people assigning them.

At some point, Aki would have to decide whether he believes him. That could become important because Aki has spent years trusting Public Safety and Makima. If Gojo shows him enough evidence that information is being manipulated, hunters are behaving as if they are being controlled, and missions are being arranged around Denji, Aki would finally have a reason to question the person he has been following.

That would give Denji something he never had in canon. Instead of being surrounded by people who only understand pieces of Makima’s plan, he would have Gojo and Aki comparing what they know before the worst part happens.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The confrontation would start once Gojo has enough evidence to strongly suspect that Makima is directly controlling people and decides he cannot safely leave Denji and the others under her authority. He would not need to know every detail about her identity before acting because the pattern would already be clear. Hunters are showing unexplained changes in behavior, devils are afraid of her, Denji is being moved through events that keep isolating him, and Makima has been trying to learn Gojo’s abilities since the day he arrived.

Gojo would probably confront her somewhere away from Denji and the others because he would not want them caught in the middle. He would also assume she has some way to attack them if she feels cornered, so Aki, Denji, and Power would need to be moved somewhere Public Safety cannot easily reach first.

Her first real problem would be Infinity. A direct attack that has to travel through space would have the same issue as anything else trying to reach Gojo. Bullets, physical force, and many obvious attacks would stop before touching him, so Makima would need to rely on abilities that do not work through normal contact.

That is where the fight becomes dangerous for Gojo. Makima has attacks that work through conditions and control rather than simply throwing something at the target. She can use other people, force contracts through those under her control, and attack from places Gojo may not be able to see. Infinity is incredible defense, but it is not a general answer to every supernatural effect in Chainsaw Man.

Gojo would still have a major advantage in direct combat. Blue could drag Makima into positions she does not want to be in, Red could tear through her body, and Hollow Purple could destroy huge amounts of matter if he decides there is no other option. The problem is that Makima’s contract with the Japanese prime minister makes killing her normally almost useless because fatal damage is transferred into illnesses and accidents affecting Japanese citizens.

Gojo would notice that problem quickly if he kills her once and she simply comes back. That would force him to stop attacking blindly because every extra death could be hurting innocent people somewhere else. He would need to understand the contract before he can finish the fight properly.

Makima would use that hesitation. She knows Gojo cares about civilians, and a defense tied to their lives gives her something he cannot ignore. She could keep putting pressure on Denji and the others while Gojo tries to find a way around the contract.

Gojo’s best option might be containment rather than killing. Unlimited Void could overwhelm Makima’s mind if she is caught inside the domain, and the effect does not work like normal physical damage. Whether her contract can redirect something like that is less clear, but it gives Gojo a way to incapacitate her without immediately tearing her body apart again.

He could also use Blue and Infinity to keep her physically isolated while Aki and the others go through Public Safety records looking for anything that explains how she keeps surviving. They might uncover fragmentary evidence pointing toward some kind of government-backed protection around Makima, but not enough to confirm its exact nature, wording, or loophole. The goal would still become finding a way to stop her without repeatedly testing a contract they do not fully understand.

Denji would still matter here because Makima’s entire obsession with Chainsaw Man gives him access to her in a way Gojo does not have. Gojo could overpower her in direct combat, contain her, protect Denji from her controlled forces, and stop her from escaping, but none of that gives him an established way to permanently kill her without triggering the protection tied to her contract. The final answer would still need to come from Denji exploiting something specific to Makima and the way she sees him.

That keeps the ending from becoming Gojo simply overpowering the main villain because he is stronger. Gojo can win the immediate fight without being able to permanently solve Makima’s contract, while his power changes the situation enough for Denji to reach the part of the conflict only he can resolve without being completely broken first.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: The best-case version of this timeline depends on Gojo and Denji eventually finding a way to stop Makima before she kills Power and fully destroys Denji’s life. If they do, Denji would come out of the story in a very different place. He would still have been manipulated for months and would still have complicated feelings toward Makima, but he would have Aki, Power, and Gojo around him when the truth finally comes out.

Aki surviving is the hardest part because the Gun devil situation could still kill him even with Gojo involved. If Gojo manages to prevent Aki from becoming the Gun fiend in the first place, then Aki could actually make it out of the Public Safety story alive. If the transformation already happens, saving him becomes much less certain, and Gojo may still have to accept that some things in this world cannot be undone.

Power has a much better chance because her death depends heavily on Makima controlling when and where she appears. Once Gojo is actively suspicious and keeping her close to Denji, Makima loses the easy opportunity she had in canon. Power could survive the main conflict and stay with Denji afterward, which would change his life more than almost anything else. If they eventually find a way to defeat Makima, that would also leave Public Safety in chaos. A huge amount of its leadership, contracts, and operations had been connected to her, and suddenly everyone would have to deal with the fact that a devil had been sittifg at the center of the organization. Gojo would probably have no interest in taking over because he already hates dealing with bureaucracies in his own world, but he would care about what happens to the hunters who were being used.

He could push for younger hunters to be given more choice over contracts and assignments, especially after seeing how easily Public Safety treated people like replaceable pieces. That would not fix the whole system, but someone as strong as Gojo openly refusing to play along would make it harder for the organization to keep doing everything the same way.

Denji would still be Chainsaw Man, and devils would still keep coming. Gojo’s presence would not remove fear from humanity or stop powerful devils from being born. What changes is that Denji would have someone strong enough to stand beside him without wanting to own him, control him, or use him for what Pochita can do.

Gojo would probably stay a devil hunter for a while because there are still threats worth fighting and people around him he cares about. He would never become a normal Public Safety employee, though. He would take the jobs he thinks matter, ignore the ones that feel like politics, and keep getting into arguments with whoever replaces Makima.

Denji and Power would probably make his life miserable in ways he secretly enjoys, while Aki, if he survives, would become the only person in the group trying to keep everyone functioning like normal adults. The group would still be chaotic, but it would be much closer to a real family than anything Denji had before.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Gojo becoming a devil hunter would make the early Chainsaw Man story much easier in terms of raw combat, but that would not be the part that changes the timeline most. Smaller devils
would rarely be a real problem for him, and even stronger ones would have to deal with Infinity, the Six Eyes, and techniques that don’t exist anywhere else in their world.

The bigger change would come from Gojo staying close to Denji, Aki, and Power. He would notice how Public Safety uses them, question things they have been taught to accept, and make it much harder for Makima to isolate Denji the way she needs to.

Makima would still be dangerous because her powers do not rely on beating Gojo in a normal fight. She can control people, use contracts, and turn the people around him into weaknesses, which means Gojo could never treat her like another devil he can erase with Hollow Purple. Even so, Gojo being there gives Denji something he never had in canon which is someone powerful enough to challenge Makima before she finishes breaking everyone around him. That could save Power, possibly save Aki, and force Makima into the open much earlier.

So Gojo would probably become one of the strongest devil hunters in the world almost immediately, but the most important thing he changes would be giving Denji and the others a chance to reach the end of the story without losing everything first.

scripts.title: What If Gojo Had The Force

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Gojo would first notice the Force because he begins experiencing a second, unfamiliar sense around living things that does not come through cursed energy at all. His Force sensitivity is what detects it. The Six Eyes becomes useful afterward because it can confirm that there is no corresponding cursed-energy phenomenon, letting Gojo realize he is dealing with a separate system instead of an unknown part of Limitless. At first, he’d probably test it the same way he tests anything unusual, using small movements and trying to work out what responds when he focuses on it.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Gojo would first notice the Force while he’s still young enough that Limitless and the Six Eyes already shape how he sees the world, but before he fully understands what either of them will eventually let him do. The new sensation would come through Force sensitivity itself, especially around people, animals, and moments of danger. Because the Six Eyes can read cursed energy with absurd precision and shows him no matching cursed-energy source, Gojo would quickly realize this sensation belongs to something separate. At first, he’d probably assume there’s some part of his own technique he hasn’t understood yet, until repeated tests show the two systems behaving differently.

The first real sign would come when something moves without Blue. Gojo could reach for an object across the room and feel it shift toward him even though he never activated Limitless, and that would be enough to make him repeat the same test several times. He’d move the object again, try different distances, change how much force he uses, and compare the feeling to what happens when he uses cursed energy. The result would stay consistent enough that he’d eventually accept he’s working with something separate from jujutsu.

That would immediately make him curious because the Force gives him control without relying on the same mechanics he already knows. Blue creates attraction by manipulating space through Limitless, while this new ability could move an object directly through telekinesis. Gojo would start separating the two on purpose, using Blue with one hand and the Force with the other, then switching between them quickly enough to feel where one ends and the other begins. The more comfortable he gets, the easier it becomes to layer them together instead of treating them like two unrelated techniques. His perception would change even faster than his telekinesis. The Six Eyes already gives him an incredible amount of information about cursed energy, but the Force would add something more instinctive on top of that. Gojo could start sensing movement before he sees it clearly, notice someone entering a room without looking toward the door, or feel danger coming a moment before an attack actually begins. None of that would replace what the Six Eyes does because the two abilities are giving him different kinds of information, but together they’d make surprising him even harder than it already is.

That would affect training almost immediately. Sparring partners who rely on sudden attacks would find that Gojo starts reacting before their movement fully develops, and someone trying to hide cursed energy wouldn't automatically become invisible to him because the Force isn’t depending on cursed energy in the first place. Even when he can’t identify exactly what someone is about to do, he’d feel enough of the intent behind the attack to start moving early. Gojo would enjoy that more than anyone around him probably wants him to. Once he realizes the new power doesn’t follow the same rules as cursed techniques, he’d keep pushing it in ways nobody can teach him because there isn’t a jujutsu manual that explains what he’s doing. He’d be learning through trial and error, and his confidence would make him willing to test limits that a more cautious person might spend years approaching.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The biggest improvement wouldn’t come from making Blue or Red stronger. Gojo already has enormous power in both, so the Force would matter more by giving him additional control around those techniques. If Blue pulls an enemy toward a point, Force telekinesis could adjust their body during the movement, changing their angle or keeping them from recovering once the pull starts. Gojo could also use the Force on nearby objects while Blue is affecting the larger area, which would let him create several different pressures at once without asking Limitless to do everything.

Red would benefit in a similar way. The repulsive force already throws targets away with extreme power, but Gojo could use Force telekinesis immediately afterward to change where they land or stop them from escaping in the direction they want. Someone blasted backward by Red might suddenly get dragged sideways before they can regain control, leaving them open to another attack before they understand what moved them the second time.

Infinity wouldn’t need much help defensively, but the Force could make the area around Gojo even harder to approach. Infinity stops attacks before they reach him, while Force perception could warn him about threats that don’t behave like normal physical attacks. If something unusual starts happening nearby, he may feel the danger before he fully understands the technique involved, giving him more time to decide whether Infinity handles it or whether he needs to move.

Gojo could also use telekinesis on things that have already stopped in front of Infinity. A weapon hanging uselessly in the space before his body could be redirected back toward the person who threw it, or simply ripped away and dropped somewhere else. Against weaker enemies, he might barely move at all because Infinity handles the approach while the Force turns their own attacks against them.

The Force would also make his movement less dependent on Limitless. Gojo already uses Blue to move at high speed, but Force assisted movement could help with smaller corrections during combat. He could pull himself around corners, change direction in midair, or stabilize his body after being knocked off balance without using Blue every single time. Those small adjustments would matter because they let him save Limitless for the moments where it gives him the greatest advantage.

His fighting style would gradually become less predictable as a result. Gojo is already extremely good at close combat, and adding Force-enhanced movement and perception would make his timing even harder to follow. He could sense an attack beginning, move before the strike fully commits, then use a small telekinetic push to ruin the opponent's footing while he counters.

By the time he reaches his teenage years, the Force would feel less like a separate power and more like another part of how he fights. He still understands cursed energy better because he grew up surrounded by it, but the new ability would be woven into his reactions enough that he stops thinking about which system he’s using every second.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: That doesn’t mean Gojo sees the future perfectly. Force precognition is usually closer to flashes, instincts, and a sense of danger than a complete movie of what happens next, especially for someone who hasn't been formally trained. Gojo would still have to interpret what he feels, and confusing situations could give him several possible outcomes rather than one clear answer. The advantage comes from getting that warning before everyone else.

In normal missions, that could save people Gojo might have been too late to protect otherwise. If a curse is hiding behind a wall and preparing to attack someone nearby, the Six Eyes might not have a perfect view through every obstacle, but the Force could still make Gojo feel that something is about to happen. He could move first, then use Blue to pull the civilian away before the attack reaches them.

His reactions during combat would become frightening even for other skilled sorcerers. An opponent feinting with cursed energy could still fool the Six Eyes for a moment if the technique is designed well enough, but the Force might warn Gojo that the real danger is coming from somewhere else. He wouldn’t always know why the first attack feels wrong, yet that feeling could be enough to stop him from committing to the wrong defense.

That would also affect his confidence. Gojo already grows up knowing that his inherited abilities put him far above almost everyone around him, and sensing danger before it happens would make that gap feel even larger. He could walk into situations that should be risky and feel when something is wrong before anyone else notices, which gives him even more reason to believe he can handle problems alone.

The downside is that the Force responds to emotion and intent in ways cursed energy doesn't. Gojo could begin sensing fear, anger, or hostility around him without always knowing whose emotions they are, and the constant awareness might become exhausting if he doesn’t learn how to shut some of it out. The Six Eyes already forces him to process enormous amounts of information, so adding another layer of perception could make his need for control even stronger.

He’d eventually learn to narrow his attention. Instead of feeling everything around him at once, Gojo could focus on immediate threats or specific people, using the Force almost like another sense he can tune depending on what he needs. That would make him much more effective, but it would also deepen the distance between him and ordinary people because he’s experiencing every room in a way almost nobody else can understand.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The Hidden Inventory mission would be where the Force begins changing major events instead of simply making Gojo better in normal fights. When Gojo and Geto are assigned to protect Riko Amanai, Gojo would already have enough experience with the Force to feel danger before it becomes obvious, even if he still doesn’t fully trust every warning.

Toji would remain the biggest problem because his Heavenly Restriction makes him almost impossible to read through cursed energy. In canon, that lack of cursed energy lets him exploit one of Gojo’s biggest blind spots, especially after exhausting him over several days and waiting until Infinity has been running long enough to wear him down. With Force perception added, Toji’s complete lack of cursed energy stops being as useful as it was before because Gojo now has another way to sense people. The Force wouldn't automatically reveal Toji’s exact location at all times. He’s extremely skilled at hiding his presence, controlling his killing intent, and moving through crowded areas where one person can disappear among everyone else. Gojo might still struggle to isolate him until Toji gets close enough to become an immediate threat.

When Toji finally moves in with the Inverted Spear of Heaven, Gojo could feel something wrong a moment before the attack reaches him. The 6 Eyes would still see almost no cursed energy coming from the attacker, but the Force would react to the danger itself. That brief, fractional warning could be enough for Gojo to turn, move, or use telekinesis to alter Toji’s approach before the spear touches Infinity.

Toji would recognize immediately that his first attack didn’t work the way he expected. He’d adjust because that’s what makes him dangerous, using the environment, cursed tools, and speed to keep Gojo guessing while looking for another opening. Gojo would have to work harder than usual because the Inverted Spear can still cancel Limitless on contact, and Toji is one of the few people fast enough to capitalize on any mistake.

Force telekinesis would give Gojo another way to deal with the cursed tools. Rather than letting Toji reach him and trusting Infinity, he could push the spear off line or pull debris into Toji’s path before the weapon gets close. Blue could control the larger movement while the Force handles smaller corrections, making Toji’s usual rhythm much harder to maintain.

That first encounter could end without Gojo being mortally wounded. If Gojo avoids the initial stab that almost kills him in canon, the entire mission shifts. Toji would still be dangerous enough to threaten Riko and Geto, but Gojo would remain conscious and able to recognize that Toji’s real objective is Riko instead of treating the encounter like a duel he can finish on his own.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Toji wouldn't give up after missing the first ambush. He would understand that Gojo is sensing something beyond cursed energy and start trying to overload that new advantage. Instead of relying on 1 clean surprise attack, he could create several threats at once, move through blind spots, and use cursed spirits or thrown weapons to keep Gojo reacting while he looks for a path toward Riko.

Gojo would have to combine the Force and Limitless properly for the first time. Instead of simply chasing Toji, he could keep himself positioned between Toji and Riko while Geto moves her away. Blue could drag Toji off the route toward her, telekinesis could knock the Inverted Spear out of the most dangerous angle or pull Riko farther from an attack, and Force precognition could warn Gojo when Toji is about to change targets. The fight would still move fast enough that Gojo can’t think through every choice, so the powers would have to work together almost instinctively.

Toji’s physical speed would keep him competitive for a while. He could still avoid weaker uses of Blue, close distance quickly, and force Gojo to keep track of the Inverted Spear because 1 successful hit can shut Limitless down. His experience fighting sorcerers also means he’d notice which movements belong to Blue or Red and which ones seem to happen without cursed energy, giving him some ability to adapt to the Force even if he has no idea what it is.

Gojo would gain the upper hand once he stops treating telekinesis like a replacement for his cursed techniques and starts using it between them. A brief Force tug could disrupt Toji’s footing just before Blue activates, making the attraction harder to dodge. If Toji changes direction, another quick push might spoil that movement for an instant rather than reliably forcing him wherever Gojo wants. Those tiny interruptions are enough to make Blue and Red easier to land without assuming Gojo can simply hold someone as fast and physically powerful as Toji in place. Toji can survive heavy damage, but repeatedly having his timing disrupted while Gojo’s actual cursed techniques do the heavy hitting would gradually put the fight in Gojo’s favor.

The Force could also help protect Riko directly. If Toji gets close enough to attack her, Gojo could pull her away without needing Blue, which reduces the risk of using a stronger spatial technique near someone he’s trying to protect. Because Gojo is still active, physically guarding the route to Riko and helping Geto evacuate her, Toji no longer gets the clean isolated opportunity to shoot her that he receives in canon. That does not make Riko impossible to kill, but it gives Gojo a concrete way to prevent the assassination rather than assuming his own survival automatically saves her.

If Riko survives the encounter, Gojo’s life changes far beyond this fight. Geto doesn’t have to watch her die in front of him, and the chain of events that pushes him deeper into resentment begins from a different place. The problems inside jujutsu society still exist, and Geto still has to deal with the constant burden of absorbing curses and protecting people who may never understand what sorcerers sacrifice for them, but one of the most traumatic moments in his life no longer happens the same way.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: After the Toji fight, Gojo would take the Force much more seriously because it just saved him from the kind of attack his usual abilities were supposed to handle. He’d start training it with the same attention he gives Limitless, but the process would look very different because nobody in the jujutsu world can actually teach him what he’s doing. Most of the progress would come from pushing one ability at a time, comparing what he feels through the Six Eyes with what he senses through the Force, and learning where those 2 systems overlap without confusing them.

Cursed energy already comes from negative emotions, so Gojo is used to anger, stress, and fear existing somewhere in the process. The Force would react to those emotions differently, but nobody in the jujutsu world could explain that to him. Over time, Gojo might simply notice a pattern: in moments when he is genuinely angry or stops restraining himself, a telekinetic shove sometimes comes out harder or more aggressively than he intended.

At first, he probably wouldn’t treat that as a separate system to train. He would just remember that anger had produced results before and begin leaning on the feeling more often when a fight becomes frustrating or someone he cares about is threatened. The danger is that repetition gradually turns that shortcut into a habit long before Gojo understands what the Force is doing with those emotions.

Geto would probably be one of the first people to notice. If Riko survived, their relationship would already be in a much healthier place than canon, but Geto could still see how Gojo changes when he starts relying on emotion to fuel the Force. Gojo might shrug it off because he’s still in control, but the concern would stay there, especially once the gap between them keeps growing.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Saving Riko would change a huge amount of what happens between Gojo and Geto, but it wouldn't erase every problem that was already developing. Geto still spends his life consuming curses, taking on dangerous missions, and seeing how often sorcerers suffer for people who know nothing about them. The resentment could still grow, although it would happen more slowly without Riko’s death and Toji’s attack pushing everything forward at once.

Gojo would be in a better position to notice that something is changing because Force perception could give him broad impressions of tension, anger, or distress around Geto without explaining exactly what he is feeling or why. Gojo would still have to interpret those impressions through Geto’s behavior, their conversations, and what has been happening on their missions. That gives him more chances to ask questions earlier instead of realizing too late that Geto has been pulling away.

Their conversations could still be difficult because Gojo isn’t naturally good at talking about emotions in a careful way. He’d probably joke at first, then get more serious once Geto’s behavior and the uneasy impressions Gojo keeps sensing make it obvious that something is wrong. The Force does not tell him exactly what Geto is thinking, but it makes the change harder to ignore. That gives Gojo a much better chance of interrupting Geto’s downward spiral before it reaches the point of no return, but it does not guarantee he succeeds. Geto might still question why sorcerers protect non sorcerers, and he could still become angry at a system that treats young sorcerers like disposable workers. Gojo would agree with more of that than he admits because he already hates the jujutsu higher-ups and the way they control everyone beneath them.

The difference is that Gojo can offer Geto another possible direction before violence becomes the only answer he sees. By this point, Gojo is strong enough to start challenging the system directly, and the Force gives him even more confidence that he doesn’t need permission from the people running jujutsu society. If Gojo reaches Geto early enough, one plausible altered trajectory is the two of them trying to change the system from inside and outside at the same time. Geto’s other pressures still exist, so this remains a possibility rather than an automatic replacement for his canon fall.

That wouldn’t suddenly make both of them perfect reformers. They’d still be young, angry, and extremely powerful, which means their idea of fixing things could become aggressive very quickly. Gojo might start using the Force to intimidate higher ups without touching them, dragging documents across a room, breaking weapons from a distance, or making it clear that threats against students aren’t going to work anymore.

Geto would probably support some of that. The bigger danger is that Gojo starts enjoying how easy it is to force people to listen. Once telekinesis, Limitless, and the Six Eyes all work together, very few people can physically stop him. The Force gives him another tool that doesn’t even need cursed energy to be obvious, so someone standing across the room could suddenly lose their weapon or be pinned against a wall before they know what happened.
Gojo could justify using that power because the people he’s threatening are corrupt or dangerous.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: By the time Gojo reaches adulthood, his Force abilities would be much more refined. Telekinesis would be precise enough to manipulate several objects at once, Force perception would cover a wide area around him, and precognition would give him small warnings during combat before an attack fully develops.
Combined with Infinity, that would remove one of the few remaining ways enemies could hope to catch him off guard.

Gojo already keeps Infinity running automatically, so most physical threats stop before reaching him. The Force adds another layer by warning him about danger before that threat even gets close, which means techniques designed around deception or hidden movement would have to fool both systems at the same time.

Blue and Red would also become more dangerous because Gojo could use the Force to control what happens immediately before and after each technique. If Blue pulls several enemies together, telekinesis could keep them from escaping the best position. Red could throw someone away, then the Force could redirect them toward another target or stop them from landing safely.

Hollow Purple becomes easier to set up as well. Gojo wouldn’t make Purple stronger just by adding the Force, but he could improve the conditions around it. Telekinesis could hold an enemy in place while Blue and Red are being combined, or Force precognition could help him choose the moment when an opponent is least likely to move out of the path.
Reverse Cursed Technique would still handle physical damage if something reaches him.

The biggest change would still be his awareness. Gojo could walk into a room and feel where people are before seeing them, notice someone preparing to attack from another floor, or sense a general rise in fear or tension before a crowd actually panics. That would make him much better at protecting students and civilians because he gets more warning before a situation collapses. Around Yuji, Megumi, Yuta, and the rest of his students, he might sometimes sense that something feels emotionally wrong, but he would still need their behavior and context to work out who is struggling and why. Gojo still wouldn’t always respond perfectly, but he’d have more chances to notice when someone may be reaching a breaking point.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The Shibuya Incident would be where Force enhanced Gojo changes the timeline most dramatically.

Kenjaku’s entire plan depends on isolating Gojo, overwhelming the area with civilians, and then using the Prison Realm once Gojo is emotionally stunned by seeing Geto’s body. If Geto never fully broke away from Gojo in this timeline, that plan already becomes harder because Kenjaku may not have access to the same body in the first place.
Even if Kenjaku somehow still has Geto’s body, Gojo would be much harder to catch.

The Force could warn Gojo that something is wrong as Kenjaku prepares and reveals the Prison Realm. He would not automatically know its sealing condition, but the abnormal sense of danger could make him move instead of remaining close to it while trying to understand why Geto is standing in front of him. That matters because the Prison Realm needs Gojo to remain within its effective range long enough for the required subjective minute to pass in his mind. An early warning gives him a plausible chance to break that condition before the seal can complete.

The crowded station would still limit how freely Gojo can use his strongest techniques because civilians are everywhere, but Force telekinesis gives him more options that don’t require huge destructive attacks. He could move people out of danger from a distance, pull curses away from crowds, and hold enemies in place while using smaller applications of Blue and Red.

The Disaster Curses would have a much harder time controlling the battlefield. Jogo could still attack with fire and overwhelming cursed energy, Hanami could still use large scale techniques, and Choso could pressure Gojo from range, but none of them benefits from Gojo having another system of perception and movement layered on top of everything he already has. Mahito would be especially dangerous because soul manipulation doesn’t operate like a normal physical attack, but Gojo would still have Infinity between them, and the Force might help him sense Mahito’s presence or intent before a direct attempt at contact.

If Gojo realizes the Prison Realm itself is the danger, he could use the Force or Blue to create distance, pull the object away from his position, or simply refuse to remain inside its effective range long enough for the sealing condition to be satisfied. The Force is not an automatic escape after the seal succeeds; its advantage is giving Gojo another warning that may stop Kenjaku from keeping him in the required position for that subjective minute in the first place.

Without Gojo being sealed, Shibuya changes almost immediately. The Disaster Curses lose the main advantage they spent months preparing for, and Kenjaku no longer gets a free period where the strongest sorcerer is removed from the board.
Gojo could eliminate major threats much earlier, which means fewer civilian deaths and far less damage to the jujutsu world afterward.
The timeline after Shibuya would barely resemble canon.
Kenjaku would still be dangerous, Sukuna would still exist inside Yuji, and the larger problems around cursed energy wouldn't disappear, but Gojo would remain present for all of it.
And by then, he’d be far stronger than the version everyone was already terrified of.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: The biggest changes would come from the events it prevents. Toji would have a much harder time surprising him, Riko could survive, Geto’s fall might never happen in the same way, and the Prison Realm plan in Shibuya could fail before Gojo is ever sealed.

His biggest risk would come from how easily the Force responds to the parts of his personality that are already difficult to control. Gojo is confident, emotional when people close to him are threatened, and comfortable ignoring rules when he thinks the people making them are wrong. If anger keeps giving him faster results, he could start relying on it more often than he should. Even with that risk, the combo would be absurdly powerful. Gojo already controls space, keeps Infinity running almost constantly, heals himself with Reverse Cursed Technique, and can trap opponents inside Unlimited Void. Adding Force perception, precognition, and telekinesis would cover some of the few situations where enemies can still catch him by surprise.
By adulthood, Gojo with the Force would be much harder to trap, much harder to outmaneuver, and far better at protecting the people around him.

scripts.title: What If Gojo Was In The Boys

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Gojo would understand pretty quickly that Vought’s heroes aren't what they pretend to be. He’d see the way people inside the company talk about Supes like products, and none of it would impress him.

Vought would have a much harder time understanding Gojo. There’s no Compound V in his body, their strongest people can’t touch him through Infinity, and every test they try only gives them more questions about how his abilities work.

Homelander would hear about him eventually, especially once other members of The Seven start coming back with stories about a man they couldn't intimidate or even hit. At first, he’d probably assume Gojo is just another powerful Supe who needs to be reminded who runs things, but that attitude would change once he sees what Infinity actually does.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Gojo would realize very quickly that Supes in this world work nothing like sorcerers. Their powers come from Compound V, most of them are managed by corps, and even the strongest heroes are expected to care about ratings, public appearances, and whatever story Vought wants people to believe. By the time Gojo starts paying attention to the company, Homelander has already turned Vought into something much closer to his own power structure, which means Gojo would be entering at a point where the company has even less room for someone it can’t control.

His first contact with Vought would probably happen after he uses his abilities in public. It could start with something small, like Gojo stopping a Supe from hurting someone and doing it without ever being touched. Security footage would show attacks stopping before they reach him, yet there'd be nothing visible between Gojo and the person attacking him.

Vought would want him identified before anything else. They'd run his face through databases, check for old records, and look for any sign that he came from one of their programs. Nothing useful would come back. The problem gets worse once Gojo allows them to take a biological sample during Vought’s initial testing and recruitment attempt, and they find no Compound V at all.

That alone would bring him much higher up Vought's list. Gojo wouldn’t make the investigation easy because he’d probably find the attention entertaining at first. His enhanced perception would make nearby surveillance teams difficult to hide from him, especially if they physically follow or approach him, but the Six Eyes wouldn't automatically reveal every camera or distant observer Vought uses. If they send a Supe to test him, he’d understand what they’re doing almost immediately.

The first test could be someone Vought considers expendable enough to lose if things go badly. They might have a mid level Supe approach him and start a fight under the excuse of public safety, mostly so the company can see how Gojo reacts to physical attacks.

A punch would stop before reaching Gojo’s face. Trying again with more force wouldn't help, and moving faster wouldn’t change anything because Infinity isn’t a shield that gets broken by hitting it harder. The space between Gojo and the attack is divided over and over as it approaches him, preventing contact unless he allows it.

Gojo could let the Supe struggle for a few seconds, then end the fight with something simple. He wouldn't need Hollow Purple or even Red. A basic use of Blue could drag the Supe off balance hard enough to put them through a wall, or Gojo could simply close the distance himself and knock them out.

The company would know physical attacks can’t reach him, he can manipulate movement somehow, and none of it comes from Compound V. They still wouldn’t understand cursed energy, Limitless, or the Six Eyes because nothing in their science gives them a clean comparison.

He’d notice how quickly Vought turns an unexplained person into something they need to own or remove, and once he starts looking into the company’s history, he’d find plenty that interests him for the wrong reasons.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Vought would probably try the friendly approach before sending anyone important after Gojo. Someone this powerful would be far more valuable on their side, especially if his abilities could be marketed as something new.
They'd offer money, a place within The Seven, public recognition, and whatever else they think motivates powerful people. Gojo would listen mostly because he wants to see how far they take it.
The conversation would start falling apart once Vought expects him to follow rules.

Gojo already has problems with authority in his own world, especially when he thinks the people above him are protecting a broken system. Vought would give him the same feeling almost immediately because everyone around the table would be talking about contracts, approved missions, controlled statements, and how his image could be shaped for the public.

Gojo would probably joke through most of it, which would make the executives even less comfortable because they wouldn't know whether he’s taking them seriously. The moment they move into testing, things get more interesting. Vought would want to know what stops attacks from touching him, whether there’s a limit, and how long he can keep it active. They could bring in stronger materials, ranged weapons, heat, electricity, or Supes with different abilities and keep watching for any sign that Infinity weakens.

Nothing normal would give them the answer they want. Gojo keeps Infinity running automatically for most of his life, and the Six Eyes makes his cursed energy use absurdly efficient. Vought could spend hours trying different attacks and still come away with no evidence that they're draining him in any useful way.
A sniper round, hidden explosive, or sudden attack from behind would let them test whether Infinity works when Gojo isn’t paying attention.

That would probably be the point where Gojo stops treating the situation like a weird corporate meeting and starts taking Vought more seriously. Someone just tried to hurt him during a recruitment process, and Gojo would immediately understand that the company’s friendly approach only lasts while they think they can get something from him.

Vought could lock doors and deploy armed security, but none of that would hold him for long. Blue could tear obstacles out of the way, Red could send people across a room without Gojo needing to kill them, and Infinity means most of the weapons around him are useless.

Gojo isn’t behaving like one of their usual Supes. He isn’t asking for a bigger contract, trying to improve his approval numbers, or looking for a place inside Vought. They don’t have anything obvious to hold over him.

At first, he’d probably be more irritated by the way people inside Vought are talking about Gojo than by Gojo himself. Every report keeps coming back with another ability nobody understands, and people are being told not to confront him without approval.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Gojo’s first real meeting with The Seven would probably happen because Vought wants someone stronger to figure out what he can do.

A-Train would immediately stand out because of his speed. Gojo would be able to perceive enough of what he’s doing to understand the nature of his ability, but the Six Eyes wouldn’t automatically let him visually track every movement at A-Train’s full speed. That wouldn’t matter much defensively because A-Train could circle him or rush from an angle, but getting close still means running into Infinity.

Deep wouldn’t have much he could do in a direct fight, while stronger members would be more interested in whether Infinity can be bypassed through some unusual ability. Gojo would probably ask them questions while they’re testing him, partly because he’s curious and partly because he wants to understand what each person actually does.

Some of them are frightened of Homelander. Others stay because Vought gives them money, status, or protection. Gojo would see very quickly that the team doesn’t operate like a group of people who trust each other.

Starlight would probably interest him more than most because she has already seen what Vought is and doesn’t buy into the image anymore. If this happens during a point where she’s openly against Homelander and the company, she’d have no reason to hide much from Gojo once she understands that Vought can’t easily threaten him.

She could tell him about Compound V, the cover-ups, the people Vought has killed, and how Homelander has used fear to keep people around him under control. Gojo would believe more of it once he starts checking for himself.

The Six Eyes won't magically give him access to Vought's files, but Gojo is smart enough to know where to look once someone points him in the right direction. He could follow people inside the company, listen to conversations they don’t realize he can reach, and use his abilities to enter places security thinks are protected.

Most people inside Vought are careful with how they speak about him because they know what happens if word gets back. Gojo would have no reason to care about any of that, and his confidence would probably make him sound even more dismissive without trying very hard. That eventually reaches Homelander.

He’d want to meet Gojo himself, but Vought would probably delay it because they still have no idea whether Homelander can actually touch him. Gojo would find that funny once he learns they’re keeping their strongest Supe away from him.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The Boys would hear about Gojo after Vought starts moving resources around him.

Butcher would immediately want to know who he is because a man who can walk through Vought security and stop Supes from touching him sounds useful. Hughie would be more cautious because nobody knows where Gojo came from or what he wants.

Starlight could eventually connect Gojo with The Boys and explain enough about the group for him to understand why they exist, although he wouldn’t automatically agree with how Butcher handles things. Gojo has no problem killing when he thinks it’s necessary, but Butcher’s hatred of Supes often goes much further than simply dealing with dangerous people.

Gojo would pick up on that almost instantly. He might still stay and listen because The Boys know things about Vought that he doesn’t. They can show him evidence of experiments, Compound V distribution, cover-ups, and the way Vought has spent years protecting Supes who hurt ordinary people.

That would give Gojo a much clearer reason to act. He wouldn't suddenly join The Boys as another member, though. Gojo is used to making his own decisions, and Butcher trying to point him toward targets would probably annoy him more than anything.

Hughie and Starlight would have a better chance of working with him because they could explain what's happening without pretending they control what Gojo does next. Once Gojo sees enough evidence, he'd start going after parts of Vought directly. He could enter labs that The Boys would normally spend weeks trying to reach. Locked doors wouldn’t matter much, armed guards couldn’t stop him, and most Supes sent to defend the site would have no way around Infinity.

That would create one of the first major changes to the timeline. Vought’s secret programs become much harder to protect when Gojo can physically enter them and leave with evidence. The Boys no longer need every operation to depend on sneaking through security or blackmailing someone on the inside.

Homelander would take that personally. This isn’t just someone refusing to join Vought anymore. Gojo is now interfering with the system Homelander controls, and the people around him are starting to see that Vought can’t make him stop.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: He'd find him somewhere without asking the company first, and the meeting would probably stay calm for a little while because Homelander would want to see what Gojo is like before attacking him.
His physical strength is much higher, his senses are better, and the confidence around him isn’t coming from Vought marketing alone. Homelander really is one of the strongest people in this world.

That would make Gojo more interested. Homelander would probably start by telling him to stay away from Vought and The Seven, expecting the conversation to end there. Gojo wouldn't have much reason to listen, especially after everything he has already learned.

That would irritate Homelander faster than an open threat probably would. People normally respond to him before he has to do much. Gojo would keep speaking casually because he already knows Homelander can’t simply reach through Infinity and kill him.

Homelander might test that with heat vision. The beams would stop before they touch Gojo. He could increase the intensity and keep firing, but the result stays the same because the attack still has to cross the space between them. From Gojo’s perspective, heat vision gives him more information about Homelander without putting him in serious danger.

Homelander would close the distance next. His speed could let him move across the room before most people process what happened, but his fist would stop in front of Gojo just like every other physical attack.

Gojo would probably smile at that. Then he’d test Homelander back. A use of Blue could pull Homelander off his feet and drag him hard enough to tear through part of the building. Homelander would survive without much trouble, which tells Gojo exactly what he wanted to know. This opponent can take more damage than the others.

Homelander would come back much angrier after that. The first exchange still wouldn't need to become their final fight because neither one has shown everything yet. Gojo hasn’t used Red at full power, Hollow Purple, or Unlimited Void, while Homelander hasn't had enough time to understand whether there’s any way around Infinity.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: They'd study every frame from Gojo’s fights and try to find moments where something gets closer than usual. They could test whether gas works, whether sound works, whether attacks from several directions make a difference, or whether Gojo needs to consciously identify something before Infinity stops it.

Some of those questions are reasonable because Infinity does involve automatic filtering. Gojo learned to let the technique classify threats based on things like speed, mass, shape, and cursed energy, which means Vought might eventually realize the ability has rules even if they don’t understand them.

Poisoned gas might seem promising because air obviously still reaches Gojo. His automatic Infinity can classify threats with extreme precision, but filtering complex poisons was presented as a more difficult extension of that system rather than something Vought could safely assume it blocks automatically. That gives the company a legitimate reason to test airborne chemicals, even if Gojo’s perception, Reverse Cursed Technique, and ability to leave the contaminated area quickly would make turning that into a reliable way to kill him extremely difficult.

Sound would be different because Gojo normally allows harmless sound like conversation to reach him through Infinity. That means a Supe with an unusual sonic ability could at least test whether an attack carried through something his automatic filtering normally permits might slip through before Gojo recognizes it as dangerous and adjusts.

That still doesn’t mean they beat him. Gojo has Reverse Cursed Technique, extreme speed, Blue, Red, and enough combat experience to deal with opponents whose abilities don’t work in obvious ways. If Vought finds one attack that can affect him, they still have to survive long enough to use it properly.

He'd start watching Gojo more closely himself, especially after seeing Gojo interfere with more Vought operations. Homelander might notice that Gojo lowers Infinity around people he trusts or when he wants to physically interact with something.
Instead of trying to break Infinity, Homelander could attack someone near Gojo and force him to react.

This is where the conflict becomes much more serious because Gojo’s abilities make him extremely difficult to threaten personally, but the people around him don’t have Infinity. Starlight, Hughie, MM, and the others can still be hurt.

He'd stop treating the situation casually after that. If Homelander attacks Hughie or Starlight while Gojo is nearby, Blue can move them out of danger or pull Homelander away before the hit lands. Red gives Gojo a much stronger way to create distance, and Infinity still protects him while he’s doing it.

That would also change how Gojo works with The Boys. He wouldn't need Butcher to convince him that Homelander has to be stopped anymore. By this point, he has seen enough for himself. Gojo would start planning around Homelander rather than simply reacting whenever Vought sends someone after him, and once Homelander realizes Gojo is doing the same thing, their next meeting wouldn't end after a few exchanged attacks.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: After Homelander starts using other people to pressure him, Gojo would change how he handles Vought. Up to that point, he could afford to treat most encounters casually because the company had no reliable way to hurt him. Once civilians and The Boys start getting pulled into Homelander’s attempts to reach him, Gojo would have a reason to remove some of Vought’s options before the next fight begins.

He’d start with the parts of the company that keep Homelander informed and supplied. Vought relies on surveillance, security teams, private facilities, and people who track every threat around The Seven, so Gojo would make those systems much harder to use. He could enter buildings without waiting for The Boys to clear a path, take records before they’re destroyed, and remove equipment that Vought normally uses to watch people from a distance. The Six Eyes wouldn't give him access to computers by itself, but once Hughie or Starlight points him toward the right places, getting inside becomes much easier.

Vought would notice the pressure building because more of its usual responses would stop working. Sending Supes after Gojo gives him more information about them, trying to follow him only tells him who is doing the tracking, and threatening people close to him makes him take the company more seriously instead of backing off. The executives around Homelander would start realizing that every attempt to force Gojo into a normal Vought problem is making him harder to manage.

Homelander would have his own reason to stop waiting. The first encounter already showed him that physical attacks and heat vision can’t get through Infinity, and watching Vought search for a scientific answer would only make him more frustrated. He’d want to prove that the problem can still be solved through force, especially once Gojo’s presence starts making other people less afraid of him.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Homelander would probably open the 2nd fight with speed rather than conversation. He already knows getting close doesn’t guarantee contact, so he’d use heat vision from range while changing position quickly and looking for any moment where Infinity appears to drop. Gojo could read those movements much better than most people because of the Six Eyes, and he wouldn't need to chase Homelander through the air to keep control of the fight.

Blue gives Gojo a way to control position even when Homelander is flying. He could create a point of attraction beside or behind him and drag him off his line, which would make it much harder for Homelander to keep attacking from the same safe distance. If Homelander tries rushing back in, Infinity stops the hit while Gojo gets another chance to test how much damage his body can take.

Red would be a much bigger problem than Blue because the repulsive force can hit with enough power to launch opponents through structures. Homelander’s durability would let him survive it, but surviving the impact doesn’t give him a way around Infinity when he comes back. Every exchange would keep putting him in the same position where he can hurt the environment around Gojo but still can’t land the hit he actually wants.

Homelander’s speed would keep the fight from being completely one sided at first. He can cross distance extremely fast, fly from angles Gojo has to track, and keep pressure on anyone nearby if the fight happens somewhere populated. Gojo would solve that by moving the fight away from civilians as soon as he gets the chance, using Blue to reposition Homelander and himself until there’s less around them that can be used as leverage.

Gojo could start hitting much harder because he no longer has to worry about what's behind Homelander. Repeated Reds could potentially wear him down while continually disrupting his positioning, and Blue could keep dragging him back into positions he doesn’t want to be in. Homelander can survive far more physical punishment than a normal person, but he has no answer for being repeatedly moved around by an ability he doesn’t understand.

Hollow Purple would be where the fight becomes truly dangerous for him. Gojo combines Blue and Red into an attack that tears through everything in its path. That doesn’t mean Purple automatically ignores durability, since sufficiently powerful Jujutsu Kaisen characters have survived it, but Homelander has never shown a feat proving he can withstand an attack on Purple’s demonstrated destructive level. If Gojo fires Purple cleanly and Homelander fails to dodge, the damage could still end the fight there. Homelander’s best chance would be avoiding it rather than trying to tank it. His speed gives him at least some possibility of moving before the attack reaches him, especially if he recognizes that Gojo is preparing something different. Gojo wouldn't need to keep throwing Purple if the first attempt misses because every use risks destroying more of the surrounding area.

That leaves Unlimited Void. If Gojo decides the fight needs to end without risking another huge blast, Domain Expansion gives him a much cleaner option. Homelander has no domain, no cursed technique designed to counter one, and no demonstrated resistance to the overwhelming information Unlimited Void forces into a target's mind. Unless Compound V gives him some unknown resistance to that kind of information overload, being caught inside would likely leave his physical strength irrelevant because his brain would be flooded faster than he can process what's happening.

Gojo wouldn't need to keep the domain open for long. Even a short exposure could leave Homelander unable to fight properly, and once he drops, Gojo can decide whether to kill him or hand him over depending on what has happened by that point in the story.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Removing Homelander would change Vought immediately because so much of the company’s control has been built around people being afraid of him. The executives who followed his orders because they had no alternative would suddenly be dealing with someone who defeated him and has no interest in taking his place.

Gojo wouldn't want Vought. He wouldn’t become CEO, lead The Seven, or turn himself into the next public face of superhero culture because none of that fits him. He’d be far more interested in breaking the systems that allowed Vought to create and protect people like Homelander in the first place.

That would give Starlight and The Boys a chance to expose far more than they could before. Vought’s labs, Compound V records, cover ups, and internal files could come out without Homelander standing over everyone who might testify. Some Supes would run, others would try to distance themselves from the company, and a few could finally cooperate once the person they feared most is gone.

Butcher would still be a problem for Gojo because losing Homelander wouldn't automatically remove his hatred of Supes. If Butcher starts treating every powered person as the next enemy, Gojo would push back against him just as easily as he pushed back against Vought. He’d judge people by what they do, which means Starlight, Kimiko, and anyone else who has shown they’re trying to help wouldn’t become acceptable targets just because they have Compound V in their bodies.

The Seven would probably collapse rather than continue in the same form. Some members would leave, some would face criminal investigations, and Vought would have a much harder time rebuilding its old image once people understand that Homelander wasn’t untouchable. Gojo’s presence would also change how the public sees power. For years, Vought sold the idea that Supes were something only Vought could create, manage, and protect people from. Gojo breaks that story simply by existing because he has abilities the company didn’t create and couldn't control.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: The bigger change would happen before and after that fight. Vought would spend most of the story trying to understand someone who doesn't fit its system, The Boys would gain access to places they could never reach on their own, and Homelander would eventually lose the fear that keeps everyone around him under control.

Gojo wouldn't replace him at the top of Vought. He’d leave the company with far less power than it had before he arrived, while the people Homelander spent years controlling finally get a chance to decide what happens next.

scripts.title: What If Gojo Was Trapped In The Prison Realm Forever

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Gojo getting sealed in Shibuya already throws the jujutsu world into chaos. In canon, there’s still one thing everyone can hold onto, if they can free him, they get the strongest sorcerer back.
In this version, that never happens.

Every attempt to open the Prison Realm fails, and the Culling Game keeps moving without Gojo ever returning. Yuji, Yuta, Maki, Hakari, and Megumi have to plan around that from the start, while Kenjaku gets to move without worrying about Gojo suddenly showing up.

Then Sukuna takes Megumi’s body. Now there’s no Gojo fight waiting to weaken him first. The rest of the cast has to figure out how to deal with Sukuna at close to full strength while still trying to stop Kenjaku and survive everything else the Culling Game throws at them.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Everything through Shibuya would stay the same. Gojo gets sealed, Kenjaku leaves with the Prison Realm, and the jujutsu world falls apart almost immediately after. Yuji is sentenced to death again, Yaga is marked for execution, Gojo is blamed for the Shibuya Incident, and anyone trying to free him is treated like an enemy of the higher ups.

Yuta would still return to Japan and take Yuji’s execution order, then use it as a way to protect him. Megumi would still pull Yuji back into the plan for the Culling Game because Tsumiki is already trapped inside it, and the group would still go to Tengen looking for answers. Tengen gives them the back of the Prison Realm and tells them about Angel, whose technique can extinguish cursed techniques and should be able to open it.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The Culling Game would still begin in roughly the same way because most of the reasons the group enters it have nothing to do with freeing Gojo. Tsumiki is still trapped by Kenjaku’s rule, they still need points to change the game, and they still need to move through several colonies at once.

Yuji would still enter Tokyo No. 1 with Megumi and eventually run into Higuruma. Megumi would still have his fight with Reggie’s group, while Yuta goes into Sendai and Hakari handles Charles and Kashimo.

Maki becomes even more important after Sakurajima. Once she fully reaches the level that puts her close to Toji physically, the group finally has someone who can attack high level enemies without relying on cursed energy in the normal way. Her zero cursed energy gives her specific advantages against barriers and domains that identify or target people through cursed energy, though it doesn’t let her ignore every barrier automatically. Hakari would also get treated as more than backup. His domain gives him a way to keep fighting through damage that would put almost anyone else down, and Kashimo joining them gives the group another fighter who’s specifically waiting for Sukuna.

The colonies themselves would still play out close to canon at first. Higuruma still joins Yuji’s side. Kashimo still agrees to work with Hakari because he wants Sukuna. Yuta still wins in Sendai. Maki still becomes much stronger.

The divergence would come after they finally get Hana and bring her to the back gate. Angel would still use Jacob’s Ladder on it. The technique would hit the Prison Realm exactly the way it did in canon, burning through the cursed technique tied to the seal, but the gate wouldn't open properly. The seal would react, the markings would start breaking apart, and then nothing comes out.

They’d try again because nobody is going to accept that result after coming this far. Hana would use more output. Yuta could keep watch while Tengen’s remaining information is checked again. They’d move the gate, change the barrier around it, and make sure nothing outside is interfering.

It still wouldn’t work. At that point, the group would have to treat this as the actual divergence: something about the Prison Realm in this timeline is preventing the back gate from producing a working exit even after Jacob’s Ladder hits it. They wouldn’t have a canon explanation for why. Angel can damage the cursed technique tied to the seal, but for whatever reason, Gojo still can’t come out.

That would leave them with a cursed object they can hurt but can’t properly open. Yuji would take it badly because Gojo was the person who kept telling him he could grow stronger and survive all of this. Megumi would probably react more quietly, but Gojo is also the person who raised him and kept the Zenin clan from controlling his life. Yuta would feel the pressure the most because he’s already one of the strongest people left, and everyone would start looking at him the way they used to look at Gojo.

Nothing gives them a clean answer. Eventually, the group would have to accept that building every plan around Gojo coming back is getting people killed. The Culling Game is still moving, Kenjaku is still active, and Sukuna is still inside Yuji. They can keep looking for another method in the background, but they can’t wait for Gojo anymore.
From that point forward, Yuta, Maki, Hakari, Yuji, and Megumi would have to plan as if Gojo is gone for good.

The problem is that all of those wins are happening while Kenjaku is getting closer to Tengen. Once Kenjaku takes Tengen, the group loses another major source of information and barrier control. At that point, Gojo’s back gate becomes even less useful because Tengen was one of the only people who fully understood how the Prison Realm worked.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Kenjaku’s position would improve a lot once it becomes clear Gojo isn’t coming back. He already planned Shibuya around removing Gojo because fighting him directly was a bad option. In canon, even after the sealing, Kenjaku knows there’s still a chance someone could open the Prison Realm later. Here, that problem slowly disappears.
He could spend more time on the merger and Tengen without worrying that Gojo might show up halfway through the Culling Game and wipe out everything he built.

That doesn’t mean Kenjaku suddenly stops being careful. Yuta is still dangerous, Maki is harder to track, Hakari is difficult to kill once his jackpot starts, and Yuji is still connected to Sukuna in ways Kenjaku understands better than almost anyone.

Kenjaku would probably start taking those fighters more seriously earlier. Yuta becomes the obvious problem because he’s the closest thing the group has to a top level sorcerer. Kenjaku already knows Yuta can use Rika and copy cursed techniques, and he’d have no reason to give Yuta time to grow into the role Gojo used to fill.

He might try to keep Yuta away from the main barrier plans by creating problems in other colonies or sending cursed spirits toward places Yuta has to protect. Kenjaku doesn’t need to beat Yuta in a straight fight if he can keep him busy while the merger setup continues.

Maki creates another issue because barriers that recognize targets through cursed energy don’t treat her the same way they treat normal sorcerers. Kenjaku would have to account for someone who can exploit those specific blind spots and who has the speed to kill weaker curse users before they can react.
The merger itself would still be the end goal. Kenjaku wants to combine Tengen with the people of Japan and see what comes from it, and Gojo being gone makes that experiment easier to reach.
The group would know they can’t let Kenjaku keep moving forever. Yuta, Maki, Hakari, Choso, and the others would start talking about killing him before the Culling Game reaches its final stage.
The problem is Sukuna. As long as Sukuna is still inside Yuji, there’s a chance they can manage that threat separately. Then Sukuna uses Enchain.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Sukuna taking Megumi would still happen almost exactly the way it did in canon.

Yuji made the binding vow with Sukuna long before any of this. When Sukuna finally uses Enchain, he gambles that Yuji himself isn’t included in the vow’s promise not to hurt anyone during that 1 minute window. Sukuna isn’t certain that interpretation will work, but it does. He takes control of Yuji’s body, tears off a finger, and forces it into Megumi.

Megumi becomes Sukuna’s vessel. The timing would be even worse here because the group has already accepted that Gojo probably isn’t coming back. There’s no backup plan where they survive long enough to free him and let him handle Sukuna afterward.
