Mark tries using the other 2 arms to grab him, and Nolan knocks all 4 away before the Omnitrix starts flashing and turns Mark human again.

Nolan has enough information to know the aliens Mark currently understands aren't a physical threat to him. The part he can’t answer is how many transformations are still inside the device. Mark has already found several species without understanding the watch, and each one gives him a different biological ability rather than producing another version of the same power. Nolan considers taking the Omnitrix away, but the device is physically locked to Mark and Nolan has no idea what forcibly removing or damaging unknown alien technology attached to his son could do to him. Instead, he allows Mark to keep using it under the excuse that he can train him properly. For Mark, that sounds like his dad finally accepting that he can be a hero. For Nolan, keeping Mark close gives him the safest way to watch the Omnitrix while Mark discovers what else is inside it.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Mark's life changes again a few weeks later at Burger Mart. He’s taking out the trash when he throws a bag toward the dumpster and watches it sail upward until he can barely see it anymore. He stands there staring into the sky, then looks at his own hands and realizes the thing he waited his entire childhood for has finally happened.

He rushes home to tell Nolan, and this time there's no alien transformation involved when Mark proves it. His Viltrumite strength is developing naturally, and flight follows soon afterward. Nolan starts training him the way he originally planned, which mostly involves Mark crashing into things while trying to understand how flying works and Nolan telling him to get back up.

Mark initially assumes having Viltrumite powers will make some of the Omnitrix redundant. Four Arms isn’t as exciting once Mark can lift huge amounts of weight without transforming, and he no longer needs the watch just to survive ordinary criminals. Then training starts showing him how different the 2 sets of abilities really are.

In his own body, Mark can fly, fight at high speeds, take enormous punishment, and keep getting stronger as his Viltrumite abilities mature. XLR8 gives him far better movement across the ground than he currently has as Mark. Diamondhead lets him create barriers and attack from range. Other aliens Mark begins unlocking give him abilities his Viltrumite body simply doesn’t have, so the Omnitrix starts becoming a tool he chooses for specific problems instead of the source of everything he can do.

There’s also an important limitation Mark learns the hard way. His Viltrumite abilities belong to Mark’s body. When the Omnitrix transforms him, he becomes the selected species and has to work with that alien’s biology until he changes back. If Mark picks an alien that can’t fly while he’s hundreds of feet above the ground, his normal ability to fly isn’t going to save him until he returns to human form.

Nolan incorporates that into their training. He'll chase Mark through the air until Mark chooses a transformation, then immediately changes the way he fights based on whatever Mark becomes. If Mark chooses Four Arms, Nolan stays airborne and forces him to deal with an opponent he can't reach easily. If Mark uses XLR8 on the ground, Nolan makes him deal with attacks coming from above. Mark gradually stops thinking about which alien is strongest and starts thinking about what he needs at that exact moment.

Nolan sees Mark improving faster than he expected. He'd spent years preparing to explain Viltrum to a son who would eventually have the same basic abilities he does. Mark now has those abilities along with alien technology Nolan still can’t identify, and every week he becomes more comfortable using both.

Mark eventually gets his suit and starts operating publicly as Invincible. He keeps the Omnitrix visible because there isn’t much point pretending the giant green symbol appearing on every transformation is unrelated to him anymore. Most civilians don’t understand what it does, but Cecil certainly wants to.
Before Cecil can properly approach Mark about it, portals begin opening over the city.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The Flaxan invasion is Mark’s first real test against an army. He reaches the city with the Teen Team and initially stays in his normal body, flying between groups of soldiers and knocking them away from civilians. His strength handles individual Flaxans easily, but there are too many of them spreading through different streets for Mark to keep chasing 1 group at a time.

He switches to XLR8 and uses the speed to cover several blocks in seconds. Instead of trying to fight the entire army, Mark starts pulling civilians out of buildings, removing weapons from soldiers, and carrying injured people away from the fighting. He’s faster than the Flaxans can track on the ground, although he still clips a parked car on one turn because he hasn't mastered moving through crowded streets at that speed.

The Flaxans begin aging before Mark needs to figure out another solution. Their bodies deteriorate under Earth’s different passage of time, and the surviving soldiers retreat through their portals. Mark changes back in front of the Teen Team, which answers several questions they had about why Invincible suddenly disappeared when a blue alien showed up.

Robot immediately starts asking about the Omnitrix. Mark explains what little he knows and refuses when Robot asks whether he can examine it more closely. Rex makes fun of him for having an alien watch that occasionally gives him the wrong alien, while Eve is more interested in whether Mark can control when he changes back. Mark shows her he can slap the symbol to change back early, although changing into another alien normally means returning to himself and activating the watch again. If he lets the watch time out on its own, it needs time to recharge before it works again.

When the Flaxans return with equipment that compensates for Earth's time flow, Mark changes his approach. He uses Diamondhead to raise crystal barriers between their weapons and civilians while Eve helps contain the damage from above. Once enough civilians are clear, Mark changes back and uses his Viltrumite body to attack their larger equipment directly.

The Omnitrix gives the heroes more options, but it doesn’t remove the invasion. The Flaxans keep adapting, and Mark is still 1 inexperienced hero trying to protect an entire city. When Nolan arrives, he cuts through their forces at a speed Mark can't follow and gets dragged through the portal during the fight.

Mark tries to reach him before it closes and misses by seconds. He considers cycling through the Omnitrix looking for an alien that might reopen the portal, but he has no idea whether one exists and no time to learn. For once, having several alien bodies available doesn’t give him an answer.

Nolan eventually returns after spending much longer in the Flaxan dimension than Mark realizes. Mark is relieved enough that he doesn’t question what his dad did while he was gone. Nolan tells him the Flaxans won't be coming back anytime soon, and Mark takes that as another example of Omni Man saving Earth when everyone else ran out of options.

The experience leaves Nolan thinking about Mark differently. Mark’s natural abilities are developing, he’s becoming comfortable using the Omnitrix around other heroes, and Cecil now knows exactly who possesses the alien device he’s been tracking. Nolan has spent years controlling when Mark would learn the truth about Viltrum, and that window is getting smaller as Mark builds a life among Earth’s heroes.
That makes the Guardians of the Globe a more urgent problem.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Nolan knows killing the Guardians becomes riskier once Mark is active as Invincible. Mark can fly across the city on his own now, and the Omnitrix gives him several ways to reach an emergency quickly if he realizes one is happening. Nolan waits until Mark is home with Debbie before leaving, then summons the Guardians without giving Mark any reason to follow him.

The Guardians arrive expecting a normal meeting with Omni Man. Nolan attacks before they understand what he’s doing, and by the time the fight ends, every Guardian is dead while Nolan is badly injured. Mark never gets the chance to intervene because he doesn’t know the fight is happening until Cecil’s people have already found the bodies.

Seeing Nolan unconscious beside the dead Guardians hits Mark differently now that he’s started fighting alongside other heroes himself. He assumes whoever did this nearly killed his dad too and starts wondering whether any of his transformations could've helped if he’d been there. Nolan eventually wakes up and gives Mark no reason to suspect him, while Cecil begins working through the evidence from the scene.

Cecil's investigation now includes another concern. Mark is Nolan's son, has recently developed powers similar to his father’s, and possesses alien technology the GDA doesn’t understand. Cecil doesn’t accuse Mark of anything, but he has Donald keep tracking every transformation they can identify. If Nolan’s story starts falling apart, Cecil needs to know exactly what Mark is capable of before deciding how much he can tell him.

Mark keeps working as Invincible while Nolan recovers, which eventually brings him to Machine Head’s penthouse with Titan. Mark walks into that fight with much more confidence than the original version of himself would’ve had. He has Viltrumite strength, several transformations, and enough experience to think he can find an answer once he sees what he’s fighting.
Then Battle beasttr hits him.

Mark survives the first exchange in his Viltrumite body and immediately understands that trading punches is going to get him killed. He creates distance long enough to activate the Omnitrix and chooses 4 Arms, hoping the extra size and strength will help him control Battle Beast’s weapon. Mark catches the mace with 2 hands and uses the other 2 to attack, but Battle Beast tears the weapon free and sends him across the room before Mark can capitalize on it.

The fight exposes a weakness Mark hasn't dealt with before. Having more transformations gives him more choices, and Battle Beast is experienced enough to punish the time Mark spends figuring out which choice works. Mark knows what Four Arms and Diamondhead can do against ordinary enemies. He has never tested them against someone capable of tearing through Viltrumite level opponents, so he’s learning their limits while Battle Beast is beating him into the floor.

Battle Beast eventually leaves because nobody there can give him the fight he wants. Mark realizes Four Arms is taking damage the transformation cannot survive and changes back before Battle Beast lands the worst of the beating. The remaining hits tear through Mark’s Viltrumite body instead. He survives with severe injuries, and his Viltrumite healing keeps him alive, but the beating stays with him because it is the first time he’s had both sets of abilities available and still had no way to win.

Nolan sees the injuries after Mark comes home and understands another consequence of letting him carry the Omnitrix around Earth. Mark nearly died while wearing a device containing technology Nolan still hasn't figured out. If Battle Beast had killed him and taken it, Nolan might've lost any chance of controlling where the Omnitrix ended up.

Mark takes a different lesson from the same fight. He starts spending more time learning the aliens he already has instead of treating the dial as a collection of emergency answers. When he trains with Nolan again, he asks Nolan to keep fighting after every transformation and force him to switch strategies whenever an alien stops working.

Nolan agrees because training Mark still gives him the best view of what the Omnitrix can do. At the same time, Mark is getting stronger in his own body, learning the watch faster, and becoming more connected to the heroes Nolan eventually expects him to stand against. Nolan can see that waiting much longer to reveal Viltrum is only going to make that conversation harder.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: The truth about Nolan starts coming apart while Mark is still recovering from Battle Beast. Debbie has been questioning what happened to the Guardians, Cecil has been investigating Nolan since the massacre, and Mark has spent months being personally trained by his father, When Mark watches Nolan kill the Immortal in front of the whole world, he recognizes movements he’s seen during their training sessions. He still hopes there’s another explanation because accepting what he saw means accepting that almost everything Nolan taught him about being a hero came from the man who killed the Guardians.
Nolan realizes there's no story left that Mark will believe, so he flies him away and tells him about Viltrum. He explains why he came to Earth, what the Empire expects from him, and why

Mark developing his powers was so important. Mark listens until Nolan starts talking about Earth as a planet they can rule together and describes the people Mark grew up around as lives that will disappear long before either of them gets old.

Nolan even uses the Omnitrix to make his point. Mark has already experienced how different alien species can be from each other. Four Arms can lift things humans never could, XLR8 can cross a street before anyone notices he moved, and Diamondhead can take a bullet without being seriously hurt. Nolan thinks living inside those bodies should make Mark understand why Viltrumites don’t see every species as their equal, but Mark has come away from those transformations with the opposite experience. He tells Nolan that becoming stronger than Debbie never made her life mean less to him, and turning into another species never changed who he was when he changed back.

Nolan helped Mark train with Diamondhead and already knows what he likes doing with the transformation. Mark raises crystal between them, and Nolan changes direction before the barrier finishes, coming around the side and smashing him through his own structure. Mark fires shards after him and uses the few seconds Nolan spends avoiding them to get away from the civilians gathering nearby, but Nolan catches him before he can put much distance between them.

When Nolan takes the fight toward a train, Mark realizes what he’s doing and changes into XLR8. He races ahead along the tracks, tears open the doors, and starts carrying passengers away before Nolan reaches them. Mark can only move a few people at a time, and the train is still full when Nolan catches him and knocks him away from the tracks. Mark changes back during the impact and tries flying toward the remaining cars, but Nolan grabs him before he reaches them.

Seeing people die in front of him sends Mark straight back to the Omnitrix. He gets 4 Arms and attacks without thinking about how Nolan trained him to use the form. Mark catches Nolan with 2 hands and uses the other 2 to keep swinging, forcing Nolan backward for a moment before Nolan gets underneath him and drives a punch into his stomach. Four Arms folds around the hit, and Nolan follows it with another that sends Mark across the ground.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: After Nolan leaves Earth, Mark spends months recovering and working more closely with Cecil and the Guardians. During that time the GDA helps him test more transformations, including Upgrade, a species that can merge with and control technology. When the Sequids take over Mars and Rus Livingston becomes the center of the hive mind, Mark joins the mission to stop them. Upgrade cannot control the Sequids themselves, but Mark uses the form to merge with the ship’s systems, opening sealed routes and controlling doors long enough for the team to push toward Rus.

They reach Rus and break the hive mind before the Sequids can overwhelm the ship again. Mark changes back exhausted, but he comes home understanding Upgrade far better than he did in any GDA test. He never had to overpower the swarm with that transformation. Taking control of the doors and corridors let the entire team reach the person they were there to save. Mark barely has time to settle back into life on Earth before a Thraxan named Nuolzot asks him to help save his planet from a meteor storm. When Mark gets there, he instead finds Nolan alive, with another family and a baby son Mark never knew existed. Their reunion barely gets started before Lucan, Thula, and Vidor arrive to punish Nolan.

Mark fights in his own body until Thula’s experience starts overwhelming him. She reads his attacks, cuts him during one exchange, and follows him before he can recover. Mark activates the Omnitrix while falling and becomes Diamondhead, causing Thula to stop for a fraction of a second when Nolan's son suddenly becomes a species she doesn’t recognize.

Mark uses that hesitation to send crystal toward her and get back into the fight. Later he returns to his Viltrumite body when he needs flight, which lets Lucan see the entire transformation happen in reverse. During their next exchange, Lucan stops aiming for Mark’s head and
reaches directly for the device on his wrist. Mark pulls the arm away and drives his other fist into Lucan before he can grab it.

Then General Kregg arrives, takes the beaten Nolan away, and orders Mark to finish what his father started on Earth. Mark is too injured to stop him, but he remembers Lucan changing targets the moment he understood the watch was responsible for the transformation. Nolan was the reason they came to Thraxa, and now they’re leaving with their first direct look at the Omnitrix. Lucan and Thula’s reports give Viltrum its first real intelligence on the device, including that Mark uses it to become unrelated species and that it appears physically locked to him. While Mark recovers on Thraxa, Andressa asks him to take his baby half-brother back to Earth, and Debbie agrees to raise him as Oliver.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Angstrom Levy attacks Mark at home before Viltrum gets another chance. He keeps opening portals whenever Mark closes the distance, throwing him through realities faster than Mark can understand where he’s landed. Mark initially stays in his own body because flight and Viltrumite durability can handle most of the falls, until Angstrom drops him deep underwater where the pressure starts crushing him before he can reach the surface.

Mark changes into Ripjaws and immediately handles the water better, swimming upward until another portal opens in front of him. Angstrom sends him through and drops Ripjaws onto dry ground, where Mark’s new body starts struggling almost immediately.He slaps the symbol to change back before the dry air finishes him, while Angstrom watches from the other side and realizes the environment can be used against whichever alien Mark chooses.

Angstrom starts exploiting that. Mark lands somewhere dangerously hot and chooses Heatblast because it is one of the forms he already knows can tolerate the environment. Angstrom watches the choice, then makes the next portal deliberate, dropping that body somewhere its abilities give Mark very little advantage. He repeats the pattern with the transformations Mark reveals, observing how each alien handles a world before choosing an environment that works against it. Mark keeps trying to answer each new world with another transformation and spends more time looking at the Omnitrix while Angstrom decides where the fight happens next.

Mark finally quits chasing him through the portals. When another one opens underneath him, he lets himself fall, twists around during the drop, and grabs Angstrom's arm before the portal closes. Angstrom immediately starts jumping between dimensions with Mark attached to him, slamming them through several environments while trying to shake him loose. Mark holds on until they eventually return to the reality where Debbie and Oliver are waiting.

Angstrom goes after Mark’s family the moment they return, and Mark’s patience disappears. He gets his hands on Angstrom and starts hitting him in his Viltrumite body. The Omnitrix remains available on his wrist while Diamondhead could restrain Angstrom or XLR8 could get Debbie and Oliver out of the room, but Mark keeps swinging until Angstrom stops fighting back.

Mark finally pulls his fist away and looks at what's left of Angstrom. Debbie gets him moving again, and Mark takes her and Oliver somewhere safe before returning home later. He sits in the damaged house with the Omnitrix still on his wrist, knowing he had more choices than he’d ever had during the original fight and ignored every one of them once his family was threatened.

That experience changes how Mark approaches the next Viltrumites who come for him. Their behavior has changed too. They attack hard enough to restrain him while repeatedly avoiding strikes that could destroy his left arm, and one of them eventually pins that arm behind Mark’s back while another grabs the Omnitrix and tries to force it off.

The device stays locked in place. Mark headbutts the Viltrumite holding him and manages to reach the dial with his thumb, transforming into Big Chill while both attackers still have him restrained. His body becomes intangible and passes straight through their hands, leaving them grabbing empty air as Mark moves through the floor beneath them.

He comes back through the ground, freezes one attacker's leg long enough to stop his charge, and returns to his normal body once he needs to fight in the air again. The Viltrumites eventually retreat without the Omnitrix, but Mark has learned they were willing to leave without killing him. Whatever information Lucan brought back from Thraxa has changed what the Empire wants from Nolan’s son.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Conquest arrives already knowing about the watch. Mark reaches for the Omnitrix during their first exchange, and Conquest crosses the distance before Mark can finish selecting anything. He catches Mark’s wrist, punches him through a building with the other hand, and goes after the same arm when Mark tries again.

Mark understands after the second attempt and leaves the dial alone. He fights as a Viltrumite, letting Conquest keep watching his left hand while Mark uses everything Nolan taught him about fighting in the air. Conquest still dominates the exchanges, but after several minutes of Mark refusing to touch the watch, he stops reacting every time that arm moves.

Mark waits until Conquest grabs him by the throat. His fingers finally reach the dial while Conquest is holding him close, and Big Chill replaces Mark's body before Conquest can squeeze. Mark phases through his hand, passes through Conquest’s chest, and freezes the air around his face as he comes out behind him.

Conquest tears through the ice and charges. Mark phases through the first hit and tries freezing him again, but Conquest adjusts quickly enough to catch Mark when he becomes solid. Big Chill gets slammed into the ground, and Mark changes back before Conquest can keep attacking a body that can’t survive many direct hits from him.

Civilians are still trapped around the battlefield, so Mark uses XLR8 during the next opening and clears several nearby buildings while Conquest is recovering. He changes back and flies upward, deliberately drawing Conquest away from the streets. Conquest follows because Mark is still the only person there giving him the fight he came for.
Once Conquest understands that Mark is using the watch whenever he needs to change the fight, he attacks the device itself. He catches Mark’s arm and starts crushing it hard enough that

Mark can feel the bones beginning to give. Before Conquest can tear the arm away or destroy the device, the Omnitrix’s emergency safeguards trigger and force an automatic transformation, choosing from Mark’s available forms based on the immediate need to keep its wearer alive rather than waiting for him to finish a manual selection.

Mark uses the emergency form only to survive the immediate exchange and create distance before the Omnitrix returns him to his own body. He follows Conquest away from the city instead of treating the automatic transformation as something capable of overpowering him, moving the rest of their fight away from civilians.

Conquest eventually gets the upper hand again, and Eve joins before Mark is killed. When Conquest badly injures her, Mark feels the same rage that took over against Angstrom. He charges, stops himself before reaching Conquest, and hits the Omnitrix instead.

Big chill Appears again. Mark phases through Conquest’s first punch and lets Conquest’s momentum carry him forward, then changes back behind him and locks both arms around his torso. Eve attacks from the front while Mark keeps Conquest trapped through the impact. Conquest breaks loose badly injured, and Mark stays in his own body for the final exchange until they bring him down.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: By this point, the Viltrumites have enough information about the Omnitrix to consider taking Mark alive more valuable than simply killing him when possible. They've seen him become several unrelated species, watched him use abilities their own biology can’t reproduce, and failed to remove the device from his wrist. By then, Nolan has broken out of the Viltrumite prison with Allen and come back to Earth to stand with his son. The Empire’s next attack on Earth comes with orders to capture Mark if possible and recover the Omnitrix intact for study, while still allowing the attackers to use lethal force if preserving him or the device starts costing them the fight. That gives Mark and Nolan an advantage before the fighting even starts, but only until the Viltrumites realize Mark is exploiting their restraint.

Mark notices Viltrumites pulling strikes whenever his left arm gets caught between them and the watch. During one exchange, he deliberately raises that arm as an attacker comes toward him, forcing the Viltrumite to redirect at the last second. Nolan hits him from the side while Mark transforms into Big Chill and phases through another attacker trying to restrain him. The
Viltrumites eventually realize Mark is exploiting their orders and stop giving him those openings, turning the fight back into the kind of brutal close range battle they're comfortable with.

One of them manages to catch Mark before he can transform and drives him through several buildings. Mark gets back into the air, takes another hit, and tries reaching the dial while the Viltrumite stays on top of him. Nolan is occupied with the others, leaving Mark alone against someone strong enough to keep damaging him faster than his Viltrumite body can recover. Mark finally gets his hand onto the Omnitrix and cycles through the transformations he knows. He could choose Way Big and risk causing even more destruction around the city, while Big Chill gives him a way out of the Viltrumite’s grip without turning the entire area into a bigger battlefield. Mark chooses Big Chill, phases through the next punch, then passes directly through the Viltrumite and freezes him as he comes out behind him.

The ice only holds for a moment, but Mark only needs that moment. He changes back, grabs the Viltrumite while his movement is slowed, and carries him high above the city before the fight continues. Nolan eventually reaches him battered and exhausted after barely incapacitating one attacker and forcing another out of the fight, making it clear the assault has been anything but routine. Mark uses the Omnitrix to create one more opening against the Viltrumite still on him, and Nolan capitalizes on it from the side. Even together they need a brutal final exchange before they finally bring the last attacker down.

When the fighting is over, Mark looks at the damage below them and thinks back to when the Omnitrix first landed on Earth. Back then, he wanted whatever alien looked strongest because he'd spent his entire childhood waiting to feel powerful. Years later, he has his Viltrumite strength, transformations capable of doing things his own body never could, and enough experience to know that having another option doesn’t always mean he should use it.

The Omnitrix also changed the choice Nolan tried to make for him. Nolan wanted Mark to see himself as a Viltrumite and eventually accept everything that came with it, but Mark has spent years becoming species from across the universe and returning to the same life afterward. He still loves Debbie, still protects Earth, and still decides for himself what being Nolan’s son means.

Mark leaves the battlefield and flies home in his own body. The Omnitrix is still there when he needs another species, but Mark finally has enough experience to know when he can handle a problem himself. He spent years waiting for his Viltrumite powers and even longer learning what the watch could turn him into, and after everything with Nolan and the Empire, he gets to decide what kind of hero he becomes with both.

scripts.title: What If Invincible Was In Infinity War

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Mark Grayson was still recovering from his father's beating when the sky tore open.
He tumbled onto a dusty construction site in New York. He pushed himself out of the concrete, bleeding and bruised. The skyline was familiar enough to recognize. Almost everything else felt wrong.

Only a few blocks away, Peter Parker was on his patrol when his Spider-Sense flared up. He followed it to a crater where he found a teenager in a yellow and blue suit lying in the rubble. What none of them realized was that their sudden meeting was about to rewrite history.
Thanos was weeks away from invading Earth. But he had no idea he was about to face a Viltrumite.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter Parker stayed on the nearby rooftop for several seconds before moving closer. His Spider-Sense had warned him moments before the impact, but nothing about the teenager standing inside the crater suggested another attack was coming. The boy looked confused and exhausted, with a damaged yellow and blue suit covered in dust from the fall. Peter had seen plenty of strange things since becoming Spider-Man. A teenager appearing in the middle of an empty construction site was still new.

Mark Grayson was trying to make sense of what he was seeing. He knew the city was New York, but it wasn't the New York he had grown up around. The skyline was familiar enough to recognize, yet almost everything else felt wrong. The people were strangers, the buildings were unfamiliar, and none of the technology or organizations he expected to find seemed to exist. His phone was useless. He had no way of knowing whether whatever had brought him here could happen again.

Mark explained that he was from another universe. He had been traveling through his own world when something unexpected happened and left him somewhere completely unfamiliar. He couldn't identify what had caused it. Whatever had torn the sky open hadn't left him with an explanation, and he had no way of knowing whether it could happen again. He had no way of knowing whether he could return. The explanation sounded impossible, but Peter had already lived through enough impossible events that he couldn't simply dismiss it.

Mark also had no reason to trust the first person he encountered in a completely unfamiliar world. Peter understood that, so he didn't push him for every detail. Instead, he explained that he knew someone who might be able to help. Tony Stark had access to technology far beyond anything Peter could build himself, and Peter had already seen him deal with problems that seemed impossible at first.
Mark agreed to follow him.

Before they left, Peter noticed something else. The crater was much deeper than it should have been from an ordinary fall, yet Mark had walked away from the impact. Most of the injuries Peter could see looked older, already beginning to heal from whatever had happened to Mark before he arrived. Peter didn't know what Mark was capable of. But he was beginning to understand that the teenager in front of him wasn't simply another young superhero.
For now, all he knew was that he had found someone who needed help.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Peter took Mark to Tony Stark because there weren't many people he could think of who could make sense of what had happened. Tony's first concern wasn't whether Mark was telling the truth. It was whether Mark was dangerous. The fact that Mark was a teenager didn't change that. He had appeared without warning, survived an impact that would have killed an ordinary person, and possessed abilities that Peter couldn't fully explain.

Mark cooperated. He had nothing to hide, and he needed help finding a way back to his own universe. Tony used what equipment he had to study Mark's physiology, and the first readings looked remarkably human. Deeper scans were different. There were cellular properties Tony couldn't explain, even though the basic structure was still recognizable. Biological rather than mechanical. Not enhanced. Just built differently.

Mark explained what he could about Viltrumites. His people were naturally stronger, faster, and more durable than humans, and many of them could fly. His own abilities had been developing since he inherited them from his father. He didn't present himself as some unstoppable warrior. He was still learning how to use what he had.
For the time being, Mark would stay somewhere secure while Tony worked on understanding the dimensional event that brought him there. Peter continued visiting.

Mark still wanted to return home. He thought about his mother. About his friends. About the life he'd left behind in a universe where he at least understood the rules. But for the first time since arriving, he wasn't alone.
Something was approaching Earth.
Tony Stark was already dealing with signs that the next threat would be unlike anything they had faced before.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Bruce Banner came through the New York Sanctum in a way that made it clear something had gone very wrong. He had been sent back to Earth after an encounter with an enemy he couldn't stop, and the message he carried was simple.
Thanos was coming.

Mark had never heard the name. Peter hadn't either. Tony hadn't. Bruce explained who Thanos was, that he had already attacked him, and that Earth was in danger of being drawn into something much larger than another alien invasion. Tony didn't recognize the name, but he recognized the kind of threat Bruce was describing.
Before they could make a proper plan, the attack began.

A large alien ship entered the skies above New York and moved toward the area surrounding the Sanctum. The people arriving weren't there for a general assault. They were searching for something specific. Doctor Strange had the Time Stone. Ebony Maw and Cull Obsidian had come to take it.

Tony moved into position. Bruce was still struggling with the fact that Hulk refused to come out after his defeat. Peter was nearby, and Mark joined the group when he realized the threat was already moving through the city.

Cull Obsidian was the first major obstacle. Enormous, heavily armed, and strong enough to push through defenses that would stop most opponents. Peter immediately understood that this wasn't a criminal he could handle alone. Mark recognized something different. Cull was powerful. But he wasn't stronger than Mark.
Their first clash proved it.

Cull attacked with his weapon, and Mark intercepted the strike. The impact drove Mark backward but didn't knock him down. He'd already learned from Peter that keeping a powerful opponent focused on one target was a mistake — so instead of standing in the middle of the street and trading punches, he grabbed Cull and carried the fight away from the civilians. Cull couldn't fly. Every time he hit the ground and tried to return to the others, Mark intercepted him, redirected his attacks, and kept him away from the street.
The more dangerous opponent was Ebony Maw.

Maw didn't need to overpower Mark physically. His abilities allowed him to manipulate objects around him with precision, turning the environment itself into a weapon. Cars, pieces of metal, stone, and debris moved through the air at his command. Mark could survive most of it. That didn't mean he could ignore Maw.

Maw quickly understood that Mark's physical strength was the wrong problem to solve. He focused on Strange and the Time Stone. His goal was never simply to defeat the heroes in the street. He needed the Stone, and Strange was the person standing between him and it.

Peter tried to help. Tony followed. Mark moved toward Strange as soon as he realized what Maw was attempting. The fight became a race rather than a battle. Maw began taking Strange toward the ship while the others tried to stop him. Peter attached himself to the spacecraft, Tony pursued in his nanotech armor and deployed the Iron Spider suit to Peter as he ran out of oxygen, and Mark flew after them without needing assistance.
Maw now had another problem to deal with. He had expected Earth's defenders to be dangerous. He hadn't expected one of them to be a Viltrumite.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Mark reached the Q-Ship before it could get far from Earth. Peter was already attached to the outside of the vessel, while Tony followed behind in his nanotech armor. The three of them made it aboard before the ship left the atmosphere, with Strange already being held captive by Ebony Maw.

Maw had Strange restrained in the center of the ship. He was trying to remove the protection surrounding the Time Stone, using his abilities to inflict precise injuries while demanding that Strange give up the Stone. Mark could see that Strange was being kept alive deliberately. Maw wasn't trying to kill him. He needed the Stone intact.

Maw sent pieces of the ship across the room. Mark tore through the first wave, but Maw kept reshaping the environment around him. Metal folded across Mark's arms and legs, broke apart when he moved, and immediately reformed from another direction. None of it could hold him for long. It didn't need to. Every second Mark spent tearing through it gave Maw more time to work on Strange.
Peter and Tony attacked from the opposite side.

The distraction gave Strange an opening. Tony used the moment to damage part of the ship's structure, creating a weakness in the hull. Peter moved Strange away from Maw while Mark continued keeping Maw occupied. The plan wasn't perfect. It didn't need to be. They only needed enough time to separate Maw from his prisoner.

Mark grabbed Maw and drove him through one of the ship's interior walls. Maw recovered quickly and used his abilities to throw Mark back. Mark hit the wall hard enough to damage the structure behind him. He got back up before Maw could follow.
Tony realized the ship itself could be used against him.

He created a controlled breach in the hull, exposing the interior to space. The sudden loss of pressure pulled Maw toward the opening. Maw tried to hold himself in place, but the force was too much. Peter and Tony secured themselves while Mark grabbed onto the ship and watched Maw disappear through the breach. As soon as Maw was clear, Tony's nanotech sealed the damaged section and restored the ship's pressure.

With Strange rescued and Maw gone, the group had a new problem. Thanos still wanted the Time Stone, and they had no way of knowing how close he was to getting the others. Tony made the decision to head for Titan. Peter stayed with him. Mark did too.

None of them knew exactly what they would find when they arrived. They only knew that if Thanos was as dangerous as Bruce had claimed, waiting for him to reach Earth could be the worst option available.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: The ship entered Titan's atmosphere and descended toward the surface. The planet was almost completely abandoned, covered by the remains of structures and vast areas of rocky ground. Tony had expected to find Thanos immediately. Instead, they encountered another group that had reached Titan first.

Peter recognized them from information Tony had given him. The Guardians of the Galaxy had been tracking Thanos as well, although neither side knew what the other group intended to do. Star-Lord, Drax, Mantis and the others were already prepared to fight when the two groups encountered each other.
The situation became chaotic before anyone had enough time to explain themselves.

Peter tried to keep the confrontation from becoming serious while Tony and Star-Lord attempted to determine whether they were dealing with enemies or potential allies. Drax was ready to kill everyone in the immediate vicinity regardless of whose side they were on, which wasn't helpful. The other Peter — Parker, not Quill — quietly noted to himself that two people named Peter had somehow ended up on the same abandoned alien planet. He kept that observation to himself. It didn't seem like the right moment.
Once the misunderstanding was cleared up, the reason they were all on Titan became obvious. They were looking for Thanos.
They knew Thanos was close. What they didn't know was exactly when he would arrive, or what condition he would be in when he did.
Strange used the Time Stone to examine possible outcomes.
This time, Mark was part of the equation.

Strange moved through millions of futures in silence. When he returned, his expression hadn't changed — but something in it was different. He had seen outcomes that hadn't existed before Mark arrived in this universe. Most of them still ended the same way. But there was one altered path where Mark's presence changed enough moments for them to win.
Strange said nothing about what that future required. He only knew that what happened on Titan was part of it, even if the fight itself didn't end with Thanos defeated.
He only said that they had one chance.
Mark didn't know what Strange had seen. He only knew they were running out of time.

The group prepared for Thanos's arrival. Tony worked with Peter and the Guardians to establish a plan built on distraction — keep Thanos occupied long enough for Mantis to use her abilities. Mark would be the most dangerous part of the attack. His job wasn't to defeat Thanos by himself. It was to keep him occupied and create an opening for the others.
Thanos arrived before they were ready.
He appeared on the surface of Titan with several Infinity Stones already mounted in the Gauntlet. His attention immediately went toward the group standing between him and the remaining Stones.
Mark moved first. He flew toward Thanos and struck him hard enough to send him across the battlefield.

Thanos recovered in seconds. He answered with a physical attack of his own, and Mark realized the problem almost immediately. He had fought people who were stronger. He had fought people who were faster. He had never fought someone who used both of those things the way Thanos did. The Titan wasn't simply reacting. He was already predicting Mark's next movement before it happened. Mark's second strike hit air.
The rest of the team joined the fight.

Peter used his webs to restrict Thanos's movements. Drax attacked from close range. Star-Lord fired from a distance while Tony tried to keep Thanos focused on multiple targets. Strange stayed back, using his magic to limit the Titan's options.

Mark changed approach. If Thanos was going to read his momentum, he'd stop giving him momentum to read. He attacked from different directions, forcing Thanos to keep turning, landing glancing strikes instead of committing to one angle. It worked better. He connected with two clean hits, and one of them actually forced Thanos backward.
Then Thanos used the Space Stone specifically on Mark.

Space folded around Mark before he could react. Thanos displaced him far across Titan, beyond the ruined structures surrounding the battlefield. Mark recovered immediately and turned back, but the distance was the point. By the time he returned, Thanos had already turned his attention toward Tony. He had identified Mark as the physical threat and moved him out of the equation with a single Stone. Peter and Tony were suddenly defending without their most durable asset.
A damaged craft cut across the battlefield before Mark could make it back. Nebula emerged from it already injured from Thanos's captivity and joined the fight against her adoptive father.
Tony's armor absorbed the first attack. The second damaged it.
Mark came back harder.

He drove himself toward Thanos again before the Titan could reach Tony. This time he wasn't trying to win. He was trying to make himself impossible to ignore. He hit Thanos from the side and wrapped his arms around him, giving the others the opening they needed.
Mantis moved into position.
The plan worked.
Mantis connected with Thanos's mind and his movements slowed immediately. Not completely — she had to fight for every second of contact — but it was enough. The others rushed forward.
Tony locked onto the Gauntlet with his armor. Strange used his sling ring to keep Thanos's wrist from moving. Mark used both hands to pull the Gauntlet away from Thanos's body.
It was coming off.

For the first time since landing on Titan, Mark felt like they might actually win. He could feel the Gauntlet moving. Tony had two fingers underneath it. Peter's hands closed around the outer edge and pulled.
Then Star-Lord found out what had happened to Gamora.
Peter saw the expression on his face and understood what was about to happen. He tried to stop him. The situation moved too quickly.
Star-Lord struck Thanos.

Mantis's hold broke. Thanos came back to full awareness in an instant. The Gauntlet was already partly off his hand, and Mark did not simply let go. He kept pulling as Thanos surged forward, wrenching the Gauntlet sideways while Tony and Peter tried to hold it in place. Before they could finish removing it, enough of the Gauntlet remained seated for the Power Stone to flare. The uncontrolled burst tore Mark and the others away from him and sent them across the battlefield.
The opportunity was gone. Thanos still had the Gauntlet.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Thanos recovered faster than Mark expected.

The Power Stone had thrown everyone across the battlefield, but the Titan was already moving. Mark pushed himself up and immediately understood the situation clearly. His ribs hurt. One side of his face was swollen. His breathing had become heavier. He was still capable of fighting. But the gap between being able to continue and being able to win was becoming obvious.

He flew toward Thanos again and caught him before he could reach the others. The two collided near the remains of one of Titan's ruined structures. Mark drove Thanos through the wall and followed him inside, landing several punches before Thanos managed to grab him.

Thanos had the advantage in experience and technique. He waited for Mark to commit to another attack, then redirected him and drove him into the ground. Mark tried to get back up. Thanos struck him again.
Peter saw Mark take the hit and immediately moved toward him. Tony pulled him away from the fight. Peter couldn't help Mark by getting himself killed. That was becoming harder for Peter to accept.
Thanos struck Mark across the chest and sent him through a section of ruined machinery. Mark hit the ground hard and stayed there.
Peter landed beside him.

Mark tried to stand. Peter could see he was badly hurt. His left arm was already beginning to swell, and his breathing was uneven. He had taken punishment that would have ended an ordinary fight several times over, but even Viltrumite durability had limits. He could heal from severe injuries. He wasn't immune to them.
Thanos approached.
Then Thanos attacked Tony.

Tony used everything his armor had left, but Thanos eventually broke through his defenses. Mark tried to reach them, but Thanos used the Space Stone to keep him away. Tony took a severe wound. Peter reached him first.
Strange looked at the Time Stone.

He understood what had to happen. This was one of the choices he had already seen. He gave Thanos the Stone in exchange for Tony's life. Mark watched the exchange from the ground. Five Stones were now in the Gauntlet. Only the Mind Stone remained.

Thanos disappeared from Titan before anyone could stop him. The battlefield became quiet. Mark pushed himself upright and looked toward Peter and Tony. Tony was alive, but badly injured. Peter was beside him, trying to keep him conscious.
Mark had failed to stop Thanos on Titan.
And now Thanos was heading for Earth. Mark knew exactly what that meant. He had one chance left. Wakanda was the last place between Thanos and the Mind Stone. Strange knew it too.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: There was no time for a return trip in the Q-Ship. Thanos could cross the distance instantly with the Space Stone.
Strange opened a sling-ring portal back to Earth. The other side showed the Sanctum in New York.

Tony was badly injured, Mark could barely move his left arm, and Peter stayed close to Tony as they crossed through. Once they were back within range of Earth's communications, Tony connected to the information coming out of Wakanda. The Avengers were already there. So was Vision.
Wakanda had the last Stone.
Strange opened another portal.
They stepped into a battle that had already begun.

The Outriders were pouring through Wakanda's defenses while Steve, Natasha, Sam, Bruce and the Wakandan army tried to hold them back. Vision was still injured, and Shuri was working to remove the Stone from his head without killing him.

Mark joined the fight despite his condition, but he quickly realized that fighting the Outriders wasn't what mattered. Every second they kept the army away from Shuri was another second she had to finish the procedure.
Thor arrived with Rocket and Groot. Stormbreaker tore through the Outriders and gave the defenders room to breathe. For a moment, the battle finally began moving in their favor.
Then Thanos entered the battlefield.
He arrived alone. The Black Order had already failed to stop the Avengers, and his army was still fighting around them. Thanos didn't care. He had five Infinity Stones. He only needed one more.

The Avengers attacked him together. Mark went after him as well. This time, Mark didn't try to fight Thanos alone. He had learned from Titan. Steve and Bruce kept Thanos's attention whenever they could. Natasha and Sam attacked from a distance, creating distractions and openings instead of trying to match him physically. Strange used his magic to keep Thanos from moving directly toward Vision, while Mark used his speed to take advantage of every opening the others created.
Then Thanos began using the Stones.

Mark was thrown aside by a wave of energy and landed hard enough to break through the ground. He tried to stand. His injuries had caught up with him. His body was recovering, but not fast enough to keep pace with the fight.

Tony was still too badly injured to fight at full strength, but he used what remained of his armor to support the others from a distance. Peter stayed mobile, pulling people out of Thanos's path whenever the Titan broke through.
Wanda remained near Vision. She knew what would happen if Shuri ran out of time.
Shuri was almost finished.
That became the entire fight. They didn't need to defeat Thanos yet. They needed to keep him away from Vision for a few more seconds.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Thanos forced his way through the Avengers and moved toward Vision.

Strange opened portals across the battlefield to redirect Thanos's attacks. Mark hit him from the side. Thor attacked from the other direction. Peter covered the gauntleted hand in webbing whenever Thanos tried to close it, but the strands tore almost as quickly as he could replace them.
None of it stopped Thanos for long.
But it slowed him down.
Shuri finished separating the Mind Stone from Vision.
For the first time, the Mind Stone was out of Vision before Thanos could take it. Vision collapsed nearby, weakened by the extraction but alive.
Wanda moved toward the separated Mind Stone.
She understood what the others didn't need to explain. The Mind Stone couldn't remain intact. The entire battle had bought her the opening she needed.
Wanda destroyed the Mind Stone.
Thanos saw what had happened.
The Time Stone began to glow.
Mark remembered what they had learned on Titan. Thanos activated the Gauntlet by closing his hand. Mark didn't know exactly what the Titan was about to do. He only knew they couldn't let him finish.
Mark was already close.
He forced himself forward with everything he had left and drove his remaining hand across Thanos's gauntleted palm, wedging the fingers open before they could close.
Thanos tried to pull free. Mark held on.

Peter reached them a second later. He wrapped several webs across the gauntleted fingers and pulled in the opposite direction. The webbing wasn't strong enough to restrain Thanos by itself. It only had to buy Mark another second.
Strange bound Thanos's other arm. The Titan broke through the restraint almost immediately, but the delay created one more opening.
Thor took it.
Stormbreaker cut through the energy Thanos released toward him and struck the Titan in the chest. Thanos dropped to one knee with the axe buried in his body.
Mark kept the Gauntlet open.
Peter kept pulling.

Thor ripped Stormbreaker free and brought it down against the damaged edge of the Gauntlet. Mark pulled at the same moment. The combined force tore it free from Thanos's hand and sent it across the battlefield.

Strange immediately opened a portal beneath the Gauntlet. It dropped through and disappeared into the Sanctum before Thanos could reach it. The five Stones remained locked inside. No one had to touch them.
Without the Gauntlet, Thanos was still monstrously strong. But he no longer had five Infinity Stones answering every movement.
Stormbreaker had already left him badly wounded. Mark was barely standing, but Thor, Strange, Wanda, Peter, Steve, Bruce and the others were still between Thanos and any path back to the Stones.
For the first time since arriving in Wakanda, retreat became the better option.

One of the surviving Black Order transport craft from the invasion was still grounded beyond the battlefield. Thanos forced his way toward it while the others tried to stop him. Mark attempted to follow, but his body finally gave out. He dropped to one knee. Peter caught him before he hit the ground.
Thanos escaped.
The battle was over. The Snap never happened. No sudden silence across the universe. No billions of people disappearing. No Avengers standing helplessly as their friends turned to dust.
Mark needed extensive time to recover from the injuries he had suffered on Titan and Wakanda. Peter stayed with him while the surviving heroes dealt with everything that had happened.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Vision survived.

Tony recovered from his injuries. He had come closer to dying on Titan than most people knew, and the only reason he was still alive was because Strange had made the same trade he would have made regardless of whether Mark was there. Vision survived because Shuri had finished separating the Mind Stone before Wanda destroyed it. Mark understood how close both of them had come to dying. That didn't make any of it easier to watch.
For Mark, the strangest part came afterward.

He had entered this universe expecting to spend the rest of his life trying to find a way home. Instead, he had become involved in a war that had nearly destroyed the Earth. He had fought alongside people he'd never heard of before arriving. He had nearly died beside a teenager who had become one of the first people in this universe he genuinely trusted.
Mark still wanted to go home. Nothing had changed about that. His mother was still in another universe waiting for a son who didn't know when he was coming back. That weight hadn't gone anywhere.

Thanos was still somewhere in the universe, alive, but the five Stones he had brought to Earth were now inside the recovered Gauntlet in the Avengers' possession. The Avengers had prevented the Snap, but they hadn't ended the threat forever. They had bought themselves time. That time existed because Mark had been there. Not because he had defeated Thanos alone — he hadn't, and he never could have. But because he had changed enough moments for the heroes to reach a different outcome.
Mark Grayson had tumbled into this universe broken and bleeding, with no way home and no reason to trust any of it.

scripts.title: What If Iron Man Failed In 2008

sections.name: INTRO
paras: By the time Iron Man opened in May 2008, Marvel had already spent years trying to change the way it made money from movies.

Spider-Man was making billions for Sony. The X-Men had become one of Fox’s biggest franchises. Marvel owned the characters, but other studios were financing the films and keeping most of the upside. So Marvel decided to take a much bigger risk and start producing movies itself.
Iron Man was the first real test of whether that idea could work.
In our timeline, it did. The movie became a hit, Robert Downey Jr. turned Tony Stark into one of the biggest characters in Hollywood, and Marvel suddenly had a reason to keep going.
But if the exact same movie had opened to weak ticket sales, Marvel would’ve been in a difficult position almost immediately.

The Incredible Hulk was already finished and coming out 6 weeks later, so Marvel couldn’t simply abandon the experiment. At the same time, the company still had much bigger plans sitting in development, including Thor, Captain America and eventually the Avengers.
Those movies only made sense if Marvel could prove people wanted to see these characters.
If Iron Man failed, the company would have to make that decision before it had much time to recover.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: A weak Iron Man opening wouldn’t have given Marvel much time to respond. The Incredible Hulk was already finished and scheduled for June 13, 2008. Universal was handling distribution, the marketing campaign was already moving, and Marvel had already spent the production money. Whatever the company thought about Iron Man, Hulk was still going to theaters.
That made it much more important in this timeline.

If The Incredible Hulk performed well, Marvel could argue that Iron Man had been the wrong character or the wrong release rather than proof that the studio model itself was broken. If Hulk also struggled, Marvel would have two disappointing releases within six weeks and very little evidence that audiences wanted a new line of Marvel-produced films.

The real movie earned about $265 million worldwide against a production budget reported around $150 million. It wasn’t a major hit even with Iron Man succeeding beside it. In this timeline, there’s no reason to assume Hulk suddenly performs better just because Marvel needs it to. A similar result would leave the company with two films that failed to generate the kind of momentum its future slate depended on.

In reality, the financing still put important film rights at risk. The $525 million facility was secured by pledging film rights tied to Marvel properties as collateral, meaning a serious financing default could put characters central to the studio's future plans at risk.
Marvel’s next problem would be deciding which projects were still worth that risk.

Iron Man 2 would become the easiest movie to question. A sequel to a film that had just disappointed at the box office would be difficult to justify at the scale Marvel originally planned. Thor and Captain America were different. Neither character had been tested yet, so cancelling them immediately would mean abandoning years of development without knowing whether either one could work.
The Avengers would be the project in the most danger.

Marvel’s plan depended on audiences becoming familiar with several individual heroes before bringing them together. If the first two releases had already struggled, spending even more money on a crossover built around those films would look far less attractive.
By the end of 2008, Marvel Studios probably wouldn’t be dead.
It would be smaller and under pressure to prove that one of its remaining characters could succeed before the interconnected plan became too expensive to defend.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: By late 2008, Marvel’s problem would be overconfidence. The company had built its new film business around a $525 million financing facility, but that money wasn’t an unlimited pool Marvel could keep drawing from forever. The facility had financial conditions attached to future borrowing, and later films would require Marvel to put more of its own money into production.
At that point, the original Phase One plan would probably start changing.

Iron Man 2 would be in the most obvious danger. In reality, Marvel moved quickly on the sequel after the first film succeeded. In this timeline, there’s no strong reason to spend another large budget trying to revive a character who had just failed to connect with audiences.
Thor and Captain America would be harder decisions.
Both films were already part of Marvel’s planned slate, but neither character had been tested in theaters yet. Marvel could still argue that one of them might succeed where Iron Man had failed.

The safer move would be to slow development, reduce budgets where possible, and avoid committing to several expensive productions at once. Marvel’s 2008 filings show that Iron Man 2, Thor, Captain America and The Avengers were all being developed as future releases, so the company wouldn’t be starting from scratch when it reconsidered them.
The Avengers would become much harder to justify.

That movie only works financially if the individual heroes create enough interest to make the crossover feel larger than any one release. After 2 disappointing films, Marvel wouldn’t have that proof. The Avengers could stay alive as a long term idea, but the rush toward a 2011 or 2012 crossover would likely stop.
Kevin Feige’s position would change with it.

He could still argue for keeping the characters connected, but the people approving budgets would now have very little evidence that audiences cared about that connection. Shared continuity might survive through smaller references and post credit scenes while Marvel focused on making one successful movie first.
The company’s next move would probably be less dramatic than selling characters off immediately.
Marvel could delay productions, look for outside financing, renegotiate parts of its existing arrangements, or bring in a larger partner willing to absorb more of the risk.
That last option becomes important very quickly because less than a year later, Disney enters the picture.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: In August 2009, Disney agreed to buy Marvel Entertainment in a deal valued at about $4 billion. That decision wasn’t based on Iron Man alone. Disney wanted Marvel’s character library, licensing business, publishing operation, merchandise potential, and access to an audience Disney wanted more of. But Iron Man had also shown that Marvel could turn a character outside the Spider-Man and X-Men tier into a major movie franchise.
In this timeline, that proof is gone.

Disney could still be interested, but the conversation changes. Marvel’s characters are valuable, while its attempt to operate as an independent film studio now looks much riskier. If Disney still completes the acquisition, that weakness could push the purchase price lower, delay the deal, or give Disney more leverage over how Marvel’s film division is run.
The most realistic outcome probably isn’t Disney shutting Marvel Studios down completely.

If Disney still completes the acquisition, it already has the money, distribution network, and marketing reach Marvel lacked. If Marvel’s biggest problem was the financial risk of producing expensive films on its own, Disney could solve part of that problem simply by owning the company.

That doesn’t mean Kevin Feige keeps the same freedom he eventually gained in our timeline. A Marvel Studios that had already delivered two weak releases would have much less bargaining power inside Disney. Future movies would likely face tighter budgets, more oversight, and a much stronger demand for proof before Disney committed to a large crossover.
Thor and Captain America could still survive because Disney would be buying a library of characters it had an incentive to develop. What probably changes is the pace.

Instead of racing toward The Avengers, Disney could treat each character as a separate test. If Thor works, make another Thor movie. If Captain America works, continue that franchise. Only after one or both succeed does a crossover become worth revisiting.

The studio might survive the failure of Iron Man, but the version that survives would be less independent and much more cautious. The idea of connecting everything could remain alive inside the company without becoming the central business model.
And if The Avengers never reaches theaters in 2012, the consequences stop being limited to Marvel.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The biggest industry change would probably come in 2012.

In our timeline, The Avengers made more than $1.5 billion worldwide and proved that separate superhero films could feed into one larger event. After that, every major studio had a reason to study the model. Warner Bros. pushed harder toward connecting its DC characters. Sony looked for ways to expand Spider-Man beyond one hero. Universal later tried to connect its classic monsters.
Without that success, studios lose the clearest example that this kind of planning can work on a large scale.

Superhero movies would still be everywhere. The Dark Knight had already become a major hit in 2008, and Spider-Man and the X-Men were established franchises before Marvel Studios existed. The genre wouldn’t disappear because Iron Man failed.

Warner Bros. would still have Batman, Superman and the rest of DC, but there’d be less pressure to rush those characters toward a crossover. Man of Steel could still happen. A new Batman could still appear after Christopher Nolan finished his trilogy. The difference is that Warner Bros. wouldn’t have a $1.5 billion Avengers movie sitting across town proving that a team up was worth accelerating toward.

Sony would face a similar situation. Spider-Man was already valuable enough to support sequels and reboots on his own. Without Marvel showing how much money could come from a larger connected world, Sony would have less reason to build an entire film strategy around supporting characters and villains who had never carried movies themselves.
The change wouldn’t stop every shared universe from happening. Godzilla and Kong, for example, had decades of crossover history that existed long before the MCU.
What disappears is the assumption that every valuable property should become one.
Hollywood would still make sequels, spin offs and franchises. It would just have less evidence that audiences wanted several different series tied together into one continuing story.

That could make the 2010s look much more fragmented. Batman would be Batman. Spider-Man would stay mostly inside Spider-Man movies. The X-Men would continue under Fox. Marvel’s own characters might exist in several smaller franchises instead of one enormous timeline.
And that would change the people attached to Marvel just as much as the movies themselves.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Robert Downey Jr. would still come out of 2008 in a better position than he entered it.

Even if Iron Man disappointed financially, his performance could still be one of the most praised parts of the movie. Tropic Thunder would also arrive later that year and earn him an Academy Award nomination. His comeback wouldn’t suddenly disappear.

Without a successful Iron Man franchise, Downey probably doesn’t become the face of the largest film series in Hollywood. He also loses the enormous negotiating power that came from returning as Tony Stark across sequels and Avengers movies.

That doesn’t mean he leaves blockbusters behind. Sherlock Holmes was already another major studio project, and its success could still give him a commercial franchise. His career would probably remain a mix of large movies and smaller roles rather than becoming so closely tied to one character.
Kevin Feige’s future would be less secure.

His influence grew because Marvel’s strategy kept working. Iron Man succeeded, the later films held together, and The Avengers eventually proved that the shared structure could generate something much larger than the individual franchises.
Remove those results and Feige has less evidence that his approach deserves more control.

If Disney still acquires Marvel, he could remain involved in production, but he’d likely be operating inside a more cautious system. Disney might still value his knowledge of Marvel’s characters while giving senior executives much more control over budgets and release decisions.

The interconnected idea could survive with him. It just wouldn’t have the same power behind it. That difference matters because the MCU was built through accumulation. Each successful movie made the next experiment easier to approve. Without that chain of successes, Feige could spend years trying to reach the same destination through smaller projects, or Disney could eventually decide that individual franchises were producing better returns.
Either way, the version of Marvel Studios that made The Avengers, Guardians of the Galaxy, and eventually Infinity War would be much less likely to develop on the same schedule.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Sony and Fox would become even more important to Marvel’s presence in theaters.

Fox already had the X-Men, and Sony already had Spider-Man. Those franchises didn’t depend on Marvel Studios succeeding. Both studios had their own contracts, their own production teams, and their own reasons to keep making movies as long as audiences kept buying tickets.
The biggest difference would come later.

In our timeline, Marvel Studios eventually became successful enough to negotiate Spider-Man into the MCU through Sony. Without that success, there’s little reason to expect the same arrangement. Sony would have much less incentive to enter a creative partnership over Peter Parker with a studio that had never built a dominant connected franchise.

That could leave Spider-Man entirely under Sony for much longer. The studio might continue with direct sequels, reboot again when necessary, or try different spin offs around characters it already controlled. Some of those ideas could still happen, but they wouldn’t be built around joining a larger Marvel universe.
Fox would also face less pressure to make the X-Men feel like Marvel Studios movies.

The X-Men films were already comfortable operating as their own franchise, with Wolverine spin offs and different generations of the main team. Without the MCU becoming the standard everyone was compared against, Fox could keep following that model for longer.
That doesn’t guarantee better movies or cleaner continuity. The studio would still make its own decisions, and some of the same problems could still appear.
What changes is the target.
There’s no Avengers benchmark pushing every Marvel property toward larger crossovers, cosmic threats, and a single shared timeline.

Characters like the Guardians of the Galaxy would probably remain far less famous. Thanos would stay a character known mainly by comic readers unless another studio found a completely different reason to use him. Even Iron Man could return eventually, but he’d be remembered as a character from an unsuccessful 2008 experiment rather than the center of modern superhero cinema.
By the middle of the 2010s, audiences could still have plenty of superhero movies. They just wouldn’t be watching one connected Marvel story unfold across all of them.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: By the late 2010s, Hollywood would still be dominated by franchises. That trend was already much bigger than Marvel. Fast & Furious, Mission: Impossible, Transformers, Jurassic Park, Star Wars, and other long-running series would still give studios plenty of reasons to favor familiar properties.
What changes is the structure of those franchises.

Without The Avengers proving that several separate movies could be combined into one larger event, studios would have less reason to build entire slates around future crossovers. Post credit scenes might still exist, but they probably wouldn’t become such a common way to advertise another movie years in advance. Studios would be more likely to focus on direct sequels and spin-offs that could stand on their own.

DC would probably feel this difference the most. Warner Bros. would still want Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman and its other major characters in theaters, but the pressure to get them into the same movie as quickly as possible would be lower. A connected DC universe could still happen eventually, but there’d be less reason to treat Marvel’s release schedule as something that had to be matched.

Some other shared universes would still appear for reasons unrelated to Marvel. Godzilla and Kong already had a long history together. Horror franchises had crossed characters over before 2008. Studios had been experimenting with connected properties for decades.
The MCU changed how aggressively Hollywood pursued the idea.
Without it, the cinematic universe becomes one option instead of the default ambition attached to every large collection of intellectual property.
That also changes what kinds of superheroes get expensive movies.

Marvel’s success proved that characters with limited mainstream recognition could become major attractions if audiences trusted the larger brand. Without that trust, studios would be more cautious about spending huge amounts on something like Guardians of the Galaxy. The safest characters would keep receiving most of the attention.
Batman would still be important.
Spider-Man would still be important.
The X-Men would still be important.
The gap between those established names and everyone else would be much harder to close.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Marvel Studios probably survives in some form.
That’s the biggest difference between a realistic version of this timeline and the idea that one failed movie immediately destroys the company.

Marvel still owns valuable characters. It still has licensing revenue, publishing, merchandise, and relationships across Hollywood. Even after 2 disappointing films, there would still be reasons for another company to invest in Marvel or for Marvel to keep experimenting with lower risk productions.
What probably dies is the original speed of the plan.

A failed Iron Man followed by an average or weak Incredible Hulk would make it much harder to justify moving directly into expensive solo films and then an Avengers crossover. Marvel would need another successful movie before the interconnected strategy regained credibility.

Disney could provide that second chance if the acquisition still happens. With Disney’s money behind it, Marvel Studios could continue without relying so heavily on the independent financing model that made the original gamble so dangerous.
The result would likely be a slower and more supervised version of Marvel Studios.

Thor or Captain America might become the movie that finally works. If one of them became a major hit, Marvel could gradually return to the crossover idea. An Avengers movie might still happen eventually, but later and under very different circumstances.

There’s also a real possibility that the connected plan never becomes the center of the business. Disney could decide that separate franchises are safer and allow successful characters to continue on their own.
Either way, the Hollywood we know doesn’t develop on the same schedule.

The importance of Iron Man wasn’t that Marvel would have vanished without it. The movie gave Marvel proof at exactly the moment it needed it. That proof made the next gamble easier, then the one after that, until an Avengers crossover stopped looking reckless and started looking inevitable.
If the first movie had failed, Marvel would have spent years trying to earn that confidence back.
And while Hollywood might have eventually stumbled into shared universes anyway, Marvel forced the entire industry to accept that blueprint decades ahead of schedule.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Iron Man failing in 2008 probably wouldn’t have killed Marvel Studios overnight. The company had too many valuable characters, too many existing business lines, and too much development already underway for everything to disappear after one bad release.
What it would have changed was Marvel’s willingness to keep taking the same kind of risk.

Without a successful Iron Man, The Avengers becomes much harder to reach on schedule. Disney’s interest in Marvel could still exist, but the studio division would enter that relationship from a weaker position. Kevin Feige would have less freedom, Robert Downey Jr. would never become the center of a decade long franchise, and characters like the Guardians of the Galaxy might never get the chance to become household names.
Superhero movies would keep going. Batman, Spider-Man and the X-Men had already proved that.
The missing piece would be Marvel’s proof that audiences would follow several separate franchises into one larger story.
Without that example, Hollywood probably still reaches shared universes eventually.
It just takes a very different road to get there.

scripts.title: What If Iron Man Was Reborn With His Memories

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Tony Stark dies knowing he finally got it right.
Then he wakes up decades earlier with every memory still intact.

He remembers Afghanistan, the Avengers, Ultron, Civil War, Thanos, the Snap, and the moment that killed him. He also remembers Pepper as his wife and Morgan as his daughter, even though neither of those relationships exists yet in this version of his life.

This time, Tony already knows what's coming, but changing even one of those events could make everything he remembers after it less reliable. Saving his parents, avoiding Afghanistan, or stopping Ultron before it exists might fix one mistake while creating another problem he never had to face the first time.
And Tony Stark has never been very good at leaving a problem alone once he thinks he can fix it.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Tony’s first few minutes back would be spent trying to prove to himself that this is real. His body feels wrong because it’s younger, his chest is clean, and the room around him belongs to a life he hasn't seen in decades. Once he gets to a computer and checks the date, the confusion disappears fast. It's 1991, Howard and Maria are still alive, and Tony has been dropped into his own life only months before the night that destroyed his family.

He’d remember December 16 immediately. He saw the footage of Bucky stopping their car, killing Howard, and strangling Maria, and that date stayed with him long after the Civil War fight ended. Back then, Tony reacted to the truth while he was standing in front of the man who did it. Now he has years of memories that came after that moment, including everything he learned about HYDRA controlling Bucky and everything Steve tried to explain to him.

Tony wouldn’t spend much time wondering whether he should interfere. He knows exactly what losing his parents did to him, and he also knows their deaths were part of a larger HYDRA operation.
