That could be the first real argument between them. Butcher would tell Yuji that leaving Supes alive is how Vought keeps winning, while Yuji would see somebody who has spent so long fighting monsters that he’s started deciding what people deserve before they get a choice.
The situation would get worse when Vought arrives.

Instead of trying to arrest the Supe publicly, company security would immediately focus on controlling the evidence and identifying Yuji. The injured hero would be moved into Vought custody, witnesses would be separated, and Yuji would hear employees talking about the incident like a publicity problem rather than a crime.
That would settle a lot of the uncertainty Annie created earlier. Vought knows what this man has been doing and cares more about preventing another scandal than the people he hurt.

Yuji still wouldn't decide that tearing down the entire company is something he can do with his fists. He’s strong enough to beat most people Vought sends after him, but decades of experience would tell him that destroying a building doesn’t destroy the system running out of it. He'd want names, records, and proof that can’t disappear when Vought decides to blame one employee.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Vought would stop treating Yuji like an unknown curiosity once footage from the second incident reaches them. The first video only showed him catching debris and moving quickly. The next one shows him taking hits from a Supe, putting that person down without visible effort, and then standing between the body and Butcher when the situation is already over.

Ashley would want him contained before more videos appear, while different people inside Vought would disagree about what “contained” means. Someone whose powers don’t come from Compound V could become a research target, a public relations problem, or a possible new hero depending on how cooperative he is. Homelander would care for a much simpler reason: there’s a powerful person walking around New York that Vought can’t explain and apparently can’t order around.

Their first meeting shouldn’t happen in Vought Tower. Yuji could be helping at the scene of an apartment explosion after hearing it from several blocks away. He gets people out before the fire department can reach the upper floors, carries part of a collapsed wall away from trapped residents, and stays until everyone he can hear inside is accounted for. By the time Homelander arrives, most of the actual rescue is already finished.

Homelander would immediately understand why Vought sent him. Yuji looks young, has no costume, isn’t trying to get in front of the cameras, and just moved enough concrete to make it obvious that the first videos weren't exaggerated. Homelander could approach him like he’s welcoming another Supe into the club, asking who trained him and which company he belongs to while cameras gather around them.

Yuji wouldn't know enough about Homelander personally to hate him yet. He’d recognize him as Vought's biggest hero and probably assume the public reputation has at least some truth behind it, even after everything Annie and Butcher have shown him about the company. He also wouldn't act impressed just because everyone else around them does.

When Homelander asks where the powers came from, Yuji could explain that they didn’t come from Compound V. That would be the first answer that genuinely gets Homelander’s attention because Vought has built its entire understanding of superheroes around the drug that created him.

Homelander might test him without making it look like a fight. He could squeeze Yuji’s shoulder much harder than a friendly gesture requires or step into his space waiting for the usual nervous reaction. Yuji would notice exactly what he’s doing, but he’s spent his life standing in front of curses and sorcerers who wanted him dead, so intimidation from a stranger isn't going to make him react the way Homelander expects.
Yuji wouldn’t challenge him either. He’d just move Homelander’s hand off his shoulder and go back to checking whether the paramedics need help.

That small reaction would probably annoy Homelander more than an insult. Yuji isn’t trying to prove he’s stronger, and there’s no crowd pleasing rivalry Homelander can turn into television. He simply doesn’t treat him like someone who gets to control the room.

Homelander could leave without starting a fight because doing it in front of cameras makes no sense, especially when Vought still wants to understand what Yuji is. The conversation would be enough for him to tell Ashley that he wants everything they can find on the new guy.

Yuji would have his own reason to remember the meeting. Homelander’s public smile disappears the second the cameras turn somewhere else, and the way Vought employees move around him feels different from how they treat every other Supe Yuji has seen. They aren't simply respectful around him. They're careful.

Annie would later tell Yuji why. She could explain Flight 37, what Homelander has done to people who threaten his position, and how little control Vought actually has over him when he decides he doesn’t care about the consequences. Yuji wouldn’t automatically accept every detail without evidence, but Annie has already been right about enough of Vought that he’d take the warning seriously.

That would also make him rethink the meeting outside the apartment. Homelander wasn't another corporate hero trying to size up competition. He was checking whether Yuji was someone he could intimidate before deciding what to do with him.

Yuji still wouldn't go looking for a fight. He knows almost nothing about Homelander’s actual limits, and even his own newer abilities aren't automatic answers to Supe durability. Modulo Yuji can use Shrine, Blood Manipulation, Black Flash, and the physical reinforcement he’s spent decades refining, but he’d need to see what Homelander can survive before assuming any of

those techniques can put him down. His Modulo appearances also show that his Shrine and Blood Manipulation have developed substantially since the Sukuna fight, including controlled slashes and blood attacks with far greater range than he had as a teenager.

For now, Yuji would focus on Vought itself. Annie has access from the inside, the Boys know where a lot of the bodies are buried, and Yuji is one of the few people involved who can walk into a dangerous situation without immediately worrying about whether the Supe on the other side can tear him apart.

Homelander would become the part Yuji can't ignore for much longer, especially once he realizes the strongest person in this world is also the one everyone around Vought seems most afraid to confront.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Yuji would start working with Annie and the Boys more regularly after learning what Homelander is actually like, but he still wouldn't become another member of Butcher's crew. He’d help when civilians are in danger, follow leads that could expose Vought, and step in against Supes when there’s no other option. He’d also keep pushing back whenever Butcher treats killing a Supe as the easiest answer, which would make their partnership useful without ever becoming comfortable.

Annie could use her access inside Vought to pull records on settlements, missing footage, and incidents that were quietly buried before the public ever heard about them. The Boys already know some of those stories, but Yuji would give them a way to revisit cases they normally couldn't touch because the Supe involved was too dangerous. Instead of sending Kimiko into every fight or trying to improvise another weapon, they could bring someone who can survive long enough to get people out and keep the target from disappearing.

One of those cases could involve a Supe who had been used by Vought for private security work and then quietly removed from the spotlight after several people died around him. The company never publicly admits what happened, and the man keeps working through shell contracts because he’s still useful. Yuji could go with Annie to meet one of the surviving witnesses and learn that Vought paid the family, moved the Supe somewhere else, and threatened to bury them in legal costs if they kept talking.

When the Supe realizes somebody is talking to the witness again, he could come after them before Vought has time to move either side. Yuji would meet him outside the family’s home and get a much better look at what higher end Compound V durability can handle. The man could take several reinforced punches without going down and keep fighting after being thrown
through concrete, which would force Yuji to stop treating every Supe like the one he handled earlier.

That would end the fight hard enough for the Boys to understand there’s another level to what Yuji can do. The Supe survives, but the hit leaves him unable to keep fighting, and Annie gets the family out before Vought security arrives. Yuji would also learn something useful from the exchange: Compound V can produce bodies far tougher than the first people he encountered, so assuming the same attack works on Homelander would be reckless.

Vought would hear about the Black Flash even if nobody understands what they saw. Cameras could catch the impact, the strange distortion around it, and the fact that Yuji hits a durable Supe much harder than his earlier footage suggested. Ashley would start pushing harder to identify his abilities, while Homelander would stop treating him like an interesting new face and start thinking about whether Vought has allowed a threat to grow in front of him.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Homelander wouldn’t confront Yuji immediately after that because he’d want to know what the limits are first. He could have Vought send other Supes near situations where Yuji is expected to appear, then watch footage of how he handles each one. Some would be strong, some fast, and some would have abilities that force Yuji to react differently, which gives Homelander a better picture without risking another public scene.

Yuji would notice the pattern before Vought gets everything it wants. The same company keeps placing powered people near cases Annie is investigating, and several of those encounters feel less like accidents once the Supes start testing him instead of dealing with whatever problem brought them there. He could tell Annie that Vought is trying to measure him, then deliberately stop showing everything he can do.

That would be easier for this version of Yuji because he isn’t the teenager who used to solve every problem by pushing himself harder until something broke. If an opponent can be stopped with reinforcement and normal strikes, he wouldn't reveal Shrine. If someone can be restrained without Blood Manipulation, he'd keep it hidden. The longer Vought watches him, the more incomplete their picture stays.
Homelander would eventually decide he needs a direct answer.
He could find Yuji away from cameras this time, somewhere after one of Annie’s meetings with the Boys. Homelander wouldn't bother with the friendly introduction again because he already
knows Yuji isn’t interested in Vought, and Yuji has now interfered with enough company business that pretending otherwise wastes both their time.

Homelander might start by asking why Yuji keeps involving himself in things that have nothing to do with him. Yuji’s answer would probably be simple. People were getting hurt, so he helped them. He wouldn't give Homelander a speech about justice or tell him he plans to destroy Vought, because at this point Yuji is still trying to understand how far the corruption reaches and what can actually be changed.

That answer would irritate Homelander because it puts them on opposite sides without Yuji needing to announce it. Homelander protects people when it serves his image or gives him control, while Yuji will throw himself into danger for someone he met 30 seconds ago. Neither of them has to say the comparison out loud for Homelander to feel it.

He could test Yuji physically before leaving, moving fast enough to grab him by the throat and drive him through a wall before anyone nearby can react. Yuji would take the hit, reinforce his body, and get back on his feet without giving Homelander the panic he was looking for. He still wouldn't swing back immediately because one attack doesn’t tell him whether Homelander is trying to start a full fight or simply intimidate him.
That would make Yuji take the investigation more seriously instead of pushing him toward an immediate rematch.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Yuji could start helping Annie build something Vought can’t erase with another settlement. Rather than chasing every bad Supe individually, they’d focus on records showing how the company responds after civilians are hurt. Hughie could help organize names and dates, Frenchie could trace shell companies used for payments, and Annie could identify internal Vought departments that keep appearing around the same kinds of incidents.

Yuji’s role would be keeping the people providing that evidence alive long enough for it to matter. Witnesses who once refused to talk could be more willing once they know Vought can’t simply send a Supe to scare them into silence, and Yuji wouldn't need to threaten anyone to make that work. His presence alone changes the calculation because for the first time, some of these families have someone between them and the people they're afraid of.

Butcher would still want something stronger than exposing settlements. He'd argue that Vought can survive another scandal and that Homelander can survive almost anything the public learns about him as long as nobody can physically stop him. Yuji wouldn’t disagree with the first part,

but he’d reject the idea that killing Homelander solves everything else automatically. Vought existed before Yuji ever met him, and replacing one violent Supe with another company favorite doesn't fix the system that kept creating the problem.

That disagreement could become more serious once Butcher gets access to Temp V. Yuji would immediately recognize what he’s doing even though he doesn’t understand the drug itself yet. Butcher is giving himself powers because he thinks being strong enough to fight Homelander is the only way to finish the job, and he’s willing to risk what the drug does to his body to get there. Yuji wouldn't lecture him about sacrificing himself because that would be hypocritical coming from someone who spent years doing exactly that. He'd be more concerned that Butcher is becoming willing to use the same logic he hates in Vought: take whatever power is available, accept the damage later, and convince yourself the result justifies it.

Their argument would get interrupted before either one changes the other’s mind. Vought could locate one of the witnesses Annie has been protecting and send a stronger team to retrieve the evidence before it gets released. Yuji would arrive with Butcher and Kimiko, which creates the first fight where he has to deal with several Supes at once while protecting people who can’t survive a stray hit.

One of the tougher Supes could survive several reinforced hits and force Yuji to use Shrine, but Yuji still wouldn't throw a lethal slash through him just to test his durability. He could deliberately limit the cut enough to leave a deep wound without bisecting him, then follow with close range strikes once the opening is there while Kimiko and Butcher deal with the others long enough for the witnesses to escape. The amount of punishment the Supe survives would still show Yuji that higher end Compound V bodies can take far more than the people he handled earlier.

The Boys would get the evidence out, but the fight would cost them the secrecy they had left. Vought now knows Annie is actively helping Yuji and the Boys build a case, while Homelander knows Yuji has been hiding abilities from him. That would be enough to bring the conflict into the open.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Homelander would stop waiting once the evidence starts reaching the public. Vought could still deny individual stories, attack witnesses, and flood the news with distractions, but Annie releasing internal records makes the problem harder to contain. Homelander would care less about the legal details than the fact that Yuji has become the person making everyone around him braver.
He could go after Annie because he knows Yuji will come. Yuji would arrive before Homelander can seriously hurt her, and this time neither of them would have much reason to pretend they're

only talking. Annie already knows enough to understand Homelander won't stop because somebody asks him to, while Yuji has now seen what Vought does to people who threaten the company and how much of that behavior Homelander personally reinforces.

Heat vision would force Yuji to keep moving rather than tanking everything to prove a point. He can reinforce and heal, but there’s no reason to stand inside a sustained beam if he can avoid it. Blood Manipulation could give him a way to interrupt Homelander at range, especially if he uses it to attack the eyes or force Homelander to move instead of expecting blood alone to pierce through his body.

Shrine would become more important once Yuji lands it directly. The slash cuts Homelander and makes him bleed, confirming that cursed techniques can meaningfully damage him even if they don't simply ignore his durability. From there, Yuji knows he has the power to hurt Homelander; the harder problem is landing enough damage while dealing with his flight, speed, heat vision, and willingness to endanger everyone around them.

Homelander would become much more dangerous once he realizes Yuji can hurt him. He’d stop trying to dominate the fight cleanly and start using everything around them, throwing Yuji through occupied buildings or moving toward civilians because he knows Yuji will break off to save them.

Yuji would leave openings every time someone else is about to die because he isn’t going to watch civilians get crushed just to keep pressure on Homelander. Homelander could exploit that repeatedly, forcing Yuji to choose between attacking him and catching debris, pulling people out of buildings, or stopping a vehicle before it hits a crowd.
That would keep the fight from becoming a simple question of who hits harder. Yuji can hurt Homelander, but Homelander is willing to use the city around them in a way Yuji never would.

The Boys and Annie would need to help with evacuation rather than trying to beat Homelander themselves. Once fewer civilians are nearby, Yuji finally gets the space to fight without constantly breaking away, and that’s where Homelander starts losing the biggest advantage he created for himself.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: A Black Flash would be the first hit that really changes Homelander’s confidence. Yuji has spent decades using cursed energy more naturally than he could as a teenager, and landing one cleanly on someone already carrying damage from Shrine would hit far harder than the strikes Homelander has been shrugging off. It still shouldn't be treated like an automatic kill, but it could break bone, stagger him badly, and prove that Yuji has enough power to finish the fight if he gets the right opening.

Yuji’s best chance to end it would come when Homelander gets angry enough to rush him directly again. Yuji has spent most of the fight learning the timing, and he could take the first hit on purpose to keep Homelander close for the follow up. A Shrine slash at close range could open the same damaged area, followed by another reinforced strike or Black Flash before Homelander can pull away.

That combination could put Homelander down once the accumulated Shrine damage and Black Flashes finally overwhelm him. Yuji wouldn't assume Homelander is dead just because he stops moving, and he also wouldn't keep attacking after the threat is clearly over. He'd refuse to execute an incapacitated Homelander, but that creates another problem immediately: nobody has a proven prison that can hold him once he fully recovers. While Homelander is unconscious and badly injured, Annie and the Boys could use access seized from Vought to move him into the strongest reinforced containment site the company has available, with Yuji staying there as the actual failsafe while the evidence is released publicly. The facility itself may not hold Homelander once he recovers, and everyone would know that. The point is to buy a temporary window in which Vought can't quietly erase the evidence, with Yuji still present if Homelander wakes before they find a longer-term solution.

Taking down Homelander still wouldn't destroy Vought by itself. The company has money, contracts, politicians, lawyers, and other Supes who were part of the system long before Yuji arrived. Annie and the Boys would need the records they collected to keep exposing how the company operated, while Yuji becomes much more useful protecting witnesses and stopping Vought from solving every problem through intimidation.

Butcher would probably hate that Yuji refuses to finish Homelander if he’s still alive, and that disagreement wouldn't disappear just because they fought on the same side. Yuji could respect what the Boys are trying to stop while still refusing to become another person who decides everyone with powers is disposable.

That's why Modulo Yuji would have a much better chance in The Boys universe than his younger self. He has the strength to survive against most Supes, the techniques to hurt opponents who can take normal physical punishment, and enough experience to avoid turning every problem into a fight before he understands it. More importantly, he’s lived long enough to know that beating the strongest person in the room doesn’t automatically fix what allowed that person to control everyone around them.

Homelander would be the hardest fight, but Vought would be the harder problem. Yuji could survive both, help break the company’s hold over the people it created, and give the Boys a way to challenge Supes without becoming exactly like the people they’re fighting.

scripts.title: What If One Below All Hulk Was In The MCU

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If one below all Hulk entered the MCU, the Avengers would think they were dealing with another version of Bruce Banner until they saw what was wearing his body. This is the future Hulk from Immortal Hulk after the One Below All has taken control, the vessel that ultimately survives into the next cosmos and becomes the Breaker of Worlds. By that point, they are dealing with something far beyond the kind of strength the MCU has faced before.

So when he appears in the MCU, hitting him harder isn’t going to get the Avengers very far. Thor and Captain Marvel can throw everything they have at him, Wanda can try getting inside his head, and Strange can start looking for a way to contain him, but they’re dealing with a Hulk whose real problem goes much deeper than his body. Every failed attempt gives the One Below All more time to tear through a universe that has no idea what just arrived.

And the Avengers can’t afford to spend the whole fight treating him like their Banner. Once Strange realizes what's behind this Hulk, the mission changes completely. They have to figure out whether the MCU has any way to contain the One Below All's vessel before the future that produces the Breaker of Worlds starts repeating itself here.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: The One Below All-possessed future Hulk arrives on Earth a few months after Endgame, when Bruce Banner is still living as Smart Hulk and the Avengers are only beginning to rebuild after Thanos. Satellites pick up a massive object entering the atmosphere without a ship, slowing only slightly before hitting an empty stretch of land hard enough to trigger earthquake warnings across several states. Bruce is called because the first clear image from the crater shows a green humanoid large enough that everyone immediately assumes another Hulk has somehow been created.

Bruce reaches the impact zone with Sam and a small Avengers response team while the military keeps its distance. From a few hundred feet away, the creature looks close enough to Hulk that Bruce understands why everyone called him, but the resemblance gets worse the longer he looks. The face is his, the body is built like Hulk, and the gamma readings are stronger than anything Bruce has ever measured from himself, yet the person standing in the crater shows none of the anger, confusion, or aggression Bruce associates with his own transformations.

Bruce tries speaking first because he still thinks there could be another Banner inside. He introduces himself, asks whether the creature understands him, and mentions Hulk by name, hoping for any reaction that proves there is a person behind the body. The Breaker of Worlds looks at Bruce for several seconds and then turns toward the nearest population center without answering, which tells Bruce more than a roar or attack would have.

Sam starts clearing every road in that direction while Bruce moves in front of the creature and tries again. He keeps his hands down and tells it that nobody needs to fight, but the future Hulk reaches out and throws him aside with one casual movement. Bruce crosses miles
before hitting the ground, tearing through trees and rock hard enough that he needs several seconds before he can even push himself upright.

The hit tells Bruce how badly they misunderstood the situation. His own Hulk has fought Thor, survived enormous impacts, and taken punishment that would kill almost anyone else, but this thing moved him without effort and immediately returned to the same path it had chosen before Bruce arrived. It has no interest in proving it is stronger, and it does not follow Bruce after putting him out of the way.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Strange arrives after Bruce sends him the gamma data and footage from the crater. Bruce expects him to focus on the physical similarities between the 2 Hulks, but Strange is more interested in what his magic detects underneath the gamma signature. The future Hulk is physically present on Earth, yet the radiation seems entangled with something that does not belong to ordinary space, as though the body carries a metaphysical seam to somewhere outside the MCU.

He examines that seam from a distance instead of immediately using the Mirror Dimension or trying to remove the creature’s soul. Strange has dealt with possession, astral projection, and beings from other dimensions, but this does not behave like a second personality sitting inside a human body. The Hulk in front of them feels more like a vessel marked by a connection rooted in its gamma nature, and the deeper Strange follows it, the less it resembles any normal mind he could separate from a host.

Bruce compares Strange’s description with the gamma readings and finally understands why his instruments keep producing impossible results. The radiation around the future Hulk rises and falls without matching what the body itself is doing, almost as if the gamma signature includes something his instruments cannot reduce to ordinary radiation. Bruce starts treating the body as the visible end of a much larger supernatural gamma system, which means destroying tissue may solve nothing if the force behind it can keep using the vessel.

Bruce watches closely because the regeneration matters more to him than the strength. Damage that should at least slow a normal Hulk disappears before it changes the creature’s behavior, and Strange senses the outside presence becoming clearer every time the body is injured. That suggests the healing factor is only part of the problem, because whatever is connected to this Hulk is helping keep the vessel functional.
The Avengers stop trying to overpower him after that. Thor and Carol stay close enough to redirect him if he reaches civilians, while Bruce, Strange, and Wong begin working on the connection itself.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The next several hours change the situation from an Avengers emergency into a global one. The future Hulk keeps moving at a steady pace through evacuated territory, forcing governments to close airspace, clear highways, and move entire communities without knowing whether the creature intends to stop anywhere. News footage spreads faster than the Avengers can explain what is happening, and people see what looks like Bruce Banner walking through military zones while the real Bruce is appearing on emergency broadcasts asking everyone to stay away.

Strange eventually finds the pattern before Bruce does. The route is not pointing toward an Avengers facility, a major city, or any known source of gamma radiation, but it does line up with Kamar-Taj. Strange's best guess is not that ordinary portals are feeding the Hulk. It is that the intelligence behind the vessel has noticed the MCU's sorcerers probing its gamma-linked connection and is moving toward the people most capable of interfering with it.

Kamar-Taj begins evacuating before the future Hulk is anywhere near it. Wong moves students, relics, and records into separate safe locations while Strange prepares wards meant to study and contain the specific supernatural signature he has been sensing around the vessel. Bruce joins them because he needs to understand why something powered by gamma radiation would react to magic at all.

Wanda arrives while the evacuation is happening and immediately asks whether anyone has found a living mind inside the creature. Bruce tells her the body belongs to another version of him, but Strange cannot tell whether any Banner consciousness survived what took control of it.

Wanda offers to make contact from a distance while Strange monitors the gamma-linked seam and Bruce watches every change in the field. Nobody treats this as a rescue attempt yet. They first need to know whether there is still a person to rescue.

The moment Wanda touches the mind, she finds fragments of Banner everywhere: childhood, rage, fear, and years of fighting with Hulk. But the fragments behave like memories left inside the vessel, not a buried consciousness answering her. Wanda keeps searching for the person those memories belonged to and finds only a much larger darkness occupying the space where that person should be.

She also sees pieces of a future that none of them were prepared for. There are dead worlds, empty stretches of space, and the same Hulk-shaped vessel moving through a universe that has already lost almost everything around it. Wanda cannot tell which images are memories or impressions from the force behind him, so Strange cuts the connection before she gets pulled any deeper.

Wanda tells Bruce that the body came from a future where this process did not stop with Earth. She found Bruce's memories inside it, but no separate Bruce responding from beneath the presence. What she felt around those memories was larger than Hulk and far older than the life Bruce recognizes as his own. Bruce starts digging through what Wanda brought back, looking for any name or idea that might explain what his counterpart became.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The name Bruce finds is the One Below All. It appears repeatedly around the pieces Wanda recovered, attached to memories of gamma energy, death, and a place beneath the ordinary structure of reality. Bruce cannot verify every part of what he is seeing, but there is enough consistency for Strange and Wong to take the idea seriously instead of treating it like damaged memories from another universe.

Bruce and Strange test that theory without putting anyone else in front of the Hulk. Instead of simply closing portals, Strange layers wards around the gamma-linked seam he has been sensing while Bruce watches the field. The readings distort within seconds, and the creature turns toward Strange, giving them their first clear proof that there is deliberate intelligence behind the vessel and that it notices attempts to interfere with the connection.

The future Hulk changes course and starts following Strange himself. That does not prove normal dimensional travel powers the connection; it proves the presence behind Hulk can recognize when Strange is touching the specific supernatural structure around its gamma signature.

Strange leads it away while Thor and Carol remain ready to keep the Hulk from reaching populated areas. He uses portals only for the Avengers' own movement and keeps them well away from the vessel, while Bruce compares the gamma readings against each attempt to probe the seam directly. The strongest spikes come from the magical interference itself, not from ordinary travel between two places.

They test that idea with the Mirror Dimension because Strange can control the environment without sending the Hulk somewhere inhabited. The future Hulk enters and immediately turns on Strange, but the important result appears in Bruce's readings: the abnormal gamma signature and the presence behind it remain attached even after the body has been removed from normal space.

The attempt still gives them useful information. Dimensional relocation by itself does not sever whatever links the vessel to the One Below All. Strange now knows he cannot simply put the future Hulk in the Mirror Dimension and call the problem solved, while Bruce has confirmation that the connection survives being moved out of ordinary space.

Their remaining option is far riskier. Strange could use the Mirror Dimension and layered wards to isolate the vessel long enough for Wanda to examine what remains inside without assuming that relocation itself breaks the connection. Bruce knows there is no guarantee she will find a recoverable Banner, but he also knows that punching the body until the universe runs out of stronger heroes will get them nowhere.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: The Avengers move the operation far away from Earth before attempting another probe. Carol and Thor spend a prolonged fight repeatedly driving the future Hulk away from populated space and toward an off-world route Strange has prepared, never pretending either of them can simply carry an actively resisting vessel wherever they want. Strange handles the final displacement toward an empty moon and prepares a layered magical containment field around the vessel, while Wanda waits beside Bruce for the moment the gamma-linked seam becomes easiest to examine. Bruce has spent the entire trip studying the memories Wanda recovered because he wants to know whether any coherent part of his counterpart survived.

Strange closes the containment field around the Hulk while Carol and Thor break away. He presses directly against the specific gamma-linked seam he identified earlier, and Bruce's instruments immediately jump beyond their previous limits as the supernatural signature becomes easier for Strange and Wanda to distinguish from the body's ordinary radiation.
The change is brief, but it gives Wanda a cleaner path into the residual memories without pretending that an ordinary portal has exposed a weakness.

Wanda enters the mind again with Strange anchoring her to their side. She passes through the same broken memories as before, but this time she can separate more of Banner's history from the presence occupying the vessel. She follows every trace that feels like Bruce and waits for something to answer her.

Nothing does. The memories react because the vessel still contains the life Banner lived, but Wanda cannot find an independent consciousness behind them. She realizes the horrifying possibility is the simplest one: the One Below All is not suppressing a recoverable Bruce at this stage. It is wearing what remains after Bruce is gone.

Wanda stays long enough to pull one more sequence from the memories. She sees the One Below All using Hulk as a vessel far into the future, long after the people Banner once knew are dead, and understands that the body in front of them is the result of a process that has already reached its endpoint in that reality. Whatever resistance Banner once offered happened before the vessel reached the MCU.

The presence notices Wanda before she can search further. Strange feels the gamma-linked seam surge against his containment and pulls her out while Carol and Thor move back in. The future Hulk turns toward them with a clear purpose, and Bruce realizes their experiment has finally done something the earlier attacks never managed to do: they got the attention of the thing behind Hulk.

Now Bruce knows his counterpart's memories survived even though the person apparently did not, Strange knows the gamma-linked seam can be interfered with locally, and Wanda knows the One Below All is aware of them. The Avengers have finally found something they can test, but doing it again means reaching directly toward the same force that erased another Bruce Banner.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Bruce stops thinking about the future Hulk as another version of himself once Wanda confirms that she cannot find a surviving Banner consciousness inside him. The memories she pulled out show a life that once belonged to Bruce, but at this stage they appear to be residue carried by the vessel rather than a person waiting to regain control. Earth has inherited the endpoint of that process instead of catching it early enough to save him.

That changes what Strange is willing to attempt. He no longer wants Wanda digging through the Hulk's mind every few minutes, because each contact gives the force behind him another look at how the MCU's magic works. Wanda agrees after admitting that the second connection felt easier for the One Below All to notice than the first.

There is no reason to keep risking Wanda in search of a Banner she has already failed to find. Their next plan has to target containment of the vessel and its gamma-linked seam, not a rescue from inside.

Bruce focuses on the gamma side while Strange studies the supernatural side, and their notes keep pointing toward the same problem. The Hulk's body is physically in the MCU, but its gamma signature contains a metaphysical component Strange can touch without understanding its true source. Bruce cannot prove the One Below All is literally sending power through a doorway every second, but the readings change when Strange directly interferes with that seam, which gives them something local to test.

Bruce wants to take that much further and build a region where Strange's wards press against the gamma-linked seam from every direction. Strange warns him that the MCU has never contained anything on the scale they are talking about, especially a vessel whose true source may exist beyond the universe they can reach. Their goal becomes creating a short disruption in the local connection, then seeing whether the body changes.

Carol moves the future Hulk away from Earth again while Thor keeps his attention whenever he turns back. They lead him toward an empty stretch of space Strange selected because there are no inhabited worlds nearby and because Wong can establish the containment wards without putting Kamar-Taj at risk.

Once he reaches the chosen area, Wong and the other sorcerers activate the wards together. They are not closing generic dimensional routes; they are concentrating everything Strange learned onto the specific supernatural gamma seam around the vessel. Wanda watches from outside the sealed zone without entering his mind. Bruce's equipment catches the first real change they have seen since the creature arrived.
The gamma output falls.

It only lasts a few seconds before the readings recover, but the Hulk reacts during those seconds. His movements hesitate and his posture changes, suggesting Strange can disrupt the vessel's local supernatural gamma state even though nobody knows whether the One Below All itself has been weakened at all. Strange tells everyone to remember exactly what happened: they may have found a way to interfere with the connection locally, not a way to hurt the entity behind it.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Bruce spends the next several hours trying to understand why the drop happened. He compares it against every earlier test and realizes the change only appeared when Strange deliberately pressed his wards against the gamma-linked seam.

Ordinary portals and dimensional travel were never the weakness. The useful variable is the specific magical interference Strange developed after studying the vessel, and even that only disrupted the abnormal gamma signature for seconds. Bruce refuses to call it a weakness in the One Below All itself.

Strange stops opening portals anywhere near the future Hulk anyway, not because they feed the connection, but because every unnecessary spatial effect complicates the one signal Bruce and Strange are trying to isolate. The decision costs the Avengers their easiest method of redirecting the Hulk while keeping the experiment clean.

Wanda asks whether the disruption is enough to search the memories again, but Bruce says no. They already learned the important part: his counterpart's memories remain, while no recoverable Banner answered her. Bruce would rather use the brief disruption to improve containment than keep feeding Wanda into the same darkness.

Bruce refuses to treat the Quantum Realm like a magic prison simply because it is strange enough to be useful. Scott can confirm that entering it changes the normal relationship between distance and time, but he cannot promise the Hulk would become weaker there, stay trapped, or lose any connection to the One Below All.

They agree to use the Quantum Realm for one purpose only: battlefield removal. If they can push the vessel through a controlled opening and destroy their access point behind it, they may be able to strand the Hulk somewhere that does not provide an immediate route back to Earth.

The plan is dangerous because nobody knows whether the Quantum Realm can contain the vessel for minutes, years, or at all. They are not betting on it weakening the One Below All. They are betting that even an entity this powerful still needs a usable route if its physical vessel is going to return to the MCU.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Scott helps rebuild a much larger Quantum Tunnel using Wakandan power systems and the surviving designs from the original time-heist equipment. Bruce keeps the device focused on moving a single target in one direction. Nobody is trying to travel through history or test a new weakness. They need one opening large enough to force the future Hulk across the boundary and then destroy the doorway behind him.

Carol and Thor bring the future Hulk toward the tunnel after another exhausting attempt to keep him away from Earth. The Hulk has become more violent since Strange began interfering with the gamma-linked seam, but Bruce refuses to interpret that as proof the One Below All is weaker. It may simply know what the Avengers are trying to do.

They force him through the tunnel by attacking from opposite sides while Strange keeps his containment wards focused on preventing an immediate reversal. The moment the Hulk crosses into the Quantum Realm, Bruce's monitors lose most of the signal because the vessel is no longer in the same environment as the equipment. That tells them where the Hulk is, not whether the One Below All has become weaker.

Wanda does not go in after him. She already knows there is no recoverable Banner waiting for another conversation, and following the vessel into an unknown realm would only give the One Below All another target. Scott begins collapsing the tunnel the moment Carol and Thor clear the opening.

For a few seconds the future Hulk is visible through the unstable connection, still moving with the same purpose and showing no obvious sign that the Quantum Realm has diminished him. Bruce gets exactly the answer he feared: this is containment by distance and access, not a cure.

Strange reinforces the collapse from the MCU side while Bruce watches for any sign that the vessel can force the doorway wider. Nobody knows whether the One Below All can eventually create another route on its own.
That uncertainty is the entire gamble. The Avengers only need the existing tunnel to close before the Hulk can reverse direction.

The future Hulk turns toward the exit as the connection destabilizes. Carol and Thor are already clear, and Scott triggers the final shutdown while Strange compresses every ward he can around the opening.

The future Hulk hits the Quantum Tunnel from inside the Realm, and the entire system tears itself apart around the connection. Bruce watches the exit collapse before the Hulk can follow, leaving everyone staring at a dead screen while the sensors lose him completely.
For several minutes, nobody knows whether they just trapped the future Hulk or merely delayed the moment he finds another way out.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The answer almost comes when Quantum Realm energy begins spiking across systems Scott did not know were connected anymore. Strange feels pressure against several places on Earth even though every normal portal remains closed, and Bruce realizes the future Hulk may be searching for a route back through the same physics the Avengers used during Endgame. The experiment never proved the One Below All was weaker. It only put the vessel somewhere with fewer obvious doors to Earth.

Scott starts shutting down every piece of surviving quantum technology he can find. Wakanda destroys the rebuilt tunnel, Avengers equipment is physically dismantled, and Fury sends teams to secure old facilities connected to the original project. Bruce knows they cannot erase every possible route into the Quantum Realm, but reducing the number of machines capable of opening one at least removes the easiest paths back.

Wanda carries one useful conclusion from the earlier mind probes even though there is no Banner left to rescue. The vessel still contains Bruce's memories, but the One Below All is the intelligence using them now. There is no internal ally the Avengers can count on if containment fails.

Bruce does not turn those memories into a rescue plan. His counterpart appears to be gone, and pretending otherwise would only tempt them into opening another connection to the vessel. Their best chance is to keep every known route closed and respond if the Hulk finds one they missed.

Strange and Wanda prepare for one final remote watch without opening a physical portal. Wanda does not enter the Hulk's mind again; she helps Strange recognize the same supernatural signature if it presses against the MCU from the other side.
Bruce stays connected through their equipment because he wants the scientific and magical warnings compared in real time. If the vessel finds a route back, they may have only seconds to close it.

The pressure rises while the future Hulk searches the Quantum Realm for an exit. Strange cannot see the vessel directly, but the same gamma-linked signature begins gathering around a residual weak point left by old quantum research and the Avengers' own earlier access to the Realm. The Hulk is not remotely operating the machinery or creating a doorway from nothing; it is finding an existing connection that was never completely isolated.

Bruce recognizes the pattern from their earlier tests, but he does not mistake it for Banner fighting back or the One Below All weakening. Something on the other side is trying to turn a possible route into an opening.

The future Hulk eventually starts forcing that residual connection wider from its side. Strange feels the existing weak point destabilizing beneath an abandoned quantum research site, and Carol reaches the location before it opens far enough for Hulk to cross. Thor joins her while Wanda helps Strange track the supernatural pressure, giving Bruce only a few seconds to coordinate the shutdown.

Strange collapses the forming route while Carol and Thor destroy the machinery around it. The pressure on Wanda vanishes with the opening. Nobody mistakes that for defeating the future Hulk; they only know they closed one more door before the vessel crossed it.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: The Avengers spend weeks waiting for another quantum breach because nobody is willing to assume the future Hulk is gone. Bruce keeps every sensor he can build pointed toward the same fluctuations that preceded the attempted opening, while Strange watches for the supernatural gamma signature around sites most likely to overlap with quantum technology. Nothing appears, but the absence of another attack only proves that the Hulk has not found a route back yet.

Bruce refuses to call the crisis solved. Wanda found his counterpart's memories but no surviving Banner consciousness, and nothing about the Quantum Realm changed that. The last thing they know for certain is that the tunnel closed with the vessel on the other side.

Earth survives, although nobody involved believes they defeated the One Below All. Strange never reached the entity itself, Wanda never overpowered it, and Thor and Carol never came close to permanently destroying the body it was using. They used the Quantum Realm as battlefield removal and then destroyed the routes they knew how to control.
That is containment, not a discovered weakness. They have no evidence that the One Below All's hold became weaker inside the Quantum Realm, only that its physical vessel has not returned yet.

That answer is much worse than the Avengers usually get after winning. The future Hulk still exists somewhere inside the Quantum Realm unless something there destroys him, and nothing the Avengers used in this crisis demonstrated a way to directly kill the One Below All. Opening the wrong quantum route in the future could give the Hulk another path back, which means the Avengers have to treat some of their own technology as a potential doorway from that point forward.

Bruce takes responsibility for tracking those risks because the vessel is still the body of another version of him, even if Wanda could not find that person's consciousness anymore. He works with Scott and Wakanda to identify every surviving system capable of reaching the Quantum Realm, and Strange keeps records of the supernatural gamma behavior they saw around the Hulk. They cannot guarantee that no route will ever open again, but they can make sure nobody casually rebuilds the same doorway without understanding what could be waiting behind it.

The fight also changes how Bruce sees the Hulk in himself. He has spent years learning to live with his own anger and power, while the future vessel showed him a version of that existence where Bruce eventually lost everything that made the body his. He keeps studying the supernatural side of gamma with Strange because he has now seen enough to know that his science alone does not explain every version of what Hulk can become.

If the One Below All-possessed Hulk had arrived and simply stayed on Earth, the Avengers had no demonstrated way to permanently stop him. Thor and Carol could redirect him for a while, Wanda could read the memories left in the vessel, and Strange could interfere with its supernatural gamma signature, but none of the methods available to them in this crisis demonstrated a way to destroy the One Below All or permanently kill the body it had been using for ages. The only reason Earth survives is because the Avengers gamble on battlefield removal, force the vessel into the Quantum Realm, and close the routes they know how to control.

Even that leaves the central threat unresolved. The MCU manages to keep the future Hulk out of its universe, but it never proves that it can kill him, never establishes that the Quantum Realm weakens the One Below All, and never reaches the force responsible for creating the vessel. If that Hulk ever finds another way out, Earth is right back where it started, except this time the thing coming for them already knows exactly how they stopped him once.

scripts.title: What If Saitama Met Spider Man

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If Saitama met Spider-Man, Peter would probably think he was just some random guy who wandered into a fight.

I'd set this after No Way Home, with Peter living alone in New York. Saitama gets thrown into the MCU after a spatial distortion from one of his fights and lands there with no idea what happened. Peter only starts taking him seriously when Saitama casually does something impossible, like stopping a falling vehicle with one hand.
From there, Peter gets obsessed with figuring out how he’s that strong, while Saitama starts noticing how seriously Peter takes saving people even when he knows he can get hurt.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Saitama would end up in the MCU because of a monster from his own world that can distort space. I'd set this after Saitama has already dealt with enough bizarre abilities that seeing space bend around an enemy doesn’t completely throw him off. The monster keeps escaping through short tears that open between different parts of City Z, and Saitama only gets involved because one of those openings tears through a grocery store he was heading toward. He follows the monster through 2 of its portals, catches up, and punches it just as it tries to open another one.

The monster dies instantly, but the portal doesn’t close with it. The tear starts collapsing while Saitama is still partly inside, and the space around him folds in on itself before he can jump back. A second later, he drops onto the roof of an apartment building in New York hard enough to crack the concrete. Saitama gets up expecting another part of City Z, looks around, and realizes immediately that none of the buildings, signs, or streets match anywhere he knows. His phone doesn’t connect to the Hero Association network, there are no monster alerts, and even the skyline is wrong. He walks to the edge of the roof, looks down at the traffic below, and starts piecing together that the portal sent him much farther than another district. Saitama doesn’t panic because that really isn’t how he reacts to anything anymore. He mostly looks annoyed that he has no idea how he is supposed to get home.

This is post No Way Home Peter, so Spider Man is already back to working alone in New York. He has no Avengers team around him, no one remembers Peter Parker, and most of his nights are spent dealing with whatever problems he runs into while patrolling. He notices the impact on the rooftop because it is loud enough to shake windows below, swings over expecting an explosion or someone hurt, and instead finds a bald guy in a yellow suit standing beside a crater while checking a phone that clearly is not working.

Before Peter can get much further, police sirens start getting louder several blocks away. Peter heads toward them and expects Saitama to stay behind, but Saitama jumps after him and clears several buildings in one shot. That is the first moment Peter realizes the guy beside the crater probably was not exaggerating about anything.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The sirens are coming from an armored truck robbery that has already gone wrong. One of the thieves clips another car trying to get away, the truck jumps the curb, and it starts sliding toward a crowded intersection. Peter reaches it first, fires webs around the front axle, then anchors himself to a streetlight to pull the truck away from the people crossing.

He manages to slow it, but the truck is heavy enough that he is still getting dragged forward. Peter adds another web line and keeps pulling while the people ahead start clearing out. Saitama lands near the intersection, sees the truck coming toward him, and simply puts one hand against the front of it.

The truck stops so hard that the back wheels lift off the road before crashing back down. Peter is still attached to it when it happens, and the part that gets him is how little effort Saitama seems to use. Peter knows what it feels like to stop vehicles and hold several tons of weight, so he can tell right away that Saitama is operating on a completely different level.

One of the thieves climbs out and fires at Saitama before Peter can reach them. The bullet hits Saitama and does absolutely nothing, and he barely reacts before Peter handles the robbers himself, webbing the gun away and knocking both men down before they can hurt anyone else. That matters because Peter is still doing what he normally does instead of standing around while Saitama solves every problem for him.

Once the police take over, Peter follows Saitama because the portal story now sounds a lot more believable. He starts trying to understand where Saitama’s strength comes from, assuming there must be some kind of enhancement, experiment, or technology involved. Saitama gives him the same training explanation he gives everyone, and Peter spends several seconds waiting for the part that would make it scientifically possible.
There is no other part.

Peter is convinced Saitama is messing with him, but Saitama really does not care enough to invent a better answer. He explains that he is a hero back home, that monsters appear all the time, and that he usually deals with them when they get in the way. Peter starts realizing that Saitama being absurdly strong is probably the least confusing thing about him.

The portal itself is what keeps Peter interested. If a spatial tear moved Saitama between universes, Peter wants to know whether it left anything behind and whether another one could open. Saitama also wants a way home, so they finally have a reason to stick together beyond Peter being curious.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter takes Saitama back to his apartment and starts going through everything he can find from the time Saitama arrived. The place is small, full of homemade equipment, spare web fluid, tools, and whatever electronics Peter can afford to keep around. Saitama notices the setup but does not make a big deal out of it, while Peter immediately starts digging through traffic cameras, power logs, and local reports.

He finds a brief electrical disturbance around the exact block where Saitama appeared, along with several frames from a camera that caught the air above the rooftop bending inward just before he landed. Peter zooms in and realizes the distortion is not behaving like a normal explosion or electrical discharge. The image bends toward one point, collapses, then snaps back.

Peter builds a small sensor from equipment he already has and goes back to the rooftop with Saitama. The readings around the impact point are weak at first, but instead of fading they slowly start getting stronger. Peter checks the numbers again because that should not be happening if the portal was completely gone.

Asmall tear opens several feet above them and lasts less than a second, but a chunk of broken concrete drops through and smashes onto the roof. Saitama recognizes the material from City Z, which confirms the tear is still connecting both universes. A second opening appears a few blocks away almost immediately after, this time over a street, and pieces of metal start falling through toward traffic.

Peter swings over and catches one piece with webbing while Saitama grabs another before it hits a car. By the time the tear closes, Peter has enough readings to see that both openings are part of the same pattern. The original portal never fully sealed, and now it’s reopening at different points around New York.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Peter starts tracking the new tears as they appear across the city. They are still small and only last a few seconds, but every one leaves the same energy signature behind. Some open onto empty streets in City Z, while others drop pieces of debris through before collapsing again. The time between openings keeps shrinking, which tells Peter the problem is getting worse.

His first attempt to predict the next opening is wrong. He assumes the tears are simply spreading outward based on distance and sends both of them several blocks in the wrong direction, where they end up standing outside a pizza place while nothing happens. Saitama is already losing interest when Peter realizes he has been looking at the wrong variable.

Peter recalculates using both distance and the time between each opening. The next tear forms less than a block from where he predicts, this time above an empty intersection. Nothing dangerous comes through, but it gives him enough data to see that the openings are spreading outward in a rough spiral from the original rooftop instead of appearing randomly.

Saitama does not understand most of the math and does not pretend to. He only cares whether any of this gets him home faster. Peter tells him that knowing where the next tear forms gives them a chance to study one before it disappears, and that is enough to keep Saitama around while Peter keeps working through the pattern.

The next opening appears near a construction site and immediately becomes more dangerous. Part of a crane disappears through the tear while the other half stays behind, twisting the whole structure sideways with workers still hanging from it. Saitama jumps up and catches the crane before it collapses, but that only stabilizes the biggest piece.

Peter handles everything happening around it. He catches a worker whose harness snaps, webs falling steel away from traffic, and pulls loose scaffolding back against the building before it comes down on the sidewalk. Saitama can hold more weight than everyone else there combined, but Peter is the one moving between the smaller dangers before they turn into bigger ones.

That is when Saitama starts paying more attention to how Peter works. Peter is not just reacting after something goes wrong. He is constantly looking for what is about to fail next, and Spider Sense lets him move before the danger is obvious to everyone else. Saitama has spent years ending fights almost instantly, so watching someone deal with a situation where there are several problems happening at once is actually new to him.
Once the workers are safe, Peter checks the sensor again and sees a much larger spike forming. Every reading they have collected points toward one place now, and the signal is moving toward Midtown.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Peter follows the signal into Midtown and realizes the next opening is already forming before they even get there. Windows are vibrating, traffic lights are flickering, and loose objects are slowly sliding toward a point several stories above the street. Peter clears people away while Saitama helps move anything too heavy to get out quickly.

The tear opens wide enough for both of them to see City Z on the other side. Saitama recognizes the neighborhood where he killed the monster, and Peter can see that the area around that original location is distorted too. The first portal connected both worlds for only a moment, but the damage never disappeared. Every smaller opening since then has been pulling the 2 sides closer together.

The wider the portal gets, the stronger that pull becomes. Cars start lifting off the street, glass breaks out of nearby buildings, and pieces of both cities begin getting dragged toward the same point. Saitama tries hitting the edge of the distortion, expecting the force to collapse it, but the impact makes the opening expand instead.

Peter finally has enough information to understand what is happening. The tear is absorbing energy from anything that hits it, which means Saitama’s strength can actually make the problem worse if he uses it the wrong way. Peter starts working through a way to collapse the connection from both sides instead of attacking the portal directly.

That creates the first real problem they cannot solve separately. Saitama is the only one who can safely cross the unstable tear and reach the City Z side, while Peter is the one who understands enough of the pattern to coordinate what needs to happen on both ends. If Saitama leaves too early, Peter is stuck dealing with the New York side while the city is still being pulled apart. If Saitama stays, the tear keeps growing.

Peter starts putting together a plan that uses Saitama’s strength only where it helps instead of treating it like the answer to everything. Saitama watches him work while the street around them is starting to come apart and realizes Peter is still more worried about the people trapped nearby than whether the plan is going to hurt him.

That is where their relationship starts shifting. Peter has spent the entire night trying to understand how anyone could be as strong as Saitama. Saitama is beginning to understand why someone who is nowhere near that strong keeps choosing to run toward danger anyway.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Peter still doesnt have enough information to tell Saitama where to hit, so he stops treating the portal like one object and starts comparing what happened at every tear they already saw. The

smaller openings all lasted longer whenever debris crossed through them, and the Midtown tear spiked again after Saitama hit its edge. Peter cannot prove the portal is simply “absorbing force,” but he can tell that disturbing the boundary makes both sides react, so throwing more power at it without understanding the pattern would be a bad idea.

Saitama crosses first because he is the only one Peter trusts to survive if the tear suddenly shifts. Peter clips one of his homemade sensors onto Saitama’s suit and keeps another on the New York side so he can compare the readings. The signal cuts out for several seconds after Saitama crosses, which immediately makes the whole plan feel less controlled than Peter hoped, but it comes back in short bursts once Saitama reaches City Z.

Saitama drags one chunk of concrete away from the center and Peter sees the New York reading dip. When Saitama moves the same piece back, the signal rises again. Peter repeats the test with a second piece before trusting it and gets the same result. Peter cannot tell exactly why, but material closest to the rupture is clearly reinforcing the connection. One section of warped ground beneath the City Z opening produces the strongest response, giving him a physical anchor to track while the tear keeps rebuilding around it.

While Peter is working that out, Saitama notices movement underneath the wreckage in City Z. The spatial monster he killed earlier was not alone. Another creature had been following it because it fed on the energy left behind every time the first monster opened a tear. It stayed away while Saitama was fighting, then moved into the ruined area after he disappeared and started feeding on the unstable space around the original rupture.

Saitama starts toward it because killing the monster is still the obvious answer from where he is standing. Peter stops him before he gets close and explains that if the creature is full of the same energy holding the tear open, killing it right beside the rupture could dump all of that back into the connection. Saitama looks at the monster, then at the sensor Peter taped to his suit, and gives him time to come up with another way to separate the 2 problems.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Peter's first idea is to pull the creature away from the City Z opening before Saitama hits it. That falls apart almost immediately when the monster realizes the portal itself is its food source and refuses to move more than a few feet from it. Saitama tries dragging it physically, but the creature anchors parts of its body into the warped ground and starts tearing pieces of the street loose with it, making the distortion even worse.

Peter changes the plan instead of forcing the first one to work. If the creature refuses to leave the energy source, they can make the other side more attractive. Peter starts feeding controlled electrical bursts into the New York edge using equipment from nearby construction crews, keeping the output far below anything Saitama did with his punch. The portal reacts just enough for the monster to notice, and Peter watches the City Z sensor spike as its attention shifts.

Saitama stays behind it on the City Z side and keeps it from backing away whenever the current stops. He does not need to hit hard. A shove against one shoulder is enough to make the creature realize the route behind it is worse than the one in front. Peter gradually increases the time between each electrical pulse, forcing more of the monster through before it gets the next burst.

That works until the creature panics halfway through. Its front half is already hanging over New York while the rest of its body is still locked into the City Z street, and it starts thrashing hard enough to tear the edges of the portal wider. Peter has to cut the electrical feed completely before the opening grows any more, which also means the creature immediately starts trying to pull itself back.

Peter switches tactics again. He swings close enough to get its attention and starts webbing its face and eyes, then moves farther down the street every time it lashes out. The monster cannot reach him without pushing more of itself into New York, and Saitama keeps pressure from the other side so it cannot retreat cleanly.

One of the attacks clips the side of a building instead of Peter and sends part of the upper wall toward the street. Peter leaves the monster for a few seconds, catches the biggest section with webbing, and redirects it into an empty lane before swinging straight back. The creature has already started retreating by then, but Saitama has both hands against its back and simply refuses to let it move the other way.

Peter gets close enough again for the monster to follow him, and this time the last section of its body finally clears the portal. The second it does, the City Z sensor drops sharply because the creature is no longer feeding directly from the warped ground. Saitama jumps through after it and knocks it several blocks away with a controlled hit, sending it toward a wider part of Midtown instead of through the nearest building.

Peter lands beside him and checks the sensor before either of them assumes the problem is solved. The portal is still open, but the readings have stopped climbing for the first time since they reached Midtown. Peter tells Saitama they finally separated the creature from the energy source, which means hitting it is no longer going to feed the tear the same way.

Saitama looks down the street as the creature gets back up and starts moving toward them again. Peter barely has time to finish saying that this is probably the part where punching it helps before Saitama is already walking toward it.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The creature becomes much harder to control once it realizes Peter is trying to lead it away from the portal. Instead of chasing him directly, it starts attacking whatever forces Peter to turn around. A delivery truck gets thrown into traffic, Peter has to web it sideways before it hits another car, and the monster changes direction while he is distracted.

Saitama catches on before Peter has to explain it. He steps into the monster’s path and forces it back toward the open construction zone Peter has been trying to reach, using short hits that change its direction without sending it through another building. Peter notices the change and starts using smaller web attacks because he knows Saitama will cover the bigger movements. For the first time, neither of them has to stop and explain what the other should be doing.

The creature starts using the city itself once it realizes it cannot catch either of them cleanly. It slams both arms into the street and sends a shock through the surrounding buildings. Peter feels the danger through Spider Sense before he understands where it is coming from and changes direction immediately when part of an apartment facade starts peeling away.

He gets across the street before the first section falls, catches 2 people off a fire escape with webbing, and pulls loose metal away from the sidewalk while the wall keeps coming down behind them. Another slab starts dropping above Peter while his hands are already tied up, and Saitama gets there in time to hold the whole thing overhead. Peter gets the people clear, checks the windows above them for anyone else, then points Saitama back toward the creature because it is already trying to leave the area.

They finally force it into the construction zone, where the surrounding buildings are farther back and most of the workers have already evacuated. Peter still checks the area before giving Saitama the opening because he does not want to assume the site is empty just because it looks empty. Once he knows there is nobody directly behind the creature, he gets clear and lets Saitama stop holding back.

Saitama ends the fight with one punch that sends the monster straight upward instead of through the street. The impact is still ridiculous, but this time there is no collapsing building behind it, no traffic in its path, and no portal close enough to react to the force.
Peter watches the monster disappear into the sky and asks whether fights back home usually end that quickly.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: With the creature gone, the portal starts weakening because it is no longer being fed from the City Z side. Peter's sensors finally show a consistent cycle instead of random spikes. Both openings widen, contract, then widen again with the same pattern a few seconds apart. Peter's best hypothesis is that they do not need to overpower the portal at all. If they interrupt that cycle at the moment both sides contract together, the connection might finally fail to rebuild.

Saitama goes back through to City Z while the opening is still stable enough to cross. Peter leaves one sensor with him and keeps the other in New York, then starts watching the timing between both sides. The first attempt fails because Saitama moves too early and the City Z opening rebounds before New York reaches the same point. Nothing gets worse, but Peter now knows the timing has to be almost exact.

On the second cycle, part of a damaged office building near the New York side shifts toward the portal. Peter can see people still inside through the broken windows, which means he cannot just stand there watching the sensor until the perfect moment arrives. He webs himself to the building, swings across, and starts getting them out while the readings continue changing behind him.

Saitama sees Peter disappear from the sensor’s camera and understands what happened without needing another explanation. Instead of hitting the portal because the window is almost there, he waits. That would have been completely unnecessary for him at the beginning of the day, but by now he trusts that Peter is not delaying because he is unsure of himself.

Peter gets the last person clear, swings back to the sensor, and catches the next contraction starting. He calls the timing as both sides line up, testing his best hypothesis, and Saitama uses a much smaller strike directly into the physical anchor Peter identified beneath the City Z opening. The point is not to overpower the tear or hit its boundary again. The strike breaks the material reinforcing the connection at the exact moment both sides are already trying to close, leaving the portal nothing stable to rebound around.

The New York opening begins folding inward instead of expanding again. Peter anchors himself with webs while loose debris gets pulled toward the shrinking center, and Saitama moves away from the City Z side before it closes around him. The distortion collapses down to a small point, flickers once, and disappears while both sensors finally drop back to normal.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Peter stays on the rooftop for several minutes after the portal disappears because he does not trust the first clean reading. Nothing comes back. No second tear opens across the city, the electrical disturbance fades, and the pieces of City Z that crossed over stay exactly where they landed.

On the other side, Saitama is back in his own city standing beside the wrecked street where the whole thing started. He checks his phone, sees the Hero Association network again, and realizes he missed enough time that Genos has already sent him several messages asking where he went.

One last residual flicker of the collapsing connection appears between the 2 worlds before it disappears completely. It is only wide enough for Peter and Saitama to see each other, and Peter immediately uses the few seconds they have left to tell Saitama that he still does not believe 100 push ups explain anything he saw. Saitama tells him that skipping the air conditioner was important too, which does absolutely nothing to help.

Peter tells him that if another portal monster shows up, he should probably avoid punching it while standing inside the portal. Saitama admits that is fair, then looks at Peter’s torn suit and asks why he kept jumping back into the fight when he knew Saitama could handle the monster. Peter gives him a simple answer. People were still in danger, and standing around waiting for somebody stronger was never really an option for him.

Saitama understands that better than Peter realizes. He has spent years looking for opponents strong enough to make him feel something again, but Peter spent the entire day fighting things that could actually hurt him and never seemed to consider quitting because of it. Saitama does not suddenly become excited about hero work again, and Peter does not walk away wishing he had Saitama’s strength. They just understand each other a little better than they did when they met.

The tear closes before Peter can ask another question. Saitama heads home and realizes the supermarket sale he was trying to reach ended hours ago, while Peter goes back to his apartment with a damaged suit, several pieces of impossible sensor data, and absolutely no scientific explanation for how 100 squats turned anyone into that.

scripts.title: What If Spider-Man Became A Green Lantern

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Peter Parker was still learning how to live in a city where nobody knew his name when a green light came through his window.

He had been awake since midnight. His hands were producing webbing on their own now, and he had not told anyone, because there was nobody left to tell. The green light hung in the middle of the room and waited for him to put it on. It was a Green Lantern ring, and it had come a very long way to find him.

Four days earlier, a Green Lantern named Vaska Tenn had died out past the edge of Corps territory. She spent the last ninety seconds of her life holding a green wall in front of a transit lane full of sleeping passengers, so that the thing killing her could not reach them. Her ring came off her hand and began searching for a replacement. When it failed to find a qualified successor in the territory it was meant to cover, the Corps' emergency protocols widened the search into nearby unassigned and understaffed sectors. It passed over soldiers and kings and creatures who had never doubted themselves once.

Bill Metzger had been hiding since the night on Roosevelt Island. He still knew how to build a machine that switched a person's powers off, and that knowledge was the only thing he had left. But he had no idea that the Sinestro Corps were already looking for him.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: The No Way Home spell had already happened. Everyone who knew Peter Parker forgot him. Peter walked into the coffee shop and chose not to tell MJ the truth. After that, he rented a cheap apartment in Queens.
