The only things he had were a folding table, a sewing machine for his new suit, a police scanner, and E.V., the assistant he had built himself once Stark's tech was gone. She answered whenever he spoke to her. Nobody who remembered him did.
Then Damage Control came to him.

Peter took the partnership because he was alone and the agency was the first thing that had offered him help. He met a girl named Jean Grey whose sister had died inside a federal laboratory. He learned from Bruce Banner how a device could reach into a person's biology and switch their powers off. He built one himself, against Banner's advice, and he built the first one for his own body, because his body had started changing in ways he could not stop. After that he built a version that worked on anyone, and he used it on Jean Grey to stop her, and that was how Damage Control got hold of her.

Peter watched Banner lose control of himself. He fought what was left of Banner on Roosevelt Island and lost. He survived that night only because he pulled his own mask off, so that Banner would recognise his face and stop hitting him. Banner had been his professor at Empire State University. Peter took his own inhibitor off that night and did not put it back on.

The wreckage was easy to list. Bruce Banner went into a psychiatric ward under an official story that nobody believed. Jean Grey left the city on a bus. Bill Metzger disappeared during the chaos and stayed disappeared, wanted by the government, with every page of the inhibitor design still in his memory. The design was not keyed to one specific mutation: its adaptive system analyzed abnormal biological or energy activity in an enhanced subject and tuned the suppression output to that pattern. Ned shook Peter's hand outside a deli and said his name. MJ knew what Peter was and still did not remember him.

Eleven nights after Roosevelt Island, Peter could not sleep. He went down to the basement just after midnight and fixed the boiler for Mrs. Ocampo, who ran the building. He did not simply repair it. He rigged a bypass around the part that kept failing, so that it would keep running when he was not there to nurse it.

His own body had become the thing he understood least. The webbing came out of his arms now instead of his shooters. A car alarm two blocks away was loud enough to hurt. He had woken up on the ceiling twice that week with no memory of climbing up there. Bruce Banner was the only man alive who might have explained any of it, and Banner was locked in a psychiatric ward that Peter had no legal way to enter, because Peter Parker was nobody.
He went outside anyway. He always went outside. He came back in a little after two. At 2:14 in the morning, something green came through the window.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The last time something powerful had told him he was chosen, he had ended up in a workshop building a leash for a girl whose sister was already dead. So he put the ring ina coffee can and put the coffee can in a drawer. The ring came out of the drawer. He left it ina locker at the Port Authority bus terminal and it was back on his nightstand before he was.

He put it together on his folding table out of a rewired multimeter and a salvaged spectrometer head, because his first instinct with anything he did not understand had never been to hit it. The results told him nothing. The ring had no mass that made sense. It gave off no emission in any band he could detect. It sat in his makeshift cradle producing a light his equipment insisted was not there.

It also repeated one sentence every few seconds and never changed a word. It told him that Peter Parker of Earth had the ability to overcome great fear, and it welcomed him to the Green Lantern Corps.

The sentence described somebody brave. It described somebody who ran toward things. Peter had spent the previous two nights unable to sleep because of what his hands were doing, and an hour on the floor working up the nerve to open his own front door. He told the empty room that it had the wrong person, and that he was not being modest about it.
He put it on before dawn on the third night, because he had run out of other ideas. The light went up his arm and felt like cold water.

A lantern came with it, hand-sized and green, about the shape of a railway lamp. The ring drew its charge from the lantern. The lantern drew from something called the Central Power Battery, on a planet called Oa, and Peter had never heard of either. He charged the ring for the first time in a rented room with the blinds down. He put the lantern in a shoebox under his bed.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The ring ran on four things.

Willpower supplied the strength. Imagination supplied the shape. Concentration kept the shape in the air once it existed. The fourth rule mattered more than the other three for somebody like Peter. A Lantern had to actually understand the object he was building. Picturing it was not enough, and the more complicated the object became, the harder it was to hold.
Most recruits found that limiting. Peter had reverse-engineered a power suppression device in a borrowed laboratory before any of this started.
His first construct was a fist. It came out lopsided and lasted about two seconds.

The Corps had recruited builders before. Engineers, architects and field surgeons had all worn the ring, and their constructs came out looking like their work, because the ring drew on whoever wore it. Peter making things was not new. What Peter made them for turned out to be.
On his fourth night with the ring, a scaffold let go on Astoria Boulevard with two men on it.

Peter did not build a net. The problem with catching a falling body had never been the catch. It was the deceleration. A net that stopped a man instantly would kill him about as efficiently as the pavement. He needed a structure that gave way in a controlled sequence and bled the energy off as it went.
So he built a crumple zone. Thirty feet of green honeycomb, with the cells collapsing one rank at a time. Both men hit it and walked away with bruises.
Peter landed beside them and said it out loud, the way he talked to himself in a workshop. He did not want a structure that held. He wanted one that failed on purpose, in stages.

The nights after that were the best he had spent since the spell. He stopped a robbery in Jackson Heights with a compliant gripper, soft-jawed and conforming, because he had broken a man's wrist by accident once and had not forgotten it. He worked a fire on Steinway Street with a metering gate and a switchback ramp, because four hundred people trying to leave one building at once was its own problem, separate from the smoke.
He tried a ring-web exactly once. It performed worse than the ones his body now made for free, and he never tried it again.
He talked the entire time he worked. He had always talked when he was frightened, since he was fifteen, and the jokes had never been about being funny. They were what he did instead of stopping.
On the sixth night a construct came out wrong.

He had pictured a simple brace with four legs. What formed in front of him had eight, arranged the way a spider arranges them, and he had not designed a single one of them. The ring built what he imagined. Something in what he imagined had changed.
Peter stopped talking. He stood on the roof and looked at the thing his own head had made, and he told nobody about it.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Bruce Banner's window was on a secure floor of a psychiatric hospital uptown. It was sealed, high, reinforced and watched, and Peter had not been able to get near it for weeks. The ring changed that.
He did not break in. He built a lattice down the airshaft, sat on the ledge outside and talked to Bruce Banner through the glass. Nothing got broken and nobody got rescued.
Peter had come for the wrong thing. He wanted to know what was happening to his body, and Banner could not tell him, because it was certainly not Banner's week.
But Peter repeated the ring's sentence, and Banner laughed at it.

Banner told him the grammar was wrong. Overcoming was not something a person finished. Banner had been afraid of himself that morning and expected to be afraid of himself the next morning, and managing it once bought him nothing at all. He had walked into a laboratory every day of his adult life on those terms.
Banner said the other thing on his way out, and he did not mean anything by it.

A machine that switched a person off did not care what kind of person it was switching off. The people who had taken Peter's design apart to study it had not stopped existing when the agency collapsed. Somebody still had the drawings.
Peter climbed back up the airshaft in worse shape than he had gone down. The ring was brighter than he had ever seen it. He looked at it the whole way home and could not work out why.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: On the seventh night his spider-sense gave him four seconds of warning, which was more than it had ever given him, and he still nearly went off the roof.

Two of them came down through the cloud, and both of them wore green rings. The first had a body that had clearly not evolved anywhere near Earth. The second stood close to eight feet tall and wore no mask at all.
The big one landed, looked Peter over and did not seem impressed. He called him a poozer.

His trainer was Kilowog, the drill instructor of the Green Lantern Corps and the Lantern of a sector a long way from this one. Poozer meant useless rookie. Kilowog had inherited the word from his own instructor and used it on everybody.

Peter asked why the ring had picked him, and he asked it fast, because he was in trouble and talking was what he did in trouble. Eight billion people lived on the planet underneath them. Soldiers lived down there. So did people who ran into burning buildings for a living.

Kilowog told him that Sector 2814 had never received a permanent Lantern assignment. In this universe, Earth had never produced the Green Lantern history it did in other timelines, and chronic Corps understaffing had left 2814 vacant throughout the Corps' history.

Not recently lost. Never permanently filled. The sector had remained a blank line on the duty roster because it was quiet, it was far out, and there had always been worse fires elsewhere. No Sector House had ever been built there. Nobody had ever been permanently posted. The universe held three thousand six hundred sectors, with two Lanterns to a sector at full strength, and the Corps had not been at full strength in a very long time.
Peter was not replacing one of Earth's usual Lantern legends. He was the first permanent name Sector 2814 had received in generations.
They took him to Oa.

He saw the Central Power Battery, which every ring in the Corps drew from, and he saw the Guardians of the Universe, who had built it. A four-armed administrator called Salaak kept the Book of Oa and knew where every Lantern in the Corps was standing at any moment. Salaak entered him into the book as Parker, Peter, 2814.1.
It was the first time since the spell that anyone had written his name down knowing it was his. Peter watched the pen the whole time and did not say a word, which for him was unusual.

He learned the Oath after that. Almost every Lantern knew it. It did not charge the ring, because the charge came from the lantern. Lanterns said it while the charge ran, because the Corps had decided a long time ago that this was a thing a person should have to say out loud.
In brightest day, in blackest night,
No evil shall escape my sight.
Let those who worship evil's might Beware my power, Green Lantern's light.
He said it for the first time in a hall full of strangers and stumbled on the third line. Nobody laughed, because everyone in that room had stumbled on it once.
Then training started, and Peter failed it.

He did not fail the building. His constructs were the best rookie work Kilowog had seen in years, and Kilowog told him so once, grudgingly, and never again. Peter failed the pressure test. A Lantern had to hold a structure while an instructor tried to break his concentration, and Peter could do that for hours.
Then Kilowog put a civilian into the scenario, and the construct died in Peter's hands. It happened every time.

Peter braced for an order to get over it. Kilowog gave him something else instead. Kilowog had left sixteen billion people behind to take this job, on a world that shared one mind, and joining the Corps had meant walking out of that forever. He knew what he was looking at. The problem was not what Peter carried. The problem was that Peter thought all of it had to be held up by him alone. Every recruit who arrived with nobody left thought that, and it was the thing that killed them.

The Guardians raised a colder objection. They had solved this particular problem long ago by setting their own emotions aside entirely, and their verdict was not that Peter was weak. Their verdict was that they could not predict him. They had no model for a recruit who ran on the exact input they had removed from themselves.
Kilowog bought him two weeks. [PART 6] They gave him the sector.

Peter spent another two weeks finding out what the word meant, and he was good at the work, because he was careful and he listened. He sealed a breached hull with a two-door airlock instead of a bubble, because the actual problem was a pressure differential. He splinted a failing spar and ran a load path around the crack.

The scale of it was the part nobody had prepared him for. A sector held billions of stars. On the duty roster Peter was not the Green Lantern of New York, and he was not the Green Lantern of Earth. He was the Green Lantern of 2814, and Earth was a rounding error inside the assignment.

The job also had a hard limit, and the limit was practical. Every additional construct divided Peter's attention and ring output. The farther apart and more complicated the tasks became, the less effectively he could sustain either one. Divided attention was not a figure of speech out there. It set the ceiling on how many places one person could be.
Somewhere in that second stretch, the thing that had killed Vaska Tenn found him.
It looked Peter over, told him Earth would supply plenty of candidates, and left. It left because it had already found one of them, in a motel room in Connecticut. [PART 7]
Above him, out in the sector, a station was coming apart with tens of thousands of people aboard. Below him, a fire had started in his own building, and Mrs. Ocampo's boiler room sat underneath it.

The two emergencies did not turn out to be the same emergency. Nobody else covered either one. No construct could be in two places, because divided attention was a real limit and Peter had already been taught exactly what it cost.
He made the choice and went up.
He was right to go. Tens of thousands of people were on that station and one building was burning on one street, and he was the only Lantern within reach of either. The arithmetic was not close.
He got everyone off the station.
The block was still standing when he came back. The bypass he had rigged in the basement had held exactly as designed, and the boiler never faulted.
The stairwell collapsed instead.
Mrs. Ocampo had let him pay rent late twice without mentioning it. She had gone up that stairwell to knock on doors.
Ned was not in the building. He never found out that any of it had happened.
Peter sat on the roof until the sun came up and did not say anything at all. He had been right to go. Anyone who ran that arithmetic would have told him he was right to go. She was still dead.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Bill Metzger had been in the wind since Roosevelt Island.

He had no agency and no badge. He had a face on federal watch lists, an investigation with his name on it, three rented rooms in three states, a bag, a laptop and everything he had learned about switching people off.

Metzger did not think of himself as a frightened man. He had decided a long time ago that people with powers were a danger to everyone else, and he had been calling that decision competence ever since. He sat on the end of a motel bed at four in the morning most nights, unable to sleep because of what people like Peter Parker could do, and he called that vigilance instead of calling it terror.
A yellow ring came through his window while Peter was on Oa.

Green rings looked for the ability to overcome great fear. Yellow rings looked for the mirror image of that, which was the ability to instill it. The Sinestro Corps had been recruiting on those terms for a long time. Metzger of the planet Earth qualified without any difficulty at all.
They took him to Qward, at the centre of the antimatter universe, where the yellow rings were made, and they rebuilt him the way the Sinestro Corps rebuilt everyone.

The first thing a man with a tool limited only by imagination pictured was the machine he had spent a year perfecting on other people's children. Metzger started by reconstructing the adaptive emitter principles he remembered from Peter's inhibitor and testing them at short range. Once he proved the yellow construct could analyze an enhanced subject's abnormal biological or energy activity and tune its suppression output the same way the original device did, he realized the ring could replace the physical emitter network with a distributed construct and scale the pattern outward. The scale introduced a weakness: covering a continuous mile-wide area forced overlapping sections of the suppression pattern to meet along a narrow seam where the geometry closed. Metzger accepted it because he could reinforce that seam with additional ring output. Then he expanded the field over Queens at three in the afternoon and held every inch of it himself.

The field was a wall. Every construct Metzger built after that was a wall, a cage or a giant hand. A yellow ring made what its wearer pictured, and Metzger had spent his whole career picturing ways to hold people down.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Peter went up four hundred feet of green truss, building it as he climbed. The field came on and every enhanced person inside a mile dropped into the street.

His powers went out like a switch. Strength, reflexes, adhesion and the spider-sense all stopped at once, and the spider-sense was the one that mattered. It had always been an early warning, arriving before the thing it warned about. Peter was left with the ordinary kind, the kind that showed up at the same moment as the thing.
For the first time Peter was a Green Lantern and nothing else, running on the one quantity the ring measured.

Metzger told him what came next. He did not need names or files to do it. The street below them was already full of people who had dropped where they stood, and the schematic in Metzger's head still had Peter's handwriting on it. He told Peter that he had built the first one, and that he wanted him to watch what came of it.
Peter opened his mouth to answer him. He had answered every single one of them since he was fifteen years old.
Nothing came out.

Four hundred feet below, Ned was standing outside the deli looking up. He had not dropped, because there was nothing in him for the field to switch off. He was one man on a sidewalk under a mile of yellow light. Peter could not go down to him without telling Metzger exactly who mattered.
Then his will stopped.

The construct did not flicker. All four hundred feet of it let go at once, and then it came apart the way he had built everything to come apart since Astoria Boulevard, one rank at a time, the whole way down.
He did not catch himself. He fell more slowly, and he lived.

He hit a rooftop hard enough to break two ribs. A construct dying that badly sent the backlash straight back into the Lantern who built it, and the pain of it kept him on the roof. He lay in the yellow light and could not get up.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Nobody came for him. There was no speech.
Peter lay on his back and did the only thing he had ever been good at, which was work the problem.

He read the sentence again. He had been reading it wrong since the first night. He had taken it for a compliment and concluded the ring had made a mistake, because the ability to overcome great fear sounded like a description of somebody brave.

It was not a compliment. It was a requirement, and a requirement named its own input. Nobody could overcome something he did not have. A man with nothing to overcome would have failed the test by passing it.

The ring had been at its brightest on the night he climbed out of Banner's airshaft in worse shape than he had gone in. Maximum load, maximum output. Peter had watched it happen and written it off as a malfunction.
Peter had been treating his own terror as the flaw that broke his constructs. The ring had picked him for it.

There was a second consequence, and it was older than he was. The Corps had learned that the old weakness to yellow could be overcome by recognizing and mastering the fear behind it. Rookies were especially vulnerable because they had not learned to do that yet. Peter had spent months treating fear like evidence that he was failing. Now he finally understood that feeling it was not the same thing as surrendering to it.

So Peter said all of it out loud on a rooftop with two broken ribs, and he did not make any of it funny. He had been frightened of losing people since he was fifteen. He was frightened of what his hands were doing. He had been frightened every night before he went out, and there had never been a night when he was not.
What changed was that he stopped designing his constructs as though he would be calm when he used them. He started building them to survive the moment his hands shook.
He said the Oath alone, out loud, to nobody, and he did not stumble on the third line. [PART 11] Peter went back up and did not throw a punch.

He measured first. He flew a lattice of fine green filaments through the boundary of the field and watched where they failed. One narrow irregularity appeared where the suppression weakened. Only after finding it did Peter recognize what Metzger had done: scaling the original emitter into overlapping sections had created a closure seam where the geometry met.

He went after Metzger's concentration instead of his structures. He built decoy load paths, shapes that looked like they were about to take weight and never did. A man running on terror was already spending most of his attention on threat assessment, and an ambiguous shape cost him more to process than a threat did.

A block on Northern Boulevard started to sway. Peter put a tuned mass damper into it, a counterweight on a spring matched to the building's own period, and it cost him the initiative to do it. He caught a building instead of catching Metzger. He put the switchback ramp back up over the crowd underneath.
Metzger threw a cage at him, and Peter did not break it.

He braced it. He welded a green frame into the bars, used the cage as the truss he had been missing, and built his own structure on top of a construct made out of somebody else's terror. Metzger had been handing him raw stock all afternoon.
Metzger hit the same place he had hit before. The people below. The certainty that Peter would be responsible for all of it.
It worked. Peter hesitated and the construct failed. It failed in stages, because he had built it to, and what was left of it still held his weight.
He went back up, and the construct came out with eight legs again. This time he had meant it to. He stopped fighting the shape his own head kept making and used it.

The field came apart at the seam Metzger had been reinforcing, because he had been paying for decoys all afternoon and no longer had enough ring output left to keep that weak point closed in a wall a mile wide. Peter's powers came back. The change in his body arrived as something other than dread for the first time since it started. He fired an organic web-line off a green anchor built to hold it and swung, with the hard light doing the structure and the spider doing the rest.

The restraint that finished it was the soft-jaw gripper, scaled up, conforming instead of clamping. It held Bill Metzger without breaking anything of his while he shouted about what people like Peter were going to do to the world.
Then the front of a building let go over a street full of people, and there was no time to design anything.
So Peter built a wall. It was crude. He held it up with two broken ribs and both hands shaking, which was exactly how Vaska Tenn had held hers.

sections.name: PART 12
paras: The yellow ring came off Metzger's finger and started looking for somebody else.
It stopped in front of Peter and began telling him that Peter Parker of the planet Earth had the ability to instill great fear. It broke off partway through, because he was already wearing one.
It had not been wrong. Peter knew it had not been wrong. He had spent the last hour frightening a man who deserved it and enjoying more of that than he wanted to think about.

Federal agents took Metzger, seven weeks after they had started looking for him. A detective named Jean DeWolff wrote down what a young man in a hand-sewn suit told her and did not ask him for his name.
Peter did not argue that Earth was special. The Guardians had heard that from every recruit who ever missed home. He gave them an engineering argument instead.

A Sinestro Corps officer had crossed a sector line and found a finished weapons programme and a man to run it inside a week. It was still out there and it was coming back, because it had never come to conquer anything. It had come to harvest. An unassigned sector still had people in it. It just had nobody watching, and that was what the officer had come for.
The Corps had done this before. It stayed out of the Vega system for generations, and what moved into the gap was exactly what the Corps existed to stop.

The Corps had built a system where every sector's coverage depended on one person's will not breaking. The Corps also recruited specifically for people whose will had already been tested, which meant it already knew that a will breaks. He was not asking them for an exception. He was asking them to stop designing as though the failure would never happen.

The Guardians did not agree with him and still could not predict him. They did the administrative thing anyway, for cold arithmetic reasons, using the same criterion they had used to doubt him. For the first time, a second ring went out to Sector 2814.

Peter did not get to be everywhere. That had never been available. He got a partner he had not met, and he was going to have to trust a stranger with his own street, which frightened him more than the sector ever had.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Peter was on a duty roster now, and the roster was a bill rather than a prize.

He would be called away. There would be a night when Queens needed him and he was not on the planet, and somebody would pay for that. The second ring did not stop it happening. It only meant the odds were no longer one man against a sector.

Mrs. Ocampo stayed dead. Peter had been right to go, and being right did not get him forgiven and did not get him blamed, which was worse than either, because it meant the same night would come again and the arithmetic would not help.

He watched the deli from across the street for a while and did not go in. Whatever Ned had or had not got back belonged to Ned, and Peter had learned what happened when he decided these things for other people. He fixed the streetlight on the corner instead, properly, so that it stayed fixed.

Every night he took the lantern out of the shoebox under his bed and charged the ring against it, and he said the Oath out loud while it charged. It was the only time anyone said his name in that apartment, and he was the one saying it.

Peter Parker had been frightened since he was fifteen years old, and whenever it mattered, he went out anyway. That was the whole test. He had been passing it for years before the ring arrived to measure it.
He built one fist with it, and it lasted about two seconds. What he got good at was a structure designed to fail on purpose, in stages, so that everything underneath it survived the failure.
The ring gave Peter Parker the power. He brought everything else with him, including the fear that got him picked.

scripts.title: What If Spider-Man Got Compound V

sections.name: INTRO
paras: What if Spider-Man got Compound V after No Way Home, at a point where Peter’s already on his own and trying to rebuild his life from scratch? One bad encounter with a Vought shipment could leave him with something in his system that was never meant to mix with spider powers in the first place.

At first, Peter would probably think the V just made him stronger, until new abilities start showing up that don’t feel anything like what the spider bite gave him. Then he finds out where Compound V comes from, what Vought has been doing with it, and why they’re suddenly very interested in the fact that Spider-Man now has it too.

That would put Peter in a very different kind of problem, because this time the people coming after him want to study him, control him, and figure out how to turn Spider-Man into something they can profit from.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter would still be living on his own in New York after No Way Home, using the homemade suit and patrolling most nights because Spider-Man is one of the few parts of his life he still has control over. One night, he sees a guarded transport force another car off the road and follows it, assuming he’s dealing with some kind of weapons shipment.

The guards would be better equipped than normal criminals, but they still wouldn’t be able to keep up with Peter once the fight starts. During the struggle, the back of the transport gets damaged and one of the refrigerated cases breaks open. Several injectors spill across the floor, and before Peter can figure out what they are, a damaged one hits him in the side.
He pulls it out, but most of whatever was inside is already in his system.

Peter would get away from the transport before his body starts reacting. His heart begins racing, his muscles tighten, and small electrical sparks start jumping from his fingers. When he fires a web to swing away, the charge runs through the strand and blows out a nearby streetlight.

He barely reaches a rooftop before another burst knocks out the electronics around him. Peter would initially think he was poisoned, but his body starts recovering between each burst much faster than he expects. His breathing settles and the electrical charge slowly starts building again whenever he moves.

Once he gets home, Peter would inspect the puncture wound and go through everything he remembers from the transport. The only useful clue is something one of the guards shouted when the case broke, Compound V.

He’d search the name and quickly find Vought, a company tied to superheroes, security, and people with abilities Peter has never heard of before. There wouldn’t be much public info about Compound V itself, which would give Peter even more reason to look into it.

By the next morning, Peter would still have no idea what Compound V is doing to him, but Vought would already know that 1 dose from the transport is missing. Peter would keep the damaged injector and start looking for answers before the company realizes Spider-Man was the one who got exposed.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Peter would spend the next few days testing what Compound V actually did to him. This particular exposure seems to have given him one new mutation: his body generates and stores bioelectric charge, especially while he’s moving hard, swinging, or fighting. The charge starts sitting in his arms and hands until he gets rid of it, and the punches, web shocks, and other electrical tricks he develops are different ways of releasing that same stored energy. If he pushes too long, the charge starts jumping into whatever he touches, which makes normal patrols a lot harder than they used to be.

He’d figure out pretty quickly that the power works best through things he’s already using. A charged punch hits harder, but Peter would probably use the webs more because they give him distance. He can web someone’s arm or stick them to a wall, then send a controlled shock through the strand instead of getting close. He can also dump some of the charge into metal surfaces when it starts building too much, which helps stop the bigger bursts he had on the first night.

He’d start changing the suit almost immediately. The homemade suit already proves he can build around limited resources, so he could add conductive material into the gloves and soles to give excess energy somewhere safer to go. Testing would also show him that his body has a finite amount of charge it can store safely. Once he crosses that threshold, the buildup becomes increasingly unstable and starts discharging on its own. Peter can still direct it for a brief window after crossing the line, but the longer he waits, the less control he has. The suit helps manage ordinary buildup, but it doesn’t fix the actual issue because the power is coming from his body, and Peter still has no idea what Compound V is doing to him long term.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter would start with the transport company and work backward from there. Vought owns enough smaller businesses and medical programs that the first searches don’t give him much, but the truck route leads him to a storage facility connected to one of their research divisions.

He breaks in at night and starts going through their internal system. Most of the files are routine shipment records, but eventually he finds medical documents tied to children who later became supes. Peter would keep digging because the dates don’t make sense at first. Some of the treatments happened years before those people ever showed powers publicly.
That’s when he finds Compound V listed as the common factor.

The records make it clear that Vought had been giving the drug to children and tracking what powers developed afterward. Some parents knew. Some records suggest others were told the treatments were for something else. Peter would also find notes about failed subjects, unstable reactions, and adults who died after being exposed.

His own case would stand out immediately. Peter already had altered biology before the injection, then survived an adult dose and developed a new power within hours. Vought would have no normal comparison for that. Their working hypothesis would be that his preexisting enhanced physiology helped him tolerate the exposure, but without a comparable subject they couldn’t know that was actually the reason. Peter would understand why the guards reacted the way they did once they saw the electricity.

He’d copy everything he can before leaving, including the names of several facilities and people involved with distribution. At that point, Peter’s problem gets much bigger than figuring out what happened to his body. He knows Vought is still moving Compound V around, and there are probably more people being used in the same system that created The Seven.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Vought would know about Spider-Man before Peter knows how much they've learned about him. The security footage from the truck gives them his suit, his webbing, and the first electrical discharge. Once they compare that with later sightings around New York, they can tell the electricity appeared after the transport incident.

They’d want a blood sample more than anything else. Peter already had powers, survived Compound V as an adult, and developed something new without losing his original abilities. That’s the kind of case Vought would want in a lab.
Peter would take the equipment apart, copy whatever data he can, and find that some of it is being sent to a facility he hasn’t seen in the Compound V files yet. That becomes his next lead.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Peter would follow the surveillance data to a Vought facility that handles supe testing and medical research. He gets inside through the upper floors, avoids most of the security, and reaches a records room before the building locks down around him.

Black Noir would be the first real problem because he can get close without giving Peter much warning. Peter’s spider-sense still catches the attack, and the two of them end up fighting through the lab while Peter tries to keep the files he copied from getting destroyed. Noir is stronger and tougher than the Vought guards Peter has dealt with, but Peter is faster and much harder to catch.

The electricity gives Peter another option when Noir starts pushing through the webs. Peter charges one strand while Noir is pulling against it, and the shock briefly disrupts him enough for Peter to create distance. Peter would be surprised that it affects Noir at all because he still hasn’t tested the power on another supe, but he wouldn’t assume the same shock will always work that well.

A-Train arrives before Peter can get out, and that fight would be much harder to control. Peter’s spider-sense warns him when A-Train is coming, but knowing an attack is coming doesn’t mean his body can react quickly enough to counter every movement from scratch. Peter would have to cover narrow hallways and likely routes with webbing in advance, turning the environment into obstacles A-Train has to avoid or hit. Peter could keep some of those pre-positioned strands charged so contact triggers the electrical effect without requiring him to recognize A-Train’s movement and respond at superspeed.

That slows A-Train down enough for Peter to reach an exit, where Starlight finds him before he can leave. Peter would expect another fight, but she’d be more interested in why he broke into a Vought lab. He wouldn't tell her everything, especially with security closing in, but mentioning Compound V would be enough to change the conversation.

PART 6Peter would spend the next few days going through the material he copied from Vought. There would be enough locations, shipment numbers, and internal notes for him to start seeing how Vought moves Compound V around the country. Some facilities handle storage, some handle testing, and others exist mostly to clean up the people who survive an experiment badly enough that Vought can’t put them in front of a camera.

Peter wouldn't try to hit every location. He’d focus on the places still receiving adult doses because those records are the closest thing he has to understanding what’s happening inside his own body. One site outside the city would stand out because several subjects were transferred there after developing unstable powers, and some of those files suddenly stop without any discharge record or follow-up treatment. Peter would take that as a sign that the people didn’t simply leave.

He’d break into the facility expecting another lab and find something closer to a holding center. There’d be reinforced rooms, medical equipment, restraints, and several people who clearly aren't there by choice. Some would be recovering from V exposure, while others would have powers they can’t control well enough for Vought to market. Peter would recognize parts of his own first night in what he’s seeing. One person can’t stop producing heat through their skin, another keeps shaking because their nervous system is reacting badly, and a third has been sedated so heavily they can barely stay awake.

Peter would start getting them out before he worries about taking more evidence. He’d cut power to the locks, web cameras, and guide people through service corridors while trying to keep the alarms from spreading through the whole building. His new electrical ability would help here because he can overload security panels without destroying every door around them, although holding back would still matter. A full discharge could knock out the building, but it could also shut down medical systems keeping some of the patients stable.

Vought security would catch up before everyone gets out, and Peter would have to fight while protecting people who can barely move. That changes how he uses the electricity. Instead of big bursts, he’d keep it controlled and send short shocks through webs to drop weapons or lock muscles for a second. He’d still rely on speed, webbing, and spider-sense for most of the fight because those are the abilities he trusts.

The hardest part would come when one of the unstable subjects panics and their power starts going off inside the hallway. Peter would have to stop fighting long enough to help them calm down and move everyone away from the danger. That moment would matter because it shows where Peter’s head is compared with Vought’s. They see failed products. Peter sees people who need help.

He’d get most of them out and send emergency services toward the building without giving away where he lives or who he is. Before leaving, Peter would take another set of records showing exactly who approved the experiments and how long Vought had been hiding the failed cases.

Their first real meeting should happen during one of Peter’s patrols instead of inside Vought Tower. Peter would be dealing with a normal emergency when Homelander lands nearby and waits for him to finish. That alone would tell Peter more than a public introduction would. Homelander wouldn't be there to help anyone. He’d be there because Peter has become part of his day.

Homelander wouldn’t make that easy. He’d ask about the Compound V exposure, how Peter feels, whether his powers have changed, and whether he’s thought about joining Vought. The questions would sound casual, but Peter would hear the same thing underneath all of them. Vought wants to know exactly what he became.
Peter would dodge the questions and try to swing away, and that’s when Homelander would test him.

He wouldn’t need to throw a full punch or move anywhere near his maximum speed. Homelander would deliberately make a sudden grab or fast movement toward Peter just to test his reactions, which would be enough to trigger spider-sense. Peter would react before he fully understands what Homelander is doing, twist away, and land several meters back.

Peter would know immediately that staying there is a bad idea. He’d use buildings, traffic, and narrow spaces to make following him more annoying, but Homelander can fly and doesn’t have to respect the same routes Peter does. The chase would get dangerous fast.

Peter’s spider-sense would keep him alive, but it wouldn’t suddenly make him faster than Homelander. If Homelander closes the distance and gets a hand on him, Peter would feel how big the strength gap is. He could shock him through contact and probably make him react, but there’s no reason to assume one electrical burst would put Homelander down.

That would be Peter’s first useful piece of information. Electrical contact can at least make Homelander react, but Peter has no reason yet to treat electricity as a weakness or assume a stronger shock will reliably stop him.

Peter would use the shock to break contact, web two buildings at once, and pull himself hard through a narrow gap where Homelander can’t follow without smashing through the structure. He’d keep changing height and direction, using every part of the city to make the chase harder. Homelander could still catch him if he commits fully, so Peter’s real goal would be getting somewhere crowded enough that Homelander has to decide how obvious he wants to be. Peter already knows Vought cares about image. So he’d use that against him.

Once there are cameras and people everywhere, Homelander would have to stop treating it like a private hunt. He could still threaten Peter, but tearing through a packed street just to grab one masked hero would create questions Vought doesn’t want.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Peter would start working through the files more carefully and look for the people who keep the system running. He wouldn't need to fight all of them. Some are doctors, accountants, drivers, lawyers, and middle managers who’ve spent years moving information around because they assume nobody outside Vought will ever see it.

Peter would start leaving copies of specific files in places Vought can’t easily pull back. Journalists get pieces of shipment data. Lawyers connected to families affected by Vought receive medical records. Government investigators get names tied to adult V trials. Peter wouldn't dump everything at once because that gives Vought one big target. He’d spread the evidence out enough that stopping one leak doesn’t stop the others.

Starlight could become useful here because she knows how Vought works from the inside. Peter still wouldn’t trust her completely, but after their first encounter, she could make contact away from Vought property and give him information she plausibly picked up through her own time inside the company: people she dealt with, departments she encountered, routines she saw, and locations or names she heard connected to sensitive work. She wouldn’t know Vought’s entire hidden structure, so Peter would still have to verify which of those leads actually connect to Compound V.

Peter would probably be cautious with her at first. He’s already seen how Vought uses people, and anyone wearing the Seven name comes with risk. What would convince him is information he can verify himself. If Starlight gives him a location and Peter checks it, then finds exactly what she described, he’d start giving her more room.

One of their biggest targets would be a lab working on adult Compound V stabilization. Peter would want it shut down because the research could eventually make what happened to him repeatable. Vought wouldn’t need children anymore if they can reliably turn adults into supes. Peter and Starlight could hit the place from different sides. She handles internal access while Peter moves through the lab and destroys the equipment that can’t be safely removed. Peter’s electrical power would be useful because he can fry servers and control systems without blowing up the building, but he’d still copy as much data as possible before shutting anything down.
The complication would come when Peter finds research based on his own case.

Vought has been using every recording, sensor reading, and blood trace they managed to collect to build a model of how Compound V interacted with his altered biology. They still don’t have enough to reproduce it, but they’re closer than Peter expected.
That would bother him because the thing he’s trying to understand about himself has already become a research project for people he doesn’t trust.
Peter would destroy the physical samples and take the data, but he’d know some of it probably exists elsewhere. Vought doesn’t keep something that valuable in one building.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The full fight with Homelander should happen after Peter has already damaged Vought’s Compound V operation enough that Homelander can’t ignore him anymore. Peter and Starlight would be trying to get another group of test subjects out of a facility when Homelander arrives before they can leave.

Peter would know from the first encounter that running in a straight line won’t work. He’d tell Starlight to get everyone out while he keeps Homelander busy, which is a terrible matchup for Peter physically but gives the people inside a chance to escape.

Homelander would come at him hard enough this time that Peter can’t treat it like a warning. Spider-sense would save him from the first few attacks, and Peter’s movement would make him harder to hit than most people Homelander fights. He’d use walls, ceilings, machinery, and webs to keep changing direction instead of staying in open space.

Peter could land hits, but they wouldn’t do much at first. Even with Compound V, his punches aren’t suddenly on Homelander’s level. The electricity helps more because Homelander has less experience dealing with something that can travel through webs and hit from angles Peter doesn’t have to physically reach.

Peter would start layering the attacks. He webs Homelander’s arm, sends a charge through the strand, then uses the second of hesitation to pull a heavy piece of equipment into him. None of it wins the fight, but it keeps Homelander from getting a clean hold.

The problem is that Peter has to keep moving to survive, and movement keeps building more charge. He'd start feeling the electricity piling up faster than he can safely release it. His hands shake, the suit starts sparking around the seams, and Peter knows another uncontrolled burst is coming if he keeps pushing.

Homelander eventually gets close enough to grab him and slams him into the floor. Peter’s existing enhanced durability would keep him alive, but he’d still be badly hurt. Homelander could break ribs, injure his shoulder, or leave him struggling to breathe after only a few clean hits.

Peter would still be badly injured, but the next grab would be where he takes the risk. Instead of trying to keep the electricity below the safe limit, he’d deliberately let the buildup cross it. He would only have a brief window before the overloaded charge starts escaping unpredictably, so Peter would use that remaining control to dump everything through Homelander at once.

The discharge would be much bigger than anything Peter has used before. Lights across the facility would blow and nearby systems would shut down. Peter would discover in that moment that a discharge this extreme can briefly disrupt or stagger Homelander enough to make him lose control of Peter, but that observed result wouldn’t prove electricity is a general weakness or guarantee the same trick will always work.
It still wouldn’t knock him out. That’s important because Peter shouldn’t suddenly beat Homelander just because he got Compound V.
The blast gives Peter time, and that’s all he needs. He’d web part of the structure above Homelander, pull it down, then move toward the exit while Homelander is buried for a few seconds.
Peter would be exhausted by that point because releasing that much charge leaves his muscles weak, while the damage from the fight is still slowing him down.
Starlight would have the last people outside, and Peter would get far enough away before Homelander comes back through the wreckage.
Peter would be fine with that. He doesn’t need to beat Homelander in a clean 1 on1 fight if the people Homelander was supposed to stop him from rescuing are already gone.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Once the major facilities start getting exposed, Vought would have a much harder time hiding the adult trials and the people they kept locked away. Peter’s evidence would already be spread across enough places that deleting one server or threatening one journalist wouldn't solve it. Peter would still have to decide what to do about the Compound V inside him.

By now, his body has mostly stabilized around the bioelectric mutation. The electricity is easier to control, his suit handles the buildup better, and he knows roughly how far he can push before the charge becomes dangerous. His recovery from serious injuries still comes from the enhanced physiology he already had before Compound V, not a second healing ability from the V.

Removing it would be difficult because the V has already changed his body. Peter could look through Vought’s research for a way to reverse the effects, but there probably wouldn’t be a safe answer waiting for him. Most of their work is about creating powers, not taking them away. Peter would have to live with the fact that this is part of him now.

That wouldn’t mean he starts treating the power like a gift from Vought. If anything, knowing where it came from would make him more careful with it. He’d keep using the electricity when it helps, but he’d never want it to become the reason he thinks he can solve everything.
That matters because Peter’s biggest wins in this story wouldn’t come from overpowering people.

He gets the test subjects out because he chooses to help them before taking more evidence. He hurts Vought by spreading information instead of trying to destroy one building. He survives Homelander because he understands the fight is buying time for other people to escape.
Compound V gives him more power, but Peter is still making the same kinds of choices he made before he ever knew Vought existed.

Vought would take serious damage from the leaks, although a company that large wouldn’t disappear overnight. Some facilities would close, employees would start covering themselves, and people inside the company would begin turning on each other once they realize evidence is already outside Vought’s control.

Homelander would still be out there too. Peter knows he can survive an encounter with him if everything goes right, but he also knows how quickly that fight could go wrong. That keeps him from becoming reckless just because the V made him stronger.
He’d go back to patrolling New York, now carrying a power he never asked for.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Getting Compound V would make Spider-Man stronger, but it wouldn’t make his life easier. The electricity gives Peter better range, more options against stronger opponents, and another way to use the webs he already relies on. It also gives him something new to control every time he’s moving through a crowded city.

The bigger problem is what comes with learning where the power came from. Peter would find people Vought experimented on, records showing how long the company has been manufacturing supes, and research built around turning what happened to him into something they can repeat.

He’d eventually become dangerous to Vought because he can’t be bought the way they’re used to buying heroes. Peter doesn’t care about a contract, a movie deal, or having his face on a billboard. He cares that people are being hurt, and once he sees that happening, he keeps getting involved.
Even Homelander wouldn't change that. Peter probably couldn’t beat him in a straight fight, but he could survive long enough to ruin what Homelander is trying to protect and get other people out.

So Compound V would give Spider-Man another power, but it would also give him an entire new problem to deal with. Peter would still be Spider-Man at the end of it. He’d just have Vought wishing he never touched that truck in the first place.

scripts.title: What If Spider-Man Had Mahoraga

sections.name: INTRO
paras: After the memory wipe spell, Peter’s life is already falling apart. Aunt May is gone. His friends, MJ and Ned don’t remember him. He’s crashing in a tiny apartment and patrolling at night since that’s the only thing that gives him a sense of purpose. However, somewhere out there, in a universe that has nothing to do with radioactive spiders, there’s a whole different kind of power running the whole show. Cursed energy. The very thing that fuels jujutsu sorcerers and cursed spirits in the Jujutsu Kaisen universe.

Because of the rift, Peter is exposed to a massive amount of cursed energy which rewrites Peter’s brain structure and he inherits the crown jewel of the Zenin clan, the Ten Shadows Technique. The same technique that belonged to ““the potential” himself, Megumi Fushiguro. The technique allows the user to summon a spiritual familiar aka shikigami from their shadow and command them. And, today we’ll see exactly what would happen when Spidey doesn't just inherit that great power. He inherits Mahoraga.
The strongest and most uncontrollable shikigami in the JJK verse.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: After being exposed to cursed energy, nothing happens to Peter at first. He is completely fine. But, after a week, Peter just feels off. He assumes he’s simply exhausted. And honestly, that makes perfect sense. He has been through an insane amount of trauma. He’s sleeping badly. He’s been eating whatever he can afford. And, spending most of the nights stopping crimes by himself. However, he slowly starts to doubt himself as he starts seeing strange grotesque creatures that he has never seen before. They’re curses. But, Peter doesn’t know what they are. Also, his spider-sense, the thing that keeps him sharp and saves him from danger starts giving wrong signals which he finds strange.

As time goes by, it only gets worse. He’s out on patrol, breaking up a group of goons trying to rob a corner store. One of the men turns around and fires at him. Peter dodges it easily, webs the gun, punches another guy and kicks the third one into a stack of boxes. Everything looks like it’s just another easy night for him. However, his spider-sense suddenly starts to disorient him. He fires his webs randomly. He freezes. He thinks something is behind him. Peter turns. But, there’s nothing behind him. He then looks to his left, but again there’s nothing. This distraction is enough for one of the goons to hit him in the head with a metal pipe.

However, he still wins the fight. Because, come on, a few goons with crowbars or metal pipes aren’t enough to stop him. But something’s wrong and he knows it. And, then a man with a metal tail and a serious grudge against Spider-Man shows up. It’s Scorpion. On a normal night, dealing with Scorpion is “small potato stuff’. But, tonight he looks like a big one. This is the night Spidey’s body is completely rewiring itself from the inside out. His spider-sense is tweaking and his single greatest advantage is actually holding him back.

So, when Scorpion swings the tail, Peter gets hit by it. He gets clipped. Then clipped again and again. For the first time in a long time, Spider-Man feels fear. He’s getting completely outclassed by a guy he usually toys with. It’s not that Scorpion somehow got stronger all of a sudden. No, it is Peter’s own systems betraying him at the worst possible time. He shoots his webs in the wrong direction once again. And, that’s where Peter completely loses himself. By the time Spidey manages to scare Scorpion off, he’s bruised and bleeding. He drags himself up to the rooftop. He sits down and tries to understand what just happened.

But, no matter how much he could theorize, he simply can’t figure it out. While he’s sitting there, confused and beat up, something else is happening in his body. All that cursed energy he has been soaking up has hit a tipping point. Losing people close to him. The trauma of nearly getting killed. And, the sheer volume of energy his body has absorbed triggers something inside him. A technique. One of the most powerful of them all. However, Peter has no idea what he’s going through. He has got no idea what cursed energy even is. He just thinks he had a really really bad night and wants to forget about it.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: After an unforgettable night, Peter gets home. It’s around 2 in the morning. He downs a couple of painkillers and heads to bed still half in his suit. He’s exhausted and just wants to sleep. But, before he passes out, he does something he’s been doing since he was a kid. He messes around making shadow animals on the wall using his phone’s flashlight. It’s a little habit he picked up. He then creates a dog head shape with his hands. He has done it many times whenever he struggles to fall asleep. Tonight, though, it’s different. In the JJK verse, a shikigami is summoned through the Ten Shadows Technique by forming a shadow puppet with hands that matches the shape of the shikigami. But, Peter is completely unaware that he has a brand new supernatural technique running through his body.

And, this time around, his freshly awakened cursed energy actually has somewhere to go. The next morning, he wakes up with a rib still aching and almost falls out of bed. And, that’s when he notices that there are two wolves. One is pure white with three small black dots on its forehead, while the other is jet black with three white dots on its forehead. They're big, lean and powerful. They’re like something between wolves and spirits made of shadow. Their eyes are calm, almost curious as they watch Peter with no hostility. But, Peter being Peter, does not scream. Okay, he screams a little. However, his brain which has survived aliens, wizards and a literal multiverse collapse is basically like, “Well, why not wolves now?” At first, he doesn’t move. The wolves don’t move either. He then slowly closes his eyes again, waits two seconds and opens them, hoping he’s just imagining things.

But, the wolves are still there. He slowly reaches a hand out. The white one sniffs it. It doesn’t attack. Instead, it nudges his hand almost asking him to pet it. Peter smiles and says, “Oh...you’re friendly.” This is not what he expected after everything that’s been happening to him lately. But, after he blinks and opens his eyes again, they're gone. They completely vanish, leaving Peter shocked. He tells himself that his delusions have gotten so bad that he’s hallucinating dogs now. He then spends the whole day distracted. He keeps catching flickers of movement in the shadows. A dog shaped shadow. A pair of eyes following him from his own shadow. He starts to think that he’s losing his mind. As the days go by, he passes by this small cluttered antique shop. Yeah, the kinda place that sells international artifacts and old books nobody asked for. And, over there, he spots a framed print of a black wolf and a white wolf. The same wolves. The same symbols on their foreheads that look exactly like the ones he saw that fateful morning.

Peter dashes into the store like he’s possessed. The shop owner who has seen every kind of strange customer imaginable isn’t even that surprised. Peter points at the framed print and asks, “Where did you get that, Sir Shopkeeper?” “It’s Mario”, he replies before revealing that he picked up that strange old looking book in an alleyway a couple of weeks ago. Yeah, the same time the multiversal rift happened. The second Peter touches the book, he feels it. So, he buys it on the spot and rushes home to read it. However, his curiosity doesn’t stop him from reading it on his way home. As it turns out the book is a field guide to the Ten Shadows Technique. It talks about the Zenin clan. It talks about cursed energy. It talks about shikigami. And, all sorts of other stuff that sounds like magic to Peter. He asks himself, “Oh, so | can summon these shadow puppies now?” He finds information on the Divine Dogs, the same ones he encountered that day.

However, what really catches his attention is something called the Divine General. And, that it is the most powerful of all of them. Even his spider-sense starts tingling as he reads about it. With all the warnings about the Divine General, Peter knows it’s no joke. So, he stands in his room, clasps his hands together in the shape of the Divine Dogs and tries to summon them. He forms the hand sign. Nothing happens. He tries again. Still nothing. Peter looks at his hands and shouts “Come on...shadow puppies get summoned!” And, yet again nothing. He checks the book again to see whether he is doing it the right way. He feels like a guy trying to perform a magic trick at a kid’s birthday party. He tries again and again. Then, he remembers the shadow puppet he made that night. Peter tries to recreate it. His fingers form the perfect shape. And, he puts his focus solely on summoning them. Finally, the shadow on his wall peels itself off the surface and the white dog steps out. Peter breathes a sigh of relief. He then tries to summon the black dog and he succeeds.

He tells himself that this is already going far better than the last time he fought something outworldly. From there on, Peter starts working through the book’s ritual system. He learns that a Ten Shadows user has to summon and defeat each shikigami to make it their own. So, Peter spends the next couple weeks doing exactly that. He summons and subjugates one shikigami after another. He summons Nue. Toad. Great Serpent. Rabbit Escape. Max Elephant. Round Deer. Piercing Ox. Each one is different and unique from the last and teaches him something new about how his technique works. And, then he gets to the last entry in the book. The one with the big warning label. A gigantic humanoid shikigami. A massive wheel behind its head. A sword in its hand. It simply looks majestic. And, at the same time deadly. Eight Handled Sword Divergent Sila Divine General Mahoraga.

He learns that in the entire recorded history of the Ten Shadows Technique, not a single user from the Zenin clan had managed to tame this shikigami. Not even one. It’s not just strong. It’s more than that. And, that’s what makes it far more dangerous than any other shikigami that exists. But, Peter wants to see what it can do and can’t contain himself from summoning it. He finds an abandoned industrial area far away from the main block. He doesn’t know exactly what will happen. The only thing he knows is whatever he is trying to summon is not gonna be easy to deal with. Peter reads that paragraph about four times. “With this treasure | summon...” He messes it up a couple of times before finally taking a deep breath and summons the shikigami who stands right behind him. He whispers, “Let’s see if what the book says about you is all talk and no bite or if you're the real deal.” He would soon find out. The book wasn’t lying.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The entire floor goes cold. The shadows on the floor stretch and twist unnaturally. The lights flicker. And then it’s just there. The Divine General. Mahoraga. A huge hulking, muscular humanoid figure with a wide grinning jaw and an alien-like tail appendage extending from the back. “You have a sword? That is awesome, Mahoraga or Makora or whatever you're”, he says. But, most importantly, a massive wooden wheel with eight handles floats above it and it’s more than just a decoration. Mahoraga stomps the ground. Peter immediately starts flipping around the wrecked place. But, it becomes obvious to him that it’s nothing like fighting Scorpion or any other supervillain he had faced. Every hit Peter lands, whether it’s a punch or a kick, it does less and less damage each time. The wheel keeps turning. Peter is stuck in a situation that could possibly end him. This is what makes Mahoraga terrifying. Its adaptation isn’t limited to something specific. It can almost adapt to anything.

In the Shibuya arc, Sukuna fought Mahoraga who eventually defeated it. However, Mahoraga adapted to Sukuna’s slashing attacks to the point where it aurafarmed as it walked straight through them. So, Peter does the only thing he can do right now. He runs. Not away, but he buys some time and uses every ounce of his parkour skills to keep Mahoraga occupied. And, here’s where Peter shows why he is Spider-Man. His greatest power was never really his strength or crawling walls. It’s his brain. This is the kid who built his own web fluid in a high school chemistry lab. The kid who was chosen by Tony Stark as his protege. So, after understanding physical attacks don’t work against the shikigami, he starts observing it closely. He finds out that the wheel only spins when Mahoraga takes damage and also notices it takes time to fully process a new type of attack before it can counter. The trick isn’t hitting harder. So, Spidey starts mixing it up.

First, impact webbing. Then, an electrified web cartridge. Followed by an EMP pellet. Peter keeps changing what he uses so he doesn’t rely on an attack Mahoraga has already started adapting to. It’s not enough to win. But, just enough to survive and buy time. Right then, Peter remembers something from the book. He realizes that the only way to take out Big Raga is to hit it with something completely different before it can adapt to that attack too. And, that’s exactly what Sukuna also did during his fight against Mahoraga. He spent the entire time slashing Mahoraga over and over. However, after figuring out the shikigami’s ability, Sukuna switched it up and finished Mahoraga with a single attack from his Divine Flame before it could adapt to the new attack.

However, Peter simply can’t summon Divine Flame like the King of Curses. He has to win by being Spider-Man. And, he had already planned for a situation like this. He has a modified thermal cartridge in his utility belt. But, the cartridge itself isn’t the weapon. It’s only the trigger. Peter lures Mahoraga into an abandoned industrial testing chamber built around an experimental plasma furnace designed to flash-vaporize heat-resistant aerospace materials. The chamber was made to contain temperatures far beyond anything Peter could produce with his own tech. So, he rigs the old fuel system and furnace around his thermal cartridge, turning the entire chamber into one focused blast instead of trying to overpower Mahoraga with something from his utility belt. But, would it take out Mahoraga? That’s the question Peter is puzzled by. Still, he leads the shikigami, baits a swing and slides under it to provoke it. Mahoraga is visibly annoyed. It starts closing in on Spidey and nearly grabs him. But, that’s exactly what Peter was hoping for.

As the shikigami lands in the right spot, Peter activates the cartridge. The furnace ignites around Mahoraga all at once, concentrating the full plasma blast inside the sealed chamber before it has time to adapt to the new phenomenon. The blast completely incinerates the shikigami and with that Peter is finally able to take it down. He summons Mahoraga as the shikigami kneels in front of him. The massive, ancient creature that was supposedly untamable is waiting for Peter’s command. “So we're friends now, buddy,” Spidey says. And, just like that, Peter has done something nobody would’ve expected. He has defeated Mahoraga. He won because he studied the problem. Understood the adaptation. Used his spider-sense. Used his technology. And, most importantly created the perfect environment around him. Peter Parker did what Peter Parker always does. He found a way. Using Nue, he flies home and stares at his bedroom ceiling as he wonders how the whole thing started all because he made some shadow puppets that night.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: With Mahoraga in his arsenal, Peter is far stronger than he has ever been. At the same time, he is terrified of what he’s capable of now. So, he writes notes. He creates rules. And, sticks them to the wall of his apartment. Rule number 1. Never summon Mahoraga unless absolutely necessary. Rule number 2. Never assume Mahoraga will solve everything. And, finally rule number 3. Never forget rule number 1 and 2. Peter looks at the rules. He calls it, “Perfect”. He also becomes more versatile than he has ever been. His spider-sense tells him where the danger is. His tech gives him different options for attacking. His webs let him control the battlefield. His shikigami give him support. And Mahoraga adapts to phenomena that he can’t handle. The Divine Dogs become his favorite as they’re perfect for tracking criminals. Meanwhile, Nue gives him aerial support. Toad for assisting him with rescue situations. Rabbit Escape for distractions. Every new shikigami has given him more options to deal with whatever gets thrown at him. Also, by now Peter has memorized the book cover to cover and has a clear idea of what each shikigami is capable of.

Standing there, Scorpion is confused. He asks what Spidey was blabbering about some treasure and stuff. But, Spidey just smirks and tells him to brace himself. Before Scorpion could do anything, his tail is sliced in two. Scorpion can’t believe what just happened. He has no clue what he’s fighting against. All he can sense is something invisible tanking his attacks before he gets pinned down for good. The whole fight lasts less than a minute. This is probably the fastest Spidey has brought a villain to his knees. And, just like that Spidey tackles other villains like Tombstone and the Hand. Peter believes he has cracked the code. He believes he has learned to use Mahoraga less like a panic button and more like a chess piece.

But, there’s a problem. Peter is still Peter. He wants to save everyone. He wants to stop every criminal. And, wants to make sure nobody gets hurt. With Mahoraga and the other shikigami, he is capable of dealing with more enemies without breaking a sweat. At the same time, having access to something that strong also brings out a different kinda problem. It changes how one sees a problem. And Peter starts noticing it. At first, he used Mahoraga only against enhanced criminals who could actually push him. Then, it was against dangerous criminals carrying alien weapons. Then, he finds himself thinking about Mahoraga in situations where he could still handle things himself. A heavily armed crew breaks into a warehouse using stolen Chitauri tech. Peter arrives. They shoot. Peter dodges. Usually, he would web them and dismantle the weapons himself. But this time, Peter forms the hand signs. The shadows spread. The wheel appears. Mahoraga rises. The fight ends in seconds. These guys were dangerous, but Peter still didn’t need a literal war god to stop them. And, that’s the part he doesn’t really think about. As they say, when you’ve got a hammer that strong, everything starts looking like the kind of nail that deserves it. And, that’s exactly what Spidey is doing too.

However, one night he stares at his own hands, the ones he uses to form the summoning shape. He has this thought that scares him a little. He thinks, “Why am | even bothering to fight most of these guys myself anymore when | can tell my shikigami to take care of it?” That question sits with him longer than he expects. Since day one, his entire identity has been about being the guy who does things the right way. Someone who fights smart because he has to. Someone who wins through effort and heart. But, somewhere in the last few weeks, Peter has started leaning on Mahoraga the way you’d lean on a crutch when you don’t actually need it. However, he brushes it off. He tells himself he’s just being efficient. He believes that using the best tool for the job is just being smart. Well, technically he isn’t wrong. But, he’s also not entirely right. And, little did he know that choice is about to get a lot of people hurt.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: After Herman Schultz, aka Shocker sneaks out of prison, he manages to recover replacement equipment and rebuild his gauntlets. If you remember Shocker from Spider-Man - Homecoming, you know he is not exactly a top tier threat. He is the guy who was made the new Shocker after Toomes murdered the previous Shocker, Jackson Brice. He almost defeated Spidey, but Ned distracted him which gave Spidey enough time to escape and web him. Now, he’s there to take revenge for what Spidey put him through. To get his attention, Shocker tries to pull off a robbery and fires his gauntlets wildly in public. Spidey arrives and seeing Shocker terrorizing the civilians makes him mad. But, this time around, Shocker has come prepared. He fires a dart that temporarily paralyzes Spidey while he’s completely caught off guard. Peter still finishes summoning Mahoraga and tells it to take Shocker down before the paralysis fully hits him. Because of that, Peter starts getting dizzy right after giving the command. A decision that he would go on to regret.

He summons Mahoraga right in the middle of a crowded street. That too against a guy with a gauntlet and zero superhuman powers. The second Mahoraga manifests, the entire street changes. Car alarms go off from its presence. And Mahoraga being what it is, doesn’t really hold back. It’s not built to pull punches, since in its universe, it never had to. It follows Peter’s command to take Shocker down and swings so hard that it sends one car flying into another parked car. The impact literally folds the two cars together like a tortilla. And, things only keep getting worse because Peter is too dazed to guide it or change the command. Mahoraga keeps moving toward Shocker while Shocker heads straight toward a bus stop packed with people who just wanted to get home.

When Peter finally regains his senses, he watches all the chaos as Mahoraga closes in on Shocker beside the bus. He sees it happening in what feels like slow motion. He screams, “MAHORAGAAAA!” and orders the shikigami to stop. Mahoraga stops, but the damage from Peter’s earlier command is already moving. One of the cars knocked loose by the fight is sliding straight toward the bus stop. Peter throws himself in front of it using every ounce of his strength. He physically redirects the car at the absolute last second to reduce the impact. It works. Barely. Still, the impact shatters the glass which traumatizes the passengers. Luckily, there are no casualties. But, it was so close. If he was a second late, multiple people would’ve died. A mother with a stroller was standing less than 10 feet away. A kid on a skateboard was just sitting right on the bench. Peter can’t believe what he had just done. He immediately dismisses the shikigami as soon as he can breathe again.

He sits there in the wreckage of a storefront. He watches the paramedics check on people who got hurt. All because of his one single mistake. This is the moment when Peter truly sees the Ten Shadows Technique as something he needs to be careful with. Because up until now, this has been a fun power fantasy. He was already powerful enough to take on aliens and other threats even before he got an absurdly overpowered weapon. He remembers Aunt May’s words, “With great power, there must also come great responsibility.” This finally catches up to him. Peter goes home that night and plans to not summon Mahoraga anymore. Not because he’s scared. But, because he’s afraid of how easy it was to reach for the biggest hammer when he could’ve solved the problem himself.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: While Peter is going through an existential crisis, remember that crack that let cursed energy leak into Peter’s world? Well, that was never fully sealed. Because of that, the influence of the JJK verse is greater than ever and is giving birth to stronger curses in the city. After the recent incident, negative emotions are at an all time high. That’s exactly what curses need to manifest. They're born from and feed on negative human emotions like fear, hatred and despair. All that residual dread has been quietly gathering in the cracks of the city. The curses are feeding off every scared 911 call. Every panicked headline. And, every resident who has started to wonder if their city is safe.

This gives birth to a massive curse looking like a nightmare stitched together from every fear the city has been quietly creating ever since the rift opened. It’s so strong that Peter’s spider-sense goes haywire. It’s something way beyond anything Peter has faced. Simply BIG, BIG POTATO STUFF! He understands that if he doesn’t step up, the city is doomed before Doom. But, he’s afraid that summoning Mahoraga might end ina disaster like last time. So, he summons Nue to get closer to it. He orders Nue to strike the massive curse with lightning. But, it does nothing to it. He quickly summons Toad to save the civilians trapped nearby. But, Spidey knows simply rescuing people isn’t enough. He has to get rid of the monster before it’s too late.

He summons Great Serpent and Max Elephant to try to stop the curse from moving forward. But, the curse overwhelms both shikigami and Peter dismisses them before they can be destroyed. With his gadgets not working against the curse, he summons Piercing Ox which crashes into the curse and sends it into a building.
