Just as Spidey celebrates that he has finally taken it down, the curse gets back up and nearly destroys Piercing Ox before Peter dismisses it too. Then, the curse slams Spidey into the ground. Spidey wakes up. He sends Nue back. He hears people screaming. Peter looks at them. He realizes that none of his other shikigami are strong enough to actually fight or contain the curse. He is forced to take a tough decision.

With no other option, he summons the shikigami he never wanted to summon again. He chants “With this treasure, I summon Mahoraga”” as the shikigami spawns behind him. Seeing the shikigami once again brings back bad memories of what happened last time. But, he has no other choice as Mahoraga is his last hope. He then summons his Toads as support to help him and Mahoraga. However, before Spidey can team up and attack the curse together, Mahoraga slices the curse in half as the massive curse gets one-shotted by the Divine General. Spidey is dumbfounded. Well, who wouldn't be? Seeing this massive curse get killed when he and the other shikigami were struggling the whole time was not something he expected.

But, what Peter doesn’t know is that Mahoraga is simply a nightmare for curses. Since, Mahoraga”s Sword of Extermination is completely wrapped in positive reverse cursed energy, it can kill curses easily. Something that even Sukuna confirmed during his fight against Mahoraga. Still, with the curse thing gone, Spidey is finally relieved. As the toads lick his face, he laughs at how ridiculously it was of him to not summon Mahoraga in the first place. He wakes up and sees Mahoraga who is grinning from ear to ear as always. Spidey just looks at it and says thanks out loud like you would to a partner instead of a weapon.

And honestly, if there’s one thing we know about Peter Parker, it’s that he was probably always going to figure out how to carry that weight anyway. But Peter Parker is still Spider-Man. Still, the kid who jokes when he’s terrified. Still, the hero who gets knocked down and gets back up. And, now Peter has to carry the weight of his powers as he takes on supervillains and potentially powerful special grade curses and guards the city every single night.

scripts.title: What If Spider-Man Had Roblox Physics

sections.name: INTRO
paras: His body is moving wrong. Spider-Man is mid-swing over Queens — thief in sight, web locked — and instead of gliding clean between buildings, he's jerking forward in blocky angles, like invisible hinges are deciding every motion. He lets go to land. He hits the sidewalk flat on his face. Arms and legs flop in every direction. The thief freezes. Bystanders stare. Peter pushes himself up, brushes off the suit. '...I'm okay.' The impact should have broken bones. Instead, Peter feels the pain and sees his health drop, but his body doesn't translate the hit into realistic anatomical damage. Under these new rules, a brutal collision can cost health without producing the fractures or internal injuries normal physics would demand. Before he can process that, a bright red exclamation mark appears above his head. A shot echoes from the alley. He sidesteps. The bullet misses by inches. The icon disappears. His Spider-Sense has never looked like that before. Whatever has happened is not simply giving him a new power. Peter's body is beginning to behave like a Roblox player-character: Humanoid-style health, passive regeneration, exaggerated avatar movement, ragdoll states, collision glitches, and - if his health ever reaches zero - whatever Roblox considers death and respawning. His Spider-Sense is still his own, but his brain now translates its warnings into game-like UI only he can see. The laws governing Peter haven't just changed. They've been replaced. And this is only the first sign.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter keeps chasing the thief before he has time to understand what changed. His web lands exactly where he aims, but the swing feels different. His body moves in blocky motions. Even with the awkward movement, Peter closes the distance quickly. When he lands on the next rooftop, he runs into an air-conditioning unit and bounces backward as if he hit an invisible barrier. The impact barely slows him down, but it confirms that something is seriously wrong.

The thief reaches a fire escape and starts climbing. Peter tries to follow his usual route by running straight onto the wall, but his hands never stick. His biological strength is still there, and so are his webs, but the way his body interacts with surfaces has been overwritten by the avatar-style movement system. He can run, jump, fall, climb designated structures, and collide with geometry, but his normal wall-crawling adhesion no longer registers as a valid movement state. He slides all the way back to the ground before climbing the fire escape instead. As soon as he reaches the roof, the thief pulls out a handgun. A bright red exclamation mark instantly appears above Peter's head, followed by a thin red line connecting the weapon to his chest. Peter steps out of the line of fire just before the trigger is pulled. The bullet misses completely. Every shot creates the same warning, making each dodge almost effortless. His Spider-Sense is still protecting him, but now it presents the danger in a completely different way.

Once the thief realizes the gun isn't working, he rushes forward. Peter lands a clean punch. For an instant, Peter sees the impact translated through the same strange interface now attached to his own body - a chunk of damage, a health-style readout - but the thief himself has not become a Roblox avatar. He is still an ordinary human being interacting with someone whose body now follows different rules. Peter immediately pulls his punches and webs him to the roof.

That distinction matters. The new system belongs to Peter. Other people can be knocked around by his altered movement and collisions, but they do not inherit his regeneration, death state, or respawn mechanic.

Peter checks his own health bar while he's standing there. The damage from the fight is already beginning to recover. It does not vanish instantly. His health creeps upward at a steady rate, roughly one percent of the maximum bar each second. The pain fades as the lost health returns, but there are no realistic bruises or broken bones to heal because the system is tracking damage as an abstract health value rather than modeling every physical injury. Whatever changed isn't affecting just one part of his powers. It's replacing the basic rules that his entire body follows. And Peter has no idea how deep that goes yet.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The next morning, Peter finds out.

He wakes up late, grabs his backpack off the desk, and immediately sends it flying across the room. The bag hits the opposite wall hard enough to leave a mark. He picked it up the same way he always does. The difference is that his body no longer registers the weight correctly, and a small mistake in movement carries a lot more force than it should.

He gets to the bathroom in a rush and clips the edge of the half-open door with his shoulder at a shallow angle. Instead of bouncing off, his momentum carries part of his body through the geometry and he stumbles into the hallway. Peter freezes, backs up, and tries to reproduce it. Most attempts fail. After several tries, he realizes the glitch only happens when he hits a surface at the right angle with enough momentum.
By the time he makes it out of the apartment, he's already six minutes late.

On the way to school, a cab cuts across the crosswalk without slowing down. Peter steps back to let it pass, misjudges the curb behind him, and ragdolls onto the sidewalk in front of about twenty people. He stands back up immediately, completely unhurt. A woman nearby asks if he's okay. He tells her yes. He is objectively fine. He just looks like he got hit by a car.
By the time he reaches school, he has already clipped through one door, knocked a trash can into the street, and jumped half a block trying to avoid a puddle.
Peter Parker is having a terrible morning. Spider-Man, it turns out, is doing fine.

What the fall from the curb confirms — and what the ragdoll across the pavement from the night before already suggested — is that the new rules follow him everywhere, not just on patrol. His jumps carry him higher than he means to. His falls end without injuries that have any right to be absent. Objects fly further than they should when he touches them wrong. And solid surfaces sometimes let him clip through entirely - but only when he hits the geometry at the right angle and with enough momentum. He cannot simply choose to walk through any wall he wants.
The world feels less like a real place and more like a game where every object follows a set of strange rules he's still in the process of figuring out.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter spends the next several days learning that no two patrols are ever the same anymore. The strange physics continue to surprise him, even after he thinks he's figured them out. Some changes make his job easier. Others create problems that never existed before.
He still doesn't know if the changes are permanent. He's stopped actively trying to find out.

What Peter does know is that he has two separate lives to manage, and only one of them has gotten easier. Spider-Man can survive falls, dodge bullets he can see coming, and walk through walls when the angle is right. Peter Parker still occasionally clips into doorframes when he rushes through them at the wrong angle and sends his lunch flying if he grabs it wrong.

The difference becomes obvious one afternoon in the school hallway. Peter reaches into his locker, overestimates the force by about a factor of three, and sends a stack of textbooks skidding down the corridor. MJ watches the entire thing without saying anything. Then she looks at him.
"That was the least normal thing I've ever seen you do."
Peter picks up the books. "I've been having a weird week."
She doesn't push it. But she watches him walk away with a look that says she's filing the moment somewhere.
An hour later, Peter is across the city.

One afternoon, a group of robbers storms a bank in Midtown and locks the front entrance before taking everyone inside hostage. Peter reaches the building within minutes, but the front doors are reinforced and every window is covered. Normally, he would've looked for another way inside. Instead, he remembers the collision glitch he has been testing all week. Peter backs up, approaches the wall at the shallow angle that has worked before, and commits to the movement. His shoulder catches for a split second, then slips through the concrete. The rest of his body follows, and he stumbles into the middle of the lobby. It is not true intangibility; he has simply learned one repeatable way to exploit the broken collision around his own avatar-like body.

The robbers freeze in complete confusion. They know every entrance was sealed, yet Spider-Man has somehow appeared inside the building without opening a single door. Peter doesn't waste the opportunity. Within seconds, the hostages are out of danger, and the police arrive to find the criminals already tied up.

The stories spreading across New York become stranger with every passing day. Witnesses describe Spider-Man surviving falls that should be impossible and appearing inside places that nobody could reach. Some people think he's developed new powers. Others believe Doctor Strange is secretly helping him. Even Peter has no explanation. He simply accepts that the rules have changed and focuses on keeping people safe.

Not every patrol goes smoothly. During a chase across the rooftops, Peter misjudges one of his jumps and lands awkwardly on the edge of a building. Instead of catching himself, his body tumbles down four flights of fire escapes before crashing onto the sidewalk below. The people nearby rush over, expecting the worst. Peter stands back up a few seconds later. His health has dropped, and the impact hurt, but there are no shattered bones or internal injuries. The bar begins regenerating as he continues chasing the suspect. The criminal doesn't even bother running anymore. After watching Spider-Man walk away from a fall that should've been fatal, he quietly surrenders.

The footage eventually reaches people Peter has fought before. Herman Schultz - the Shocker - is still connected to pieces of the old alien-tech weapons network, and videos of Spider-Man moving like a broken game character are impossible to ignore. Schultz studies them because his entire fighting style depends on controlling distance and predicting where an opponent will land.
He decides to test the footage for himself.

Shocker ambushes Peter during a patrol in Queens and fires a concussive blast where Spider-Man should land. Peter hits the edge of a rooftop, ragdolls instead of planting his feet, and tumbles underneath the shot. Schultz corrects. Peter jumps at the wrong-looking angle, clips the corner of a rooftop obstacle, and comes out somewhere Schultz was not aiming. Every prediction is based on normal movement, and Peter's new movement keeps breaking the prediction.

The fight ends when Peter deliberately uses the same shallow-angle collision glitch he discovered at the bank, slipping through a thin divider and webbing Schultz from a direction he thought was sealed off. Shocker goes down understanding exactly one thing: Spider-Man is still beatable, but the old assumptions about how he moves are useless.

The battle confirms something Peter has been slowly realizing all week. The strange physics aren't making him unbeatable because they're stronger than his old powers. They're making him unpredictable. Every criminal, every villain, every opponent enters a fight expecting the world to behave normally. Peter is the only person who already knows those rules no longer apply.

Before long, videos of his impossible rescues begin spreading far beyond New York. Some people see a hero who's somehow become even more powerful. Others see something they can't explain. Either way, it doesn't take long before the Avengers start asking the same question everyone else is already thinking.
What exactly happened to Spider-Man?

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Peter eventually agrees to let Tony examine him after Happy insists that whatever is happening has moved beyond something Peter should troubleshoot alone. This is still before the events of Infinity War: Bruce Banner is not on Earth yet, and Steve Rogers is not casually training at Avengers Compound. Tony runs every scan he can think of. The results refuse to make sense. Peter's body shows no new mutation, radiation signature, or measurable outside energy. Biologically, he is still Peter Parker.

The demonstrations only make things stranger. Peter clears a training platform with a jump that should not work, ragdolls from a dangerous height and gets back up, then repeatedly clips against a test wall until he finds the shallow angle that lets his body pass through it. Tony has FRIDAY map every attempt. The successful clips share geometry and momentum conditions, but there is no physical mechanism in Peter's body explaining why those conditions should let matter overlap.

Tony reaches the only conclusion the evidence actually supports: he can measure what Peter's new rules do, but not what is causing them. The health system, regeneration, movement states, and collision errors behave consistently enough to test, yet there is no energy source for Tony to switch off and no biological mutation for him to reverse.
That means there is no four-hour machine that conveniently restores normal physics. Tony can help Peter document the rules, but he cannot suppress something he cannot detect.

The most useful discovery comes from repetition. Peter's passive regeneration is slow, not instantaneous. His clipping requires a favorable angle and momentum. His danger UI is simply a new visual translation of Spider-Sense, so if Peter becomes dependent on the icon instead of the instinct underneath it, he can actually make himself slower.
Tony makes him run the drills again without looking for the UI.

By the end of the session, Peter understands the condition better, but he is no closer to curing it. Tony tells him to treat the new rules like any other unstable system: learn the limits before betting his life on them. Peter returns to Queens with a list of rules instead of a solution.
He doesn't have long to sit with them.

He does not get much time to keep testing. Soon afterward, Bruce Banner crashes through the roof of the Sanctum Sanctorum with a warning about Thanos, and the events that lead Peter onto Ebony Maw's ship begin. By the time Peter reaches Titan, he is about to find out whether his new Roblox-style rules hold up against someone who can rewrite reality with one hand.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Everything Peter has learned about his new abilities gets tested the moment he arrives on Titan.

The plan begins the same way it does in the original battle. Iron Man, Doctor Strange, Star-Lord, Drax, Mantis, and Spider-Man work together to stop Thanos before he can collect the remaining Infinity Stones. Peter joins the attack, but it immediately becomes obvious that he isn't fighting under the same rules as everyone else.

Every time Thanos commits to an attack, Peter's Spider-Sense translates the danger into the exclamation-mark UI he has learned to read. The Titan still manages to hit him, and those hits matter: Peter's health drops sharply and only regenerates at the slow passive rate he discovered on Earth. He cannot erase Thanos-level damage in seconds. He has to survive long enough for the bar to recover.

The biggest surprise comes when Thanos uses the environment. Just as he does in the original battle, he tears part of Titan apart and sends enormous pieces of the moon crashing toward the surface. While everyone else searches for cover, Peter simply keeps moving. The falling debris crashes into the ground around him, but the impacts never slow him down. Every jump carries him over another obstacle, and every fall ends with him standing back up as if nothing happened.
For the first time in the battle, Thanos hesitates.

Even with four Infinity Stones, he can't understand why the teenager refuses to stay down. The Gauntlet can reshape space, time, and matter. What it can't do is predict where someone will be if that someone doesn't move like anything the Gauntlet has ever encountered. Thanos starts adjusting, watching Peter's pattern, trying to identify the logic.
Peter doesn't have one. That's the point.

He starts using the strange glitches deliberately. He attacks from awkward jump arcs and searches for the shallow collision angles that can let him clip through thin pieces of rubble. It is never guaranteed, and thick or newly formed barriers can still stop him completely. But every successful exploit forces Thanos to defend a direction he was not expecting.
The battle shifts from a contest of strength into something else entirely. And that's a fight Peter has been quietly preparing for since Queens.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Thanos adapts faster than anyone else Peter has fought.

He stops trying to overpower and starts trying to contain. Massive sections of rock rise into the air and lock into walls. The battlefield narrows. Gravity shifts without warning. Entire portions of the surface disappear and reform somewhere else. The Gauntlet isn't trying to hit Peter anymore. It's trying to reduce the number of places Peter can be.
For a few seconds, it works.

Peter runs out of usable angles. A wall forms directly in his path, too thick and too square to give him the shallow collision angle his clipping exploit requires, and he hits it instead of passing through. A second wall closes behind him. Thanos has figured out the rule. He raises the Gauntlet and fires.
The impact is the hardest thing Peter has felt since this all started. His health bar empties completely.
Everything goes dark.
Five seconds later, Peter reappears in Queens.

Not somewhere nearby. Not a few feet back. Queens. The system has finally revealed its most extreme rule: when Peter's Humanoid-style health reaches zero, his body respawns at the one location the new rules have treated as his default spawn since the transformation began back on Earth. He reappears with a full health bar, billions of miles away from Titan, and realizes that immortality comes with a brutal limitation. Dying does not return him to the fight. It can remove him from it completely.
On Titan, Peter simply vanishes from the battlefield.

The respawn does not rewind the battle, and it does not undo anyone else's mistakes. Earlier, the team had already come agonizingly close to removing the Gauntlet before Quill learned what happened to Gamora and struck Thanos, breaking Mantis' hold. That failure has already happened. Peter's new rules kept him in the fight longer than anyone expected, but the first time his health actually reaches zero, the system sends him all the way back to Earth.
Iron Man, Strange, and the others are suddenly missing one of their most unpredictable fighters at the exact moment the battle is collapsing around them.

Peter can survive death, but survival is not the same thing as being useful. Respawning cannot reset Thanos, restore the team's failed Gauntlet attempt, or put Peter back on Titan. Strange eventually surrenders the Time Stone to save Tony, and Thanos leaves with what he came for.
The outcome is still a loss, but Peter learns a much harsher rule than simple immortality: every death can remove him from the people he is trying to protect.
Peter is back in Queens knowing something he didn't know when he arrived on Titan.

He still doesn't know what caused any of this, or whether it's permanent. Tony could map the rules but could not identify anything to reverse. Whatever is underneath the strange physics, it isn't close to resolved.
But for the first time since Queens, that doesn't feel like a problem he needs to solve before he can keep going.

Five years later, the Avengers reverse the Snap and Peter returns, experiencing the lost time as only moments. After the final battle with Thanos, he goes back to Queens with the same Roblox-style physics still attached to him. Whatever changed his body's rules survived the Blip with him.

Peter's respawn mechanic does not save him from what happens next. The Snap is not ordinary damage reducing his health to zero; the Infinity Stones erase him directly. Peter is among the half of all life that disappears.
But the larger battle is not over. Thanos reaches Wakanda, takes the Mind Stone, completes the Infinity Gauntlet, and snaps his fingers.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: By the time Peter processes what happened on Titan, he has changed the way he fights.

The smooth swings, perfect landings, and graceful movement that once defined Spider-Man are gone. In their place is a hero who wins battles by taking advantage of a world that no longer follows normal physics. Every strange jump, awkward landing, and impossible movement has become another tool that his enemies can't prepare for.

Outside of combat, the changes are much harder to live with. He still occasionally clips into doorframes when he rushes through them at the wrong angle. His lunch goes flying if he reaches for it wrong. He ragdolled down a fire escape in front of MJ once and told her it was a new training exercise. She didn't believe him. He gets caught on objects that shouldn't stop him, struggles to move naturally through crowded streets, and has to think carefully about how the strange physics will affect even the smallest decisions. Being Peter Parker has gotten genuinely difficult. Being Spider-Man has never been easier.

So would Roblox physics make Spider-Man unstoppable or dysfunctional? The answer is both. His everyday life becomes unpredictable, but every battle tips further in his favor. Criminals can't keep up with movements that ignore common sense, and even some of the strongest enemies in the MCU struggle to adapt because they're still fighting with normal physics while Peter isn't.

In the end, Roblox physics make Spider-Man stronger because nobody else understands the rules he's playing by. And in a fight, the hardest opponent to beat is the one who doesn't have to follow the same rules as everyone else.

scripts.title: What If Spider-Man Had The Omnitrix

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Peter Parker was in the middle of stopping a robbery when his Spider-Sense warned him that he was about to become someone else.
He was already moving when it happened.
The Omnitrix activated on his wrist.

Green light flashed across the alley, and Peter’s body changed before he could even understand what was happening. His skin hardened into red armor. His torso expanded. 2 additional arms forced their way from his sides, and his body grew far beyond anything he’d experienced before.
The robbery stopped being important.
Peter stared at his hands.
There were 4 of them.
The transformation lasted only a few minutes, but that was enough to change the way Peter understood his own abilities. The Omnitrix had turned him into an alien.
And Peter hadn’t even chosen the transformation.

By the time the watch returned him to normal, Peter had more questions than answers. The device displayed ten unfamiliar genetic profiles, each belonging to a species he’d never heard of. Some could manipulate energy. Others possessed incredible strength, speed or intelligence. A few looked like they could survive conditions that would kill a human instantly.
Peter had no idea who had created the device or why it had ended up in New York.
He only knew one thing.
Someone had built a machine capable of changing a person into an entirely different species, and it had decided that Peter Parker was its new user.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter didn’t spend long testing the Omnitrix outside. He had no idea what it could do, and the last thing he wanted was to find out in the middle of a fight. He went back to his apartment, locked the door and started looking at the watch properly.

The face opened when he pressed the center. A small holographic display appeared above it, showing different alien forms. Peter recognized the 4 armed one from earlier, but the others were completely unfamiliar. He rotated through them one at a time, trying to figure out what he was looking at.
There wasn’t much information on the display. He could see the forms, but the Omnitrix wasn’t giving him names or instructions. Peter was going to have to work most of this out himself.
He started with the alien he’d already used.

The transformation was quick. His body changed into the same four armed Tetramand he’d become earlier, and Peter immediately noticed how different it felt compared to being human. He was much larger and stronger, but his movements weren’t natural yet. He had four arms, a different center of gravity and a body he’d never used before.
Peter picked up a heavy piece of furniture with two hands. Then he tried lifting it with one.
He could.
That gave him a pretty good idea of how much stronger this form was.

The more interesting part was what happened to Peter's instincts. His Spider-Sense belonged to his altered human biology, and the Omnitrix wasn't covering that biology with a suit. It was replacing it. While Peter was transformed, the warning sense disappeared. What remained was everything Peter had learned from years of relying on it: how to read movement, anticipate attacks and react before an opponent finished committing to them.
Peter still had it.

That meant the Omnitrix hadn’t simply replaced his body and taken everything else away. His memories were still there, his thoughts were still his own, and the warning he relied on as Spider-Man still worked.
That was important.

Peter had spent years learning how to fight with his Spider-Sense. The Omnitrix didn't carry the ability into another species, but it didn't erase the experience Peter had built around it either. If he learned how each transformation moved, he could combine those instincts with abilities he'd never had before.
Before he could test that properly, the Omnitrix started beeping.
Peter looked down. The display had turned red. A few seconds later, the transformation ended. Peter was back to normal.
He waited and watched the device. After a while, the display returned to green. So the transformations had a time limit. Peter wrote that down.

He also wrote down everything else he’d learned so far. The Omnitrix could completely change his body, it seemed to select specific alien DNA, and it eventually returned him to human form. He still didn’t know how many forms were available or who had built the device.
That last question bothered him.

Peter had seen alien technology before. The Chitauri weapons, the technology used by Thanos and the equipment he’d encountered during his time with the Avengers had all been advanced, but he could usually figure out what something was supposed to do.
The Omnitrix was different.
It wasn’t something Peter could simply take apart and rebuild.
He decided to try another transformation.

The next alien he selected was much smaller than the Tetramand. Within seconds, Peter had shrunk down to only a few inches tall. His skin had turned gray, his head had become much larger and his eyes took up most of his face.
Peter looked at himself on the desk.
This wasn’t exactly what he’d expected.
Then he looked at his laptop.
Something had changed.
The computer suddenly seemed incredibly simple.

Peter started examining the hardware and immediately understood things he hadn’t noticed before. He could follow the electrical pathways through the motherboard, understand how the components interacted and identify several inefficient parts of the design without having to think about it.
The transformation wasn’t giving him more physical power.
It was giving him intelligence.

Peter had always been smart. He’d built his own web shooters as a teenager and had spent years developing his own technology. As a Galvan, though, his ability to process information was on another level.
He picked up a screwdriver and started taking apart the laptop. For the first time, Peter wasn’t trying to figure out what the Omnitrix could do.
He was trying to figure out what the Omnitrix actually was.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Peter spent the next several minutes working as a Galvan. The difference was obvious almost immediately. He could look at a circuit board and understand how the components worked together without having to trace every connection. His hands were much smaller, but that wasn’t really a problem. His new body was built for working with technology, and Peter adapted to it quickly.

The Omnitrix itself was the main problem. Peter could understand individual systems, but he couldn’t simply look at the device and know everything about it. There were parts of its design that were completely unfamiliar, and some of the technology was operating on principles Peter hadn’t encountered before. He could tell that the watch was far more advanced than anything he’d built, but he couldn’t explain exactly how it worked yet.

Peter focused on the part he could understand. The device wasn’t storing physical alien bodies. It was holding genetic information and using that information to change the user’s biology. That explained why the transformations felt so different from wearing armor or using a machine. His body wasn’t being covered by an alien suit. It was actually becoming another species.
That also raised a question Peter hadn’t considered before. If the Omnitrix could change him into another species, then what happened to his own biology while he was transformed?
He couldn’t answer that yet.

Peter returned to human form and made another note. He’d need to test each transformation carefully before using any of them around other people. The Tetramand was strong enough to cause serious damage without much effort, and he had no idea what the other forms were capable of.
He went back to the Omnitrix and cycled through the available forms again.
One of them looked like a humanoid made from crystal.
Peter selected it.

The transformation gave him a completely different body. His skin became transparent and crystalline, and his physical strength increased considerably. Peter moved his arms and noticed that the material making up his body wasn’t behaving like normal flesh. It was much harder, and when he focused on his hands, he could extend the crystalline material into sharp shapes.
He didn’t test that ability against anything living.
Instead, Peter picked up a piece of scrap metal and struck it against his forearm. The metal bent. His arm didn’t.

That was enough for Peter to understand that this transformation had defensive advantages that his normal body didn’t have. He also discovered that the crystal wasn’t simply armor. He could produce additional crystal from his body and shape it into different forms.
The next form was almost the opposite.
It looked built for speed.

Peter chose it and found himself standing on two wheels, with a striped tail, a raptor like body, and a visor over his face. His body had become much leaner, and his senses felt different. The moment he moved, he understood why.

The alien could accelerate far faster than Peter could as a human. Peter started slowly inside the apartment, then moved outside when he realized there wasn’t enough space. He ran down an empty street and immediately had to stop because his normal idea of how quickly the world should pass by no longer applied.

He didn’t need to reach his maximum speed to realize how useful the form could be. Peter already had experience moving through New York at high speed. He knew how to read traffic, predict where people would move and react to danger before it boxed him in. With this transformation, all of those skills became more useful.

Peter also realized that speed created its own problems. At that level, a mistake could hurt someone before he had time to correct it. He didn’t need to learn how fast the alien could go by crashing through a building.
He returned to his apartment and changed back.
That was going to take time.
He went back to the Galvan form and continued studying the device.
This time, he noticed something he’d missed earlier.

The Omnitrix wasn’t just showing him a list of transformations. There were additional systems hidden beneath the main interface. Peter couldn’t access all of them, but he could tell the watch had far more functions than the basic transformation system he’d been using.
He started working through the interface carefully.
Eventually, he found a reference to the device’s creator. The name meant nothing to Peter at first. Azmuth.

Peter searched through the information available inside the Omnitrix and began piecing together what he could. Azmuth was a Galvan scientist, and the Omnitrix had been designed for a purpose that went far beyond giving someone superpowers. Its creator wanted the wearer to experience life as other species and understand them from a perspective that humans normally couldn’t have.
Peter found that part interesting. The Omnitrix wasn’t designed as a weapon. At least, that wasn’t its original purpose. That made Peter reconsider the device.
He’d been thinking about it as another tool he could use as Spider-Man. Something that could make him stronger, faster or more capable when he needed it.
But the Omnitrix had been built around something much bigger than fighting.

Peter didn’t know why it had arrived on Earth, and he still couldn’t explain why it had attached itself to him. He also couldn’t tell whether someone had sent it there or whether the pod had simply been carrying it when it reached Earth.
There was one thing he could be certain of.
If a device this advanced existed somewhere in the universe, Peter wasn’t going to be the only person who knew about it forever.
And once other people found out who had it, being Spider-Man was probably going to become the easier part of his life.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter’s first instinct was to keep the Omnitrix completely out of sight. He’d learned from experience that powerful technology attracted attention, and this device was far more complicated than anything he’d dealt with before. For the next few nights, he treated it like a science project. He tested one transformation at a time, recorded what changed and avoided using anything he couldn’t control yet.

That approach worked until Peter found a transformation he couldn’t properly explain. The Omnitrix selected a small, dark figure with a large head and thin limbs. Peter assumed it was another intelligence based form, so he activated it expecting something similar to the Galvan. Instead, his body became almost completely black, with white markings across his chest and one roving eye.
Peter immediately felt different.

He could see normally, but there was something else there. The world around him seemed easier to move through. He could stretch parts of his body farther than they should have been able to go, and when he tried to move through a solid object, his body passed through it.

Peter stopped. He tried again. His hand disappeared through the wall. That got his attention. The transformation was a Ghostfreak, a Ectonurite form with abilities that were completely different from the other aliens he’d tested. Peter could become intangible, allowing him to pass through solid objects, and he could make himself invisible. Those abilities immediately reminded him of his own experience with Spider-Man, but there was an important difference.
Peter’s powers had always required him to work with the physical world.
Ghostfreak didn’t. Peter slowly moved through the wall and returned to the apartment.

He started thinking about situations where that could help. Locked doors wouldn’t matter. Walls wouldn’t matter. Someone hiding inside a building couldn’t simply disappear from him anymore. Then Peter noticed something else. The transformation felt less predictable than the others. He couldn’t explain why, but he didn’t like being in it. Peter changed back. He wrote down the abilities and moved on. That was becoming his routine. He wasn’t trying to become an expert overnight. He was building a list of forms he could trust, forms he needed to practice and forms he should avoid until he understood them better.
The Omnitrix eventually showed him another transformation that immediately caught his attention. It was covered in black and green. Peter selected it.

His body became a strange liquid-like mechanical form. His fingers stretched into cables, and parts of his body moved like living machinery. When Peter touched his laptop, the alien body connected to it. The computer changed. Peter watched the system improve in real time.
The transformation could merge with technology. Peter pulled his hand away and the laptop returned to normal.
He tried again with one of his web shooters. This time, he understood what the transformation could do.
The alien was a Galvanic Mechamorph. Upgrade.

Peter connected himself to the web shooter and immediately saw dozens of ways to improve it. The original design was still there, but the Omnitrix allowed him to modify the technology from the inside. He could increase its output, change its functions and make adjustments that would’ve taken Peter hours to design himself. That was the first time Peter understood how dangerous the Omnitrix could become in his hands.
It wasn’t just giving him different powers. Some transformations could improve the technology he already had.
Peter disconnected himself and returned to normal. He looked at his web shooter for a few seconds before putting it back on.

That combination was going to be useful. Peter continued testing the forms over the following days, but he kept one rule for himself. He wouldn’t use a transformation in public unless he already understood what it could do.

That rule lasted until the next emergency. Peter was finishing a patrol when his Spider-Sense warned him about a group of armed men entering a warehouse near the river. He landed ona nearby roof and watched them through the windows.

There were 6 of them. They had rifles, body armor and equipment Peter didn’t recognize. Normally, Peter would’ve gone in himself. This time, he had another option. He selected the speed based transformation.
Green light flashed.
Peter became XLR8.

He moved across the roof and reached the warehouse before the men even realized someone was there. Peter watched their shoulders and weapons as he moved, changing direction before they could line up a clean shot.
Peter had fought groups of armed criminals before, but XLR8 changed the way he approached the entire fight.
He didn’t need to stand in front of them.
He didn’t even need to attack them directly.
He moved between the men, knocked weapons out of their hands and pulled several of them away from the others before they could react. Within seconds, all six were on the ground and webbed together.

Peter returned to human form once the Omnitrix timed out. He looked at the restrained criminals. For the first time, he understood what the device could really add to his life as Spider-Man. He didn’t have to replace the way he already fought. He could build on it. The instincts he developed from years of using his Spider-Sense could help him control XLR8’s speed. His scientific knowledge could work with Upgrade. His experience fighting stronger opponents could help him control the Tetramand. Every transformation gave him another option, but Peter’s own judgment was still what decided how he used it.
That made the Omnitrix much more useful than simply having a collection of alien powers.
Peter just needed more time to learn.
Unfortunately, someone else had already started looking for the watch.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Peter didn’t know anyone was looking for the Omnitrix. As far as he was concerned, the warehouse fight had been another normal night. He finished his patrol, went home and spent another few hours working on the device.

The biggest problem was that he still couldn’t figure out why the Omnitrix had chosen him. He could understand how the transformations worked at a basic level, but the reason behind the selection was completely outside his knowledge. The device had arrived in an escape pod, attached itself to him and then started functioning as though that was exactly what it was supposed to do.
Peter went back to the pod.

He’d brought several pieces of it home after the crash and had spent days examining them. Most of the material was useless to him. The outer shell was made from an alloy he couldn’t identify, and the internal systems had been damaged when the pod entered Earth’s atmosphere. He couldn’t even determine where it had been traveling from.

The Galvan form helped, but even with its intelligence, Peter couldn’t instantly understand technology this advanced. He could identify patterns and make educated guesses, but there were still parts of the Omnitrix that remained beyond him.
That was actually useful.
He put the damaged pod aside and focused on the Omnitrix again.

One of the transformations he’d been avoiding was the one that looked like a walking mass of fire. Peter had already seen enough to know that it was probably extremely powerful, but he’d been reluctant to activate it inside his apartment.
He decided to test it somewhere safer.
Peter took the device to an abandoned industrial area outside the city. There were no buildings nearby that could easily catch fire, and the open space gave him plenty of room to work.
He selected the transformation. The Omnitrix changed him into a Pyronite. Peter immediately understood why he hadn’t wanted to try it indoors.

His entire body was capable of generating and manipulating fire. He could produce flames from his hands, project them outward and use them to propel himself through the air. The transformation wasn’t simply resistant to heat. Fire was part of what made the form work.
Peter spent several minutes learning how much control he actually had. He started with small flames. Then he increased the output.

He tested how accurately he could aim, how quickly he could change the direction of a blast and how much energy he could produce without losing control. The important part wasn’t finding the biggest attack he could make. Peter wanted to know how precise the transformation could be. That turned out to be one of its biggest advantages. He could use the Pyronite form without turning every fight into a firestorm. Peter eventually tested the form against a piece of abandoned machinery. A concentrated blast damaged the metal badly, but he could also produce much smaller bursts when he needed them. That gave him a better idea of how he’d use the transformation in New York.

He wouldn’t need to throw around huge attacks every time he fought someone. He could use the heat to disable weapons, create distance or stop a vehicle. Peter returned to human form and wrote everything down. He was starting to notice a pattern with the Omnitrix. The strongest transformation wasn’t always the best one.

The right transformation depended on the situation. If someone was holding hostages, the Tetramand might be too dangerous. If Peter needed to reach someone quickly, XLR8 made more sense. If he had to deal with machinery, Upgrade could be more useful than either of them. If he needed to survive an attack that his normal body couldn’t handle, Diamondhead gave him another option.

Peter rotated through the options several times and found that some transformations were unavailable. Others appeared after he’d already used them. He couldn’t tell whether the device was cycling through a larger database or whether there was some kind of selection system he hadn’t figured out. That bothered him. If the Omnitrix contained far more DNA than the handful of forms he could currently access, then Peter had only seen a tiny part of what the device could do. He returned to the Galvan form and started studying the interface again.
That changed how Peter looked at it.
The device was much older and much more important than he was. Peter returned to human form and sat at his desk. He still had no idea why the Omnitrix had ended up in New York.
He also didn’t know how long it would be before someone came looking for it. Then his computer picked up a transmission. Peter looked at the screen.
The signal wasn’t from any satellite, phone or radio station he recognized. It was coming from the damaged escape pod. Peter stared at the screen as the transmission repeated.
Someone was trying to communicate with it. He immediately went back to the Galvan form and began analyzing the signal. It wasn’t a distress call from Earth. It was a message from somewhere else.
And buried inside the transmission was a name Peter had never heard before.
Vilgax.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Peter went back to studying the Omnitrix and learned more about its history. It was designed around understanding different species by allowing its user to experience their biology firsthand. The Omnitrix contained genetic samples from an enormous number of alien species, which explained why so many different transformations were available. Peter also realized that the device had safeguards he still didn’t understand, meaning he couldn’t simply access everything stored inside it.

That changed how Peter approached the Omnitrix. Instead of treating it like a collection of superpowers, he started treating every transformation as another tool that required practice. He trained with XLR8 until he could control his speed without crashing into buildings, practiced with Tetramand so he wouldn’t accidentally use too much strength, and experimented with Diamondhead to learn how to create shields and structures instead of relying entirely on attacks. Upgrade became especially useful because Peter could connect himself to his web shooters and improve their systems without permanently changing them.

The training was interrupted when Peter detected another signal in orbit. This one was much stronger than the first. Peter realized that whoever had been searching for the Omnitrix had finally located Earth, and there was a good chance they already knew where the device was. PART 6

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Peter went outside and followed the signal without immediately approaching its source. He wanted to know what was coming before he exposed himself. Several small ships eventually entered Earth’s atmosphere and separated over New York. Peter followed one to the waterfront, where a group of Mechadroids landed and began scanning the surrounding buildings.

Peter used Diamondhead to confront them. The crystalline body allowed him to absorb attacks that would’ve seriously injured his normal body, while Peter relied on the combat instincts he had already developed to read attacks he couldn't see coming directly. He focused on removing their weapons and separating them rather than trying to overpower the entire group at once. Once they were restrained, Peter searched their equipment and found technology connected to the damaged escape pod.

The attackers were using the pod to locate the Omnitrix. Peter switched to Upgrade and connected himself to their scanning equipment, allowing him to see what it was doing. He changed the information being transmitted and sent the attackers toward a false location before destroying the scanner. The plan worked temporarily, but more transports continued arriving across the city.

Peter realized the invasion wasn’t really about taking control of New York. The attackers were trying to force him to reveal himself. He moved between their positions using XLR8, stopping them before they could reach crowded areas and using his speed and experience to stay ahead of their weapons. When the Omnitrix timed out, Peter had to rely on his normal abilities until it recharged. He used his webs and the buildings around him to separate the remaining attackers and eventually restrained several more.
By then, the transports had stopped.

Peter looked toward the sky and saw a much larger ship moving through the clouds. The smaller vessels moved aside as it approached Manhattan, making it obvious that whoever commanded the invasion had finally arrived.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Peter stayed on a rooftop and watched the large ship descend. He didn’t rush toward it because he knew the earlier attacks had been designed to keep him occupied. He wanted to know who was coming and whether there were civilians nearby before starting another fight. A smaller craft eventually separated from the main ship and landed near the waterfront, where several aliens stepped aside for a much larger figure.
Peter recognized him from the Omnitrix’s database. Vilgax had finally come to Earth.

Peter selected Tetramand and confronted him away from the busiest parts of the city. The difference in experience became obvious immediately. Peter was stronger than he had ever been as Spider-Man, and having four arms gave him more ways to attack and defend, but Vilgax was still able to keep up with him. Peter's years of combat experience helped him avoid several attacks, but Vilgax adapted quickly and eventually overpowered him.

Peter switched to Diamondhead and changed his approach. Instead of trying to match Vilgax physically, he used crystal structures to control the battlefield and limit where Vilgax could move. That worked for a while, but Vilgax learned the pattern and began moving around the barriers instead of breaking through them.

Peter then switched to XLR8 and used his speed to create distance. He wasn’t trying to defeat Vilgax anymore. He wanted to find a better way to use the Omnitrix against him. When Vilgax followed, Peter relied on XLR8's speed and his own instincts to stay ahead of his attacks and eventually created enough distance to escape.

Peter returned to human form and waited for the Omnitrix to recharge. He had learned that none of his transformations were enough by themselves. Vilgax was too experienced to be beaten by simply choosing the strongest alien available.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Once the Omnitrix recharged, Peter selected Upgrade and connected himself to the alien equipment left behind by Vilgax’s forces. He discovered that the soldiers were receiving information from the main ship, including Peter’s location. Peter altered the network and fed the soldiers false information, disrupting their ability to coordinate across the city. While he was inside the system, Peter also learned more about how the Omnitrix handled transformations. He realized he could manually switch directly from one alien form to another without returning to human form first, but every additional transformation burned through the Omnitrix's remaining operating time faster.

He then returned to Vilgax and used Tetramand again, this time relying more heavily on his combat experience and fighting with control instead of trying to overpower him. Peter managed to throw Vilgax across a rooftop, but the warlord quickly recovered and struck Peter hard enough to send him through a concrete wall.

Peter switched to Diamondhead and began using the transformation defensively. He created several barriers that forced Vilgax into a narrow path, limiting his movement and giving Peter more control over the fight. When Vilgax finally broke through the last barrier, Peter switched to Upgrade and connected himself directly to the cybernetic systems built into Vilgax’s body.

Peter couldn’t simply take control of Vilgax or shut down every system, but Upgrade allowed him to interfere with the connections between the cybernetics. He disrupted several of the systems controlling Vilgax’s equipment, making his movements less coordinated. Peter disconnected before Vilgax could grab him, but the Omnitrix was already beginning to time out again.

Peter moved away and returned to human form. He was exhausted, and the fight had made one thing clear. The Omnitrix gave him more options, but it didn’t make him unbeatable. If he kept switching forms without understanding what each one could contribute, Vilgax would eventually find a way around all of them.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Peter opened the Omnitrix and began cycling through the transformations. He wasn’t looking for the alien with the most strength or the most destructive abilities. He needed something that could give him an advantage Vilgax hadn’t already experienced. After several options passed, Peter stopped on one of the forms he’d barely tested: Stinkfly.

He selected it and transformed. Peter's body became an insectoid alien with four eyes, wings and the ability to fire adhesive slime from its eye stalks. It wasn't stronger than Vilgax. That was exactly why Peter chose it.

Stinkfly gave Peter a completely different way to control the fight. He stayed above Vilgax, coating the ground and pieces of Vilgax's equipment in thick adhesive slime. Vilgax could tear through it, but every second spent clearing it gave Peter another opening. Peter immediately understood why the Omnitrix contained so many different species. The point wasn’t to find one transformation that could solve every problem. It was about choosing the right biology for the situation and combining that with the experience Peter already had as Spider-Man.

Peter moved back toward Vilgax with a better understanding of the fight. He didn’t rush into another direct confrontation. He used Stinkfly to create an opening, then manually switched forms whenever the situation required something different. Peter no longer had his Spider-Sense while transformed, so every switch forced him to rely on the instincts and experience he had already built as Spider-Man. For the first time since Vilgax arrived, he wasn't simply trying to survive.
He was starting to control the fight.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Peter finally understood what he’d been doing wrong. He had been treating every transformation as a separate solution instead of thinking like Spider-Man. The Omnitrix gave him different bodies and abilities, but Peter’s real advantage was knowing when to change his approach. He switched forms based on what the fight required, using XLR8 to create distance, Diamondhead to block attacks and Upgrade whenever he could interfere with Vilgax’s technology. Every switch burned through the Omnitrix's remaining time faster, so Peter couldn't keep doing it forever. Vilgax eventually realized what Peter was doing and stopped trying to chase him around the battlefield. He waited for Peter to commit to an attack, then struck whenever Peter changed forms. Peter's experience kept him alive, but he was running out of room and the Omnitrix was running out of time. Vilgax knew it.

Peter used XLR8 one final time to get behind Vilgax and disrupt several pieces of his equipment before Vilgax could turn around. Peter switched into Upgrade and connected himself to the cybernetic systems. This time, he wasn’t trying to shut Vilgax down completely. He targeted the systems controlling the weapons and communications equipment, disrupting them long enough to leave Vilgax without the support of his ship.

Peter separated and switched into Diamondhead. He created a large crystalline structure around Vilgax, giving him just enough time to move away before the Omnitrix timed out. Peter returned to human form and nearly collapsed. Vilgax broke through the crystal and saw exactly what had happened. The Omnitrix was red. Peter had nothing left.

Vilgax didn't retreat. He moved straight toward Peter and reached for the Omnitrix. Peter tried to move, but he was too exhausted to get away. The moment Vilgax's hand came down hard enough to kill him, the Omnitrix reacted on its own. The red light flashed green. The device bypassed the recharge long enough to preserve its wearer and transformed Peter into XLR8.

Peter didn't waste the chance. He used the emergency transformation to race through Vilgax's disabled equipment and the remains of his communications system, ripping apart the connections Peter had already weakened as Upgrade. Then he hit the controls linking Vilgax to the forces still operating across the city. By the time Peter moved away, Vilgax's local support was gone and his ship's systems were still compromised.

The Omnitrix timed Peter out again almost immediately. But now Vilgax was the one without an easy next move. His attempt to take the Omnitrix had triggered a protection he hadn't expected, his forces had lost coordination, and his ship was no longer giving him the support he needed to keep pressing the attack. Continuing meant fighting blind while risking the Omnitrix activating another defense he didn't understand. Vilgax withdrew to the ship with what remained of his forces. He wasn't giving up on the Omnitrix. He was leaving because Peter had finally made taking it more dangerous than retreating and trying again later.

Peter had spent years learning how to be Spider-Man by making mistakes and figuring things out afterward. The Omnitrix wasn’t going to be any different. He would keep studying the transformations, learn their limits and figure out how they could work alongside the abilities he’d already developed.

The important part was that the Omnitrix hadn’t changed who Peter was. He was still Peter Parker, and he was still Spider-Man. The difference was that he now had access to abilities from species scattered across the universe, along with a responsibility that extended far beyond New York.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Peter left the waterfront before the authorities arrived. He didn’t know when Vilgax would return, and he knew other people could eventually come looking for the Omnitrix. He also knew that he couldn’t spend the rest of his life waiting for someone to attack him.
For now, he had a city to protect.
Peter activated the Omnitrix and selected XLR8. The transformation gave him the speed he needed to cross the city quickly, and he disappeared into the streets before anyone could identify him.
The Omnitrix had brought an entirely new part of the universe into Peter Parker’s life, but it hadn’t taken Spider-Man away. If anything, it had given Peter more ways to do what he’d always done.
Protect people.

And somewhere beyond Earth, the existence of the Omnitrix was already becoming known to beings who had never heard of Spider-Man before. Peter had no idea what would come looking for him next, but for the first time, he was ready to find out.

scripts.title: What If Spider-Man Was Reborn With His Memories

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Peter’s last memory is Titan. Thanos has already beaten them, the Gauntlet is almost complete, and Peter can feel himself disappearing while Tony tries to hold onto him.

Then he wakes up years earlier in Queens, back in his younger body before any of it happened. Peter remembers enough to know where all of this leads and how badly it ends. Now he has years to prepare for Thanos, and every choice he makes before then could change what happens when that fight finally comes.
And the first person he needs to convince is Tony Stark, years before Tony has any idea who Peter Parker is.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter would wake up in Queens years before Titan, back in his younger body, and the first thing he’d do is check the date. Once he realizes how far back he is, he’d probably spend the rest of the day making sure this isn’t some kind of dream. He’d check the apartment, look for May, go through old school stuff, and compare little details with wnat he remembers. Everything would match.

He’d also notice pretty quickly that he doesn’t have his powers yet. No spider-sense, no strength, no sticking to walls. He’s just Peter again, which would make the whole situation feel even stranger because he remembers being Spider-Man for years and suddenly can’t do any of it.

Peter would start writing everything down before he forgets details. He wouldn’t try to write his whole life from memory. He’d focus on the things he actually remembers that could matter later, like when he meets Tony, what he personally saw during Civil War, the Stones and people he encountered during Infinity War, and the important parts of the Titan fight. He’d know right away that some of that information could become useless once he starts changing things, but he’d still want a record of what happened the first time.

The spider bite would be the first big choice. In this scenario, Peter remembers enough about the circumstances of his original bite to know roughly when and where it happens, giving him a few days to decide whether he wants to let it happen again. He’d think about avoiding it because he already knows how much pain came with becoming Spider-Man, but he’d also remember Titan and how badly Earth needed everyone it could get.

Peter would go through with it. He’d use what he remembers to put himself back in the circumstances that led to the bite the first time because he knows he'll need the powers later. The difference is that this time he knows what's coming, so he’d be much more careful in the days after. He wouldn't have to spend weeks figuring out why he’s suddenly stronger or why he keeps sticking to things. He already knows how all of it works.

That would let him start training much earlier too. He’d work on control, movement, web chemistry, and how much strength he can safely use around normal people. Peter already remembers years of fighting experience, so even in a younger body, he’d pick things up much faster than he did the first time.

He’d also start thinking about Tony immediately. Peter remembers how important Tony becomes later, but this version of Tony has no reason to know who he is. Peter can’t just walk into Stark Tower and say he’s from the future. He’d sound insane and probably get thrown out before he gets to the useful part. So Peter would wait until he has something Tony can actually check.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Peter would spend the next few months building up enough proof that Tony can’t ignore him. He’d know that trying to contact Stark Industries as a random kid probably goes nowhere, so he’d start with technology.

Peter already remembers how his own web shooters worked, and he remembers the Stark-built suits and systems Tony personally gave him access to. He wouldn't know Tony’s private research or be able to rebuild an Iron Man suit in his bedroom, but he could reproduce pieces of technology and design ideas he personally used years later that should not exist yet.

He could improve one of his web shooter designs and recreate simplified features he remembers from the suits Tony eventually built for him. That would be enough to get Tony's attention, but it wouldn't prove time travel by itself because Tony hasn't designed those Spider-Man-specific systems yet.

Peter would eventually get a prototype or data file into Stark Industries through a competition, internship program, or direct message to one of Tony’s engineers. Once Tony sees it, he’d probably assume someone older is helping Peter or that the designs were stolen.

Peter would use things Tony can actually verify as the real proof. He could predict specific events Peter personally lived through and include details that only become checkable when those events happen. Once a few of those predictions come true, the technology stops looking like an unusually advanced kid guessing ahead and starts supporting Peter's claim that he remembers the future.

Tony would still be suspicious. He’s seen enough strange things by this point to know people can fake information, steal files, or build convincing lies. Peter would have to keep giving him things that add up.
Eventually he’d tell Tony the part that matters. Something is coming to Earth years from now, and if they wait until it arrives, they lose.

Peter wouldn’t dump every detail at once. He’d explain that there are 6 Infinity Stones, that Thanos wants all of them, and that Tony eventually ends up fighting him on another planet. He’d also tell Tony that the future Peter remembers ends with half the universe disappearing.

Once Tony confirms even a few details, Peter would have his attention. From there, their relationship would start in a completely different place. Tony wouldn't be discovering Spider-Man and trying to mentor him. He’d be dealing with a kid who already knows him, already understands his tech, and is warning him about a war that hasn't happened yet.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter would know Civil War is coming long before Tony recruits him for the airport fight, but he wouldn't know the entire plot behind it. What he remembers directly is Tony bringing him to Germany to fight Steve's side over the Accords and Bucky Barnes, and how badly the Avengers' split still affected Tony years later.

Instead of giving Tony Zemo's name or pretending he knows exactly what happened in Siberia, Peter could warn him that the conflict around Barnes becomes deeply personal and helps tear the team apart. Tony could use those fragmented clues, along with Peter's warning that someone is manipulating the situation, to investigate the bombing and Barnes more carefully when those events begin.

That wouldn't automatically reveal everything, but it could keep Tony from treating each new development at face value. If his investigation uncovers Zemo and the truth about Bucky's Hydra conditioning before the Siberia confrontation, Tony would have time to process what happened instead of learning it while standing next to Steve and Bucky after hours of fighting.

Steve would still have reasons to oppose the Sokovia Accords, and Tony would still have reasons to support them, so the political argument wouldn't disappear. The Avengers could still split over how much control governments should have, but the personal fight between Tony and Steve would be much easier to avoid.

Peter would probably get involved before the airport fight too. Tony would already know him and trust some of what he says, so Peter could help track Zemo instead of being pulled in at the last second to fight Captain America.

That could stop the airport battle from becoming as bad as it was in the original timeline. Rhodey might never get injured, Natasha wouldn’t have to turn on Tony’s side at the end, and Steve wouldn’t have to disappear for years with half the team.

Peter would still know that keeping the Avengers together matters more than winning the argument over the Accords. He saw what happened when Thanos came while Earth’s strongest people were split apart and barely talking.

The Avengers wouldn’t become perfectly united after that. There would still be arguments, and some members might refuse to sign the Accords. They’d just have a much better chance of staying in contact and working together when something serious happens.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Homecoming would change even faster because Peter already knows who Adrian Toomes is and how the whole weapons operation works.

Peter wouldn’t spend months chasing random deals around Queens trying to figure out who is selling Chitauri weapons. He’d know exactly what kind of operation he’s looking for and roughly where the first pieces start showing up.

He’d tell Tony early instead of trying to handle everything alone. Tony would probably send people to check the leads because Peter has already been right about bigger things, and they'd find enough alien weapons to prove the operation is real.

This time, Tony and Peter could move against Toomes's established operation before he ever reaches the later disasters Peter remembers, like the Staten Island Ferry or the attempt to rob the Department of Damage Control transport plane. Peter already knows what the Vulture suit can do, where the wings are weak, and how Toomes fights. He could web the turbines, stay away from the blades, and avoid getting caught off guard by the suit’s speed.

Toomes would get arrested much earlier, and the ferry disaster would never happen. Peter also wouldn't have the same fight with Tony over being reckless because he’s been much more open with him from the start.

Tony wold start treating Peter less like a kid he has to keep away from dangerous things and more like someone who keeps giving him useful information about the future. Peter would still be young, but he’d already have years of experience in his head and would make fewer of the mistakes Tony remembers seeing from him later.
Peter would also know that this is where his memories start becoming less reliable. Toomes is gone earlier, Civil War played out differently, and the Avengers are still talking to each other.
The next few years won’t match what he remembers closely enough for him to rely on exact events anymore. That would push him and Tony toward preparing for Thanos directly.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Once Civil War and Vulture are handled differently, Tony would have much more time to focus on the warning Peter gave him.

He’d start by checking everything they know about the Infinity Stones. The Tesseract is already tied to the Space Stone, and Tony could work backward through S.H.I.E.L.D. records to figure out where it went after the Battle of New York. Vision already has the Mind Stone in his head, which gives Tony 1 Stone he can actually study.

Peter could also tell Tony that during the invasion he eventually fought beside a wizard named Doctor Strange in New York who protected a green Stone inside a necklace. Peter wouldn't know the Eye of Agamotto's full history or how Strange became its guardian, so Tony would have to investigate those clues once Strange actually enters the mystical world.

Once Strange has actually become a sorcerer, Tony could approach him with Peter's description of the future battle and the green Stone. Their first meeting would probably be rough because Strange wouldn't like Tony arriving with questions about an artifact he is supposed to protect, but Peter's knowledge of Strange and the coming attack would be difficult to dismiss.

Strange and the Masters of the Mystic Arts could then identify what Peter only knew from experience: the green Stone is the Time Stone, and it is one of the objects Thanos will eventually target. That lets Tony learn the details organically instead of Peter somehow knowing mystical information he was never taught.

Wakanda would be even less clear to Peter. He would know that T'Challa fought beside the Avengers and that Wakandan forces were involved when Thanos attacked Earth, but he wouldn't know Shuri's exact capabilities or the country's full technological level. Tony would have to discover that through his later connection to T'Challa rather than getting it from Peter.

Thor would be another problem because he spends long periods away from Earth. Peter knows Thor eventually learns more about the Stones and Thanos, but Peter doesn’t know every detail of where Thor is years before Infinity War.

Peter would help with all of that while continuing to train. He’d know that his own powers aren’t enough to stop Thanos, so he’d focus on becoming better at the things he already does well. Faster web setups, better movement, stronger control over his spider-sense, and more ways to restrain someone without having to overpower them directly.

Tony would also have years to think about the Titan fight Peter remembers. Peter could explain how close they came to taking the Gauntlet off, how Strange saw millions of possible futures, and how Thanos was still able to finish the Snap. Tony wouldn’t copy that plan because the whole goal is to keep Thanos from ever reaching that point.

They'd start looking for ways to stop him before he has several Stones. That would take the story away from Peter replaying his old life. By now, too much has changed, and the next version of Thanos’ attack could happen pretty differently.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Once Tony believes him, Peter would stop treating Thanos like something they can deal with when he shows up. They’ve got years, so they’d start using that time to understand the Stones and keep track of where the ones tied to Earth might end up.

Vision would be the first one they can actually study because the Mind Stone is already sitting in his forehead. Tony would want to know how much of Vision’s body depends on it and whether removing it later is possible without killing him. They wouldn’t have Wakanda helping yet, because T’Challa hasn’t opened the country to the outside world and Tony can’t just call Shuri years early. Tony could still start doing his own work with Bruce whenever Bruce is available and build up everything they know about Vision’s systems.

Peter would also know about Doctor Strange, but going to him too early wouldn't help. Stephen is still a surgeon before his accident, and he has no idea what the Time Stone is. Peter would have to wait until Strange actually becomes a sorcerer. That would bother him because he remembers how important Strange becomes later, but messing with Stephen’s life before the accident could stop that whole path from happening.

Peter would also keep making his own web fluid and working on how quickly he can set traps. He remembers how close they came to getting the Gauntlet off Thanos on Titan, so he’d spend years getting better at using webs to hold someone stronger than him for a few seconds.

Tony could eventually build the Iron Spider earlier too. He already knows they’re preparing for a fight where Peter may end up dealing with aliens and people far stronger than anything in Queens. Peter would still want the suit to feel like something he can control himself, so Tony would give him better protection and more tools without turning it into something Peter can’t use naturally.
By then, they’d have a good amount of preparation in place before anything close to Infinity War even begins.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Peter and Tony would have to wait until the events around Civil War give them a real connection to T'Challa and Wakanda. Once T'Challa understands that someone was manipulating the conflict and the immediate crisis is over, Tony could approach him with Vision and explain the broader warning about Thanos and the Mind Stone. That gives T'Challa a reason to bring the problem to Wakanda's scientists. Shuri could then determine for herself whether the Stone can be separated from Vision, with far more time than she had in Infinity War.

That process could take months or even longer, and Tony would be fine with that. They've got time. With that advance warning, Shuri would eventually manage to remove the Stone safely, letting Vision keep living while the Stone is stored somewhere else. Wakanda could build a vault around it, Strange could add magical protection, or the Avengers could keep it moving between secure locations so Thanos can’t just follow 1 obvious target.

Strange would also have time to prepare the Sanctum for an attack. Once Peter tells him that Ebony Maw eventually comes to New York for the Time Stone, Strange could start working with Wong on ways to keep someone from taking him or the Eye out of the building.
Tony and Strange would still argue constantly because that part probably isn’t changing. The difference would be that they already know each other by the time Thanos becomes an active threat.

Thor would also be far more useful for the parts of the plan that require space travel because he understands the galaxy and has connections outside Earth. Peter's warning could give Thor a reason to investigate Thanos and places like Nidavellir, but it wouldn't automatically give him Stormbreaker years early. If Ragnarok still costs Thor Mjolnir, the known Thanos threat could then give him a reason to seek Eitri for a weapon capable of killing Thanos. Peter would also know the Guardians exist, but he wouldn't have a simple way to contact them.
By the time Thanos starts making serious moves, Earth would already have a team that knows what he wants and has spent years preparing around the Stones.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The first major attack would probably still come from the Black Order, because Thanos needs the Stones and Earth still has at least 1 of them.

Maw and Cull arriving in New York would play very differently. Tony would already know who they are. Strange would know exactly why they’re there. Peter would already have the Iron Spider ready, and Wong would have the Sanctum prepared for someone trying to take the Time Stone.

Maw’s telekinesis would still be dangerous because he can move people and objects around without getting close. Strange could use portals to keep changing the angles, while Tony attacks the ship and Peter keeps civilians away from the fight.
Peter would know that letting Maw take Strange into space creates a huge problem. He’d focus on stopping that before it happens.

Tony could hit the ship’s engines while it’s still over New York, and Strange could portal parts of the ship away if he gets a clean chance. Peter could web Maw’s hands and arms whenever Strange gives him an opening, because Maw uses very precise movements when controlling objects.
Cull would be easier to manage with more Avengers nearby. Steve, Rhodey, or Vision could already be on the way because the team hasn’t been split for years.

The attack could end with Maw and Cull captured or killed before the ship ever leaves Earth. The other Black Order members would have a harder time finding the Mind Stone too. With Shuri having already removed it from Vision, attacking Vision in Scotland gets them nothing.
