They’d have to figure out where the Stone was moved, and the Avengers could use that to pull them toward a place they chose themselves.

Thanos would realize pretty quickly that Earth knew he was coming. That could push him to change his own plan. He might come personally earlier, send more forces, or go after other Stones before trying Earth again.
Peter wouldn’t know what he chooses because this part never happened in the future he remembers. The team would have to deal with whatever comes next without using Peter like a guidebook.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Thor would be the person most likely to help them find Thanos before he reaches Earth. If he’s been checking what’s happening around the galaxy, he could eventually connect with people who have actually dealt with Thanos directly and help the team turn Peter's warning into a real location instead of assuming the original Titan encounter will repeat itself.

That could bring the Guardians into the story. Gamora and Nebula would immediately become important because they know how Thanos operates. Peter would remember meeting them on Titan, but he wouldn’t know where Thanos will be in this altered timeline. Using what they know about Thanos' ship routes, troop movements, and the Stones he still needs, Gamora and Nebula could narrow down where he is heading next and give the strike team a specific location to intercept him.
Nebula would know how Thanos’ ships move, where he keeps troops, and how he fights. Gamora would know even more about his habits and what he'll do once he’s close to finishing the Gauntlet.

Peter wouldn't know the rule behind the Soul Stone. He was never on Vormir and never learned exactly how Thanos got it before the Snap. If Gamora keeps that information hidden, the Avengers wouldn’t suddenly have it either.

They’d focus on stopping Thanos before the Stones become impossible to protect. If Gamora or Nebula can locate him while he only has 1 or 2 Stones, Tony could bring a team built specifically around taking the Gauntlet away, while the Stones on Earth stay protected somewhere else.

They also wouldn't have to bring every hero into space. Steve, Natasha, Wakanda, and other Avengers could stay behind to protect Earth while Tony, Strange, Thor, Peter, and whoever else is needed goes after Thanos.

The important lesson from Titan would be the strategy, not the location. If Mantis gets control during the planned interception, Quill would already know he has to stay away until the Gauntlet is off.

Tony could build clamps around the wrist. Strange could use portals to keep Thanos’ other arm away from the Gauntlet. Peter could web the fingers together and hold the joints while Thor keeps pressure on Thanos from the other side.

If Ragnarok has already cost Thor Mjolnir and the altered timeline has subsequently led him to forge Stormbreaker with Eitri, Thor would have a weapon that can seriously hurt Thanos. Wanda could also be part of the attack if they decide bringing her is worth the risk. Her power gives them another way to hold Thanos in place without getting close.

The fight would still be brutal because Thanos doesn’t need a full Gauntlet to be dangerous. With the Power Stone and Space Stone alone, he could tear through most of the group if he gets room to move.
The team would have to keep him busy long enough for Mantis to work. Once she does, everyone knows exactly what comes next.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Peter would be in almost the same position he remembers for a few seconds, holding Thanos down while everyone pulls at the Gauntlet.
The difference would be everything they changed before getting there.

Tony and Strange have worked together before. Thor is already part of the plan. Quill knows what happened last time and stays away from Thanos while Mantis keeps him under. Peter has spent years practicing ways to hold someone stronger than him.

Tony could lock the Gauntlet around the wrist so Thanos can’t close his hand easily. Peter could web every finger separately instead of throwing webbing around the whole arm. Strange could use portals around the elbow and shoulder to keep the arm stretched away from Thanos’ body. The Gauntlet could come off. The second it does, Strange would send it through a portal to an inaccessible location elsewhere near the chosen battlefield. Nobody would leave it sitting beside Thanos while they decide what to do next.

That would separate Thanos from the Stones immediately without relying on Strange opening an interplanetary portal back to Earth in the middle of the fight. Once Thanos is contained or defeated, the heroes could decide how to move and separate the Stones safely.

The fight would keep going because Thanos is still strong enough to kill people without the Gauntlet. If Thor has Stormbreaker by this point, he could go straight at him with it. Wanda could hold him down when he tries to move. Tony could attack from range while Peter stays out of the direct fight and keeps webbing Thanos whenever he gets close to someone.

Thanos would still hurt people. He could break armor, injure Thor, or throw Peter hard enough to take him out of the fight for a while. Peter’s memories give them preparation, not a perfect battle where nobody gets touched.

The Avengers would have a much better chance once the Stones are gone. Thor and Wanda together could do serious damage, especially if Thanos doesn’t have the Stones helping him escape or block their attacks. Strange could keep him from simply leaving through another ship or portal.

sections.name: PART 11
paras: Stopping Thanos before the Snap would save everyone Peter watched disappear, but Peter would still be living in a world that went in a completely different direction because of him.

Tony would still be alive. Natasha wouldn’t have to die on Vormir. Steve wouldn’t lose 5 years of his life after the Snap. May wouldn’t disappear and come back years later. Peter would keep living through those years normally instead of vanishing at 16 and returning to a world that had moved on without him.
There'd still be problems after Thanos. His armies wouldn't disappear just because he’s dead, and the Infinity Stones would still be dangerous enough that nobody would want them sitting together.

Strange could keep the Time Stone. Wakanda could continue protecting the Mind Stone after Shuri safely removed it from Vision. Thor could take the Space Stone somewhere away from Earth, and the Power Stone could be returned to the people responsible for guarding it if that’s still possible in the new timeline.
They'd probably keep the Stones separated because Peter has already shown everyone what happens when 1 person gets all 6.
Tony would know by then why Peter was so desperate to keep him alive.
Their relationship would probably be closer than it ever was the first time because Tony met Peter years earlier and watched him grow into Spider-Man instead of meeting him shortly before Civil War.
Peter would still finish school, keep seeing May, and keep patrolling New York. He’d have better training and more experience than the version of himself who first met Tony.
He’d also know that the future can change in ways he never saw coming.

That would probably keep him from trying to control every event after Thanos. He already changed enough to save everyone from the Snap, and trying to keep forcing the world toward some perfect version could cause problems he has no memory of anymore.
Peter would go back to being Spider-Man with the people he lost still alive around him. (No need for an outro)

scripts.title: What If Spider-Man Was Trained By Gojo

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Peter Parker is still early in his career as Spider-Man. He has superhuman strength, speed, agility, a Spider-Sense that warns him when danger is coming, and homemade web-shooters that let him move through Queens faster than almost anyone alive. But he is still inexperienced, still learning what his powers can and cannot solve, and he has never encountered anything like cursed energy.

Satoru Gojo looked at the teenager hanging from the ceiling and decided he was interesting. Peter didn't need more power. He needed someone who could show him what his abilities were actually capable of. What happens when the strongest sorcerer alive starts training Spider-Man from the beginning — before Tony Stark, before the Avengers, before any of it — is not what you're expecting.

sections.name: PART 1
sections.label: The First Encounter
paras: The timeline begins before Peter Parker has become involved with the Avengers. He's still operating around Queens in his homemade suit, using web shooters he designed himself, fighting ordinary criminals and the occasional enhanced individual. He's already unusually capable — strong enough to lift cars, fast enough that most opponents can't land clean strikes, and smart enough to have built technology that puts him years ahead of anyone his age. What he doesn't have is any exposure to the supernatural.
That changes when a dimensional anomaly briefly connects his universe to the world of Jujutsu Kaisen.

The crossover introduces a cursed spirit into Peter's world. In jujutsu terms, cursed spirits are beings produced from accumulated negative human emotion — invisible to ordinary people and normally impossible to exorcise through ordinary physical force alone. The dimensional overlap also brings Peter into contact with the same cursed-energy system Gojo's world operates on. Peter doesn't gain an innate technique from this; he simply proves capable of producing and learning to control cursed energy once Gojo shows him how. A person who cannot perceive cursed energy can still be attacked without understanding what is happening to them.
Peter's situation is unusual because his Spider-Sense still responds to the danger.

It doesn't give him the ability to see the spirit. It gives him the warning — that immediate, wordless certainty that something is about to hit him. He reacts before he understands what he's reacting to, jumping clear of a debris strike he never saw coming. When the strike happens again, he fires a web into empty air and feels it attach to something solid. The outline of the curse becomes something he can track, even if he still can't see it.

The problem is that his attacks aren't exorcising it. His strength connects, but ordinary punches aren't enough to properly damage the curse, and Peter has no cursed energy or cursed tool to bridge that gap. He's fighting something he can't meaningfully put down, with a threat sense that tells him where to dodge but not how to win. He defaults to the only reliable option he has — keep moving, keep the spirit occupied, and don't let it land anything clean.
That's when Gojo arrives through the same dimensional anomaly.

He understands the threat immediately. His Six Eyes — an ability that gives him extraordinary perception of cursed energy — let him analyze the spirit and the situation within seconds. He also notices Peter almost immediately. The teenager has no jujutsu training, no cursed technique, no formal background in anything Gojo recognizes. He's surviving entirely through physical ability and an instinctive danger sense that Gojo finds genuinely unusual.

Gojo uses Cursed Technique Reversal: Red to destroy the curse. He generates positive energy through reverse cursed technique and feeds it into Limitless, producing the reversed application of the technique: a violent repulsive force powerful enough to exorcise the spirit in one strike.

The threat is gone. Peter drops to the warehouse floor. And Gojo takes a long look at the teenager who just survived a cursed spirit encounter with zero preparation and no understanding of what he was fighting.

Peter isn't a sorcerer. He hasn't been trained in cursed energy, and there's no evidence he was born with an innate technique. His abilities come from the radioactive spider bite that transformed him. His Spider-Sense is part of that transformation — not a jujutsu ability wearing a different name.
But Gojo doesn't see a dead end.

He sees a teenager who already has extraordinary physical capabilities and an instinctive awareness that might be worth something if it was properly developed. He decides to find out how far that goes.

Peter's first encounter with a cursed spirit becomes the beginning of something much larger. But the question now isn't just whether Gojo's interest is justified — it's what he intends to do with it, and how much of Peter's existing identity will survive what comes next.

sections.name: PART 2
sections.label: Learning the Foundation
paras: Gojo's first decision is straightforward. He gives Peter four months.

Not a formal agreement — more of a statement. He tells Peter that if the concept of a spider-powered teenager learning jujutsu is going to mean anything at all, Peter needs to demonstrate over the next four months that it's worth taking further. Gojo will come back to Queens several times a week and teach Peter the fundamentals. If Peter proves he can handle it, the training will continue after that initial trial — and eventually Gojo will introduce him to the actual jujutsu world in Japan.
If it doesn't justify it, Gojo will have had an interesting experience and Peter will go back to fighting criminals without cursed energy.

Peter agrees immediately and spends the first three sessions unable to do anything Gojo asks. Cursed energy doesn't respond to physical strength. It doesn't respond to intelligence, either — at least not in the way Peter is used to applying it. Peter tries to analyze it like an engineering problem and finds that there's nothing mechanical to grab onto. The energy follows its own rules, and those rules aren't written down anywhere. Gojo has to correct the same mistake multiple times before Peter's attempts start producing consistent results. The frustration is genuine. Peter has never been bad at learning something quickly, and being comprehensively bad at this for weeks is a specific kind of difficult for someone used to picking things up fast. His first real breakthrough is cursed energy reinforcement — coating the body with cursed energy to enhance physical abilities and make attacks more effective against supernatural opponents.

The change in his combat performance is immediate. His punches hit harder. His durability improves when he reinforces himself before an impact. His movements become more effective because he can combine his natural agility with cursed energy instead of relying entirely on his physical foundation.

Gojo watches this for a moment and then says, with the particular boredom of someone describing the weather, "You know, most people's first reinforcement attempt breaks their own fingers. Yours is already cleaner than Nanami's was at this stage. Don't let it go to your head." He then assigns Peter three more weeks of basic repetition exercises, because that's what Gojo considers an appropriate response to genuine progress.

The consistency challenge is harder than learning the technique. Peter has spent years moving on instinct — Spider-Sense warns him, his body reacts before his mind catches up. Cursed energy requires a different kind of discipline. He has to maintain deliberate control while simultaneously moving, attacking, protecting himself, and managing his web shooters. The number of things he needs to manage at once is genuinely overwhelming in the early stages. Gojo's solution is controlled cursed spirit encounters.

Peter begins fighting curses under conditions Gojo has arranged. Early encounters are less about winning and more about keeping cursed energy active while he moves. He discovers that his webs still function usefully — they restrain physical targets and reveal the outlines of invisible spirits — while cursed energy allows him to reinforce the attacks that follow. The combination starts to produce something recognizable as a fighting style, even if it's still rough. Then he fails.

Six weeks into the trial, during one of these controlled encounters, Peter moves to finish a curse before it can reach an alleyway behind a restaurant. He's confident. He's been reinforcing consistently for weeks. He fires a web, closes the distance, and goes to exorcise it — and his cursed energy control fails under pressure. The energy dissipates at the wrong moment. The spirit gets past him.
A delivery worker who had stepped out of a side door catches one strike before Gojo can intervene. The man survives. The injury isn't permanent. But he gets hurt, and Peter is the reason.

Gojo exorcises the curse and doesn't say anything critical. That's almost worse. Peter is quiet for a long time, and what he comes back to training with after that is something that goes beyond wanting to learn quickly. He's been fighting criminals for years and always operated on the assumption that his speed and strength would prevent collateral damage. This is the first time he's been directly wrong about that. It costs him something — not his confidence entirely,
but the comfortable assumption that learning new abilities is just a technical problem with a technical solution.
He goes back to the fundamentals harder than he had before.
Gojo notices the difference. He doesn't comment on it directly, which is its own kind of instruction.

Peter also starts improving his cursed energy control under pressure rather than just in controlled exercises. He learns to reinforce specific parts of his body at the right moment — legs before explosive movement, arms immediately before striking — instead of wasting energy across his entire body. He begins experimenting with using cursed energy around his web-based attacks — reinforcing his arms before a hard web-yank, his legs before changing direction, and his grip when a restraint is under pressure. The synthetic web fluid itself isn't magically converted into cursed energy; Peter is learning to use reinforcement to make the movements and physical follow-ups around his equipment more effective. His Spider-Sense and cursed energy control start functioning as a single system rather than two separate tools.
By the fourth month, he's not just surviving encounters with curses — he's finishing them. The foundation is solid.

The question Gojo set at the beginning of the year is getting closer to its answer. But the foundation is only the first part. Before Japan, before whatever Gojo is building toward, Peter still needs to understand what his specific advantages actually are — and what they can't do.[PART 3 — Perception and the Limits of Spider-Sense]
Gojo's next area of focus is perception.

His Six Eyes make him extraordinarily capable of seeing and processing cursed energy — the precision they provide is part of what makes Limitless as powerful as it is. Peter doesn't have anything like that. His Spider-Sense works differently. It's a danger warning, not a perception ability. It tells him something is about to hurt him. It doesn't tell him what that something is, how it works, or what its technique does.

Gojo's insight is that teaching Peter to develop cursed energy sensing could give him a second source of information that, used alongside Spider-Sense, becomes considerably more useful than either ability alone.

The early practice is slow. Cursed energy perception requires the kind of accumulated experience that most trained sorcerers build over years, and Peter is starting from nothing. He can barely distinguish variations in cursed energy at close range, let alone read what a specific technique does or where a hidden spirit is positioned.
But Spider-Sense keeps running underneath all of it.

When a cursed spirit approaches during training, Peter feels the danger before he consciously identifies what he's sensing. With enough repetition, he starts connecting that instinctive warning to the actual presence of cursed energy. The two abilities don't merge into a new version of the Six Eyes — Peter doesn't suddenly gain Gojo's precision, and he can't reproduce the analytical depth that makes those eyes exceptional. What changes is that Peter becomes better at interpreting information his own body is already giving him.
This changes his combat style in practical terms.

Before, Peter often reacted after Spider-Sense warned him. With training, he starts using the warning to predict where an attack is likely to originate and moves before the threat fully develops. Cursed energy sensing adds another layer — he can now detect the presence of spirits he previously couldn't locate at all, and he can recognize when a sorcerer nearby is using cursed energy, even if reading the technique itself remains beyond him.
His movement system starts to become something genuinely unusual in the jujutsu context.

Most sorcerers develop their combat style around two-dimensional ground movement, with occasional vertical elements. Peter has been moving in three dimensions since he was fifteen. He uses web lines to reposition in midair, changes direction during swings in ways most opponents can't anticipate, and approaches targets from angles that someone standing on the ground is unlikely to account for. Cursed energy reinforcement makes those movements faster and more stable. His Spider-Sense helps him decide when to change direction before an attack arrives.

Gojo notes — correctly — that Peter's greatest advantage isn't raw power. It's information. He receives constant warnings about threats around him, and his physical abilities let him respond to those warnings extremely quickly. Cursed energy training doesn't transform that into an omniscient system. It makes Peter better at using the information he was already getting.
But Gojo also makes sure Peter understands the limits.

Spider-Sense tells him that danger is coming. It doesn't explain what an opponent's technique does, or how to counter it, or whether greater speed will solve the problem. Powerful sorcerers can create conditions that Spider-Sense doesn't automatically clarify. A warning that danger is approaching and an understanding of what to do about it are two different things, and Peter needs both.

So Peter learns to combine instinct with observation. He watches opponents before engaging. He studies how they use cursed energy. He pays attention to movement patterns. Then he lets Spider-Sense fill in the information he can't consciously process in time.

It becomes the core of his fighting style. And it's going to matter — because what Gojo is building toward requires Peter to be functional in environments where standing still and studying an opponent first isn't an option.

sections.name: PART 4
sections.label: The Technique Question
paras: At some point, Gojo has to answer a question he's been working around for months.
Can Peter develop a cursed technique of his own?

In jujutsu, an innate technique isn't something a sorcerer invents through practice. Innate techniques are engraved in the brain at birth, and most sorcerers spend their entire careers refining the specific technique they were born with rather than developing new ones. Learning to control cursed energy doesn't automatically produce a technique. The two things are related but separate.

Peter's abilities came from the radioactive spider bite. There is no reason to assume that the bite secretly gave him a jujutsu technique, and Gojo doesn't treat it that way. Instead, he tests whether Peter already possesses an innate technique that has simply never manifested.
The answer is no.

Peter can manipulate cursed energy, reinforce his body, and apply what he's learned to his existing fighting style. But nothing presents itself as an innate technique, and Gojo doesn't push him toward one. That limitation actually clarifies Gojo's approach rather than complicating it. Peter doesn't need a cursed technique. His physical abilities already give him an unusual foundation. His Spider-Sense gives him an advantage most sorcerers don't possess. Gojo redirects the training toward something more productive: getting Peter to apply cursed energy with enough precision that the absence of a technique stops being relevant.
Peter's web shooters become especially important here.

They're an extension of his intelligence and engineering ability. Instead of inventing a fictional cursed energy web ability, Peter learns to incorporate cursed energy into the way he already uses his equipment. He reinforces his body before launching from a web line, giving the movement more force and stability. He uses cursed energy to strengthen his grip when an opponent tries to break through a web restraint. He reinforces his physical strikes after using his webs to control positioning.

The result is a fighting style that looks familiar from the outside but has become considerably more sophisticated in practice. Peter can move through a battlefield using his webs while maintaining cursed energy reinforcement. He can fight cursed spirits using tools he designed himself. He can switch between ranged control and close-range combat without abandoning either system.

Gojo eventually pushes Peter toward something harder than reinforcement — precise concentration of cursed energy into individual strikes, applied with enough control that the force doesn't scatter. The improvement is less dramatic than learning a new ability but more significant in practice. A skilled sorcerer doesn't simply produce as much cursed energy as possible. They control exactly how and where it's applied.

Peter's intelligence makes him particularly good at this. He treats combat like a problem that can be analyzed. He notes what works, identifies mistakes, and changes his approach after every session. Gojo provides the experience Peter lacks. Peter's ability to absorb and apply those lessons quickly does the rest.
By the end of the four-month trial Gojo originally proposed, Peter has developed something he couldn't have described at the start — a personal cursed energy fighting style that doesn't belong to any
existing school of jujutsu because it was built around abilities that no sorcerer in the jujutsu world possesses.

Gojo watches a training session near the end of the four months and makes a decision: Peter is worth continuing to train. Japan can come later. For now, Peter still has a life in Queens, and Gojo has no intention of rushing him into jujutsu society before he's ready.

sections.name: PART 5
sections.label: The Psychological Shift
paras: The most significant change Gojo makes to Peter is psychological.

Peter's biggest problem has never been a lack of power. Even before meeting Gojo, he was already considerably stronger and faster than ordinary humans. His problem has always been learning how to use that power while managing everything that comes with being Spider-Man — the losses, the guilt, the constant weight of knowing that being fast enough and strong enough still hasn't been enough sometimes.
Gojo understands that problem better than he lets on.

He's spent years carrying the expectations that come with being the strongest sorcerer alive. He knows what it means to possess overwhelming power while still being responsible for protecting specific people who get hurt anyway. His response to that weight is very different from Peter's — Gojo's confidence reads as casual to the point of arrogance — but the source of it isn't
arrogance. It's the product of having genuinely worked through what it means to be as powerful as he is and decided to own it rather than apologize for it.
His teaching reflects that.

Gojo doesn't push Peter toward cruelty or indifference. What he pushes against is hesitation. Peter has a habit of holding back because he knows how easily his strength could seriously injure someone. That caution is part of what makes him a hero. But it can also make him slow in situations where being slow means someone else gets hurt — which Peter already knows from the encounter six weeks into their training.
Gojo forces him to be more decisive. He teaches Peter that protecting people doesn't require apologizing for having the power to do it.

Peter's personality doesn't change. He remains talkative, prone to making jokes when he's nervous, and genuinely troubled by the parts of this work that have costs. He still overthinks. He still cares about every person in every situation more than is probably strategically useful. Gojo's influence doesn't alter any of that. It gives those qualities a more stable foundation — something Peter can actually stand on instead of sinking into.

Gojo also teaches Peter that strength carries responsibility. That lesson matters because Gojo's philosophy as a teacher isn't simply about creating powerful fighters. It's about helping younger sorcerers build enough strength and independence to make their own choices about the world they're inheriting.
Peter fits naturally into that.

He already wants to protect people. He doesn't need to be convinced that responsibility matters. What he needed was a teacher who didn't treat his existing capabilities as a problem to be managed but as a foundation to be built from.

The technology question also gets addressed here. Tony Stark's engineering isn't something Peter rejects as a concept. Peter is an inventor, and his web shooters are already evidence of what he can produce under constraint. Gojo's influence teaches him something more specific: his equipment should support his abilities rather than substitute for weaknesses in his fundamentals.

Peter keeps developing his technology. At the same time, he becomes capable of fighting without depending on it. If his web shooters are damaged, his physical abilities and cursed energy control remain. If his technology fails, Spider-Sense and his combat training still function. He becomes more independent without losing the part of himself that makes him want to build things in the first place.

By the time Tony Stark finally finds him, the difference in Peter is obvious. Not louder or more aggressive — just more settled. More comfortable with the specific person he is rather than the one he thought he was supposed to become. Gojo's four-month trial has ended, but the training hasn't. Peter continues practicing with him whenever the dimensional connection allows it, building on the fundamentals while still living his life in Queens.
That matters, because the next person who tries to shape Spider-Man isn't a sorcerer. It's Tony Stark.

sections.name: PART 6
sections.label: The Airport
paras: By the time the Avengers begin dividing over the Sokovia Accords, Peter has already spent several months developing his abilities under Gojo. That is not enough time to turn him into a veteran sorcerer, but it is enough to make him noticeably more disciplined than the teenager Tony Stark expected to find. Tony can still discover Spider-Man and recognize his potential. What he finds is a kid who has already had a powerful mentor drilling judgment, control, and independence into him.

Tony offers Peter access to advanced technology and recruits him for the confrontation in Germany. Peter accepts the trip — partly because Tony is offering him a chance to help, and partly because refusing would mean staying home while a fight between Avengers is about to happen. But Gojo's training has made one thing clear: having power doesn't mean surrendering your judgment to someone else. Peter agrees to work with Tony, not to switch his brain off for him. Tony still gives him the upgraded Spider-Man suit and transports him to Germany, preserving the relationship that can later lead to the Iron Spider armor.
Once the airport fight begins, Peter's priority quickly becomes preventing serious injuries rather than blindly helping one side defeat the other.
His presence immediately changes the dynamic.

Peter begins on Tony's side, because that is the situation he agreed to enter, but he doesn't treat Steve's team like villains. His priority is stopping the fight before someone is seriously injured or killed. He uses his mobility to separate combatants and restrain people rather than trying to hurt them.

Bucky becomes one of his first targets because Tony's team is trying to prevent Steve and Bucky from leaving, and Peter has been told that Bucky is a dangerous enhanced fugitive. Peter does not yet know the full story about Zemo or the other Winter Soldiers. Peter's Spider-Sense lets him react to Bucky's attacks before they connect, while his cursed energy reinforcement gives him enough physical strength to control the Winter Soldier without destroying his arm. Sam presents a different problem — his aerial mobility means Peter has to use his webs to interfere with the wings and bring the fight back toward the ground where it's more contained.
Then Scott grows.

Ant-Man's Giant-Man form is the most immediate threat to the airport structure and everyone in it. Trying to overpower him directly would cause exactly the kind of damage Peter came to prevent. Peter does something Gojo would recognize immediately — he stops trying to solve the problem through force and starts using the environment. He attaches web lines to stable structures and uses his mobility to redirect Giant-Man's movements away from other combatants. His objective isn't to knock Scott unconscious. It's to make sure the airport doesn't become a disaster.

The Peter Parker who first started operating in Queens might have thrown himself directly at the biggest threat and hoped his strength was enough. This version analyzes the battlefield first. Peter eventually reaches Steve and Bucky. He understands — without agreeing with every decision Steve has made — that Steve is trying to protect someone he believes is being wrongly treated. That understanding keeps Peter from escalating the fight further. His involvement doesn't end with one side defeating the other. It shortens the battle and limits the damage.

Steve and Bucky still escape. The Sokovia Accords aren't resolved. Peter doesn't have the authority to fix any of that. But when it's over and Peter is walking away from the airport, there's one quiet moment that stays with him — the realization that every person on both sides of that fight was trying, in their own way, to do the right thing. That's not a comforting thought. It's a complicated one.
Tony watches Peter leave and realizes, for the first time, that someone else already taught this kid how to be dangerous. He doesn't know who. He intends to find out.

sections.name: PART 7
sections.label: The Vulture
paras: Peter's next major challenge is closer to home. Adrian Toomes has built a criminal operation around salvaged alien technology left from the Battle of New York. The Vulture suit gives him aerial mobility, heavy weaponry, and the ability to attack from angles that most opponents can't account for.

In the original timeline, Peter's lack of experience makes Toomes a serious threat. This version of Peter approaches the situation differently. His months of training have taught him to investigate before engaging. He studies Toomes' operation first — identifies the locations where equipment is being moved, observes the Vulture suit's capabilities, and looks for the specific limitations before the first confrontation.

Toomes can attack from altitude, change direction quickly, and fire weapons from a distance. But he can't make Peter's Spider-Sense disappear. Every time Toomes dives or fires, Peter receives the warning. The first confrontation is considerably shorter as a result.

Toomes attacks from above at high speed. Peter moves before it connects and attaches several webs to the suit. Rather than trying to overpower the entire machine, he uses the webbing to restrict the Vulture's movement and his cursed energy reinforcement to hold position while Toomes tries to break free. Peter redirects him away from populated areas using the surrounding structures and his own momentum. Toomes escapes, but Peter now understands what the suit can and can't do.

The second encounter happens at one of Toomes' facilities. Peter targets the suit's mobility rather than trying to destroy the whole machine — webs into the wings, cursed energy reinforcement to tear away sections of equipment when Toomes gets close enough.
Toomes eventually loses control of the suit and crashes.
Peter catches him.

That moment — catching the man who just spent two fights trying to kill him — demonstrates what Gojo's training actually changed. Peter is considerably stronger now. He also hasn't become careless with that strength. He turns Toomes over to the authorities, secures the Chitauri technology, and the damage from the whole encounter is a fraction of what it was in the original timeline.
The Vulture was still a human criminal using technology. What comes next is going to be something else entirely.

sections.name: PART 8
sections.label: Titan
paras: Thanos is a different category of problem.

By the time the Avengers learn that Thanos is actively pursuing the remaining Infinity Stones, Peter is far more experienced than the teenager Tony originally tried to recruit. He's spent years developing his physical abilities, cursed energy control, and combat instincts. He still isn't close to Gojo's level. But he has become an unusually capable hybrid fighter. The question the whole training arc has been building toward — how far can Spider-Man go — is about to get a real answer, against an opponent the answer turns out to matter against.

Peter's relationship with Tony continues after the airport, even if this version of Peter is more independent than the one Tony originally mentored. That relationship still gives Tony a reason to build the Iron Spider armor as an emergency upgrade. So when Peter follows Ebony Maw's ship out of Earth's atmosphere, Tony can deploy the suit to keep him alive during the ascent. Peter then joins Tony, Doctor Strange, Peter Quill, Drax, and Mantis on Titan. The objective is to stop Thanos and remove the Gauntlet before he can complete it.
Thanos possesses four Infinity Stones: Power, Space, Reality, and Soul. He is physically overwhelming even without them. The Stones give him access to abilities Peter has never encountered.
Peter's Spider-Sense reacts the moment Thanos attacks.

The warnings come early and continuously. That gives Peter opportunities a normal human wouldn't have — but it doesn't make him immune to Thanos's strength or the effects of the Stones. He knows the attacks are coming. He still has to move fast enough to matter.

Peter reinforces himself more aggressively than he has in any previous fight. His strength and durability increase. He moves around Thanos using the debris scattered across Titan, combining web lines with cursed energy-enhanced jumps to prevent himself from becoming a stationary target. For a period, he can contribute meaningfully — evading direct strikes, using webs to interfere with Thanos's movement, landing reinforced hits when the opportunity opens. The difference in power remains enormous. The Power Stone produces devastating attacks. The Space Stone lets Thanos manipulate distance and reposition himself. The Reality Stone creates an entirely different problem because it alters the environment around Peter — changing matter, reshaping the battlefield — in ways that make conventional movement and web-based strategies unreliable. Spider-Sense warns him that danger is coming. It doesn't explain how a Stone is changing the physics of the space he's moving through.
Peter eventually gets an opening.

He concentrates cursed energy into a physical strike with a precision he's been building toward for years, and for once the timing aligns almost impossibly well. His cursed energy lands within one millionth of a second of the physical impact. Space distorts around the hit and the force spikes far beyond an ordinary reinforced punch. Peter feels the difference immediately. It isn't an innate technique, and it isn't something he can simply activate on command. Everything Gojo taught him about timing and control has finally created the conditions for a Black Flash.

The impact catches Thanos off guard. A being whose durability has absorbed everything the Avengers and the Guardians have thrown at him takes a hit that registers. For a fraction of a second, Peter sees it — the slight shift in Thanos's attention, the recalibration of what the Titan is treating as a threat.

It doesn't end the fight. It doesn't place Peter anywhere near Thanos's level. But it proves something real: that Peter can hurt an opponent whose durability is completely beyond anything he's previously faced. Years of training produced something in that single moment that no amount of borrowed technology could have replicated.

Thanos adapts immediately, using the Stones to control distance and pull Peter onto the defensive. Spider-Sense keeps him alive. The Stones keep the fight from being winnable. Peter continues alongside the others — creating openings, keeping pressure distributed, giving the team another fast-moving presence — but the plan fails. Thanos obtains the Time Stone from Doctor Strange and leaves Titan.
Peter survives.

The experience changes what he understands about his own strength. Against most opponents, his combination of physical ability, Spider-Sense, and cursed energy gives him enormous advantages. Against Thanos, those advantages weren't enough. He's become powerful. He hasn't become invincible. That distinction sits with him differently than it might have before the Black Flash — because now he knows exactly what he can do, which makes knowing what he can't do more precise.

sections.name: PART 9
sections.label: Jujutsu High and Mahito
paras: Gojo eventually takes Peter to Japan and introduces him to Jujutsu High.

The higher-ups push back immediately. An outsider with no innate technique, trained privately by Gojo without formal institutional review, representing an unknown variable in a system built on classification and controlled information. Gojo gets Peter in by bargaining for it — the specifics of what he offers are typically unstated, because Gojo finds it entertaining to make the higher-ups nervous — but Peter arrives knowing his presence is contested.

For Peter, this is the first time he's experienced the jujutsu world as something other than an unexplained threat appearing in his city. He meets students who have grown up understanding cursed energy and have spent their lives learning to fight curses. The differences in their approaches to the work are immediate.

Yuji Itadori is an exceptionally capable physical fighter who became involved with jujutsu after becoming the vessel of Ryomen Sukuna. His instinct for combat and his natural relationship with cursed energy is something Peter finds genuinely impressive. Megumi Fushiguro's Ten Shadows Technique — the ability to summon shikigami from shadows — is the kind of innate technique Peter was told he doesn't have, and watching it work gives him a concrete sense of what that absence means in comparison. Nobara Kugisaki's Straw Doll Technique attacks targets through physical connections involving her nails and a straw doll, operating on principles that require the soul-based understanding Peter is still building.

Peter's approach is less specialized than any of theirs. He doesn't have an innate technique. He has physical abilities, Spider-Sense, web shooters, and cursed energy reinforcement working together. In collaborative missions, the versatility of that combination turns out to be genuinely useful — he can move through urban environments quickly, restrain curses with webbing, and use cursed energy to finish what his physical attacks start. His Spider-Sense adds a warning system that can identify threats outside his normal visual range.
Then he encounters Mahito.

Mahito is a Special Grade cursed spirit. His Idle Transfiguration allows him to reshape the soul through physical contact, and because changes to the soul produce corresponding changes to the body, his technique can kill or permanently alter a person in a single touch.

Peter's Spider-Sense reacts to Mahito more intensely than almost anything Peter has encountered since Thanos. The warning is continuous and urgent. But it doesn't explain what Idle Transfiguration does. Peter understands that physical contact is dangerous — he keeps his distance, uses webs to restrict Mahito's movement, attacks from positions that make direct contact difficult. His cursed energy reinforcement increases the damage his physical strikes can do.

Mahito's durability is deceptive. He isn't simply healing ordinary injuries. Idle Transfiguration lets him maintain and reshape the form of his own soul, and his body follows that shape. Peter's cursed-energy-reinforced strikes can still hit Mahito, knock him back, interrupt his movement, or physically displace him, but they do not accumulate meaningful lasting damage unless Peter can affect the soul itself. Overpowering Mahito through raw physical force therefore isn't a reliable way to win.

The fight becomes a battle of information. Peter's Spider-Sense gives him an advantage when Mahito approaches, but Mahito is intelligent enough to recognize patterns in Peter's movement. He starts using transfigured humans and altered body configurations to create positions where Peter has fewer safe routes. Peter has to keep moving — pulling himself across the environment with webs, changing direction constantly, using everything Gojo taught him about staying calm when a situation becomes unpredictable.
And then Peter runs directly into the limit.

He doesn't possess Yuji's unusual awareness of the soul that comes from sharing a body with Sukuna. Peter has learned that souls exist and understands the theory behind techniques that affect them, but knowledge is not the same as direct perception. His reinforced attacks can physically move and disrupt Mahito's body, but they cannot reliably damage the shape of Mahito's soul the way Yuji's attacks can.
Peter survives by refusing to let Mahito land what he needs.
Not a triumph. Not a retreat, exactly. A recognition — in the middle of a fight that Peter cannot win the way he expected to — that he has found the actual boundary of his abilities.

Peter eventually realizes that surviving the fight and winning it are two different problems. Spider-Sense gives him just enough warning to avoid Mahito's hands, so Peter uses his webs and three-dimensional movement to create distance and escape rather than gamble on a battle he has no reliable way to finish. Mahito tries to close the gap, but Peter is built for movement through a city and refuses to give him the contact he needs. Peter finally reaches a safe distance as Gojo closes in on the disturbance, forcing Mahito to abandon the pursuit rather than remain for a confrontation with him. Peter is breathing hard in an alleyway somewhere he doesn't immediately recognize, and the feeling he has isn't quite defeat. It's something more unsettling — the specific knowledge of what he cannot do. After years of building a fighting style that covers almost every situation, he has found one it doesn't cover.
Gojo uses it as another lesson. Some techniques require specific counters, specialized knowledge, or cooperation between sorcerers. Becoming stronger doesn't remove that requirement.

Peter goes back to studying. Not reluctantly. He goes back because Mahito has shown him exactly what he needs to understand next — and unlike the early months of cursed energy training, this time he already knows what it means to be genuinely not ready for something.[CLOSING — What Gojo Built]

After everything — the first four months in Queens, the continued training, the airport, the Vulture, Titan, Jujutsu High, Mahito — the answer to the original question is clearer than it was in that warehouse.
How far can Spider-Man go with the strongest sorcerer alive as his teacher?

Far enough to produce a Black Flash against Thanos. Far enough to enter the airport on Tony's side without surrendering his own judgment or escalating the damage. Far enough to move through the jujutsu world as something the higher-ups didn't predict and can't cleanly classify. Not far enough to beat Mahito by strength alone. Not close to Gojo's level, and never going to be — because Gojo's specific combination of Six Eyes and Limitless belongs to Gojo and isn't transferable.
But that was never really the point.

Gojo's greatest contribution isn't a new identity for Peter Parker. It's the training that let Peter become more fully the one he already had. Spider-Man, with the actual foundation to use what he can do. A fighter who combines physical ability, Spider-Sense, technology, web mobility, and cursed energy reinforcement into a style that neither universe originally had a name for.

The jujutsu higher-ups still don't know what to do with him. Tony Stark still wants to understand who trained him and what he used. Mahito still exists, and Peter still can't beat him the way he can beat everything else.
Which means the training isn't finished. It was never going to be.
That's the part Gojo understood from the beginning — and the part Peter is only now starting to realize he's actually comfortable with.

scripts.title: What If Spider Man Had Shadow Extraction

sections.name: INTRO
paras: What If Spider-Man Had Shadow Extraction?

So, this guy is Peter Parker. Before the memory wipe spell, the world knew he was Spider-Man. But, after that, no one remembers the man behind the mask. He is all alone in this new world and even his friends don’t have a single memory of him. All he can do is watch over them as he spends his days guarding New York and catching criminals. But, suddenly portals open all around the planet and monsters begin flooding through them. This is the exact moment when the events that were supposed to happen to Sung Jinwoo happen in Spidey’s universe. And, today we'll see what would happen if Spider-Man got the system and eventually unlocked one of Jinwoo’s strongest skills, Shadow Extraction. The same skill that made his shadow army possible. However, Peter is not Jinwoo, he is Spider-Man. The guy who believes that with great power comes great responsibility. So, giving him an ability that can literally turn his dead enemies or even allies into members of his army is something Peter would never even dream of doing. Because using such a power like that goes against everything he believes in.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: However, this new world forces him to do it and it all starts with a missing person’s case tied to an abandoned subway extension that was sealed off years ago. Usually, this would be the kind of thing that wouldn’t make the news. But this is exactly the kind of thing Peter can’t help but check out. He enters the abandoned subway and finds a mysterious portal that seems to be calling him in. He enters the gate even after his spider-sense tells him that something doesn’t add up. But little did Peter know that it wasn’t just New York. These portals called gates had popped up all over the world and connected Earth to dangerous dungeons filled with monsters. Right as he enters, he finds a green skinned humanoid walking towards him. At first, Spidey thinks that someone is cosplaying like Green Goblin and goofing around. But, the monster roars. It strikes him with the club which Spidey barely manages to dodge. Spidey realizes that what he is dealing with isn’t human, but a real goblin. Using his webbing, he traps the goblin on the ground and goes ahead to check out the place. However, more goblins start swarming him, so Peter punches one of them and kills it instantly. Peter freezes when he realizes what he did. He had no idea the goblin was that fragile compared to the enemies he normally fights, and even if these monsters are dangerous enough to kill humans, he doesn’t want killing them to become his first option. He deliberately holds back against the rest of the goblins unless lethal force becomes unavoidable, then moves forward only to find a new path opening up. He senses an ominous feeling coming from that path and every cell in his body warns him not to go any further. But, Peter ignores it since whatever is inside is eventually going to come outside and he might be the one who has to deal with it. Over there, he finds a huge door that opens into a room full of giant statues. He looks around the place and tries to read the giant board. As he is reading it, the door suddenly closes and Peter is trapped.

He realizes that something is wrong with the statues and notices one of them watching him. He immediately backs off, but the statues start moving toward him. He tries to stop them using his webs, but it’s of no use. So he tries to swing around to avoid getting caught by the statues only to get shot by laser beams from the center statue’s eyes. As Peter falls, one of the statues slices both of his hands. He is then stabbed and thrown into the middle of the room as the other statues smash his legs while Peter screams in pain. His vision starts fading and the last thing he sees is the giant statue standing above him. Then, everything goes black.

He gets a notification “You have acquired the qualifications to be a player. Will you accept?” Then, another one pops, saying that his heart will stop in 0.02 seconds if he chooses not to accept. He accepts it. Whatever the System does next restores enough of the damage to keep him alive, and when Peter opens his eyes again, he’s no longer inside the dungeon. He’s in a hospital. He can’t believe that he is still alive. The last thing he remembers is a bunch of statues surrounding him before one of them hit him with a sword. Right then, a man dressed in a black suit enters. He reveals that they found him unconscious outside the abandoned station. Peter asks how long he had been knocked out.

The man reveals that it’s been more than a month since they had hospitalized him. Peter is shocked. He asks whether they saw the monsters and statues over there. Hearing this, the man in the black suit tells him that they didn’t see anything like that. But, at the same time, he confirms that monsters have started invading the planet through portals that have mysteriously opened all over the world. Tokyo has them. Seoul has them. And, not surprisingly New York has them too. Also, Peter learns that superheroes aren't the only people with powers anymore. Because of the gates, some humans have developed supernatural abilities and these people are called hunters. They are ranked from E-Rank all the way to S-Rank. After hearing all of this, Peter thinks that he’s in a completely different world.

However, he warns Peter that he needs to be careful if a dungeon break happens. A dungeon break is what happens when a gate is left uncleared for 7 days which causes the monsters inside to flood out. He reveals that a dungeon break recently happened near Midtown School of Science and Technology which killed several people and left many injured. Hearing this, Peter’s heart skips a beat. He asks details about the deceased and the man shows him the initial casualty report, which lists MJ and Ned among the people found completely unresponsive after the attack. Peter is devastated. He can't believe his friends are dead. They were the only people he had left after Aunt May died. Now, with them gone, he is completely heartbroken. The man asks whether Peter knows them. To which Peter replies “No, Sir...” as he fights back tears. The man leaves and Peter relives all the good times they shared, completely forgetting that he has to finish his daily quest.

As he falls asleep, he gets yanked into the penalty zone and is chased by massive centipedes. Even worse, he’s simply told that he has to survive there for hours before he'll be let out. Peter has nothing to defend himself with. All he can do is run. He keeps running until the time runs out and he’s suddenly back in his hospital room. He catches his breath and can’t help but wonder what just happened to him. He realizes that he needs to get stronger so that others don’t have to lose their loved ones like he lost his friends. The next day he checks out the system and realizes that he has become something called a player. So, before getting into generational debt which he might have already had, he leaves hospital to test out his new abilities and see what else the system can do.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: After finishing his daily quests, Spidey enters a dungeon to see how different it is from the one he previously entered. He finds it similar except that it closes after the dungeon boss is defeated. He easily defeats all the monsters and levels up which is something a normal hunter can’t do. He starts clearing dungeons one after another and gets rare items which he sells in the system's shop. With every dungeon he clears, his strength, agility and other stats are increasing. Not only that, Peter notices that the system isn’t just making him more powerful with each level, but it’s also changing the very limits of what he is capable of.

However, he manages to find a way to take them down before entering a room with a throne. As he wonders what this is all about, he senses a presence that makes him feel like whatever he is about to face next is not going to be easy. A single knight walks in front of him. He is clad in blood-red armor and carries a sword with a presence completely different from all the monsters Peter has just fought. The system tells him that this is the Knight Commander, Igris the Bloodred. The Knight Commander simply points at Spidey, telling him to brace himself before smashing him into a wall. He then slices through the pillars of the room like they’re nothing as Peter struggles to stay on his feet.

Right then, Spidey’s web-bombs activate which traps lgris who is unable to free himself. Peter reveals that he silently planted the bombs and that he was waiting for the right moment to trap him. He then pulls out his sword and strikes the knight repeatedly before the system confirms that the target has been defeated. He gets a bunch of rewards after defeating him. But, right after that, strange portals open up and he gets surrounded by monsters. The sheer number of monsters wears Peter down as they keep coming one after another. However, Peter isn’t the type to give up this soon. He notices that someone in the crowd is responsible for summoning all these monsters and immediately takes them out.

With the casters down, he starts getting rid of the remaining monsters until the entire arena is empty. Peter has successfully survived the challenge. He gets a notification that he has obtained the Necromancer class. However, because his total advancement points from defeating all the enemies exceeded the required threshold his class evolves from Necromancer into the Shadow Monarch. He looks around at the dead monsters and the system notifies him that Shadow Extraction is now possible. The system asks him to come up with a command word to use it.

He thinks of something like “Rise and shine” or “Wakey, Wakey’”, but rejects them because they sound too childish and cringe. So, he takes “Rise” from the first one and changes it to “Arise”. As he says the command word, the fallen monsters rise once again. However, this time they aren’t fighting him. They will be fighting for him from now on. Then, Peter looks toward the Knight Commander, Igris. He looks at him and asks him to join his cause and help him save people before saying, “Arise.” The knight rises and just like that Peter has found his very first commander and an army that will help him deal with whatever is going on in the planet.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: As Peter swings across New York, he hears reports of something ugly happening in the dungeons lately. Hunters are dying. At first, it looks like just “another” dungeon accident. However, Peter notices a pattern and finds the whole thing very fishy. He finds out that the sudden increase in deaths isn’t because of monsters. But, because of other hunters. He figures out that a group of hunters who call themselves “The Arachnids’” are behind it. They deliberately abandon weaker members in the middle of dungeons and let them die on purpose or straight up kill them. Then, they take the dead hunter’s entire share of the rewards and move on to their next victim.

He finds the group and sneaks behind them as they enter a gate. But, the moment Peter enters, the color of the gate changes. The entrance turns blood red and closes instantly. It's a Red Gate. A special kinda dungeon that traps everyone inside and doesn’t allow them to leave once they've entered. The gate will only open when the boss is defeated, a dungeon break happens or the entire party is killed. The party also notices the gate changing color and is shocked to see what Spidey is doing with them. The people who were hired to be sacrificed surround Spidey and start questioning him. Seeing this, Peter realizes that these guys are too innocent. At the same time, he notices that the group leader and his crew aren’t exactly happy to see him. As they move forward, Spidey senses something flying toward them. But, one of the guys from the group leader’s gang brushes it off, saying he couldn’t hear anything only to get shot right in the head. They’re ice arrows. As Spidey looks around, he sees a bunch of creatures with long ears shooting at them. He tells everyone to stay alert and immediately fires his webs to stop them. The hunters close in and take out the archers as the whole unit is wiped out.

But, this is just the start as the dungeon boss confronts the whole group. The presence makes the low level hunters panic as they tell Spidey to stay close to them. While this is going on, the other hunters move forward only to get killed one by one by the dungeon boss and its army. Seeing this, Spidey has no choice but to reveal his true power. He summons his soldiers and Blood-Red Commander Igris. The hunters are terrified when they see them. Peter tells them to stay put and leaves a couple of soldiers behind to protect them. He rushes forward as the dungeon boss and Peter engage in a sword battle. With Igris supporting him, they team up and kill the dungeon boss as the gate finally opens.

He checks to see if any of the hunters from the leader’s gang are alive. But, all of them are dead, except the leader. So, he removes the leader’s gear only to realize that the group leader was none other than Scorpion. When their eyes meet, Scorpion immediately pushes Spidey away. Suddenly, he starts acting strangely as if he’s possessed. He immediately gets buffed up, grows a huge scorpion tail and poisonous fangs. The bloodlust makes Peter’s system recognize him as a threat and orders him to eliminate Scorpion. But, Peter doesn’t want to do it.

Meanwhile, Scorpion tells him flat out that he’s going to kill him. He tells Peter that he has been waiting for this moment as he swings his huge tail and sends Peter flying into the forest. But, Peter quickly gets back up and punches Scorpion hard. But, Scorpion barely budges and jabs him with his poisonous fangs. Peter collapses. But, thanks to the skill that he got after surviving the first dungeon, he doesn’t get affected by poison. However, he’s still no match for Scorpion alone. So, he calls on Igris to give him a hand. This makes things harder for Scorpion as he now has to face both Peter and the Blood-Red Commander.

Still, Peter and Igris struggle to completely control the battlefield. And, it’s because Peter hasn’t made a proper decision yet. He looks at the notification again. He can’t bring himself to kill Scorpion. Once he does that, he can never go back. However, he looks at the poor hunters who would be the next on the chopping block if he doesn’t kill Scorpion. And, this version of Scorpion might cause even more chaos if left outside. So, Peter orders the hunters and shouts “Get to the gate. Now!” But, they simply don’t wanna leave him behind. So Peter shouts again, “Don’t worry about me. Goooo!”

Now, it’s just Peter, Igris and Scorpion. Peter tells himself that he will no longer hold back. He pounces on Scorpion with full force and attacks him with everything he got. He smashes the armor on Scorpion’s face which makes Scorpion go mad. Before Spidey can dodge, Scorpion grabs him by the throat and tries to strangle him. But, Igris arrives just in time and cuts off his hand. Peter falls to the ground. As Scorpion gets distracted by Igris, Peter wraps him in multiple layers of webbing, immobilizing Scorpion. This gives Igris the perfect opportunity to cut off his tail and Peter breaks through his helmet and beheads him using his sword.

As Peter stands over Scorpion’s corpse, his hands start shaking. He can’t believe that he just killed a human. The system tells him that he can use Shadow Extraction. Peter hesitates. He doesn’t want to turn a dead man into his shadow. He was not a monster. Still, knowing that Scorpion wasn’t exactly a good guy, Peter decides to give hima chance to redeem himself as a shadow soldier. He looks at the corpse and says “Arise” as darkness spreads across Scorpion’s body.

A black version of Scorpion rises from the ground. He still has the same look, but now with an open face helmet. The system notifies him that he should give him a name. So, Peter keeps the old name and simply calls him “Scorpy.” The shadow looks happy and Peter orders his shadows to get back. While, Peter has just created his first shadow from a human being, “the one behind all” is watching Peter’s evolution and is excited to see everything running exactly as planned.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: With the Red Gate cleared, Peter reports everything to America’s Hunter Association, the Federal Bureau of Hunters. He tells them about what happened in the dungeon, how it suddenly turned into a Red Gate and that Scorpion, the one responsible for the hunter killings is dead. However, Peter doesn’t tell them the full story about Shadow Extraction or how Scorpion is now part of his army. He doesn’t know how the world would react if they discovered that he could turn dead enemies into soldiers. Peter realizes that he has to be careful not only with his enemies, but also with the world around him. He has become something nobody could have imagined. A superhero who can summon a massive army of shadow soldiers instantly. And a man who can turn the dead into literal weapons.

The head of the association is relieved to hear that low rank hunters no longer have to fear their fellow hunters. He thanks Peter for helping them out. But, suddenly a huge rock smashes into the building which takes out several staff members near him. The one behind the attack is Doctor Strange. Peter is confused. Strange isn’t supposed to be an enemy. No, he’s the man who helped him during the multiverse crisis and also during the fight against Thanos. But, something about Strange is different today. He’s attacking random buildings and opening portals everywhere as he watches people panic and run through the streets. So, Peter gets closer to him and tries to talk him down. “Hey, Stephen, it’s me.” But, Strange doesn’t stop and hits Peter with a spell that sends him flying through a building. Peter gets back up and keeps trying to restrain Strange instead of seriously hurting him, using his webs and shadows to divide his attention. But, when Strange tears through the restraints and prepares another spell toward the people below, Peter realizes he can’t keep holding back. He closes the distance and lands a desperate lethal strike before Strange can fire it. The spell collapses, and whatever was controlling Stephen finally lets go as his body starts falling.

Before Stephen falls to the ground, Peter catches him. He apologizes to Strange for killing him. Strange who is back to normal is glad that he is no longer under someone’s control. Peter asks who did this to him. But, before Strange can answer, he starts glitching and is unable to answer before breathing his last. Peter gets a notification that Shadow Extraction is possible. He stares at the notification for a long time and almost refuses it. He doesn’t want to turn someone he respected into a soldier, especially after being the one forced to kill him. But Strange spent his life using that power to protect people, and Peter can’t bring himself to let all of it disappear when it could still save lives. He hates the choice, but convinces himself that preserving Strange’s power is better than losing it completely.

Peter closes his eyes and says “Arise” and Strange’s shadow appears right in front of him. He feels bad for turning someone he respected into a soldier. Peter immediately pulls his shadows back as he doesn’t want anyone to see what he can do. However, members of the Federal Bureau of Hunters watch him resurrecting Strange and start questioning what kinda power he has. Spidey doesn’t reveal much and only lets them know he can bring the dead back to life. Everyone in the room is stunned. However, knowing that they recently found a 15 year old boy with the upgrading ability, they realize they’re still figuring out what else the gates have introduced to the world.

The leader of the association tells him that this ability is extremely dangerous for the public to know about, so they assure him that this information won't get out. He also reveals that the gates have brought a new type of disease and their scientists are trying to figure out a cure. The leader then shows Peter pictures of a few people who have been affected by the new disease. However, what Peter sees shocks him. In one of those pictures are none other than MJ and Ned. He can’t believe they’re still alive. Apparently, the initial casualty report was wrong. MJ and Ned had been found completely unresponsive and were listed among the dead, but doctors later detected that they were still alive and transferred them for treatment. The dungeon break had exposed them to enormous amounts of mana which caused the Eternal Sleep Disease. Knowing that his friends are still alive, Peter starts looking for a way to cure them.

First, he defeats the massive dog guarding the entrance and then starts defeating monsters floor after floor. The higher he goes, the stronger the enemies become. Even when there are times he wants to give up, he keeps going because he isn’t fighting just for himself. He is fighting for his friends, Ned and MJ and he knows this might be the only way he gets to save them. After a long and brutal fight, he finally reaches the last floor and finds the demon king waiting for him with a massive wyvern. The system identifies him as Baran, the Monarch of White Flames. The Demon Monarch is incredibly powerful with lightning filling the entire battlefield. Spidey summons all of his shadows and launches an attack on the Demon King and his army.

Peter orders lgris, Scorpy and Strange to take care of the army, while he focuses on Baran. The battle is intense, but Spidey eventually manages to defeat the Demon Monarch. He tries to use Shadow Extraction on Baran, but the system rejects the attempt and the Demon Monarch never rises. Peter still receives the rewards and collects all the materials needed for the cure, then he leaves the place and heads straight to the facility. He sneaks in and gives both Ned and MJ the Elixir of Life. At first, nothing happens. But soon, they both wake up as Peter leaves before they can see him. Though, they still don’t remember him, he’s glad they’re alive. For the first time since May died, Peter finally feels a sense of relief that he hasn't felt in a very long time.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: When Peter is experimenting with his new skill, Shadow Exchange, he gets a call from the Hunter Association asking him to assist with the Jeju Island raid. They explain that the Japanese and Korean Hunters Associations are doing a joint raid to deal with the massive ant threat. He meets the leaders of both associations and a couple of S-rank hunters who reveal that anyone below S-Rank won't be taking part in the mission, since it could be too dangerous for them. So, when they ask Spidey to join and boost their firepower, he rejects the offer. He says that New York is his primary responsibility and that he can’t leave the city unprotected.

Hearing this, they understand Spidey’s situation and leave the meeting. However, Spidey isn’t that cold hearted enough to just sit back and watch people get hurt. He knows the mission is dangerous, but at the same time he has to protect New York. So, he secretly sends some of his shadow soldiers along with the S-rank hunters and hopes nothing goes wrong. The raid officially begins as Peter watches the live broadcast of what’s happening. At first, everything goes exactly as planned. The S-Rank hunters enter the island and move through the ant colony.

They work together perfectly as a team and reach the Ant Queen’s chamber in no time. The S-Rank hunters manage to defeat the Ant Queen and it looks like the mission is a success. However, suddenly a humanoid ant walks towards them as all the hunters can do is watch. It’s the Ant King. Seeing the Queen dead, the ant lets out a roar before devouring her body. He then smashes one of the hunters like a baseball who crashes in the ceiling before falling down. The other hunters attack him, but they are also defeated who can’t believe such a powerful monster exists. He’s fast, he can speak and he can heal himself. Watching from New York, Peter realizes the hunters are about to be wiped out. One of the shadow soldiers he secretly sent with them is already on Jeju, so Peter uses Shadow Exchange and instantly switches places with it. Just before the Ant King devours one of the hunters, Peter steps in.

He knocks the Ant King back and gives the injured hunters healing potions to help them recover. The Ant King is perplexed. He can sense an aura of immense strength coming from Peter, so he asks whether Peter is the king of the humans. Peter replies “No, Sir Ant. I’m more like a superhero.” The Ant King isn’t impressed and strikes him with his claws. Peter barely dodges as the first strike literally destroys the ground. Peter starts swinging around looking for a way to counter the Ant King. He tries to web him, but his claws are sharp enough to easily rip through the webs. Right then, Igris emerges from Peter’s shadow and blocks the attack. The Ant King doesn’t hold back and starts throwing hands with the knight. Seeing that Peter is trying to catch him off guard, the Ant King calls all the ants to attack Peter and the remaining hunters.

So, Peter summons his shadow army and tells Igris to join them and help the hunters while he takes on the Ant King. Peter manages to strike the Ant King in the chest, making him bleed. However, this only makes Peter’s situation worse as the mad ant king starts moving faster than Peter’s eyes can keep up with. He realizes that the only way to defeat the Ant King is to slow him. So, Peter starts planting a new type of spider-bomb and uses Ruler’s Hand to drag the Ant King into the range, trapping him. He then attacks the Ant King with his Demon Monarch’s Daggers until the creature is shredded into pieces.

But, the Ant King heals himself and Peter continues following him like a hunter chasing its prey. Knowing that Peter is coming at him with killing intent, the Ant King tries to change the tactics. Bult, it’s already too late as Peter delivers the final blow. The system confirms that the Ant King is defeated. This is the strongest monster he has ever defeated. A creature that nearly wiped out all the S-Rank hunters. Right then, the system tells him that he can extract the Ant King’s shadow. However, the extraction fails. This is the first time something like this has happened to him.

He tries again, but it fails. He gets a notification telling him that he only has one attempt left and won’t be able to resurrect again. With all his hope riding on the final attempt, Peter gives it one last shot. The Ant King’s body starts moving and the shadow rises up. He kneels before Peter and looks up, asking him to give him a name. Peter names him Beru. He then helps evacuate the injured hunters and stays behind to finish the job. As Peter starts taking out the rest of the ants, he looks at Igris, Scorpy, Strange and Beru proudly realizing just how far he has come.

And, that’s where we're going to end this part. With Beru in his army, Peter is stronger than ever. However, Peter still doesn’t know who is behind all the gates or who created the system. He also doesn’t know what his true purpose is as the Shadow Monarch and has no idea that his biggest fight hasn’t even started yet.

scripts.title: What If Spider Man Was In Jujutsu Kaisen

sections.name: INTRO
paras: MCU Spider-Man lands in the Jujutsu Kaisen world immediately after No Way Home, and his Spider-Sense starts warning him before he even understands what's attacking him. Peter can dodge the danger, but all he sees at first are objects moving on their own and people getting hurt by creatures his eyes can’t properly make out.

That gets the attention of Jujutsu High pretty quickly. Gojo and Megumi are looking at a teenager with no cursed technique who can still react to curses before they strike, while Peter is trying to understand why monsters apparently exist everywhere and almost nobody around him can see them.

Peter already knows how to fight stronger enemies and figure things out under pressure, but this world runs on rules he’s never seen before. Once he gets pulled into Yuji’s life, Spider-Man has to learn those rules fast enough to keep helping people without letting the jujutsu world change the kind of hero he is.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: A few weeks after No Way Home, Peter is swinging through New York in the suit he made for himself when the sky ahead of him splits open for less than a second. It looks close enough to the cracks he saw around the Statue of Liberty that he turns toward it on instinct, but the opening expands before he can get away and pulls him straight through.

Peter falls out above Tokyo and barely catches the side of a building before hitting the street. By the time he climbs onto the roof, the opening is already gone, his phone has no service, and every landmark around him tells him he isn’t anywhere near New York. He spends the next hour moving through the city trying to work out where he is and whether the same kind of portal could still be nearby.

Spider-Sense hits before he finds any answers. Peter ducks and a metal sign behind him bends hard enough to rip free from the wall, even though he never saw anyone touch it. Another warning makes him jump sideways as cracks run across the pavement where he had been standing.

Peter starts treating it like an invisible attacker. He fires webs through the space around him until one strand catches on a body he still can’t see, then gets ripped apart as the creature lunges again. Spider-Sense keeps giving him enough warning to stay ahead of the attacks, but Peter has no idea how large the thing is or where its limbs begin.

He spreads webbing between walls, streetlights, and parked cars so anything moving through the area has to disturb it. A section of the web suddenly caves inward, and Peter slams both feet into the exact spot before swinging away. The hit connects with something solid and knocks it back, but Peter quickly realizes physical contact is not the same as actually damaging or exorcising a curse. There’s still nothing visible in front of him.

Megumi arrives while Peter is setting another web trap.
