He sees a curse chasing a masked stranger who’s reacting to attacks he clearly can’t see, and Peter sees a teenager summon a white dog and a black dog from his shadow. The dogs tear into the creature, and Peter finally catches a distorted glimpse of its shape as cursed energy spills from the body.

Peter removes his mask once Megumi starts questioning him, mostly because the conversation is already too strange for another secret identity problem. Megumi asks which jujutsu school he belongs to, Peter asks what jujutsu is, and both of them realize very quickly that the other person is working with a completely different understanding of what just happened.

Megumi explains curses while Peter explains Spider-Sense. Peter can feel an attack coming before it reaches him, but he can’t see the creature clearly enough to know what it is doing. Megumi has spent his whole life seeing curses and finds it hard to believe someone with almost no usable cursed energy just survived several minutes against one completely blind.

Peter goes with him once he hears how common curses are. He has no way home yet, no money that works here, and nowhere else to get answers about the invisible things trying to kill people around him. Jujutsu High at least has people who can explain what he just fought and maybe someone who understands the kind of dimensional accident that dropped him into Tokyo.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Gojo spends the first meeting switching between taking Peter seriously and finding the entire situation hilarious. Peter tells him about the portal, New York, Doctor Strange, and a spell that almost tore open the multiverse, while Gojo listens long enough to decide that Peter probably isn’t lying. He still asks Peter to crawl across the ceiling afterward because Megumi mentioned the wall-sticking and Gojo wants to see it himself.

Peter’s lack of cursed energy becomes more interesting once Gojo tests Spider-Sense. He flicks an eraser toward the back of Peter’s head while talking, and Peter catches it without turning around. Gojo tries from different angles, adds fake movements between throws, and eventually gets told to stop treating Peter like a carnival game.

Gojo gives him a pair of lenses prepared to see curses. The first time Peter wears them, he realizes how many creatures have been sitting around places he already walked through without ever knowing they were there. Some are tiny enough to ignore, while others cling to buildings or follow people closely enough that Peter immediately starts asking why nobody is clearing them out.

Megumi explains that sorcerers already spend their lives doing exactly that and there aren't enough of them. Peter understands the manpower problem, though accepting it is harder when he can now see what ordinary people are walking past every day. He asks Gojo to teach him enough to keep himself alive before worrying about anything more complicated.

Peter accepts that faster than Gojo expects. He has fought aliens, drones, enhanced humans, and people with magic before, so learning another set of rules doesn’t scare him as much as fighting without knowing the rules at all. He starts writing down everything Megumi and Gojo tell him, then compares it with what Spider-Sense actually does during training.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Megumi brings Peter along when he’s sent to Sugisawa High to recover one of Sukuna’s fingers. Peter has already heard enough about cursed objects to know that leaving a preserved finger inside a school is somehow normal by jujutsu standards, and Megumi gets tired of hearing him complain about it before they reach the building. The box is empty when they arrive, and cursed energy is already spreading through the school.

Yuji’s friends have taken the finger upstairs and removed the seal. Peter’s lenses show curses gathering around the building from several directions, while Spider-Sense keeps firing every few seconds as more of them get closer. He and Megumi split up once they hear people inside. Peter reaches the occult club first and pulls one student out through a window while Megumi attacks the curse holding the other. Yuji comes crashing into the fight a moment later despite having no idea what he’s looking at, and Peter has to stop himself from asking why another completely normal teenager is running directly toward a monster.

Yuji’s physical ability makes the answer even stranger. He jumps distances Peter doesn’t expect from someone without cursed energy and keeps moving after hits that would drop most people instantly. Peter covers him with webs while Megumi works on actually exorcising the curse, and the 3 of them manage to keep everyone alive until a stronger curse reaches the finger.

Yuji eats it before Peter understands what he’s about to do. The change in his body is immediate, and Spider-Sense spikes so violently that Peter lands on the opposite side of the room before Sukuna has even finished looking around. Peter can tell the person in front of him is carrying a completely different level of danger from anything he has seen so far

Sukuna notices Peter reacting and turns toward him. Peter doesn’t know who Sukuna is yet, but he sees the markings, hears the change in Yuji’s voice, and keeps enough distance that he can move if the next warning comes. Megumi gives him the shortest explanation possible while trying to decide whether he needs to fight Yuji’s body.

Yuji takes control again before that happens. He looks down at his hands, realizes everyone is staring at him, and asks whether his friends are safe before asking what he just swallowed. Peter watches Megumi explain the execution problem and immediately understands that this kid's life has become part of something much bigger than anything Yuji agreed to.

Gojo arrives soon after and treats Sukuna’s vessel with enough confidence that Peter finally understands why Megumi kept talking about him like he could solve anything. Peter stays close anyway, because Yuji has spent the last hour making the same kind of stupid decisions Peter recognizes from himself. By the time they leave the school, Peter already knows he’s going to have a hard time watching the jujutsu higher ups treat Yuji like a container instead of a person.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Yuji joins Jujutsu High, and Peter ends up training beside him because both of them are entering the same world from the outside. Yuji has cursed energy now because of Sukuna, while Peter still has none he can meaningfully use, so their lessons start in completely different places even when Gojo puts them through the same exercises.

Their physical sparring gets competitive almost immediately. Yuji can take more punishment than Peter expects and has enough raw strength to make Peter respect every clean hit, while Spider-Sense makes actually landing those hits frustrating. Peter starts correcting the way Yuji loads up his punches, and Yuji keeps trying increasingly ridiculous feints to make Spider-Sense give Peter the wrong read.

Nobara joins soon after and decides Peter’s entire situation sounds fake until she sees him stick to a wall. Peter decides not to explain the Avengers, Thanos, or the multiverse until someone specifically asks, because every additional detail makes Megumi look more tired. The 4 of them settle into missions quickly once Peter proves he can contribute without having a cursed technique.

Peter spends his free time changing his web shooters for this world. He builds cartridges that spread thin web lines through hallways and rooms, letting him track movement whenever an unseen curse disturbs them. The prepared lenses stay his main way of seeing curses, but the web network gives him another option if the glasses break during a fight.

Gojo later gives him small amounts of cursed material that can be worked into specialized equipment. Peter manages to coat certain web cartridges with enough cursed residue to make them more useful against weaker spirits, although the supply is limited and the webs still don’t turn into a substitute for a proper sorcerer. He keeps most of those cartridges for emergencies and uses regular webbing for movement and rescue work.

The execution hanging over Yuji makes those conversations harder. Yuji talks about eating all of Sukuna’s fingers like his eventual death is already part of the plan, and Peter keeps pushing back whenever he hears it. Peter has already watched people decide their own lives are worth less than everyone else’s, and he refuses to encourage Yuji to spend the next few years treating himself like ammo.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: The juvenile detention center is the first mission where Peter realizes how little his normal experience means against the upper end of jujutsu. The moment he enters the building, Spider-Sense turns into constant pressure instead of a clean warning. Every hallway feels dangerous because the space itself has been distorted by the curse inside.

Peter keeps the lenses on and stays close to Yuji while Megumi leaves to find Nobara after she is separated from the group. The Finger Bearer appears before they have a chance to regroup, and Peter's first web shot gets torn apart almost instantly. Yuji attacks anyway, forcing Peter to follow before the curse can crush him.

Peter can dodge individual strikes, but he can’t find a safe rhythm because cursed energy is exploding through the entire area. He pulls Yuji out of one attack with a web line, gets clipped by another, and realizes they aren't doing meaningful damage in return. His strength lets him survive the exchange longer than an ordinary person could, yet the curse barely reacts when he lands a clean hit.

Yuji decides to give Sukuna control once they run out of room. Peter tries to stop him, but Sukuna is already standing there by the time Peter reaches him. The Finger Bearer dies almost immediately, and Peter gets another reminder of how far above them Sukuna is when something that nearly killed both of them disappears in seconds.

Spider-Sense never settles while Sukuna has control. Peter keeps moving because every change in Sukuna’s posture feels dangerous, and Sukuna starts noticing how early he reacts. A slash cuts through the wall beside Peter after he dodges, giving him his first look at an attack he sensed without ever seeing it travel.

Sukuna tests him again from another angle. Peter moves before the cut reaches him, but the warning still doesn’t tell him what Sukuna did or how wide the next slash will be. He understands enough to know that repeatedly dodging an invisible technique isn’t a plan he can trust forever.

Sukuna turns toward Megumi once Peter stops being entertaining. Peter follows and stays between them whenever Spider-Sense warns him Megumi is about to be hit, but he can’t attack Yuji’s body freely when Yuji could regain control at any second. Sukuna eventually tears out Yuji's heart, making that restraint far worse because Peter now knows exactly what happens if Yuji comes back.

Yuji takes control anyway. Peter catches him as his body gives out and immediately starts looking for anything he can do, while Megumi tells him there’s no normal way to survive without a heart. Peter keeps trying until Yuji stops responding because accepting that answer after a few seconds isn’t something he knows how to do.

Peter leaves the detention center thinking Yuji died to keep Sukuna from hurting them. He has only been in the jujutsu world for a short time, and he has already watched adults send teenagers into a building where nobody knew a special grade was waiting. By the time Gojo hears what happened, Peter has plenty of questions about the people deciding which young sorcerers are considered acceptable losses.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Yuji comes back before Peter has enough time to accept that he died. Gojo keeps the resurrection secret from Megumi and Nobara while Yuji trains and takes missions with Nanami, a grade 1 sorcerer Gojo trusts, but he lets Peter in on it after a few days, so Peter spends those weeks working harder with Megumi and Nobara and taking every mission more seriously than before. He also starts asking Gojo much more direct questions about who approves missions, how grades are assigned, and how often students get sent into situations where the information turns out to be wrong.

When Gojo finally takes Peter to see Yuji in secret, Peter stares at him for several seconds before saying anything. Yuji expects a joke or a hug and gets both eventually, but Peter is angry first because Yuji had already decided his own life was expendable before he died. The argument never turns ugly, although Peter makes him promise that the next time death starts looking like the easiest solution, he tells somebody before making that choice alone.

Mahito becomes the first curse Peter genuinely struggles to understand even after he can see him. His body moves normally enough for Spider-Sense to track attacks, but the danger around his hands feels different because a single touch can affect the soul instead of simply hurting flesh. Peter learns that lesson without being hit when he watches what Mahito does to transformed humans and realizes none of his normal medical knowledge can explain what happened to them.

Junpei’s situation pulls Peter in earlier because Yuji talks about him almost immediately. Peter recognizes a lonely kid being pushed toward someone dangerous and tries meeting him before Mahito has enough time to finish manipulating him. Junpei is suspicious of another stranger asking personal questions, but Peter gets farther than most adults would because he doesn't lecture him about being angry at the people who hurt him.

The difference comes when Mahito finally reaches Junpei directly. Peter's Spider-Sense goes off before Mahito’s hand touches him, and Peter yanks Junpei backward with a web line hard enough to throw both of them across the room. Mahito misses the contact that originally killed him, and Yuji reaches the fight while Junpei is still alive.

Peter stays almost entirely defensive because getting close to Mahito is too dangerous. Spider-Sense gives him enough warning to avoid several touches, but he has no way to damage Mahito’s soul and quickly realizes punching him accomplishes very little. Nanami and Yuji carry that fight, and Yuji is the one who can really hurt Mahito because living with Sukuna inside him lets him sense the shape of a soul and hit it directly.

Mahito escapes once the fight turns against him, leaving Junpei alive and completely shaken by what almost happened. Yuji still wants to kill Mahito after seeing the transfigured humans and everything he did to Junpei, while Peter understands the anger without pretending he has a clean answer for it. He starts treating Mahito as the first enemy in this world where his usual rule of restrain first and figure it out later could get somebody killed before the webbing even lands.

Junpei doesn't immediately become another frontline sorcerer after surviving. What happened with Mahito leaves him shaken, and Peter is one of the people who argues against treating survival as a reason to throw him into more danger. Junpei still begins learning how to understand his cursed technique and spends more time around Yuji and Jujutsu High, but for now his biggest change is much simpler: Yuji gets to keep the friend he was supposed to lose.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Shibuya begins with Peter knowing only that curses and curse users are behind the attacks, and very little about what they actually want. The barriers trap civilians and separate sorcerers across the district, while Peter gets pulled into rescue work almost immediately because web-swinging lets him move through areas where trains, roads, and crowds have completely locked up. Spider-Sense is constantly active from the number of curses nearby, so Peter has to stop treating every warning like a personal attack and focus on what is directly in front of him. Gojo still enters the station alone because the civilians packed around him make most backup more dangerous than useful. Peter wants to follow, but Gojo tells him to stay above ground and keep evacuation routes open until they understand the barriers. Peter hates the order and follows it because thousands of people are already trapped where he can actually help.

The first major change comes once the higher-ups realize multiple teams are being pushed toward specific locations instead of randomly attacked. Peter starts mapping the barrier edges, cursed sightings, and civilian movement on his phone, then notices that the curse users are leaving certain corridors open long enough to funnel sorcerers through them. Megumi uses that information to avoid one ambush, and the teams begin sharing movement instead of operating almost blind.

Peter reaches the station after Gojo is sealed, and the news hits him harder than he expects. Everyone around him has spent years acting like Gojo is the one person who can always fix the situation, and suddenly every decision falls onto people who were depending on him. Peter has already lived through losing the person everyone expected to save the day, so he focuses on keeping the group moving before panic turns into another problem.

Yuji eventually runs into Choso while Peter is helping civilians through another section of the station. By the time Peter reaches him, Yuji is badly injured and Choso has already decided something about their relationship that Peter has no context for. Peter gets Yuji out while Choso hesitates, using webs through the narrow corridors instead of trying to fight someone whose blood attacks are filling the space.

Peter leaves the unconscious Yuji hidden so he can go back for trapped civilians, and while he is gone Jogo finds Yuji and forces more fingers into him, so Sukuna still takes control. Peter knows the change happened before he sees him because Spider-Sense suddenly becomes unbearable across several blocks. He swings toward the warning and arrives too late to stop Sukuna from beginning the fight with Jogo, which quickly turns into destruction Peter cannot meaningfully interfere with and ends with Sukuna killing Jogo.

He spends that fight saving whoever he can reach. The speed and scale of Sukuna’s attacks make approaching the center suicidal, while Spider-Sense keeps warning Peter about danger coming from entire sections of the city instead of one direction. He pulls people through windows, webs debris before it crushes trapped civilians, and stays far enough from the fight that one slash cannot remove him before he understands where it came from.

It gets even worse when a badly injured Megumi summons Mahoraga as a last resort. Peter is already working near the outer edge of the area Sukuna will eventually devastate when Spider-Sense suddenly becomes overwhelming. He moves outward immediately, and that head start is the only reason he gets beyond the worst of Malevolent Shrine once Sukuna opens it to destroy Mahoraga. People deeper inside the Domain’s range have no chance to follow him.

Yuji returns to his body afterward and sees what Sukuna did. Peter finds him before he can disappear into the ruins alone, and this time he does not try telling Yuji that none of it matters because Sukuna was in control. He tells him the people who are still alive need him moving, then stays beside him until Yuji can stand without staring at the destruction around them.

Junpei becomes part of what keeps Yuji moving afterward. He isn't in the center of Shibuya's fighting, but when the survivors reconnect, Yuji sees someone Mahito was supposed to take from him still alive. Junpei can't erase what Sukuna did or the people Yuji just watched die, and he doesn't try. He only reminds Yuji that disappearing into the ruins would leave the people who survived without him too. Coming from someone Yuji once tried to save, that lands differently than another order from a sorcerer.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The aftermath of Shibuya leaves Peter with fewer illusions about how much one person can fix. Gojo is gone, Nanami is dead, Nobara is critically injured, and Yuji has become the target of another execution order while Sukuna remains inside him. Peter starts helping Megumi hide Yuji because turning him over to the higher-ups feels impossible after watching what their decisions already cost.

Junpei stays close during that period without suddenly becoming strong enough to belong in the battles ahead. He helps where he can, keeps training at a safer pace, and gives Yuji one relationship that isn't built around Sukuna, execution orders, or the next catastrophe. Peter notices the difference because saving Junpei didn't stop Shibuya or fix the jujutsu world. It just meant one person who should have been gone is still there, and sometimes that is enough to change what happens to everyone around him.

Yuta returns as Yuji’s appointed executioner, and Peter initially assumes they are going to have to fight him. Spider-Sense reacts to Yuta and Rika strongly enough that Peter knows attacking first would be a terrible idea, so he watches instead and notices Yuta keeps creating openings where Yuji could survive. Once Yuta reveals Gojo asked him to protect Yuji, Peter understands why the fight felt wrong from the beginning.

The curse user in Geto’s body turns out to be Kenjaku, an ancient sorcerer, and the Culling Game he set up at the end of Shibuya begins soon after, and Peter becomes useful for reasons that have very little to do with cursed techniques. The colonies separate players through barriers and unfamiliar rules, while Peter is good at moving through ruined urban spaces, locating civilians, and building quick maps from whatever information the group can gather. He also starts modifying his lenses so they can record cursed signatures as visual changes, giving non-sorcerer equipment a rough way to track where strong cursed activity happened.

He enters one colony with Yuji because separating them after Shibuya is asking for both of them to make worse decisions alone. Peter handles players whose techniques rely on straightforward physical attacks much better than expected, using Spider-Sense and mobility to stay outside their preferred range. The stranger techniques are where he struggles, especially once conditions, barriers, and rules become part of the attack instead of fists or projectiles.

Higuruma becomes one of the clearest examples. Peter cannot dodge a courtroom Domain by moving faster because the technique changes the rules around everyone inside it. Spider-Sense warns him as the Domain forms, but once Judgment begins he has to listen, understand what the technique is doing, and stop treating movement as the answer to every threat.

Yuji’s trial still forces him to confront Shibuya and the people Sukuna killed through his body. Peter watches him accept blame too quickly and realizes how far Yuji’s guilt has gone since the detention center. After Higuruma backs away from killing him, Peter tells Yuji that taking responsibility for what he can control is different from claiming every death connected to Sukuna as his own choice.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Sukuna taking Megumi’s body hits Peter differently from every other disaster because he watches it happen to someone who has been beside him since his first night in this world. Yuji survives the transfer and immediately tries to chase Sukuna, while Peter goes after him because nobody has time to process what just happened. They reach Megumi’s body and find Sukuna already testing Ten Shadows like he has been waiting years for the chance.

They fail to get Megumi back. Sukuna escapes after securing enough control over the body, and Peter has to drag Yuji away before chasing turns into suicide. Yuji takes that failure personally because Megumi spent so much time trying to save him, while Peter is carrying the same thought from a different direction after Megumi was the first person in this world to help him. Gojo eventually returns, which gives everyone time to plan for Sukuna without pretending they can simply overwhelm him. Peter studies every record available on Sukuna’s slashes, Malevolent Shrine, Ten Shadows, and Mahoraga because his best contribution is understanding where somebody without cursed techniques can still affect the fight. Most of what he finds tells him the same thing: getting close during the main battle would probably get him killed without helping Gojo.

Peter accepts staying out of the opening fight. He watches Gojo and Sukuna through the monitoring setup with everyone else and pays close attention to Mahoraga because adaptation is one of the few mechanics he understands conceptually from his own world. Once Mahoraga starts changing around Infinity, Peter realizes Sukuna is using the shikigami to learn instead of simply letting it fight for him.

He starts going through the footage frame by frame. The slashes that eventually get through Infinity show changes in where Sukuna is aiming and what Mahoraga is responding to, although Peter cannot translate cursed technique theory well enough to know the exact answer. He tells Yuta and Kusakabe that Sukuna appears to be waiting for Mahoraga to demonstrate an interaction he can reproduce himself.

That warning does not automatically save Gojo. The people watching still do not know exactly when Sukuna will find the answer or what the final slash will target, and Gojo is fighting too fast for Peter to feed him instructions every few seconds. What changes is that Yuta, Yuji, and the others are already prepared for Sukuna to unveil something new if Gojo loses.

When the attack finally cuts through Gojo’s defenses, Peter sees it through the monitoring setup. He cannot reach Gojo before the slash lands, and he cannot tell exactly how Sukuna bypassed Infinity. What he does understand is that Sukuna found the answer he had been waiting for Mahoraga to demonstrate, and Peter immediately passes that warning to the people preparing to go in next.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Gojo still falls, which removes the person Peter spent the entire story thinking could survive almost anything. Peter does not get time to process it because Kashimo, the Culling Game player who volunteered to fight Sukuna next, enters immediately and is killed soon after, everyone else keeps moving through the order they prepared, and Yuta kills Kenjaku before joining the fight against Sukuna. Peter waits until Sukuna is occupied before joining Yuji, because getting onto the field too early would only give Sukuna another target he can remove with one slash.

His role is built around movement and information. Spider-Sense gives Peter early warnings when Sukuna aims at him or Yuji, while webs let him change Yuji’s position without forcing Yuji to stop attacking. The warning that Sukuna developed a new kind of slash also means Peter watches Sukuna’s activation tells as closely as Spider-Sense itself. Once the fighters understand that the attack requires visible preparation after Gojo, Peter reacts to Sukuna’s hand sign, incantation, and directional gesture whenever he can instead of waiting to see where the slash travels.

Malevolent Shrine remains the worst possible matchup. Peter can feel the Domain coming, but once its effective area covers everything around him, speed cannot guarantee safety against repeated slashes appearing across the entire range. He uses the warning to leave before the Domain fully stabilizes whenever possible and depends on the sorcerers with actual anti-Domain options when escape is no longer available.

Yuji becomes the key to saving Megumi because his attacks can reach the boundary between Sukuna and the body he stole. Peter focuses on keeping Yuji close enough to keep landing those hits, using webs to pull him back after Sukuna throws him away and intercepting physical attacks that would break Yuji’s rhythm. He never becomes the person who can damage Sukuna most, but he keeps creating seconds where the people who can hurt him get another chance. Peter eventually takes a slash he cannot fully avoid while moving Yuji out of its path. Spider-Sense gives him enough warning to turn what would have cut straight through his torso into a deep hit across his side, and he stays conscious long enough to web himself away from the next attack. Yuji tries to check on him, but Peter sends him straight back toward Sukuna because Megumi is still inside.

Megumi finally begins resisting once Yuji reaches him enough times. Sukuna loses control in small pieces, and those mistakes give the group openings that did not exist earlier in the fight. Peter returns after sealing the wound as well as he can and uses every web cartridge he has left to interfere with Sukuna’s movement for a few seconds while Yuji closes the distance again.

The final separation still depends on the sorcerers’ original finishing chain. Nobara’s Resonance through Sukuna’s last finger creates a critical opening, Megumi resists from inside, and Yuji uses the chance to tear Sukuna away from Megumi’s body. Peter helps keep the battlefield clear and stops Sukuna from using wounded fighters as easy targets, while Spider-Sense lets him react to the last desperate attacks without pretending he can suddenly overpower the King of Curses. Once Megumi is free, Sukuna refuses Yuji’s offer to keep living and finally dies.

The bigger change is what happens to the people around him. Junpei survives, Yuji has someone challenging his habit of treating death like a responsibility, Megumi has another person trying to bring him back once Sukuna takes his body, and the students gain someone who questions the parts of jujutsu society they grew up accepting. Peter never becomes comfortable with how easily that world sacrifices young sorcerers, and living there for years does not make him stop pushing against it.

He stays Spider-Man because the same thing that made him put on the mask in New York still works in a world full of curses. Peter keeps showing up when somebody is in danger, even after learning that Spider-Sense cannot save everyone and there are attacks no amount of agility can dodge. Jujutsu changes how he fights and how much he understands about losing people, but it never gets him to accept that trying to save them was the mistake.

scripts.title: What If Spider Man Was Reborn As Modulo Yuji

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Peter Parker had already lost one life before he actually died.
By the end of No Way Home, everyone who mattered to him had forgotten he existed, including MJ and Ned. That being so, he still chose to keep being Spider-Man.
Years later, that choice would eventually cost him his life. But that wasn’t the end... Peter was born as Yuji Itadori.

At first, Yuji had no idea there had ever been another life. He grew up normally, with no spider powers or memories of NYC. Eventually, small pieces started coming back. Places he’d never been. People he’d never met and fights he didn’t remember fighting.

By the time Yuji became involved with jujutsu, Peter’s old memories were already starting to affect the way he thought and fought. He didn’t have Spider-Man’s powers anymore, but he still remembered how Peter Parker was selfless and protected people.

Yuji didn’t wake up one morning with Peter Parker’s entire life in his head. The memories came back slowly enough that for years he didn’t even realize they were memories. He’d recognize places he’d never visited. New York felt familiar even though he never went there. Some mornings he would wake up knowing the names of May, MJ, or Ned. As he got older, those fragments started connecting.

The clearest memories were usually bad ones. May dying. At this point, he didn’t have the emotional connection with May as he does being Peter Parker. Memories of fighting Green Goblin. Then there was the last memory of Peter Parker’s life, whatever had finally killed him years after everyone had forgotten who he was.

It was only when Yuji reached high school that he realized he had been Peter Parker. That didn’t suddenly make Yuji feel like he was living someone else’s life. Wasuke was still his grandfather. His childhood in Sendai was still his childhood. Peter’s memories felt more like another part of himself that had taken years to surface.
Those memories did change him. Yuji had always been unusually willing to help people. He remembered what happened when Peter looked away from something because he thought it
wasn’t his problem. He also remembered Peter’s resilience. Years of fighting people stronger than him, making decisions under pressure, and finding ways out of situations that should’ve killed him.

None of Peter’s physical abilities carried over. Yuji didn’t have Spider-Sense; he couldn't stick to walls or produce webs. The strength Yuji had was already his own. He’d been unusually strong long before he knew anything about cursed energy, and Peter’s memories didn’t change that. The only thing that changed was how he used it. This only started to matter once Megumi Fushiguro came looking for the cursed object at Yuji’s school.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Yuji’s first encounter with curses still began at school. Megumi Fushiguro came looking for Sukuna’s finger, only to discover that the seal around it had already been removed. By the time Yuji reached the school, the people inside were in danger, and curses had gathered around the finger.

Peter’s memories didn’t give Yuji a hidden solution here. He still couldn’t see curses properly before entering the situation, and he still knew nothing about cursed energy. Those memories changed how quickly he accepted the danger once he saw it. Yuji entered the school and fought with the same physical ability he already had in canon, but Peter’s combat experience was starting to affect how he used it. Old instincts helped him judge distance and use the environment around him to his advantage.
But this was not enough...

Against a curse, normal strength could only take him so far. Yuji eventually reached the same desperate choice that changed his life originally and swallowed Sukuna’s finger to gain cursed energy. Canonically, Yuji does this while trying to save his friends, becoming Sukuna’s vessel in the process.

The moment Sukuna appeared, Peter’s memories made Yuji understand that this wasn’t anything like gaining another power. Yuji had no way of knowing exactly what Sukuna was yet, but his memories of Peter’s experience with danger told him that something willing to take control of his body couldn’t be treated lightly. When Yuji regained control, that was the first thing he wanted to understand.
Then Gojo entered his life.

Once Yuji learned what cursed energy actually was, Peter’s old way of thinking became useful in a completely different way. He wanted to know why cursed energy behaved differently depending on emotion. He paid attention to where it moved through his body during a strike. He noticed the lag between his natural speed and the cursed energy right behind it. He kept adjusting his timing and speed. Peter’s intelligence doesn’t necessarily make him stronger than everyone around him, but it makes him learn everything much faster.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Yuji’s first few months as a sorcerer forced him to relearn how to fight. Peter spent years relying on a body that could react to danger before he saw it and move with far more freedom than a normal person. Not to mention he could stick to walls. Yuji had none of that. His body was already far stronger and faster than an ordinary human, but the advantages were different, and trying to copy Spider-Man exactly would not be the best choice.

Peter remembered how to read an opponent while fighting, how to notice habits, and how to change an approach when something wasn’t working. Yuji started applying those instincts to close-range combat. He would watch where opponents looked before attacking. He would test their reaction to pressure and became more comfortable changing his timing instead of throwing every punch the same way.

Yuji’s natural speed created a problem because his cursed energy initially couldn't keep up with his strikes. The first impact came from his fist, followed by a second impact when the cursed energy hit. Gojo recognized this as Divergent Fist. At first, Yuji found the delay interesting because of Peter’s old combat experience. 2 impacts from 1 punch sounded useful until Yuji started training with Todo during the Goodwill Event.

But Yuji understood the difference. Instead of trying to preserve Divergent Fist because it was unusual, he worked on fixing the flaw it had. He had to make cursed energy and his body move as one. This meant breaking habits carried over from Peter’s old fighting style.

Todo’s training pushed him toward that control. Yuji entered the fight knowing that one mistyake could get him or Todo killed. Todo also told him that he wouldn't help until Yuji managed to land Black Flash. Black Flash occurs when cursed energy is applied within a small fraction of a second after a hit. Even experienced sorcerers can’t activate it whenever they want.
Yuji stopped thinking about Peter’s old body. He stopped forcing cursed energy into his strike and focused on getting Yuji’s movement and cursed energy to work together.
Then...he landed it.

Black Flash had shown him cursed energy in a way his regular training hadn’t. Once he reached this state, his control improved drastically. During the fight with Hanami, he managed 4 Black Flashes in succession which matched Nanami’s record.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Getting better at jujutsu didn’t make Yuji any better at dealing with what came with it. Junpei was one of the first reminders. Yuji tried to reach him before Mahito could pull him any further in, but wanting to save someone didn’t guarantee that he could. Mahito transfigured Junpei in front of him, and Yuji couldn’t reverse what had been done.

Yuji carried memories of seeing people die in Peter’s life. That didn’t make watching it happen again easier. If anything, having both lives made the failure worse. Yuji remembered May dying because Peter couldn't save her. He remembered everyone Peter had lost before that. Now there was another name attached to the same feeling.

Mahito also taught him something Peter’s previous enemies never could. There were curses Yuji couldn’t reason with. Peter had spent much of his first life holding back. Even when someone was trying to kill him, his goal was normally to stop them. Jujutsu forced Yuji into situations where that rule couldn’t always survive. Mahito wasn’t a damaged person who could be restrained and handed over to somebody else. He was a curse that deliberately reshaped humans for his own amusement.

When Sukuna took control, Yuji could do nothing while his own body was used to kill on a scale Peter had never experienced. Sukuna’s fight with Jogo devastated a large part of Shibuya, and his later use of Malevolent Shrine caused even more destruction. When Yuji regained control, he was left standing in the aftermath.

His first instinct was to blame himself. Peter had spent years taking responsibility for anything he believed he could’ve prevented. Yuji already carried a similar tendency, and putting those two histories together made Sukuna’s actions almost impossible for him to process. It didn’t matter that Sukuna had been controlling the body. Yuji had swallowed the fingers. Sukuna was inside him. To Yuji, that was enough to make the deaths feel like his responsibility.
Then Shibuya kept taking people from him.
Yuji watched Mahito kill Nanami. Shortly afterward, Nobara was struck by Idle Transfiguration while fighting Mahito, leaving Yuji believing he’d lost her too.

By then, there wasn’t much separating Peter’s old grief from Yuji’s new one. He stopped fighting for a moment because he genuinely couldn't see the point anymore. Todo was the one who pulled him back into the battle. He reminded Yuji that the sorcerers who had died had entrusted something to the people still alive. Yuji couldn’t undo what had happened to Nanami or everyone Sukuna had killed, but he could decide what happened next.
By the time Sukuna took Megumi’s body, Yuji had already spent months learning how dangerous it was to depend on strength alone. Against Sukuna, that lesson mattered more than ever.

Peter’s experience didn’t give him some hidden plan for beating the strongest sorcerer in history. Most of what Sukuna could do was completely outside anything Peter had dealt with before. What Peter could bring was his habit of learning while a fight was happening. If something worked once, Yuji paid attention to why. If it failed, he changed it instead of repeating the same attack and hoping for a different result.
The month before the fight in Shinjuku gave him more tools than he’d ever had before.

Yuji consumed the remaining Death Painting Wombs, which helped give him access to Blood Manipulation through the connection with his brothers. He also trained reverse cursed technique, giving him a way to heal injuries that would’ve ended his fights earlier in the series. Neither ability came easily. Yuji wasn’t suddenly as skilled with Blood Manipulation as Choso, and healing himself still required cursed energy and concentration. That was exactly the kind of problem Peter’s memories had taught Yuji to work through. He couldn't turn jujutsu into normal science, but he understood his own body well enough to make Blood Manipulation practical. Instead of trying to copy everything Choso could do, Yuji focused on techniques that worked with the way he already fought. Controlling his blood helped him recover from damage and gave him another option when an enemy created distance.
Then Yuji saw Shrine awaken during the fight with Sukuna. Sukuna’s cursed technique

had been engraved into Yuji after sharing his body for so long, but Yuji’s version didn’t appear exactly the way Sukuna used it. When it finally surfaced after Yuji’s string of Black Flashes, he had another ability he barely understood in the middle of the hardest fight of his life.

That became especially important once Yuji understood that he could target the boundary between Sukuna and Megumi’s souls. Instead of only trying to damage Sukuna’s body, he could attack the connection keeping Sukuna inside Megumi.

Peter had spent years looking for ways to win without destroying the person he was trying to save. Yuji had spent months refusing to abandon Megumi even when Sukuna had taken almost everything from him.

Yuji eventually pushed himself even further and opened his own domain. He still wasn’t more skilled than Sukuna, but he didn’t need to become another Sukuna to beat him. The entire fight had been about separating the King of Curses from the people he’d used as vessels.

When Sukuna was finally torn away from Megumi, Yuji was still willing to give him one last chance to return to his body rather than die but Sukuna refused. Peter Parker had spent his first life trying to save people whenever there was still something left to save. Yuji Itadori had reached the same conclusion after seeing far worse things than Peter ever had.
PART 6 Sukuna’s death didn’t end Yuji’s life as a sorcerer.

For a while, things were almost normal again. Megumi survived. Nobara was alive. Yuji kept taking missions, and the world slowly moved forward without Sukuna hanging over it. Then the years started passing. Yuji noticed that everyone around him was changing faster than he was.
Decades passed, and Yuji still looked young.

By the time of Modulo, 68 years had passed since the events surrounding Sukuna, yet Yuji was still alive and physically far younger than someone his age should've been. His altered body after everything involving Sukuna and the Death Paintings had left him with a lifespan far beyond that of an ordinary human.
For Yuji, everyone else kept getting older. Friends retired. Their bodies weakened. New sorcerers appeared who knew the names Gojo, Sukuna and the Culling Game as history instead of memories.

Yuji remembered all of it. He remembered being a teenager standing beside Megumi and Nobara, and now he had to watch the same generation reach the end of lives that his body seemed determined to outlast.
Peter’s memories made that harder in a different way. His first life had already taught him what it felt like to lose everyone around him. His second life had finally given him people again.

Now time was taking them too. Yuji gradually withdrew. It wasn’t because he’d stopped caring about people. The opposite was closer to the truth. After enough funerals, forming another connection meant knowing there was a good chance he’d eventually be standing at that person’s funeral too.
That isolation carried into the person Yuji became by 2086.

But he didn’t spend those decades doing nothing. His cursed techniques kept developing. Blood Manipulation and Shrine were no longer abilities he’d awakened in the middle of one desperate battle. He had decades to understand them, combine them with his close range fighting style
and remove weaknesses that only existed because he’d originally learned everything so quickly.

By the time the next major crisis reached Japan, Yuji wasn’t the inexperienced vessel Gojo had once brought into Jujutsu High. He was one of the last people alive who personally remembered the world before it. Then a spaceship arrived carrying 50,000 Simurians.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: By 2086, the world Yuji had grown up in barely existed anymore. Jujutsu society had changed, technology had advanced alongside it, and most of the people connected to the era of Sukuna were gone. Then the Simurians arrived. They were an alien species capable of using jujutsu, and they came to Earth looking for somewhere their people could live. Japan quickly became central to the situation because cursed energy and sorcery were already deeply tied to the country. Maru was sent to work with Tsurugi and Yuka Okkotsu while both sides tried to determine whether humans and Simurians could actually live together.

Yuji’s first reaction would've been very different from most sorcerers. Peter had already seen aliens before. He’d fought alongside some of them, fought against others and nearly died on another planet because of Thanos. That meant the fact that the Simurians came from somewhere else wouldn't tell Yuji anything about whether they were dangerous.

He’d want to know what they actually wanted. Tens of thousands of beings capable of using cursed energy had arrived on Earth, and nobody could guarantee what would happen if relations collapsed. At the same time, treating the entire species as an enemy before they'd done anything would only make that outcome more likely.
He’d spent part of his first life being blamed for things Spider-Man hadn't done. In his second,
he’d been sentenced to death simply because Sukuna existed inside him. He knew what it felt like to have people look at what you could become and decide that was enough to judge who
you already were.

Maru had already been placed alongside Yuka and Tsurugi as part of the effort to test whether coexistence was possible. Yuji would want that process to continue instead of letting fear make the decision first. That didn’t mean he trusted the Simurians blindly. Peter had learned that lesson too many times. Yuji would pay close attention to their cursed techniques, how their society worked and whether their leaders were telling Japan everything. He’d also watch how Japanese jujutsu authorities responded, because either side could turn a tense situation into a disaster.
For decades, Yuji had mostly kept himself away from the next generation. The Simurians gave him a reason to stop doing that. If this situation was handled badly, Tsurugi and Yuka could inherit a war.
PART 8 Maru was exactly the kind of person Yuji wouldn’t want judged by his species.

He was a Simurian representative, but he wasn’t simply there to threaten Japan or prepare an invasion. He worked directly with Yuka and Tsurugi and showed genuine interest in Earth and the people living there. That made him one of the most important pieces of the entire coexistence effort. Yuji would recognize something familiar in that situation.

Peter Parker had spent most of his first life living behind a mask while people argued about what Spider-Man was. Yuji’s second life had been even worse. For a long time, almost every major decision about his future came back to Sukuna. People who barely knew Yuji were willing to kill him because of what lived inside his body.

Maru faced a different version of the same problem. Every mistake he made could become evidence against his entire species. That's where Yuji’s involvement could begin changing the original course of events.

He wouldn't treat Maru like someone who constantly needed to prove that Simurians deserved to exist on Earth. He’d judge individual actions as they happened. If Maru helped someone, that mattered. If another Simurian did something dangerous, Yuji wouldn’t automatically place that guilt on Maru.

At the same time, Peter’s memories would keep Yuji from becoming naive about the larger situation. Thanos had also believed he was helping people. Mysterio had built an entire false identity around appearing heroic. Peter had learned the hard way that understanding somebody's motivation didn’t mean accepting what they did.

Yuji would carry that lesson into every conversation surrounding the Simurians. He could understand why a displaced people were desperate for somewhere to live without agreeing that desperation gave them the right to harm humans.

That approach would also affect Tsurugi and Yuka. Instead of simply telling them what to think, Yuji would force them to separate fear from evidence. They were the ones actually working alongside Maru. They’d seen how he behaved when nobody was asking him to represent his entire species.

In reality, his body had carried Sukuna, absorbed the remaining Death Painting Wombs and changed so much over the decades that he no longer aged like a normal person. Peter’s memories only complicated that further. Yuji had effectively lived in 2 different worlds already. That made the arrival of a third feel less impossible than it did to everyone else. For the first time in years, Yuji was standing beside them, trying to make sure they didn’t repeat the same mistakes his generations had already made.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The situation finally broke apart once the fighting spread across Tokyo. At that point, Yuji had more than enough power to throw himself into the biggest battle he could find. He could’ve gone after Dabura, or stepped into what was happening between Maru and Tsurugi but he didn’t.

Yuji had spent long enough fighting beside other sorcerers to know that being the strongest person nearby didn’t mean every fight belonged to him. Yuka had her own battle with Dabura, while Tsurugi and Maru were dealing with something Yuji couldn’t solve by simply arriving and hitting harder.

Tokyo had another problem. Cursed spirits were spreading through the city, and ordinary people were caught in the middle. That was where Yuji went. He started moving through the affected areas and exorcising anything threatening civilians. Decades of experience showed immediately. The Yuji who had once needed several punches to understand an opponent was gone. He could reinforce his body, use Shrine at close range and switch between techniques without having to stop and think through every step.
When Osuki attacked him, Yuji took the attack, controlled the exchange and landed a Black Flash. The bigger difference in this version was what happened after.

Peter’s memories had trained Yuji to think beyond the opponent standing directly in front of him. While moving through Tokyo, he’d be paying attention to where curses were gathering, which areas had already been evacuated and which sorcerers were being pulled away from more important positions. That allowed him to treat the outbreak like one connected problem instead of dozens of separate fights.

He didn’t need to personally exorcise every curse. If another sorcerer could handle one area, Yuji moved on. If civilians were trapped somewhere, that took priority. If a curse was slowing him down without posing an immediate threat to anyone else, he had no reason to waste time proving he could beat it.

Peter’s memories only reinforced that instinct. He had learned the same lesson in another life: being able to intervene didn’t always mean intervention would help. So he trusted Yuka and Tsurugi and kept Tokyo from collapsing around them.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Once the immediate fighting began to settle, Yuji finally reached the part of the crisis that brute force couldn't fix.
Maru wanted a lasting answer to the problem of cursed spirits.

That eventually brought the 2 of them into the pathway of souls, where the situation became much stranger than another battle in Tokyo. Maru’s plan involved Mahito, whose technique could interact directly with souls.

For Yuji, seeing Mahito again would’ve brought back one of the worst periods of his life. But this wasn't Shibuya anymore. Mahito was restored to full power, and the first thing he did was challenge Yuji.

Decades earlier, that fight had nearly broken Yuji. Now he had become far stronger, and more importantly, Mahito no longer had the same advantage over him. Yuji understood souls, had spent years developing attacks that could target them directly and had already fought Sukuna at a level far beyond the teenager Mahito once tormented.

Once Mahito was under control, Maru could move forward with the Ritual of Harmony. Yuji wasn’t replacing Maru’s solution. Peter’s memories simply made him more cautious about accepting a permanent change to cursed energy without understanding exactly what it would do.

Before agreeing to move forward, Yuji pushed Maru to work through the consequences and safeguards with him. If Mahito’s technique was going to alter the relationship between the soul, the body and cursed energy, they needed to know what the ritual was changing, who it could affect and what would happen if something went wrong.

That extra scrutiny didn’t create a different ritual. It made Yuji more deliberate about helping Maru carry out the plan they already had instead of treating Mahito like a weapon they only needed to point in the right direction.
The Ritual of Harmony eventually succeeds. The cursed spirits spreading through Tokyo disappear, and Yuka and Tsurugi survive the damage they suffered during the conflict.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: By the time Yuji reaches the end of this story, Peter Parker’s memories have been part of him for decades, shaping how he fights, how he thinks, and how he responds when someone else is in danger. They were never a second consciousness inside him. They were memories of a life Yuji now understood as his own past.

But Yuji’s second life changed those memories too. Peter used to carry every failure like it was his responsibility to fix everything himself. Yuji learned that sometimes helping people means trusting them, stepping back when someone else has to fight their own battle, and accepting that saving everyone was never something one person could do.
He was still carrying Peter Parker with him.
He just wasn’t living Peter Parker's life anymore.

scripts.title: What If Spider Man Was Worthy of Mjolnir

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If Spider-Man was worthy of Mjolnir, Peter wouldn't find out during some quiet test with the Avengers. He’d discover it in the middle of the Endgame battle, when there isn’t time to think about what the hammer means or whether he deserves it. Steve has already proven he can lift Mjolnir, Thanos is tearing through the battlefield, and Peter is still trying to keep the Infinity Stones away from him while everyone around him is getting overwhelmed.

Peter sees somebody about to be killed with Mjolnir lying nearby and reaches for it because it’s the fastest thing he can grab. The hammer moves. Peter barely has time to register what happened before it slams into his hand and lightning runs through him. Thor sees it from across the battlefield, Steve sees it too, and Peter is standing there holding a weapon almost every Avenger failed to move years earlier.

That gives Peter far more than another way to hit people. Mjolnir lets him call the hammer back, fly with it, channel lightning, and use the power given to whoever the hammer accepts as worthy. Peter already has Spider-Sense, webs, superhuman agility, and the kind of reflexes that let him move through fights completely differently from Thor, so the hammer immediately becomes part of the way Spider-Man fights instead of replacing it.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Peter comes back through Strange’s portal with Titan still sitting in his head like it happened a few minutes ago. He remembers Tony holding him while he disappeared, then suddenly he’s standing 5 years later in the middle of a battlefield full of people he’s never met. There’s no time for anyone to explain what happened because Thanos’s army is already pouring through the ruins and every person who can still move is being pulled into the fight.

Peter stays near the people carrying the Nano Gauntlet and uses the Iron Spider suit the way he already knows how. He webs weapons out of people’s hands, pulls wounded fighters away from crowded areas, and lets the mechanical legs cover angles he can’t reach himself. When T’Challa passes him the Gauntlet, Peter wraps it against his body with several layers of webbing and starts moving before the people around him even finish shouting where he needs to go. Half of Thanos’s army immediately starts following him. Peter’s Spider-Sense catches attacks before he sees them, but the battlefield is too crowded for him to avoid everything cleanly. He dodges one blast, gets clipped by another, swings underneath a piece of falling debris, and lands near a Wakandan fighter who's been knocked down with several Outriders closing around him.

Peter fires webbing toward the closest one and yanks it off balance, but the others keep coming. He looks around for anything heavy enough to stop them and sees Mjolnir lying beside a broken section of stone only a few feet away. Peter grabs the handle because it’s the fastest thing within reach, fully expecting the hammer to stay exactly where it is.

Miolnir comes off the ground so easily that Peter nearly throws himself backward with it. The movement catches the first Outrider completely off guard, and Peter swings on instinct, sending it across the battlefield before turning the hammer into the next attacker. Lightning crawls over the head of Mjolnir and across the Iron Spider suit while Peter stares at what he’s holding for half a second longer than he should.

Thor notices from farther across the battlefield and slows down when he sees the hammer in Peter’s hand. Steve looks over a moment later because he knows exactly what just happened, and Tony catches the same image while flying overhead. Peter looks toward Thor like he’s waiting for somebody to tell him there’s been a mistake, but Thor only points back toward the fight and shouts for him to keep moving.

Peter doesn’t have time to ask anything else, so he starts running again with the Gauntlet still strapped against his chest. He throws Mjolnir toward the next group blocking his path and fires a web line in another direction before the hammer even reaches them. Mjolnir tears through the first target while Peter swings around the second, and his Spider-Sense warns him just before the hammer returns from behind, letting him catch the handle without turning around.

The movement feels strange for about 10 seconds before Peter starts adapting it to things he already understands. He throws Mjolnir ahead, lets the hammer pull him off the ground, releases before it drags him too far, then catches part of the wreckage with a web and changes direction in the air. When the hammer comes back, Peter uses the return path to hit something chasing him instead of simply catching it as soon as possible.

Peter still has no idea why Mjolnir moved for him. He doesn’t stop to think about whether he deserves it either, because there are people getting hurt around him and all 6 Infinity Stones are sitting against his chest. As long as the hammer keeps answering him, Peter keeps using it to get the Gauntlet farther away from Thanos.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Peter asks what that means while ducking under incoming fire. Thor tells him Odin placed an enchantment on Mjolnir when he banished Thor to Earth, and the hammer only answers someone it considers worthy. Peter stares at him like that explanation somehow made the situation more confusing, but Thor leaves him with the hammer because they still need the Gauntlet moved.
Peter starts using Mjolnir around his own instincts instead of copying Thor. He webs 2 enemies together, pulls them into the same line, sends the hammer through both, then changes position
before it comes back. Against anything too large to move with webbing, Peter starts using the webs to change his own angle and lets Mjolnir provide the force he normally wouldn’t have.

The lightning takes longer because Peter doesn’t understand what actually makes it happen. He raises Mjolnir the way he saw Thor do it and gets a small charge through the suit, then tries again while moving and barely produces anything useful. Thor notices from across the fight and yells that Peter is thinking too hard, which doesn’t help nearly as much as Thor probably thinks it does,

A Leviathan comes over the battlefield before Peter gets another chance to figure it out. Webbing won't stop something that large, so Peter throws Miolnir directly toward its head and focuses on hitting the exact place he wants rather than trying to summon lightning separately. The charge builds through the hammer on its own, and a bolt follows the throw hard enough to tear across the Leviathan’s armor while Peter swings underneath it.

Peter lands harder than he expected because he still isn’t used to how much force Mjolnir lets him put behind a movement. He’s already strong enough to lift cars and stop moving vehicles, but the hammer gives him attacks that can cause much more damage than anything he usually throws around New York. Peter immediately becomes more careful about where he aims once he sees what the lightning did to something the size of a Leviathan.

Carol reaches him soon afterward, and Peter gives her the Gauntlet because she has the clearest path toward the quantum tunnel. He keeps Mjolnir and follows from another angle, using Spider-Sense to catch enemies trying to intercept her before they get close. Peter clears one route with the hammer, swings underneath the next group, then calls Mjolnir back through anyone following behind him.

Thanos destroys the van before Carol can get the Gauntlet through. The explosion throws Peter across the field and separates him from Mjolnir while Carol hits the ground closer to Thanos. By the time Peter gets his head up, Thanos already has the Gauntlet and is pulling it onto his hand. Peter sees the Stones begin lighting up as Thanos starts bringing his fingers together. He reaches toward Mjolnir without taking his eyes off the Gauntlet, and the hammer rips itself out of the rubble before Peter even finishes extending his hand. The second the handle reaches him, Peter lets it pull him straight toward Thanos.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Peter’s Spider-Sense spikes as Thanos starts positioning the Gauntlet to close his hand, warning him before the Snap is actually underway. Peter calls Mjolnir and lets the hammer pull him into the fight before Thanos can finish bringing his fingers together. Mjolnir catches him across the head while Peter fires webbing around the Gauntlet fingers, buying less than a second before Thanos tears through it. Peter’s Spider-Sense warns him before the counterattack, so he drops underneath the punch and sends Mjolnir past Thanos instead of trying to block something that would probably flatten him.
The hammer keeps going while Peter webs himself to the opposite side of the fight. He calls Mjolnir back after Thanos turns toward him, and the return path catches Thanos from behind

before Peter reaches out and takes the hammer again. Steve sees what Peter is doing and moves in with the shield, forcing Thanos to split his attention between 2 people attacking from different angles.

Peter throws Mjolnir toward Thanos again, and Steve catches it on the way back long enough to land a hit of his own. Steve sends the hammer back toward Peter while Thor comes in from the other side with Stormbreaker, and Peter catches it while moving around another attack. Nobody is standing in front of Thanos long enough to trade strength with him because Peter keeps the fight moving around the hand holding the Stones.

Thanos still manages to put Steve down and catches Thor hard enough to knock him away. Peter stays close because his Spider-Sense gives him enough warning to avoid the first few strikes, although the difference in experience is obvious whenever Thanos forces him into a position he didn’t plan for. Peter gets clipped once and goes through a section of debris before Mjolnir returns to him and pulls him back into the fight.

Carol reaches the Gauntlet arm and catches Thanos at the wrist. Peter lands beside them and webs 2 of the fingers apart while Mjolnir hits the outside of the Gauntlet, forcing Thanos to use his other hand to deal with Peter. Carol pulls at the metal around his wrist while Peter keeps changing where the pressure is coming from.

Thanos headbutts Carol and nearly gets his hand free. Peter reacts before the Gauntlet rises far enough for another Snap and throws Miolnir straight down onto Thanos’s wrist. The hammer drives his arm into the broken ground, and Thanos immediately starts tearing through the earth underneath it instead of trying to lift Mjolnir itself.

Carol only needs the delay. She grabs the Gauntlet with both hands and starts pulling while Thanos is using his free arm to get Peter away from the hammer. Peter calls Mjolnir back at the exact moment Carol gets the Gauntlet over Thanos’s knuckles, and the metal comes free before he can close his hand again.

Carol takes the Stones into the air while Tony reaches the fight expecting to find Thanos seconds away from winning. Tony sees the Gauntlet already gone, Peter holding Mjolnir, and Steve getting back to his feet with Thor beside him. He changes direction and goes after Thanos instead of moving toward the Stones.

The fight becomes much more manageable once nobody has to stop a Snap every few seconds. Tony attacks from above while Steve and Thor keep Thanos occupied on the ground, and Peter uses Mjolnir to interrupt every attempt Thanos makes to chase Carol. Thanos is still strong enough to hurt anyone there, but he can’t reach the Stones while 4 different people keep forcing him to turn.

Wanda arrives while Thanos is dealing with Thor and catches him from behind with her magic. Carol has already destroyed his ship, so he can’t order the bombardment that broke Wanda’s hold in the original battle. Steve takes his legs out with the shield, Thor knocks his weapon away, and Peter drives Mjolnir into his chest when he tries to force himself back up.

Thanos finally stays down long enough for Thor to finish him with Stormbreaker, and with Thanos dead and his ship already gone, the heroes who came through the portals wipe out what's left of his army. Tony stays on his feet because nobody needs him to steal the Stones and use them himself. Peter only realizes how close Tony had been to dying much later, when Strange explains that in the successful future he saw on Titan, Tony was the one who used the Stones and died. This outcome simply was not among the futures Strange examined.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Tony finds Peter after the battle and immediately starts checking the Iron Spider suit for damage while Peter is still holding Mjolnir. Peter keeps looking between Tony and Thor because neither of them seems nearly as confused as he is. Thor eventually walks over, points at the hammer, and asks Peter to lift it again now that nobody is trying to kill them.

Peter raises Mjolnir without effort. Steve watches from nearby, and Tony gets the same look he had years earlier when almost everyone at Avengers Tower tried and failed to move it. Peter asks Thor whether the enchantment could've been damaged during everything that happened with Hela, and Thor tells him the hammer wouldn't be answering him at all if that were the case. Peter starts giving Thor every reason he can think of for why the result doesn’t make sense. He brings up Washington, the ferry, Titan, the times Tony had to rescue him, and all the decisions he’s made that went badly. Thor lets Peter finish because he knows worthiness has never meant never making a mistake, especially after everything Thor himself had to go through before Mjolnir accepted him again.

Thor asks Peter what he was thinking when he first grabbed the hammer. Peter tells him a Wakandan soldier was about to get killed and Mjolnir was the closest thing heavy enough to stop it. He never thought about whether the hammer would move until it was already in his hand.

That explanation sits with Peter longer than anything Thor says about Asgard. Peter didn’t reach for Mjolnir because he wanted the power or because he thought lifting it would prove anything about him. He saw somebody in trouble and grabbed the only thing within reach, which is the same decision Peter has been making since before Tony ever gave him a suit.

The Avengers still need to return everything taken from the past, and Mjolnir belongs back in Asgard in 2013. Steve prepares to take the hammer with the Infinity Stones, and Peter gives it to him as soon as he understands why it has to go back. He doesn’t ask whether Shuri or Tony can duplicate it, and he doesn’t try to find a loophole that lets him keep using it.

Thor notices Peter hand over a weapon he only learned he could wield a few hours earlier. When Peter catches him watching, Thor tells him he made the right call and leaves it there. Steve takes Mjolnir with him when he enters the quantum tunnel, and Peter watches the hammer disappear knowing the next time he sees it could be years away.
Peter goes home without Mjolnir, but Tony is still alive. There is no funeral at the lake and no final recording from Tony for Peter to replay while he tries to understand what he lost. Tony
steps away from most Avengers work after the battle because Pepper and Morgan are waiting for him, but he stays close enough to notice Peter changing.

Peter becomes more careful during normal Spider-Man work. He spends longer checking whether civilians are clear before committing to a fight and starts replaying decisions afterward whenever somebody gets hurt. Tony initially assumes Endgame scared him until Peter admits that knowing Mjolnir found him worthy makes every bad decision feel harder to excuse.

Tony tells Peter that the hammer did not recruit him into another job. Whatever Mjolnir saw was already there before Peter ever touched it, so trying to rebuild his entire personality around an Asgardian weapon would probably make him worse at being Spider-Man. Peter still thinks about the hammer after that, but he stops treating every patrol like another chance to prove it made the right choice.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Tony surviving changes Quentin Beck’s plan before Peter ever reaches Europe. Beck still resents Tony for taking his work, still has access to former Stark employees, and still has the technology needed to create enormous illusions. What disappears is the easiest part of his original plan, because there is no dead Iron Man leaving behind a hero-shaped gap Beck can walk into.

Beck builds the attacks around Tony instead. His team plants old Stark components around the sites of manufactured disasters and makes the Elementals look connected to technology that escaped Stark’s control. Beck wants governments asking why another global crisis keeps tracing back to Tony while Mysterio appears as the person cleaning up the mess.

Fury pulls Peter into the investigation because the attacks keep involving systems Peter recognizes from Stark technology. Tony can investigate from the United States, but he has no interest in abandoning Pepper and Morgan every time somebody triggers another emergency overseas. Peter is already traveling with his class, so he agrees to help Fury identify what the attackers are using while trying to keep most of the trip normal.

Beck meets Peter during one of the attacks and presents himself as somebody who has been tracking stolen Stark technology for months. He doesn’t tell Peter he comes from another universe because Tony, Fury, and Strange would all have ways of asking questions Beck doesn’t want to answer. Beck keeps his story grounded enough that Peter has no immediate reason to reject it.

Peter likes him because Beck doesn’t talk down to him. He listens when Peter explains what he sees, treats Spider-Man like someone useful, and never pushes Peter to become the center of the operation. Beck also understands exactly where Peter’s pressure is coming from once Peter mentions that people keep expecting more from him after Endgame.
Beck tells Peter that being capable of helping doesn’t make him responsible for every dangerous thing happening on the planet. Peter hears that differently now because he has

spent months trying to understand what Mjolnir accepting him was supposed to mean. Beck never learns the full story, but he sees enough to know Peter is scared of becoming the person everyone automatically calls whenever something goes wrong.

Peter keeps working with him while sending Tony everything he finds. During an attack in Prague, Peter's Spider-Sense reacts to a street that appears empty, and he moves before a drone round passes through the image covering it. Peter lands behind what looks like a collapsed wall and realizes the warning in his head does not match what his eyes are showing him.

He spends the rest of the attack testing that feeling without letting Beck know. Peter fires webbing through debris that should be solid, gets close enough to flames to realize there is no heat, and notices Mysterio reacting to attacks a fraction of a second before they appear. By the time the fight ends, Peter has enough inconsistencies to stop treating Beck like an ally he simply hasn't known very long.

That puts Beck in a much worse position than he expected. Peter hasn’t handed him control of anything important, Tony is now actively looking for him, and the fake attacks are becoming harder to maintain once Peter knows what to look for. Beck has to decide whether to abandon the Mysterio identity or remove Peter before Tony finds the people behind it, which pushes the conflict away from the version Peter originally faced in Europe.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Once Tony confirms Beck's illusions are built from stolen Stark technology, Peter stops treating Mysterio like somebody he can reason with alone. Tony starts tracing the drone network while Fury’s operation coordinates with authorities to flag facilities, movements, and financial or logistical support tied to Beck’s team, which forces Beck to abandon the slow public rollout he originally wanted. Instead of spending months building Mysterio into a global hero, he decides to destroy the evidence, disappear, and make Peter look responsible for the final attack if he can.

Beck chooses London because Peter’s class is already there and because the city gives him enough surveillance, crowds, and tall structures to hide hundreds of drones inside one enormous illusion. Peter reaches the bridge before Tony does and sees a giant Elemental tearing through the river, but this time he already knows most of what he is looking at is fake. He stops chasing whatever the projection wants him to see and starts watching the physical damage instead, following broken windows, moving water, and every place his Spider-Sense reacts before the illusion catches up.

The drones are spread too far apart for Peter to destroy them one by one, so he starts connecting them with web lines while moving through the projection. When one drone tries to reposition, it drags another off course, and the illusion starts tearing open in sections because Beck’s machines can no longer hold their assigned positions. Peter never gets a clean view of Beck, but he keeps shrinking the space Beck can hide inside until Tony arrives above the bridge and starts taking remote control of whatever drones still answer Stark architecture.

Beck responds by dropping the illusion entirely and ordering every remaining drone to fire. Peter has spent most of the fight avoiding images, and now he suddenly has dozens of real weapons pointed at the bridge, the surrounding streets, and his classmates. He uses the Iron Spider legs to cover the closest angles, webs several barrels upward, and pulls 2 drones into each other before their shots can reach the crowd.

Tony handles the larger clusters from the air while Peter goes directly for Beck. The final room is filled with copies of Beck holding guns, but Peter closes his eyes once he understands what he is seeing and lets Spider-Sense guide him through the first shots. He webs the real weapon away, catches Beck before he reaches another drone control, and keeps him conscious long enough for Fury’s people to take him into custody.

Tony takes over the drones and wipes the footage Beck's team recorded before any of it can be released, so Peter comes home without his identity exposed and without the world turning against him. That means there is no desperate visit to Doctor Strange, no botched memory spell, and no multiversal crisis dragging villains from other realities into New York. Peter still has problems waiting for him, but they come from the life he already has instead of a disaster created by trying to make everyone forget who he is.

Tony notices the difference when Peter returns. A year earlier, Peter probably would have tried to solve Beck's entire operation by himself because he would have been afraid asking for help meant he was not ready. This time he called Tony as soon as the evidence stopped making sense, and Tony tells him that decision probably saved more people than any punch he threw in London.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Years later, Jane travels to New Asgard and the shattered pieces of the original Mjolnir Hela destroyed reform for her, giving the present-day hammer a path back into the story without changing Steve returning the 2013 version. Peter is curious enough to visit after learning Jane can wield it, although he spends most of the trip hoping nobody asks him to prove anything in front of Thor and Jane.

Jane asks anyway after Thor tells her what happened during Endgame. Mjolnir is sitting beside her while Peter explains that he only held it during the battle and has not touched it since Steve returned it to the past. Jane tells him that if he is still wondering whether the first time was an accident, there is a very easy way to find out.

Peter puts his hand around the handle and lifts Mjolnir without resistance. There is no army around him, no Infinity Stones to protect, and no immediate danger giving him something else to focus on, so the moment hits him differently.
