Thor watches closely, Jane smiles because she already expected the result, and Peter lowers the hammer as soon as he realizes everyone is waiting for his reaction.

He gives Mjolnir back to Jane because she is the one using it. Peter does not ask Thor whether he can borrow it, and he does not start planning around having access to Thor’s power again. The hammer answering him is enough to confirm that whatever it recognized during Endgame is still there, even after years of mistakes, fights, and decisions Peter wishes he could redo.

For the first time, Peter hears his own logic coming from somebody else and does not like where it leads. Jane tells him people are going to die if she stays behind, while Peter points out that she is treating every emergency like it has to be solved by her personally. Neither of them wins the argument because both of them have spent years making the same choice for different reasons.

When Gorr makes his final move, Thor asks Peter to carry Mjolnir into the fight Jane is too weak to survive. Peter hesitates because the hammer feels like Jane’s weapon now, but Thor reminds him that leaving it unused will not help her or anyone trapped in the attack. Peter takes it and heads into the fight with Thor while Jane remains with the doctors.

Peter handles the hammer differently than he did during Endgame because he has no Infinity Stones forcing him to sprint from one target to the next. He uses Mjolnir to pin falling structures long enough for civilians to escape, calls lightning only when there is enough open space to control where it lands, and switches back to webbing whenever the hammer would create more force than the situation needs. Thor notices Peter spending more time protecting escape routes than trying to hit the strongest enemy on the field, which is exactly why giving him Mjolnir makes sense.

When Gorr is finally stopped, Peter returns the hammer to Jane and tells her she does not have to prove anything by using it again immediately. Jane understands the point because Peter is standing in front of her as another person the hammer accepts, and he still chose to give it back instead of treating every future problem as his responsibility. Because Peter fought Gorr in her place, Jane avoids the final use of Mjolnir that would have pushed her already advanced cancer toward the immediate ending she faced in the original timeline. She survives that crisis and gains more time, but Peter has not cured her underlying cancer. She keeps Mjolnir, but the next time her condition gets worse, she waits longer before reaching for it.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Peter’s relationship with Mjolnir changes after Jane because he finally stops treating worthiness like a verdict on whether he is a good enough person. The hammer is still powerful enough to change almost any fight he enters, but Peter has now watched somebody hurt herself by believing that having access to power creates an obligation to use it every time. That makes him much more selective whenever Jane is medically unable to wield Mjolnir and chooses to make the hammer available to Peter if he genuinely needs it.

That threshold gets tested when a damaged alien craft crashes outside New York and releases a creature strong enough to tear through armored vehicles. Peter reaches it first and tries handling the fight normally because there are still people trapped around the crash site. His webs slow the creature down, but they keep snapping whenever it gets enough leverage, and Peter cannot move it far enough away from the nearby highway before more cars reach the area.

Peter calls Mjolnir only after the evacuation begins falling behind. The hammer crosses miles to reach him, and Peter uses the first throw to knock the creature away from the road instead of hitting it directly toward the traffic. He follows with webs around the legs, pulls from one side while Mjolnir returns from the other, and keeps turning the creature until its body is facing away from the people still running.

The combination works because Peter never treats the hammer like a replacement for his own abilities. Spider-Sense tells him when the creature is about to charge, webs let him change where the body is moving, and Mjolnir provides the force he cannot produce safely by himself. When the creature finally breaks loose and leaps toward the highway, Peter throws the hammer under its path and uses the returning impact to redirect it into an empty field.

Tony watches footage from the fight afterward and points out that Peter only used lightning once. Peter explains that there were too many cars nearby for him to feel comfortable throwing bolts around, and Tony laughs because Peter finally has access to one of the most ridiculous weapons on Earth and is somehow becoming more conservative with it.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The first people to seriously exploit Peter’s connection to Mjolnir are not Asgardians or cosmic enemies. A defense contractor studying footage from Endgame becomes obsessed with the idea that Earth cannot rely on enchanted weapons choosing the right people whenever another Thanos-level threat appears. Their engineers begin building a mechanical weapon designed to imitate the parts of Mjolnir they can measure, including high-speed recall, electrical discharge, and enough artificial gravity control to make the weapon nearly impossible for a normal person to stop.

The prototype has none of Odin’s enchantment, which makes it much easier for the wrong person to use. When Peter gets called to stop a field test that has turned into an armed standoff, Jane is using Mjolnir elsewhere and Thor is off-world. Peter arrives with his normal suit and realizes very quickly that he is fighting somebody who built a weapon specifically from footage of the way he used the real hammer.

Peter lets the weapon pass him, webs the handle during the return, and attaches the other end to a steel column at an angle the guidance system does not expect. The hammer tries correcting toward its user, pulls itself sideways, and smashes into the column hard enough to damage part of its control system. Its next return wobbles, which gives Peter enough time to get close to the person controlling it.

The user switches to manual movement and starts swinging the weapon directly. That makes the attacks harder, but it also brings the hammer close enough that Peter can keep himself inside the range where every missed strike threatens the person holding it. Spider-Sense lets Peter move around each swing while he webs joints in the suit controlling the weapon, gradually limiting how much the operator can turn.

Thor hears about the fight later and asks Peter whether facing a fake Mjolnir without the real one bothered him. Peter admits that it would have a few years earlier because he used to think worthiness meant he had been given access to some higher level of being a hero. By this point, he knows the hammer can add abilities, but it cannot make the decisions that matter for him.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Years after Endgame, Mijolnir has become part of Peter’s life without becoming part of every Spider-Man story. Mjolnir remains Jane’s weapon while she is able to wield it, and Peter only keeps it for longer stretches when her condition prevents her from using it and she chooses to leave it available to him. The rest of the time he still moves through New York with webs, Spider-Sense, and whatever suit he built for himself.

That balance gets tested during an attack in New York when an enhanced attacker damages a crowded bridge before Peter can move the fight away from it. Peter reaches the collapsing section first and uses layers of webbing to hold it together while civilians cross toward solid ground. He does not call Mjolnir immediately because bringing the hammer through a packed evacuation route could create another danger before everyone is clear.He takes a hit and nearly loses the web lines, but the last group of civilians reaches solid ground before the bridge gives way. Peter releases the webbing, swings away from the collapse, and only reaches for Mjolnir once there is nobody underneath the path it will take back to him. The hammer crosses the city and strikes the attacker from behind before landing in Peter’s hand. Thor arrives while Peter is already pushing the fight away from the damaged streets. He joins Peter without asking for Mjolnir, using Stormbreaker while Peter combines the hammer with webs and movement that now feel completely natural together. The 2 of them finish the fight faster once Thor arrives, but Peter spends just as much time catching falling debris and moving civilians as he does attacking whoever caused the damage.

Afterward, Peter prepares to return Mjolnir to Jane. Thor tells him Jane already made it clear Peter can keep the hammer available while her condition prevents her from using it, which Peter accepts without the awkward argument he would have started years earlier. Peter has carried the weapon enough times to stop treating possession of it like proof that he deserves anything.

He eventually returns to Queens with Mjolnir stored somewhere safe instead of carrying it openly during patrol. The hammer gives Peter flight, lightning, and enough additional power to stand beside Thor against threats that once would have been far outside Spider-Man's weight class, but the years after Endgame teach him that none of those abilities decide when he should use them.

Peter was worthy before he ever knew Mijolnir would move for him, and every important choice afterward comes from the same instinct that made him grab the hammer in the first place. When somebody needs help, Peter looks at what is in front of him, figures out what he can do, and doesn’t think of the aftermath tha may lead as a result of that decision

scripts.title: What If Springtrap Ate Homelander On Accident

sections.name: INTRO
paras: There are very few ways Springtrap could ever kill Homelander, and almost none of them involve actually fighting him.

William Afton is trapped inside a decaying animatronic body that can barely pass for human anymore, while Homelander can fly, tear people apart with his hands, and burn through them with heat vision. If the 2 simply met in a room and decided to fight, Springtrap wouldn't last long. So that isn’t what happens.

After Springtrap appears in The Boys universe, Vought gets hold of him and starts trying to figure out why there’s still something alive inside the suit. Homelander eventually gets involved out of curiosity, and a series of bad decisions leaves him much closer to Springtrap than anyone should’ve allowed.
Homelander ends up dead, Springtrap ends up with part of him inside his body, and instead of rejecting the Compound V, whatever has kept William alive for all these years begins absorbing it.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Springtrap’s arrival in this universe would be confusing long before it became dangerous. Vought would first hear about him through reports of some kind of damaged animatronic moving around on its own, which sounds less like a Supe problem and more like something security could handle. That changes once the first team actually finds him and realizes there’s a human body fused inside the suit.

William wouldn’t explain much. He’s spent decades hiding what he is, and waking up ina completely different world isn’t going to make him suddenly cooperative. His first instinct would be figuring out where he is, who has authority, and whether anyone here understands what’s keeping him alive. Vought would only make that easier by treating him like an unidentified specimen instead of a person.

The first tests would immediately stop making sense. Springtrap has a pulse only in the loosest possible sense, sections of his body are badly decomposed, and there’s no obvious medical explanation for how he can still move. Vought scientists would assume there has to be some kind of Supe ability involved, but blood work wouldn’t show Compound V. That makes him more interesting because Vought is used to being able to trace powers back to something they created.

That would be enough for them to move him somewhere secure and start running more invasive tests. William wouldn’t enjoy being restrained, but he also wouldn’t immediately start trying to escape. Vought is giving him information without realizing it. Every conversation around him tells him more about Compound V, Supes, and how much power the company has over the people it creates.

The idea of Compound V would get his attention quickly. William has spent most of his existence chasing ways to survive death, and now he’s in a world where a corporation can inject children with something that rewrites their bodies and gives them abilities no normal human should have. Even if he doesn’t understand the science yet, he’d recognize the value immediately.

Vought would be studying Springtrap for the exact opposite reason. They’d want to know if whatever keeps him alive could be reproduced. A body that continues functioning through catastrophic damage has obvious military and medical value, especially if they can somehow combine it with Compound V.

They’d bring Homelander in. Not because they need him to fight Springtrap, but because Vought already understands Homelander’s biology better than almost any other Supe. Comparing the company’s most successful Compound V subject to something that survived without V gives the scientists a baseline they can actually work with.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Homelander’s first reaction to Springtrap wouldn’t be fear. It would probably be disgust.

From his perspective, William is barely alive, trapped in a filthy suit that smells like something should’ve been buried years ago. The idea that Vought considers him worth studying would almost be insulting. Homelander has spent his entire life being treated as the company’s greatest achievement, so watching scientists get excited over a broken animatronic would annoy him more than anything else.

Homelander is terrible at hiding how much he needs to be the most important person in the room. William has manipulated children, adults, and entire situations by understanding what people want from him, and Homelander makes that unusually easy. He wants admiration, obedience, and proof that he’s superior.

At first, he’d probably visit the lab just to remind everyone how insignificant the experiment is. He’d ask why they’re wasting time on something he could destroy in seconds, and eventually he’d want to prove it. Vought wouldn't stop him completely, because seeing how Springtrap responds to damage is exactly what they’re studying.

The first controlled test would be simple. Homelander hits him but not hard enough to tear him apart, but far beyond what a normal human could survive. Springtrap gets launched into the reinforced wall, sections of the suit crack, and for a moment everyone assumes the experiment is over.

Then William starts moving again. That wouldn’t make Homelander think Springtrap is stronger than him. It would make him curious because the damage clearly worked. The suit is broken, the body underneath is worse, and somehow the thing is still conscious.

The researchers would want to repeat it with better monitoring and William would let them. Every test teaches him something about Homelander. How quickly he moves, how much force he uses when he’s barely trying, and how everyone in the room behaves when he gets irritated. Springtrap still has no realistic way to beat him, but William isn’t thinking about beating him yet. He’s watching.

The experiments also start revealing something strange about Springtrap’s body. Damaged tissue doesn’t regenerate the way Compound V healing would work, but the body keeps forcing itself to function anyway. It’s less like healing and more like death has somehow stopped being the final step.

Most of the tests would appear to fail. The V enters damaged tissue and disappears from their readings faster than expected, but Springtrap doesn’t suddenly gain powers. The researchers assume his body is breaking it down.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Homelander would become more involved once he realizes the scientists are using samples connected to him.

He wouldn't like the idea of any part of what makes him special being wasted on Springtrap. That insecurity would come out as confidence, with Homelander insisting that if they want to know whether the rabbit can survive Compound V, they should stop using tiny amounts and actually test it.

The researchers would push back because they don’t know what will happen. Homelander wouldn't care. From his perspective, the worst outcome is Springtrap dies and everyone finally stops talking about him.

So Vought prepares a larger exposure test. Because they are putting an unknown remnant creature, a concentrated dose of Compound V, and Homelander around the same chamber, the researchers insist on activating the lab’s highest-rated emergency restraint protocol before they begin. It is calibrated from Homelander’s own Vought testing data. Nobody expects it to hold him permanently; it is there to buy a few seconds if the experiment goes catastrophically wrong.

The plan would be controlled. Springtrap gets secured inside a reinforced chamber, a concentrated dose of Compound V is introduced directly into damaged tissue, and Homelander stays nearby in case William somehow becomes dangerous.

The Compound V hits Springtrap’s system and his body reacts violently. The remnant keeping William alive doesn’t treat the V like normal biology would. Instead of spreading through a healthy circulatory system, it starts collecting around whatever remains of his nerves and tissue, almost as if the body is trying to rebuild itself using material it was never designed to process. William starts convulsing hard enough to damage the restraints.

For the first time, he sees something in the chamber producing enough force to matter, even if it's nowhere close to threatening him. He moves in because he wants a closer look and because he’s convinced there’s no possible way this can go badly for him.

Springtrap doesn’t break it through strength. The Vought equipment does it for him. The reaction inside his body causes a power surge, one of the restraints tears loose, and an emergency mechanism starts cycling the chamber before the researchers can shut it down.
Homelander steps in to stop William from getting out.

Springtrap lashes out on instinct and catches Homelander’s arm which does absolutely nothing. Homelander laughs, grabs him, and starts forcing him back into the chamber. William’s damaged jaw catches on Homelander’s glove and tears open further, leaving exposed metal and broken teeth where the suit has fused around his mouth.

Homelander could end the situation instantly. Instead, he decides to humiliate him. He pushes his hand into Springtrap’s mouth, mocking how little danger William actually poses while the scientists are screaming at him to step back from the unstable chamber.
Then the emergency door slams.

It doesn’t kill Homelander. It catches his arm and shoulder for less than a second before he tears through it, but that moment is enough to pull him off balance while Springtrap is still clamped around his hand.
Homelander reacts by firing heat vision inside the chamber.

That turns the failed experiment into a disaster. The blast tears through equipment containing concentrated Compound V, ruptures part of the chamber, and sends fragments of metal and pressurized chemicals across the room. Homelander survives the explosion easily, but a sharpened piece of the containment assembly gets driven into the side of his head near the ear, one of the few areas we know can be injured by concentrated force.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: William wouldn’t understand what had just happened any better than the scientists watching it. Homelander is still alive, but he’s disoriented, bleeding heavily around the side of his head, and furious enough that he’s no longer thinking clearly. He grabs Springtrap and starts tearing pieces off the suit, which should’ve ended with William scattered across the lab.

The containment system had been built to restrain Supes if the Compound V trial produced an unexpected reaction. Once the chamber detects Homelander’s biometric profile inside the emergency zone, it activates restraints designed around the strongest subject Vought has data for.

They were never meant to hold him permanently. One locks around Homelander’s neck and pulls him backward while Springtrap is still attached to his arm. Another catches his torso. Homelander starts ripping through both almost immediately, but the angle forces his head against the damaged section of the chamber where the metal fragment is already lodged beside his ear.

William sees the blood. That’s the first moment he understands Homelander can actually be hurt. Springtrap stops trying to escape and goes after the injury. It isn’t a calculated master plan. William has seconds to act, his body is barely functioning, and Homelander is already breaking free. He bites into the damaged area because it’s the only part of Homelander he’s seen bleeding.
The broken metal around Springtrap’s jaw digs into the wound as he does it and Homelander panics.

That makes everything worse. Instead of carefully removing William, he jerks his head away while Springtrap’s jaw and the containment fragment are still caught inside the damaged tissue. The movement tears the wound open much farther than either one of them could’ve managed alone.
Homelander finally breaks the restraints.

He turns toward Springtrap, ready to kill him, but the accident has compounded the same injury several times. The heat-vision blast first drove the containment fragment into the demonstrated vulnerable tissue around Homelander’s ear. The emergency restraints then forced his head against it, Springtrap’s damaged jaw anchored the wound, and Homelander’s own violent attempt to tear himself free drove the already-embedded metal substantially deeper. The show never establishes that Homelander’s skull or brain become normally vulnerable through the ear, so this outcome depends on that existing injury creating a path the surrounding mechanical forces can catastrophically worsen.

In this scenario, that compound injury is enough to kill him. Their strongest Supe has just died in a lab accident involving an animatronic rabbit, a containment door, his own heat vision, and several decisions everyone in the room is immediately going to pretend they didn’t approve.

Springtrap is still on the floor beside him and William is chewing. His jaw locked during the struggle, damaged tissue and blood were forced into the suit, and by the time William can move properly again, part of Homelander is already inside him.

Homelander’s blood and damaged tissue have mixed directly with the dead tissue inside Springtrap. The difference is not that his blood contains some enormous reservoir of raw Compound V. The earlier purified V had trouble integrating with William’s remnant-infused corpse, while Homelander’s cells come from a body whose biology has already been successfully rewritten and stabilized by V. Whatever keeps William alive begins incorporating that already-altered material instead of trying to process raw V on its own. The dead tissue around his arm tightens. Metal that had been hanging loose gets pulled back against the frame. One of the researchers tries to restrain him and Springtrap throws the man across the room without meaning to. William looks down at his hand. He senses his strength has increased.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Vought’s first instinct after Homelander dies would be to lock down the entire lab and figure out how much of the disaster they can hide. Springtrap is still in the room, Homelander’s body is still on the floor, and the security footage makes it very clear that this wasn’t some clean assassination they can explain away later. The research team would want to focus on what changed inside William, because the accident only becomes stranger once they realize the Compound V in Homelander’s blood didn’t just pass through Springtrap’s damaged body. It stayed there.

The first changes would be physical. William’s body is still decomposed and still fused with the suit, but the parts that should barely function begin producing far more force than they did before. He can stand without fighting against every damaged joint, the frame around him stops feeling as heavy, and restraints that used to hold him start bending when he pulls against them. That would be the first moment Vought understands that they aren't looking at a failed exposure anymore. The V is doing something, even if it isn’t rebuilding William into anything close to a normal human body.

Homelander’s Compound V isn’t restoring Springtrap. It’s reinforcing what’s already there. The remnant infused body is still refusing to die the way it always has, but now it has enough strength behind it that surviving damage isn’t the only thing William can do. He starts becoming harder to damage in the first place, and every test gives the researchers a worse result than the one before it. Impacts that would’ve ripped sections of the suit apart barely move him, and parts of the frame that were already failing begin holding together under forces they were never built to handle.

Homelander’s altered tissue is not restoring Springtrap into a normal body. Vought’s tests suggest something stranger: the remnant-infused tissue is using the incorporated cells as a biological template. The changes appearing in William increasingly follow the same expression pattern Vought already recorded in Homelander, even though the result is being built through a corpse fused to an animatronic frame. That gives the researchers a reason to expect that later abilities may resemble the donor’s instead of becoming a completely unrelated Compound V mutation.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: William would let the testing continue because, for once, Vought and he want the same thing. They need to know what the altered tissue did to him, and William wants to know exactly how much stronger his body has become. Vought has another reason to accept a risk that should terrify them: Homelander is dead, his disappearance cannot be hidden forever, and Springtrap is the only surviving result that might show them a path toward replacing the power they just lost. Stopping the experiment is safer. Continuing it might preserve the entire hierarchy Vought built around having someone like Homelander at the top. The difference is that Vought still thinks this information will help them control William later, while William is treating every session like free training.

The strength comes first, and it keeps increasing. At the beginning, William is just strong enough to break restraints and damage reinforced doors. A few days later, the same tests have to be redesigned because he’s already outgrown them. He isn’t casually operating at Homelander’s level yet, but the direction is obvious enough that nobody in the lab is comfortable standing too close anymore.

The durability follows the same pattern. Springtrap was already abnormal because damage that should’ve killed William decades ago never finished the job, but now the damage itself is becoming harder to cause. Blunt impacts stop doing much. Gunfire becomes pointless. Even testing stronger weapons gives Vought less information than they hoped because Springtrap’s body and the suit around it are both becoming increasingly difficult to break apart.

The enhanced senses would probably be the first power William actually enjoys. His body has spent years limiting him, and suddenly he can hear people talking through walls, pick out footsteps before someone reaches the door, and notice details in a room he never would’ve been able to process before. That creates a problem for Vought almost immediately because the staff can’t discuss him privately anymore unless they move far enough away or start taking precautions they never needed with earlier subjects.

Flight is much less graceful. William has never had a reason to understand how moving through the air works, and his body is still an uneven combination of corpse, metal, and animatronic parts. The first successful attempt would probably end with him hitting a wall because he can lift himself but has no idea how to stop. After that, every session becomes a little cleaner. He learns how to hover, how to change direction without spinning himself around, and eventually how to move fast enough that the indoor testing areas are no longer safe.

The heat vision would show up last, and unlike the others, there probably wouldn't be a controlled discovery. William would feel something building behind the damaged eyes of the suit, turn toward whatever has his attention, and fire before either he or the researchers realizes what’s happening. The beam cuts through equipment on the other side of the room and leaves everyone staring at the damage while William figures out what he just did.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Outside the lab, Homelander’s disappearance would become impossible to hide for long. He has public appearances, interviews, Seven meetings, and an entire company built around keeping him visible. Vought can cancel a few things and blame a classified mission, but every day he remains gone creates more questions, especially from people inside the company who know Homelander doesn’t normally disappear without making sure everyone notices.

The Seven would realize something is wrong before the public does. Starlight would notice how carefully Ashley avoids answering direct questions, A-Train would start worrying about what Homelander’s absence means for everyone underneath him, and The Deep would probably become more concerned with whether the person above him in the hierarchy is actually coming back. Black Noir is the easiest member for Vought to bring into the truth because he isn’t going to panic publicly or start asking questions in front of cameras.

The problem is that there is no usable version of the truth. Vought can’t announce that Homelander died during an experimental accident after putting his hand inside Springtrap’s mouth. It would destroy the image they spent years building around him, and the details are too ridiculous to control once they become public. Even if they clean up the language, the core story is still that the strongest Supe on Earth died in a lab because everybody involved kept making worse decisions.

So Vought does what it always does and starts building another explanation. Homelander is handling something overseas. Homelander is on a classified assignment. Homelander is taking temporary leave after years of public service. None of those stories can last forever, but they buy Vought enough time to decide whether Springtrap can somehow become part of the solution.

William looks exactly like the kind of thing Vought would normally hide in a basement and deny ever existed. There’s no clean costume redesign that fixes the fact that he’s a rotting rabbit suit with a corpse inside it, and William has no interest in letting the company rebuild him into something more presentable. Marketing can suggest armor, repairs, a new name, or some carefully invented origin story, but he doesn’t need any of it.

William would listen because every offer teaches him more about what Vought has. By the time The Seven are finally brought in to see what happened, Springtrap is already strong enough that the room feels wrong the moment he moves. Watching him lift off the ground would be bad enough. Watching his eyes begin to glow red would make the connection obvious even before Ashley explains it. Homelander is gone but Springtrap has his powers.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The Seven wouldn't react to Springtrap as one group because each of them would understand the situation differently. A-Train would immediately start thinking about what happens to people when Vought finds a better version of them, while The Deep would mostly want to avoid becoming the first person asked to test whether Springtrap is actually as strong as the reports say. Starlight would see the larger problem faster than either of them. Homelander was dangerous because Vought gave someone enormous power and then spent years protecting him from consequences. Now they’ve responded to his death by doing the same thing again with someone they know even less about.

William would make that comparison worse because he doesn’t behave like Homelander. Homelander often acted on impulse, wanted everyone around him to recognize his importance, and could be manipulated through his need for approval. William doesn’t care whether the Seven respect him. He watches them because he wants to understand what they can do, and once he understands that most of them are weaker than the abilities developing inside him, the hierarchy becomes obvious without anyone saying it out loud.

Vought would still need proof that Springtrap can function outside controlled testing, so they’d start sending him on assignments away from the public. These wouldn't be heroic rescues. They’d be situations where the company wants a dangerous Supe contained, a facility cleared, or something destroyed without creating questions they have to answer later. William would accept because every mission gives him another chance to test himself against something that fights back.

The company would eventually want a direct test against another Supe, and Black Noir makes the most sense because he’s experienced, durable, and reliable enough that Vought can trust him not to turn the event into a public disaster. The goal wouldn't be to kill either of them. They just need to see whether William can actually handle someone who knows how to fight back. Noir would have the technical advantage immediately. He’s faster in close exchanges, more experienced against other Supes, and far better at using the environment than William is. The problem is that Springtrap can now afford mistakes Noir can’t. William can take hits, let Noir get closer than he should, and wait for one opportunity to grab him. Once that happens, the difference in raw strength becomes much harder for Noir to overcome.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: By this point, Vought has made the same mistake they made with Homelander. They’ve confused cooperation with control. William stayed because the labs, the testing, and the access to other Supes were useful to him, but none of that means he sees himself as one of their employees. Once he understands his new body well enough, the arrangement stops giving him much.

Ashley would try to keep him around without making it obvious that Vought is terrified of what happens if he leaves. More testing gets offered, then access to stronger Supes, then private facilities nobody else is allowed to see. William listens to all of it because every offer gives him another look at how the company operates, and by now he understands Vought almost as well as Vought understands him. He knows which people actually make decisions, which people are only pretending they do, and how quickly everyone changes their story when something threatens the company.

Homelander disappearing was already enough to make Butcher suspicious, but rumors about a new Vought asset with similar powers would push him much harder. Hughie and Starlight would eventually connect the timing, and once they realize this new figure appeared almost immediately after Homelander vanished, they’d start looking for whatever Vought buried.

Springtrap flying is already hard enough to process. Watching him use heat vision makes the situation clear. Vought didn’t replace Homelander with another Supe. They somehow let a decades-old killer absorb enough Compound V to inherit most of his abilities.

Butcher would want him dead immediately. That's much easier to say than do. William was already hard to kill before Vought touched him, and now most conventional weapons barely slow him down. Even if The Boys found something capable of damaging the new body, there’s no guarantee destroying the suit solves the remnant problem underneath it. Butcher would be looking at something developing the same kinds of physical advantages Homelander had, attached to a person who had already survived death multiple times before getting them.

Starlight would be more worried about what William actually wants. Homelander wanted control, admiration, and the feeling that everyone around him needed him. William doesn’t care about any of that. He has no interest in becoming America’s favorite hero, and he isn’t emotionally tied to Vought enough for the company to keep pulling him back.

William decides he’s finished. He doesn’t need to break out of a cell or fight through the Seven. He just walks toward the exit and waits to see whether anyone is stupid enough to stand in front of him. The security teams wouldn't matter, and sending Noir or another Supe after him would only risk proving to everyone in the building that Vought has no real way to stop its own experiment.

Ashley would understand that before anyone else does. So she lets him leave. The company would try to frame it internally as a controlled release, maybe even tell itself that William is still technically cooperating, but nobody involved would believe that. Vought no longer knows where he'll go, who he'll target, or whether he'll ever answer another call.

For the first time since Homelander died, William Afton is free again. Only now, freedom means something very different. He can cross cities in minutes, hear people before they know he’s nearby, tear through almost anything put in front of him, and survive damage that would’ve destroyed Springtrap before. The suit is still rotten, the body inside it is still wrong, and none of Homelander’s powers have made William any less dangerous as a person.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: He wouldn’t take the cape, he wouldn’t smile for cameras, and he definitely wouldn’t care about replacing Homelander in the public eye. What he would take is the strength, the durability, the flight, the senses, and the heat vision, then use them however he wanted once Vought stopped being useful.
Homelander was terrifying because he had almost unlimited power and spent years believing nobody could tell him no.
William Afton spent most of his existence with almost no power at all and still kept finding ways to survive, manipulate people, and come back.
Giving that person Homelander’s ablities would create something Vought was much less prepared for!

scripts.title: What If Sukuna Bonded With Venom

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Yuji Itadori had spent years carrying something inside him that wanted him dead.

Sukuna was already a problem Yuji understood. The cursed object inside his body had a mind of its own, a history older than modern jujutsu, and enough power to turn Yuji into a threat capable of killing everyone around him. Yuji’s one advantage was that his body could contain Sukuna without immediately losing control.
Then something else entered the equation.

A symbiote from another universe found Yuji and bonded with him, expecting a normal human host. Instead, it encountered another consciousness already living inside the same body. Sukuna immediately understood that the creature could make his vessel stronger, and he had no intention of sharing his body with anything he considered inferior.
The symbiote had other ideas.

For the first time, Yuji wasn’t the only person fighting Sukuna from inside his own body. Venom had its own instincts, its own sense of survival, and its own reasons for refusing to become Sukuna’s weapon. The 3 of them were now trapped together, and every time Sukuna took control, the other two had to decide whether they were better off fighting him separately or working together.
That decision would eventually change the fate of the entire jujutsu world.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: The symbiote had no idea where it was. It had been separated from everything it knew and left in a world with unfamiliar energy, unfamiliar life and no connection to its original home. It survived by moving from place to place until it found a human host strong enough to carry it. That search eventually brought it to Tokyo, where it sensed something unusual in Yuji Itadori.

Yuji was walking home after a mission when the symbiote found him. His body was already far stronger than a normal person’s, and the cursed energy surrounding him made him stand out from every other human nearby. The symbiote approached without understanding what it was sensing. It only knew that Yuji was unusually durable and that something inside him felt different from anything it had encountered before.

It reached him before Yuji realized what was happening. The black organism spread across his clothes and attached itself to his body, searching for a way into its new host. Yuji immediately felt that something was wrong. The symbiote pushed deeper, attempting to connect with his nervous system and establish the bond it normally relied on with a host.
Instead, it encountered Sukuna.

The symbiote could sense that another consciousness existed inside Yuji, but it had no reason to understand what Sukuna was. It followed the connection deeper and found itself in a space that didn’t resemble the human mind it expected. Sukuna’s presence was overwhelming, and the symbiote quickly understood that Yuji wasn’t the only being capable of influencing the body it had just entered.

Sukuna noticed it almost immediately. He had spent years understanding cursed energy, souls and the unusual relationship between a vessel and the entity inhabiting it. The symbiote didn’t fit any category he recognized. It wasn’t a cursed spirit, and it wasn’t another human soul. It was alive in a completely different way, yet it had managed to enter the same body as him.
That alone made it interesting.

The symbiote tried to establish control over Yuji’s body before Sukuna could interfere. Sukuna resisted. The struggle didn’t happen through a simple battle of strength because neither of them was controlling the same part of the body in exactly the same way. Yuji still possessed his own consciousness, Sukuna had control over his cursed energy and the symbiote had attached itself to the physical body.
For several moments, all three fought for influence.

Yuji eventually forced himself back to the surface, but the symbiote remained attached. Its black material covered his body before retracting beneath his clothes, leaving only a faint sensation across his skin. Yuji could feel another presence inside him, separate from Sukuna and separate from himself.
Sukuna could feel it too.

The symbiote had entered Yuji looking for a host. Instead, it had found a vessel already occupied by one of the most dangerous sorcerers in history. Sukuna quickly understood the potential of having a living organism capable of changing the physical body around him.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: The first few days were enough to show Yuji that the symbiote was different from Sukuna in almost every way. Sukuna existed as a separate soul within the vessel, while the symbiote was physically attached to Yuji’s body and could spread through it whenever it wanted. Yuji could feel the organism moving beneath his skin, responding to danger and reacting to his thoughts even when he wasn’t consciously asking it to.

The symbiote also began learning from him. It picked up basic memories, understood his connection to the people around him and became familiar with the instincts that had kept Yuji alive as a sorcerer. It didn’t immediately understand cursed energy, but it could feel when Yuji reinforced his body with it. The difference became obvious during his next mission.

A curse attacked Yuji from behind. Before he could turn around, the symbiote reacted on its own. Black material spread across his arm and formed a shield just as the attack landed. The impact pushed Yuji across the ground, but the added protection kept his arm from breaking. Yuji recovered and destroyed the curse with a cursed energy enhanced strike.
The symbiote had protected him without being told to.
That changed how Yuji viewed it.

It wasn’t simply an organism waiting for instructions. It had instincts and could make decisions, which meant it could also choose to act against him. Yuji began testing the limits of the bond carefully. The symbiote could reinforce his limbs, form tendrils, create protective layers around his body and recover from injuries much faster than Yuji could on his own. It could also change its shape almost instantly, allowing Yuji to create weapons or shields without carrying anything.
Sukuna watched all of it from inside the vessel.

He wasn’t interested in the symbiote’s concern for Yuji. What caught his attention was the way the organism responded to physical damage. It could rebuild parts of its own body, alter its shape and remain functional even after suffering injuries that would cripple a human. Sukuna understood the advantage immediately. His cursed techniques were already dangerous, but they were still being used through Yuji’s human body.
The symbiote gave him another layer between his cursed energy and the limits of the vessel.
Sukuna eventually tested that theory himself.

When he took control of Yuji’s body, the symbiote reacted differently than it did with Yuji. It spread across Sukuna’s limbs and formed around his hands, responding to his movements while resisting his attempts to command it directly. Sukuna tried to force it into a shape he wanted, but the organism resisted. It followed the physical movement of the body without accepting Sukuna as its owner.
That irritated him.
For now, he couldn’t completely control it.
That didn’t mean he couldn’t use it.

Sukuna began experimenting with his cursed energy while the symbiote covered his body. The results were immediate. His physical strength increased because the organism reinforced the vessel, while cursed energy reinforcement pushed the enhanced body even further. The symbiote could also reshape itself around his movements, creating additional protection around areas Sukuna expected to be attacked.
The important difference was that the symbiote wasn’t giving Sukuna more cursed energy. It was making the body carrying that cursed energy harder to damage.
The symbiote was becoming useful. That was exactly what Sukuna wanted. The problem was that the symbiote was learning too.

Every time Sukuna took control, it experienced his actions through the same body as Yuji. It began to understand the difference between Yuji’s instincts and Sukuna’s. Yuji fought because someone needed help. Sukuna fought because nothing stopped him from taking what he wanted.
The symbiote didn’t need to understand human morality to recognize the difference. For the moment, it remained with Yuji because Yuji was the host it had chosen.
But Sukuna was already trying to change that relationship.
And the longer the three of them remained together, the more difficult it would become to decide who actually controlled the body.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Sukuna eventually stopped treating the symbiote as something that could simply be ignored. It had already changed the physical limits of Yuji’s body, and Sukuna wanted to know exactly how far those changes could go. The next time he took control, he allowed the symbiote to spread across his entire body instead of forcing it away.

The result was immediate. Black material covered Yuji’s skin and formed a layer around Sukuna’s arms, chest and legs. It reinforced the vessel while remaining flexible enough to move with him. Sukuna could feel the organism responding to his movements, but it still wasn’t following his commands. When he formed a blade from his hand, the symbiote changed its shape to accommodate it rather than creating the weapon itself.
Sukuna began testing what happened when he combined the organism with his cursed techniques.
He started with Dismantle.

The slash left his hand and crossed the street before cutting through a concrete building. The symbiote reacted to the release of cursed energy by tightening around his arm. Sukuna noticed that the organism could respond to the movement of his cursed energy even though it couldn’t produce cursed energy of its own.
That gave him an idea.

Sukuna allowed the symbiote to form a long tendril from his arm and released Dismantle at the same moment. The cursed technique still behaved as Sukuna’s technique, but the tendril gave him another way to position himself and attack. He could use the biomass to pull himself toward a target, change his angle in midair or restrain an opponent before using a slash.
The symbiote wasn’t changing Dismantle.
It was giving Sukuna more ways to use it.

The same principle applied to Cleave. Sukuna couldn’t simply turn every piece of the symbiote into an automatic Cleave weapon, but he could use the organism to bring an opponent into range and then apply the technique through direct contact. A tendril could wrap around a target, pull it toward him and create an opening for Cleave.
This made Sukuna far more difficult to approach.
The symbiote also learned from Sukuna’s fighting style.

It began anticipating the movements he preferred. When Sukuna raised one arm to attack, the organism could reinforce the opposite side of his body in preparation for a counterattack. When he jumped, it could form tendrils behind him and pull his body through the air. When an opponent tried to strike from behind, the symbiote could react before Sukuna physically turned around.
Sukuna appreciated the efficiency.
He still hated the fact that the organism could act without his permission.
That became obvious during another mission.

A curse attacked Yuji while Sukuna was in control. Sukuna prepared to counterattack, but the symbiote suddenly pulled his body backward. The movement avoided an incoming strike that Sukuna had already seen. He immediately understood what had happened.
The symbiote had acted on its own.
It had protected the host without waiting for him.
Sukuna attempted to force the organism back into place. The symbiote resisted for several seconds before finally returning control of the body.
That was the first time Sukuna understood the real problem.
The symbiote was another living presence sharing his vessel.

Sukuna could overpower most people through cursed energy, but the symbiote wasn’t a sorcerer standing in front of him. It was spread throughout the body he needed to use. If he wanted complete control, he couldn’t simply destroy it without also damaging the vessel.
For now, he decided to tolerate it.
That decision would become increasingly difficult once Sukuna discovered the symbiote’s weaknesses.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: During a later fight, an enemy attack produced a high-pitched vibration that caused the black material covering Yuji’s arm to suddenly retract. The symbiote convulsed and pulled itself away from the source of the sound.
Sukuna noticed immediately. The organism had a weakness. He began looking for the second one.

Sukuna had never been the type to ignore a weakness once he discovered one. The symbiote’s reaction to the sound had already given him something useful, but he needed to know whether the problem was limited to one frequency or whether the organism was vulnerable to a broader range of attacks.
He tested it carefully.

The first experiments were enough to confirm that intense sound could disrupt the symbiote’s ability to maintain its form. The organism pulled away from Yuji’s skin, lost control of the shape it had created and struggled to remain attached. Sukuna didn’t need to understand every detail of its biology to recognize the practical problem. If an opponent discovered the same weakness, the symbiote could become a liability.
The second weakness appeared when the organism was exposed to extreme heat.

Sukuna used a controlled amount of his flames and watched the reaction. The symbiote immediately pulled its mass away from the heat source. Parts of its outer layer began to deteriorate before the organism repaired itself and returned to Yuji’s body.
Sukuna now understood the limits of his new advantage.
He didn’t try to remove those weaknesses. Instead, he began learning how to fight around them.

The symbiote could retract its outer layer and protect the most vulnerable parts of its body. It could also move through Yuji’s body instead of remaining exposed on the surface. When Sukuna used his flames, the organism learned to retreat rather than absorb the full force of the heat.
Sukuna knew how to use cursed energy. The symbiote knew how to keep itself alive.
Neither trusted the other, but both were capable of recognizing when working together was more useful than fighting.
The more they fought together, the harder they became to separate.
Yuji noticed the change.

Whenever Sukuna took control, the symbiote no longer fought him constantly. It remained cautious, but it had started recognizing that Sukuna’s cursed energy could protect it from attacks that would otherwise damage the organism. Sukuna, in turn, had stopped trying to force the symbiote into submission every time it resisted.
Neither of them had accepted the other. They had simply found a reason to cooperate.
The symbiote had become an extension of his fighting style without becoming part of his cursed technique.
That distinction mattered.
Sukuna still had the same cursed energy, the same techniques and the same limitations. What changed was the body carrying them.
And eventually, that difference became obvious during the Shibuya Incident.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: When Gojo was sealed inside the Prison Realm and the fighting across Shibuya intensified, Yuji was pulled deeper into the conflict. The number of Sukuna’s fingers inside his body continued to increase, and every additional finger made the entity inside him harder to contain.
The symbiote could feel the change before Yuji fully understood it.
Sukuna’s presence was becoming heavier. Yuji could barely keep him contained. Then Jogo found him.

The disaster curse had brought enough of Sukuna’s fingers to force another transformation. Yuji’s body began reacting as the cursed energy surged through him, and the symbiote immediately tightened around his organs and muscles to protect itself from the pressure.
It wasn’t enough.
For the first time since the bond began, the symbiote felt Sukuna completely overwhelm the vessel.
Yuji disappeared beneath the weight of his own cursed energy.
Sukuna opened his eyes and the symbiote realized it was about to experience what its host had been fighting against from the beginning.
The change happened the moment Sukuna took control.

Jogo had given Yuji ten more of Sukuna’s fingers, bringing him to fifteen in total, and the effect was immediate. Sukuna’s presence became far stronger than it had been during his earlier appearances. The symbiote struggled to contain the pressure moving through the vessel, but it adapted its shape around him and reinforced the body as Sukuna’s cursed energy pushed it beyond anything Yuji had previously experienced.

The result wasn’t a new source of cursed energy. Sukuna remained limited by his own reserves and output. What changed was the body carrying that power. The symbiote reinforced Yuji’s muscles, protected his organs and created additional material around his limbs whenever Sukuna moved.
Sukuna noticed the difference immediately.
Jogo confronted him soon afterward.

The disaster curse had been responsible for restoring Sukuna to a much greater level of strength, and he wanted that power turned against humanity. Sukuna had no interest in becoming anyone’s subordinate, but he accepted Jogo’s challenge because it gave him an opportunity to test the limits of his new body.
The fight quickly moved through the streets of Shibuya.

Jogo’s flames covered the area around them, forcing the symbiote to react. Heat remained one of its weaknesses, and Sukuna could feel the organism pulling its exposed mass closer to Yuji’s body whenever the flames reached them. It didn’t make the symbiote immune to fire. Instead, it reduced the amount of biomass exposed to the attack and relied on Sukuna’s cursed energy reinforcement to protect the vessel.
Sukuna adapted to the limitation without slowing down.
Eventually, Jogo used Maximum: Meteor.

The massive attack descended toward Shibuya, dragging debris and vehicles into its path as it approached the ground. Sukuna recognized that taking the attack directly would be unnecessary, so he used the symbiote’s tendrils to pull himself away from its trajectory. The organism anchored itself to nearby structures long enough to redirect his movement before retracting back into his body.
The meteor struck Shibuya and devastated the surrounding area.
Sukuna survived.
Jogo was already exhausted.
Sukuna then used the technique he had relied on to finish him in the original course of events. He summoned the flames of Furnace. Its destructive power was enough to overwhelm Jogo’s flames.

The heat hit the symbiote immediately. It pulled itself beneath the outer layer of Yuji’s body as far as the bond allowed while Sukuna reinforced the vessel with cursed energy. Even then, Furnace nearly destroyed it. Large sections of the biomass burned away, and what remained stayed buried against the host until the temperature dropped. It survived, but only barely.
The symbiote reacted to the heat by retreating closer to Yuji’s body.
Sukuna released the attack. Jogo was incinerated.

The symbiote had now witnessed Sukuna kill a powerful cursed spirit without hesitation. It had already understood that Sukuna was dangerous, but watching him destroy Jogo after accepting the fight simply for his own amusement gave the organism a clearer picture of the person sharing its host.
It didn’t like what it was learning. Sukuna barely noticed. His attention had already shifted to another source of cursed energy.
Megumi was nearby.
More importantly, Megumi had summoned Mahoraga.
The fight began.
Mahoraga charged first.

Sukuna met it head-on, using the symbiote to reinforce his limbs while he fought with his own physical ability. The creature’s strength forced him to take the battle seriously. Sukuna used Dismantle several times, cutting into Mahoraga’s body and watching the wheel above its head turn.
The damage didn’t stay.
Mahoraga recovered from the injuries, and its next movements showed that the adaptation had already begun.
Sukuna changed his approach.

He used the symbiote to create additional limbs and tendrils, forcing Mahoraga to respond to attacks coming from different angles. The organism didn’t give those attacks any supernatural properties. It simply allowed Sukuna to control more of the battlefield at once.
Mahoraga continued adapting.
Sukuna understood what was happening. His slashing attacks were becoming less effective, and continuing to rely on them would give Mahoraga more time to adapt.
That was when Sukuna made his decision.
He expanded Malevolent Shrine.

The domain manifested across the surrounding area without forming a traditional closed barrier. Sukuna deliberately reduced its range to roughly 140 meters because Megumi was still nearby and he needed to keep him outside the domain. Malevolent Shrine could extend farther, but Sukuna limited it while relentlessly applying its slashing attacks. The symbiote reacted to the domain differently from ordinary cursed energy.

It couldn’t stop Malevolent Shrine’s sure-hit effect, and it didn’t become part of the domain itself. Instead, it covered Sukuna’s body and protected the vessel from the debris and physical destruction surrounding him.
Mahoraga was repeatedly cut by Sukuna’s slashes.
The wheel turned again.
Sukuna understood that Mahoraga had adapted to his slashing attacks. He needed something different before the shikigami could recover completely.
He used Furnace.

The domain had already filled the area with the aftermath of its own destruction, allowing Sukuna to use the technique on a scale far beyond the narrow flame attack he had used against Jogo. The resulting explosion consumed Mahoraga before it could recover and adapt to the flames. The symbiote pulled itself tightly against Yuji’s body as the heat spread through the area.
Even Sukuna’s new partner had limits.
It survived, but the experience changed something inside it.
The symbiote had already seen Sukuna kill Jogo. Now it had watched him destroy Mahoraga and devastate a large part of Shibuya simply to accomplish his objective.
Yuji eventually returned to consciousness.
He saw what remained of the city.
The destruction was no longer something he could separate from Sukuna. He had experienced the massacre through the same body, and the symbiote had experienced it alongside him.
For the first time, Yuji and the symbiote reached the same conclusion.
Sukuna couldn’t be allowed to remain unchecked.
The symbiote still feared him. Yuji still struggled to contain him.
But now they had something neither had possessed before. An ally inside the same body.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Yuji woke up with the symbiote still attached to him.

The damage across Shibuya was difficult to understand from inside the body. He remembered pieces of what had happened, but the memories weren’t complete. He could feel Sukuna’s actions as if they had happened to someone else, yet every movement had still come from his own body.
The symbiote had experienced everything with him.
For the first time since the bond began, it pulled away from Sukuna instead of moving closer to him.
Yuji understood why.

Sukuna had always been dangerous, but there had been a difference between knowing that and watching him use his freedom. The symbiote had seen Jogo die. It had felt the heat from Furnace. It had experienced Malevolent Shrine from inside the same body. It now understood that Sukuna didn’t need a reason to destroy something beyond wanting to do it.
Yuji couldn’t defeat Sukuna by himself. The symbiote couldn’t either. That left them with one option. They had to work together.

The alliance didn’t make them friends. Yuji still didn’t completely trust the organism inside his body, and the symbiote still didn’t understand humans well enough to share all of his priorities. What they did share was a simple goal. Neither wanted Sukuna controlling the body whenever he pleased.
The symbiote began testing how much influence it could maintain while Yuji was conscious.

It could move through Yuji’s body, reinforce damaged tissue and cover his skin almost instantly. It could also resist Sukuna’s attempts to reshape the vessel when he took control. That resistance wasn’t enough to stop Sukuna, but it could make certain movements more difficult.
Yuji learned to take advantage of those moments.

When Sukuna tried to force control over an arm, Yuji pushed against him mentally while the symbiote reinforced the same muscles from the outside. When Sukuna attempted to move the body before Yuji was ready, the symbiote could delay the movement long enough for Yuji to regain control.
The effect was small.
Against Sukuna, small was enough to matter.
Sukuna noticed.
Sukuna eventually understood that destroying it would be dangerous.
The organism was too deeply integrated with the vessel.
That limitation gave Yuji and the symbiote something they had never had before.
Time. They could wait. Sukuna couldn’t.
He wanted freedom from Yuji’s body, and the longer he remained inside a vessel that resisted him, the more he became interested in finding another one.
Megumi had always been the obvious choice.

Sukuna had recognized the potential of the Ten Shadows Technique long before Shibuya. He had seen enough of Megumi’s abilities to understand that the technique could give him options Yuji never could. More importantly, Megumi’s body had none of Yuji’s unusual resistance to Sukuna’s control.
The symbiote sensed the change in Sukuna’s attention.
It didn’t know exactly what he was planning, but it understood that he was looking for somewhere else to go.
Yuji reached the same conclusion.
If Sukuna ever found another vessel, the symbiote would have to decide whether it stayed with Yuji or followed him.
That question became harder as the Culling Game progressed.
Then the opportunity arrived.

Megumi’s sister was revealed to be Yorozu, an ancient sorcerer who had incarnated within Tsumiki’s body. The revelation shattered Megumi’s remaining hope of saving her normally. Sukuna recognized the moment immediately.
Megumi was vulnerable.
That was what Sukuna had been waiting for.
The symbiote felt Sukuna’s attention shift toward him and tried to warn Yuji through the bond. Yuji understood before Sukuna made his move. There was no time to stop him. Sukuna activated Enchain.

The binding vow gave him control of Yuji’s body for one minute. The agreement also prevented him from harming anyone during that period, a condition he had accepted when the vow was originally made. Sukuna had deliberately hidden the agreement from Yuji by making him forget it, and he had been waiting for a situation where the restriction could work in his favor. Yuji tried to resist. The symbiote resisted with him. Sukuna still took control.
The symbiote wrapped itself around Yuji’s fingers. Sukuna tried to separate it. It held on. He understood what it was doing immediately.

The organism knew he was preparing to transfer himself into Megumi. It didn’t know exactly how he intended to accomplish it, but it knew that leaving Yuji meant leaving the host who had allowed it to survive.
Sukuna forced the symbiote away from his hand.
It returned. He tried again. The organism spread farther across his arm. Sukuna finally stopped wasting time.

Sukuna concentrated part of his soul and cursed energy into one of Yuji’s physical fingers. He tore the finger off, turning the severed flesh into a cursed object, exactly as he had planned long before this moment. The symbiote had already left a thin layer of its living biomass around the finger before Sukuna took control, and when Sukuna tore it away, that biomass went with it.

Yuji fought harder. The symbiote followed. For a moment, Sukuna’s movement slowed. That was all the resistance they could create. Sukuna tore the finger away and immediately forced Megumi to consume it. The transfer began, pulling Sukuna out of Yuji’s body and into his new vessel. This was the same basic method Sukuna used in canon when he escaped Yuji and incarnated inside Megumi.
But this time, something came with him.
When Megumi consumed the severed finger, the symbiote biomass entered his body with the cursed object and immediately searched for a new host as Sukuna’s transfer began.
Sukuna had expected to leave the organism behind. He hadn’t considered that part of it had already been carried with him.

Black material spread across the severed finger and disappeared beneath the surface. The transfer completed. Megumi’s body became Sukuna’s new vessel. The symbiote was there too. Yuji remained behind.
For the first time since Sukuna entered his body, Yuji was completely alone.

And for the first time since the symbiote found him, Venom had lost its original host. Inside Megumi’s body, Sukuna immediately understood what had happened. The symbiote had been pulled into the transfer with him.
Sukuna took that as proof that he had finally won.

He was wrong. The symbiote hadn’t followed him because it wanted Sukuna. Part of it had been carried into Megumi with the severed finger, and once the transfer began, it had attached itself to the new vessel to survive.
Sukuna had escaped his cage. He had gained the Ten Shadows Technique. And without realizing it, he had carried the one thing capable of resisting him into his new body.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Megumi’s body changed the balance immediately.

Sukuna had spent years trapped inside Yuji, unable to use his full potential whenever he wanted. Megumi gave him access to the Ten Shadows Technique, a cursed technique Sukuna had already recognized as unusually valuable. The symbiote gave him another advantage. It could reinforce Megumi’s body, protect damaged areas and reshape itself around Sukuna’s movements.
The combination was powerful, but it wasn’t unlimited.

The symbiote still couldn’t produce cursed energy, and it couldn’t use the Ten Shadows Technique by itself. Sukuna remained responsible for summoning the shikigami and controlling his cursed techniques. The organism could only interact with what was already there.
Sukuna began testing that boundary.

Divine Dogs emerged from Megumi’s shadows as they normally would. The symbiote remained attached to Megumi instead of spreading onto the shikigami. It reinforced Sukuna’s vessel while the Ten Shadows Technique operated separately.
Nue emerged next. The symbiote still remained on Megumi’s body, reinforcing his movement and durability while Nue attacked through the Ten Shadows Technique exactly as it normally would.
But one shikigami mattered more than all the others.
Mahoraga.
Sukuna already knew what the Divine General could do. He had fought it in Shibuya and understood that its adaptation made it one of the most dangerous shikigami in existence.
Instead, Sukuna used the organism to protect himself while Mahoraga fought.
That became important when the time finally came to confront Gojo.
Gojo had been unsealed, and the battle between the two strongest sorcerers of their era was unavoidable.

Sukuna entered the fight in Megumi’s body with the Ten Shadows available to him and the symbiote spread across his body. The black material moved around his arms and shoulders, changing shape whenever he moved.
Gojo immediately recognized that Sukuna had gained something else.

The symbiote couldn’t touch Infinity on its own. Physical tendrils stopped before reaching Gojo, just like any other physical attack. Sukuna understood that immediately and stopped wasting attacks on the barrier.
He needed a way around it.
The fight became a battle of techniques rather than brute strength.

Gojo’s Limitless prevented direct physical attacks from reaching him, while Sukuna used Domain Amplification when he needed to fight at close range. The symbiote helped him maintain his physical condition through the exchanges, but it couldn’t solve the central problem. As long as Infinity remained active, Sukuna still needed another method to reach Gojo.
The domain clashes began.

Malevolent Shrine and Unlimited Void collided, forcing both sorcerers to rely on their understanding of barrier techniques and cursed energy. The symbiote remained close to Sukuna’s body throughout the exchanges, repairing physical damage where it could while Sukuna used Reverse Cursed Technique for injuries that exceeded what the organism could handle.
Venom experienced something it had never encountered before.
It could understand physical combat. It could understand pain. It could understand survival.
But it couldn’t understand why Sukuna was willing to keep risking everything simply to prove that he could defeat Gojo.
The longer the fight continued, the more obvious the difference became.
Sukuna wasn’t fighting simply because he needed to survive.
He wanted to win.
Mahoraga eventually became the key.

Sukuna used the Ten Shadows Technique to bring the shikigami into the battle and allowed its adaptation to develop against Infinity. The process took time, and Gojo recognized the danger. He focused on destroying Mahoraga before its adaptation could become complete.
The symbiote helped Sukuna protect the shikigami whenever Gojo created an opening, but it couldn’t prevent Gojo from attacking Mahoraga directly.
Gojo eventually destroyed it.
For a moment, the fight appeared to be over.
Sukuna had lost the shikigami that had provided him with the model he needed.
Then he used what Mahoraga had taught him.

Sukuna had observed Mahoraga’s adaptation and understood that the shikigami had eventually changed the target of its attack. Instead of trying to reach Gojo through Infinity, Mahoraga had attacked the space that Gojo occupied. Sukuna applied that principle to Dismantle.
He no longer needed to cut through Infinity. He could target the world around it. The symbiote moved across his arm as Sukuna prepared the attack.
Venom understood what was about to happen. It also understood that there was nothing it could do to stop Sukuna through physical strength.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Sukuna released the slash.

The attack didn’t behave like the ordinary Dismantle attacks Venom had seen before. Its target had changed. Sukuna wasn’t simply sending a blade toward Gojo. He was extending the target of his cursed technique to the space and world containing him.

Venom understood what was about to happen before Sukuna could complete the attack cleanly. The symbiote suddenly pulled back from Sukuna’s arm and jerked the limb off line at the exact moment he was setting the target. Sukuna still released the slash, but the cut tore through the space beside Gojo instead of the space he occupied. The symbiote felt Sukuna’s satisfaction disappear immediately. Then it understood what victory would have meant.

Gojo was the strongest obstacle between Sukuna and complete freedom. If he died, Sukuna would have very few people left who could challenge him directly. The Culling Game was still underway, Kenjaku’s plans were continuing and the merger involving Tengen remained a possible future outcome.
Venom had no interest in any of that.
It had spent enough time inside Yuji and Megumi to understand humans, cities and the world around them. It had also learned something about Sukuna that Yuji had known from the beginning.

Sukuna didn’t care what remained after he won. The symbiote’s priorities were different. It needed a living host. It needed a world where those hosts existed. It needed somewhere to survive. Sukuna’s complete victory threatened all three.
Venom finally stopped trying to become part of Sukuna’s power.
It started looking for a way to resist him.
The symbiote couldn’t cancel cursed energy. It couldn’t erase Dismantle. It couldn’t suddenly become stronger than Sukuna.
What it could do was control its own mass.

It began separating from the parts of Megumi’s body that Sukuna was using most heavily. The movement was subtle enough that Sukuna didn’t immediately notice. The symbiote pulled away from his arms and chest, retreating into areas where it could remain connected without directly interfering with the cursed technique.
Sukuna noticed the change too late.
The organism suddenly pulled back.
His arm remained intact, but the additional reinforcement disappeared.

Sukuna tried to force it back. The symbiote resisted. Sukuna had spent months treating the organism as another weapon. He had never needed its permission before because he could simply use the body while it remained attached. Now that Venom had decided to withdraw its cooperation, Sukuna couldn’t force the organism to enhance every movement without risking damage to Megumi’s body.
The symbiote detached from his outer body and fell across the ruined ground.
Sukuna was left standing without it.
His cursed energy hadn’t disappeared. His Ten Shadows hadn’t disappeared. His physical abilities hadn’t suddenly become those of an ordinary human.
But he had lost the additional protection and mobility the symbiote had provided.
Venom had chosen its own survival.
Sukuna turned toward it.
For the first time since their bond began, the organism wasn’t afraid of what he would do.

It had already made its decision. Sukuna tried to attack. The symbiote moved away before he could reach it. Gojo had already realized the interrupted slash had been meant to bypass Infinity entirely. The moment Sukuna’s attention shifted, Gojo took advantage of the opening.
The battle continued.

Sukuna was still extremely dangerous, but he no longer had the physical support he had grown accustomed to. Gojo now understood that Sukuna had found a way around Infinity, and the fight returned to a technical battle between two sorcerers who both understood what the other was capable of.
The symbiote stayed out of the fight.
It watched. It could have returned to Sukuna. It chose not to.

That decision didn’t guarantee Gojo’s victory. Sukuna was still Sukuna, and the outcome of the battle depended on the state of both fighters, their techniques and the damage they had already suffered.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Sukuna had entered the relationship expecting another weapon. The symbiote made his body stronger, gave him new ways to move and allowed him to combine his cursed techniques with an organism that could reshape itself around him. But the greatest change wasn’t physical.
It was the fact that Sukuna could no longer assume that every advantage he gained would remain his forever.

Yuji had spent years resisting Sukuna because he wanted to protect the people around him. Venom resisted for a different reason. It wanted to survive. Those motives weren’t identical, but eventually they led to the same decision.
Sukuna could be powerful enough to dominate almost anyone around him.
He couldn’t force another living creature to want the same things he wanted.
That was the mistake he made with Venom.
He treated the symbiote like an extension of his own power when it was always another living being sharing the same body.
And once Venom decided that helping Sukuna meant destroying the world it needed to survive, it stopped helping him.

scripts.title: What If Sukuna Was In The Avengers

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Loki thought he was arriving on Earth at the perfect time. S.H.I.E.L.D. was divided, the Avengers barely knew how to work together, and the Chitauri were waiting for him to open the way.

Then Sukuna appeared, fully incarnated in his original body. For this scenario, he has Shrine, Reverse Cursed Technique, Malevolent Shrine, and Divine Flame, but none of the abilities he only gained later through Megumi or Mahoraga.

He had no interest in protecting Earth, joining the Avengers, or helping Loki conquer anything. To Sukuna, this was simply a new world filled with people he didn’t understand yet, and that made observing it more interesting than destroying everything immediately.
That changes once the invasion begins.

The moment New York fills with Chitauri soldiers, Leviathans, and enough chaos to turn the city into a battlefield, Sukuna finally has a reason to get involved. The problem for the Avengers is that the person helping them stop Loki might be more dangerous than the army they’re fighting. PART 1
Sukuna appearing in the MCU shortly before Loki’s invasion wouldn’t immediately look like an Avengers level emergency.

At first, S.H.I.E.L.D. would only know that something unusual had happened. A man with no identification, no known connection to any enhanced individual, and abilities that don’t match any technology or alien species they've encountered has suddenly appeared on Earth. That alone is enough to put him on their radar, but Sukuna wouldn’t give them much to work with. He has no reason to announce himself. This world is unfamiliar, and Sukuna is intelligent enough to understand that charging into the first group of armed people he sees gains him nothing. He’d spend his first stretch simply watching how this Earth works. The existence of modern cities, advanced weapons and public knowledge of figures like Thor would interest him, but none of it would make him cautious in the normal sense.
