Homelander would survive the first attempt and respond violently. He could tear through the chamber, destroy most of Otto’s equipment, and force the fight back into open space, but now he’d be injured and furious. Otto would still have to stay alive long enough to finish the job, which means the fight becomes far less controlled than anything he planned.

At that point, Otto would probably have to rely more heavily on Spider-Sense and Peter’s natural agility than on technology. He could keep moving through the remains of the facility, using collapsed structures and broken machinery to stay out of Homelander’s direct line of sight while continuing to pressure whatever injury he managed to create. He wouldn't try to overpower him because that would waste the one advantage he managed to create.

If Otto’s first successful ear attack proves that his equipment can actually deliver enough concentrated force to meaningfully worsen the injury, repeated attacks around the same area could potentially leave Homelander unable to fight effectively. If his equipment can’t reproduce enough force, Otto loses that route entirely and would need to disengage or rely on whatever other parts of the plan actually proved effective. Even if the ear strategy works, bringing Homelander down would remain a possible outcome rather than something Otto can assume will happen.

That decision would force Otto to confront something he’s been avoiding since arriving in this world. He came here believing that most of The Seven were dangerous because nobody held them accountable. Now he has Homelander helpless in front of him, and nobody is strong enough to stop Otto from deciding what happens next.
For the first time, he’d have to ask whether being willing to do more than Peter actually makes him a better Spider-Man, or whether it simply makes it easier to justify crossing another line.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Otto would probably stop short of killing Homelander. Not because he suddenly adopts Peter’s exact philosophy, and not because Homelander deserves sympathy. Otto would stop because he finally sees where his own logic has been taking him. Since arriving, he has treated almost every problem as something that could be solved through better control, better planning, or someone intelligent enough to make the decisions everyone else keeps getting wrong.

Vought thinks the same way. The company decided it could create Supes, control them, hide their mistakes, and decide which consequences mattered. Homelander took that further by believing his strength gave him the right to stand above everyone else. Otto has been looking down on both of them while repeatedly making the same assumption about himself.

That realization wouldn't turn him humble overnight, because Otto is still Otto. He’d continue believing he’s smarter than almost everyone around him, and he’d still think many of Peter’s methods are inefficient. What changes is how comfortable he feels using superiority as an excuse to make every decision alone. The Boys would arrive expecting a very different outcome. Butcher would probably want Homelander dead while he’s vulnerable, especially after everything he’s done. Otto would refuse to hand the situation over to him, which would create one final clash between them. Butcher would accuse Otto of losing his nerve, while Otto would see Butcher’s obsession for what it is. Killing Homelander may prevent future harm, but Butcher also wants the satisfaction of finally seeing him die, and Otto has spent enough time around him to know those motives are tangled together.

Hughie and Starlight would support keeping Homelander alive if there’s a realistic way to contain him. That creates another problem because Vought cannot be trusted with him, and a normal prison means nothing to someone with his abilities.

The same preparation that let Otto hurt Homelander could become the basis for emergency containment, but Otto would know it is temporary and experimental. If the fight confirms that a specific sonic effect can disrupt Homelander repeatedly, Otto could incorporate that exact effect into the emergency containment alongside reinforced restraints designed around Homelander’s movement, isolated systems he can’t easily destroy from one point, and remote monitoring through Spider-Bots. If the sound never proves reliably useful, he wouldn’t build the containment system around it.

It wouldn’t be a sustainable prison yet. Homelander recovering and tearing through the system remains a serious possibility, so Otto would use Vought’s research and everything learned during the fight to search for a longer-term answer while the emergency setup is still holding. For once, he wouldn’t pretend the problem is solved just because he built the first containment system.

Vought would suffer even more from what Otto releases afterward. He has already copied records connected to Compound V, cover ups, deaths, internal communications, and Homelander’s behavior. Once Homelander can’t protect the company through fear, Otto could distribute the evidence through several independent channels so Vought has no single server or witness to silence.

The Seven would start falling apart quickly after that. Starlight would have far more room to oppose the company openly, while members like A-Train would have to decide whether protecting Vought is still worth anything once the system around them begins collapsing. Black Noir’s future would depend on whether he survives his earlier encounter with Otto and how much evidence becomes public about what Vought used him for.

Butcher wouldn’t suddenly trust Otto either. If anything, seeing Otto defeat Homelander would make him more cautious because now he knows exactly what Spider-Man can do when he prepares seriously. The difference is that Butcher would also know Otto had the chance to kill Homelander and chose not to, even after spending most of their time together arguing that harsher methods were sometimes necessary.
Otto wouldn’t ask for approval. He’d simply continue doing what he thinks Spider-Man should do, only with a little more awareness of how easily certainty can become arrogance when nobody pushes back.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Superior Spider-Man would probably do better in The Boys universe than Peter initially would because Otto has fewer limits on how far he’s willing to prepare and how aggressively he'll deal with people like Homelander.

Vought and The Seven would constantly reward the part of Otto that believes power should belong to the person most capable of using it, and for a while he'd see their failures as proof that he was right.

If Otto manages to bring Homelander down after confirming enough of his experimental counters during the fight, the real lesson would come from realizing how easy it is to become the kind of person he spent the entire story judging.

scripts.title: What If Thanos Snapped The Other Half

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If Thanos snapped the other half of the universe away, almost every Avenger who survived Infinity War would disappear instead.

Tony, Steve, Thor, Bruce, Natasha, Rhodey, Rocket, and Nebula would all be gone. But Spider-Man would still be standing on Titan with Doctor Strange, Star Lord, Drax, and Mantis, while Black Panther, Wanda, Falcon, Bucky, and Nick Fury would survive back on Earth.

And Doctor Strange would know immediately that this wasn’t the future he was expecting. He'd already watched 14,000,605 possible outcomes and found only 1 where they beat Thanos. Tony was supposed to survive the Snap in that future, which means the moment Tony disappears instead, Strange knows they've entered a different outcome.

Now half the universe is still gone, Thanos still has all 6 Infinity Stones, and the exact group that eventually discovered time travel in Endgame no longer exists. The heroes left behind have Wakandan technology, sorcery, alien knowledge, and some of the most powerful people in the MCU, but none of them know how to bring everyone back.
So if the other half survived, they'd have to find their own way to undo the Snap.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: The Snap finishes on Titan, and Peter waits for the same feeling Strange saw in the future he expected. It never comes. Peter stays exactly where he is, along with Strange, Quill, Drax, and Mantis. Tony is the one who starts fading instead. Peter reaches him before he disappears, but there’s nothing he can do as Tony turns to dust in front of him.

Nebula disappears next. That leaves the Titan group staring at an empty battlefield with no idea what happened anywhere else. Strange understands more than the others because he remembers the futures he searched before giving Thanos the Time Stone. The outcome he chose depended on Tony surviving this moment, and Tony is gone. Strange can remember what happened along the paths he personally viewed, but those visions don’t give him a map of everything that happens from here. They've already moved away from the sequence he was trying to create.

Quill wants to go after Thanos immediately. Gamora is dead, Nebula just disappeared, and he knows Thanos escaped Titan with the Stones. Strange stops him because they don’t even know where Thanos went, and chasing him with 5 people would accomplish nothing. Their first priority is finding out whether Earth still exists and who survived there.

Strange opens a portal back to Earth and brings Peter and the Guardians with him. Peter arrives without Tony, still wearing the Iron Spider suit Tony gave him, and has to explain to people who barely know him that Tony disappeared on Titan. Strange learns Wong is gone and
contacts the remaining Masters of the Mystic Arts, while Quill starts trying to figure out whether any of the Guardians are still alive elsewhere.

Wakanda has been hit by the opposite version of the disaster. T’Challa, Shuri, Wanda, Sam, and Bucky are still there, but Steve, Thor, Bruce, Natasha, Rhodey, Rocket, and Okoye are gone. Wanda is sitting near Vision’s body after watching Thanos kill him for the Mind Stone, except she doesn’t get the 5 years of nothing that followed in the original timeline. She has to remain there while everyone around her starts realizing half the world has disappeared. T’Challa and Shuri immediately turn Wakanda into one of the main places coordinating the response. Their country still has its king and its leading scientist, along with most of the infrastructure that existed before the battle. Wakandan aircraft begin searching surrounding areas while Shuri tries to determine what happened from the energy readings left behind by the Snap.

Nick Fury survives too, and so does Maria Hill beside him. Fury sees people and vehicles vanishing across the city and reaches the pager he carries for emergencies involving Carol Danvers. This time he gets to finish what he was trying to do. He sends the signal and remains alive to explain exactly why he sent it when Carol eventually receives it.

Within the first day, the surviving heroes begin finding each other. Strange brings the Titan group into contact with Wakanda, Fury starts rebuilding communication between whatever governments and agencies are still functioning, and Peter keeps asking whether anyone has found Tony. Nobody has.

Then Strange tells the group the part he’s been avoiding. Before the Snap, he searched 14,000,605 possible futures and found 1 where they eventually won. He gave Thanos the Time Stone because that future required Tony to survive Titan, and Peter realizes what Strange is telling them before anyone else says it. The future Strange bet everything on is already gone.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Carol reaches Earth after receiving Fury’s signal and finds him waiting for her instead of an empty pager lying in the street. Fury gives her the quickest explanation he can, then takes her to Wakanda because it has become the safest place to gather the surviving heroes. Carol meets T’Challa, Shuri, Strange, Wanda, Sam, Bucky, Peter, and the remaining Guardians there, and Quill immediately wants to know whether she can find Thanos.

Finding him is possible because the Stones released an enormous amount of energy when Thanos used them. Shuri has data from the Wakandan battlefield, Strange knows what the Stones were capable of, and Carol can help search beyond Earth once they narrow down what they're looking for. The Guardians also know enough about interstellar travel to identify worlds where Thanos could disappear without drawing attention.
Strange knows they can’t assume the Stones will remain available forever. In the future he originally followed, Thanos eventually made it impossible for the surviving Avengers to simply

take them back and reverse what happened. Strange doesn’t have a recording of every conversation or coordinate from that future sitting in his head, so he can’t point to a planet and tell everyone exactly where Thanos is. He can warn them that waiting for him to return would be a mistake.

Their search eventually tracks the enormous second release of Infinity Stone energy. The heroes realize Thanos has used the Stones again, and Carol carries a smaller group toward the source while the Guardians provide the spaceflight knowledge she lacks. Wanda insists on going because Thanos killed Vision in front of her, while Strange comes because he understands the Stones better than almost anyone left.

They reach the Garden and find Thanos badly injured. Carol attacks before he can properly respond, Wanda tears apart the defenses around him, and Strange restrains his remaining arm before Thanos can close his fist. Quill reaches him a moment later and demands to know what happened to Gamora, but Thanos has already accepted whatever they plan to do to him. Strange checks the Gauntlet and finds what he was afraid of. The Stones are gone.

Thanos tells them he used the Stones to destroy the Stones so nobody could undo his work. Wanda nearly kills him on the spot, while Quill has to be pulled away after Thanos confirms Gamora died obtaining the Soul Stone. Killing him now gives them revenge and nothing else. Strange forces the group to confront that before anyone makes the decision for everyone.

They bring Thanos back alive which mmediately creates arguments on Earth. Wanda wants him dead, Quill wants him dead for Gamora, and entire governments want the person responsible for wiping out half their populations executed. T’Challa sees more value in keeping the only person who actually wielded all 6 Stones alive until they understand what he did, while Fury wants every piece of information Thanos has about the Stones, their origins, and whether their destruction can be reversed.

Thanos doesn't give them a hidden solution. He destroyed the Stones at the atomic level and believes his work is permanent. Strange can’t use the Time Stone because it no longer exists in a usable form, and Wanda’s connection to the Mind Stone doesn’t let her recreate the other 5. The group that reaches Thanos faster than the original Avengers did still ends up with the same larger problem. Half the universe is gone, and taking the Gauntlet away from Thanos is no longer an option.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The next several years look very different with T’Challa and Shuri still alive. Wakanda opens more of its resources to the outside world as governments struggle with missing workers, abandoned infrastructure, food distribution, and millions of families suddenly cut in half. T’Challa spends far more time dealing with the political consequences of the Snap than fighting, while Shuri builds systems that let surviving countries share resources and keep basic services operating.

Fury rebuilds his network around whoever is left. Sam and Bucky become 2 of the people he can send when a crisis needs more than local authorities, although neither of them tries to become Steve. Sam still has the wings and Bucky still has decades of combat experience, so they spend much of the early period dealing with problems created by governments and criminal groups collapsing after the Snap.

Peter’s life changes even more. May survived the Snap in the original timeline’s dusted half, so she’s still here with him, but Tony isn’t. Peter goes back to Queens after Titan and tries returning to school while carrying memories nobody his age can understand. A large part of his class survived too, including Ned and MJ, because they were among the people originally dusted. Instead of all of them disappearing together and returning at the same age 5 years later, they have to grow up inside the world Thanos created.

Peter keeps being Spider-Man because stopping would leave him thinking about Tony. The Iron Spider suit eventually becomes difficult to maintain without Tony’s systems and infrastructure behind it, so Peter returns to building more of his own equipment. Shuri can help when the suit suffers damage he genuinely can’t repair, but she doesn’t become his replacement Tony. Peter gradually becomes much more independent because there’s nobody standing behind him with another suit whenever he gets in trouble.

Wanda has an even rougher 5 years. Vision stays dead, and there’s no Snap taking her away moments after losing him. Shuri had already been working on separating the Mind Stone from Vision before Thanos attacked, so Wanda eventually returns to Wakanda and asks whether anything from that work can help. Shuri can recover information from what remains of Vision, but she can’t restore the person Wanda lost without the Mind Stone and the parts of his consciousness that died with it.

The Guardians eventually leave Earth again. Quill, Drax, Mantis, and Groot search for whatever remains of their old life, but the Benatar isn’t waiting for them on Titan and Rocket is gone. They eventually acquire another ship and begin moving between worlds affected by the Snap, finding the same collapse everywhere they go. Quill also keeps looking for any evidence that Gamora could somehow have survived Vormir, even after everything they learn tells him she didn’t. Strange spends those years in a stranger position than anyone else. He knows what happened in the successful future he saw, including pieces of the route that eventually brought everyone back, but knowing that Tony solved a problem doesn’t give Strange Tony’s knowledge. He can tell the others that the successful future eventually involved people reaching the Stones through different points in time, but he never personally saw how the survivors built that system while he was gone. The people who originally made that answer possible are gone.
Their best lead eventually comes from 3 people who barely knew the Avengers.
Hank Pym, Janet van Dyne, and Hope van Dyne all survived this Snap.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Scott Lang disappeared while Hank, Janet, and Hope were preparing to send him into the Quantum Realm. The equipment is still there, the Pym family still has access to Pym Particles, and Janet has something nobody in the original group of survivors possessed at the beginning of Endgame. She spent decades inside the Quantum Realm and already knows that time behaves strangely there.

Fury eventually connects Hank with Shuri after hearing Strange’s description of the successful future. Hank initially hates the idea of handing his work over to another government or superhero team, especially after everything that happened with S.H.I.E.L.D. Janet is the person who gets him to listen because Scott disappeared with everyone else, and if the Quantum Realm gives them even a chance of finding him again, she wants to understand it.

Janet immediately focuses on the part Strange can’t explain. She warned Scott about time vortices because they exist inside the Quantum Realm, and now Strange is telling her only that the successful future somehow involved reaching the Stones through different points in time. He cannot give her the mechanism that made it possible. Hank has the particles and equipment to enter the Realm, Janet understands its behavior better than anyone alive, and Shuri has the computing power to start measuring what happens during controlled tests.

Their first attempts don’t send anyone into the past. Tiny probes enter the Quantum Realm and return with clocks that disagree with the amount of time measured outside. Another comes back after only minutes in Wakanda while its internal systems record far longer. Janet helps Hank adjust where they enter, and the difference changes again.
That gives Shuri data she can work with.

She begins mapping how different routes through the Quantum Realm affect elapsed time instead of trying to invent a time machine from nothing. Hank modifies the tunnel so they can reproduce the same entry conditions, while Janet identifies regions she remembers avoiding because their behavior was unstable. Strange occasionally uses astral projection to observe without physically entering, giving them another way to compare what happens inside with the passage of time outside.

But inconsistent clocks are not enough to choose a year and travel there. They spend months turning those measurements into a navigation system that can reproduce specific temporal exit points. Janet supplies what she knows about the Realm, Hank controls the entry and return conditions, and Shuri builds models from every successful probe until they can deliberately target the same point more than once. Only after that breakthrough do they have something closer to controlled time travel.The discovery changes everything because they finally have a route that doesn’t depend on rebuilding the destroyed Stones. They can go to periods when the Stones still existed.

It also gives them a much harder problem than the original Avengers faced. Strange knows the original Time Heist worked, but several of the people who carried it out are now dust. They have to decide which points in history they can safely enter with the people they still have, how to return the Stones afterward, and whether changing any of those encounters could create consequences Strange never saw.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: This team can approach that day differently because Strange doesn’t need to steal the Time Stone from the Ancient One without explanation. He can go to the Sanctum himself, tell her who he is, and explain that he eventually becomes her successor. She'll still have every reason to question him, especially when he asks for the Eye of Agamotto, but Strange knows enough about the Ancient One, Dormammu, and his own future at Kamar-Taj to prove he isn’t a random thief looking for an Infinity Stone.

Peter and Sam handle the Space Stone because both can move through New York without immediately looking like alien invaders. Their proposed target is the Tesseract after the Avengers capture Loki, and Strange has already warned them that taking it during the middle of the battle would risk changing too much. They consider waiting until the fighting is over and following the transfer instead, using Peter's ability to move through the building and Sam’s aerial view to avoid running directly into their earlier counterparts. But the post-battle custody chain is exactly where the plan becomes unreliable: Loki can get access to the Tesseract and escape with it, turning what looked like the cleaner window into another uncontrolled variable.

The Mind Stone is harder because it remains inside Loki’s scepter and quickly becomes tangled with S.H.I.E.L.D. and HYDRA. Bucky volunteers because he knows exactly what HYDRA was doing inside S.H.1.E.L.D. during that period. Going back there means walking near people who
were still controlling and torturing his younger self, but it also gives him knowledge nobody on the original Time Heist team had.

Wanda refuses to stay behind once they start planning for the remaining Stones. The Mind Stone created her powers and was part of Vision, while Thanos took it from Vision directly in front of her. She can sense and manipulate Infinity Stone energy in ways most of the team can't, making her useful if anything goes wrong during retrieval. Strange still warns her that seeing Vision or trying to change what happened to him could create a completely different problem from the one they're trying to solve.

The Guardians provide the route to the Power and Soul Stones. Quill knows exactly where he found the Orb on Morag, and he can tell them when his younger self arrived there. Vormir is different. They know Gamora died there and eventually learn why when Thanos explains what obtaining the Soul Stone required. Nobody wants to discover whether the Stone will demand another sacrifice from them.
Strange suggests avoiding that problem by going to a point after the Soul Stone has already been obtained. That means confronting Thanos before the Snap.

Peter understands what another trip to Titan could mean. Somewhere in that past, Tony is still alive. Wanda knows Vision is still alive in Wakanda. Bucky and Sam know Steve is there too, and the Guardians know Gamora’s death has already happened by the time Thanos reaches Titan.
They've finally found a way into the past. Now they have to retrieve 6 Infinity Stones without turning the mission into an excuse to save every person they already lost.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Once Hank, Janet, and Shuri can reliably send people to a chosen point in the past, the group spends weeks trying to turn the 2012 plan into something they can actually survive, and every version still ends at Vormir or in a fight with Thanos. Strange eventually pushes them away from visiting several different years at all because every trip creates another place where they can lose someone, expose themselves, or interfere with events they barely understand. He knows they need all 6 Stones, and there was already a moment in their own history when all 6 were sitting in the same place.

Thanos had them immediately after the Snap. Going back to Wakanda during the battle would mean fighting Thanos while everyone else is still trying to stop him, and Strange knows how badly that already went. Shuri finds a much cleaner opening in the records from 2018. Wakanda detected the first enormous release of energy when Thanos snapped, and several weeks later
the surviving heroes detected another release from the planet where they eventually found him. That second surge was Thanos destroying the Stones.

The plan becomes much smaller after that. They don’t need to steal 6 Stones across different points in history. They need to take 1 damaged Gauntlet from an injured Thanos and get back through the Quantum Realm before he can stop them.

Mantis immediately becomes one of the most important people on the mission. She already held Thanos under once on Titan, and she remembers how difficult it was even with several people restraining him. This time they can approach while he’s alone and recovering, which gives her a much better chance of keeping him unconscious long enough for everyone else to remove the Gauntlet.

Carol goes because she can physically hold Thanos if he wakes up. Wanda goes because her powers can control individual parts of the Gauntlet without touching the Stones directly, and she has already proven she can overpower Thanos when he doesn’t have a chance to use them. Strange handles their escape route, while Quill insists on going with Mantis because he refuses to send her near Thanos without him.

Peter wants to join them too. Tony disappeared in front of him 5 years ago, and this is the first real chance they've had to bring him back. Strange initially tells him the team already has enough people, but Peter points out that he was one of the people who almost pulled the Gauntlet off Thanos on Titan. He knows how Thanos moves when someone goes for his hand, and his webs give them another way to control the arm without standing close enough to get hit. T’Challa agrees to let Peter go after speaking with him privately. Peter is 22 now, and T’Challa has watched him spend the last 5 years working beside Wakanda instead of waiting for Tony to return and solve things for him. Shuri gives Peter a fresh set of web cartridges and checks the Iron Spider suit one last time, while Hank prepares enough Pym Particles for an emergency return if their first route closes.
Thanos smiles and refuses to answer but Strange doesn’t need him to. Shuri already has the exact timestamp of the second energy surge, and the team has chosen a point 3 hours earlier.
Strange only came to see whether Thanos would react when he heard the plan, and the silence tells him enough.

A few minutes later, Hank activates the quantum platform. Peter looks around at the people staying behind, then closes his helmet as the machine begins shrinking them. Their target is a quiet planet in 2018 where Thanos still believes he has already won.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: The team emerges several miles away from Thanos’s hut because Strange doesn’t want the quantum arrival happening close enough for the Stones to detect anything unusual. The Garden looks peaceful from a distance, with crops growing around the small home Thanos built for himself and no armies or defenses anywhere nearby. Quill hates how normal it looks after everything Thanos did to get there.

Strange sends his astral form ahead first. Thanos is inside and alone, sitting near the window with the damaged Gauntlet still attached to his left arm. The metal is burned almost black around the Stones, and the entire side of Thanos’s body carries the damage from the Snap. He eventually lies down without removing it.

Mantis waits until Strange confirms that Thanos is asleep. He opens a portal only large enough for her to reach through and place both hands against Thanos’s head, keeping the rest of her body safely on their side. The moment she touches him, her expression changes because the same grief she felt on Titan is still there, except now it sits underneath the certainty that Gamora’s death accomplished what he wanted.

She pushes deeper and keeps him asleep. Strange opens the portal wider. Wanda enters first and wraps red energy around Thanos’s left hand, separating each finger so he can’t close his fist if he wakes. Carol takes the arm at the elbow, while Peter covers the Gauntlet itself with several layers of webbing and starts pulling from the opposite side.

The Gauntlet moves. It got farther off Thanos’s hand on Titan than Peter remembered. The damaged metal has loosened around his burned arm, and Carol slowly forces it over his wrist while Wanda keeps every finger spread apart. Mantis starts shaking as Thanos fights against her control without fully waking, and Quill holds her shoulders to keep her steady.

Peter pulls harder and gets the Gauntlet past Thanos’s knuckles then Thanos’s eyes open. Mantis cries out as she loses contact, and Thanos immediately tries to close his hand. Wanda already has his fingers locked apart, but the Power Stone begins glowing anyway as Thanos forces enough movement through the damaged Gauntlet to activate it. Carol drives his arm into the floor before he can direct the energy at anyone.
The explosion tears apart half the hut.

Peter gets thrown outside with the Gauntlet still attached to his webs. Carol stays on Thanos and takes the first punch when he gets to his feet, while Wanda grabs his left arm again before he can call the Gauntlet back with the Space Stone. The damage from the first Snap has slowed him down, but he still has enough strength to send Carol through the remains of the wall. Thanos breaks free and charges toward Peter. Strange opens a portal under Peter before Thanos can reach him. Peter drops through with the Gauntlet in his hands and lands beside Quill, while Strange immediately closes the opening between them and Thanos. Wanda and Carol are still on the other side.

Thanos turns on Wanda first. He can’t use the Stones because the Gauntlet is gone, but he’s still physically stronger than almost anyone Wanda has fought. She catches him with red energy before he reaches her and slams him into the ground hard enough to crack it, then keeps him there while Carol comes back through the field and hits him from above.

Strange reopens the portal behind them. Wanda releases Thanos and crosses first, while Carol backs through after her without giving him another chance to grab anyone. Strange closes the portal as Thanos reaches it, leaving him alone on the Garden without the weapon he sacrificed everything to complete.
They disappear into the Quantum Realm with the Gauntlet. From Thanos’s perspective, the entire attack lasted less than 2 minutes.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: Shuri has the containment chamber ready when the group returns to 2023. Peter places the Gauntlet inside without touching any of the Stones directly, and the entire room lights up as Wakandan equipment begins measuring the energy coming from it. For the first time since 2018, all 6 Infinity Stones exist in their timeline again.

Wanda steps forward after that. Her abilities came from the Mind Stone, she held back Thanos while destroying that same Stone, and she has spent the last 5 years learning how to control power that was still developing when Vision died. None of that proves the Gauntlet won't kill her. Her connection to the Mind Stone may help her sense what the Stones are doing, but nobody has evidence that it gives her enough resistance to survive channeling all 6 at once.

Shuri modifies the Gauntlet around Wanda’s arm rather than building another one from the beginning. Eitri already created this weapon specifically to channel all 6 Stones, and replacing its entire structure with Wakandan technology would mean guessing at work none of them fully understand. Shuri reinforces the damaged sections, adds insulation around Wanda’s forearm, and builds an emergency release that can remove the Gauntlet if Wanda loses consciousness before she snaps.

Peter stays in the room while they prepare her. Wanda notices him watching the Gauntlet and knows exactly who he’s thinking about because she has spent 5 years doing the same thing with Vision. Peter asks whether the Stones could bring back people who died before the Snap too.
Wanda looks toward the Mind Stone.

Vision wasn’t dusted. Gamora wasn’t dusted either, and neither were the countless people who died during everything that led to Thanos completing the Gauntlet. Wanda could try asking for more than the return of the people Thanos erased, but nobody in the room knows what happens once they start using the Stones to rewrite deaths that weren't part of his original Snap. Strange tells them to keep the command exact. They know the Stones erased half of all life and should be able to restore those same lives because that is what happened in the future he originally saw. Adding Vision, Gamora, or anyone else turns the Snap into a different act with consequences he has never witnessed.
Wanda hates the answer and still accepts it.

When she puts her hand into the Gauntlet, the Stones activate before Shuri finishes locking the final support around her arm. Energy runs through Wanda’s body and sends her to one knee, while the Mind Stone glows brighter than the others for several seconds. Wanda forces herself back up and keeps her fingers open while Shuri watches the readings climb.

Carol moves closer in case she falls. Strange keeps the room shielded, and Peter stays behind the containment line while Wanda struggles to keep her arm raised. She thinks about Vision, then about everyone who has spent 5 years living with an empty place where somebody used to be.
She closes her fingers.

The Snap sends a burst of energy through Wakanda strong enough for Shuri’s systems to detect it across the entire country. Wanda is thrown backward when the Gauntlet releases, and Carol catches her before she hits the floor. For several seconds nobody knows whether she survived. The Stones remain inside the damaged metal while Wanda’s left arm and shoulder are severely burned, and Shuri rushes in as soon as the energy readings fall. Wanda is alive, but whether her connection to the Mind Stone helped her endure the Snap or she simply survived an enormous gamble is impossible for them to know.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Steve returns near the place where he vanished and immediately reaches for his shield because the last thing he remembers is Thanos escaping through a portal before Steve himself started turning to dust. Instead, Bucky is standing several feet away looking 5 years older. Sam finds Steve a few moments later, and neither of them has time to explain much before Thor and Bruce reappear nearby.

Natasha and Rhodey return elsewhere, while Rocket comes back demanding to know where Groot went. Nebula reappears on Titan and finds the planet empty until Strange sends a portal for her. Tony returns there too, standing in the same place where Peter watched him disappear. Peter goes through the portal himself.

Tony barely has time to look around before Peter reaches him. He recognizes the Iron Spider suit first and then realizes Peter looks different underneath it. Peter removes the helmet, and Tony stares at someone who was 17 the last time he saw him and is now standing there as a 22-year-old man.

Peter tells him it worked. Tony asks what worked, and Peter starts explaining while Strange opens more portals to bring everyone back to Earth. Tony eventually learns that he was gone for 5 years, Peter kept being Spider-Man without him, Wakanda became the center of the recovery effort, and the people Thanos left behind found their own way into the Quantum Realm.

The reunion doesn’t stay happy for long because Strange reminds everyone that the Gauntlet they used doesn’t belong in 2023. They stole it from a branch of 2018 where Thanos had already completed the Snap, and leaving that reality without the Stones would permanently deprive it of them. They have already changed that branch by attacking Thanos and taking the Gauntlet, so putting the Stones back cannot restore its original history. It can only return what they removed and leave that altered reality with its own chance to continue. Wanda is in no condition to return with them. Shuri is treating the damage to her arm, and even speaking takes effort after channeling all 6 Stones. Strange chooses Carol, Mantis, and Peter because they were part of the original theft and already know exactly what happened inside the Garden hut.

Tony immediately objects to Peter going anywhere after learning he just got him back. Peter tells him he has already been living with this mission for 5 years and was one of the people who took the Gauntlet in the first place. Tony looks like he wants to argue, then realizes everyone else in the room is treating Peter like an adult because that is what he became while Tony was gone.

Strange reminds them that returning the Gauntlet is about restoring what they removed from the branch, not using the trip to rewrite what already happened to their own timeline. Their goal is to put the Stones back into that reality before Thanos can leave the Garden and turn the missing Gauntlet into a permanent disaster.

Strange visits present-day Thanos one last time before they go. He tells him the Snap has been reversed and watches the first real change in Thanos's expression since his capture. Thanos asks whether they killed another universe to do it.
Strange tells him they're going back to make sure they didn’t.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Strange keeps the portal open behind the group while Carol carries the Gauntlet inside a Wakandan containment case. They don’t try to put it back on Thanos’s arm. Peter sets the case down several yards away, and Strange tells Thanos every Stone is still inside.
Thanos doesn't believe them until the case opens.

The 6 Stones light up in front of him, and for a moment nobody moves. Thanos looks from the Gauntlet to Peter and realizes the boy standing there is older than the one he fought on Titan. He understands that they came from years after his victory and that returning the Stones means they already used them for whatever brought them there.

He asks whether his Snap survived. Peter tells him no. Thanos starts toward the Gauntlet, and Carol moves between them before he gets close. Strange tells him they could take the Stones again if they wanted to, but they came back because this universe still needs them. Returning the Gauntlet cannot erase what the team already changed or what Thanos now knows. What he chooses to do with the Stones after that belongs to this altered branch.

Mantis watches him carefully as Thanos approaches the case. She can feel the anger underneath everything else now, along with the same grief that was there on Titan. He has already sacrificed Gamora, already completed the Snap, and now people from the future have shown him that his victory can be undone.

The group leaves before he can decide what to do next.Back in 2023, the world has a problem much larger than any battle. Billions of people have returned to a civilization that spent 5 years learning to function without them. Families have changed, children have grown up, homes belong to different people, and entire countries have reorganized themselves during the missing years.
The Avengers are different too. Steve comes back to a Bucky and Sam who learned to operate without him. Thor returns to a world where T’Challa spent 5 years helping coordinate global

recovery while Wakanda stayed open to the outside. Rocket discovers that Groot grew for another 5 years without him, while Quill has to explain that Gamora still isn’t coming back. Tony has the strangest adjustment with Peter. He remembers a teenager reaching for him on Titan only a few seconds before Tony himself turned to dust. Peter remembers watching Tony disappear, going home without him, finishing school, continuing as Spider-Man, helping Wakanda, and spending years working toward the mission that eventually brought Tony back. The surviving half never became replacement Avengers during those years. T’Challa stayed T’Challa, Shuri solved the problems she understood, Hank and Janet supplied the piece of science nobody else had, Strange gave them the information he genuinely knew without pretending he could see every new future, and Wanda became strong enough to take the risk nobody else could safely take for her.

Thanos erased Tony, Steve, Thor, Bruce, Natasha, and several of the people who eventually reversed the Snap in the original timeline. He still left behind Hank Pym, Janet van Dyne, Shuri, Doctor Strange, Wanda Maximoff, Captain Marvel, and enough people willing to spend 5 years finding another route.

Peter eventually leaves Wakanda with Tony beside him. Tony keeps asking questions about everything he missed, and Peter keeps realizing how much of his life now exists outside the version Tony remembers. When they finally take off, Peter flies beside him because he already learned how to keep going while Tony was gone.

scripts.title: What If Thanos Was A Sith Lord

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Thanos would still spend years conquering worlds before he ever starts collecting the Infinity Stones, but the Force would make that part of his life much more dangerous. He'd first notice it in small ways, sensing attacks before they happen or moving something without touching it, then spend years learning how far those abilities can actually go.

As his control improves, the dark side would fit naturally with the way he already sees himself. Thanos has enormous patience, discipline, and conviction, but he also carries anger and resentment underneath all of it, which gives him exactly the kind of emotions a Sith can turn into power.

By the time he begins hunting the Stones, the Avengers would still be facing the same Thanos who believes wiping out half of all life is necessary. The problem is that now he can use the Force before the Gauntlet ever comes into play.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Thanos would first notice the Force long before the events of Infinity War, back when he was still expanding his armies and conquering worlds one at a time. At that point, he already has the strength, durability, intelligence, and patience that make him dangerous without any supernatural help. The Force would begin as something he doesn’t fully understand, probably during combat when he senses an attack a fraction of a second before it happens or reacts to movement he shouldn’t have been able to see coming.

At first, Thanos would assume it comes from instinct. He’s spent years fighting powerful opponents and surviving battles most people wouldn’t walk away from, so unusually sharp reactions wouldn't immediately seem supernatural. That explanation becomes harder to accept once the same thing keeps happening. He starts receiving brief impressions of danger or hostile intent before some attacks and betrayals, although the clarity depends on his focus and the circumstances rather than functioning like an automatic warning against everything around him. He also occasionally causes objects around him to shift when his anger spikes.

The first clear sign could happen during one of his conquests when he reaches for a weapon that’s several feet away and it moves toward him without anyone touching it. Thanos would stop treating these moments as coincidence after that. He’d start experimenting privately, testing whether he can move smaller objects on command and whether concentration makes the effect stronger. His progress would be slow because he has no teacher yet, but Thanos is patient enough to keep working at something until he understands the basic rules.

That would interest him immediately because Thanos already believes strength and sacrifice are necessary to impose order. He wouldn't be drawn to the Sith because he wants chaos or mindless destruction. He’d be drawn to them because their philosophy gives him a framework for a power he already feels growing inside him, and because the idea of turning emotion into strength fits the way he has lived for years.

Finding actual Sith knowledge would be harder than finding stories about it. Thanos might have to tear through old temples, steal holocrons, interrogate people who recognize the symbols, or hunt down someone who has studied Sith teachings without necessarily being a Sith themselves. Eventually, he would need to obtain functioning instructional holocrons containing sufficiently complete teachings recorded by actual Sith masters, giving him something substantial enough to study beyond scattered legends. That process could take years, which gives his growth enough time to feel believable.

By the time he finds something useful, Thanos would already know the basics of telekinesis and heightened awareness. The Sith material would teach him how much deeper the Force can go and, more importantly, how emotion affects it. Once he starts deliberately feeding anger and conviction into those abilities, his progress would accelerate.
That’s where his path toward the dark side really begins.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: In Star Wars lore, using the dark side doesn't automatically make someone a Sith Lord. The Sith are an exclusive order bound by the Rule of Two and strict master apprentice lineages, which is why even trained dark side assassins like Ventress never officially held the title. Thanos wouldn't have a living master to formally teach or induct him into the Sith Order, but he also wouldn't care about their traditions. He would reconstruct and adopt the Sith tradition from the teachings he has recovered, claiming the mantle of Sith Lord for himself even without an official master-apprentice lineage, and mold the dark side around the way he already fights.

Telekinesis would be the first thing he seriously masters. Thanos already relies on overwhelming physical pressure in combat, so he’d use the Force to extend that pressure beyond arm’s reach. He could pull enemies toward him before hitting them, throw people into walls, drag weapons away, and pin weaker opponents long enough to finish them. As his control improves, he’d start using those abilities while moving instead of needing to stop and concentrate.

The dark side would also affect the way he handles pain. Thanos already has absurd durability, but Sith teachings often encourage using pain and anger as fuel instead of treating them as distractions. If he takes a serious hit, he could push himself harder through the Force instead of slowing down, which makes wearing him down even more difficult.

Force barriers would come later because they require more control than simply throwing something across a room. Once Thanos understands how to push outward in every direction, he could start deflecting debris, softening explosions, and blocking attacks that would normally force him to rely entirely on durability. The barrier wouldn’t make him invulnerable, especially against something as powerful as an Infinity Stone or Stormbreaker, but it gives him another layer of defense before anything even reaches his body.

Force lightning would take longer still. Thanos has enough anger and willpower to use it eventually, but it shouldn’t appear early because it requires a deeper connection to the dark side and much finer control. He’d probably discover it years into his training, perhaps during a moment where someone seriously threatens Gamora or humiliates him in battle. The first burst could be uncontrolled and short, followed by years of refining it into something he can use deliberately.

By this point, Thanos would be developing into something close to a Sith master in practice even if his training path looks very different from Darth Sidious or Vader. He’s learning through conquest, testing techniques against real opponents, and building each ability around a body that was already incredibly dangerous.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Thanos’ armies would benefit from his Force abilities almost immediately because he’d become much harder to stop in the places where he personally leads an attack. Before, a powerful defender might have been able to slow him down long enough for civilians to escape or reinforcements to arrive. Once Thanos can sense attacks early and throw people around without touching them, those encounters become shorter and more one-sided.

He could walk through defensive lines while pulling guns out of soldiers’ hands, pushing vehicles off course, and knocking groups of fighters away before they ever get close. Heavy weapons would still matter, but even those become less reliable if Thanos can feel where an attack is coming from and create a barrier before it hits.

The Black Order would adapt around that as well. Ebony Maw would probably be the most interested because his own telekinetic abilities already resemble part of what Thanos is learning through the Force. Thanos could study Maw’s precision and use that as a practical model for improving his own control, even though the source of their powers is different.

Corvus Glaive and Proxima Midnight would benefit from fighting alongside someone who can disrupt enemy formations before they attack. Thanos could pull a target off balance and let 1 of them finish the job, or use the Force to create openings while the Black Order closes in from different directions. Cull Obsidian would need even less help because his strength already makes him devastating once he reaches someone.

Gamora and Nebula would experience the biggest personal change. Thanos would still take Gamora after destroying half of her people because the core motivation behind that decision remains the same. He sees talent in her and decides to raise her as his daughter, but now he also understands that emotional attachment can create powerful feelings, and powerful feelings can feed the dark side.

That could make his training of Gamora even harsher. He might also test whether fear, anger, and pain make her stronger. Gamora’s resentment toward him would grow faster because she’d recognize that he’s deliberately pushing her toward emotions he knows she hates feeling. Nebula would suffer even more under that system. Every time she loses to Gamora, Thanos could still replace parts of her body, but he might also treat her anger as something useful instead of something to calm. He’d tell her to hold onto it, use it, and come back stronger next time. That creates a version of Nebula who is even more consumed by resentment because the person abusing her is also encouraging her to build her identity around that anger.
Thanos would probably see that possibility and still accept it. In his mind, if they become strong enough to challenge him, that proves his methods worked.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Gamora would eventually realize that Thanos is using the Force during training long before she understands what it is. He could disarm her without touching her weapon, sense attacks she thinks are hidden, and stop her movement with a gesture whenever he wants to prove a point. That would make defeating him feel almost impossible while she’s growing up because every improvement she makes physically gets answered by an ability she doesn’t have.

She’d start adapting anyway. Gamora is smart enough to learn that Thanos’ Force awareness still depends on his focus and the circumstances around him. She could rely more on misdirection, unpredictability, distractions, indirect attacks, and the environment, waiting for moments when his attention is divided instead of always trying to beat him directly.

Nebula would approach the problem differently. She might rely more heavily on technology, ranged weapons, traps, and cybernetic upgrades because those give her ways to attack from angles Thanos can’t always control at once. The fact that both daughters are trying to find ways around his Force abilities would make them even more dangerous by adulthood.

Thanos’ use of the Force would also change how he handles disobedience. If he catches a warning of hostile intent at the right moment, he could stop an attacker before they get close, making ordinary assassination attempts much less reliable without making him impossible to surprise. If he already suspects someone is hiding something, he could also deliberately try to force his way into their mind and probe for information. That would take conscious effort rather than passively revealing every rebellious thought, and a strong-willed target could potentially resist or obscure what he gets.

Gamora’s eventual decision to betray him would need to be more careful. She already understands that Thanos can read danger in the moments before an attack, so she wouldn't try to simply stab him while standing in front of him. She’d wait until she can leave his control entirely, then work against him from somewhere his abilities can’t immediately reach.

Nebula might still attempt direct attacks because her anger makes her more willing to take risks, and those attempts would probably end badly. Thanos could stop a blade in midair, slam her against a wall, and disable her before she touches him. Every failed attempt would reinforce how difficult he is to kill.

By the time both of them reach adulthood, they’d know that fighting Thanos means dealing with two separate problems at once. His physical strength can overpower almost anyone who gets close, while the Force makes getting close much harder in the first place.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Thanos would still view the Infinity Stones as the only way to carry out his plan on a universal scale. The Force makes him more powerful, but it doesn’t let him erase half of all life with one decision. His goal remains the same, so eventually all of the Sith training becomes another tool helping him reach the Gauntlet.

The Power Stone would be the first major test of how dangerous that combination has become. If Thanos takes Xandar by force, the Nova Corps would have to deal with someone who can tear through defenses physically while also throwing ships, weapons, and soldiers out of position through telekinesis. Even if he can’t move an entire capital ship casually, he could disrupt formations enough for his army to break through faster.

Once he has the Power Stone, the scale changes again. Thanos already knows how destructive it is, but his Force awareness could help him control when to use it because he can sense threats before they reach him. Instead of waiting to be hit and then responding, he could anticipate where the strongest resistance is coming from and use the Stone there first.

The attack on Thor’s ship would become even more brutal. Hulk rushing Thanos could still lead to a close fight, but the Force makes the matchup much worse for Hulk. Thanos could sense the initial charge, redirect Hulk’s momentum with telekinesis, and use Force enhanced reactions to avoid more of the heavy punches. He’d still rely on technique and strength because those are enough to beat Hulk in canon, but now he has ways to control the fight before Hulk even gets his hands on him.

Loki’s assassination attempt would also fail even faster. The moment Loki moves with the blade, Thanos could sense the intent and stop his arm before the weapon gets close. Loki’s trickery might still create a brief opening, but Thanos would be much harder to surprise at point-blank range.

The Space Stone would give him another layer of mobility that works extremely well with the Force. He could teleport across huge distances with the Stone, then use precognition and telekinesis once he arrives. That makes ambushes against him much less reliable because he can appear in a location, immediately sense danger, and start controlling the battlefield before anyone has time to adjust.

Gamora would know better than anyone how serious this is. She already spent years training against Thanos while he only had the Force, and now he’s adding Infinity Stones on top of it. Her decision to protect the location of the Soul Stone would become even more desperate because she understands that every Stone removes another weakness the Avengers might have used.

By the time Thanos heads toward the rest of the Stones, he wouldn't be entering Infinity War as a villain who only becomes overwhelming once the Gauntlet fills up. He would already be one of the most dangerous fighters in the universe before adding the first Stone, and every new one would make a direct confrontation harder to survive.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: The fight on Titan would change heavily because the original plan already depended on everyone hitting Thanos from different angles and keeping him occupied long enough for Mantis to get control of his mind. With the Force, Thanos would be much better at tracking those attacks before they fully develop. Spider-Man moving through portals, Iron Man firing from a distance, Strange opening new angles, and Drax charging in would still create pressure, but Thanos could react earlier and use telekinesis to disrupt the timing that made the plan work. Doctor Strange would probably be the biggest problem for him because Strange can alter space in ways that don’t behave like normal physical attacks. Thanos could sense danger from the spells, but knowing something is coming doesn’t automatically tell him how a portal is going to reshape the battlefield. Strange could still bind him, redirect attacks, and force him to deal with effects that can’t just be pushed away with raw telekinesis.

Iron Man would also adapt once he sees what Thanos is doing. Tony could spread his attacks out more, use remote weapons, and make Thanos divide his attention between several threats at once. That would matter because even a powerful force user still has to process what’s happening around him. The Avengers’ best chance would come from overwhelming that attention rather than trying to overpower him directly.

That could stop the Gauntlet removal attempt way earlier. Even if they still manage to restrain him for a few seconds, years of Sith training could give Thanos more mental discipline to fight for conscious control once Mantis begins affecting his mind. That might help him resist or recover sooner, but there’s no established reason that pain or anger would directly counter her powers. Mantis would still be capable of affecting him because her abilities work on beings far beyond normal humans, so whether Sith discipline meaningfully shortens her hold would remain uncertain.

Peter Quill’s reaction to Gamora’s death would still make the situation worse, although it may not be the single moment that ruins everything anymore. Thanos would probably already be close to breaking free before Quill loses control, and once the restraint weakens, a Force push could clear most of the group away from him.

After that, Tony’s one-on-one stretch becomes even more dangerous. Thanos could stop nanotech blades before they reach him, pull Tony out of the air, and use force enhanced reactions to avoid attacks that originally managed to draw blood. Tony would still be creative enough to land some hits, but the margin for error becomes much smaller.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Once Thanos reaches Wakanda, the Avengers would have even less time to stop him. By that point he has several Infinity Stones and the Force on top of them, so almost every physical obstacle becomes easier to handle.

Steve, T’Challa, Bucky, Sam, Rhodey, and the others could still rush him, but Thanos wouldn’t need to let everyone reach him. He could knock groups backward with telekinesis, pull weapons away, and keep stronger fighters off balance while walking toward Vision. Anyone trying to tackle him from the side could get caught before making contact.

Wanda would still be the most serious threat because she can attack him while destroying the Mind Stone at the same time. Her power is strong enough to hold back the canon version of Thanos even while she’s focused on Vision, so she should still be able to resist his Force abilities for at least some time.

Thor’s arrival remains the one moment where Thanos is in real danger. Stormbreaker was powerful enough to push through a blast from the completed Infinity Gauntlet and bury itself in Thanos’ chest. Force precognition would give Thanos a better chance of sensing that attack before it reaches him, which could completely change the ending. He may feel the danger early enough to move, create a barrier, or use telekinesis to alter the axe’s path before it hits center mass.

Stormbreaker is still extremely powerful, so Thanos shouldn’t casually stop it in midair. Thor has thrown it with enough force to overpower a direct Gauntlet attack, and trying to catch it with telekinesis alone could fail. The more believable change is that Thanos has an earlier warning and moves enough that the axe hits somewhere less fatal, or combines the Force with the Gauntlet to redirect it slightly.

That might mean Thor hits his shoulder instead of his chest. If that happens, Thanos has an even easier path to the Snap. He’d still be hurt badly, but the injury would be less severe, and once the Stones are complete there’s very little anyone can do before he uses them.
Half the universe would disappear again, except the Avengers would now know they came even closer to losing before Thor arrived.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: In canon, the Avengers catch him in a weakened state and Thor kills him before he can do much. A Sith Thanos might receive an earlier warning of hostile intent before they enter the room, but destroying the Stones has catastrophically damaged his body and left him exhausted. That condition would severely limit how effectively he can concentrate on advanced Force techniques, so sensing the Avengers slightly sooner does not restore him to anything close to his normal combat ability.

He might manage one brief Force push, a weak barrier, or an attempt to move before they fully surround him, but even those responses would be unreliable in his condition. Captain Marvel and Thor are still far too much for this badly injured version of Thanos, so the Garden encounter should end with him being overwhelmed and killed much like canon, just with slightly more warning. The larger change comes when the 2014 version of Thanos enters the story. This version hasn't collected the Stones yet, but he already has years of Sith training. That makes the final battle at the Avengers compound much harder because he can use the Force freely without relying on the Gauntlet.

Thor, Steve, and Tony attacking him together would still be one of the strongest combinations he’s ever faced. Thor has Stormbreaker and Mjolnir, Tony has upgraded armor, and Steve eventually proves he can use Mjolnir effectively enough to hurt Thanos.

Force enhanced reactions would help Thanos handle that pressure. He could sense Steve coming from behind, pull one of Thor’s weapons off course, or knock Tony out of the air before switching back to close combat. His double edged sword would still be useful, but he wouldn’t have to rely on it every second.

Captain America with Mjolnir could still catch him off guard at first because the sudden change in Steve’s abilities would be something Thanos hasn't fought before. Once he understands what’s happening, precognition and telekinesis would let him recover faster than the canon version did.

Thor becomes the bigger problem because both of his weapons are powerful enough to seriously injure Thanos. He could try pulling Stormbreaker away, but Thor’s control over the weapon and the amount of power behind it make that difficult. A Force barrier could buy time, but repeated hits from Mjolnir and Stormbreaker would eventually break through if Thor keeps the pressure up.
Tony would use that opening to attack from range, which once again forces Thanos to divide his attention. This would probably become the hardest fight of Thanos’ life before the portals open.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Once everyone returns through the portals, Thanos would have to deal with far more opponents than any Sith technique can easily control. He could throw dozens of weaker fighters aside, block projectiles, and sense attacks coming from multiple directions, but there are simply too many powerful people on the field for him to dominate everyone at once.

Doctor Strange would be especially dangerous because his portals and magical restraints can attack from angles that Force awareness doesn’t automatically solve. Wanda would also be a major problem, especially once she confronts Thanos directly.

In canon, Wanda overwhelms him badly enough that he orders his own ship to fire on the battlefield just to escape. The Force would help him survive longer against her because he could push back telekinetically and use barriers against some of her attacks, but Wanda’s raw power should still be enough to pressure him heavily.

Their fight could become a direct contest of control. Wanda tries lifting and crushing him while Thanos uses the Force to anchor himself, tear apart the ground around her, and throw debris from several directions. He could make her work much harder for every advantage, but if she stays focused on him, she still has the power to eventually overpower his defenses.

Captain Marvel would be another major problem because she can fly through Sanctuary II and physically overpower Thanos even when he has the Gauntlet. Force telekinesis might slow her or redirect her briefly, but she’s strong enough that simply throwing her across the battlefield won't remove her for long.
The real danger would come when Thanos gets near the Infinity Stones.

A Sith version of Thanos could use telekinesis to pull the Gauntlet toward himself instead of needing to physically reach it every time. That would make the final chase much harder because anyone carrying the Stones could suddenly feel them being dragged away. Spider-Man might manage to hold on with webs, Black Panther could fight the pull with his own strength, and Captain Marvel could probably resist it better than most. Wanda could directly contest Thanos’ telekinetic pull, while Doctor Strange could interfere with magic or redirect the Gauntlet’s path, turning control of it into another battlefield struggle rather than letting Thanos automatically drag it to himself. He would still only need one opening to win that contest.
Tony would eventually realize the same thing he does in canon...beating Thanos physically may not be enough once he gets his hands on the Stones.

If Tony still gets close enough to transfer them into his armor, Force awareness gives Thanos a better chance of noticing something is wrong before he snaps. He might catch a sudden warning from Tony’s hostile intent or the immediate danger around him and react before Tony fully pulls away, but the Force wouldn’t specifically let him sense the Infinity Stones transferring through the nanotech.
That makes the original Endgame ending much less reliable.

The Avengers would need someone to occupy Thanos while Tony takes the Stones, and Doctor Strange could be the person who creates that opening. Strange could bind Thanos’ arm or distort the space around the Gauntlet for a few seconds, while Thor or Captain Marvel keeps his attention elsewhere. Tony then has a chance to pull the Stones away before Thanos understands what happened.
Even then, Thanos could try using the Force after realizing Tony has them. He could pull Tony toward him, choke him, or drag the armor apart before the Snap happens.
Tony would have only seconds. If he manages to snap before Thanos reaches him, the result is still the same. Thanos and his army disappear, and Tony dies from using the Stones.
The difference is that this version requires much tighter coordination because Thanos has another way to interfere even after losing the Gauntlet.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Thanos becoming a Sith Lord would make almost every part of his MCU journey easier for him. His early conquests would become faster, Gamora and Nebula would grow up dealing with abilities they can barely counter, and by the time he starts collecting the Infinity Stones, he’d already be one of the most dangerous fighters in the universe without them.

The Force also fits him unusually well because Thanos has the patience to spend years mastering it and enough anger underneath his calm personality to draw heavily from the dark side. Telekinesis, precognition, barriers, and eventually Force lightning would give him more ways to control fights where he already has the advantage physically.

Infinity War would probably still end with the Snap, and it may happen even more easily because the Titan plan becomes harder to execute and Thor has less chance of landing a perfect hit with Stormbreaker.

Endgame would still give the Avengers a path to victory, but it would require more coordination than the original battle. Thanos could interfere with the Gauntlet from a distance, sense attacks before they happen, and protect himself without any Stones at all.

scripts.title: What If The Avengers Fought Gojo

sections.name: INTRO
paras: The fight would probably begin with the Avengers trying to contain Gojo before they understand what his abilities actually do. Iron Man could scan him, Thor or Hulk could test him up close, and the first few attacks would all run into the same problem because Infinity stops anything that has to physically reach him. For this matchup, the roster combines the major heroes active across Infinity War and Endgame at their established late-Infinity-Saga power levels, even if they were not all together at the same moment in canon. The Guardians of the Galaxy are included as part of that composite lineup.

That would change the way the Avengers approach the fight pretty quickly. Tony would start looking for a rule behind the barrier, Strange would focus on whether space or magic can get around it, and Wanda would become much more important once normal attacks keep failing. Gojo, meanwhile, would be learning just as much about them through the Six Eyes and would know very quickly which members of the team are actually dangerous.
From there, the matchup comes down to whether the Avengers have a real way past Infinity before Gojo starts removing their strongest options with Blue, Red, Hollow Purple, or Unlimited Void.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: The Avengers wouldn't open by throwing everything they have at Gojo because they’d have no idea what they’re dealing with yet. The conflict could begin after Gojo appears near an Avengers controlled operation and refuses to cooperate when they try to identify him. Tony would scan him, Strange would notice that whatever energy Gojo uses doesn’t behave like anything he recognizes, and Steve would keep the situation from turning into a fight while they still have a chance to talk. Gojo would probably find the whole thing more interesting than threatening, especially once he realizes how many different types of powers are standing in front of him. Things would get worse once the Avengers try to contain him. Tony could put up barriers around the area, War Machine could move into position, and Spider-Man might be sent in first because he can restrain someone without immediately trying to hurt them. Peter’s webs would stop before reaching Gojo, hanging in the space in front of him without ever making contact, and the same thing would happen when Tony fires a low power repulsor shot to see whether the effect only works against solid objects. Infinity doesn’t block attacks by absorbing their force. From the audience’s perspective, anything approaching Gojo slows as the space between them is divided again and again, which is why simply adding more speed or strength doesn’t solve the problem. Tony wouldn’t know that underlying Limitless explanation yet; his scans would only show that attacks slow dramatically near Gojo, never meet a conventional barrier surface, and don’t get through simply by adding more speed or force.

Tony would recognize very quickly that this isn’t behaving like a normal force field. There’s no visible surface, no point where the attack hits and transfers energy, and no sign that the defense is weakening after repeated contact. His first instinct would be to change the type of attack rather than keep firing harder, which is where the rest of the team starts getting involved. Thor could throw Mjolnir or Stormbreaker from another angle while War Machine fires from above, giving Tony several different speeds and masses to compare at once.
Every attack would stop before touching Gojo.

Gojo wouldn't stay completely defensive while they test him. Blue would let him pull someone out of position without having to close the distance normally, and he could use it lightly enough to avoid seriously hurting anyone while still showing the Avengers that standing farther away doesn’t make them safe. Blue manipulates space to create attraction toward a chosen point, so someone like War Machine could suddenly be dragged out of the air while Tony is still trying to understand what caused it.

Gojo would notice the same thing from the other side. Most of the team is dangerous in straightforward ways, but Strange is using abilities that don’t look anything like the physical attacks Infinity has already stopped. Wanda would stand out for the same reason once she begins using her power without throwing anything at him.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Hulk would probably be one of the first people to prove that brute force isn’t enough. If he charges Gojo and throws a full punch, the result would look almost ridiculous because all that strength still has to cross the space between them. His fist would slow before making contact, leaving Hulk pushing forward against something that never quite becomes a surface he can hit. Thor would get the same answer in a different way. Stormbreaker can cut through extremely durable targets and channel enormous amounts of lightning, but the weapon still has to reach Gojo first. Throwing it directly at him means Infinity has something approaching through space, so the axe slows before touching him just like Peter’s webs and Tony’s repulsors did.

Lightning creates a more interesting test because electricity doesn’t behave like a thrown weapon, but Thor is still directing an attack toward Gojo from outside Infinity. Gojo’s automatic defense is capable of filtering incoming threats based on properties like speed, mass, shape, and danger. Under the crossover assumption that Infinity recognizes Thor’s directed magical lightning as an incoming threat, that makes a straightforward lightning strike another poor way to get through. JJK never tests Infinity against MCU-style magical lightning directly, so that interaction wouldn’t be absolute. Captain Marvel would create the best physical test because she combines flight, speed, durability, and enough power to tear through enormous ships. She could hit Gojo from above at a speed far beyond Hulk or Thor’s first attempts, but that still doesn’t remove the space she has to cross before contact. Her momentum would keep carrying her forward while Infinity slows the final distance more and more, and Gojo would have time to respond before she ever reaches him.

That doesn’t make Carol useless. Her durability means she can survive attacks that would remove weaker Avengers immediately, and her speed makes it much harder for Gojo to casually control her position with weaker applications of Blue. If Gojo uses Red, she could be blasted backward and still recover quickly enough to rejoin the fight.

Hulk and Thor would also be difficult to put down with casual attacks, so Gojo would have to spend more effort if he wants the heavy hitters gone. Red would be useful for creating distance because it produces a powerful repulsive force, while Blue could pull them into bad positions or keep them from surrounding him effectively.

Ant-Man and Wasp would create another test because shrinking changes the scale of the attacker, but it doesn’t remove the distance between them and Gojo. Scott becoming microscopic doesn’t place him inside Infinity automatically. He still has to move toward Gojo from somewhere outside the technique, and Infinity can stop things based on more than just their visible size.

Wanda would probably be the first person on the field to stop caring about touching Gojo at all. Once the physical roster has shown Tony what doesn’t work, the fight would move toward attacks that don’t need to travel into Gojo in the same way.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: His first idea would probably be attacking the environment around Gojo rather than Gojo himself. Destroying the ground under him, collapsing structures nearby, or changing the battlefield doesn’t require anything to touch his body. That could force Gojo to move and give the Avengers more information about how he responds when the threat comes from the space he’s already standing in.

Gojo can handle that easily enough. Gojo can use Limitless-enhanced movement and spatial manipulation to reposition at high speed, and he has enough mobility to avoid falling debris or a collapsing floor without dropping Infinity. Tony would still get useful information because he can now see that Gojo’s movement is tied to the same general ability as his defense.

Another option would be saturation. Tony, War Machine, the Guardians, Thor, and Captain Marvel could attack from several angles at once and see whether Infinity has a limit on how many threats it can process. That test wouldn’t work either because Gojo isn’t manually choosing one attack at a time.
