Once the last ships are away, Loki could bring Surtur’s crown to the Eternal Flame and start Ragnarok deliberately. Thor would stay with Hela long enough to keep her from reaching Loki before the crown reaches the Flame, then leave with the others before Surtur reaches his full size.

Asgard would still be destroyed, but the people leaving it would be in a much better position than the refugees Thor remembers. Frigga would still be alive, Brunnhilde would already be with them, Loki would be fighting beside Thor, and most of the population could be gone before the destruction starts.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The next problem would be the Tesseract because Loki never brought it back to Asgard after New York. The Battle of New York never happened in the same way, so the Space Stone would still be on Earth with S.H.I.E.L.D. unless somebody deliberately moved it.

Fury would have no history with this Thor yet, so Thor couldn't walk into the room expecting trust. He could explain what the Tesseract actually is, tell Fury that other civilizations know about it, and warn him that someone powerful enough to attack entire worlds will eventually come looking for it.

Tony would probably become interested the moment he hears that the Tesseract is part of a larger problem outside Earth. His original obsession with preparing for another alien invasion grew after New York, so removing that battle changes a lot about how he develops. Thor could warn him about Thanos without trying to recreate the fear that drove Tony toward Ultron.

Steve would still eventually return, and Fury could bring the team together before their first war as a group. That gives them more time to train, but it also means they never learn to work together by surviving the Chitauri attack in Manhattan. Thor would know what each person is capable of, while this version of the team has never actually fought beside each other.

A better option could be keeping it on Earth under heavier protection while the Avengers and Asgard both know where it is. Thor would avoid pretending he knows some perfect hiding place because he doesn’t. He could make sure the people guarding it finally understand that the cube is more than an energy source.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The Mind Stone would be much harder for Thor to account for because it never reaches Earth through Loki.

In the original timeline, Thanos gave Loki the scepter containing the Mind Stone before the invasion of New York. Once Loki stays in Asgard, that chain disappears. HYDRA never gets the scepter through the aftermath of New York, and the experiments that changed Wanda and Pietro cannot happen the same way.

Wanda and Pietro could remain ordinary Sokovians unless something else changes their lives later. Ultron would also be far less likely to exist because Tony and Bruce never use the Mind Stone to complete the program, which means Vision never gets created from the body Ultron built for himself. Thor would remember all 3 of them as people who eventually fought beside him or the Avengers, yet none of them may become the people he knew.

Thanos would probably still control the Mind Stone unless he gives it to someone else. Thor never saw where it was kept before Loki received it, so there is no memory he can use to track it down. He would have to accept that one of the Stones is already somewhere inside Thanos’ reach.

The Power Stone gives him more to work with. Thor knows the Stone eventually ended up under Nova Corps protection on Xandar and that Thanos later took it from the planet, even if he never witnessed the chain of events that brought it there. He could warn the Nova Corps that an Infinity Stone will eventually come into their possession and that Thanos will want it, which may change how they handle the situation once it reaches them.

The Time Stone would bring Thor to the Ancient One instead of Doctor Strange. Strange may still be working as a surgeon at this point, while the Ancient One already understands cosmic and magical threats. Thor could tell her that someone is collecting Infinity Stones and that Earth holds at least 2 of them if the Tesseract remains there.

Thanos would eventually notice that places connected to the Stones are getting warned before he reaches them. Xandar could increase protection around the Power Stone, Earth could stop treating the Tesseract like ordinary tech, and the Reality Stone would never be sent to the Collector.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Nidavellir would be one of the last places Thor could still warn before Thanos reaches it. He remembers finding Eitri alone after Thanos forced the dwarves to build the Infinity Gauntlet and killed almost everyone else, so Thor could go there while the forge is still active and the dwarves are still alive.

Eitri would probably be confused when Thor asks about Stormbreaker years before he ever becomes king. Thor could explain that he remembers using the weapon against Thanos and that it was strong enough to reach him even when the Infinity Gauntlet already held all 6 Stones. The dwarves may still refuse to make it immediately. Stormbreaker was meant to be a king’s weapon, and Thor would be asking for it while Odin is still alive and Asgard is not yet facing the crisis that originally led him there. Thor could bring Odin into the decision and explain why preparing the weapon matters before Thanos gets anywhere near Nidavellir.

If Odin agrees, Thor could have Stormbreaker long before Ragnarok and spend years learning how it handles. The dwarves could also prepare their own defenses and make sure Thanos cannot walk into the forge with almost no warning.

Thanos could respond in ways Thor never saw the first time. He could attack Nidavellir with a larger force, target Eitri somewhere else, or look for another way to use several Stones if the original Gauntlet becomes impossible to obtain. Thor would only know how Thanos solved that problem once, and there is no reason the same answer has to survive all these changes.

When the war finally reaches them, Thor could gather the people who are still around because of what he changed. Loki would never have served Thanos, Brunnhilde would already be back with Asgard, Frigga would still be alive, and Earth’s heroes could have years of warning before their first fight with him.

Thanos could arrive with fewer Stones and still be dangerous enough to tear through most of them. Thor remembers watching him beat Hulk without using the Stones and knows how easily he killed Loki once he had control of the Statesman, so Thor would plan around everyone attacking together rather than treating the fight like his chance to settle an old score.

If Stormbreaker gives him an opening, Thor already knows what pride cost him the first time. He wouldn't stop to watch Thanos suffer or wait for him to understand who landed the blow. Thor would finish the fight before Thanos has another chance to use whatever Stones he managed to collect.

Whether that kills Thanos before the Snap would depend on what the new timeline looks like by then. Thor could prepare for the enemy he remembers, while Thanos has spent years reacting to choices Thor never made the first time. By the time they finally meet, both of them would be entering a fight that did not exist in Thor's old life.

scripts.title: What If William Afton Killed Henry Emily

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Henry Emily is one of the few people in FNAF who actually understands William Afton, the company they built together, and the machines behind everything that comes later. He’s also the person who eventually creates the FNAF 6 trap that finally brings William, the animatronics, and the whole mess into 1 place.
So if William kills Henry early, years before any of that happens, he removes one of the only people who could've figured out what he was doing and fought back.

From there, William gets control over the business, the designs, and the animatronics without Henry around to question him. Charlotte’s future changes, the Missing Children case gets harder to uncover, and William has much more room to push his experiments wherever he wants.
The question is whether that actually helps him in the long run, because once William’s own creations start turning against him, Henry won't be there to clean any of it up.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Fredbear’s Family Diner would still begin with William Afton and Henry Emily running the business together. Henry would handle a lot of the design work and mechanical side, while William would be involved with the suits, the business, and the systems around the restaurant. At this point, they'd still look like partners from the outside, but Henry would already be noticing things in the workshop that don’t line up with the work they agreed on.

It would start with small stuff. Parts go missing from storage, certain suits have been opened after hours, and William keeps making changes that never show up in the normal maintenance notes. Henry knows the machines well enough to notice when something has been moved or rebuilt, so he’d start checking the workshop more carefully instead of assuming it’s sloppy record keeping.

Eventually, Henry would find something William can’t explain away easily. William could be making unauthorized changes to springlock components, building concealed prototypes, or bypassing safety systems without documenting any of it. None of that proves he is already designing the later Funtime machines, but Henry would immediately question why William is hiding dangerous work from his own partner.

Henry would start keeping copies of records and checking what William works on after hours. He could find altered maintenance logs, sketches for concealed mechanisms, and records showing William deliberately disabled safety systems during unauthorized tests before rewriting the paperwork to hide what happened. Henry still wouldn’t know William’s full plan, but he’d now have evidence that William is knowingly putting people at risk and falsifying company records to cover it up.

Once Henry confronts him, William would understand the danger right away. Henry knows the machines, knows the company, and now has records that could expose deliberate safety violations and a cover-up to police or anyone else who starts asking questions. If Henry leaves with copies of the files, William could lose control of the business and attract serious attention before he gets much further with anything.

He could damage part of a springlock mechanism before Henry starts a late repair, then make sure Henry is the only person in the room when it fails. Another option would be setting up a heavy animatronic frame or electrical system to kill him while making the scene look like something broke during maintenance. William would pick whatever leaves the least evidence pointing back to him.

Afterward, William would be the person explaining the accident to everyone else. He could hand over maintenance records he already changed, blame old equipment, and point out that Henry was working alone when it happened. Fredbear’s is still small enough that a serious workshop accident would be believable, especially if the person controlling most of the records is also the person who caused it.

Any copies Henry kept inside the building would disappear before anyone gets a chance to look through them. William would also start searching for anything Henry might’ve taken home, because he’d know Henry was careful enough to keep evidence somewhere else.

Henry’s death gives William control much earlier than he had in the normal timeline. From here, every major decision around the restaurants, the suits, and the animatronics can move in whatever direction William wants.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: He'd keep the springlock suits in use because they’re still useful to him. If employees complain about failures or injuries, William can blame training, bad maintenance, or people ignoring safety rules. He’d know how dangerous the suits are and would still keep them around because they give him access to characters like Spring Bonnie while also giving him something the company can explain as normal equipment.

Charlotte’s life would change right away because Henry is gone before William ever kills her in the original timeline. Depending on who takes care of her afterward, she could leave the restaurant completely for a while. She’d still remember her father becoming more stressed before his death, especially if Henry had started acting nervous around William or keeping her away from parts of the building.

William would keep track of her because he’d know Henry could’ve told her something before he died. Charlotte might be too young to understand the details, but even remembering a folder, a locked drawer, or something Henry said could become a problem years later.

The Puppet also changes because Charlotte may never die outside the restaurant in the same way. FNAF never gives a definitive reason William chose to kill her, so Henry’s death does not guarantee Charlotte survives. But if removing Henry also changes the circumstances that originally put Charlotte alone outside the restaurant and in William’s path, she could stay alive much longer, which means the Puppet would remain an ordinary security animatronic for now.

At home, that would make things worse for Michael, the Crying Child, and Elizabeth. William would spend more time around the restaurants and his private projects, and he’d have even less patience for what’s happening between his kids.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The Crying Child would still grow up around Fredbear’s and still be terrified of the animatronics. William’s changes could make that fear even worse because the restaurant is now being run by someone who keeps testing things behind closed doors and has fewer people around him willing to say no.

Michael would still bully his younger brother with the Foxy mask, and his friends could still join in. Henry’s death wouldn’t remove that family problem, and William being more distracted could make it easier for Michael to keep doing it without anyone stepping in.

The birthday could still end the same way. Michael and his friends lift the Crying Child toward Fredbear, his head gets pushed into the mouth, and the bite leaves him badly injured. Whatever exact failure causes Fredbear’s jaw to clamp down, the result would still be enough to kill him. William would now control the response inside the company. Fredbear’s could close for a while, the equipment could be checked, and William could make sure the public explanation focuses on unsafe behavior around the animatronic. Any records showing how badly the suits had been maintained or changed would be easy for him to clean up before outside people get involved. The Crying Child’s death would also give William another reason to study the machines more closely. FNAF never gives a clean answer for every part of William’s motivation, so this doesn’t need to become the single reason for everything he does later. It can be one of the events that pushes him deeper into watching what happens when someone dies around the animatronics. He could take Fredbear apart afterward and look for anything unusual, but unless the machine actually shows a repeatable supernatural effect, that inspection would not give him evidence of possession yet.

Michael would be left dealing with the guilt while William becomes more focused on the restaurant. Their relationship could get worse much earlier, especially if William blames Michael for the bite while also refusing to deal with what happened in any normal way.

Elizabeth would still be younger and would spend years growing up around whatever new machines William starts building. By this point, William has lost 1 son and removed the only business partner who might've pushed back against the direction he’s taking.
That gives him even more freedom when the Missing Children case begins.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: William could still murder the Missing Children because Henry's death doesn’t remove the choices that lead him there. The big change is that William now controls more of the building around those murders.

He knows the security layout, controls access to the suits, and can change maintenance records if anything looks suspicious afterward. If he uses the Spring Bonnie suit to lure children away from the main floor, there’s nobody with Henry’s knowledge checking whether the suit was moved, worn after hours, or returned in the wrong condition.

The investigation would still be serious because children have disappeared from a family restaurant, but William would have more time to clean things up. He could change logs, move footage, and make sure certain rooms look empty before police get a good look at them.

The children might still end up connected to the animatronics after their deaths, but this is one of the biggest uncertainties in the new timeline. Charlotte may still be alive, so the Puppet wouldn’t be there playing the same role it had in the original story. The murders could still create the conditions for haunting or remnant, but without the Puppet’s intervention there is no guarantee the spirits attach to the same animatronics, in the same way, or as quickly.

If some of the machines do begin behaving strangely after the murders, William would pay attention. An animatronic could move when the power is off, react differently when he enters the room, or show movement that doesn’t match anything in the programming. Unlike his inspection of Fredbear after the Bite, this would give him repeatable behavior he can actually test, making the Missing Children cases the first clear evidence in this timeline that something supernatural may be happening.

If William suspects that effect is tied to the machines, one plausible experiment would be removing parts and testing them separately. If a piece of metal still seems to show the same strange effect after being taken out, he could compare samples and watch what changes when they’re heated, moved, or placed into something else. That would be William testing a theory, not following a process the games explicitly show him using.

If those experiments produce repeatable results, they could push his remnant research forward earlier. He still wouldn’t have the whole answer, but he’d have a reason to keep testing the possible connection between death, metal, and the animatronics.

Michael could also start noticing how strange his father has become around the restaurants. William keeps disappearing into locked rooms, takes parts from machines after hours, and starts treating the animatronics more like experiments than entertainment.

Charlotte could become important again as she gets older. If Henry hid anything outside the restaurant before he died, she could eventually find it. Even a few notes about William changing the machines would be enough for her to start asking why her father died shortly after he became worried about him. William would have to decide how much attention Charlotte is worth once she starts digging.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: As William gets more evidence that death can affect the machines, he would have a reason to move beyond modified restaurant animatronics and build something specifically for controlled experiments. That could eventually lead him toward the Funtime designs: machines able to isolate children, capture them, and give William a more deliberate way to study what happens after death. Once Baby exists for that purpose, Elizabeth would still be fascinated by her. William would warn her to stay away because he knows what the animatronic is built to do, but Elizabeth wouldn’t understand why a machine made by her father would be dangerous to her.

If she gets close while nobody else is around, Baby’s system could still activate and kill her. William would then have another case where someone he knows ends up connected to a machine. If the earlier Missing Children produced similar supernatural behavior, he could compare what happens with Baby to those cases and start getting a better picture of how possession and remnant might work.

He could move the Funtime machines underground once the project becomes too dangerous to keep around the public. Circus Baby’s Entertainment and Rental could still happen in some form, giving William a place where the animatronics can be stored, tested, and rented out without people seeing what happens behind the scenes.

Michael would eventually start connecting the disappearances in his own family with the restaurants. His younger brother dies at Fredbear’s, Elizabeth vanishes around William’s new animatronics, and his father keeps spending more time in locked facilities while children disappear from the business.

That gives Michael a reason to start looking through William’s work himself. Once Elizabeth is trapped inside Baby and the Funtimes are being kept underground, William could use Michael’s concern for his sister to send him into the facility with a specific job: find Baby and bring Elizabeth back out. Baby would have her own reason to cooperate at first, because Michael gives her and the other Funtimes access to someone they can manipulate while they look for a way out. If they eventually combine into an Ennard-like body, using Michael as a disguise becomes a practical escape plan rather than an event that happens automatically. That keeps a version of the Sister Location path possible while giving William, Michael, and the Funtimes separate reasons for entering the same chain of events.

Once Michael comes back, William has a much bigger problem. His son now knows enough about the underground facility, Baby, and the Funtime animatronics to understand that these deaths keep leading back to him.

Henry won't be there later to build the FNAF 6 trap, so Michael’s role would keep growing from this point. If anyone is going to follow William through the old restaurants and figure out how to stop what he created, Michael would have to do far more of it himself.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: By the time William has the Missing Children case and Elizabeth to compare, he could have enough examples to believe that at least some animatronics can carry something after death. He still wouldn’t understand every rule, and without Charlotte becoming the Puppet the results may not match the original timeline, but repeated supernatural behavior would be enough to convince him the effect is real.

One plausible direction for his research would be taking parts from machines that seem affected and testing them away from the restaurants. If metal from one machine still appears to react after being moved somewhere else, William could compare it with other samples and test whether heat changes the effect. Remnant and heat become important later in the series, but this exact experimental path would be William working his way toward that knowledge in this altered timeline rather than something the games explicitly establish step by step.

William would know Michael is searching eventually. He’d see missing files, opened rooms, or security systems being accessed at places only a few people even remember. That would make him more careful around Michael, especially once he realizes his son survived something that should’ve killed him.

William could even become interested in Michael’s body after the Ennard incident. Michael’s survival would be another example of someone continuing after death in a way that doesn’t make normal sense. William would want to know why, which could make their relationship even worse.

By now, William would have several different things to study at once: haunted animatronics, remnant, Elizabeth inside Baby, and Michael somehow still alive. He’d keep pushing because every answer gives him another question.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Charlotte surviving this long would give the timeline another problem William didn’t have in the same way before.

As she gets older, she’d be able to look back at what happened to Henry and compare it with everything that happened around Fazbear Entertainment afterward. Children disappear, restaurants close, animatronics are pulled from service, and William keeps showing up around every major part of it.

She might still have something Henry left behind. It doesn’t need to be a perfect file explaining everything. Even a few notes about William changing animatronics, using the workshop late at night, or keeping hidden designs could be enough for Charlotte to start digging.

She’d probably talk to old employees first. Some would remember Henry being worried before he died. Others could remember arguments between him and William or changes made to the workshop shortly before the accident.

That would give Charlotte a reason to stop believing the official story. She could eventually reach Michael too. Their lives would already be connected through the company, and Michael would have much more direct knowledge about William by this point. He could tell her about the underground facility, Elizabeth, and the machines William built there.

William would eventually realize Charlotte is involved. By then, killing her would create more attention than it would’ve years earlier. She’s older, she’s already asking questions, she has started sharing what she finds with Michael and other people, and those people know she is investigating Henry’s death. If she suddenly disappears, suspicion would point straight back toward William. That makes watching her, misleading her, or trying to scare her away safer than murdering her outright, giving Charlotte a believable reason to stay alive even after she becomes a threat.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: William’s research would eventually bring him back to the older animatronics.

If his experiments convince him that some of the Missing Children are attached to the older animatronics, he could still dismantle those affected machines and take parts from them. That preserves a version of one of the most important pieces of the original timeline without assuming the haunting developed exactly as it did with the Puppet present.

If the children’s spirits are attached strongly enough to those machines, they could still react when William dismantles them. That could put him in the same kind of situation where the spirits corner him inside an old location. He’d panic and use the Spring Bonnie suit because he knows the children associate it with him and he expects the suit to protect him or scare them off.

Michael and Charlotte wouldn't immediately know where he went. William could simply disappear from the records for years. Michael would keep checking old Fazbear properties, while Charlotte would keep tracing anything connected to Henry and the missing children. They might assume William fled until stories start coming out about an old horror attraction built from Fazbear pieces.

That brings them toward Fazbear’s Fright. Springtrap could still be found and brought into the attraction because workers searching old locations wouldn’t know what's inside the suit. Once Michael realizes what they found, he’d have a much better reason to go there personally.

The fire could still happen, but it would be Michael trying to kill William instead of Henry setting up the final plan. Springtrap could survive that fire just like he does in canon. That would be the moment Michael realizes burning 1 building and hoping William stays inside isn’t enough.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: After Fazbear’s Fright, Michael and Charlotte would know William can survive things that should’ve killed him years ago.

They'd also know that some of the supernatural animatronics or affected parts are still out there in different forms. Elizabeth is inside Baby, the Funtime animatronics have become something else, and pieces from any older machines William confirmed were affected may still exist because he spent years moving parts around.
This is where Henry’s absence would hurt the most.

Henry knew the machines, the company, and enough about what William had created to build the FNAF 6 trap in the original timeline. Michael and Charlotte would have to reach a similar solution from what their own failed attempt teaches them instead of somehow inheriting Henry’s plan.

Charlotte could use Henry’s old blueprint archives to understand the old Fazbear buildings, service corridors, and basic containment systems. Michael could contribute what he learned from the newer facilities, but neither of them would need to recreate Henry’s specialized FNAF 6 machinery.

The Fazbear’s Fright fire would give them the first part of that answer. Michael already tried burning William inside a building and learned that fire means very little if the target can escape the hottest areas or survive until the structure opens around him. Charlotte could use Henry’s old building plans to identify a much simpler solution: turn an existing warehouse or abandoned Fazbear property into a physical containment structure instead of trying to engineer another advanced animatronic system.

From there, their requirements become much clearer: bring the remaining threats to a location they control, separate them before they can interfere with each other, remove their escape routes, and only then start a sustained fire. They could modify the structure with reinforced sections and manually controlled remote bulkheads, then leak enough information to draw the animatronics there.

Michael would probably be the one inside. He already knows Baby will recognize him, and William would likely follow any sign that Michael has found something important. Molten Freddy or whatever remains of the Funtime group could also be drawn in if they think the location has parts, power, or people they can use.
Charlotte would stay outside the main trap and control the bulkheads and ignition system remotely. That would give them a better chance than putting both of them inside with everything.

Instead of simply setting another building on fire, they’d design the structure like an architectural incinerator trap. Reinforced bulkheads could seal each section, fuel could be placed around the areas where the animatronics are expected to gather, and the exits could be locked remotely before ignition so the heat stays concentrated inside. The plan would rely on simple physical containment and sustained fire rather than Henry-level robotic engineering.

Michael would still have to keep William there long enough. That could mean letting Springtrap think he finally found Michael alone. The risk would be huge because Michael isn’t Henry and doesn’t have the same control over every machine in the building. If 1 animatronic gets loose early, the whole plan could fail. Charlotte would be the person keeping the building running while Michael moves everything into place.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: William would probably reach the trap believing Michael and Charlotte still don’t understand everything he’s done.

He’d have spent years staying ahead of them. Henry died before he could expose him, the Missing Children case never fully reached him, Elizabeth became part of his experiments, and even the springlock failure couldn't finish him.
That would make him overconfident by the time Michael and Charlotte finally get everyone into the same place.

Michael would keep William inside while Charlotte seals the building. Baby and the other remaining animatronics would already be trapped in their own sections, and the fire would start once there’s no clean route out.

William could still try to break through the walls or force one of the doors open, but the building would be designed around keeping the heat inside. Michael and Charlotte would also know from the earlier fire that they need much more than a few burning rooms.

Michael would deliberately choose to stay inside. After watching William survive the springlock failure and then escape the Fazbear’s Fright fire, he wouldn’t trust a remote trap alone to keep his father contained until the building is fully sealed and burning. Michael would decide that if someone has to remain inside to stop William from finding another way out, it should be him. His body is already barely human after what happened with Ennard, and ending William and what their family became would matter more to him than escaping. Charlotte could remain outside and control the fire long enough to see the building fully collapse. William would have gotten much more time because Henry died early. His remnant research could go further, he’d have better control over the company, and nobody would be there to challenge his machines when the worst parts of the story started.
It would also create 2 people who spend years learning how to replace what Henry would’ve done alone.

Michael knows William personally and survives enough of his experiments to understand how dangerous he is. Charlotte grows up with a reason to question Henry's death and eventually finds enough of his work to help finish what he started.
William could still end up trapped in the same kind of fire, just years later and after causing even more damage.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: Killing Henry early would help William for a long time. He’d get more control over the company, hide the Missing Children case better, and push his work with remnant and the Funtime animatronics further without Henry checking what he was doing.
The timeline would change most around Charlotte and Michael. Charlotte could survive, while Michael would have to take a much bigger role once he understands what his father created.

William could avoid Henry’s original FNAF 6 trap, but that wouldn’t guarantee he escapes forever. Michael and Charlotte could eventually build their own version of the plan, and by then they'd have years of evidence showing exactly what William has become.

scripts.title: What If William Afton Never Discovered Remnant

sections.name: INTRO
paras: William Afton discovering Remnant is one of the biggest reasons the FNAF timeline gets as dark as it does. Once he realizes that death can leave something behind inside the animatronics, murder stops being only about the victims. It gives him a way to experiment, build new machines around that discovery, and eventually chase the idea that he might be able to survive death himself.

In this version, that realization never happens. William can still become a murderer, and the Missing Children can still end up possessing the animatronics, but he never understands why any of it is happening. He sees machines acting in ways they should not, notices things he cannot explain, and keeps running into evidence that his victims are somehow still present, but he never learns how to turn that into a system he can study or control.

That would change far more than William's end goal. If Remnant never becomes the reason behind his experiments, then the Funtime animatronics, the Scooper, Circus Baby’s later purpose, Michael's role, and even the events that eventually create Springtrap all have to be reconsidered. Some of those things might still exist for completely different reasons, while others may never happen at all.

William would still be dangerous without Remnant. The question is what kind of nightmare he creates when immortality is no longer the thing driving him, and whether never understanding the supernatural actually saves anyone in the long run.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: The timeline can still begin close to normal because William doesn’t need Remnant to become dangerous. Fredbear’s Family Diner still exists, William still works alongside Henry, and the Afton family can still fall apart around the restaurants they helped create. The Bite of 83 can still happen because nothing about that accident depends on William understanding possession. Michael and his friends still scare his younger brother, the prank still goes too far, and William still loses a son without learning anything useful from the death.

That loss could make William more unstable, but it should not suddenly become proof that he starts murdering people to discover immortality. FNAF has never given us one clean canon explanation for why William commits his earliest murders, so this version does not need to invent one. Whatever cruelty, anger, resentment, or need for control already existed in him can still push him toward violence. The important change comes later, when the supernatural consequences of those crimes start appearing and William fails to understand what they mean. Charlie can still become one of his earliest victims. William kills her outside the restaurant, the Puppet reaches her body, and Charlie still possesses it. From William’s point of view, though, none of that gives him a scientific breakthrough. If the Puppet later moves differently, appears where it should not, or behaves as if it recognizes people, William can explain it away as damaged programming, Henry changing the machine, or his own paranoia after the murder. He does not look at Charlie's death and think that a human soul has entered an animatronic.

That difference matters because whatever normally leads William to recognize Remnant and deliberately experiment with it never happens here. Death can happen near machinery and the machinery can become haunted, but he never identifies the supernatural connection as something he can reproduce or control. Supernatural events can happen right in front of him and he still sees separate problems instead of one system.

The Missing Children Incident can therefore still happen. William uses Spring Bonnie to lure children away from the public areas of Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza and kills them, while the Puppet helps their spirits become tied to the animatronics. Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and Golden Freddy can still become haunted because William understanding possession was never required for possession itself.

What changes is William's interpretation afterward. He may notice that certain animatronics seem unusually aggressive around him. A machine could turn its head when it should be shut down, follow him through a room without receiving a command, or react differently when he gets close. William knows enough about robotics to understand that the behavior is wrong, but every explanation he reaches stays mechanical. He checks servos, rewrites code, replaces parts, and becomes increasingly irritated when none of it fixes the problem.

Instead of seeing the murdered children as proof that death can be turned into a resource, William begins seeing the possessed animatronics as evidence that Freddy’s technology is unreliable. That keeps him dangerous, but it sends his curiosity in a completely different direction. He is still surrounded by ghosts. He just never realizes that the ghosts are the reason the machines keep coming back to life.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: William could still create the Funtime line because he is an engineer who wants more control over the business after his relationship with Henry breaks down. Instead of building them around supernatural experimentation, he builds them as a commercial advantage. They would be more advanced than the older Freddy's characters, capable of voice imitation, better movement, automated entertainment, and performing with less staff around them. William would still want machines that can manage children and crowds with very little human supervision because that gives him control over the restaurant without depending on employees.

He may even keep some disturbing features if murder is already part of his life. William does not suddenly become harmless because Remnant is gone. A hidden storage compartment or isolated capture system could still make sense for a murderer who wants an easier way to

separate children from adults. The major difference is that he has no reason to design the machines around extracting anything from their victims afterward. Killing is the end of the crime instead of the beginning of an experiment.

That would make Circus Baby especially important. William can still create her as the centerpiece of Circus Baby’s Pizza World, and Elizabeth can still become fascinated with the machine her father built. Removing Remnant does not automatically remove Baby’s child-capture machinery, especially if William still wants the Funtimes to help isolate victims. Elizabeth could still die if he builds the same lethal mechanism. For this branch, though, the Funtimes remain dangerous without Baby receiving the exact capture system that killed Elizabeth in the original timeline, because William never develops that specific design around the same goals.

Elizabeth therefore has a much better chance of surviving childhood. William can still be cold, controlling, and secretive around her, but in this branch Baby lacks the specific lethal capture mechanism that made approaching her fatal in the original timeline. Elizabeth can actually attend the restaurant, interact with the animatronics, and go home afterward instead of becoming trapped inside the machine William created.

That one survival changes the Afton family immediately. Michael has already lost his younger brother because of the Bite of 83, but now he does not lose Elizabeth to Circus Baby as well. William still becomes more distant and dangerous, yet the family does not collapse in exactly the same way. Michael has fewer reasons to spend years chasing the consequences of his father’s experiments because one of the biggest consequences never happens.

Circus Baby’s Pizza World could also last longer. In the normal story, the location closes almost immediately under a cover story after Elizabeth’s death. Without that accident, William has no reason to shut everything down after opening day. The restaurant could become a genuine competitor to Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza and give William a separate business where he controls the technology, staff, and security.

That does not make it safe. If William is still murdering children, a restaurant full of advanced machines could give him more opportunities to hide what he is doing. The difference is that he is using the machines as tools for ordinary crimes rather than as part of an attempt to understand death itself.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: The underground rental facility would probably be where the timeline begins breaking apart completely. Circus Baby’s Entertainment and Rental exists to store and rent the Funtime animatronics, but the facility is also tied to the machinery William uses for far darker work. The Scooper becomes especially difficult to justify in the same form once Remnant disappears from William’s goals because its later importance comes from more than simply repairing animatronics.
William could still build an underground maintenance facility if the Funtime business succeeds. Expensive animatronics need repairs, spare parts, storage, testing rooms, and somewhere they

can be serviced without customers watching. Employees could still work below ground while the characters are sent to parties and private events. The location would look less like a hidden laboratory and more like an unusually secure robotics workshop.

The Scooper would be the biggest change. William might still need a heavy machine capable of removing damaged internal components from a Funtime shell, but it would only be industrial equipment. It would not be designed around injecting or moving supernatural material because William has no idea that material exists. There is no reason for him to build a system whose real value comes from manipulating Remnant.

That makes Sister Location almost impossible to happen the way we know it. Elizabeth is still alive, so Circus Baby does not contain her spirit. The other Funtimes may still have advanced artificial behavior, but William has not been collecting haunted metal and using it in experiments. There is no clear path toward the same group of trapped personalities becoming Ennard, and there is no reason for Michael to enter the facility because his father tells him to find his sister. Michael's adult life becomes much less supernatural because of that. He can still hate William, especially as he grows older and begins understanding what kind of person his father really is. The guilt from the Bite of 83 also stays with him. What disappears is the direct mission that drags him into William’s underground facility and ends with him being scooped.

Without that event, Michael never becomes the walking corpse kept alive after Ennard uses his body. He stays human, which changes nearly every later situation where his ability to survive impossible injuries allows him to keep chasing William. If Michael eventually decides to investigate his father, he has to do it as a normal person who can actually die.

William would also have less control over Michael because he cannot use Elizabeth as the reason to send him somewhere dangerous. If he wants Michael gone, he would need another excuse, or he would have to confront the fact that his oldest son is starting to ask questions. That can make their relationship more direct. Michael may begin noticing missing children, closed restaurants, strange reports about the animatronics, and William's habit of disappearing whenever another incident happens.

Elizabeth could notice the same things from a different angle. She grows up around William's newer machines instead of becoming one of them, and she may understand the Funtime business better than Michael does. That gives the siblings a reason to compare what they know. Michael knows how William acts at home, while Elizabeth knows what happens around the new restaurant and maintenance facility.

William has spent years getting away with crimes because everyone around him sees separate pieces. The children disappear at Freddy's. Strange behavior happens with the animatronics. The Funtime machines belong to another company. Michael and Elizabeth are among the few people close enough to William to realize all of those events keep leading back to the same man.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The possessed Freddy's animatronics would still eventually become William's biggest problem because they are one part of the supernatural story he cannot erase by refusing to understand it. The Missing Children are still inside the machines, and their anger toward him does not depend on whether he knows why they are moving.

As the restaurants age and close, William could return to old Freddy’s locations for practical reasons rather than Remnant. He may want to destroy evidence connecting him to the Missing Children Incident, recover valuable parts, or remove animatronics that seem to react to him in ways he cannot explain. Every time he sees one of the old characters move when it should be inactive, he becomes more convinced that the machines themselves are defective.

He starts dismantling them because he thinks the hardware is the problem. Freddy goes first, then Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy. William pulls them apart and sees nothing inside that explains their behavior. There is no glowing substance, no obvious device, and no piece of machinery he can point to as the cause. All he finds are old endoskeletons, damaged parts, and decades of neglect.

The spirits can still appear after the shells are dismantled. William may see the children around the abandoned building or find himself being followed through rooms that should be empty. By this point, even William has to consider that something supernatural may be happening. He knows they resemble the children he killed, but he still has no idea what the phenomenon is, how it works, or how it could be reproduced or controlled. Suspecting that the dead are somehow still present is not the same as discovering Remnant as a usable mechanism.

Fear finally replaces curiosity. William stops trying to study the old machines and starts trying to escape them. That could still send him toward the Spring Bonnie suit because the suit represents the identity he used when he killed the children and is one of the few things in the room he knows how to use. If the ghosts surround him in the safe room, William could climb inside it for the same immediate reason as the original scene. He wants to hide and scare them away.

The springlocks can still fail. This version of William becoming Springtrap would carry a very different meaning, though. He does not enter the suit after years of learning that supernatural forces can keep people alive. He has no reason to think death inside an animatronic could preserve him. The suit fails because William makes a desperate choice while terrified, and when the mechanisms crush him, he believes he is dying.

Whatever supernatural mechanism normally allows William to persist as Springtrap can still operate here; the only thing this scenario removes is his understanding and deliberate use of Remnant. He wakes trapped inside Spring Bonnie with no scientific explanation for why he is still conscious. For the first time, the same supernatural world he spent years refusing to understand becomes impossible to ignore because he is now trapped inside its consequences.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Becoming Springtrap would finally prove to William that death does not work normally around these machines, but it still does not mean he discovers Remnant. He knows only what happened to him. He died inside the Spring Bonnie suit and some part of him remained attached to it afterward. He has no idea how to remove that effect, reproduce it, transfer it, or use it intentionally.

The decades before Fazbear’s Fright could still pass with William sealed away. The safe room is hidden, the old location disappears from public use, and William remains inside until people searching for old Freddy’s material eventually find the Spring Bonnie suit. They would have no idea that the corpse inside is still conscious, so Springtrap can still be moved into Fazbear's Fright as an attraction.

Michael's role would be different by this point because he is still alive in a normal human body. If he has spent the missing years investigating William, he may already suspect that his father vanished around one of the old Freddy's buildings. He could follow rumors about Fazbear’s Fright because the attraction is collecting objects from the exact restaurants connected to William's crimes.

Elizabeth could still be alive as well, giving Michael someone who remembers William from the same household instead of another possessed animatronic he needs to rescue. The 2 of them may disagree over how much William was responsible for, especially if Elizabeth spent more time believing their father’s explanations, but the appearance of Springtrap would give them physical proof that William never simply disappeared.

William waking inside Fazbear’s Fright would also change how he behaves. He cannot look at his condition and think he successfully achieved immortality because he never wanted this result and does not know how it happened. His first goal would be escaping the building and finding some way to separate himself from the suit. He may seek out old Afton technology because it is the only technology he trusts, even though none of it was designed to solve the problem he now has.

That could make him more desperate than the original William. He has spent his life believing every problem can eventually be controlled if he understands the machine well enough. Now his own body has become the machine he cannot explain. He could tear apart old animatronics,
search abandoned facilities, and revisit places connected to his victims looking for any clue that explains why he survived.

By the end of this stage, the timeline has reached a strange middle ground. William still becomes Springtrap, but nearly everything that normally surrounds that transformation has changed. Elizabeth is alive, the Funtimes never become part of a Remnant experiment, Ennard does not need to exist, Michael is still physically human, and William has finally been forced to accept that there is a supernatural element to what happened. He just still has no idea what that force is or how to control it.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Fazbear’s Fright would still be one of the most important turning points because it puts William back into the world after decades of being trapped inside Spring Bonnie. The difference is that he would come out of that room with no plan for immortality, no understanding of Remnant, and no idea why he survived. He only knows that the suit failed, his body died inside it, and somehow he remained conscious long after he should have been gone.

Once the attraction starts operating, William would have time to study what happened to himself in a way he never could while sealed inside the safe room. He can move the suit, react to people around him, and recognize places from his old life, but he is still stuck inside a decayed body and damaged springlock frame. The employees running Fazbear’s Fright would treat Springtrap like the perfect piece of authentic Freddy's history, which gives William access to old props, training tapes, and pieces recovered from previous locations.

Those materials would interest him because he is now looking for any connection between the old restaurants and what happened to him. He remembers the children, remembers the animatronics behaving strangely, and now knows that he continued existing after dying inside one of the suits. He may finally accept that the deaths and machines were connected, but that is still very different from understanding a usable substance behind them.

The fire at Fazbear’s Fright could still happen, either through faulty wiring or because Michael eventually decides burning the building is the safest way to destroy William. Michael would have much more reason to approach the situation carefully because he is still a normal human. He cannot walk into a burning building expecting to survive, so he would need to trap William first, make sure exits are blocked, and get out before the fire spreads.

William surviving that fire would make the situation even worse for Michael. From William's perspective, dying in the springlock suit was already impossible enough, and now severe fire still fails to remove him completely. He would begin to understand that whatever keeps him
attached to Spring Bonnie is extremely difficult to break, but he still has no way to use that knowledge on anyone else.

Michael and Elizabeth could finally end up on the same side because William returning removes the last uncertainty around his disappearance. Michael knows Springtrap is their father, Elizabeth has the technical knowledge to understand the suit, and both of them now have a reason to stop him before he reaches another Freddy's location.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Henry would eventually become the person most capable of understanding how much of the old Freddy’s history is still unresolved. Charlie was killed, the Missing Children never truly disappeared, William vanished, and stories about possessed animatronics would have followed the company for years. Even if Henry never develops a scientific explanation for Remnant either, he would have enough evidence to understand that the spirits are still tied to the machines. Michael’s investigation of Springtrap and the Fazbear’s Fright incident could also give Henry evidence that William survived inside the suit.

That could still lead to the basic idea behind Freddy Fazbear’s Pizzeria Simulator, but the trap would need a different target list. Scrap Baby would not exist because Elizabeth never died inside Circus Baby. Molten Freddy would also be extremely difficult to create because Ennard never forms through the same Sister Location events, and the Funtimes are not part of William's supernatural experiments.

Henry could instead build the restaurant around the haunted animatronics that actually remain in this timeline. Lefty can still exist if Henry designs it specifically to capture the Puppet and bring Charlie into one controlled location. Springtrap can still be lured because William would recognize another Fazbear operation as a place where old equipment, records, or people from his past might appear.

The remaining Missing Children would require more work because their original shells were dismantled years earlier. Their spirits could still be attached to pieces of the old animatronics or remain connected to whatever survived from Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and Golden Freddy, but Henry would have no perfect way to know which scattered pieces still carry them. His goal would be recovering whatever remains of the haunted originals he can identify and gathering it into one building, hoping the same fire can release whatever spirits are still attached instead of allowing the haunting to continue through another generation of restaurants.

Michael could still volunteer to run the location, but now his reason is much simpler. He’s not an undead man trying to complete a mission after Sister Location. He is William’s surviving son, still carrying guilt over his brother’s death, who has spent years watching the consequences of his father’s crimes continue. He knows William is likely to come if the restaurant looks connected to the old company, and he knows Henry needs someone William might underestimate.

Elizabeth could help from outside the building. Her knowledge of Afton robotics could be useful for identifying William's old systems, shutting down escape routes, and understanding how Springtrap might move through the ventilation or maintenance areas. Henry may not fully trust her because she is William’s daughter, but Michael would know she is one of the only people who can tell them what parts of the old technology still belong to him.

William walking into the trap would happen for a different reason than simple bloodlust. He would believe Henry has gathered old Fazbear technology that might explain his condition. After surviving the springlock failure and another fire, he would be desperate enough to search anywhere connected to the original haunted machines. If he sees Lefty, pieces of old animatronics, or records from the early restaurants, he could convince himself that Henry finally discovered the answer he never did.

Once William realizes the building is a trap, he would try to escape rather than treat the fire as another experiment. Michael and Henry would already know how difficult he is to destroy, so the building would need sealed exits and enough heat to damage both the suit and whatever remains attached to it. Michael could leave before the final ignition in this timeline because he is still physically alive and has no reason to stay behind just to die with William.

Henry may stay anyway. His connection to Charlie gives him a reason to see the plan through until the end, especially if Lefty and the Puppet are still inside. Michael surviving the fire would give the Afton family a very different ending because one son can finally walk away from the restaurant instead of disappearing with everyone else.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The company could still return years later and try rebuilding its image through virtual reality. Old circuit boards and recovered hardware may still be scanned to speed up development, especially if the company is trying to recreate old character behavior without rebuilding every system from scratch. But William does not need to survive inside that hardware for the modern story to begin.

Instead, the Mimic-era threat can develop independently of William. A system built to copy behavior can absorb Fazbear imagery, stories, and patterns associated with the murders, allowing an Afton-like persona such as Glitchtrap to emerge without literally being William’s uploaded consciousness.

That would make Glitchtrap a continuation of William’s legacy rather than another stage of his immortality. The software can imitate the rabbit imagery, manipulation, and behavior associated with him because Fazbear Entertainment keeps feeding old material back into modern systems, not because William intentionally transferred his soul into a computer.

Vanessa could still become a target because the Mimic-based program needs a human agent if it wants influence outside the game. Repeated contact with the software could manipulate her toward recreating behavior and imagery associated with Afton even though the real William is no longer directing it.

That could pull the surviving Afton children back into the story one last time, except now they are dealing with technology reproducing their father’s legacy rather than another version of William himself.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Security Breach would change heavily because the entire underground history beneath the Pizzaplex is different. There is no reason for the same remains of Circus Baby, Ennard, or Molten Freddy to exist, and the final location Henry burned would contain a much smaller group of haunted machines. The Pizzaplex could still be built above old Fazbear property because the company has a habit of burying its past instead of dealing with it, but what waits underneath would not match the original nightmare.

A Mimic-based threat could still operate beneath or through the Pizzaplex without William physically returning. If Vanessa is manipulated, she can help the system recreate Afton’s rabbit imagery and methods, making it look as though William’s influence has returned even when the thing directing her is copying him rather than preserving his consciousness.

That would make Gregory and Glamrock Freddy’s involvement easier to separate from William’s original immortality story. They are discovering that Fazbear Entertainment has once again reused dangerous technology and allowed a system shaped by its own history to turn those patterns against people.

Michael and Elizabeth could exploit that difference. Their father’s crimes created the imagery and behavior being copied, but the new threat depends on modern hardware, software, and network access rather than William’s soul surviving inside another body. Elizabeth’s technical knowledge could help trace the systems carrying it while Michael handles the physical danger around the Pizzaplex.

Instead of another fire being the only answer, they could help Gregory and Freddy isolate the relevant systems and destroy the hardware carrying the active program at the same time. That would not erase everything William did, but it could stop this new machine from continuing to reproduce his behavior.

William’s story can therefore end with Henry’s trap while the consequences of his crimes continue into the modern era. He never masters soul transfer, never uploads himself, and never creates a controlled immortality system. What survives is the pattern he left behind, copied by technology that does not need William himself to still be alive.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: By the end of this version, William still manages to create a terrible timeline, but the damage spreads in a much narrower direction. The Missing Children Incident can still happen, Charlie can still die, and the original Freddy’s animatronics can still become haunted. William is still responsible for those crimes because removing Remnant does not remove the part of him that was willing to murder children in the first place.

Elizabeth surviving becomes one of the largest changes in the entire story. She never becomes Circus Baby, which prevents the same Sister Location chain from forming. Michael is never sent underground to find her, never gets scooped, and never survives as a corpse because Ennard uses his body. Both Afton children remain human long enough to understand what their father became and eventually work against him.

The Scooper becomes ordinary industrial equipment or disappears if William never has a reason to build it in the first place. Ennard and Molten Freddy lose the conditions needed for their normal creation, which removes a huge section of the later supernatural timeline. Henry's final trap still has a reason to exist because Charlie, the Missing Children, and William remain unresolved, but the group gathered inside is much smaller.

William's own fate becomes more ironic because he still reaches the springlock failure even though he never spends his life trying to become immortal. He hides inside Spring Bonnie because the spirits corner him, the suit kills him, and the same supernatural force he refused to understand keeps him trapped inside it. Every later survival happens to him before he understands how or why.

That also changes what immortality means for him. William never gets the satisfaction of believing he solved death. His continued existence is a series of prisons. First he is sealed inside Springtrap for decades, then survives fire in a damaged body. Years later, what returns through Fazbear Entertainment’s modern systems is his image and behavior being reproduced by technology, not William’s consciousness surviving again.

His children would be in a much better position than they are in the original timeline. Michael still has to live with the Bite of 83 and everything William did afterward, while Elizabeth grows up knowing her father became a murderer. They lose family members and spend years dealing with Freddy’s, but neither of them is forced into the supernatural fate William created for them in the normal story.

The Missing Children still suffer the most because William's ignorance does not free them automatically. Their possession begins because of his murders, and their spirits may remain connected to the animatronics until Henry finally gathers what is left and destroys it. Removing Remnant research stops William from exploiting them further, but it does not undo the crime that trapped them there.

That is probably the biggest difference in the final timeline. William Afton would still be a monster, and Freddy’s would still become haunted, but the nightmare would stop expanding through deliberate supernatural experimentation. He would never build a reliable way to harvest
death, never understand why the machines are possessed, and never turn the deaths of children into a path toward planned immortality.

By the time William finally disappears for good, the story would be smaller, but it would still be recognizably FNAF. The original murders still poison everything that comes afterward, yet entire branches of the timeline never form because William never learns what is hiding inside the machines he created.

scripts.title: What If William Afton Never Had Children

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If William Afton never had children, some of the biggest events in FNAF disappear before they ever get a chance to happen. There's no Michael bullying his younger brother, no Crying Child dying in the Bite of ’83, and no Elizabeth getting killed by Circus Baby. William still meets Henry, still helps build the restaurants, and still has access to the same technology, but the entire Afton family storyline around him is gone.

That doesn’t automatically make William a better person. FNAF never gives us a clean canon answer saying his children are the reason he starts killing, so removing them doesn’t erase every path toward Charlie’s murder, the Missing Children Incident, or his later obsession with possession and Remnant. It does change the circumstances around all of those events, because William no longer has a family tragedy pushing him in any specific direction and nobody like Michael exists later to spend years following the damage he leaves behind.

The timeline would start changing almost immediately. Fredbear’s loses the exact chain of events that causes the Bite of 83, Circus Baby's story changes before Elizabeth can ever enter the picture, and Sister Location can’t happen the same way without Michael. From there, the bigger question is whether William still becomes the man behind the murders on his own, and what happens to the rest of the franchise if there’s nobody in his family left to become either a victim or the person trying to stop him.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Without Michael, Elizabeth, or the Crying Child, William's early life around Fredbear’s changes before any of the supernatural parts of FNAF begin. He can still meet Henry Emily, help develop Fredbear’s Family Diner, and work with the springlock suits because none of that requires William to be a father. Henry still has Charlie, which means the partnership is immediately more uneven on a personal level because Henry has a family tied to the restaurant while William goes home without anyone waiting for him.

The Bite of '83 disappears in the form we know completely. There’s no Crying Child terrified of the animatronics, no Michael tormenting him with the Foxy mask, and no birthday prank ending with Fredbear crushing his head. Fredbear’s can still have safety problems because springlock technology is dangerous on its own, but the specific tragedy that defines the Afton household never happens.

That matters for William because we can’t use the Bite as a guaranteed explanation for anything he does afterward. The games never cleanly tell us that William starts killing because his son dies, and the exact order of several early events has been debated for years. In this timeline, we don’t need to solve that debate because the child who could’ve been part of that motivation simply doesn’t exist.
William's relationship with Henry becomes the first major pressure point instead. Henry has Charlie, a family life, and a creative partnership with William, while William’s entire identity can

become more concentrated around the business itself. That doesn’t automatically turn jealousy or resentment into murder, but it removes the family life that would’ve occupied part of William's attention outside the restaurants.

If William still develops the same need for control, recognition, or superiority that eventually defines his canon actions, Fredbear’s gives him somewhere to express it. Henry is the other brilliant creator beside him, and every success belongs to both of them rather than William alone. Charlie also represents something Henry has outside the company, while William in this version has built almost everything important in his life around machines, restaurants, and the person standing beside him designing them.

Charlie’s murder can therefore still happen without pretending William needed one of his own children to die first. We know William kills her in the game continuity, but the games leave room around the exact personal motive behind that act. In this alternate timeline, the safest path is keeping the murder rooted in William himself rather than inventing a revenge story the canon never confirms.

One night, Charlie ends up outside one of the restaurants while William is there. The exact circumstances can differ because we're already off the original timeline, but William still gets the same opportunity to isolate Henry's daughter away from everyone else. If he crosses that line here, the first murder becomes even more revealing because there’s no Afton family tragedy we can point to afterward and say William was reacting to it.

Henry loses Charlie while William still has nothing comparable taken from him. That makes the imbalance between them much uglier because Henry is grieving a child while the person responsible can continue standing beside him as a business partner. William has now committed the act that starts the supernatural side of the timeline without losing a son or daughter of his own first.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Charlie’s death can still lead to the Puppet becoming haunted because her possession doesn’t depend on any of William's children existing. The Security Puppet was built around protecting Charlie, and her death still gives the timeline its first major example of a murdered child becoming connected to an animatronic. William may not understand what happened immediately, but the restaurant now contains anomalies suggesting that something about Charlie's death did not end normally.

That suspicion is where William’s path can begin changing more sharply. If he notices the Puppet behaving in ways it shouldn't, returning to places connected to Charlie, or responding with knowledge no machine should possess, his interest doesn’t have to come from grief over his own family. He’s a technician staring at behavior that makes him suspect something of Charlie may have remained, without yet knowing whether that is really possession or how it happened.
The Missing Children Incident can still happen after that because none of the victims need to be Afton children. William still has access to the restaurants, still knows how the mascot suits work,

and still has the ability to lure children somewhere employees or parents can’t immediately see. The absence of Michael, Elizabeth, and the Crying Child removes 3 major victims or participants from the larger franchise, but it doesn’t remove the conditions that let William target other children,

His reason for doing it can also become more focused in this version without pretending we know every thought canon William had. The first murder may begin from whatever personal darkness already existed in him, while the strange behavior around Charlie leaves him with a disturbing suspicion afterward. If something of a dead person can remain around a machine, William has a reason to test whether the same result can happen again.

That makes the Missing Children Incident more than a repetition of Charlie’s murder. William is now watching to see whether his suspicion produces another supernatural result. He uses the Spring Bonnie suit to lure the children because it gives him privacy and trust, then the murders create the haunted Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, and Golden Freddy situation that drives so much of the early franchise.

Charlie’s role becomes even more important because she can still be the one who helps give the murdered children a way to remain through the animatronics. William doesn’t control that process, and that distinction matters because the supernatural result he’s trying to understand is already developing beyond anything he designed. He knows he caused the deaths, but the exact reason those children remain active inside the characters isn’t something he fully owns. Freddy Fazbear’s Pizza still becomes associated with disappearances, rumors, foul smells, strange animatronic behavior, and eventually declining public trust. The company can cover things up, reopen, rebrand, or move locations just as Fazbear Entertainment repeatedly does elsewhere in the series. None of that requires an Afton child to keep the restaurants alive, because the company already has its own incentive to survive scandals and protect the brand. The biggest missing piece during these years is Michael. In the original timeline, Michael eventually becomes one of the people moving through locations connected to William and dealing with consequences William left behind. Here, there’s nobody in William’s family growing into that role, which means the haunted restaurants can continue without a son quietly becoming one of the few people personally invested in tracing William through them.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Circus Baby changes more dramatically because Elizabeth no longer exists to become its first major victim. William can still eventually build the Funtime animatronics with hidden mechanisms for isolating, capturing, or killing children, because those features belong to his work rather than to Elizabeth herself. Exactly when and why he develops them becomes harder to pin down once the timeline changes, but his existing murders and growing interest in the supernatural still give him a plausible route toward the same kind of project.

Circus Baby therefore becomes dangerous without ever killing William’s daughter. The machine can still be programmed to count children, wait until a target is isolated, and use the mechanism inside its body once nobody else is watching. If a child eventually gets too close, that victim
would be someone outside William's family, which changes his reaction immediately because he doesn’t have a personal daughter trapped inside Baby afterward.

That also means Baby’s personality can’t develop around Elizabeth in the same way. Any possession would depend on whoever actually dies to the machine, and if nobody dies to Baby before the facility is shut down, then Baby may remain an advanced but unpossessed animatronic for much longer. The exact outcome should follow whatever happens in this alternate facility rather than forcing Elizabeth’s story onto a random replacement child.

William’s Remnant experiments can still develop because he has already seen enough haunted machinery to know there’s a pattern worth studying. He doesn’t need Elizabeth to prove possession exists if Charlie and the Missing Children have already done that. What changes is the emotional distance, because every soul William studies now belongs to somebody else’s child.

That could make his experimentation colder rather than more personal. There’s no daughter inside Baby creating a family connection to the underground facility, and there’s no son he can later send there to deal with what happened. William can treat the entire location more like a laboratory, using rental operations and private maintenance as cover while he studies how haunted material behaves.

The Sister Location storyline as we know it disappears almost completely. Michael never receives instructions from William, never travels underground looking for Elizabeth, never gets manipulated by the Funtimes, and never gets scooped. Ennard also loses the exact escape route it used through Michael’s body, which means the animatronics need a completely different opportunity if they ever want to leave the facility.

That could leave the Funtimes trapped much longer. Employees might disappear, maintenance crews could report impossible behavior, and the facility could eventually be abandoned while the animatronics remain underneath it. William's experiment survives, but the story no longer has a convenient Afton family member walking directly into the middle of it and giving the animatronics a human body they can use.

William also loses one of the clearest people who could eventually confront him with knowledge of what he built. Michael never sees the facility from inside, never survives the Scooper, and never emerges with a reason to find his father afterward. Every secret William buries underground becomes harder for anyone outside his operation to connect back to him.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The missing Michael changes the later Freddy's locations just as much as Sister Location. We can't automatically assume every security guard associated with the games was Michael and then replace him with a random employee doing the same job, because that would erase the point of removing him. Some locations can still hire night guards, but those people are employees trying to survive a dangerous shift rather than William’s son following a personal trail.

The haunted animatronics would still attack guards because their aggression and possession don’t depend on Michael being present. Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, Foxy, the Puppet, and the other haunted characters can continue behaving dangerously around adults after hours, while Fazbear Entertainment keeps minimizing the problem to protect itself. What disappears is the larger family connection tying those nights back to William through Michael.

William can still return to an abandoned Freddy's location and dismantle the animatronics.
