His reasons could include destroying evidence, recovering haunted material for experimentation, or trying to understand the spirits more directly after years of observing them. In this version, that dismantling can also feed directly into his Remnant work: material taken from the original haunted animatronics gives the later Funtime experiments a plausible connection back to the Missing Children, even if the exact transfer mechanics remain uncertain. The children’s ghosts can still appear afterward because they’re the victims William murdered, and none of them needs Michael to lead them back to him.

That means the Springtrap origin can survive the alternate timeline with relatively little forcing. William gets cornered by the spirits near the old Spring Bonnie suit and climbs inside because it’s familiar and gives him somewhere to hide. Moisture, movement, and failing springlocks can still cause the suit to snap shut around him, trapping William inside the same technology he once used to lure children.

The important change is what happens after William disappears. There’s no Michael searching for him, no son hearing rumors about another Freddy's location, and no family member who knows enough about William's habits to suspect that an abandoned springlock suit might contain him. William can remain sealed away for years while everyone outside assumes he vanished, died, or simply escaped responsibility.

Henry is one of the few people who could eventually start connecting the pieces. Charlie is dead, the restaurants have accumulated multiple disappearances, William has vanished, and the machines continue behaving in ways Henry can no longer explain through engineering alone. Unlike Michael, Henry has direct knowledge of the company’s earliest years, access to old records, and years to compare William's access to the suits, sealed rooms, buildings, and periods surrounding the disappearances. Those records and surviving evidence can gradually point him toward William as the common link even before Henry understands Remnant, the Funtimes, or what happened underground. Every part of the case takes longer because the person who knew William as a father never existed.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Fazbear’s Fright can still discover Springtrap decades later because that part of the timeline depends more on people digging through abandoned Fazbear locations than on the Afton family. The attraction wants authentic props from the old restaurants, and eventually somebody finds the sealed room containing the Spring Bonnie suit. They bring it back thinking they’ve found the perfect centerpiece, never realizing William is still inside.
FNAF 3 changes because the night guard has no reason to be Michael. Whoever is working there could be an ordinary employee who gradually realizes the attraction contains something

alive, along with hallucinations and remnants of a history Fazbear Entertainment spent years burying. Their goal is surviving the building rather than confronting a father they've spent years trying to find.

The fire can still happen, but its meaning changes completely. If faulty wiring or deliberate human action burns Fazbear’s Fright, there’s no reason to frame the event as Michael finally trying to destroy William unless the alternate timeline earns that person separately. Springtrap surviving the fire remains possible because William’s condition inside the suit has already pushed him far beyond ordinary human survival.

Henry’s return becomes the more important late-game development. By this point, he has spent years living with Charlie’s murder, the Missing Children, the collapse of the restaurants, William's disappearance, and enough evidence to realize the supernatural consequences never ended. Once he learns William survived inside Springtrap and discovers that other haunted animatronics are still active, Henry has a reason to plan one final attempt at gathering everything together.

The FNAF 6 plan can’t work exactly the same way because Michael isn’t there to run the restaurant and knowingly remain inside when Henry sets the building on fire. Henry has to take a more direct role or build the trap so it doesn’t require a disposable manager sitting in the middle of it. That changes the entire emotional structure because Henry can’t rely on William’s son to help clean up the Afton family’s mess.

He might operate the location himself under another identity, automate more of the salvage process, or bring the animatronics in through systems that don’t require somebody continuously working inside the building. Whatever method he uses, the goal remains collecting William, the remaining haunted machines, and Charlie in one place where the fires can finally destroy the bodies trapping them.

The disturbing part is that William reaches this point with fewer personal consequences touching his own family along the way. Every child he studies, kills, or turns into evidence for his experiments belongs to somebody else, while there’s no Elizabeth trapped inside one of his machines and no Michael eventually coming back toward him. Removing William’s children erases some of the franchise’s biggest tragedies, but it doesn’t automatically erase the person who caused the others.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Molten Freddy is still one possible outcome if the remaining Funtimes eventually find another way out of the facility. They might use a technician, break through maintenance access, or escape after the underground location is abandoned and begins falling apart, but none of those routes is guaranteed without Michael giving Ennard the escape it had in canon. If the Funtimes do escape, and if William has already incorporated haunted material from the dismantled Missing Children animatronics into his Remnant experiments, they could retain that broader connection to those victims and eventually become something resembling Molten Freddy. If either step never happens, Henry’s final roster would simply have to include whatever haunted remnants actually survive this timeline instead.

Lefty can still be built because Charlie is still inside the Puppet. Henry’s entire reason for creating Lefty remains intact, and in this timeline Charlie becomes even more central to his final plan because she’s the only surviving part of his own family still trapped in the machinery William helped create. Henry isn’t just trying to destroy William anymore; he’s trying to free his daughter after decades of watching the consequences of that first murder spread through every restaurant that came after it.

Springtrap also has every reason to follow the bait. William has spent years trapped inside the suit, survived the fire at Fazbear’s Fright, and watched Fazbear Entertainment repeatedly drag pieces of its own past back into the open. A new restaurant carrying familiar technology and signs of haunted activity would be enough to pull him toward it, especially if Henry intentionally leaves clues suggesting that other possessed animatronics are gathering there.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Once Springtrap, Lefty, and whatever other haunted remnants actually survive this timeline are inside the building, Henry can finally close the trap. That could include Molten Freddy or a version of Baby if the Funtime branch develops far enough, but the original FNAF 6 roster is no longer guaranteed. The ending still has a path to happen, but Henry has to take more responsibility for the final moment because Michael isn’t there to stay behind. He either enters the building himself once everything is secured or runs the fire remotely while knowing he may never see Charlie directly before she’s gone.

| think Henry entering at the end makes the most sense for this version. He has spent years trying to understand how William destroyed his family and corrupted the machines they built together, and by this point he has no reason to keep putting the burden onto employees who never asked for any of it. Once the doors lock, Henry can stay long enough to confirm every target is inside before starting the fire from the same building.

That changes the emotional center of the ending. William isn’t being confronted by his son because Michael never existed, so the final person standing against him is the business partner whose daughter he murdered at the beginning of the entire timeline. Henry and William started together, built the earliest characters together, and now Henry is the one closing the last restaurant around him.

Charlie’s presence matters just as much because Henry finally has a chance to free her without needing to preserve the Puppet or the company that trapped her there. Lefty was only ever a container, and the fire gives Henry the opportunity to destroy the machinery binding her to the world while taking William down at the same time. If the plan works, Charlie’s story can end without Michael ever becoming part of it.

Molten Freddy and the remaining Funtimes would be harder to account for because they don’t carry the same Afton family connection. Henry still has a reason to destroy them because they're built from William’s experiments and can plausibly contain Remnant tied back to the Missing Children through the material William recovered from the original animatronics. The exact way those souls or that Remnant are distributed through the Funtimes can remain uncertain, but Henry has every reason to treat Molten Freddy as another surviving branch of the same murders rather than an unrelated set of victims.

The fire would still be aimed at destroying the physical vessels and releasing whatever remains inside them. FNAF has never made the mechanics of Remnant simple enough to treat fire like a guaranteed scientific reset button, but Henry clearly believes heat can neutralize what William has been preserving through the machines. In this timeline he’d make the same gamble because every other attempt to contain the problem has already failed.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The biggest difference after the fire is that there’s no Michael left as part of the ending. Nobody can look back and frame the franchise as a father and son story where William creates the horror and Michael spends years trying to clean it up. The entire conflict becomes much more focused on William, Henry, Charlie, and the children William murdered.
That makes William feel even more isolated. He has no family legacy attached to the restaurants, no daughter inside Baby, no son following him across decades, and no Crying Child

whose death can be connected to the beginning of his obsession. Every major supernatural disaster after Fredbear’s comes from people outside his family being pulled into whatever William decides to do.

That actually makes the alternate timeline useful because it strips away one of the biggest excuses people sometimes build around him. William can’t point to a family tragedy and say everything started because he wanted to put someone back together. Charlie dies first because he chooses to kill her, the Missing Children die because he chooses to continue, and the later experiments grow out of what he learns from those murders.

Henry would probably understand that more clearly than anyone by the end. He spent decades watching William move from business partner to murderer to experimenter while every personal loss fell onto other families. By the time the final fire starts, Henry isn’t trying to redeem William or understand what broke him anymore. He’s trying to stop someone who kept finding new ways to make other people pay for whatever was happening inside his head.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: There’s also a much larger butterfly effect on Fazbear Entertainment after William disappears because Michael never becomes a quiet link between the company’s old crimes and its later locations. Fazbear can still Keep reopening, rebranding, and burying scandals, but fewer people remain with firsthand knowledge of what William built underground or how many haunted machines were connected to him. That gives the company even more room to turn the past into rumors once Henry is gone too.

Decades later, that could make the VR era and the company’s attempt to turn old stories into entertainment even easier. Fazbear Entertainment would still have archives, old circuit boards, damaged animatronic parts, and decades of stories surrounding William, but there’d be less surviving testimony from anybody inside the Afton family. The company could dismiss even more of its own history as exaggeration because the people closest to William are either dead or never existed.

Whether Glitchtrap still appears becomes much harder to answer because the modern digital threat doesn’t have to depend on William himself literally surviving the earlier fires. Michael's absence doesn’t automatically prevent Fazbear Entertainment from scanning old circuit boards or legacy systems into the VR project, so an Afton-like digital entity could still emerge if contaminated or Mimic-related hardware and software reaches the developers. The exact identity behind that entity can remain uncertain, but the path becomes less personal and more corporate, with Fazbear accidentally recreating or importing a threat because it keeps recycling material it should have left buried.

Vanessa could still become a target because she has no connection to the Afton family and doesn’t need Michael to exist. If an Afton-like Glitchtrap entity survives into the digital era, it can still manipulate somebody completely outside William's original family and create another generation of victims through the company that refuses to stop reopening. That makes the pattern even darker because the threat can keep using new people even after every personal connection from William's original life is gone.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: Charlie’s murder can still happen because nothing about that crime requires William to be a father. The Missing Children Incident can still follow if William independently becomes interested in what happens after Charlie possesses the Puppet, and Remnant experimentation can grow from the same discovery once William realizes dead children are somehow remaining inside machines. That gives the supernatural side of the franchise a path forward without pretending one of William's children secretly caused everything.

Springtrap can still exist because the ghosts William murdered can still corner him and force him toward the Spring Bonnie suit. Fazbear’s Fright can still uncover him decades later, and Henry can still eventually build a final trap once he understands enough of what William became. The difference is that Henry has to finish the story without Michael standing beside him, which puts the entire ending back onto the 2 men who built the original restaurants and the daughter whose murder pushed the timeline into something neither business partner could ever control.

William himself becomes harder to excuse in this version. There’s no dead son people can use to explain his first murder, no Elizabeth trapped inside Baby to motivate his experiments, and no family tragedy forcing him toward the supernatural. If he still becomes obsessed with Remnant and immortality, that obsession grows out of what he chooses to investigate after killing other people’s children.

That also means the alternate timeline could end up feeling colder than the original one. William has fewer personal attachments, fewer people close enough to challenge him, and nobody like Michael who can survive long enough to keep following him across multiple locations. The restaurants still become haunted, but the Afton family stops being the center of the tragedy because there is no Afton family left beyond William himself.

A childless William probably creates fewer specific tragedies because Michael, Elizabeth, and the Crying Child never suffer any of the things attached to them in canon. It doesn’t automatically save Charlie, the Missing Children, Henry, or anyone else William eventually targets, though, and it may leave William even more isolated once he starts treating death and possession like problems he can study.

The final answer is that removing William’s children would completely reshape FNAF, but it wouldn't remove the person responsible for most of its horror. If William still chooses murder, the tragedy survives without the Afton family around him, and this time there’s nobody from his own bloodline left to follow behind him and clean up what he created.

scripts.title: What If William Afton Was Never Springlocked

sections.name: INTRO
paras: William Afton’s springlock failure is the moment that turns him into Springtrap and locks him away for decades. By the time anyone finds him again, Fazbear Entertainment has changed, Michael has spent years searching for answers, and William is barely human anymore.
This time, the suit never goes off.

William still ends up cornered by the spirits of the children he killed, and he still climbs into Spring Bonnie because he thinks the suit will protect him. But when nothing happens, he now knows the children are still there, that death didn’t get rid of them, and that whatever is inside those animatronics can survive long after the bodies are gone.

Instead of spending the next 30 years trapped behind a wall, William walks out of that restaurant alive with proof that possession is real and more time to figure out how it works. He can keep experimenting, keep covering his tracks, and keep moving while Michael and Henry still have no idea where he is.
And without Springtrap ever existing, almost everything that comes later would have to happen differently.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: The timeline would stay the same right up until William is cornered in the old Freddy’s safe room. For this timeline, we’ll place Michael’s trip to Circus Baby’s underground facility and the Scooping Room shortly before William’s final return to Freddy’s, since the games do not establish that ordering cleanly enough to treat it as certain. William sends Michael there, then leaves to dismantle the Freddy’s animatronics before he knows what happened to his son. William has already dismantled the original animatronics, the spirits of the Missing Children are still there, and they force him back toward the Spring Bonnie suit he used years earlier. William climbs inside because he knows the children remember that suit and expects it to give him enough protection to get past them.

This time, the springlocks hold. A believable reason is that William had already been handling the suit while stripping the building, and he noticed how dangerous the damp safe room had become before putting it on. He could clear and dry the mechanism as much as possible, then move away from the section of the ceiling where water is dripping directly onto the suit before climbing inside. The room would still be damp, the suit would still be dangerous, and William would still be taking a huge risk, but the mechanism never gets the direct moisture exposure that triggers the full failure in the original timeline.

The important part for William is what happens before he gets out. He has now seen the children’s spirits directly, and there is no way to explain them away as malfunctioning animatronics anymore. They appear after he dismantles the machines, recognize him, and react to him as the person who killed them. William would be terrified in that moment, but once he realizes the suit is staying together, that fear would turn into curiosity very quickly.

He would leave the safe room with a completely different understanding of what he had been studying. Before this, he could connect strange behavior to the animatronics and to whatever remained inside the metal, but now he knows the victims can continue even after their bodies and machines are damaged. That gives him a much clearer reason to keep digging into Remnant instead of treating possession like something he only half understands.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: William would return to the dismantled animatronic parts because that room just proved something he had spent years trying to understand. He wouldn't go back and rebuild Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy as if nothing happened, but he could take specific pieces from the endoskeletons and keep them somewhere private where the spirits can’t surround him as easily. His experiments would become more controlled from this point, even if the results are inconsistent. He could take metal from one haunted animatronic and place it into a separate frame with new motors and clean wiring, then compare the movement against a normal piece built the same way. If the haunted metal repeatedly reacts differently, William gets a stronger sign that whatever remains after death can move with the material itself, even if he still cannot predict exactly when or why it happens.

Heat would become part of the testing too because later FNAF material connects Remnant to metal and temperature. William could start with simple changes, heating samples enough to look for changes without immediately destroying them, then cooling them and repeating the tests. Some attempts might do nothing while others produce noticeable differences, so he wouldn’t suddenly understand every rule. He would be building a record of patterns and working theories instead of getting a clean formula.

The biggest discovery could come if he moves a haunted piece into a machine that had never been involved in a death and eventually sees that machine behave differently after the transfer. One result would not prove a universal rule, but repeated reactions would give William something he can keep testing. He could begin to suspect that the effect can be carried from one body into another through the metal instead of assuming another murder has to happen inside each machine.

Michael would have no idea William is still active yet, but William would already be thinking about him. After surviving the safe room, William could return to the underground facility to check what happened to Michael and find that Ennard has escaped. He could inspect what was left behind: the Scooper, its Remnant system, and whatever operational records survived. If those traces show that the machine was used on Michael, and William later observes that his son is still walking around after an event that should have killed him, the connection would be impossible for him to ignore. Michael becomes one of the strangest examples William has ever seen, and studying what happened to him might teach William even more than another piece of haunted metal.

That gives William a new target for his research without forcing him into another abandoned restaurant. He can keep working from hidden facilities, old company spaces, and whatever equipment Fazbear Entertainment has already forgotten about while staying far away from the spirits that almost trapped him.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Michael’s search for William would change because his father never vanishes into a sealed safe room. After Sister Location, Michael already knows the underground facility was connected to William, knows Elizabeth was inside Baby, and knows his own body survived something that should have killed him. If William is still moving around, Michael would start finding evidence that somebody is actively cleaning up behind him.

The first sign could be an old workshop Michael remembers from childhood. He goes there expecting abandoned equipment and finds that parts have been removed recently, storage has been emptied, and certain records are missing while older junk is left behind. That would tell him the place was not simply cleared years ago because someone chose exactly what to take. Michael could start checking other locations tied to William and Fazbear Entertainment. At one site he might find a new lock on a room that was supposed to be abandoned, while another has power running to a section nobody uses anymore. He wouldn’t immediately know where William is living or what he is doing, but the pattern would be enough to show his father never really stopped.

William would notice Michael eventually because the same old facilities keep getting disturbed after he leaves them. A cabinet he locked gets opened, a file he left behind disappears, or a security system logs someone entering with knowledge of a code only family or senior staff would know. William would quickly realize Michael is following him rather than stumbling into these places by accident.

That would change how William handles his son. He knows Michael survived Ennard, so simply assuming he can kill him once and move on would be stupid. He could start feeding Michael false trails instead, leaving behind records that point toward empty properties or old machines that have nothing to do with his current work.

Michael could follow one of those trails and realize too late that it was planted. A facility that looks promising might contain just enough recent activity to make him think William was there, but all the useful equipment is already gone. The only thing William leaves behind is proof that he knows Michael is searching.

From that point on, their relationship becomes more direct without requiring them to meet face to face. Michael starts treating every clue like it might be bait, and William starts moving equipment sooner because he knows his son is getting closer. The search would stop feeling like Michael digging through the past and become a fight over who can read the other person first.

William could also start watching Michael from a distance. He would want to know whether Michael’s body is still changing, whether he still reacts to injuries normally, and whether whatever kept him alive can be reproduced. Michael may think he is hunting William while William is using that search to study him in return.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: William would also change the way he deals with haunted locations after what happened in the safe room. He now knows the spirits can recognize him even after their animatronics are dismantled, so walking into another building full of possessed machines becomes a risk he no longer needs to take himself.

The company’s habit of reopening, rebranding, and reusing old pieces would help him. Fazbear Entertainment keeps dragging its own history forward, which means old animatronics, spare parts, costumes, and maintenance equipment continue moving between locations instead of being destroyed. William could take advantage of that without needing official control of the company anymore.

He would also become much more selective about what he keeps. Anything tied strongly to one of the children could be stored separately so several spirits are never concentrated in the same room around him again. He could work with small amounts of haunted metal instead of rebuilding full animatronics and waiting for them to wake up.

William might even try controlled exposure on himself, starting with amounts small enough that he expects to survive if the result goes wrong. He would be far more careful than someone chasing immortality blindly because he now knows the material can carry consciousness and that bringing the wrong thing into his own body could give him a problem he cannot remove. The results could be inconsistent. He might notice that some injuries seem to heal differently or that he tolerates damage better after certain exposures, while other attempts produce no obvious benefit at all. That does not mean he becomes immortal overnight. William would keep pushing because he has already seen Michael survive death, Elizabeth continue inside Baby, and the Missing Children remain active long after their murders.
Springtrap never gets created because William has no reason to put himself back inside that thing unless everything else fails.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Fazbear’s Fright could still be created years later because the people behind the attraction are looking for authentic material connected to the original Fazbear restaurants and the darker history surrounding them, whether William became Springtrap or not. That search could lead them back to abandoned buildings and eventually the old Freddy’s safe room as they collect props, recover old arcade cabinets, and bring in pieces of animatronics to make the place feel authentic.

What they would not find is William sealed inside Spring Bonnie. The safe room could still be discovered, but instead of finding Springtrap, the workers might find evidence that someone had been there long after the restaurant closed. Missing animatronic parts, moved equipment, an opened maintenance area, or old notes that do not match the company’s official records could become part of the attraction because the owners think it makes the story creepier.

Michael would hear about Fazbear’s Fright because the attraction is built around the same history he has been following for years. He could take the security job for the same basic reason he gets involved with other Fazbear locations: it gives him access to old material and a chance to see whether anything connected to William appears.

The building would still be dangerous because the attraction is full of old parts tied to haunted locations. The Phantom animatronics could still work as hallucinations or supernatural effects around the pieces being collected there, depending on how much haunted material the owners actually bring into the building. Michael would be walking through a place built from the remains of the same history he has been chasing.

The real discovery would come from something the owners found in the safe room. Michael could recognize a maintenance note written in William’s style, a modified part that matches equipment from the underground facility, or a list of serial numbers tied to machines William had moved after the original Freddy’s closed. None of that tells him where William is now, but it proves his father returned to those old locations after the murders.

William would learn about Fazbear’s Fright too. A public attraction built around Fazbear history is exactly the kind of place that could accidentally expose something he left behind, so he would have a reason to visit or send someone in before opening night. He could try to recover one piece of evidence without revealing that he is still alive.

If the attraction still burns, William could even use the fire to his advantage. Any records or equipment he cannot recover could disappear in the damage, and people would assume the blaze destroyed whatever strange evidence the attraction had collected.
Michael would leave the fire knowing his father had been active much more recently than he thought.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: After Fazbear’s Fright, William would stop treating Michael like someone he can mislead forever. Michael has now followed enough of the trail to connect the old restaurants, the underground facility, and the equipment William moved after the Missing Children animatronics were dismantled. William would know that another mistake could give Michael something solid enough to take to Henry.

That possibility would bother him more than Michael alone. Henry understands the machines and the company in a way Michael never will, and if Michael brings him evidence that William is still alive and still moving haunted equipment, Henry could start putting together pieces he missed years earlier.

William could try getting ahead of that by approaching Henry indirectly. He might send old company documents anonymously, feed him a false location, or make it look like someone else has been stealing Fazbear equipment. The goal would be to keep Henry looking at the wrong part of the story while William moves whatever he still needs.

Henry would eventually notice inconsistencies in those records. A part number could belong to an animatronic that was supposedly destroyed years earlier, or a maintenance form could include changes only William would have understood. Henry would start comparing the new material against his own records and realize somebody with old company knowledge is still active.

Michael could then bring him the pieces he found at Fazbear’s Fright. The info from the attraction would line up with Henry’s records closely enough that William stops looking like a dead man from an old case and starts looking like someone who has been working in the background for years.

That would be the first time William has 2 people chasing the same trail from different directions. Michael knows the underground facility, Elizabeth, and what William did to him personally. Henry knows the older restaurants, the springlock suits, and the company history William spent years manipulating.

William would respond by moving his research again, but this time he would leave something behind on purpose. He could abandon a small amount of haunted material in a place Michael is likely to find, knowing Michael will take it to Henry because neither of them wants it sitting loose. The sample would be bait in a different way than William’s earlier false locations. He would watch what Henry does with it, which machines he brings near it, and whether Henry understands enough about Remnant to become useful.

By the time Henry realizes he is being watched, William could already have learned something from the reaction. He would know whether Henry is preparing to trap him, whether Michael is working with him directly, and how close either of them is to understanding the experiments that kept Michael alive.

FNAF 6 would start taking shape from there, but Henry's goal would be larger than trapping William alone. Elizabeth would still be active through Baby, the spirits tied to the Missing Children would still need to be dealt with, and Charlotte would still be part of the haunted history Henry wants to end. He could build the restaurant around the same broader idea of drawing the remaining haunted entities and material into one controlled place so the fire can release what is still trapped there. William is the exception. Because he is still a living, cautious man instead of Springtrap, Henry cannot rely on the same salvage bait to bring him in. William can recognize a suspicious restaurant, refuse to enter, and send somebody else to check it first, so Henry and Michael would need a separate layer of bait designed specifically around his Remnant research.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Henry would realize pretty quickly that William is trying to study him just as much as Michael is trying to track William. The Remnant sample left behind after Fazbear’s Fright would make that obvious once Henry compares it with his own records and sees that it was placed where Michael was likely to find it.

Instead of chasing the next location William leaves behind, Henry could spend time testing the sample with Michael before trying to bait William. Henry already understands Fazbear machinery, while Michael can describe the Scooper, the underground facility, and what happened to his body after Ennard. By combining that with repeated tests on the sample, they could learn a few genuine reactions without fully understanding Remnant itself. Once Henry can reproduce enough of those real effects, he could use them to build a false breakthrough. He and Michael would make it look like they had figured out how to move Remnant into a new body without losing the effect. Most of what William inspects would be real machinery and real reactions; the staged part would be how close Henry claims they are to solving the same problem William had spent years working on.

Michael would help sell it by moving equipment between old Fazbear properties where William already knows how to watch him. He could deliberately let William see certain machines, then take them somewhere Henry controls. William would assume Michael is being careless because he finally thinks he has something important.

The part William cannot check from outside would be the machine holding the sample. Henry could keep it deeper inside the building and only run the decisive test while Michael is physically connected to the setup, making the reaction impossible to measure properly from a distant camera or by sending somebody else inside. William would eventually see enough of the machine reacting to know that something real is happening, but the readings, sample, and connection to Michael would only be available inside.

That would be enough to make entering the building a calculated risk instead of simple curiosity. William has already spent years wondering why Michael survived the Scooping Room, and Henry would be presenting what looks like the first chance to directly measure that survival against a controlled Remnant transfer. If William wants the sample and the readings for himself, he has to get close enough to inspect the apparatus while the effect is happening.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: William would enter the building only after watching it long enough to convince himself Henry is hiding research instead of setting a trap. He would keep close to the exits at first, check every room before moving deeper, and pay attention to anything that looks too deliberate. Henry would let him do that because the outer sections are supposed to look ordinary.

Michael could be waiting near the machine Henry wants William to see. He would show him pieces from older animatronics, notes from the Remnant sample, and a test frame that reacts in a way William recognizes from his own experiments. That would get his attention because the setup would use real haunted material and real results, even if Henry is exaggerating how much he understands.

William still wouldn't touch the machine right away. He’d look at how it’s powered, where the sample is mounted, and what Henry changed from a normal Fazbear frame. If the whole thing was fake, William would probably see through it within minutes, so Henry would need enough real work behind the setup to make the result believable.

Michael could then show him a second frame that failed during an earlier test. The metal around the sample housing might be scorched, with a few parts taken from an old Funtime system and others pulled from a standard Fazbear endoskeleton. William would recognize enough of the hardware to know Henry has been trying to combine different pieces instead of just storing them.

Michael could tell him the earlier tests were done in another room because the first machine overheated. William would follow because failed experiments would be just as useful to him as successful ones. The further he goes, the less direct his route back to the entrance becomes, but nothing around him would feel like a trap yet.

Inside the next room, William could find the damaged frame and start taking it apart himself. He might notice Henry stopped the heating process earlier than he would have, then explain that the effect was probably still present when they shut it down. Michael wouldn’t need to ask many questions because William would keep talking once he is focused on the work.

He could also realize that one of the samples came from the material he intentionally left behind for Michael to find. That would tell him Henry and Michael have been studying exactly what he wanted them to study, which would make him more confident that he is watching their progress rather than being led somewhere.

Michael could bring up his own condition at that point and ask whether the same thing keeping the sample active is what kept him alive after Ennard. William might avoid giving him a full answer, but he could say enough to make it obvious he has been thinking about Michael's body for years. He might point out that Michael's survival lasted far longer than a normal Remnant reaction should, which would confirm that William has been watching him much more closely than Michael realized.

That would change the mood between them without stopping William from looking through the equipment. Michael finally gets proof that his father treated his survival like another experiment, while William is still trying to understand how Henry got this far without him.

Henry could be listening from another part of the building and recording everything William says. William would end up confirming details about heat, transfer, and Michael’s survival that Henry never knew for certain before.

By the time William realizes the conversation has gone on too long, he would already be several rooms inside. 1 door behind him could lock without making much noise, while another remains open farther ahead so he doesn’t immediately notice the path changing.
William would finally turn back when something about the room stops making sense. Maybe a door he left open is closed, or a light near the entrance has gone dark.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: William would go straight for whatever can still get him out. He knows Henry well enough to understand that the building will have backup systems, so breaking one control panel would not solve everything. He would look for power lines, door motors, ventilation controls, and any section that lets him get around the locks instead of wasting time trying to force the main exit. Michael would have to keep him away from those systems while Henry closes the remaining routes from outside. William is still human, but he knows the building and the kind of machinery Henry would use better than almost anyone else. If he gets enough time, he could find something Henry missed.

William could also use Michael against him without pretending he suddenly cares about repairing their relationship. He could bring up Elizabeth, the Crying Child, or Michael’s survival after Ennard because he knows those are the questions Michael has carried for years.
The point would be distraction. Every second Michael spends listening gives William another chance to reach a panel or open a maintenance route.

Michael would understand that once William starts talking more than he ever did when Michael was actually looking for answers. He could stop responding and keep forcing him away from the exits instead.

The fight would become physical once William realizes talking is not working. He could still hurt Michael badly, especially because Michael’s body has already been damaged by everything that happened underground. Michael’s ability to keep moving after injuries would help him survive, but it would not make the fight easy.

Henry would start the burn while William is still trying to reach the controls. The fire could begin in several sections at once so William cannot simply run toward the part of the building that has not caught yet.
William would realize quickly that Henry is using heat because he knows what it does to Remnant.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: William’s experiments might keep him moving through the initial injuries longer than Henry expects.

If he had spent years exposing himself to small amounts of Remnant, his body could survive injuries that would normally stop someone much sooner. He might still be able to stand after severe burns or keep forcing doors after Michael thinks he should be down.

The fire would also show the limit of everything William learned. His body is still failing as the temperature rises, and any advantage the Remnant gave him would start disappearing as sustained heat damages and neutralizes its effect.

Michael could reach the final exit while William is still trying to follow him. Henry would keep the door open long enough for Michael to get through, then close it before William reaches the other side.
William would be left inside without Spring Bonnie, without another body to hide inside, and without enough time to rebuild anything.

He could keep moving until the building starts coming apart around him, but there would be nowhere left to go. The same man who spent years using abandoned rooms, hidden workshops, and old company buildings to stay ahead of everyone would finally be trapped in one he cannot leave.

Henry would not treat his own survival as automatic. His guilt over Charlotte, the company, and everything his creations helped enable could still leave him prepared to remain nearby when the fire starts, just as he would have in the original timeline. Michael, however, has spent years actively working beside him in this version of events, and once William and the remaining haunted material are contained, Michael could refuse to let Henry turn the plan into a suicide. Henry would ultimately leave with him because neither of them needs to stay inside for the fire to work. Once the structure is gone, they could go through whatever remains and make sure the haunted material William collected was destroyed instead of letting it get moved into another Fazbear location again.

William avoiding the springlocks would still have helped him for years. He would learn more about Remnant, keep control of his own movements, interfere with Michael’s search, and get much closer to understanding why death does not work normally around the animatronics.

It also means he never becomes Springtrap. When Henry finally gets him into one place, William has no suit keeping his body together after the fire and no decades of supernatural survival already built into him. All the extra time he gained would only make the final trap harder to build.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: William would probably get closer to the immortality he wanted by avoiding the springlock failure. He would have years to test Remnant properly, study Michael’s survival, and learn from the spirits instead of sitting behind a wall unable to do anything.
But staying human would leave him with 1 weakness he never had as Springtrap. Once Michael and Henry finally get him somewhere he can't escape, his body can still fail.
So avoiding the springlocks would make William more dangerous for most of the timeline, but it would also give Henry and Michael a version of him they could actually finish.

scripts.title: What If YOU Became A Viltrumite

sections.name: INTRO
paras: If you became a Viltrumite, the first thing you’d probably think about is the power. You could fly, move faster than any normal person could react, survive injuries that should kill you, and eventually become strong enough to fight people who can level cities.

The part you wouldn't be ready for is how dangerous your own body becomes the second those abilities kick in. You’d still have the instincts of a normal human, except now grabbing a door too hard can tear it off, trying to catch yourself can crack concrete, and your first attempt at flight could send you through a wall before you even understand how you moved.

That would happen after a GDA accident leaves you critically injured and doctors use experimental treatment built from recovered Viltrumite biological material to keep you alive. The treatment works far better than anyone expected, because instead of just healing you, it starts rebuilding your body around Viltrumite genetics.

By the time Cecil realizes what happened, you're no longer a normal human with a few new abilities. Your body is becoming functionally Viltrumite, rapidly developing the same strength, durability, healing, and flight that makes people like Mark and Nolan so dangerous, while the full extent of the transformation is still unknown.
And now you have to learn how to live with all of it before the Viltrumite Empire finds out you exist.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: You'd still be completely human when the accident happens. The GDA is cleaning up the remains of a Viltrumite fight outside the city, and most of what's left has already been moved into containment by the time you get caught near the site. A damaged transport unit fails while you're close enough to take the blast, leaving you with internal injuries the medical team doesn’t think you're going to survive.

Cecil doesn’t have some finished procedure waiting to turn humans into Viltrumites. What the GDA has is preserved Viltrumite tissue, experimental regeneration technology, and doctors willing to combine them in an emergency treatment because every normal option has already failed. The tissue is only supposed to help your body repair the damage long enough for the surgeons to stabilize you, but something unprecedented happens when the experimental regeneration process begins integrating the Viltrumite material. Instead of remaining foreign tissue, it starts progressively rebuilding your cells around Viltrumite genetics, something neither the GDA nor Viltrumite biology has ever been shown to do to an adult human.

You wake up hours later feeling better than someone in your condition should. The internal bleeding has stopped, fractures are already closing, and the tissue damage around your chest is repairing faster every time the doctors scan it. Everyone assumes the treatment worked unusually well until the healing keeps going after the injuries are gone.

Your blood starts changing first. The next set of samples no longer looks like a human body carrying foreign cells, and the doctors repeat the test because they think something contaminated the equipment. The second sample comes back the same, then the third shows that more of your tissue is beginning to resemble the Viltrumite material they used during surgery.

You wouldn't understand how serious that is until you reach for the rail beside your bed and bend it around your hand. You pull away too quickly, tear the metal loose, and send part of it into the wall while everyone in the room backs up at once. You still feel like yourself, but the distance between what you intend to do and what your body actually does has suddenly become enormous.

Cecil has you moved into a reinforced room before you’re even comfortable standing. He tells you the GDA doesn't know exactly what the treatment did, only that the change is continuing and stopping it might be impossible without killing you. When you ask whether you're still human, he avoids giving you an answer until another round of testing confirms what he was already worried about.
Your body is becoming increasingly Viltrumite, and the abilities appearing so far suggest the change may eventually reach far beyond what the GDA can confirm this early.
That choice is what brings Mark Grayson into the room the next morning.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Mark would expect the strength to be the first thing you struggle with because he remembers what it felt like when his own powers started developing. He’d quickly realize your situation is worse. Mark grew into Viltrumite biology naturally and had years of ordinary movement behind him before the powers fully arrived, while your body changed in a matter of days and now expects you to understand force you've never had before.

He starts by making you do boring things. Pick up a cup without crushing it, open a door without ripping the handle off, catch a ball without flattening it, sit down without cracking whatever is underneath you. You'd probably get frustrated because you know you're capable of lifting far more than any of those objects, but Mark keeps you there until your hands stop destroying everything they touch.

The first real scare happens when one of the GDA technicians drops a metal case behind you. You turn without thinking and move fast enough to cross the room before you even register what you're doing, catching the case before it hits the floor. The case survives, but you don’t stop where you meant to and end up driving your shoulder through the wall behind it.

That's when speed starts feeling more dangerous than strength. You can decide to move somewhere and arrive before your brain has fully processed the distance, which means reacting normally is suddenly enough to send you across a room. Mark stops treating the training like a strength lesson and starts teaching you how to slow yourself down before every movement becomes a collision.

You'd also discover durability by accident instead of letting Cecil shoot you on the first day. During one of those speed drills, you miss a turn and hit a reinforced support hard enough to bend it around your body. The impact makes enough noise to bring everyone running, but you come out with a shallow cut across your shoulder and a bruise that starts fading while the medical team is still checking you.

The healing becomes harder to ignore once Cecil asks whether you're willing to test it properly. You agree because you need to know what happens if you’re hurt somewhere Mark isn’t around to help, and the doctors make a controlled cut deep enough to require stitches on a normal person. The wound starts closing before they finish cleaning it, and within minutes the skin is already pulling back together.

You'd probably spend that night touching the spot and trying to find where the cut was. The strength and speed can still feel like abilities you switch on by moving differently, but healing happens without asking you. Your body has stopped behaving like the one you grew up with even while you're lying still.
By the next morning, you ask Mark to teach you how to fly!

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Mark takes you somewhere far enough from the city that a bad landing won't put anyone else in danger. He explains what flying feels like as simply as he can, but most of it sounds useless until your feet actually leave the ground. There’s no muscle you can consciously tighten and no normal human movement that produces the effect, so the first few minutes are mostly you lifting a few inches, panicking, and dropping back down.

The first time you really get it, you go far higher than Mark intended. You focus on moving upward, your body responds much harder than it did during the earlier attempts, and suddenly the field underneath you looks much smaller than it should. You stop trying to rise, but stopping the thought doesn’t immediately fix your momentum and you keep climbing long enough for the ground to disappear behind cloud cover.
That's when the fear hits. Your body can survive the fall, but every instinct you've had your entire life is screaming that there’s nothing underneath you and you need to find the ground.
You try correcting too quickly, rotate sideways, and start falling while making the exact kind of panicked movements Mark told you would make things worse.

He could catch you easily, but he doesn't unless you're actually about to hit someone because you need to learn what happens when you lose control. You eventually manage to slow yourself, level out, and stop the fall a few hundred feet above the ground. It isn’t graceful, but for the first time you're hovering because you chose to instead of because your body accidentally lifted you. The fear turns into excitement almost immediately.

You try moving forward slowly and feel the air moving around you while nothing is holding you up. Once the control starts making sense, you push harder and cover more distance in a few seconds than you could’ve crossed in a car. Mark stays beside you while you start laughing because there’s no way around how incredible it feels to realize the ground doesn’t matter anymore.

That excitement almost gets someone hurt later in the session. You accelerate farther than Mark told you to, see an empty road ahead, and decide you can stop whenever you want. A maintenance truck turns onto the road just as you start slowing down, and you're still moving fast enough that correcting toward either side could put you through the cab.
You pull upward at the last second and miss it by a few feet.

Nobody inside the truck even understands what almost happened, but you do. You'd been having fun for less than an hour and came close to killing people who had nothing to do with your training because you assumed your durability meant you could afford a mistake.

The next several days become less about discovering new abilities and more about making the ones you have safe enough to use. You practice carrying weighted dummies without crushing them, matching the speed of moving vehicles before touching them, and landing softly enough that the ground doesn’t crack every time your feet come down.

By the end of the week, Cecil thinks you're improving fast enough to continue training outside the GDA. You still haven’t decided whether you want anything resembling a superhero life, but that question gets answered for you when a real emergency happens close enough that you can hear it before anyone gives you permission to leave.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: You're inside a GDA training facility when you hear the collapse several miles away. At first, it sounds like thunder, then the emergency channels light up with reports that an apartment building has partially come down after a gas explosion. Mark is on the other side of the state dealing with another emergency, and Cecil tells you to stay where you are because you haven't been cleared to operate around civilians yet.

You could've listened to him. Instead, you think about the truck you almost hit and every hour you've spent learning how to control your strength specifically so you wouldn't hurt people when it mattered. Staying inside while you can hear people trapped under concrete feels worse than risking another mistake, so you tell Cecil where you're going and leave before he can lock the facility down around you.

The scene is nothing like training. Firefighters are trying to hold people back from a structure that’s still shifting, survivors are screaming from different floors, and every instinct you have tells you to grab the largest piece of concrete and move it out of the way. You stop yourself because pulling the wrong support could bring another section of the building down on everyone underneath it.

You start with the people closest to open space. Instead of flying them out at full speed, you carry them carefully, match their bodies to your movement, and hand them directly to paramedics before going back inside. When part of the ceiling begins falling over a rescue crew, you hold it long enough for everyone to clear the room, then lower it instead of throwing it somewhere else and creating another problem.

The hardest rescue comes when you hear a woman and her daughter trapped below a collapsed stairwell. The concrete above them is carrying part of the floor, so ripping it out would probably drop everything else on top of them. You brace the structure with your body, lift just enough weight to open a gap, and let firefighters crawl underneath while you keep several tons from shifting another inch.

Another part of the building gives way while you're still holding it. You turn your body over the firefighters and take the impact across your back, feeling the floor come apart around you without losing your grip. Once everyone is clear, you push the debris away slowly enough that nothing else collapses behind it.

By the time the last ambulance leaves, your clothes are ruined and there are dozens of phones pointed at you. Cecil arrives furious because the entire reason he wanted you contained was to prevent exactly this kind of public exposure, but yelling at you becomes harder when the firefighters standing nearby are explaining how many people wouldn’t have made it out without you.
You don’t apologize for leaving.

That decision changes everything afterward. The GDA can't pretend you don’t exist once footage shows someone flying out of a collapsed building with civilians in their arms, and Cecil can’t put you back inside a lab without admitting that the person everyone just watched saving people is being treated like a prisoner.
That understanding lasts until you accidentally discover what he built in case you do.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Cecil lets you continue training after the rescue, but the freedom comes with more GDA supervision and a new set of rules about when you can respond to emergencies. You agree to most of it because you don’t want to spend every day fighting the people teaching you how to survive your own body, although you make it clear that if civilians are about to die and you can reach them, you're not waiting for permission.

A few days later, one of your training sessions goes wrong when you hit a reinforced wall harder than expected. The impact trips a hidden system inside the facility, and before anyone can stop it, the entire room seals around you. Heavy doors drop over the exits, the ventilation shuts off, and a low frequency vibration begins running through the structure.
You don’t know what it is, but Mark reacts immediately.

He tells Cecil to shut it down while you're still trying to understand why the room was designed to trap you in the first place. The vibration isn’t strong enough to seriously hurt you, but it makes it harder to keep your balance, and Mark recognizes the idea behind it because Viltrumite equilibrium can be disrupted by certain frequencies.

Cecil kills the system before it goes any further, then admits that the room was part of a contingency plan. It was an existing GDA Viltrumite-containment prototype built from everything they had already learned about Viltrumite weaknesses, and once the first tests showed your transformation was continuing, Cecil quietly had it activated and adapted for you in case you lost control or decided you didn’t want to cooperate anymore.

You'd be furious because you chose to stay. You agreed to the tests, let them study your blood, trained under their supervision, and kept coming back even after you proved you could leave whenever you wanted. Cecil would tell you that none of that changes what you're capable of, especially when Earth already survived one Viltrumite deciding humanity was beneath him.
What changes is that you stop letting Cecil decide what your powers are for.

You begin responding to emergencies because you choose to, not because the GDA assigns them. A train derailment gives you one of the first real tests of everything Mark taught you when several cars leave the track at high speed. Your first instinct is to grab the front car and stop it immediately, but you realize everyone inside would keep moving even if the train doesn't.

You match its speed instead, brace yourself against the side, and begin slowing the entire line gradually while keeping the cars from rolling farther. It takes longer and looks far less impressive than simply catching the train, but the passengers survive because you finally understand that saving someone with Viltrumite strength is usually about using less of it.

Footage from that rescue spreads much farther than the apartment collapse. People begin comparing you with Invincible, reporters start asking where another flying powerhouse came from, and the GDA's cover story that you're simply an enhanced person working with them doesn’t answer why nobody has any record of you before now.

You choose to keep helping anyway. That choice is what eventually exposes you to people far beyond Earth. By this point, the Empire already understands Earth's unusual compatibility with Viltrumite genetics, while Thragg still leads Viltrum. A Viltrumite operative monitoring the planet would see enough footage to recognize the way you move, the strength you're displaying, and the fact that a person who appears completely human is flying with abilities that look disturbingly familiar.
Earth was only supposed to have a very small number of people with Viltrumite blood.
Now there’s another one, and nobody in the Empire knows where you came from.

When Cecil tells you an unidentified Viltrumite has changed course and is heading toward Earth, he doesn’t need to explain who they're coming to investigate. You made the decision to stop hiding, and now somebody from the Empire has seen enough to come looking for you.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: The Viltrumite reaching Earth wouldn't come down throwing punches. Anissa would arrive because the Empire would want answers before it decided whether you were a problem, and seeing you in person would confirm very quickly that the footage wasn’t some human imitation of Viltrumite abilities. She could hear your heartbeat, watch the way you hold yourself in the air, and recognize that your body moves much closer to a Viltrumite than any enhanced human she has seen before.

You'd meet her with Mark nearby, but she wouldn’t be especially interested in him at first. Mark is already something the Empire understands. You're the stranger who apparently started human and now carries a body close enough to theirs that even Anissa can’t explain it by looking at you.

She’d ask where your parents are from, whether you know your bloodline, and who performed whatever process changed you. When you tell her you were born completely human, she wouldn't believe it until Cecil sends enough biological data to prove there was no hidden Viltrumite ancestry before the accident.

That result would make you more valuable instead of less. The Empire already knows humans are unusually compatible with Viltrumite biology, which is one of the reasons Earth matters so much to them. An unprecedented process that can take a normal adult and convert the body this far without reproduction would be far more useful than another soldier. If it could be repeated, the Empire wouldn't need to wait generations to rebuild its population.

Anissa wouldn't explain all of that like she’s giving you a history lesson. She'd simply tell you that Viltrum would want to examine you and that going willingly would make everything easier. From her perspective, the offer is generous because she sees Viltrumite power as an improvement over the life you had before.

The fact that your body changed doesn’t make your old life meaningless, and hearing Anissa talk about humanity like a weaker stage you happened to escape would bother you almost immediately. You could tell her that becoming stronger didn’t erase where you came from or give another species ownership over what happened to you.

She'd probably find that answer disappointing more than insulting. Your body looks Viltrumite while your values still sound completely human, which is exactly the conflict the Empire would want corrected before you become harder to control.

Anissa could test you without turning the meeting into a full fight. She moves suddenly, catches your arm, and tries pulling you off balance hard enough to see how you react. A few weeks earlier you might have panicked and overcorrected, but now you’ve spent enough time training with Mark that you move with her instead of fighting the first ounce of force.

Cecil wouldn't love that last part because the research is technically sitting in GDA systems, but he'd understand why you’re drawing the line now. Until Anissa arrived, your transformation was mainly an Earth problem. Now the same records that might help the GDA understand you could also tell the Empire how to make more people like you.
Anissa leaves without attacking because she has what she needs for the moment. She knows the transformation is real, she knows you're staying on Earth, and she knows you won't cooperate voluntarily.
You'd spend the next few days waiting for her to come back.
Instead, the first person who tries to use your transformation against you is Cecil.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: He could ask for another round of tissue samples, deeper scans, and access to the preserved material used during your treatment. You'd agree to some of it because you still want answers too, but you'd insist on being present whenever the original samples are moved or tested. That would frustrate Cecil because he’s used to deciding what information is too dangerous for everyone else to see.
The tension would get worse when you discover the GDA has already tried reproducing part of the reaction in cell cultures.
You'd shut the research down yourself.

Cecil could argue that destroying the work only leaves Earth less prepared if the Empire already understands more than they do, but you’ve now heard exactly how Anissa talks about the process. A repeatable conversion method wouldn't stay a medical curiosity. Viltrum could use it to manufacture more soldiers, and Earth governments would have plenty of reasons to wonder what a human army with Viltrumite bodies could do.

Mark would probably understand your decision even if he doesn’t agree with destroying every piece of data. He knows better than almost anyone how quickly Viltrumite biology turns into a question of control, and he also knows Cecil well enough to believe that contingency plans can become weapons once he thinks the stakes are high enough.

You wouldn't erase everything because doing that could kill your only chance of understanding future complications in your own body. Instead, you separate the transformation records from the parts that could help reproduce it. Medical information stays with the GDA under tighter access, while the experimental work gets destroyed before either side can build on it.
That choice would make you responsible for yourself. The Empire wouldn't need Cecil's files if it can take you alive.

That's when the next Viltrumite comes differently. Anissa gave them a report on what you can do, so whoever returns isn’t there to politely ask whether you want to visit Viltrum. A stronger operative could intercept you while you're away from the city and make it clear that the Empire wants your body intact enough to study.

You'd try leaving the fight before it reaches civilians because that's one lesson you've learned better than anything else. Instead of trading punches over a highway or inside a neighborhood, you fly straight upward and force the Viltrumite to follow you into open sky.

Mark has trained with you while holding back. This Viltrumite doesn’t. The punch catches you across the ribs and sends you miles before you can stop yourself. Your body survives, but the pain is completely different from hitting concrete or taking a controlled GDA test. You finally understand what Mark meant when he warned you that Viltrumite durability matters much less when the person hitting you has the same kind of strength.
The operative is heading toward Earth again because dragging you down there gives him more opportunities to corner you, and you know exactly who ends up underneath that fight if you let it happen.
For the first time, you’re using your new body against someone who knows how to use theirs better than you do.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: You wouldn't beat an experienced Viltrumite by suddenly discovering that you're stronger. The gap in experience would show almost immediately, especially once the fight stops being a straight exchange. He knows how to change direction at full speed without losing control, how to use momentum before contact, and how to keep attacking after a hit sends both of you across miles of open sky.
What keeps you alive is everything you learned because you didn’t grow up Viltrumite.

When he charges again, you don't try to overpower him. You move with the hit, turn as he commits, and let his speed carry both of you past each other instead of taking the full impact through your chest. The next time he reaches for you, you drop underneath him and force him to correct while you already know where you're going.

You'd still get hurt pretty bad. He catches you eventually, drives you through a mountain far from the city, and tears your shoulder badly enough that your arm stops responding properly. Your healing starts working almost immediately, but it can’t rebuild major damage in the middle of a fight fast enough to make the injury irrelevant.
That forces you to make a decision Mark couldn't make for you.

You could call him and turn this into a 2 on 1 fight, but the Empire came because of you and will keep coming as long as it thinks you’re simply another asset Earth is hiding. If Mark solves this encounter for you, Viltrum learns that separating you from him is all it has to do next time.

You decide to keep fighting long enough to make the operative change his goal. Instead of trying to knock him unconscious, you start damaging the things he needs to take you alive. You break fingers when he reaches for you, attack the arm he keeps using to restrain you, and force every grab to cost him something. When he gets you around the neck and starts dragging you away from Earth, you stop fighting the direction he wants and accelerate with him.
For a few seconds, he thinks you’ve lost control. Then you turn both of you directly toward a barren section of the Moon.

The impact wouldn't kill either of you, but you’ve spent enough time learning how your own body handles sudden stops to know exactly how ugly it’s going to be. You pull away at the last moment while he keeps most of the speed you helped build, and he hits hard enough to disappear beneath the surface.
You don't stand there waiting for him to get back up. You leave while your shoulder is still healing, reach Mark, and tell Cecil exactly what happened before the Viltrumite can recover and follow.
You didn’t defeat the Empire. You made taking you alive expensive enough that the next decision has to come from someone higher up.
That decision eventually reaches Thragg.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: Thragg wouldn't care that you survived one operative or managed to embarrass another. What matters is what your existence could mean for a species that nearly died during the Scourge Virus and has spent years rebuilding through the few Viltrumites who remain. Humans already reproduce unusually well with Viltrumites, but your transformation suggests there may be another route entirely.
He wouldn't come to Earth personally just to drag you away. He could send a message through the Empire offering something much more dangerous than a fight: a place among them.

You would be allowed to live as a Viltrumite, train with people who can actually teach you the limits of your new body, and stop spending the rest of your life aging past everyone you care about without anyone who understands what that feels like. In return, the Empire gets access to the biological process that created you and expects you to accept Viltrumite authority.
For the first time, Viltrum has something to offer that you can’t get from Cecil or Mark.
People who may still be alive when everyone else you know is gone.

You'd still know what accepting that means. Their longevity comes with an ideology built around conquest, strength, and deciding that weaker civilizations should be ruled for their own good. You already rejected the idea when Anissa first came to Earth, but now the Empire is offering you a way to avoid a future you've only recently started thinking about.

You decide to hear them out in person even though you know walking into Viltrumite territory could easily become a trap. It is an enormous gamble, but the Empire is offering answers about your new body and future that nobody on Earth can give you, and you decide that understanding what your life could become is worth the risk. You tell Mark and Cecil where you're going, leave a copy of everything you know about your transformation behind, and make it clear that if the Empire tries taking you somewhere against your will, Earth should assume the deal is over.
The temptation ends when you see how they treat everyone else.

You could witness a world the Empire has already brought under control, with local leaders following Viltrumite demands because everyone remembers what happened the last time someone resisted. Nobody needs to be getting beaten in the street for you to understand the threat. People obey because they know exactly what the people above them can do.
Thragg would see that as order. You'd see the future Anissa was offering Earth.

When you finally meet him, he wouldn't need to threaten you immediately. He could explain that humans are compatible enough with Viltrumites that your transformation makes biological sense even if the method is new, and that the Empire could use the process to restore what the Scourge nearly destroyed. Then he asks you to give them what remains of the research but you refuse.
This time the refusal carries much more weight because you came willingly, saw what they were offering, and made the choice after understanding exactly what you could gain from it.
Thragg would let you leave the room and wouldn't let you leave Viltrumite territory.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: You'd know the fight begins before anyone throws a punch because the guards around you stop behaving like escorts. The Empire still wants you alive, which gives you a narrow advantage because everyone coming after you has to control enough force to avoid destroying the thing they're trying to study.

You wouldn't try fighting your way through every Viltrumite between you and open space. A few months ago, having this body might have made that sound possible. After getting beaten by one experienced operative, you know exactly how stupid that would be.
Instead, you use the part of your life they keep dismissing. You think like someone who spent almost their entire existence human.

You've spent your entire transformation learning how dangerous overwhelming force can be, so you move through the facility by breaking only what you need, use doors and structures to interrupt pursuit rather than standing and trading hits, and keep changing direction before the people following you can turn the chase into a straight speed contest. None of that is enough to outfight experienced Viltrumites for long, but it buys you the seconds you need to reach the laboratory.

If Thragg wants the transformation process, then anyone examining the samples taken since you arrived becomes part of the threat. You reach the laboratory before the Empire finishes analyzing enough of your blood, destroy the stored samples, and wipe whatever biological data you can access before the scientists understand why you're there.

Several Viltrumites reach the lab before you can leave, and now there’s no reason for them to keep the facility intact around you. You'd get hit hard enough to break bones, lose enough blood for your healing to struggle keeping up, and realize very quickly that you aren't going to overpower the group.
Your goal changes from escaping cleanly to making sure the research doesn't survive even if you don't.

You tear into the facility's power systems while the fight continues and send the laboratory into a cascading failure. The cascading failure finally creates the opening your movement alone could not. The Viltrumites have to split their attention between keeping hold of you and stopping the destruction from spreading through the sections carrying their own people.

You accelerate toward open space with injuries you can barely feel individually anymore because too much of your body hurts at once. One of them catches your leg before you clear the structure, and you turn back instead of trying to pull free.
You hit him with everything you have. Once you're in open space, you don’t stop to see who follows.
You head for Earth because you already made the decision the Empire wanted from you. Being biologically Viltrumite doesn’t make Viltrum your home.

By the time you return, Cecil would probably have every weapon he owns ready because he has no idea whether the person coming back is still you. Mark would meet you first, see the injuries, and understand from the fact that you came alone that the offer didn’t end the way Viltrum expected.

You'd tell Cecil to destroy the remaining reproducible treatment research on Earth and this time he agrees. You keep the medical information needed to understand your own body, while the samples and biological data you could reach off world are gone.
