He has spent the entire time being hard on Spider-Man, but when Peter is at his weakest, Frank is still there. For someone who has spent years convincing himself that getting close to people only puts them in danger, Peter is being forced to confront the fact that people are choosing to stay anyway.

Jean leaves after saving Peter’s life. She doesn’t stay in New York, and where she goes next is left unknown. What matters is what she leaves behind in Peter. She made him understand that trying to suppress every part of himself was not protecting anyone. His body had been changing throughout the movie, and he had spent much of that time trying to stop it with technology. Bruce and MJ had already warned him that forcing something natural back down could make things worse. Jean is the person who finally makes that lesson personal.

Bruce’s situation does not quietly reset either. After what happened when Jean controlled him and removed his inhibitor, he steps away to recover and work out what the transformation did to him instead of immediately returning to normal. Metzger is still missing. Jean came close to killing him, Peter stopped her, and Metzger escaped during the chaos after Peter went down. He remains on the run. Damage Control is no longer something Peter can look at the same way. He trusted them when Jean first appeared, and that trust helped put her back into the hands of the people responsible for Sara’s death.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Frank helps him get out without exposing his identity, and you stay close enough to make sure he actually gets home instead of trying to disappear the second nobody is watching him. Peter does not argue much. After everything that happened with Jean, Bruce and Damage Control, he does not have the energy to keep pushing everyone away. Before you leave, he finally makes a choice he would not have made when you first met. He takes off the mask himself and tells you his name. Peter Parker.

For the first time since you met him, he lets you see what his life actually looks like. It’s smaller than you expected. There is no team waiting for him or headquarters watching over New York with him. Most of what Peter has built around himself is designed to function without anyone else because he thought that was how he protected people.

What changes is that he stops treating that isolation as proof that he should keep disappearing. You start seeing him outside emergencies. Sometimes it’s only for a few minutes, and sometimes he still leaves because something is happening somewhere else in the city. What matters is that he comes back.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: The city doesn’t go back to normal after Jean leaves. Bruce steps away to recover, Metzger is still missing, Jean is somewhere outside New York, and Damage Control still has secrets left behind. Peter knows there will be more problems. For once, he doesn’t act like he has to face all of them alone.

Your friendship with Peter stays small. You grab food after patrol, sit with him while he works on equipment, and sometimes Frank shows up just long enough to complain about Peter taking unnecessary risks before staying anyway.

MJ and Ned are still complicated. MJ has read Peter’s letter, but knowing what they used to be does not restore the memories or feelings the spell took from her. The terrace and necklace suggest something may still be there, and Ned shows signs of the same uncertainty, but nothing is fully restored. Peter no longer treats that uncertainty like something he has to run away from.

You woke up expecting a normal day in New York. Now Jean Grey has been inside your head, Punisher knows who you are, and Spider-Man trusted you enough to tell you his name. You came into this world as another person in the crowd. You don’t leave it that way.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: By the end of Brand New Day, you haven’t replaced Spider-Man, saved New York by yourself, or become the strongest person in the city.
What you changed was smaller, and probably more important.

You were there when Peter trusted the wrong people. You were there when Jean stopped being a threat and became someone he understood. You saw Peter nearly lose himself trying to suppress everything he thought made his life dangerous, and you stayed long enough to watch him finally stop doing that.
Now Jean is gone, Metzger is still out there, MJ and Ned may be starting to remember pieces of what they lost, and Peter isn’t living like he has to face all of it alone anymore.
Because this time, when Spider-Man swings back into New York, there’s someone waiting for him when he gets home.

scripts.title: What If YOU Were In The Boys

sections.name: INTRO
paras: You’ve seen The Seven your entire life.

They’re on television, in movies, literally everywhere. Homelander gives speeches about protecting America, Vought turns every rescue into an ad, and most people have accepted that this is just what the world looks like now.
You’re one of them.
At least…until you take a shortcut home one night and hear someone arguing behind a closed loading dock. You almost keep walking then the door opens and a man stumbles outside.
He’s wearing a Vought badge. A second later, A-Train comes out behind him.
You freeze.
There’s nobody around. The man is terrified, and A-Train is trying to get something from him.

Then A-Train notices you. The man uses that second to run but doesn’t make it far. By the time you reach him, A-Train is already gone. The man is dying, but he’s still holding onto a small flash drive.
He gives it to you before you can ask what it is. You take it home and by morning, Vought knows you have it.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: You don’t open the flash drive right away. You spend most of the morning thinking about getting rid of it but the problem is the 2 people standing outside your apartment.
They don’t look like security guards. They don’t need to. One of them shows you a Vought ID and asks if they can come inside. The other already knows where you were last night.

That answers the first question you had. A-Train told someone. You let them in because refusing would only make you look worse. They never accuse you of anything. They explain that there was an incident involving a Vought employee, that you were unfortunately nearby, and that the company wants to make sure you aren’t dragged into something you don’t understand.

Then they offer you money and the money is more than you make in a year. All you have to do is sign an agreement saying you didn’t see anything unusual, hand over anything the employee gave you, and stop discussing the incident.
You’ve already seen what happens to someone who gets on the wrong side of A-Train. Taking the money means this ends today.

You don’t have the flash drive anymore. Before Vought arrived, you copied everything on it onto your computer and hid the original in a secure off-site place you can’t casually revisit without exposing it. You don’t even know why you did it. Maybe because the man died getting it to you. Maybe because Vought showing up this quickly made you realize whatever is on it matters. Once they search your apartment, leaving the original untouched becomes deliberate. If they’re watching you, going back for it could lead them straight to the one copy they missed.
You tell them the employee never gave you anything.
The woman sitting across from you doesn’t react. She slides the agreement closer and tells you the offer still stands.
You sign it and they leave. That should make you feel better. Instead, you spend the next hour staring through your window to see if they’re still outside.

Eventually you open the files. Most of them mean nothing to you. Shipment numbers. Medical records. Payments routed through companies you’ve never heard of. Several files are corrupted, and others are protected.

Inside are records connected to hospitals across the country. Infants are listed by identification numbers instead of names. There are dates, dosages and references to something called Compound V. You have no idea what Compound V is. Then you notice some of the names attached to later files. Supes.
The connection still isn’t clear enough to understand, but it’s enough to make one thing obvious. The man A-Train killed wasn’t stealing money. He was trying to get information out of Vought.

So you start looking into him. His name barely appears online. Vought has already released a statement saying one of their employees died during an attempted robbery near company property. There’s nothing about A-Train being there.

They were checking whether you knew enough to become a problem. You spend the rest of the day making copies. Instead of dumping everything online, you send a small, deliberately incomplete sample through an anonymous account to a reporter who has covered Vought before. You strip out anything obvious that identifies you, but the sample still contains enough of the dead employee’s internal file structure and timestamps for someone already following A-Train to connect it to his death. Butcher gets hold of that sample while monitoring Vought and A-Train leads, then matches it to the unidentified witness Vought has quietly been trying to locate. Another copy goes somewhere Vought won’t find by searching your apartment. You keep the third. That trail is what brings Billy Butcher to you. You don’t know his name yet. You only know that when you leave work two days later, there’s a man waiting across the street who has been watching the building for almost an hour.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: You don’t go straight home. The man follows anyway. You change direction twice, stop inside a crowded store and leave through another exit. 10 minutes later, he’s still there.

At that point you know it isn’t paranoia. You head somewhere public and wait. He finally approaches you. He knows about the dead Vought employee. He knows A-Train was there, and somehow he knows you received something before the man died.
Instead, he brings up Robin Ward.
You’ve seen her death on the news. A-Train ran through her in the middle of the street. Vought treated it like a terrible accident, paid compensation and moved on.
Butcher tells you there was more to it. A-Train wasn’t responding to an emergency when he hit Robin. He was moving through the city while using something Vought doesn’t want anyone asking about.
Compound V.
That gets your attention. You still don’t trust him, but now he’s said the same name that appears all over the files. Butcher realizes it immediately. You don’t confirm anything. You don’t have to.

He tells you he knows someone connected to Robin and that they’ve been looking into A-Train. If you have evidence connecting him to Vought, he wants it. You ask what happens if you give it to him. It’s pretty clear he wants to hurt Vought. That’s when you realize Vought isn’t the only group willing to drag you into something bigger than yourself.
You leave without giving Butcher the files. He lets you go. That worries you more than if he had tried to stop you. That night, someone breaks into your apartment and your computer is gone.
So is every piece of paper connected to the files. Whoever searched the apartment even checked places you wouldn’t have thought to hide anything.

Vought knows you lied. You call the number Butcher gave you. This time, he doesn’t come alone. Hughie looks nothing like the person you expected Butcher to work with. He seems almost as uncomfortable being there as you are.
Then you recognize him.
Robin’s boyfriend.

That makes the whole thing harder to dismiss. Hughie doesn’t try to sell you on some war against superheroes. He tells you what happened to Robin and how quickly Vought reduced her death to paperwork and a settlement.
You show them one copy of the files. Not all of it. Butcher notices. You tell him that’s the deal. If something happens to you, the rest goes somewhere else.

Together, you go through the material. Hughie notices references to A-Train that match what they’ve already been investigating. Compound V appears beside medical shipments, private clinics and expenses that don’t make sense for a superhero company.
But there still isn’t one document that plainly explains what it does. You need something current. Something tied directly to A-Train. Butcher already has a lead.
Popclaw.

You don’t know who she is yet, but Hughie does. She’s a Supe, and A-Train has been seeing her in secret. Butcher wants to use her to get closer to whatever A-Train is hiding. That’s when you find out what working with The Boys actually means.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: You refuse to go anywhere near Popclaw. Butcher thinks that’s funny. You’ve already watched A-Train kill someone over these files. Walking into the home of the woman he’s secretly seeing sounds like a good way to become the next person Vought has to explain away.
So you make Butcher change the plan. If Popclaw is connected to Compound V, you don’t need to confront her. You need to know who is supplying it.

That gives Mother’s Milk something useful to work with. He enters the situation differently from Butcher. He actually wants to know where you got the files, what you copied, and what Vought might already know about you. He also points out something Butcher hasn’t. If Vought searched your apartment but left you alive, they still aren’t sure how much evidence escaped.
That uncertainty is keeping you alive. So you use it. Instead of disappearing, you go back to Vought.

You contact the same people who offered you money and tell them someone has approached you asking questions about the dead employee. You don’t mention Butcher. You make it sound like you’re scared and want Vought to handle it. They aren’t surprised someone is investigating.
They just want a description and know what was asked.
Most importantly, they want to know whether the stranger mentioned A-Train or Compound V.
You never said Compound V.
They did.

You leave the meeting knowing the name matters even more than you thought. Vought leaves the meeting thinking you’re frightened enough to cooperate. Both sides are wrong about part of the conversation. What you don’t notice is that the meeting also gave Vought a chance to compromise your phone with a tracking tool disguised as part of their security check-in. From that point forward, they aren’t tracking Butcher in real time. They’re tracking you, and your movements are about to lead them somewhere they already associate with him.

The audio isn’t enough to expose Vought by itself, but now The Boys have something the stolen files didn’t give them, proof that Vought security recognizes Compound V and considers questions about it dangerous.

That’s the first time you see the difference between them. MM wants to build a case. Butcher wants a weakness he can use against a Supe. Hughie is somewhere between the two. The Popclaw lead moves forward without you entering her apartment. Through surveillance, they confirm A-Train is still seeing her. They also see enough to realize his behavior has changed. He’s nervous, moving quickly and keeping things away from Vought’s normal channels.
One of the shipment codes appears again. This time, there’s an address attached. You recognize the format from the hospital records. The Boys prepare to check it out. You’re supposed to stay behind.
And for once, you agree. Then your phone rings. It’s the Vought woman who came to your apartment.

She asks where you are. You give her the first normal answer that comes to mind. Then she asks why the phone they’ve been tracking was near a building already associated with Billy Butcher twenty minutes earlier.
You don’t answer immediately. A few seconds later, Butcher’s phone rings too.
He looks at the screen, then at you. The address they were about to investigate is no longer safe.

Vought knows you found The Boys. MM and Frenchie check your phone immediately and find the tracking tool Vought planted during the meeting. They remove it before you move again, but the damage is already done. Vought has a record of where you’ve been since leaving Seven Tower, including enough repeated stops and connections to start narrowing down the places The Boys use. And somewhere inside Seven Tower, A-Train is about to find out you’re still alive.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The files finally start making sense once MM compares the hospital records with A-Train’s supply.
Compound V isn’t just something certain Supes use after getting their powers. Vought has been giving it to children.

Until now, you thought Vought was covering up drug use and protecting A-Train. The truth is much bigger. The heroes you grew up watching weren’t simply born different. Vought had a hand in creating them.
You still need proof strong enough to survive Vought trying to bury it, so you make a decision Butcher doesn’t expect.
You tell them Butcher found you and you want out. You say you’re willing to give back what you have if they pay you and keep him away from you.
While you keep their attention on you, Hughie and MM use the hospital information to confirm that Compound V has been administered to children.
The meeting gets worse when Homelander walks in.
He already knows you’ve been around Butcher. He asks whether you gave him anything.
There’s no point pretending you aren’t terrified. You let him see it and focus on the one thing that might keep you alive.
You tell him Butcher still thinks you’re useful.
If Homelander kills you now, Butcher will know Vought is scared of whatever you saw. If you stay alive, Vought can still use you to find out what he knows.
Vought created Supes and for the first time, you’re carrying something that could actually hurt them.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: Butcher immediately wants to use the evidence. That’s when you start realizing being useful to him can be dangerous too. He doesn’t care how close you came to dying in Seven Tower. He cares that the plan worked.
So you stop giving him everything. You make another copy of the Compound V evidence and hide it without telling him. Hughie catches you, but instead of stopping you, he helps.
Neither of you wants Butcher deciding by himself when the evidence gets used or who gets sacrificed along the way. Then Popclaw dies. Vought calls it an overdose but it seems super sketchy.
She was connected to A-Train and Compound V, just like the employee you saw die at the beginning. Now another person who could lead back to the truth is gone.

Popclaw’s death changes the calculation. Vought is no longer just burying information; people connected to the same chain are dying. Leaving the original flash drive untouched now feels more dangerous than risking the trip to recover it. You decide to retrieve it before Vought can narrow down where you hid it. Hughie comes with you. The drive is still there.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: Then…. A-Train finds you.
There’s nothing you can do physically. A-Train could kill you before Hughie even knew what happened.
So you don’t try to run. He wants the drive. You tell him killing you won’t solve anything.

Copies already exist, and you prove at least part of that before he can dismiss it. You name a file detail that only someone holding the drive could know and tell him Hughie already has material from the same cache outside your control. Then you make the larger claim: if you disappear, everything else you have gets released.
That isn’t entirely true, but enough of it is. You also tell him Butcher has evidence connecting him to the first Vought employee’s death. He actually doesn’t but A-Train doesn’t know that.
You’ve learned something important since this started. You don’t survive Supes by being stronger than them. You survive by making sure killing you creates a bigger problem than leaving you alive.
A-Train lets you go because he can’t afford to find out you were telling the truth.

When you get back, Butcher discovers you kept evidence from him. He’s furious but you don’t back down. Vought tried to buy you. Homelander tried to scare you. A-Train almost killed you. You’re not going to hand everything over to another person who sees you as a useful piece on the board.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Butcher doesn’t forgive you for keeping evidence from him, but he also can’t afford to push you out. The files you copied are still one of the best chances any of you have of proving what Compound V actually is, and Hughie wants to get them somewhere Vought can’t erase them. MM agrees. Butcher keeps dragging the conversation back toward Homelander, and after everything you’ve seen from him, you finally stop pretending that isn’t a problem.

You tell him the truth. Every plan is supposed to be about hurting Vought, but the second Homelander enters the picture, everybody else becomes expendable. You don’t know every detail of Butcher’s past, but you know enough to understand that this stopped being a normal investigation a long time ago. If getting closer to Homelander meant risking you, Hughie, or anyone else in the room, you’re not convinced he’d hesitate.

You give Hughie the copy you kept from him and tell him to get it out before anyone can change their mind. It needs to go somewhere Vought can’t buy, threaten, or quietly delete. You don’t care whether Butcher likes the timing anymore. The evidence belongs outside this room.

Before Hughie can get far, the safehouse is compromised. The tracker itself is gone, but the location history Vought collected before MM and Frenchie removed it gave them enough to map your recent movements and narrow down the network of places connected to The Boys.

Vought moves quickly enough that there isn’t time to hold the location. Everyone scatters, and somehow you end up leaving with Butcher. He already has another plan forming, and you can tell from the way he explains it that he expects you to be part of it.

He wants to use the evidence as leverage against Madelyn Stillwell. If Vought thinks you still control material that could damage the company, Butcher believes Stillwell might come personally or at least send someone important enough to pressure. You hate the idea because it once again depends on somebody believing you’re worth keeping alive, but this time you set the terms. Before the meeting, a small authenticated packet from the Compound V files is sent to an outside reporter, with the larger cache arranged to follow whether the meeting works or not. Butcher doesn’t control that part.

Stillwell doesn’t come. Once she realizes Butcher is behind the leverage attempt and that the material involves Compound V, she alerts Homelander rather than walking into the meeting herself. Homelander chooses to handle it personally. Seeing him again is worse because this time you know exactly what he is. There isn’t any public image left in your head to soften it. He’s standing in front of you because the evidence has become an existential problem for Vought and because Butcher is involved.
Butcher starts pushing him almost immediately. You can tell where it’s going, and you know there’s no version of this where provoking Homelander ends well for you.

So you cut across Butcher’s plan and tell Homelander the part that actually matters. The Compound V evidence is already outside Vought’s control, and this time you can prove it. You show him confirmation that an authenticated piece of the files has already reached an outside reporter. Hughie has more, other copies exist outside the building, and the first leak is already beyond recovery. Killing either of you might stop people, but it won’t put the information back inside Vought.

You don’t try to make yourself look brave. You’re terrified, and hiding that from someone like Homelander would probably make you look more suspicious anyway. You just keep talking long enough for him to understand that this is an information problem.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: The first reports begin appearing before Vought can fully contain them. At first they’re small pieces, then more documents surface and people start connecting them. Parents linked to Vought medical programs begin asking questions, reporters compare dates, and old stories about Supes suddenly look different when Compound V is added to them.

You helped make sure of that because you never allowed one person to hold the only copy. If Butcher had controlled the evidence, he might have used it as leverage. If Vought had recovered it, it would’ve vanished. Spreading it was the only reason the truth survived long enough to become somebody else’s problem too.

Butcher still isn’t satisfied. The company is hurt, but Homelander is still alive, and that’s the part he cares about most. He starts talking about the next move almost immediately, while everyone else is still trying to work out whether Vought is about to come through the door again.

You stay with Hughie, MM, and Frenchie. None of them are harmless, and none of them can promise you safety, but at least they’ve stopped treating you like evidence. Then Frenchie shows you something recovered during the chaos.
A vial of Compound V.

You’ve spent this entire story surviving people who could kill you without effort. A-Train already found you once. Homelander knows your face. Vought knows you helped expose them. Taking V would give you a chance to stop being physically helpless.

The drug itself isn’t what made every Supe you’ve met into a monster, but you’ve seen what happens when power gets wrapped inside Vought’s system. You’ve also spent days proving that being powerless doesn’t mean being useless. Every time you survived, it happened because you kept information back, noticed what someone wanted, or made killing you more complicated than leaving you alive.
You put the vial down.
Not because you’re certain you’d become like Homelander, and not because you suddenly think being normal is noble. You just don’t trust Vought enough to let something they created become part of you.

There’s no big reconciliation between you and Butcher. He’ll keep chasing Homelander, and you know sooner or later that obsession is going to drag him into something worse. The difference now is that you no longer have to go wherever he decides the fight should lead.

sections.name: OUTRO
paras: You entered this world like almost everyone else, believing The Seven were heroes because that was the version Vought had spent years selling.

You saw what A-Train did when nobody was watching. You learned how quickly Vought could rewrite a death, pay off a witness, or turn a problem into paperwork. You stood in front of Homelander twice and survived without ever pretending you had a chance against him. You also learned that being against Vought didn’t automatically make Butcher someone you could trust with your life.
Most importantly, you survived because you stopped letting any one of them control what you knew.

That decision is what gets Compound V into the open earlier than Vought planned. The company still exists, Homelander is still out there, and The Boys are nowhere near finished, but the world now knows there is something underneath the superhero image Vought spent years protecting.

scripts.title: What If You Were Chosen By A Green Lantern Ring

sections.name: INTRO
paras: A Green Lantern ring can cross the universe looking for 1 person, and somehow it stops at you. 1 minute, you're living a normal life, and the next, a glowing green ring is flying straight toward you because somehow, out of everyone it could have chosen, the Corps’ successor system identified you as someone capable of overcoming great fear.

You wouldn’t know how to use it, you wouldn’t understand why it picked you, and your first constructs would probably fall apart the second you panic. Then the ring would take you to Oa and drop you into a Corps filled with people who have spent years doing this.
From there, you’d have to figure out what being chosen actually means before your first real mission.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: You’d be chosen on an ordinary night, which would probably make the whole thing feel even stranger. There wouldn't be a battle happening around you or some obvious reason for an alien weapon to suddenly appear. You could be walking home, leaving work, or sitting outside when a green light cuts across the sky and starts moving directly toward you.

At first, you’d assume it’s a drone or something falling until it changes direction every time you move. The object would stop in front of you long enough for you to see that it’s a ring, then a voice comes from it and identifies you by name before saying you have the ability to overcome great fear. You wouldn’t get much time to process that because the ring would slide onto your finger and lock itself in place.

The first thing you’d notice is that your body suddenly feels lighter. A green glow wraps around you, your clothes are replaced by a Green Lantern uniform, and information starts hitting you faster than you can understand it. The ring can translate languages, create constructs, protect you in space, and answer questions, but knowing those functions exist doesn’t mean you suddenly know how to use them.

You’d test the easiest thing first and immediately learn that the ring listens to thought more literally than you expect. If you picture a chair, a glowing chair might appear in front of you, but it could disappear as soon as your attention shifts. If you try making something more complicated, parts of it could form incorrectly because you're thinking about the object instead of holding a clear image of how it works.

Flight would be even worse. The ring can carry you, but your first attempt could send you several feet off the ground before panic makes you drop again. The aura would catch you before you hit the pavement, leaving you hovering awkwardly while you try to figure out how much of the movement comes from thought and how much comes from actual control.

You’d probably start asking the ring questions as quickly as possible. It could tell you that it belonged to a Green Lantern who can no longer serve, that you’ve been selected as a replacement for a Lantern assigned elsewhere in space, and that you’re expected to report to Oa for processing and training. The phrase “intergalactic peacekeeping organization” would be enough to make you realize this isn’t some superhero gadget you found by accident.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Your first trip through space would probably be terrifying for reasons the ring never thinks to explain. You’d be moving faster than anything you’ve ever experienced while planets and stars pass around you, and the only thing keeping you alive is a device you learned existed less than an hour ago. The ring would regulate your speed and protect you from the environment, but your body would still react like you’re doing something impossible.

Oa would make that feeling worse in a different way. You’d arrive over a planet filled with Green Lanterns from species you’ve never seen before, some humanoid and others so unfamiliar that the ring has to explain what you’re looking at. Every one of them is wearing some version of the same symbol now sitting on your chest.

You’d be brought before Lantern personnel who already know a ring selected someone new from Earth. Nobody would celebrate much because replacements usually mean another Lantern died or became unable to serve. That would be your first reminder that the ring didn’t choose you for a costume. Somebody had a job before you, and even though the ring found its successor on Earth, that vacant assignment elsewhere in space now belongs to you.

Kilowog would probably be the first person who makes that clear in a way you understand. He’d look at your shaky constructs, ask how long you’ve had the ring, and tell you that whatever you did back home doesn’t matter if you can’t keep a shield together when something is trying to kill you.

Training would begin with very basic control. You’d have to hold a simple shape in place while Kilowog hits it from different angles. The first few attempts would collapse almost instantly because every impact makes you think about the hit instead of the construct.

You’d start understanding that willpower isn’t the same thing as wanting something badly. The ring responds best when you can make a decision and keep holding onto it even while your body is telling you to stop. If you’re trying to make a wall while also thinking about whether the wall is strong enough, the doubt gets built into what you’re making.

The Corps would also explain the ring’s charge. You’d receive a personal power battery and learn the oath used to recharge the ring, along with the fact that the ring doesn’t provide unlimited energy forever. Running low in the middle of a mission is a real problem, especially for someone inexperienced enough to waste power making oversized constructs.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Your constructs would start becoming more personal once the basic drills stop being enough. Kilowog could tell you to stop copying whatever the Lantern beside you is making because you're wasting time translating somebody else’s instincts into your own head. The ring works through your imagination, which means the easiest construct to maintain is usually something you already understand well.

If you grew up playing games, building things, drawing, working with computers, fixing cars, playing sports, or doing anything else that trained you to visualize movement, that would start showing up in what you create. Instead of making a generic wall, you might build interlocking panels that shift around an impact. Instead of forming a giant hand to grab someone, you could make several smaller restraints that lock around different joints.

You’d still make plenty of mistakes. During a flight drill, you might create a complicated construct around yourself and spend so much concentration maintaining it that you miss the obstacle directly ahead. In another exercise, you could trap an opponent successfully and then lose the construct because you start celebrating before the drill is over.

The ring would also introduce you to its information systems. You could ask it about known species, locations, laws, and recorded threats, but there’d be limits to how much information you can process while fighting. Trying to have the ring explain an alien weapon while you're also maintaining 3 constructs could leave you distracted enough to get hit.

A veteran Lantern could spar with you and expose another weakness you haven’t thought about yet. You might be good at building defenses around attacks you can see, but struggle when the opponent stops trying to overpower you and starts making you choose between several problems at once.

They could send an attack toward you while another construct threatens a civilian dummy behind you. Your first instinct might be to protect yourself, then realize too late that the exercise was testing where your attention goes when you're afraid of getting hurt.
Then you’d get assigned your first mission.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: Your first mission wouldn't be a war or a planet ending crisis. The Corps would send you with an experienced Lantern to investigate a distress signal from a transport vessel that stopped responding near the edge of your sector. On paper, it would look like the kind of assignment given to someone who still needs supervision.

You’d arrive expecting mechanical trouble and find the ship drifting with most of its systems offline. The hull would still be intact, but several sections inside would be damaged and the crew would be scattered through areas where life support is failing.

Your partner would tell you to start moving people toward the functioning sections while they figure out what happened. That sounds simple until you realize the ship was built for a species much larger than you, several corridors are blocked, and some of the passengers panic the moment they see 2 Green Lanterns enter.

You’d have to use the ring for things you barely practiced on Oa. A construct could hold damaged doors open while you move people through, another could seal a crack in the hull, and the translation system would let you explain what you’re doing to passengers whose language you’ve never heard before. As you start evacuating the crew, the raiders responsible for disabling the transport emerge from another section of the ship and open fire.

Your first instinct might be to build something huge and end the fight quickly. Your partner would stop you because filling a narrow ship corridor with a giant construct could crush the same people you’re trying to protect.

You’d have to work smaller. A thin barrier could split the corridor and block incoming fire while you send several restraints around the raiders’ weapons. Another construct could pull civilians behind cover without dragging them across the floor.

You'd notice the shield becoming thinner and respond by feeding more power into it, which makes the ring’s charge drop faster. Your partner would tell you to stop thinking about how much damage the shield can take and decide where you need it to stay.
You'd narrow the barrier, strengthen the section covering the civilians, and use the power you save to disarm the last raider.

Nobody would die, but the ring would be much lower than it should be for a mission that small. Your partner wouldn’t call the mission a failure. They’d point out that you protected everyone and solved the problem, then make you look at how much energy you burned doing it.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: The first mission would change the way you train when you return to Oa. You’d stop measuring progress by how large or detailed your constructs look and start timing how long you can maintain them while moving, talking, and dealing with distractions.

Your style would become more efficient because you’d start thinking in layers instead of single large objects. Small platforms could redirect someone’s movement, narrow restraints could lock weapons in place, and several simple pieces could combine into something stronger without making you visualize one huge complicated machine.

Kilowog would start making the exercises harder once he sees you're getting comfortable. He could shut off parts of the training area, force you to navigate without the ring giving you a clean map, or put you against an opponent who spends the entire fight trying to distract you instead of overpowering you.

The opponent could make you think you’re losing even when you aren't, forcing you to split your attention between what’s actually happening and everything you're afraid might happen next. Your constructs would start flickering again because the ring responds to how clearly you can hold onto a decision, and fear makes every possibility feel equally important.

You'd eventually learn that overcoming fear doesn’t mean making it disappear. The ring chose you because you can keep moving while fear is still there, which is much harder than acting fearless when nothing is really at stake.

Reports would start coming in from several worlds in your sector describing the same strange pattern. People aren’t being attacked directly at first. Entire populations are abandoning cities, turning on each other, or refusing to leave shelters because something is making their worst fears feel real enough to control their decisions.

The Corps would send experienced Lanterns to investigate, and you'd be attached to one of those teams because the affected systems sit close to the sector you're being trained to protect. The ring wouldn't identify a normal weapon or known army behind the incidents. The only thing connecting the planets would be the way fear spreads before the actual damage starts.

sections.name: PART 6
paras: The investigation would take you to the first world where the fear outbreak has spread far enough to collapse normal life. The streets would still be intact and there wouldn’t be an army waiting for you, but thousands of people would be hiding indoors because they’re convinced something terrible is outside. Some are seeing creatures that aren't there, while others are convinced their families are about to betray them or that leaving shelter means certain death. Your ring would confirm that most of what people are seeing has no physical mass. That makes fighting it much harder because there’s nothing obvious to punch or trap in a construct. You could build barriers around civilians and carry people away from dangerous areas, but the fear would follow them because the source is affecting their minds rather than the buildings around them.

At first, the effect would be subtle enough that you might mistake it for nerves. You'd start wondering whether your ring is losing charge faster than it should, whether the veteran Lantern beside you is about to leave you behind, or whether the Corps made a mistake sending you here. The thoughts would become harder to ignore until your constructs start responding to them, with shields appearing smaller and restraints breaking sooner because your concentration is splitting between the mission and everything you think might go wrong.

The experienced Lantern with you could recognize what’s happening and tell you to pull back, but the evacuation would already be falling apart. A transport full of civilians could lose control after its pilot panics, forcing you to catch it before it crashes into the city below. You’d make the construct around it too large at first, feel it flicker, then remember what you learned on your first mission and reduce it to the parts that actually need support.

You'd stabilize the transport, but the fear attacking you would shift immediately. Instead of making you afraid of failing the mission, it would start using something more personal. The ring can scan your body and answer questions, but it can’t decide which fear matters most to you. Whatever that is, the attack would find it and make it feel close enough that you start reacting as though it’s already happening.

That would give the Corps its first real clue. The effect isn’t random and it isn’t simply making everyone afraid of the same thing. Something is monitoring people's emotional responses, testing what affects them until it identifies the fear that produces the strongest reaction, and then feeding that fear back until they stop making rational decisions.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: The Corps would trace the outbreaks back to an abandoned station drifting between inhabited systems. Energy readings around it would resemble the emotional spectrum enough for the Lanterns to know the attacks aren’t ordinary technology, but the signal would be unstable and difficult for the rings to classify. You’d go in with a small team because sending dozens of Lanterns into something that can weaponize fear against them could create a bigger problem than the one they’re trying to solve.

Inside, the station would be almost empty. There’d be no huge army defending it, only machinery built around collecting emotional responses from nearby populations and amplifying them across enormous distances. Whoever created it had figured out how to turn fear into a feedback loop, making people more afraid as the machine records their reactions and sends them back stronger.

You'd try destroying the equipment and discover that the station reacts to anyone attacking it. The moment your construct hits one of the central systems, the fear effect around you spikes hard enough to break your concentration. The ring would stay on your hand and keep functioning, but everything you make starts collapsing because you can’t hold a clear image for more than a few seconds.

You’d start using the ring differently. Instead of creating anything complicated, you’d make the smallest constructs you can hold without losing them, using simple platforms, narrow braces, and short barriers to move deeper into the station. The fear would still be there, but you’d stop spending energy trying to overpower it and focus on one immediate action at a time.

That would get you close enough to find the actual core. The machine would show you exactly why the ring chose you at the worst possible moment. Whatever fear it has been using against you would become so convincing that leaving the station suddenly feels safer than taking another step. Your ring could even warn that your concentration is dropping, which would make the thought of failure feel more real because now there’s measurable proof that you’re struggling.

You wouldn’t beat that by convincing yourself there’s nothing to fear. You’d know the fear is real because some version of it could happen, and that’s exactly why it works. What changes is that you decide what you’re doing anyway.

Your construct would steady enough for you to reach the core, but destroying it still wouldn’t be simple. The station has been feeding on fear from entire populations, so the amount of stored energy inside is far beyond what your ring can safely contain by itself.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: You'd realize that blowing up the core could release everything it has collected at once, sending another wave through every world already connected to the station. The veteran Lanterns could evacuate and call for more help, but millions of people would remain exposed while the signal continues spreading.

The ring would identify a second option. If someone enters the core’s control chamber and manually redirects the stored energy away from the network, the station can be shut down without releasing the entire charge. The problem is that whoever does it would be standing inside the strongest concentration of the fear effect.

You’d go in because you're already closest and because waiting gives the machine more time to spread. The moment the chamber closes around you, every fear it found earlier would hit at once. Your constructs would disappear almost completely, your flight would become unstable, and the ring’s voice would keep reporting how badly your focus is dropping.

You'd have to operate the controls while your own mind is telling you to leave. The station would make you see the consequences of staying, then show you versions of what happens if you fail. You’d know some of those images are false, but knowing that wouldn’t stop your body from reacting to them.

You’d stop trying to hold one enormous construct around the entire core and use the style you developed during training. Several smaller pieces would lock the unstable systems into place while another redirects the energy through the station’s external channels. You’d keep each construct simple enough that you can rebuild it quickly whenever your concentration slips.

The veteran Lanterns outside would handle the energy as it leaves the station, but the controls stay in your hands. You’d have to keep choosing the next step until the feedback network starts shutting down world by world.

Your constructs would return to normal almost instantly, and the station would finally go silent. The people affected across the sector would still need time to recover, but the thing amplifying their fear would be gone because you stayed inside long enough to finish the shutdown.

Back on Oa, nobody would pretend that 1 mission turned you into an expert. You’d still have plenty to learn, and experienced Lanterns would remain faster and more precise with their rings. The difference is that you’ve now handled a situation where training could only take you so far, and the decision that finished the mission was yours.

scripts.title: What If Yuji Joined The Avengers

sections.name: INTRO
paras: Yuji would probably get along with the Avengers faster than anyone expects. Steve would like that he runs toward danger without thinking twice, Peter would finally have someone his own age who understands what it feels like to be thrown into fights, and even Tony would have a hard time arguing with someone who keeps saving people.

Then Sukuna opens his mouth and things go left. Because every time the Avengers bring Yuji into another fight, they’re also bringing along someone who has absolutely no interest in being a hero and gets more curious every time this universe shows him something or someone stronger.

sections.name: PART 1
paras: Yuji would come from shortly after Shibuya, with 15 of Sukuna’s fingers already inside him and everything that happened there still fresh in his head. He has already fought Mahito, learned how much damage Sukuna can cause when he gets control, and reached the point where using cursed energy in a fight is normal for him. He still wouldn't have the later abilities he develops much further into the manga, so most of what he brings to the MCU is his physical strength, cursed energy reinforcement, close-range experience, and the possibility of Black Flash when the timing happens naturally.

The crossover would happen while Yuji is moving through the damaged remains of Shibuya after the barriers used during the incident have started breaking down. 1 section could collapse incorrectly while Yuji passes through it, folding the space around him instead of simply dropping the barrier. Yuji would feel cursed energy distort around his body, lose his footing, and wake up somewhere that looks nothing like Tokyo. The barrier would close behind him before he understands what happened, leaving him in New York in 2012 with no obvious way back.

For the first few hours, Yuji would think he had somehow been thrown into another part of the world. His phone still works as a device, but none of his contacts connect, searches for the people he knows lead nowhere, and there’s no record of jujutsu society. He’d also notice that New York doesn’t feel like the cities he knows. His own cursed energy is still there and Sukuna is still inside him, yet he isn’t finding the same constant presence of curses that should exist around millions of people.

Yuji wouldn’t stay unnoticed for long because he’d eventually see someone in danger and react before thinking about how strange his abilities look here. If a car loses control near a crowded street, Yuji could stop it from crushing someone by catching part of the frame and forcing it away. People would record enough of that for S.H.I.E.L.D. to notice a teenager displaying strength far beyond anything a normal human should have.

Natasha would be sent to find him before Fury sends an armed team. She'd quickly realize Yuji is confused rather than hiding some larger plan, and Yuji would cooperate once she says S.H.I.E.L.D. might be able to investigate the energy event that brought him here. He wouldn't know whether they can actually help, but he has nowhere else to start.

The conversation would get much worse when Fury asks whether anything else came through with him. Sukuna could form a mouth across Yuji’s cheek and answer before Yuji gets the chance, making everyone in the room realize there is another person inside the body they have been examining. Yuji would explain what Sukuna is, how the fingers work, and why killing Yuji was considered an acceptable solution back home. He wouldn't hide Shibuya either, because if S.H.I.E.L.D. is going to keep him around, they need to know what happened the last time Sukuna was given control.

Fury wouldn't let Yuji walk freely after hearing that, although Yuji wouldn't fight him over it. The part Natasha would notice is that Yuji doesn’t argue that Sukuna is harmless or promise he can control every situation. He agrees to stay somewhere secure because he already knows what happens when people underestimate the thing inside him.

A few days later, the Tesseract facility would be attacked and Loki would escape with the cube, Clint, and Selvig. Yuji wouldn’t know any of those names yet, but he would notice Sukuna paying attention when S.H.I.E.L.D. starts moving around him differently. For the first time since they arrived, Sukuna would be interested in something happening outside Yuji’s body, which would give Yuji another reason to find out what Fury is dealing with.

sections.name: PART 2
paras: Fury would keep Yuji away from the Tesseract investigation while he starts assembling the Avengers. Steve is brought in, Natasha goes after Bruce, and Tony begins working through the energy data while Yuji remains under observation because nobody knows how Loki’s mind control would interact with Sukuna. Yuji would understand the concern, although sitting in a room while other people are preparing for an attack would get harder the longer it goes on. Tony would eventually meet him because Fury wants another opinion on the readings around cursed energy. Tony could watch Yuji reinforce his fist and hit a testing surface hard enough to damage equipment built for enhanced people, then spend more time looking at the sensors than at the punch itself. Yuji would explain that cursed energy makes his existing body stronger and that his best attacks still depend on getting close enough to hit someone, which gives Tony a much clearer idea of where Yuji fits compared with people like Thor or Hulk.

Steve would approach him more simply. He’d ask why Yuji agreed to stay confined when he could probably break through most of the room around him, and Yuji would tell him that keeping other people safe is more important than proving he can leave. Steve would understand that answer without needing to know everything about jujutsu society, and their relationship would start there rather than through another round of tests.

Once Loki is captured and brought onto the Helicarrier, Fury would finally let Yuji closer because they already have several enhanced people aboard and Yuji has been cooperative. Loki would notice him quickly, especially once Sukuna makes himself known from inside Yuji’s body. Loki understands possession and mind control well enough to recognize that Sukuna isn’t simply another personality, but he wouldn't have the scepter with him in the cell. At that point it’s already down in the lab with Bruce, Tony, and the others, so Loki could only probe Yuji through conversation and try figuring out what kind of being is sharing his body.

That chance would come during the attack on the Helicarrier. Once Barton’s team hits the ship, Loki escapes his cell and eventually gets the scepter back, which is when using it on Yuji actually becomes possible. If Yuji gets in his way while Loki is trying to leave, Loki could press the Mind Stone against him expecting the same result he got with Clint.

The effect should still reach Yuji, because there’s no reason cursed energy would automatically make him immune to the Mind Stone. He’d feel his thoughts being pushed on and his body starting to respond to someone else’s control, but Yuji’s mind is already occupied by Sukuna as well. Sukuna wouldn’t suddenly make the Mind Stone powerless, but he would have every reason to resist another person trying to take control of the body he considers his own territory. That could give Yuji a brief opening that Clint never had. Instead of instantly becoming Loki’s servant, the control starts taking hold while Sukuna pushes back from inside, leaving Yuji disoriented and fighting for control long enough to rip the scepter away from his chest. Loki would realize he can affect Yuji, but controlling him cleanly is much harder than controlling a normal human, and Yuji would come out of the encounter knowing the weapon is dangerous enough that he can’t let Loki touch him with it again.

sections.name: PART 3
paras: Yuji would enter the Battle of New York with Steve because the streets are where he can help the most. He can’t fly after Chitauri vehicles and doesn’t have an attack that lets him knock a Leviathan out of the sky, but he can move through wreckage faster than normal soldiers and fight Chitauri troops at close range without needing ammunition. Steve could keep directing civilians toward safer routes while Yuji clears whatever gets between them and the next building.

The regular Chitauri would be dangerous enough that Yuji still has to pay attention. Cursed energy reinforcement can help him take impacts and hit much harder, but an alien energy weapon is still something he has never been shot with before. He’d close distance quickly, break weapons whenever he gets a chance, and use cars or debris for cover instead of standing in the street assuming his body can survive anything.

Steve would adjust to Yuji quickly because Yuji doesn’t need complicated instructions. If Steve tells him a building needs clearing, Yuji can get inside, pull trapped people out, and keep Chitauri away from the exit until everyone moves. Natasha could send him toward ground units near Stark Tower while she works her way toward the portal, giving the team another person who can hold a street without tying down Hulk or Thor.

The Leviathans would still be outside Yuji’s weight class. He could jump onto one when it passes close enough to a building and damage exposed equipment or knock Chitauri riders off, but stopping the whole creature is something Hulk and Thor are much better suited for. Yuji would learn that difference quickly and use his strength where it actually helps instead of spending half the battle trying to prove he can hurt the biggest target.

Sukuna would be unusually quiet while all of this happens. Thor, Hulk, the Tesseract, and the portal would give him far more to watch than the Chitauri soldiers themselves, and Yuji would notice that Sukuna is studying the people around him instead of constantly talking. That would make Yuji uneasy because Sukuna paying attention usually means he has found something worth remembering.

Yuji’s biggest contribution would come when a section of the battle moves into a crowded evacuation route. A group of Chitauri could cut civilians off while Steve is dealing with another attack, leaving Yuji to hold the street by himself for several minutes. He’d start taking hits as the numbers build, and the pressure would force him into the kind of complete focus where Black Flash becomes possible.

Yuji wouldn’t decide to use it on command. He could land a normal punch, hit the timing perfectly by chance, and send cursed energy through the strike within that tiny window. The Black Flash would destroy the Chitauri he hits and give Yuji enough room to break through the group before more civilians get caught behind them.

That would be the first time Tony’s sensors catch what cursed energy looks like when Yuji reaches that level of timing. Tony wouldn’t understand the technique from a distance, but he would remember the spike for later, giving the Avengers another example of how different Yuji’s abilities are from the energy sources they already know.

When Tony carries the missile toward the portal, Yuji would remain on the ground helping Steve move people away from the area around Stark Tower. He wouldn’t suddenly become part of the nuclear solution because there’s nothing in his abilities that helps Tony survive space or redirect the missile.

After the portal closes, Yuji would have his first real look at what the Avengers accomplished together. No single person solved the invasion, and that would matter to someone coming from a world where the strongest sorcerer often carried responsibilities everyone else built their plans around. Yuji wouldn’t officially join anything that night, but Steve would make sure he has somewhere to stay while Fury and Tony continue searching for a way to send him home.

sections.name: PART 4
paras: The next few years would give Yuji a life in the MCU that has very little to do with being held by S.H.I.E.L.D. Tony would keep investigating the dimensional event that brought him there, but the original barrier collapse left almost nothing they can reproduce. Doctor Strange hasn’t become a sorcerer yet, and none of the technology Tony has access to can safely open another universe based on a single unexplained event.

Yuji would spend more time with Steve because Steve understands having your entire world disappear without pretending the 2 experiences are identical. They'd train together, and Steve would quickly learn that Yuji’s fighting style comes from someone who expects every exchange to happen at close range. Yuji could learn more disciplined defensive movement from Steve, while Steve would get used to sparring with someone whose punches become much heavier the moment cursed energy reinforces them.

S.H.I.E.L.D. would occasionally ask Yuji to help with situations involving enhanced people or alien material left after New York, but he wouldn’t become one of Fury’s agents. He’d work when the mission makes sense and spend the rest of his time trying to build something resembling a normal life, which would also keep the Avengers from feeling like the only thing he has left.

The HYDRA reveal would change that arrangement quickly. Once Steve learns that HYDRA has been operating inside S.H.I.E.L.D. and Project Insight is designed to kill people based on what an algorithm predicts they might eventually do, Yuji would understand the problem without needing a long explanation. He comes from a society where the people in charge sentenced him to death because of the danger inside him, so the idea of killing someone for what they might become would hit close enough that he’d side with Steve almost immediately.

Yuji could help during the collapse of S.H.I.E.L.D. by handling the physical obstacles Steve and Sam run into while Natasha works on exposing HYDRA publicly. He could break through secured areas, fight HYDRA agents without slowing the group down, and keep people off Steve while the Helicarrier plan moves forward. He still wouldn’t replace any of them because he doesn’t know the systems, the intelligence network, or the larger plan well enough to lead it himself.

The more personal change would happen after the organization falls apart. S.H.I.E.L.D. was the group that found Yuji, housed him, kept records on Sukuna, and supported Tony’s attempts to understand how he arrived. Once it disappears, there is no institution keeping Yuji in the MCU anymore. He could leave, disappear into another city, or stop getting involved with the Avengers entirely.

Yuji would choose to stay near them because by then he trusts the people more than the organization that introduced them. Steve has treated him like a person from the beginning, Natasha knows exactly how dangerous Sukuna is without making every conversation about it, and Tony has spent years trying to solve a problem that might never have a clean answer.

That decision would put Yuji with the team when they begin tracking HYDRA’s remaining bases and eventually recover Loki’s scepter in Sokovia. By then, Yuji isn’t waiting for Fury to tell him whether he’s allowed to help. He’s there because this has become his fight too.

sections.name: PART 5
paras: The attack on HYDRA’s Sokovian base would begin like another Avengers mission until Wanda reaches Yuji. He’d already be fighting alongside Steve and Natasha through the outer defenses when Wanda starts using her powers to push the team into visions built from their fears. Yuji has enough trauma for her to work with, and Shibuya would be the obvious place for his mind to go. Wanda’s power would reach deeper than Yuji expects and begin dragging him back toward the destruction Sukuna caused there. The problem for Wanda is that Yuji’s mind isn’t occupied by Yuji alone. As her influence moves further in, she could become aware of another consciousness and briefly find herself somewhere resembling Sukuna’s innate domain rather than remaining entirely inside the memory she was trying to control.

Sukuna would already be waiting for her. Wanda wouldn’t know what the place is or why someone else is looking back at her from inside Yuji, and Sukuna wouldn't explain it. He could react with enough hostility that Wanda pulls herself out before she gets the same amount of time inside Yuji’s head that she has with the other Avengers. Yuji would come back to himself shaken by the memory, while Wanda leaves knowing the teenager she just attacked contains something that noticed her presence and could respond.

Yuji wouldn’t suddenly become immune to Wanda after that. If she gets another clean chance to affect him, her powers are still real and Sukuna has no reason to rescue Yuji simply because he dislikes intruders. The encounter would matter because Wanda now knows Sukuna exists before she ever joins the Avengers, and Sukuna has seen a power that can reach into a mind without using cursed energy.

Tony and Bruce would still create Ultron after Wanda’s vision pushes Tony further into his fear of another invasion. Yuji wouldn’t be in the room when they make that decision, and his cursed energy wouldn't give him any special way to detect an artificial intelligence spreading through computer systems. Once Ultron attacks, Yuji could destroy individual bodies easily enough while still being almost useless against the part of Ultron that lives across networks.

That keeps his role physical once the team reaches Sokovia. Yuji could move through collapsing buildings, carry injured civilians, and smash drones away from evacuation routes while Tony, Vision, and the others deal with the larger technological problem. He’d work especially well around Hawkeye because Clint can identify where people are trapped while Yuji has the strength to reach them quickly.

Wanda would eventually fight beside him after turning against Ultron, which would make their first interactions uncomfortable. She knows what she encountered inside him, and Yuji knows she saw memories he never wanted anyone in this universe to experience. There wouldn't be time to resolve that while the city is rising, so they’d simply work around each other and deal with the conversation later.

Pietro’s death would still happen because Yuji isn’t fast enough to replace him when the Quinjet opens fire on Clint and the child. Yuji could be somewhere else clearing drones or getting civilians toward the lifeboats when Pietro makes that choice, and he would only learn what happened after the shooting stops.

Yuji would take the death hard without turning it into another repeat of Shibuya. He has already learned that freezing in the middle of a disaster only leaves more people without help, so he’d keep moving through the evacuation even while the loss sits with him. Steve wouldn’t need to give him a speech because Yuji is already doing what Steve would ask him to do.

After Sokovia, Wanda would join the new Avengers while carrying the memory of what she saw inside Yuji. That gives the team a new problem they haven’t had before: someone besides Yuji has now directly encountered Sukuna and knows there is far more happening inside him than S.H.I.E.L.D.’s old sensors ever showed.

Zemo could make things worse once he starts working through leaked HYDRA and S.H.I.E.L.D. files. He wouldn’t need to change his entire plan around Yuji, but finding a classified report that says an Avenger once carried a being responsible for thousands of deaths would be useful. Rather than leaking it before Vienna and creating another public crisis around the Avengers, Zemo could keep the information in reserve while he focuses on turning the team against itself.

Yuji would hate seeing Shibuya reduced to headlines written by people who weren't there. He’d still go with Steve when Bucky is blamed for the Vienna bombing because the evidence against Bucky starts looking wrong once Steve explains what HYDRA did to him. Yuji knows exactly how ugly it gets when everyone decides someone is guilty because of the thing controlling their body, so he’d want Bucky brought in alive long enough to find out what actually happened. When Zemo activates Bucky inside custody, Yuji would be one of the first people able to slow him down without using a weapon. Bucky’s metal arm would be strong enough to contest Yuji directly, but Yuji’s cursed reinforcement and close range experience would let him stay in the fight long enough for Steve and the others to respond. Seeing the trigger words work in person would also make the comparison to Sukuna uncomfortable for Yuji, because Bucky has spent years being punished for actions committed while somebody else controlled him.

The airport fight could still happen because the larger conflict hasn’t gone away, but Yuji wouldn’t fit neatly onto either side. He’d go with Steve once he believes Zemo is heading toward the other Winter Soldiers, while still thinking Tony is right that the Avengers need some form of accountability. Most of his time at the airport would be spent trying to create openings for Steve’s group to leave rather than knocking teammates unconscious, and he’d have no interest in fighting someone like Vision when the objective is getting to Siberia.

Tony would still reach Siberia and learn what happened to his parents. Yuji couldn’t fix that moment, and trying to stand between Tony, Steve, and Bucky after the footage plays would only give Tony another person to push through. He could help stop the fight from becoming even worse once everyone is injured, but the damage between Steve and Tony would remain because the argument there is personal in a way cursed energy can’t solve.

After Civil War, Yuji wouldn’t stay hidden with Steve permanently or return to Tony as if nothing happened. He’d move between the people he still trusts while refusing to sign an agreement that allows somebody to lock him away solely because Sukuna exists. That would leave him outside the official Avengers building for a while, even though almost everyone involved would still call him when something goes wrong.

sections.name: PART 7
paras: Doctor Strange would enter Yuji’s life after becoming Master of the Mystic Arts, because the Avengers finally have someone whose work is close enough to souls and spiritual energy that Tony’s machines stop being the only option. Strange would hear about Yuji through the old S.H.I.E.L.D. records and immediately want to know whether Sukuna is possessing him, sharing his soul, or attached through some other mechanism.

They wouldn’t get a miracle cure out of it. Strange could tell Yuji that forcing the separation without understanding the bond might kill him, release Sukuna in a form nobody can predict, or damage both souls badly enough that neither survives properly. Yuji would accept that answer because he’s heard worse, while Strange would keep researching without promising he can solve something that jujutsu sorcerers spent generations failing to handle.

Strange wouldn’t show Sukuna the Time Stone just to satisfy his curiosity, but Yuji already knows enough about the Avengers to understand that there are objects in this universe capable of doing things cursed techniques can't.

sections.name: PART 8
paras: When Ebony Maw and Cull Obsidian arrive in New York, Yuji would already be close enough to Strange that he gets pulled into the fight without needing anyone to call him first. He could handle Cull’s movements better than a normal human, but the strength gap would still be obvious once they clash. Yuji could reinforce his body, survive being thrown through part of a building, and get back up, while direct exchanges would still favor Cull if Yuji stays in front of him too long.

Maw would be a worse matchup because telekinesis gives Yuji very little to work with. There’s no punch to read if the pavement underneath him suddenly folds upward, and cursed energy doesn’t stop Maw from lifting his entire body off the ground. Yuji would spend more time breaking free from whatever Maw throws around him and keeping civilians away from the fight while Tony and Strange handle the parts of the battle suited to them.

If Strange still gets taken onto the Q-Ship, Yuji wouldn't follow into space because he has no safe way to survive outside the atmosphere. That keeps him on Earth when Steve’s side reunites with the others and the fight moves toward Wakanda. By then, Civil War matters less than the fact that Vision has an Infinity Stone in his head and an alien army is coming to take it. Yuji would fit naturally into the ground battle because the Outriders fight almost entirely at close range. He could reinforce his body and move through them without needing ammunition, working near Steve and T’Challa where the fighting is thickest. Black Flash could happen again during the battle if Yuji reaches the timing naturally, but it wouldn’t become something he throws out every few minutes just because the enemy count is high.

Sukuna would be paying attention to Thanos long before Yuji actually sees him. The Stones, the invasion, and the amount of power moving around Wakanda would be enough to keep him unusually focused, but he wouldn't offer Yuji another easy deal or repeat the same temptation from New York. Sukuna knows Yuji won’t hand him control simply because people are dying, so he’d wait for a situation where Yuji has fewer choices.

Thanos arriving would give him one. Yuji would see people like Steve, T’Challa, and Bruce get overwhelmed one after another, then watch Wanda destroy the Mind Stone only for Thanos to reverse the moment with the Time Stone. Yuji could try attacking him with everyone else, but 15-finger Sukuna’s vessel is still nowhere near enough to physically stop Thanos with several Stones.

Half the people around him would disappear, and Sukuna would remain inside him because they share the same body. Yuji would be standing in Wakanda while people turn to dust around him, with no enemy left to hit and no technique he can use to bring anybody back.
Steve would survive too, which means Yuji would have someone beside him who understands that the next job starts after the battle is already lost.

sections.name: PART 9
paras: The 5 years after the Snap would change Yuji more than any single Avengers mission. Those years would give him something he never had in his own world which is time to grow without constantly being pushed from 1 disaster into the next.

Yuji would work with Steve, Natasha, Rhodey, and the remaining Avengers because there are still people who need help even after the population is cut in half. His strength would be useful for rescue work, damaged infrastructure, and the smaller conflicts that continue while governments are struggling to function. He wouldn’t spend 5 years fighting supervillains every week, and that would let his role become broader than hitting whatever the Avengers point him toward. Years of fighting and training would also make Yuji far more efficient with cursed energy reinforcement and close-range combat than he was in Shibuya, even if being stranded here means he never automatically gains the later techniques he would have developed back home.

Sukuna would hate the quiet more than Yuji does. The strongest people he had been watching are dead, missing, or scattered, and the universe has been reshaped by someone Sukuna never got to fight. He’d still talk when he feels like it, but Yuji would become better at ignoring him because 5 years of sharing a body is enough time for Sukuna’s attempts to provoke him to stop working as often.

When Scott Lang returns and the Time Heist becomes possible, Yuji wouldn’t be one of the people designing quantum travel. His role would come later, once the Avengers realize they need teams protecting the operation and moving through points in history where one mistake could ruin everything. Yuji could join a team where close-range strength is useful, but the actual retrieval of Stones would still depend on the characters who know those places and events. The return of everyone who was snapped would bring Doctor Strange, Wanda, Peter, and the others back exactly as Yuji remembers them, while they would see someone 5 years older standing where the teenager they knew used to be. Peter would probably feel that difference more than most because from his perspective almost no time passed, while Yuji has lived through years Peter never experienced.
There wouldn’t be much time to deal with it before Thanos attacks the compound.

Yuji could survive the initial destruction through cursed reinforcement and help dig others out before the final battle spreads across the ruins. He’d fight beside the Avengers as everyone returns through Strange’s portals, and this time there wouldn't be any question about whether Yuji belongs in the lineup. He has already spent years keeping part of the team together while most of these people were gone.

sections.name: PART 10
paras: The final battle would also be the moment Sukuna makes his own move. Yuji would eventually see the Nano Gauntlet moving across the battlefield while everyone is trying to keep it away from Thanos. Sukuna would understand enough by then to know what the Stones are capable of, and this would be the first time all 6 are close enough for him to potentially reach at once. He could use the binding vow Yuji forgot about years ago. Sukuna saying “Enchain” would give him control for 1 minute under the same rules established back in Yuji’s world. He wouldn't be allowed to kill or hurt anyone during that time, which means the Avengers wouldn’t suddenly be fighting a full malevolent Shrine in the middle of the battlefield. Yuji would simply disappear from control while Sukuna takes over his body and immediately heads for the Gauntlet.

Wanda would recognize the change before most people because she knows what Sukuna feels like from inside Yuji’s mind. Strange would understand a second later once he sees the soul controlling the body has shifted, and both of them would realize Sukuna isn’t trying to help with Thanos.

Sukuna wouldn't be able to bulldoze through the Avengers without breaking his vow, so he’d have to move around them instead. He could use Yuji’s physical ability and cursed energy to cross the battlefield quickly, dodge attacks without striking back, and look for the shortest route toward whoever is carrying the Gauntlet.

That limitation would give the Avengers a real chance to stop him. Peter could web his legs, Strange could portal him away from the Gauntlet, and Wanda could restrain him without needing to enter his mind again. Sukuna would be forced to spend precious seconds escaping holds while refusing to injure anybody himself.

He might still get close enough to touch the Gauntlet before Strange removes it through a portal. The contact would be enough for Sukuna to feel the scale of what the Stones contain, but nowhere near enough time to learn how to use them or survive trying to command all 6 through Yuji’s body.

The minute would end before Sukuna gets what he wants. Yuji would regain control in the middle of the battlefield with no memory of the vow itself, leaving Strange and Wanda to explain what just happened while Thanos is still attacking. Yuji would be horrified that Sukuna had a way to take control he never remembered agreeing to, but there wouldn't be time for him to fall apart over it.

Tony would still end the battle by taking the Stones and snapping Thanos’ army away, because Yuji has no reason to be anywhere near a weapon that can kill someone as durable as Tony from the effort alone. Yuji would survive long enough to see Tony die after saving everyone, and the loss would hit differently after 11 years of knowing him as one of the people who kept trying to understand Yuji instead of simply fearing what was inside him.

After Tony’s funeral, Strange and Wanda would sit down with Yuji and tell him everything they saw when Sukuna took control. They now know Sukuna has at least 1 method of taking Yuji’s body under specific rules, and Yuji knows ignoring that possibility would be reckless.
